"We wish to recognise the generations of the local Aboriginal people of the Bundjalung Nation who have lived in and derived their physical and spiritual needs from the forests, rivers, lakes and streams of this beautiful valley over many thousands of years as the traditional owners and custodians of these lands."","isPublic":false,"isPublished":false,"isCurrentItem":false,"meeting":null,"reports":[],"attachments":[],"actionSheets":[],"bookmarks":[],"minutes":[]},{"id":867,"name":"PRAYER","parentId":-1,"sortOrder":3,"minutesSortOrder":3,"minutesParentId":-1,"outlineNumber":"3.","fullOutlineNumber":"3.","htmlContent":"

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor John Harris:

"Father God, I want to start by thanking You for the rain we've been enjoying.  I know this is in keeping with Your promise that as long as the earth remains there will always be seasons including seeding times and harvest times.  At the same time we're conscious there are still large parts of our country that need rain - relief from drought and from the bushfires.  So we ask that You will cause it to rain in these places too.

The challenges this nation has experienced through drought and bushfires causes us to reevaluate things in our lives.  Things that we thought we couldn't live without seem relatively insignificant when we're faced with life threatening situations.  We value the natural life You give us and the provision You make for sustaining us.  We realise how blessed we are in this nation compared to many around our world.

God, sometimes temporary hardships awaken us to what is really important and what is superfluous - what really matters and what is really irrelevant.  We recalibrate our value systems and assess our priorities.  Father God, please help us to do this - help us to distinguish between personal preferences and that which is of real importance.  Help us to know how to stand up for what is true, noble, honorable and godly.  Help us to be courageous enough to work relentlessly to ensure those things that are of greatest importance area what we attend to with a care and concern for others and not a personal agenda.

So I pray for those in this room, members of this Council who have and hold responsible positions, representing the community.  God, help them in these positions, may they have Your wisdom, Your leading,  May they stand together for the good and benefit of the community.  May they uphold Your ways and know Your blessing upon them.

We pray for our community.  We ask that the vulnerable will live in safety.  We pray the needy will know generous provision from those who have more than enough.  We pray we will all be aware of your love and care for us - thank You is something you never withhold.

It is in the name of Your Son Jesus Christ that we thank you and ask these things, Amen."

Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that the recommendations of the Ordinary Planning Committee Meeting held Thursday 6 February 2020 be adopted.

8.1.    Development Application DA19/0830 for Alterations and Additions to Existing Brewery and Replacement of CO2 Tank at Lot 207 DP 1122768 No. 35-37 Kite Crescent, South Murwillumbah

RECOMMENDED that:

1. Clause 4.6 Variation to the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 in regards to the Height of Buildings Map regarding the 1.95m height variation be supported and the concurrence of the Director-General of the Department of Planning be assumed.
2. Development Application DA19/0830 for alterations and additions to existing brewery and replacement of CO2 tank at Lot 207 DP 1122768 No. 35-37 Kite Crescent, South Murwillumbah be approved subject to the conditions as attached.

8.2.   Development Application DA19/0242 for the Erection of Dwelling to Create Detached Dual Occupancy and a Detached Garage and Carport at Lot 38 DP 263730 No. 52 Royal Drive, Pottsville

RECOMMENDED that Council:

1. Accepts the Asset Protection Zone Plan of Management for part Lot 39 DP263730 and part Lot 65 DP866656 prepared by Bushfire Risk and dated 8 January 2020 in relation to DA19/0242 for the erection of a dwelling to create a detached dual occupancy and a detached garage and carport at Lot 38 DP 263730 No. 52 Royal Drive, Pottsville.
2. Accepts the Asset Protection Zone Plan of Management for part Lot 39 DP263730 and part Lot 65 DP866656 prepared by Bushfire Risk and dated 8 January 2020 satisfies condition 13 of DA19/0242 for the erection of a dwelling to create a detached dual occupancy and a detached garage and carport at Lot 38 DP 263730 No. 52 Royal Drive, Pottsville.
3. Requires a letter as offered from the owner of the subject site that indemnifies Council from any liability of future claims relating to the management of the Asset Protection Zone and which provides an indication to Council to apply a restriction on the title of the property.

8.3.   Development Application DA19/0773 for a 'For the Love' Music Festival to be held on Saturday 22 February from 1pm until 10pm at Ebenezer Park, Tweed Heads at Lot 7339 DP 1166191; Part Lot 7340 DP 1166191; Lot 7341 DP 1166191 & Lot 7342 DP 1166191; Lot 7343 DP 1166191; Part Lot 448 DP 755740; Part Lot 653 DP 755740; Lot 704 DP 877249; Lot 703 DP 877250; Coral Street, Tweed Heads

RECOMMENDED that Development Application DA19/0773 for a 'For the Love' music festival to be held on Saturday 22 February from 1pm until 10pm at Ebenezer Park, Tweed Heads at Lot 7339 DP 1166191; Part Lot 7340 DP 1166191; Lot 7341 DP 1166191 & Lot 7342 DP 1166191; Lot 7343 DP 1166191; Part Lot 448 DP 755740; Part Lot 653 DP 755740; Lot 704 DP 877249; Lot 703 DP 877250; Coral Street, Tweed Heads be approved subject to the conditions attached to this report.

8.4.   Development Application DA04/1300.05 for an Amendment to Development Consent DA04/1300 for Integrated Housing Development incorporating 6 Dwellings being Part Two and Part Three Storey at Lot 1 DP 1106423 & Lot 15 DP 21680 No. 12 Hungerford Lane, Kingscliff; Part Lot 3 DP 1106423 No. 12-14 Hungerford Lane, Kingscliff

ALTERNATE MOTION

RECOMMENDED that Development Application DA04/1300.05 for an amendment to Development Consent DA04/1300 for integrated housing development incorporating 6 dwellings being part two and part three storey at Lot 1 DP 1106423 & Lot 15 DP 21680 No. 12 Hungerford Lane, Kingscliff; Part Lot 3 DP 1106423 No. 12-14 Hungerford Lane, Kingscliff be deferred for the applicant to provide a more detailed view loss analysis including the following:

• Photographs of seaward/water views from viewing points such as outdoor living areas, balconies, kitchen windows and living room windows from 40, 42, 44, 46 and 48 Sutherland Street and 10 and 16 Hungerford Lane.
• Views to be recorded (photographed) should include those taken at the sitting and standing height for an average person.
• Preparation of 3D models (using either architectural 3D plans or photomontages based on the photographs above) to visually demonstrate the view loss for the approved and proposed development from the viewing points identified earlier.
• The adopted viewing floor levels for any 3D architectural modelling (ie balcony height) should be confirmed by a surveyor.

The above will require the owners of adjacent properties to allow the applicant access to their properties to obtain photographs. If this permission is not granted objectors may provide the applicant with photos to assist the process.

8.5.  Planning Proposal PP19/0005 for Additional Permitted Uses at Salt Village - Part Lot 3 SP 74283 and Lot 5 DP 83483, 49-51 Bells Boulevard, Kingscliff

ALTERNATE MOTION

RECOMMENDED that that this item be deferred for the proponents to provide more detailed technical justification to demonstrate that any future medical centre use of the commercial tenancies would not create shortfalls in available on site parking in the Salt precinct and that consideration also be given to the adjacent vacant land to provide any required parking deficit.

8.6.   Variations to Development Standards under State Environmental Planning Policy No. 1 - Development Standards

RECOMMENDED that Council notes the December 2019 Variations to Development Standards under State Environmental Planning Policy No. 1 - Development Standards.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr James Owen

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)
Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

The Draft Climate Change Policy be placed on exhibition for a period of 60 days with the following changes:

    • Add a subheading to the name of the Policy titled "Zero Emissions by 2030"
    • Add in the Guiding Principles:

      The environment of the Tweed Shire is of international significance and particularly vulnerable to climate change.   Special attention needs to be given to the many species at the extent of their range that will struggle to tolerate more extreme climatic conditions.

      Governments at all levels have an obligation to protect and enhance this global asset. 

    • In the Key Priorities section:

      Add after the 8th point "demonstrates sustainability to the broader community through Council's own development/construction/maintenance activities.

      Change order of point 5 regarding targets to bring it up to point 1.

      Point 13

      Address the impacts of climate change in biodiversity conservation by increasing native forest cover and wildlife connectivity, and reducing ecosystem degradation across the Tweed Shire.

      Change to:

      Assess and address the impacts of climate change in biodiversity conservation by increasing native (delete - forest) vegetation cover and wildlife connectivity, and (delete - reducing ecosystem degradation) improving ecosystem health across the Tweed Shire.

      Point 15

      Lobby the NSW Government to investigate alternative revenue sources

      Change to:

      Advocate to the NSW and Federal Government for improved legislation and funding to address climate change.

    • Add a new point:

      Monitor and review Council’s Investment Strategy and portfolio to avoid/minimise investments in financial organisations that support the fossil fuel industry where legislatively possible and economically viable.

    • A communication and engagement plan be implemented to promote interest in, and submissions to, the Policy.
    • Add in to page 9, context:

Cities for Climate Protection Program In 1997 Tweed Shire Council joined the Cities for Climate Protection TM (CCPTM) Program, a voluntary initiative that assists local governments around the world to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in their municipality.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that:


1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 28 November 2019 be received and noted; and

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

A1 [LTC] Leisure Drive, Banora Point, Kennedy Drive, Tweed Heads West and Kirkwood Road, Tweed Heads South.

1. That the bus zone on Leisure Drive adjacent Banora Centro be extended west 12.5m to cater for an extra bus.
2. That a 30m bus zone be installed in the service road on Kennedy Drive, between 226 and 230 Kennedy Drive and a section of double centre lines be removed from Kennedy Drive to enable vehicles to exit the service road in an east bound direction.
3. That a 60m bus zone be installed on Kirkwood Road west of the shopping centre entrance, subject to evidence being provided that the buses utilising the zone are able to carry out a u-turn on Kirkwood Road in one movement.

A2 [LTC] Botany Crescent and Keith Compton Drive, Tweed Heads.

That the double centre lines on Botany Crescent extending from Keith Compton Drive, be reduced to 10m in length.

A3 [LTC] For The Love - February 2020.

That the proposed For The Love Festival on 22 February 2020 be supported, subject to:
1. NSW Police approval being obtained.
2. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Roads & Maritime Services accredited persons.
3. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
4. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
5. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.
6. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
7. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
8. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
9. That the applicant organise for the event to be listed on Council's Calendar of Events web page. Go to www.tweed.nsw.gov.au and select Our Community/Festivals Events and Filming/Calendar of Events and access the Calendar of Events site to upload the event details.
10. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
11. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
12. The event organiser is to consult with public transport providers to provide an adequate level of service for the event.
13. The use of the proposed temporary car park bordering Eden Street and Hill Street is not supported.
14. Alternate parking and suitable bus routes need to be identified by the Event Coordinator.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr James Owen

If the owners of Lot 7 DP 593200 reach a negotiated agreement with the Council under the provisions of s88b of the Conveyancing Act Council will proceed under these provisions to extend the sewerage system and retain the existing water connection to Lot B DP 419641 within the dedicated buffer area.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle, Living Waters Church, Tumbulgum:

Dear Lord,

We thank you for the recent rain that has filled our dam and greened our landscape and bought welcome relief to our farmers.  We thank you for quenching the fires that remained down the east coast, however our hearts go out to those who have lost family, animals and property.  Although many of us were on flood watch again we thank you that we were spared from pending disaster.

As council sits today to preside over matters concerning the Tweed Shire, we seek your guidance, your direction and your favour.  You love this shire and this nation, "the Great South Land of the Holy Spirit".  May you guide every decision made here today.

In Jesus name we Pray, Amen

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)
Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that the following tabled Petition(s) be received and noted.

  • Petition received on 28 January 2020 containing 1499 valid signatories regarding water extraction and advising as follow:

"We the undersigned wish to advise council of our displeasure that they are allowing water miners to continue sucking aquifers dry, while the taxpayers of Tweed Shire are/will be hit with strict water restrictions.  In this time of severe drought there should be thought given to all areas of water preservation.  to be trucking tankers of this precious commodity to other regions is a disgrace.

Aside from the actual water mining, there is the issue of water bottle pollution.  Let's make Murwillumbah plastic bottle free, by introducing more water bubblers and filtered filling stations around the town.

Your consideration of these matters would be appreciated."

  • Petition received on 10 February 2020 from 34 signatories from concerned residents of Lagoon Road and Dune Street, Fingal Head  advising as follows:

Parking issues in and around Lagoon Road, Fingal Head have now become acute.

"Over the past few years we have experienced a dramatic increase in the number of Surfing related cars parking on both sides of our narrow street on at least 3 consecutive days per week.

The escalation of parking numbers has now reached a point where on the average surf days of Friday Sat and Sunday it is difficult for an average car to navigate the street and nearly impossible for council service vehicles to collect the bins or for an ambulance or Fire engine to be able to access the street. It has also become common for residents to be unable to exit their properties without assistance to avoid damaging parked vehicles Parking issues in and around Lagoon Road, Fingal Head have now become acute.

This is common at the intersection of Dune Street and Lagoon Road.

There are a number of issues emanating from the explosion of visitors to The South Beach area which on past records looks like becoming completely unsustainable in the near future.

1/. It is common to have 50 to 70 vehicles parked for up to 4 hours, each having 2 to 3 adults who are visiting an area without toilets and in many cases using our environment in a most inappropriate manner including the Lagoon in front of our properties.Residents point to evidence that the area in around the beach is commonly polluted with faeces. This sort of behaviour can only get worse as numbers increase and is most unacceptable

2/. There is a major issue with access to and from Dune Street into Lagoon Road during these events due to parked vehicles blocking the corners and parking opposite the intersection. This is going to get much worse in a few months time

3/. South Beach is easily accessed with adequate parking in areas which have no impact on local residents, including from Mid FingaI Road, the quarry and Old Boat harbour which are suitable to accommodate all the surfing fraternities needs with out the need to impact Lagoon Road, which is too narrow, is not suitable for multiple car parking and is detrimental to both the environment, the ambience and character of the area.

4/. We understand that there have been concerns with the influx of visitors to the northern end of South Beach for a number of reason including safety, access, poor behaviour amongst others and consider there to be good cause to set in place a strategy to manage these issues into the future.

5/. The residents of Lagoon Road and Dune Street urgently request your consideration for the application of Resident parking only within these 2 streets with a South beach Parking sign be erected on FingaI Road to compensate the surfers and beach goers before they enter Lagoon Road."

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr James Owen

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)
Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

1.     Notes the unprecedented fires and extensive droughts experienced across the Australia have resulted in a current high level of interest from both the community and governments in more resilient landscape management.

2.     Notes there are many areas of the Shire, both public and private lands,that could benefit from improved regenerative land management.

3.     Notes this is an opportune time to engage the rural and wider community in regenerative landscape management.

4.     Arranges a workshop with the SoilsForLife organisation, as soon as possible, to seek information and advice on the appropriateness and potential benefits of regenerative landscape management for the Shire,  and invites representatives of the rural industries and Council's Sustainable Agriculture reference group to the workshop.

  [OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL] [AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"
Cr Reece Byrnes
Cr Warren Polglase

RESOLVED that Council:

1.       Notes community concern regarding the recent classification of Murwillumbah from regional to metropolitan (MMM1) under the Modified Monash Model.

2.       Notes Murwillumbah, now classified as metropolitan (MMM1), potentially faces a decline in a range of health programs including rural Bulk Billing Incentives, Workforce Incentive Programs and the Bonded Medical Program. The classification to MMM1 also means medical practices in Murwillumbah will only be available to General Pathway registrars and no longer to Rural Pathway registrars.

3.       Writes to the Federal Health Minister Greg Hunt asking him to reconsider the change in classification from metropolitan (MMM1) to a regional category and requested to provide an explanation of the reason for the reclassification.

4.       Writes to the local Federal Member, Justine Elliott, to seek her representation in this matter.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr James Owen

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)

PROPOSED that:

1.  Planning Proposal PP18/0004 (Version 3) to remove the enabling Clause 7.15 Water Bottling Facilities from the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014, as attached, be approved and be made under Section 3.36 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.   

2.  Council notes the correspondence from the Office of the Chief Scientist & Engineer dated 5 March 2020 received at 5.05pm and clarifies the planning proposal where required to take account of the issues raised in the correspondence.  Council acknowledges the clarifications sought to be made by the Office of the Chief Scientist & Engineer to the Agenda Report and any decision made by Council tonight takes this information into account.


SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDERS

RESUMPTION OF STANDING ORDERS

Cr Katie Milne
Cr Chris Cherry

that Standing Orders be resumed.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr James Owen

RECOMMENDED that:

1.  Council supports in principle the Planning Proposal PP18/0004 (Version 3) to remove the enabling Clause 7.15 Water Bottling Facilities from the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014, as attached, under Section 3.36 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 .

2.  Council notes the correspondence from the Office of the Chief Scientist & Engineer dated 5 March 2020 received at 5.05pm and clarifies the planning proposal where required to take account of the issues raised in the correspondence.  Council acknowledges the clarifications sought to be made by the Office of the Chief Scientist & Engineer to the Agenda Report and the decision made by Council tonight takes this information into account.

3.  Consultation with DPI Water regarding the Gateway Determination is undertaken as a matter of priority.

4.  Council attaches the letter from the Office of the Chief Scientist & Engineer dated 5 March 2020 to the Minutes.

Amendment 1 was Carried

RESOLVED that Council:

RESOLVED that the recommendations of the Ordinary Planning Committee Meeting held Thursday 5 March 2020 be adopted.

10.1    Planning Proposal PP18/0004 to Remove Enabling Clause 7.1 Water Bottling Facilities from the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014

RECOMMENDED that:

1.  Council supports in principle the Planning Proposal PP18/0004 (Version 3) to remove the enabling Clause 7.15 Water Bottling Facilities from the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014, as attached, under Section 3.36 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 .

2.  Council notes the correspondence from the Office of the Chief Scientist & Engineer dated 5 March 2020 received at 5.05pm and clarifies the planning proposal where required to take account of the issues raised in the correspondence.  Council acknowledges the clarifications sought to be made by the Office of the Chief Scientist & Engineer to the Agenda Report and the decision made by Council tonight takes this information into account.

3.  Consultation with DPI Water regarding the Gateway Determination is undertaken as a matter of priority.

4.  Council attaches the letter from the Office of the Chief Scientist & Engineer dated 5 March 2020 to the Minutes.

10.2    Variations to Development Standards under State Environmental Planning Policy No. 1 - Development Standards

RECOMMENDED that Council notes the January 2020 Variations to Development Standards under State Environmental Planning Policy No. 1 - Development Standards.

The Motion was CARRIED

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

1.      Council:

a.      Requests the owners of Lot B DP 419641 to formally request connection at their property boundary to Councils sewage system on the basis that they pay all associated costs of the connection in line with the total Burringbar Mooball Sewerage Scheme contributions as per option iii in the cost section of this report.

b.      Requests the owners of Lot B DP 419641 to formally request the transfer of the water supply connection from private to public ownership on the basis that they pay the associated costs.

c.      Signals to the owners of Lot 7 DP 593200 its intention to use its powers under section 59A and section 191A of the Local Government Act 1993 to extend the sewerage system and transfer of the water supply connection from private to public ownership across Lot 7 DP 593200 to service Lot B DP 419641 (Tweed Valley Way).

d.      Negotiates with the owners of Lot 7 DP 593200 to extend the sewerage system and transfer of the water supply connection from private to public across their land to service Lot B DP 419641 on the basis that, notwithstanding the provisions of s59A and s191A of the Local Government Act, that Council intends to seek agreement to create a “public positive covenant” under  s88 or other relevant mechanisms under s88 of the Conveyancing Act within the buffer area on Lot 7 DP 593200 (as per Schedule 1 of the Mooball Planning Agreement) to extend the sewerage system and transfer of the water supply connection from private to public ownership across Lot 7 DP 593200 to connect to Lot B DP 419641. Agreement to also include provision for Council’s right to enter the land to construct, maintain, repair and replace infrastructure, and if requested Council to consider providing a connection point to Lot 7 DP 593200 and monetary compensation in accordance with a valuation.

2.       If the owners of Lot 7 DP 593200 are not willing to come to an in-principle agreement under the provisions of s88 of the Conveyancing Act to extend the sewerage system and transfer of the water supply connection from private to public ownership across their land to Lot B DP 419641 within 48 days then Council proceeds with the provision of the above under s59A and s191A of the Local Government Act and authorises the necessary expenditure.

3.       If the owners of Lot 7 DP 593200 reach a negotiated agreement with the Council under the provisions of s88 of the Conveyancing Act then a report be prepared to Council recommending the adoption of the agreement under these provisions to extend the sewerage system and transfer of the water supply connection from private to public ownership to Lot B DP 419641 within the dedicated buffer area. 

4.       ATTACHMENT 3 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:-

(g) advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege.

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Ron Cooper
VOTE AGAINST - Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd from Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church;

"I am going to pray in the Christian tradition.  If you would like to join with me, please bow your head.  Otherwise take a moment to reflect on what will best enable good Council decisions to be made today.

Gracious God,

Thank you for today, and for the health and strength to do our daily work.

Our community and nation have been thrown from one crisis into another.  But even as we deal with COVID-19 we want to stop and be thankful for fires extinguished and dams full.

Please continue to remember us in our distress.  To people who are ill, or cut off from family, friends or work, bring comfort and help.  Protect health workers as they serve the community.  Where people are fearful, give a calm spirit.  help us show kindness to neighbours and strangers. 

We are grateful for Council, elected and staff, who work on our behalf.  Please strengthen them as they work for the benefit of our region.  Grant them wisdom and grace in difficult days.  Bless them in their decision making today, and in the outworking of those decisions into the future.

We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)

RESOLVED that the following tabled Petition(s) be received and noted.

  • Petition containing 663 valid signatories and received on 4 March 2020 entitled "Stop 5G in the Tweed Shire"advising as follows:

"We, members of the Tweed Shire community, do not consent to being irradiated by the extremely high frequencies of 5G, the telecommunications technology required for the Intemet of Things (lo'T) and Smart Cities.

Abundant peer reviewed scientiflc evidence shows exposure to radio frequency electromagnetic radiation (RF-EMR) from wireless telecommunications can cause serious harm to humans and the environment. We recognise the urgent need for an honest, worldwide review of wireless technology use.

Regulatory agencies ARPANSA and ICNIRP do not acknowledge any biological effects other than heating of tissue in exposure standards. Non -thermal bio-effects on humans and the environment are well established and cannot be ignored. These agencies cannot provide any scientific evidence that 5G is safe.

Initially utilising current networks, then moving on ta small cells and extremely high frequencies. 5G enables wireless connection of billions of devices plus public infrastructure to the internet and artificially intelligent (AI) systems.

5G, the loT and Smart Cities are predicted to radically increase energy consumption, negating efforts to reduce carbon emissions People in this community want dean technology - we do not consent to public infrastructure such as 'smart ' street lighting or the related increases in pollution and electronic waste.

This technology also poses serious risks to cyber security through privacy violations. data harvesting and ransomware attacks.

Based on the clear risk of harm to the community 8nd the environment, we implore Tweed Shire Council to adhere to the precautionary principle and halt the roll-out of 5G and loT/Smart City infrastructure in the Tweed Shire by any means possible. until safety and security can be guaranteed. There are safer technology options for the community. Our health, environment, privacy and our children's future are at stake."


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  Nil.

Cr Pryce Allsop
Cr Reece Byrnes

RESOLVED that

1.  The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee meeting held 13 February 2020 be received and noted; and

2.  The Executive Leadership Team Comments be adopted as follows:

A1 Splendour in the Grass 22 to 27 July 2020

That the submitted Traffic Control Plans for Splendour in the Grass 22 to 27July 2020 be supported.

A2 Murwillumbah Cycle Club 2020 Events - 29 February to 24 October

That the proposed Murwillumbah Cycle Club Events from 29 February to 24 October 2020 be supported, subject to:

1. NSW Police approval being obtained.
2. Endorsement of the event by Cycling Queensland.
3. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
4. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
5. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
6. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.
7. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
8. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
9. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
10. That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed. The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources. If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
11. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
12. The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
13. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.

RESOLVED that the proposed road closures associated with the Festival of Speed on Tweed from Friday 2 October 2020 and Monday 5 October 2020 be supported subject to:

1. NSW Police approval being obtained.
2. Licencing of the event by the appropriate regulatory body.
3. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 16 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
4. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns, including a letterbox drop at least 4 weeks prior to event directly affected residents.  
5. Suitable arrangements made with residents whose access to property is affected and these arrangements made in writing.
6. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of 2 weeks prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
7.  Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and this provided to Council and Police.
8. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
9.  Consultation with emergency services and public transport providers and any identified issues addressed.
10. That the applicant visit  www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
11. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
12. The event be conducted and signposted in accordance with Transport for NSW Guidelines to ensure consistency across the network.
13. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
14. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

RESOLVED that Development Application DA19/0805 for a staged rural business hub containing rural industry, garden centre, plant nursery, cafe, signage (stage 1) and dwelling (stage 2) at Lot 100 DP 1011315 Riverside Drive, Tumbulgum be refused for the following reasons: 


1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal, which seeks to construct a mixed use commercial development on a flood prone site below the 5 year ARI flood level and which gives no consideration to flood resilience or the impacts of flooding events on businesses and the local communities that they employ, is contrary to the aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to encourage a sustainable local economy and small business, employment, agriculture, affordable housing, recreational, arts, social, cultural, tourism and sustainable industry opportunities appropriate to Tweed.

2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal is contrary to the aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to promote development that is consistent with the principles of ecologically sustainable development and to implement appropriate action on climate change.

3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal, which does not address flood resilience, is contrary to the objective of Clause 7.3 of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to minimise the flood risk to life and property associated with the use of land. 

Further in accordance with Clause 7.3, the consent authority is not satisfied that the development is not likely to result in unsustainable social and economic costs to the community as a consequence of flooding.

4. Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(a)(iii) the development proposal has not demonstrated due consideration or compliance with Tweed Shire Development Control Plan 2008 - Section A3, as it relates to filling of land and the relevant controls for Tumbulgum Village. 

5. Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(b) the applicant has not demonstrated to the satisfaction of the consent authority that the proposed filling and development of the site will not negatively impact neighbouring properties. 

6. Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(b) the applicant has not demonstrated to the satisfaction of the consent authority that the proposed development will not adversely impact on the residential amenity of adjacent dwellings as a result of internal and external sources of noise, including but not limited to, noise associated with operation of the restaurant/café and associated outdoor dinnng areas, traffic noise, and operation of plant and/or machinery.   

7. Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(b) the applicant has not demonstrated to the satisfaction of the consent authority that the proposed Sewage Treatment Plant and associated effluent Land Application Area can be sited and operated on the site without adversely impact on residential amenity in terms of odour, visual and acoustic impacts. 

8. Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(b) the applicant has not demonstrated to the satisfaction of the consent authority that the proposed sewage treatment plant and associated effluent Land Application Area will not have an adverse impact on ground water as a result of damage to the plant during flood events or leaching of contaminants from the Land Application Area during prolonged rainfall events. 

9. Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(c) the development site is not considered suitable for the proposed development, as evidenced by the non-compliances with Council’s planning requirements; and

10. Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(e) the proposed development, which is located on the flood prone land raising concerns in relation to the impact of the proposed filling, the proximity of the Sewage Treatment Plant and Land Application Area to adjoining residences and the potential for impacts, the lack of information on flood resilience and the impact that future flood events could have on the viability of the business and job security, is not considered to be in the public interest.


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Pryce Allsop

Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

1.     Subject to Council adoption of the Tweed Rural Lands Strategy, that Council prepares a rural development chapter of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008, consistent with the adopted strategy and that within this proposed chapter of the Development Control Plan the requirements relating to commercial hydroponic facilities include consideration of the land use conflicts, particularly the noise associated with ventilation fans, cool rooms, generators and other noise generating equipment, is to be considered when siting such infrastructure to avoid or limit impacts on sensitive receptors (including but not limited to dwellings).
 
2.     In the interim period until the proposed aforementioned Development Control Plan is adopted, Council puts into place appropriate effective control measures as part of development assessment processes, including but not limited to consideration of visual screening, noise limits and increased setbacks to sensitive receivers, to address the land-use conflict issues associated with Commercial Undercover Horticultural and Hydroponic Facilities.

3.    Council acknowledges the uncertainty of the future of food production under climate change and in recognition of the right to farm State Government Policy, Council does not want to compromise the potential for intensive food production on fragmented rural land and seeks to have appropriate information included in planning certificates issued by Council under s10.7(5) of the EPA Act 1979.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper
VOTE AGAINST - Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

RESOLVED that the recommendations of the Ordinary Planning Committee Meeting held Thursday 2 April 2020 be adopted.

8.1      Request to Prepare a Planning Proposal - Lot 1 DP 1032820 Scenic Drive, Bilambil (known as 1 Walmsley Road)

ALTERNATE MOTION

RECOMMENDED that this item be deferred for the proponent to reach a better understanding with Council officers for appropriate requirements for environmental protection and a further report be bought back to Council.

8.2      Development Application DA18/0519 for Multi Dwelling Housing Comprising Three Dwellings, the Use of One Dwelling as Bed and Breakfast Accommodation and Ancillary Structures including Water Tanks and Detached Storage Unit at Lot 1 DP 775668 No. 217 McAllisters Road, Bilambil Heights

ALTERNATE MOTION

RECOMMENDED that this item be deferred for a site inspection and further negotiations with the owner in regard to potential vegetation screening and increased set backs for the neighbours.

8.3.    Variations to Development Standards under State Environmental Planning Policy No. 1 - Development Standards

RECOMMENDED that Council notes there are no variations for the month of February 2020 to Development Standards under State Environmental Planning Policy No. 1 - Development Standards.

RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 12 March 2020 be received and noted; and

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

A1 [LTC] Eden Street, Tweed Heads 

That: 

1. The 'double centrelines' adjacent 3-9 Eden Street, Tweed Heads be reduced by approximately 10m.

2. A length of 'yellow no stopping line' be installed from the western edge of the driveway at 11 Eden Street, Tweed Heads for 17m.

A2 [LTC] Enid Street, Tweed Heads

That the installation of a 'yellow no stopping line' is supported on Enid Street, Tweed Heads, from the driveway of Bay Grand Unit Development, south to the existing driveway of the adjacent property.  
That the Bay Grand Unit Body Corporate be requested to install a 'speed bump' and a 'stop sign' on their property for exiting motorists to reduce risk to pedestrians on the footpath.

A4 [LTC] Chinderah Bay Drive, Chinderah

That a 'yellow no stopping line' be installed 5m to the south and 5m to the north of the driveway at 164 Chinderah Bay Drive, Chinderah.

A5 [LTC] Orient Street, Kingscliff 

That:

1. Consultation be held with the bus operators servicing Kingscliff Public School as to the suitability of removing the bus zone on Orient Street, Kingscliff and using Sutherland Street, Kingscliff frontage for all pick-ups and drop offs.

2. The relocation of the existing children’s crossing and the installation of a new children’s crossing on Sutherland Street, Kingscliff to be considered when plans for the School upgrades are known.

3. Yellow no stopping edge lines be installed on Omar Street, Kingscliff into Orient Street, Kingscliff reinforcing the no stopping within 10m of an intersection.

4. Yellow no stopping edge line be installed on Orient Street, Kingscliff from the entrance of the Teachers’ carpark north to the existing Bus Zone, to improve sight distance for pedestrians.

5. The existing “5 minute 8:00am – 9:30am, 2:30pm – 4:00 School Days” parking length on Orient Street, Kingscliff adjacent to the school be changed to “No Stopping 2:30pm – 3:00pm School Days” and “No Parking 8:00am – 9:30am, 3:00pm – 4:00pm School Days”.

6. The existing “5 minute 8:00am – 9:30am, 2:30pm – 4:00pm School Days” parking length on Sutherland Street, Kingscliff adjacent to the school be changed to “No Stopping 2:30pm – 3:00pm School Days” and “No Parking 8:00am – 9:30am, 3:00pm – 4:00pm School Days”.

The Motion was Carried

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)
Cr Ron Cooper

RESOLVED that:


1. Council pursuant to Section 226(d) and Section 377 of the Local Government Act 1993, delegate authority to the Mayor and/or Deputy Mayor, and the General Manager jointly to exercise any functions of Council that may lawfully be delegated under Section 377 of the Local Government Act. This should be enacted in the event that the need arises which would limit the orderly operations of Council in regards to the operation of the governing body of elected members, including the ability to convene Ordinary and Extraordinary meetings and subject to the restrictions outlined in point (b) and point (c) below.

(b) That a list of any matters considered under such delegated authority be submitted for Council’s information as soon as possible following the execution of such delegation and be formally reported to the next available schedule Ordinary Meeting of Council.


(c) That this temporary delegation of authority only be put into effect if the elected Council is unable to meet because of a lack of a quorum from Councillors being affected by COVID-19, and the matter is unable to be deferred to a future Ordinary Meeting of Council. Further that this temporary delegation be put into effect if Council is unable to conduct ordinary meetings of Council due to restrictions imposed by relevant authorities, and the matter is unable to be deferred to a future Ordinary Meeting of Council.


(d) That this temporary delegation also apply in light of any legislative change, direction or advice arising as a direct result of COVID-19.

2. To ensure continuity of the role of the General Manager and pursuant to Section 351 of the Act, that Council endorse the following:

a. That on and from the date of this resolution, until 30 September 2020, if the appointed General Manager is sick or otherwise absent from work for a period of 2 consecutive business days, a person holding a position within the senior management team will be temporarily appointed to the position of General Manager, on and from the following day, such appointment being subject to:


(i) the maximum period of appointment being the period so specified by Section 351(2) of the Local Government Act,
(ii) the appointment terminating on the day prior to the day that the General Manager returns to work;
(iii) the person not being unable or unwilling to be so appointed.

That a person temporarily appointed as General Manager in accordance with this resolution to have, during that period, all the delegations of the General Manager given by the Council.

RESOLVED that, in order to achieve the most advantageous option for Council, the following is recommended in accordance with Regulation 178 of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2005:

1. Decline to accept any of the Offers.

2. Due to lack of competitive responses, enters into negotiations with suitable businesses (whether or not the person was a tenderer) with a view to entering into a value for money agreement in relation to the Café Gallery Licence.

3. In implementing Part (2) also considers the option of Council carrying out the requirements of the proposed contract itself.

4. A report be provided to Council on the preferred supplier for final approval by Council.

5. ATTACHMENT 1 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:-

(c) information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Late Mayoral Minute Item 9.2 was dealt with as it was ruled by the Chairperson to be of great urgency.

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:


1.  Endorses Local Government NSW’s advocacy to obtain financial assistance, employment support and stimulus funding for the local government sector from State and Federal government and calls for the package to include: 

• Increasing Financial Assistance Grants payments to 1%.
• Immediate financial assistance to support council employees, especially in early education and care.
• Providing stimulus funding to councils for projects that will boost local economies. 
• Increased access to TAFE, VET and other apprenticeship opportunities that council staff can undertake to address skill shortages, especially for staff in non-essential services who are unable to be redeployed; and 
• A reciprocal benefit to the younger generations to alleviate the Climate Change Emergency though measures such as funding for renewable energy and regenerative landscape management.

2. Writes to the State and Federal members for the Tweed Shire to confirm its support for increased financial assistance and stimulus funding for local government to help councils deliver essential services and to protect people’s health and livelihoods. 

3. Advises Local Government NSW of the passage of this Mayoral Minute and provides LGNSW information in relation to: 

• Council’s financial position, funding and resources, including details of mounting costs and declining revenues;
• Examples of service impacts of drought, bushfires and now the COVID-19 pandemic;
• Details on what council is doing to help support local businesses and your local economy, including Council’s COVID Care Package; and 
• Local economic development strategies – local employment, contracts for goods and services, public infrastructure, community services.

The Motion was Carried

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)
 
PROPOSED that:

1.    Council has been advised by the Telstra Corporation that the rollout of 5G has commenced in the Tweed Shire.  As Council was not previously advised of the commencement date for the rollout, the Chairperson now considers this to be a matter which requires urgent consideration of Council. 

2.    Council supports a moratorium on the rollout of 5G in Tweed Shire and writes to the Federal Government and relevant telecommunications agencies to seek support for such a moratorium.

The Motion was Lost

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

Cr James Owen
Cr Reece Byrnes

RESOLVED that:

1.      Council approves the temporary installation of "Road Closed" signage and “No Parking Area” signage on Letitia Road, Fingal Head, and Lighthouse Parade, Fingal Head car park from Queen and Bamberry Streets up to and including 7 May 2020 except for Letitia Road which will be 30 June 2020, subject to a barrier board being installed with the words “Road Closed” or “Car Park Closed” at the closure point, which would enable access to the area for emergency and police vehicles.  An additional sign “Authorised Vehicles Excepted” is to be installed at the Letitia Road closure at the entry to Letitia Road install a "Local Traffic Only" sign.

2.      All existing "Road Closed" signage and “No Parking Area” signage approved by Council through its resolution dated 9 April 2020, be extended up to and including 7 May 2020, with the exception of 30 car spaces in the off street car park adjacent to Lions Park south of the Cudgen Surf Lifesaving Club, which are to be signposted with a 2 hour time limit.

3.   In accordance with the Local Government Act and the Crown Land Management Act where applicable, Council closes the car parks referred to in item 1 and 2 until 7 May 2020  to all vehicles (noting the exception of Letitia Road in 1 above).

4.    The General Manager brings forward a report to the Council Meeting on 7 May 2020 to consider extensions or otherwise of the closures detailed above.


AMENDMENT 1

Cr Ron Cooper
Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)

PROPOSED that

1.      Council approves the temporary installation of "Road Closed" signage and “No Parking Area” signage on Letitia Road, Fingal Head, and Lighthouse Parade, Fingal Head car park from Queen and Bamberry Streets up to and including 7 May 2020 except for Letitia Road which will be 30 June 2020, subject to a barrier board being installed with the words “Road Closed” or “Car Park Closed” at the closure point, which would enable access to the area for emergency and police vehicles.  An additional sign “Authorised Vehicles Excepted” is to be installed at the Letitia Road closure at the entry to Letitia Road install a "Local Traffic Only" sign.

2.      All existing "Road Closed" signage and “No Parking Area” signage approved by Council through its resolution dated 9 April 2020, be extended up to and including 7 May 2020.

3.      In accordance with the Local Government Act and the Crown Land Management Act where applicable, Council closes the car parks referred to in item 1 and 2 until 7 May 2020  to all vehicles (noting the exception of Letitia Road as in 1 above).

4.      The General Manager brings forward a report to the Council Meeting on 7 May 2020 to consider extensions or otherwise of the closures detailed above.

Cr Pryce Allsop foreshadowed a further amendment.

The Amendment 1 was Lost

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Pryce Allsop

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle from Living Waters Church at Tumbulgum.

"Dear Lord, 

We come to you with heavy hearts for all those who have suffered from the pandemic that we are currently facing.  For those who have contracted the virus and those who have been affected financially.  We thank you for all the front line workers who have put their own lives at risk to help those in need.   We also thank you for your protection in seeing very little cases in our area.

We are aware that this current situation will result in mental health challenges but we also read in your word in Phil 4:6-7

"Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God. 7 And the peace of God, which transcends all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus."

So Lord we ask that your peace will reign over the hearts and minds of the people in our Shire. We especially ask for your peace to guard the hearts and minds of our Mayor and the councillors as they make decisions today, the current situations at hand and the future of this Shire.

We ask this in Jesus name , Amen."

Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:

1.  Notes the information provided in relation to fire management on Council controlled lands.

2.  Recognises this is a very important time to advocate for all local councils to optimise their fire protection works and applies to the Joint Organisation to advocate for funds for a Regional Bushfire Officer that can coordinate and apply for relevant approvals for protection works.

3.  Collaborates with the local Aboriginal community and the Rural Fire Service, in relation to fire management of Council controlled lands.

4.  Advocates to the relevant Ministers and the Local Government Association for a State-funded appropriate budget and approvals process to carry out fire management on public lands.

5.   Considers communicating and sharing best practice as advised by the authorities in relation to fire management.

The Motion was Carried

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Items 9.2 and 9.3, being Late Mayoral Minutes, be dealt with and are ruled by the Chairperson to be of great urgency.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:


1. Notes that:

a. In light of the current and anticipated impacts of COVID-19 across every sector of society, it is clear that decisive action and unprecedented investment is needed to temper the worst social and economic impacts of this crisis. 

b. Over 70 farming and conservation groups around Australia, including Landcare, the National Farmers Federation, NRM Regions Australia, the Australian Land Conservation Alliance and the Australian Association of Bush Regenerators, have come together to call on state and federal government to invest in a jobs-rich conservation and land management stimulus package as part of the economic response to Covid-19.

c. Such a program presents important opportunities for safe, meaningful and socially beneficial work as part of the ‘bridge to recovery’, while leaving enduring benefits for the environment, tourism and farm businesses.

d. Local Governments play a pivotal role in delivering conservation and land management work, such as controlling weeds, protecting and restoring habitat, and managing public land and are ideally placed to manage a surge in effort for on ground conservation work.

2. Expresses its support for state and federal government investment in a jobs-rich conservation and land management stimulus package as part of the economic response to Covid-19.

3. Writes to our local Federal and State Members of Parliament expressing our support for this proposal and urging them to support it.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd.

"Gracious God,

As Reconciliation Week comes to an end, we thank you for the many and vital ways people of the Bundjalung nation and other Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples strengthen and enrich our community.

May our region be a model for our nation of true reconciliation, expressing the dignity, care for the vulnerable, and love for justice that is appropriate for people created equal in your image.

We pray for Council’s ongoing partnership with the Aboriginal Advisory Committee, and its commitment to the Reconciliation Action Plan, that these may further strengthen our community.

Since your Word call us to act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with you, grant us grace to speak respectfully and listen humbly to one another.

Bless the work of Council today and into the future.  May Councillors and Council staff be encouraged as they remember the reasons why they have dedicated themselves to public service.  Give them joy in their work, unity in the things that really matter, and courage to boldly address the needs of our community, especially those of our most vulnerable.

We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen. "

Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)

proposed that:

A.  Development Application DA19/0802 for the demolition of existing dwelling and construction of a caravan park in 4 stages including a bore for water – Stage 1 for 8 short term sites, 62 long term sites, community centre, swimming pool, amenities, men’s shed, managers dwelling, on-site detention pond and effluent treatment system; Stage 2 for 40 long term sites; Stage 3 for 41 long term sites and Stage 4 for 21 long term sites at Lot 2 DP 803636 No. 355 Tomewin Road, Dungay be refused for the following reasons:

1. The development is likely to have adverse impact on the existing built environment as a result of the proposed density of development occurring on the land in an area which comprises of vast rural landscapes and a character which is inconsistent with the proposed development as well as the impact on existing residences as a result of the increase in population;

2. The development is likely to have adverse impact on the existing community as a result of a sudden increase in population in an area which is otherwise vastly populated and the demand the development will put on local infrastructure and services;

3. The development is likely to have adverse impact on existing agricultural land uses due to the potential conflicts between the proposed residential development occurring in a rural zone which forms part of an area which is considered to be Farmland of Regional Significance;

4. An isolated rural lot with little access to public transport and services, forms a flood island during storm events and cannot be accessed by car or foot in emergencies, containing 164 long term sites (manufactured homes), 8 short term caravan sites with a potential population of 344 – 516 people is not a suitable location for the development. The proposal is not in accordance with the principles of Tweed DCP Section A3, the Tweed Local Environment Plan and the NSW Floodplain Development Manual;

5. The development is not considered to adequately satisfy the provisions of The Tweed LEP 2014 including the objectives of the plan, the zone objectives, and Part 7 Additional Local Provisions);

6. Council is not satisfied (as per section 7.10 of the Tweed LEP 2014) that suitable essential services (the supply of water, the disposal and management of sewage and stormwater drainage) are available to the proposed development;

7. The proposed development does not satisfy the provisions of SEPP 21 Caravan Parks

(i) The application fails to satisfy the aims and objectives outlined in Clause 3 of SEPP 21 – Caravan Parks.

(ii) The application fails to satisfy the matters to be considered by Council outlined in Clause 10 of SEPP 21 – Caravan Parks.

8. The development does not comply with Tweed DCP A19 Biodiversity and Habitat Management and has not satisfied requirements under the Biodiversity Conservation  Act to determine whether a Biodiversity Assessment Report is required or not. This may have implications on bushfire management measures which need to be considered by a Bushfire Planning & Design Practitioner;

9. The application has failed to adequately satisfy the Tweed DCP Section A13 – Socio Economic Impact Assessment;

10. Consideration of the submissions made in accordance with the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act from both public authorities and local residents indicate that the proposed development is not worthy of support; and

11. The proposed development was exhibited for a period of 30 days in which members of the public raised several concerns over the development proposal and the social, environmental, economic and built environmental impacts. Based on the other listed reasons for refusal and having regard to the extent of concern raised by the public, it is considered that the proposed development is not in the public interest.

B.  ATTACHMENT 2 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(g)     advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr Pryce Allsop

RECOMMENDED that:

A.  Development Application DA19/0802 for the demolition of existing dwelling and construction of a caravan park in 4 stages including a bore for water – Stage 1 for 8 short term sites, 62 long term sites, community centre, swimming pool, amenities, men’s shed, managers dwelling, on-site detention pond and effluent treatment system; Stage 2 for 40 long term sites; Stage 3 for 41 long term sites and Stage 4 for 21 long term sites at Lot 2 DP 803636 No. 355 Tomewin Road, Dungay be deferred to:

1.  Enable staff to draft a technical further information request in the areas identified in the report for the applicant to respond;

2.  Enable the applicant 3 months to respond to the further information request;

3.  Enable staff to report the matter back to Council with an assessment of the further information request; 

4.  To arrange a site visit with the proponent;

5.  To arrange a meeting with objectors; and

6.  Following the site visit, schedule a workshop to discuss potential conditions.

B.  ATTACHMENT 2 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(g)     advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege

Amendment 1 was Carried.

VOTE FOR -Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle from the Living Waters Church at Tumbulgum.

"Dear Lord, 

As our Mayor and Councillors are here to preside over matters of the Shire, we bring before you, those who have suffered from this pandemic. Businesses and individuals that been affected financially. Also those who have been affected in their health and mental wellbeing. 

We also pray for the protection of our police force at this time and we prayer for those who have been wrongly treated. 

We ask that your peace will reign over the hearts & minds of the people in our Shire. We especially ask for your peace to guard the hearts and minds of our Mayor and the counsellors as they make decisions today, over the current situations at hand and the future of this Shire.

We ask this in Jesus name 

Amen."

Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

A.  Development Application DA19/0888 for alterations and additions to an existing water bottling facility at Lot 0 ROAD 820; Bryens Road Nobbys Creek; Lot 1 DP 799355 & Lot 121 DP 1111869 & Lot 66 DP 755715; No. 101 Bryens Road Nobbys Creek; Lot 1 DP 1241753; No. 24 Bryens Road Nobbys Creek, be refused for the following reasons:

1.    Pursuant to the NSW EP&A Act s4.15 a) i) the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 1.2 Aims of the Plan section a), b), c), d), e), f), g), and i) in that it has not been adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling is a sustainable use of this resource, or that it will not have an adverse impact on natural water systems or the potential agricultural use of the land, the environment, or other groundwater or surface users.

2.    Pursuant to the NSW EP&A Act s4.15 a) i) the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 2.3 RU2 Zone Objectives in that it has not been adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling is a sustainable use of this resource, or that it will not have an adverse impact on the environment, agricultural uses, or other groundwater or surface users, or that it maintains the rural landscape character of the land.

3.    Pursuant to the NSW EP&A Act s4.15 a) i) the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 7.15 Water Bottling Facility in that it has not been adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling will not have an adverse impact on natural water systems or the potential agricultural use of the land in regard to the sustainable use of this resource.

4.    Pursuant to the NSW EP&A Act s4.15 a) i) the application has not satisfied SEPP (Primary Production and Rural Development) 2019 in regard to the Aims of the Policy in that it has not been adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling is a sustainable use of this resource, or that it will not impact on the environment, agricultural uses, or other groundwater or surface users.

5.    Pursuant to the NSW EP&A Act s4.15 a) i) the application has not satisfied NSW EP&A Act in regard to the Objects of the Act parts a), b), c), or e) in that it has not been adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling is a sustainable use of this resource, or that it will not impact on the environment, agricultural uses, or other groundwater or surface users.

6.    Pursuant to the NSW EP&A Act s4.15 b) the application has not adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling will not impact on the environment, agricultural uses, or other groundwater or surface users, and that the rural character and amenity of the area will not be adversely affected.

7.    Pursuant to the NSW EP&A Act s4.15 c) Suitability of the Site - the application has not adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling is a sustainable use of this resource, or that it will not impact on the environment, agricultural uses, or other groundwater or surface users, and that the rural character and amenity of the area will not be adversely affected or that the rural road is suitable for the use.

8.   Pursuant to the NSW EP&A Act s4.15 d) there have been numerous submissions made in regard to the application that the application has not adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling is a sustainable use of this resource, or that it will not impact on the environment, agricultural uses, or other groundwater or surface users, and that the rural character and amenity of the area will not be adversely affected or that the rural road is suitable for the use.

9.   Pursuant to the NSW EP&A Act s4.15 e) in terms of public interest, the application has not adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling is a sustainable use of this resource, or that it will not impact on the environment, agricultural uses, or other groundwater or surface users, and that the rural character and amenity of the area will not be adversely affected or that the rural road is suitable for the use.

10.   Pursuant to the NSW EP&A Act s4.15 e) in terms of public interest, the application has not obtained appropriate owners consent for the use of the unlawful structures within the road reserve.  

11.   Pursuant to the NSW EP&A Act s4.15 e) the application will not result in any public benefit or additional employment and so is not in the public interest to provide use of public road reserve. 


B.  ATTACHMENT 3 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

RESOLVED that:


1. The existing Renewable Energy Action Plan (REAP) targets be updated to reflect the broader intent of carbon reduction and replace the target measure with tonnes CO2-e as:

-   25% less electricity related carbon emissions (as tonnes CO2-e) than 2016/17 by 2022
-   50% less electricity related carbon emissions (as tonnes CO2-e) than 2016/17 by 2025

2. A new REAP Phase 2 program of works be prepared and presented to Council for adoption by October 2020. 

3. Large-scale Generation Certificates (LGCs), GreenPower or Carbon Credits be procured annually, commencing in 2022, to meet the revised Renewable Energy Action Plan (REAP) carbon reduction targets and the renewable energy aspirations of this plan.

4.     Council continues to pursue battery storage in phase 2 of the Renewable Energy Action Plan and trials a small pilot project to test the cost benefits of this technology.

5.     Council investigates additional alternative forms of renewal energy technologies such as hydrogen, smart energy and anaerobic digesters. 

6. ATTACHMENT 1 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:-

(d)  commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
       (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
      (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or
     (iii) reveal a trade secret.

Cr James Owen
Cr Pryce Allsop

RESOLVED that:


1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 14 May 2020 be received and notes: and

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendation be adopted as follows:

A1   Kingscliff Triathlon 30 August 2020

That the road closures for the conduct of the proposed Kingscliff Triathlon on 30 August 2020 be approved, subject to:

1.   NSW Police approval being obtained.
2.   Endorsement of the event by Bicycle NSW.
3.   Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans implemented and controlled by Roads & Maritime Services accredited persons.
4.   Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
5.   The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
6.   Consultation with bus and taxi operators and arrangements made for provision of services during conduct of the event.
7.   Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.
8.   All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
9. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
10. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.

A2   Frances Street, Tweed Heads

That the installation of a “Loading Zone (7am to 9am) and (4pm to 7pm)” on Frances Street, Tweed Heads, adjacent to the driveway of the proposed development, is approved to be installed when the development at 79-81 Wharf Street is completed.

A3   Blundell Boulevard, Minjungbal Drive, Tweed Heads South  

That, in consultation with the Tweed City Shopping Centre:

1.   The pavement arrows on Blundell Boulevard, Tweed Heads South, exiting the Tweed City Shopping Centre be modified to prohibit through movements from the right lane.  
2.   The solid dividing lane line exiting the Shopping Centre be modified to an (L1) broken lane line.
3.   A “Right Lane must turn Right” R2-9 R(A) sign be installed on the approach to the intersection within the Shopping Centre.


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None
