Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)

RECOMMENDED that Council, in respect land described as Lot 3 DP 1191598 No. 67 Howards Road, Burringbar:


A.      Receives and notes this report on actions taken on noise impacts from the operation of Pocket Herbs and Produce Pty Ltd.

B.      Issues the original Prevention Notice to Pocket Herb and Produce Pty Ltd, pursuant to s96 of the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997 which states:

1.      Carry on the activity of using the "Misters" on the land in a manner that ensures that the noise emanating from the "Misters" does not exceed 40dB(A) LAeq 15 minutes at the boundary with any other adjoining property (including properties that might be separated by a road) between the hours of 7am and 6pm.

2.      To engage a suitably qualified acoustic specialist to monitor and record noise emanating from the "Misters" at the boundaries of the adjoining properties (including properties that might be separated by a road) between the hours of 7am and 6pm seven days a week. Pocket Herbs and Produce Pty Ltd is to provide to Council a monthly report provided on the last day of each month for three consecutive months. The report by the acoustic specialist is to detail the results of the monitoring and confirm any instances where the noise exceeds the limits that is specified in Point 1 above. The monitoring and compliance report is to commence from the date that the monitoring and recording commences.

C.        Obtains a professional acoustic report from JTA Consultants on two X 2 weeks of data from 5-19 March 2020 and 24 September to 7 October 2019 . The consultant is to undertake a site visit of the subject "Pocket Herbs" property and, 74 and 75 Howards Road to assist determination of mitigation measures being requested below:

Report is required to include:

  • Identification of number of times and period of time noise operations from the business exceed the Project Intrusiveness criteria at the boundary of the two nearest residences.
  • Identification of number of times and period of time noise operations from the business exceed the Project Amenity level criteria at the boundary of the two nearest residences.
  • Identification of recommended mitigation for all noise exceeding the Project intrusiveness criteria at the boundary of the two nearest residences.
  • Identification of recommended mitigation for all noise exceeding the Project Amenity criteria at the boundary of the two nearest residences.
  • Identification of the likelihood of any of the individual or cumulative noise emanating from the operation of the business meeting the offensive noise criteria under the POEO Act 1997.
  • Include as an attachment graphs of the data analysed with indication of periods where machinery noise emanating from the business has been identified.

The intention of the report it to see what operational noises are breaching the noise intrusiveness criteria at the property boundary as required by Condition 45 of DA13/0712 and have recommendations for reasonable and feasible mitigation of these noises as required under the Industrial Noise Policy. Council would also like to identify whether further POEO Act offences are likely to be occurring.

D.      Issues a letter to the business reminding them of Condition 49 of DA13/0712 which requires that all engines for vehicles remaining on site for periods in excess of two minutes are required to switch off their engines.

E.      Gives consideration to installing noise logging equipment and analysing data on an "as needs" basis into the future until the problem is resolved.


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)
Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:

1.        Submits by 5 July 2020 the submission amended with the recommendations below replacing those in the draft submission, provided to this Council meeting of 2 July 2020,  to the NSW Natural Resources Commission to consider as part of its review of the Water Sharing Plan for the Tweed River Area Unregulated and Alluvial Water Sources:

2.         Finalises the draft submission reflecting Council’s position and submit the submission by 5 July 2020.

3.         Implements cease to pump rules for commercial water bottling extraction during low flow conditions due to connectivity between the alluvial aquifers and the fractured rock aquifers.

4.         Recommends that the method used for the management of the water resource in the formation of the Water Sharing Plan recognise and be reflective of the greater propensity for low and extreme low flows due to climate change instead of long term averages.

5.         Recommends that the local water utility be provided access to at least 60ML/a under any revised or new Water Sharing Plan, dependant on studies that demonstrate an appropriate volume of water is available to maintain the ecosystem in a healthy, functioning state.

6.         Environmental flows from Clarrie Hall Dam should be reviewed to ensure best practice management of town water extraction during low flow conditions and sufficient water is available to ensure important fish refuges are maintained and are reflective of this Shire’s internationally significant environment.

7.         Environmental flows at Bray Park Weir should be reviewed to ensure best practice management of town water extraction during low flow conditions and sufficient water is available to ensure important fish passage is maintained and reflective of this Shire’s internationally significant environment.

8.         Supports the implementation of the recommendations of the NSW Natural Resources Commission's Audit report October 2019 on the Tweed River Area Unregulated and Alluvial Water Sources 2010.

9.         Prioritises options for alternative water reuse schemes and best practise regenerative landscape management to provide for population growth and more reliable and diverse water security that ensures protection of Tweed's internationally significant environment and waterways.

10.       Inserts the following preamble:

"Environmental studies, community consultation and economic analysis has consistently shown Clarrie Hall Dam has less environmental impact than Byrrill Creek Dam, is more readily accepted by the community and provides the best economic outcomes for Tweed Shire. Please find attached a table displaying the outcomes of Tweed Shire Water Supply Augmentation Options Report which identify the issues with Byrrill Creek Dam and its likely negative impacts on development in the Tweed."   

11.       Strongly supports the retention of Clause 48(1) which currently prohibits the building of a dam on Byrrill Creek.

Cr Reece Byrnes returned to the meeting.

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr Pryce Allsop

RESOLVED that Council:

1. Notes that a Part 5 Assessment and Review of Environmental Factors (under the Environmental Impact and Assessment Act 1979) for works proposed on Council Land on the Terranora Creek foreshore found that the current design is inconsistent with Council and State Government policy and would be likely to result in a significant transformation of a sensitive locality and negatively impact upon the subject foreshore’s environment, visual amenity and value.

2. Notes that in order for the proposal to progress further, current plans would need to be modified, or subjected to a higher level of assessment through an Environmental Impact and Assessment Act 1979 Part 4, Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA).

3. Requests the NSW Department of Planning Industry and Environment to provide Secretary’s Environmental Assessment Requirements (SEARs) to undertake an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) of works currently proposed by residents for the Terranora Creek foreshore reserve adjacent to Wyuna Road.

4. Seeks quotes from suitably qualified consultants to prepare the Environmental Impact Assessment in accordance with the SEARs.

5. Provides information on the cost of preparing the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) to all the residents of Wyuna Road backing onto the foreshore reserve, and include advice that it is considered highly unlikely for the works to be approved in the current form, if assessed through the EP&A Act Part 4 EIA process.

6. Seeks confirmation from the residents on whether they would commit to funding the preparation of an Environmental Impact Assessment, with all monies to be paid to Council prior to acceptance of a quote and any work commencing.

 

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)
Cr Ron Cooper

PROPOSED that Council:

1.   Advises residents that, due to the findings of the Part 5 assessment and Review of Environmental Factors that it will not support the submitted plans to construct multiple structures on Community Land in the foreshore reserve of Lot 108 DP 238224;

2.   Finalises an amended foreshore rehabilitation plan that meets legislative and policy requirements and demonstrates best practice, issues it to residents for their information, completes a Review of Environmental Factors and submits it for assessment under Part 5 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979; and

3.   Pending approval of a Council-designed foreshore management plan, identifies and commits funding to remove existing hazards and rehabilitate the foreshore.

Amendment 1 was Lost

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

 

The Alternate Motion was Carried  

VOTE FOR -Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST -Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle.

"Dear Lord,

As our Shire is facing more restrictions during COVID-19, we bring before you, those who have suffered from this pandemic. Businesses and individuals that been affected financially and face future financial hardship. Also those who have been affected in their health and mental wellbeing.

We thank you that our shire has seen minimal cases, but we pray for those in hotspots all over this nation and ask for your healing hand to prevail.

As our Mayor and Councillors preside today over matters of the Shire, we ask you to give them wisdom from above, in making decisions that affect people’s lives both now and into the future.

We ask this in Jesus name.

Amen."

ALTERNATE MOTION


Cr Katie Milne (Mayor) 
Cr Pryce Allsop

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)
Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)

RECOMMENDED that:

1. Council receives and notes the attached draft submission previously submitted.

2. Council includes the following in the final submission to be forwarded to the Department of Planning, Industry and Environment by 7 August 2020:

a.  The number of options of what is determined as 'emergency/crisis accommodation services' changes all the time especially as we currently go through this Covid crisis, and Council do not track this. In reference to domestic violence we have one refuge in Tweed Shire. We have other accommodation options that respond to DV yet these are not publicised but certainly there continues to be a need for accommodation for DV and especially as our DV rates go up through Covid. 

-The lack of access in rural and regional areas to specialist mental health including outreach services and alcohol and drug services including a detox and rehabilitation centre do not exist in Tweed.

- In 2016-17 there has been a significant increase in the primary reasons why people experience homelessness in NSW which include accommodation issues (65%); financial difficulties (53%); domestic violence and relationship issues (48%); 'other' reasoning (35%); and health reasons including mental health issues and substance abuse (27%).

- There remains difficulties along the housing continuum, up one end being the lack of available and affordable stock for ownership; to lack of available and affordable private rentals, down to associated commonwealth assistance subsidies not meeting costs of rent, to low numbers of social and affordable housing and no emergency and crisis accommodation in Tweed Shire.

b.  The addition of Cr Coopers' comments below be included in the submission:

NSW Housing Strategy Discussion Paper

Response to discussion points raised by Cr Cooper on 6 August 2020

Page

and Paragraph

Comment

Proposed Addition to Draft Submission

3 / 4

Net in migration from SE Queensland is one of the largest sources of population growth in the Shire, and generates a demand for housing, infrastructure, services and facilities.

Page 3, under the heading South East Queensland cross border integration, add a final paragraph which reads:

“While highly integrated economically and socially, South East Queensland, is one of the largest sources of population growth in the Shire, and generates a demand for housing, infrastructure, services and facilities. The Strategy should both recognise this unique locational distinction and ensure that government intervention into the housing market addresses the additional strain on local housing created by this unique cross-border association.

3/5

The banking of land and slow release of major reserves of residential zoned land is not supportive of adequate and timely supply of housing.

Page 5 under the heading Theme 1, insert an opening paragraph which reads:

“The provision of an appropriate level of supply, diversity and style of housing meeting the needs of a contemporary housing market and social needs, in appropriate locations when required is critical in addressing the need for housing in the Tweed, and address the growing inability of low and medium income earners to purchase a home.


While recognised as an approach by private landowners to their personal business practices, land banking takes land that has been identified for residential purposes, places strains on more available land parcels and leads to inefficiencies in the provision of infrastructure, services and facilities.”

5/6&7

The Discussion Paper suggests that interventions by government will be focused on growth areas; however, housing affordability and need for social housing is not confined to these areas.


Need to add a comment about the disproportionately high need for emergency housing, and affordable housing in the Tweed.

Page 5 under the heading Role of population and housing projections, add a final paragraph which reads:

“While Council is supportive of any intervention by the State Government, such intervention should take into consideration the disproportionately unaffordable nature of housing and need for emergency housing in the Tweed.”

5/8

Need to add to the Suggested response to focus on affordable housing.

Page 5 Paragraph 8, add ‘especially in areas with recognised shortage of affordable housing’, so the Proposed response now reads:

“That the paper be strengthened to demonstrate support for growth of regional towns and centres through pro-active and targeted interventions, especially in areas with recognised shortage of affordable housing’.

7/6

Amend dot point 1 by removing the word “subsidised”.

Page 7 paragraph 6, amend the first dot point by removing the word “subsidised” so that the dot point reads:

“A masterplan across the site that could have 50 dwellings within an initial stage and up to 200 dwellings in additional stages for affordable rental accommodation.”

8

General comment about the growing difficulty of low- and medium-income earners being able to afford to purchase a house.

Wording has been added to Page 5 under the heading Theme 1.


Refer to proposed addition, page 3 paragraph 5 above.

8

Planning and design play an important role in alleviating connecting communities and the mental health and wellbeing of its residents.

Page 8 under the heading Local character and design led outcomes, insert a third paragraph which reads:

“Good urban planning and design can deliver more than just efficient places to live and move around, they create opportunities for the community to be engaged, connected and through that supported. The benefits of being part of a supportive well-identified community include improvements in both physical and mental health, which in turn reduce the costs on the to address the consequences of poor health and social isolation.”


8

General comment about the role of alternative housing models and ‘intentional communities’ to support community living on shared land with shared resources.

Page 8 under the heading Local character and design led outcomes, insert a final paragraph which reads:

“Contemporary housing requirements have evolved substantially from the traditional 3-bedroom quarter acre blocks so reflective of past needs.


Alternative approaches to meeting the more diverse needs of the community should be included in the Strategy and include ‘intentional communities’ as an example of what might be possible.”


The Motion was Carried  

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd.

"Gracious God,

Thank you for today, and for the beauty of our region that refreshes our souls.

Thank you for the many people at all levels of government and in the community who work hard to keep us safe. We appreciate the opportunities we have to express community in these difficult times.

Sustain and protect those who are vulnerable. Help us to show kindness to neighbours and strangers. Give us grace to deal with the frustrations of restrictions.

We are grateful for Council, elected and staff, who work hard to provide us with a quality of life we often take for granted. Please help them as they respond to the decisions of other jurisdictions that impact our community. Give them wisdom and grace in this stressful time. Bless Council in its decision making today.

We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

1. The following tabled Petition(s) be received and noted.

• Petition containing 55 valid signatures and received on 19 August 2020 entitled "Lot 3 DP877860 farming practises impact on Kielvale residents", relating to DA20/0295 advising as follows:

"This petition of certain citizens of KIELVALE draws to the attention of the Tweed Shire council that they have been impacted on by farming practises carried out on Lot 3 DP 877860 Kielvale. 

Its quoted in DA20/0295 LUC RA page 10 Lot 3 DP 877860:

"Communications with the owner of Lot 3 DP 877860 (who is party to this application) have confirmed:" 
• "There is NO aerial spraying undertaken"
• "There is NO history of complaints by neighbouring residential uses"

Farming Practices on Lot 3 DP 877860 Kielvale have impacted on the citizens of Kielvale for many years are; 

1. Cane fire smoke
2. Chemical overspray, aerial and tractor spray
3. Dust
4. Noise from cane bin movements all through the night
5. Harvesting commencing at 4.30am"

• Petition containing 26 valid signatures (14 received were duplications) and received on 18 June 2020 entitled "Request/Support to extend Letitia Road Closure" and advising as follows:

"I would like to express my deepest gratitude to you, Mayor Milne, Councillors and the Tweed Byron Local Aboriginal Land Council (TBLALC) who voted in support of protecting Fingal Head and the surrounding Communities from the Covid-19 Pandemic.
 
The closure of Letitia Road and the Spit Road at Fingal Head, Marine Parade, Queens St, the Lighthouse Car Park, the Old Quarry Car Park, Fingal and Dreamtime Beach and all beach access points from Fingal Head to Pottsville solely to protect our communities, namely our residing aged population, our most susceptible Aboriginal Community, its Elders and those who manage daily existing health conditions was politically and socially inspiring. As you are aware the course of action to close Fingal Head, namely Letitia and The Spit Road, until the 30th June 2020, was instigated by the extremely excessive Queensland Motor Vehicle Traffic and its patrons who insisted on ignoring lifesaving daily directives from our Australian and Local Governments to remain at home at this time. The unwavering support you extended to Fingal Head and the surrounding Tweed Shire has only reaffirmed our faith in you, our elected leaders. 

The positive impact of these closures at Fingal Head has been a far greater success than anticipated. Community Safety has increased due to the extended closure of Letitia Road and has reduced the overall traffic flow into Fingal Head by approximately 85% and eventually, 98% on Letitia Road. This reduction has directly contributed to maintaining a healthy Covid-19 free community and aided our neighbourhood in areas such as: 

A marked decline of constant excessively speeding vehicles throughout the day and night on Letitia Road. The volume of daily 'near miss' pedestrian accidents by vehicle traffic who refuse to abide to the designated speed limit of S0klm, repeatedly choosing speeds of 80 - l00klm with no regard for public safety or those residents utilising the pedestrian nature strip, which is in close proximity to the road. 

As these 'near miss' accidents have exponentially increased in the past 10 years, residents have been forced to refrain this pedestrian right, before a significant or fatal incident occurs. School children riding their bicycles to the nearby Fingal Public School are exceedingly and repeatedly at high risk and must be escorted by parents to and from school on the pedestrian nature strip. The subsequent and welcomed closure of Letitia Road has now reduced this to a manageable level. 

The total elimination of destructive behaviour has equally been noted on Letitia and the Spit Road as our relative isolation and low density population directly contributes to the following negative conduct: 
" illegal Household and Hazardous Waste Materials Dumped, such as Asbestos and Toxic Chemicals
* illegal Camping and Campervans of unknown or questionable occupants, their camp and beach fires an extreme hazard to residents living in this bushland environment *illegal Fishing, Netting and Crabbing of limited Fingal species *illegal Parking *illegal 4WD access to the Spit Bushland creating tracks to accommodate 'off roading' and Fingal Beach access *Illegal Jet Ski and Boat access 

The more serious criminal activity eliminated: 
* Vehicle and Residential Break-ins
* Vehicle Theft
* Dumping and Burning of Stolen Vehicles in Dense Bushland *Serious Vehicle Accidents contributed to Excessive Speeding and Drink Drivers *Dangerous Driving, Drag Racing, Burn Outs, Road Rage, Vehicles Ramming each other, Domestic Arguments from one Vehicle to another
* Domestic Street Arguments and those Drug Induced *Local and Interstate Drug and Alcoholic Homeless Campers *Drug and 'Ice Addict' Camp Sites setting up 'Dealing stations' and having in their possession extensive knife collections *Drug and Ice Addict Vehicle and Residential Break-ins, especially into Bedrooms occupied by children *Professional Tradesmen travelling daily during and after business hours to induce or smoke Drugs and excessively speeding to and from the Spit along Letitia Road *Multiple Discarded and Used Syringes *Organised Drug induced Rave Parties and Naked Rave Parties *Assaults and Drug induced Assaults *Prowlers and Drug induced Prowlers
* Motor Vehicle occupants scouring Letitia Rd and the Spit Road for Solitary Walkers or Hikers to Assault or Sexually Assault *Paedophiles trying to abduct children *Public Masturbators on Fingal Beach, The Spit Beach Car Park, Fingal Beach Car Park and Fingal Beach Playground seeking audience from sole women, couples and children.

The extended closure of Letitia and The Spit Road has granted substantial positive developments for Fingal Head with a new and enriched environment. It has allowed the community to revitalise and prosper in so many ways, welcoming our Aged Population, Indigenous Elders, Families and Children to reconnect whilst walking, dog walking and cycling, abiding safe social distancing practices, in safety along the Letitia Road pedestrian nature strip and the greater Fingal Community Hamlet. 

In addition, an abundant return of native plant and animal species, including wallabies, echidna's, a koala and migratory birds have been repeatedly sighted in the Fingal Head area, predominantly on The Spit Peninsula, indisputably those who have struggled to cohabitate alongside the speeding vehicles and 4WD's that monopolise the road day and night dousing and coating native species with dust, noise and toxic vehicle emissions. 

Therefore, it is with great conviction and a united community agenda we support the inline request from the Tweed Byron Local Aboriginal Land Council (TBLALC) for an extension of closure on Letitia Road and The Spit Road, in accordance with the continuing Queensland Boarder closure. As Covid-19 social restrictions are progressively lifted and the greater population begin to return to the somewhat norm of social activities, especially Queensland residents, we must still ensure the health and safety of our Aged Community, Aboriginal Community and Elders, whose broader communities still remain closed and those residents with ongoing health issues at higher risk."

2.  The Petition containing 83 valid signatures and received on 16 June 2020 untitled pertaining to maintenance of Arthur and Lillian Keys Park on Piggabeen Road, Piggabeen advising as follows:

"We, the citizens of Piggabeen, petition the Tweed Shire Council to provide and install "bollards" or other mechanical methods to ensure that cars cannot continually enter and destroy the "Arthur and Lillian Keys Park", at the corner of Piggabeen Road and Omiah Way. Signs erected by the Tweed Shire Council some time ago, have done nothing to avert or prevent "HOONS" regularly using the park as a "Paddock Bashing" site. To show their contempt to the council they have even driven into the council sign itself. There are a lot more young families in our area these days and the park is a great place where the kids can run around, kick a ball, play after school or "spotlight" at dusk. When these vehicles come out here they have usually been skidding and sliding or drifting all the way along Piggabeen Rd from West Tweed, as the skid marks on the road will attest. They then simply slide their vehicle onto the park, and proceed to do doughnuts etc leaving it looking like a mud bowl. The thought of a child playing there or a kid on a pony, I feel would be the last thing the hoons would think of. Please help us to keep our children and young families safe."

Council refers this petition to the General Manager for action with consideration re:  installation of bollards.

3. ATTACHMENTS 1, 2 and 3 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.

VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)
Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that

1.      The Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards Selection Panel comprising all Councillors and the current Awardees consider Tweed Shire Australia Day Award nominations for the following categories:

  • Citizen of the Year;
  • Arts and Culture;
  • Volunteer of the Year (individual);
  • Volunteer of the Year (group);
  • Sporting Achievement (individual);
  • Sporting Achievement (group );
  • Community Event of the Year; and
  • Young Achiever in Community Service

with the option to make an ‘Honourable Mention’ to a nominee who deserves recognition for their efforts.

2.   Council supports the changes to the nomination categories and the eligibility criteria for the Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards as outlined in the report.

3.  Council continues to support, from the Australia Day budget, applications for financial assistance from non-profit organisations and community groups interested in hosting small community Australia Day events.

4.   Council supports delegation to the General Manager to determine an appropriate venue or an on-line ceremony in a COVIDSafe way.

5.  Council supports the rollover of funds from the 2019/2020 Australia Day events budget, as well as the 2019-2020 Civic Business - Civic Ceremonies budget.

6.  Council continues to explore gift ideas from local Aboriginal organisations for Award recipients.

7. Council invites the 2019 Tweed Shire Australia Day Citizen of the year, Rebecca Hogan, to be the 2020 Tweed Shire Australia Day Ambassador.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

 Cr Reece Byrnes
Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that Council:

1. Allocate sponsorship monies of $20,000 from the Tweed Holiday Parks 2020/2021 budget to local surf clubs through SLS NSW not covered by the recent State Government Shark Mitigation Program for the specific purchase of UAV’S/Drones and that appropriate sponsorship recognition be acknowledged at the receiving Clubs.

2. In recognition of the important role that local surf clubs provide to protecting visitors and locals on the Tweed Coast Reserve, and noting the impact to other potential sponsors in 2020 due to Coronavirus coupled with limited ability for normal fund raising activities a sponsorship allocation of $20,000 ($5,000 to each of the 4 clubs) from the Tweed Holiday Parks 2020/2021 budget be set aside to allow local Surf clubs to apply for the following:

• Volunteer Recruitment campaigns for all the surf clubs in the Tweed Shire Council area – 
• Additional equipment for the response to emergency incidents inclusive of inflatable rubber boats (IRBs), Jet Ski (RWC), All Terrain Vehicles (ATV) – 
• Support with required maintenance of building assets.

3. The above be put forward in the September Quarterly Budget Review.

4. Revives the Tweed Beach Safety Liaison Committee. 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

 Cr James Owen
Cr Reece Byrnes

RESOLVED that a report be prepared outlining how Council could apply for the recently announced $190 million Commonwealth Government Grant for Recycling Infrastructure to:

• Scale up Councils existing community education and behaviour change program to address contamination in domestic yellow and green bins and to reduce the amount of greenwaste and recyclables that are currently being put into red bins;

• Purchase recycling and organics waste infrastructure for use at public events to support event organisers to ensure source separation of waste streams thereby maximising recycling and reuse;

• Establish a program to assist businesses to avoid and divert business waste by segregating the waste and recoverable materials; and 

• Undertake feasibility assessments on Council using recycled materials or materials with a recycled content for construction and operational purposes. 

The Motion was Carried

ALTERNA

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)
Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council provides the completed submission form attached to this report to the NSW Department of Planning, Industry and Environment – Crown Lands with regard to the draft State Strategic Plan for Crown Land currently on exhibition with the following addition:

"1.  The Tweed Shire has only 0.99% of area remaining as Crown Lands which is significantly less than other areas around the State.

It is therefore imperative that these lands remain intact or increased for the public benefit of NSW residents and the environment.

This region is of international biodiversity significance, being the third highest biodiversity hotspot in Australia, yet with the highest number of threatened species in Australia and our koalas on the brink of extinction. 

2.  Biodiversity offsets occurring on Crown Lands are not supported as this does not support biodiversity increases and as Crown Lands should be restored and maintained appropriately as a responsibility of the State."

Cr James Owen
Cr Pryce Allsop

RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 11 June 2020 be received and noted; and

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows::

7.1  That in relation to parking issues on Sullivan Street, South Tweed Heads:

1.    Prohibitive parking signage is not supported for the following reasons:

  • There is no kerb and guttering and vehicles could park behind the signage and it would be difficult for rangers to define the nature strip area.
  • Signage would be limited to school zone times and would apply to residents as well as parents.
  • Council's parking enforcement resources may be called upon for what is primarily an amenity issue.

2.    The school should consider lodging a Section 4.55 Modification to allow the use of Sullivan Street for school pick up and drop off in consultation with residents.

7.2. Battle on the Border and Cycle for Life rides and races on Friday 25 September, Saturday 26 September, and Sunday 27 September 2020

That the proposed Battle on the Border and Cycle for Life rides and races on Friday 25 September, Saturday 26 September, and Sunday 27 September 2020 be supported subject to standard conditions of approval and current COVID19 restrictions at the time of the event:

1.      NSW Police approval being obtained.
2.      Endorsement of the event by Cycling QLD.
3.      Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
4.      Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
5.      The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any   traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
6.      Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.
7.      All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
8.      Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
9.      Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
10.    That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to  the website for approval.
11.    The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
12.    The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
13.    A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
14.    The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
15.    That the event organiser consult directly with the quarry operators and cane truck operators on Dulguigan Road and include provisions in the Traffic Management Plan to manage heavy vehicle risks on this road.
16.    That the event organiser consult with all school and public bus operators that could be affected by the traffic changes.
17.    That the event organiser consult with schools that may be affected and address issues raised.
18.    That if the contingency criterium proceeds in Murwillumbah the event must not go further than the Civic Centre and the organisers should consult directly with the managers of the hall, swimming pool and library.
19.    That Event Organisers should consult with Police in regard to the most up-to-date Covid-19 restrictions for events and public gatherings.

 7.3. Falls Festival North Byron Parklands 2020/21

That the proposed Falls Festival Byron at North Byron Parklands from 31 December 2020 to 2 January 2021 be supported, subject to the current COVID19 restrictions applying at the time of the event:

1.      NSW Police approval being obtained.
2.      Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
3.      Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
4.      The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
5.      Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.
6.      All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
7.      Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
8.      Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
9.      The applicant organise for the event to be listed on Council's Calendar of Events web page. Go to www.tweed.nsw.gov.au and select Our Community/Festivals Events and Filming/Calendar of Events and access the Calendar of Events site to upload the event details.
10.    A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, including the Traffic Evaluation Report, within 4 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
11.    The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
12.    Monitoring of vehicle volumes that arrive and depart the festival site and on the local road network.
13.    Bus bays utilised within the Tweed Shire are to be monitored and kept free from excess rubbish.
14.    That Event Organisers should consult with Police in regard to the most up-to-date Covid-19 restrictions for events and public gatherings.

 7.4. Twin Towns Triathlon Club 2020/21 Season

That the proposed Twin Towns Triathlon Club 2020 to 2021 Season be supported subject to the below conditions and to current COVID19 restrictions at the time of the event:

1.      NSW Police approval being obtained.
2.      Endorsement of the event by Bicycle NSW or Cycling QLD.
3.      Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
4.      Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
5.      The event organiser notifies Tweed Shire residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the first event for the season, showing the 2019/2020 calendar of events. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
6.      Consultation with bus and taxi operators and arrangements made for provision of services during conduct of the events.
7.      Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.
8.      All signage erected for the events to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
9.      Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
10.    Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
11.    That the applicant organise for the 2019/2020 season of events be listed on Council's Calendar of Events web page. Go to www.tweed.nsw.gov.au Our Community/Festivals Events and Filming/Calendar of Events and access the Calendar of Events site to upload the event details.
12.    The events be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.

RESOLVED that

1.  A consolidated set of amended plans are to be submitted for the approval of the General Manager or his delegate demonstrating the following:

  d) The proposed ground floor level and first floor level balconies of both units are to be fitted with a privacy screen for the length of the external side elevations and on the rear elevation for a length of 3m from each external side.

    i. has no individual opening more than 30mm wide, and
   ii. has a total area of all openings that is no more than 30% of the surface area of the screen or barrier, and
   iii. with a height between 1.7m and 2.2m.

Cr Katie Milne (Mayor)

RESOLVED that in light of advice that the Qld border may be closed until Christmas due to COVID -19 and the significant negative health, social and economic impacts this is currently having, that the Mayor write to the NSW Premier and the Queensland Premier to request consideration of options as outlined below:

1. Queensland considers amending the current style of restrictions to revert to the restrictions that were originally in place from March to July.

2. The current NSW & Queensland border bubble be extended to the southern border of Ballina Shire, NSW to encompass this critical economic zone.

3. The current NSW & Queensland border bubble be extended to north of Brisbane, Qld.

4. That critical workers from Qld outside the bubble areas be allowed into the NSW bubble areas, in-line with the current allowance for critical workers from NSW being allowed to service Qld.

5. That the NSW Premier imposes intrastate travel restrictions to the border bubble areas, or at least from any NSW COVID-19 hotspot clusters, to protect rural and regional areas such as the Tweed Shire, maintain the integrity of the border bubble and give confidence to Qld.

6. NSW commits resources to operate a Northern Rivers bubble checkpoint.

7. Consideration be given to providing increased specialist medical services to be provided in the area for northern NSW residents no longer able to be cared for in Qld.

8. NSW assists residents with financial support to quarantine in Queensland if required for essential medical, work or other purposes.

9. Further financial support is provided for NSW residents and businesses negatively impacted by the border closures.

10. Qld provides greater flexibility for compassionate grounds for NSW residents to be with their families in Qld.

11. Thanks the respective Premiers for their assistance so far.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne (Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle from the Living Waters Church at Tumbulgum.

1 Timothy 2:1-4 (NKJV)
Therefore I exhort first of all that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks be made for all men, 2 for kings and all who are in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and reverence. 3 For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour, 4 who desires all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.

"Dear Lord, 

Today as decisions are being made as to who will be our next Mayor & Deputy Mayor. According to your word, we pray and give thanks for those you have placed in authority to govern our shire. We thank you that the decisions they make, in godly reverence, will cause us to live in peace. 
May they be led by your Holy Spirit especially in the tough decisions and help them to find the truth of each situation so they can govern well.

We ask that your peace will reign over their personal lives and families and thank you for the personal sacrifice they have each given to represent us in Council.

The General Manager advised that the Manager Corporate Governance, Ms Stephanie Papadopoulos, has been appointed as Returning Officer for the election of the Mayor and Deputy Mayor.

The Returning Officer advised that 2 nominations have been received for Mayor:

·  Cr Warren Polglase was nominated by himself and Cr Pryce Allsop and has accepted the nomination.

·  Cr Chris Cherry  was nominated by Cr Katie Milne and Cr Reece Byrnes and has accepted the nomination.

The result of the Ordinary Ballot by way of open voting for Mayor was as follows:

·  Voting for Cr Warren Polglase

FOR VOTE - Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Warren Polglase

·  Voting for Cr Chris Cherry

FOR VOTE - Cr Chris Cherry, Cr Katie Milne, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr James Owen

The Returning Officer declared that as Cr Chris Cherry has received the majority of votes, she is elected as Mayor of Tweed Shire Council for the period ending September 2021.

 

The Returning Officer advised that 1 nomination has been received for Deputy Mayor:

·  Cr Reece Byrnes was nominated by Cr Katie Milne and Cr Chris Cherry and has accepted the nomination.

The Returning Officer declared that as Cr Reece Byrnes was the only nominee for the role of Deputy Mayor, he is elected unopposed as Deputy Mayor of Tweed Shire Council for the period ending September 2021.

Cr Katie Milne
Cr Pryce Allsop

RESOLVED that

 that:

1.      based on the above voting for the positions of Mayor and Deputy Mayor, the Returning Officer declared the following:

a)      Mayor for the period ending September 2021 - Cr Chris Cherry.

b)      Deputy Mayor for the period ending September 2021 - Cr Reece Byrnes.

2.     Arrangements be made for any committees and organisations to which the position of Mayor is a delegate/member be advised of the election outcome.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry, Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  Nil.

The Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle from the Living Waters Church at Tumbulgum.

1 Timothy 2:1-4 (NKJV)
Therefore I exhort first of all that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks be made for all men, 2 for kings and all who are in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and reverence. 3 For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour, 4 who desires all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.

"Dear Lord, 

Today as decisions are being made as to who will be our next Mayor & Deputy Mayor. According to your word, we pray and give thanks for those you have placed in authority to govern our shire. We thank you that the decisions they make, in godly reverence, will cause us to live in peace. 
May they be led by your Holy Spirit especially in the tough decisions and help them to find the truth of each situation so they can govern well.

We ask that your peace will reign over their personal lives and families and thank you for the personal sacrifice they have each given to represent us in Council.

We ask this in Jesus name 

Amen."

RESOLVED that Council submits the following motions for consideration at the Local Government NSW 2020 Annual Conference:

Motion: Councillors' Remuneration

"That Local Government NSW write to the Honorable Shelley Hanock MP, Minister for Local Government to request that NSW Local Government Councillors being fairly remunerated based on the fiscal, legal and community responsibilities of their roles and the time required for representation of the relevant population base."

Background
The role of a Councillor can necessitate a significant demand on time, requiring skills in such diverse areas as strategic thinking, financial management, local government legislation, community engagement, communications, conflict resolution and resilience.

Whilst the demands can be different based on Council area, population, demographics, development demands, diversity, business activity and economic/environmental significance, NSW Local Government would be better served by Councillors who can commit the time and skills needed to adequately perform the role without having to seek alternative employment.

The 'A NEW RISK MANAGEMENT AND INTERNAL AUDIT FRAMEWORK' for local councils in NSW Discussion paper released September 2019 suggests that the fees paid to the Chair and members of Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee are to be the same as those currently paid under the NSW Government’s pre-qualification scheme. This, in many cases, would see the Chair of Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee’s receive a higher fee than the minimum Councillor fee as outlined in the Local Government Remuneration Tribunal – Annual Report and Determination – 10 June 2020.

Motion: Economic Stimulus for Regenerative Landscape Management

"The Local Government NSW lobbies the Federal and NSW Governments to request a specific and significant funding stream be made available for Regenerative Landscape Management as an economic stimulus to be administered at Local Government level."

Background
Regenerative Landscape Management has the potential to create thousands of jobs, mitigate the impact of natural disasters, enhance town water supply, assist farmers, capture carbon, and transform Australia’s degraded landscapes.

Australia is in dire need of transformational change to address these issues.  Landholders are keen to make changes but they need significant financial and technical support to implement these practices. 

This COVID crisis is an opportune time to kick start Australia on a path to building back better, reconnecting our communities to the land and keeping our communities safe.  

Young people are keen to assist with this change but at the moment there are few job opportunities or career prospects in this area.   Until research and investment in this space is activated these opportunities will not be realised.  The Australian landscape is important for our national psyche and sense of well being.  Regenerative Landscape Management is a way to reinvigorate that pride and be a transformative change that will secure Australia’s future into the 21st Century.


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

ITEM NOT ON THE AGENDA - RATES INCENTIVE PRIZES 2020/2021

The Mayor advised the meeting of the following:

The Rates Incentive Scheme is a small but integral component of Council's overall rate recovery policy, approximately 7799 ratepayers paid their rates in full for 20120/21 Rating year. 42000 Ratepayers in Total).

The eNotice Competition received a total subscriptions 7163 and increase of 2000 new subscriptions, Receipt of these eNotices represent an 87.5% savings as opposed to the traditional print, envelope and posting of a paper notice as well as instant delivery for the Ratepayer.

The early payment of rates in full provides Council with an increase in its cash flow, enabling Council to create additional revenue from investments; this additional Revenue is used to provide increased funding for services.

First prize for the 2020/2021 rates Incentive scheme is a $3000 cash prize.

First prize for 2020/2021 eNotice Competition is a $1000 cash prize.

A Draw resulted in the Mayor announcing the following winners:

First prize for the 2020/2021 Rates Incentive scheme is a $3000 Cash prize - Ms Tanja L Pommersheim.

First prize for the 2020/2021 eNotice Competition is a $1000 cash prize - Mr Michael & Mrs Francine Potts

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor) congratulated the winners.

Cr James Owen
Cr Pryce Allsop

RESOLVED that:

1.  The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee meeting held 13 August 2020 be received and noted.

2.  The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

7.1    2021 Gold Coast Open Surfing Event 

That the proposed contingency Traffic Management Plan for holding the Corona Gold Coast Open Surfing Event at Duranbah between 17 March and 28 March 2021 be supported, subject to standard conditions of approval and current COVID19 restrictions at the time of the event:

1.  NSW Police approval being obtained.
2.  Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by TfNSW accredited persons.
3.  Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.
4.  All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
5.  Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
6.  That the applicant organise for the event to be listed on Council's Calendar of Events web page. Go to www.tweed.nsw.gov.au and select Our Community/Festivals Events and Filming/Calendar of Events and access the Calendar of Events site to upload the event details.
7.  The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
8.  The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
7.2    Kingscliff Triathlon - Sunday 29 November 2020 and Sunday 28 March 2021

That the proposed Kingscliff Triathlons on Sunday 29 November 2020 and Sunday 28 March 2021 be supported, subject to standard conditions of approval and current COVID19 restrictions at the time of the event:

1.      NSW Police approval being obtained.
2.      Endorsement of the event by the Kingscliff Business Chamber and Bicycle NSW.
3.      Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
4.      Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
5.      The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
6.      Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.
7.      All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
8.      Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
9.      Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
10.    That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
11.    The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
12.    The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
13.    A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
14.    The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
15.  A Road Occupancy Licence (ROL) may be required from Transport NSW for any proposed detours or access to the motorway. 
7.4    Bay Street, Tweed Heads - modify length limitation

The current signage " No Parking vehicles under 10m Excepted", located on Bay Street, Tweed Heads in the area east of Endeavour Parade, be modified to "No Parking vehicles under 7.5m Excepted".

8.1    Stokers Road, Stokers Siding

That:

1.  Council's Courtesy speed board be placed in Stokers Road to encourage safer speeds.
2.  NSW Police be requested to conduct speed patrols in Stokers Road during school zone times.
3.  '50 Ahead' and repeater speed signs be installed along this section of Stokers Road.

The Motion was Carried  

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

RESOLVED that Council: 

1. Rescinds part 2 of its resolution of 21 May 2020: 

"2. During COVID-19 at 3.00 pm with the first community access booking starting 20 mins before the formal meeting and further bookings working back in 10 minute increments."

2. Implements a hybrid model of audio visual and physical meetings.

3. Continues to exclude physical attendance of the public gallery and continues livestreaming.  In the case of Public Forum, where a member of the public is unable to attend via audio-visual means, the option be given to attend in person for Public Forum only.

4. Implements a hybrid model where the physical aspect of meetings be held at the Tweed Heads Administration Office. 

5. The start time for Council and Planning Committee meetings to be 5.30pm following Public Forum commencing from 4.30pm for the remainder of the Council term. 

6.  In the case of Public Forum, the first community access booking starting 20 mins before the formal meeting and further bookings working back in 10 minute increments.

7.  Requests that a report be brought forward on options to livestream the Public Forum.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by the Reverend Michael Boyd from the Presbyterian Church, Tweed Heads.


"Gracious God, 

Thank you for the many people who serve our community in both paid and voluntary work.  Thank you for the ways Council facilitates the care of our environment, wildlife, agriculture, our health and fitness, infrastructure, and community engagement and care.

Help them as they consider a diversity of needs and provide leadership in facilitating and delivering the services that enhance our life in this beautiful region.

Grant Council, both elected and staff, satisfaction and joy as they conduct this vital work on our behalf.

We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

RESOLVED that:


1 The following tabled Petition(s) be received and noted.

• Petition containing 51 valid signatories and received on 16 September 2020 entitled "DA20/0492 - New Generation Boarding House (NGBH) on land at 30 Philp Parade, Tweed Heads South (Lot 9 on DP1080483) " advising as follows:

"We, the undersigned local landowners, present the following submission detailing our objection to DA20/0492 for a six-room boarding house at 30 Philp Parade, Tweed Heads South. We note the application involves: 

• Six rooms
• Reference to a maximum of 12 lodgers
• Reference to preferred tenants including key workers (teachers, plumbers, nurses, retail staff, etc) and over 55-year-old females
• Six car spaces within the front setback

The application cites how the proposal is compliant with various Council policies, however, it does not at any stage identify any merit to the proposal, its position within the locality, nor how the proposal integrates with its surroundings. Ultimately, the proposal seeks to significantly increase the number of residents on the site which is: 

a. Identified for low density residential development
b. Flood prone, including high flow flooding, and without an evacuation route
c. Underneath an ever increasing, noisy flight path
d. Not within walking distance of shops or employment
e. Serviced by a single public transport route (Route 604)

Being a low-density area, residential density is confined to 1 dwelling per 450m2 of site area through the Tweed LEP 2014, unless within 300m of a business zone, which the proposal is not. As such, typically, the development potential of the site is limited to 2 dwellings, which would generally accommodate a total of 5 people according to Council's household size information at the 2016 census. The proposed density more than doubles the occupancy rate of the site, which will inevitably impact on the low-density character of the area and generate additional traffic and noise. 

The proposal is also not reflective of the character of the area. Specifically, carparking in the local area is either integrated into the building design or detached and towards the rear of the lot. Housing in the area is typically is generally forward of the car parking and includes decks and living spaces that overlook the Tweed River/Terranora Inlet. The proposed carparking is forward of the building and will provide a negative impact of the character of the streetscape and present as a commercial-style development within a low-density residential area. The application does not appear to consider any of these character-defining components of the locality, or its location immediately adjoining the Tweed River/Terranora Inlet, nor does it make an effort to integrate into the character. 

Whilst the application claims not to increase the number of dwellings under the flight path and affected by aircraft noise, as detailed above, this statement appears ignorant to the increased occupancy the development will contain. Likewise, the Flood Response Assessment Plan provided does not satisfy the minimum requirements of 'Note 5' of the Flooding Controls, despite Council's advices at the pre-lodgement meeting. The Flood Response Plan does not detail the typical demographics of occupants, likewise the application mnakes only general statements about key workers without any legitimate analysis or cross reference to local industries. Our understanding of Council's flood planning policy is not to increase the number of people within the floodplain without an emergency evacuation opportunity, and a similar risk mitigation response is in place for aircraft noise. The application is contrary to these positions and does not address these policy outcomes. 

As community members, we can see there may be a need to provide this type of living within the Shire, however they should occur within appropriate areas of the Tweed, such as within walking distance to: 

• Shops and employment
• Frequent public transport
• Areas not affected by significant flooding and aircraft noise

Further, we believe this type of development should be led by socio-economic and crime prevention studies, as opposed to ambiguous and generalised profiling as per the proposal. The river foreshore and Philp Parade is a highly used and trafficked pedestrian and recreational route, used by local residents including exercisers, families, young children, and elderly. We fear this could be compromised. 

We encourage Council to refuse this application on these grounds and ensure a policy is developed to limit future applications to well-serviced areas without land constraint that do not disrupt the existing low-density character and amenity. It is not considered appropriate to allow this development to impact the established character of Philp Parade, nor do we think it is 'good planning' to house vulnerable or low socioeconomic people away from key services."

2. ATTACHMENT 1 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

RESOLVED that:


1.     The Renewable Energy Action Plan - Phase 2 program of works as detailed in this report including behind the meter Solar PV projects at selected Council sites proceed to detailed business case development and presented to Council for adoption.

2.     Council provides a further report on the potential to utilise Council owned land at Byrrill Creek for a large scale renewable energy project.

3.     A further report be provided in regards to maximising all potential capacity to generate cost effective renewable energy, even if the paybacks are over longer periods of time, to assist in stimulating a COVID economic recovery and reducing Council's energy costs, as well as addressing the climate emergency.

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr Pryce Allsop

PROPOSED that the following amendments be made to the Rural Land Strategy:

1. The existing minimum lot size on RU1 land not to be amended or altered (delete action theme 10).

2. Agreed independent panel to review the relevance of the 40 hectare minimum lot size in Tweed Shire.

3. A plan to identify rural areas that are not suitable for agriculture and implement zoning to allow lifestyle owners to purchase and maintain smaller rural parcels within RU1 and RU2 zones.

4. Remove restrictions on Rural Land Strategy which prevent building on sloping land that is in excess of 12 degrees.

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that this item be deferred for consideration at a Councillor Workshop and a representative from the Department of Planning, Industry and Environment be invited to attend to help understand the constraints that exist from a State level to the proposed changes.

Cr Katie Milne
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that:


1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 10 September 2020 be received and noted; and

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1   Tweed Valley Triathletes Event Season 2020/21, Murwillumbah

That the proposed Tweed Valley Triathletes 2020-2021 Season  be supported, subject to standard conditions of approval and current COVID-19 restrictions at the time of the event:

1.      NSW Police approval being obtained.

2.      Endorsement of the event by Triathlon NSW.

3.      Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.

4.      Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.

5.      The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.

6.      Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.

7.      All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.

8.      Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.

9.      Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.

10.    That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.

11.    The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.

12.    The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.

13.    A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.

14.    The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

6.2  Parklets - Murwillumbah

That:

1. The installation of the Parklets in Brisbane Street and Queen Street, Murwillumbah, subject to consultation with adjacent businesses, is supported. 

2. That the temporary extension of the Loading Zone in Queen Street, Murwillumbah, 6m to the north to replace the 2P parking space, is supported.

3.    Officers undertake consultation with the business community with a view to posting specific time limits on the "No Loading" zones in Queen Street and that a report on this matter be brought forward to the Local Traffic Committee noting that this action will not impede the implementation of the Parklet project.

7.1   First Avenue, Tweed Heads

That 'No Parking 6am to 12 midday, Tuesdays only' signage during garbage service times be approved on First Avenue, Tweed Heads in association with DA19/0101.

7.2   Kennedy Drive/Norman Street Intersection Upgrade

That Officers continue to progress Preferred Option 5 for the intersection upgrade of Kennedy Drive and Norman Street, Tweed Heads in consideration of the recommendations by Council's consultants, with community consultation. 


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Council’s General Manager is employed under a Contract of Employment, which is in the standard format required by the Office of Local Government.
 
A requirement of that contract is for annual reviews to be undertaken of the General Manager's performance. Council appointed a Performance Review Panel to undertake these reviews – I am on that Panel, together with all Councillors.
 
We undertook a detailed review of the General Managers performance for the 2019/20 financial year, based on his Performance Agreement with Council. That review was held on Wednesday 26 August 2020.
 
In accordance with Guidelines issued by the Department of Premier and Cabinet, the details of this review are to be reported to Council in Closed session, and all associated documents are to remain confidential.
 
The overall outcome of the review was that the Panel agreed that the General Manager performed above Councils expectations during a difficult year.
 
Follow up areas requiring the General Manager's attention were identified and conveyed to him as part of this process. The Performance Review Panel has also prepared the General Managers Performance Agreement for 2020/21. 
 
On behalf of all Councillors, I wish to thank Mr Green for his efforts and support, which are very much valued by Council. It is not an easy job, and we appreciate the contributions he has made to better our region and the leadership he provides in our community, our Councillors and staff.  In particular, we acknowledge his outstanding leadership and contributions, supported by his Directors, Managers and staff, during these unprecedented COVID times.

REASON FOR CONFIDENTIALITY

(a)     personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors)

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that :

1. The report from the Performance Review Panel, which comprises the Mayor and all Councillors, on the outcomes of the annual review of the General Manager’s 2019/2020 performance against his Performance Agreement be received and noted.

2. The General Manager's 2020/2021 Performance Agreement be endorsed.

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr James Owen
Cr Pryce Allsop

RECOMMENDED that:

1. Council issue the operators of the Red Earth Brewery, Lot 2 DP 881996 No. 592 Cudgen Road, Cudgen, with a Statutory Notice (Order to Comply) under the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979; 

2. Should the Order not be complied with, engage Council's Solicitors to commence Class 4 Proceedings in the NSW Land and Environment Court seeking Orders to restrain the non compliance with DA17/0888.01; and

3. The General Manager or his delegate investigate any future non compliance relating to the current Red Earth Brewery operations and undertake action as necessary, including the issuing of Penalty Infringement Notices.

4. Issue a warning letter to the owners of Red Earth Brewery advising that any further breaches may result in Council pursuing further action by way of penalty infringement notices.

B. ATTACHMENT 3 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:
(e) information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Katie Milne

PROPOSED that

A. Development Application DA18/0053 for a mixed use development (restaurant, offices and dual use residential and tourist accommodation units) including works within Tweed Coast Road reserve, tree removal and extension to a right of carriageway over Lot 6 DP 872039 at Lot 6 DP 872039 Hastings Road, Bogangar; Lot 17 Section 6 DP 30043 No. 53 Tweed Coast Road, Bogangar; Road 2188; Tweed Coast Road, Bogangar be approved subject to the conditions attached to this report and amendments to Condition 26, Condition 34, Condition 94 and Condition 155 as follows:

26. The developer shall provide the following parking spaces (including parking for the disabled), in accordance with Tweed Shire Council’s Development Control Plan Part A2- Site Access and Parking Code.
       - 6 car parking spaces (including 1 car parking space for the disabled) along the development’s frontage to Tweed Coast Road;

       - 1 marked, dedicated delivery vehicle space (suitable to accommodate a standard Small Rigid Vehicle (SRV)) at the rear of the building, within the area to be dedicated as road reserve;

       - 15 basement car spaces and;

      - 7 bicycle parking spaces.

     Full design detail of the proposed parking and manoeuvring areas shall be submitted to and approved by the Principal Certifying Authority prior to the issue of a Construction Certificate for Building Works.

34. Application shall be made to Tweed Shire Council under Section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 for works pursuant to this consent located within the road reserve. Application shall include (but not limited to) engineering plans and specifications undertaken in accordance with Councils Development Design and Construction Specifications for the following required works:

  (a) Provision of 6 angled car spaces (including 1 car parking space for the disabled) along the development’s frontage to Tweed Coast Road.
- These car parks shall not impact on the existing driveway of neighbouring Lot 1 Section 6 DP 29748 and shall comply with the applicable Australian Standards (AS2890.5 - On Street Parking).
- The disabled car park shall include applicable kerb ramps.

(b) Paved footpath for the full frontage of the site’s frontage to Tweed Coast Road (excluding approved landscaping) integrated with a legible pedestrian route to the development.
- Safety balustrading shall be provide, where applicable.
The above mentioned engineering plan submission must include copies of compliance certificates relied upon and details relevant to but not limited to the following:
• Road works/furnishings
• Stormwater drainage
• Water and sewerage works
• Sediment and erosion control plans
• Location of all services/conduits
• Traffic Control Plan

(c) An amended landscape concept plan to incorporate the streetscape improvements as outlined in the `stamped approved landscape plan’ (including the provision of 1 street tree) and replacement landscape embellishment for the removed landscaping to the north of the site frontage within the Council reserve area. Landscaping shall be provided to facilitate a minimum pedestrian pathway of 1.8m wide and include vegetation to a maximum mature height of 1m (with the exception of the street tree).

94. Where access for people with disabilities is required to be provided to a building, sanitary facilities for the use of the disabled must also be provided in accordance with the provisions Part F-2 of the Building Code of Australia.

      A minimum of 20% of the residential units are to be constructed to be capable of achieving Silver Level design features under the Liveable Housing Design Guideline. 

155. Hours of operation are restricted to the following hours except where varied by Council's General Manager or delegate:
       Restaurant and Bar
       * 6am - 8pm Sunday to Wednesday inclusive and 6am to 10pm Thursday - Saturday inclusive

           Offices
       * 7.00am to 6.00pm - Monday to Sunday 


B. ATTACHMENT 8 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:
(e) information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law
