Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that the resolution made by Council on 5 March 2020 in relation 5859 Tweed Valley Way - On Site Sewage Management (Item 18.1), be amended as set out below. This is deemed to be of great urgency as the works are in progress and the amendment provides clarity as to Council’s intention.

"1. Council:

a. Requests the owners of Lot B DP 419641 to formally request connection toat their property boundary into Councils sewage system on the basis that they pay all associated costs of the connection in line with the total Burringbar Mooball Sewerage Scheme contributions as per option iii in the cost section of this report.

b. Requests the owners of Lot B DP 419641 to formally request the transfer of the water supply connection from private to public ownership on the basis that they pay the associated costs.

c. Signals to the owners of Lot 7 DP 593200 its intention to use its powers under section 59A and section 191A of the Local Government Act 1993 to extend the sewerage system and transfer of the water supply connection from private to public ownership across Lot 7 DP 593200 to service Lot B DP 419641 (Tweed Valley Way).

d. Negotiates with the owners of Lot 7 DP 593200 to extend the sewerage system and transfer of the water supply connection from private to public across their land to service Lot B DP 419641 on the basis that, notwithstanding the provisions of s59A and s191A of the Local Government Act, that Council intends to seek agreement to create a “public positive covenant” under s88 or other relevant mechanisms under s88 of the Conveyancing Act within the buffer area on Lot 7 DP 593200 (as per Schedule 1 of the Mooball Planning Agreement) to extend the sewerage system and transfer of the water supply connection from private to public ownership across Lot 7 DP 593200 to connect to Lot B DP 419641. Agreement to also include provision for Council’s right to enter the land to construct, maintain, repair and replace infrastructure, and if requested Council to consider providing a connection point to Lot 7 DP 593200 and monetary compensation in accordance with a valuation.

2. If the owners of Lot 7 DP 593200 are not willing to come to an in-principle agreement under the provisions of s88 of the Conveyancing Act to extend the sewerage system and transfer of the water supply connection from private to public ownership across their land to Lot B DP 419641 within 48 days then Council proceeds with the provision of the above under s59A and s191A of the Local Government Act and authorises the necessary expenditure.

3. If the owners of Lot 7 DP 593200 reach a negotiated agreement with the Council under the provisions of s88 of the Conveyancing Act then a report be prepared to Council recommending the adoption of the agreement under these provisions to extend the sewerage system and transfer of the water supply connection from private to public ownership to Lot B DP 419641 within the dedicated buffer area."

The Motion was Carried

Cr J Owen declared a Pecuniary/Non-Significant Interest in Item 15.1 Loan to Tweed Heads Seagulls RLFC.  The nature of the interest is that Cr J Owen is employed by Seagulls RLFC.  Cr Owen will manage the Interest by vacating the Chamber for discussion and not voting on the item. 

ALTERNATE MOTION


Cr Ron Cooper
Cr Pryce Allsop

RESOLVED that:

1.  Council increases the loan by an amount of $85,000 to a total of $285,000.

2.  Defers commencement of repayments of the loan to twelve months from the commencement of the grant.

3. Council advertises the proposed 5 year licence to Tweed Heads Seagulls RLFC Ltd. (ABN 53 106 910 203) of Council-owned community land at 15 Carramar Drive, Tweed Heads West (Lot 25 on DP1017105).

4. Should no reasonable objections be received when the proposed licence is advertised, Council approves granting the licence to Tweed Heads Seagulls RLFC Ltd. (ABN 53 106 910 203) of Council-owned community land at 15 Carramar Drive, Tweed Heads West (Lot 25 on DP1017105).

5. All necessary documentation in relation to this matter to be executed under the common seal of Council.

6. If reasonable objections are received when the proposed licence is advertised, a report will be brought back for further Council consideration.

7.  Council seek the Minister's approval is this is required for the term of the licence.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase, Cr James Owen

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins from Murwillumbah Church of Christ & NSW RFS Chaplain:

"Dear Father,

I acknowledge that You are our refuge and strength, always available to help us in our times of trouble. 
 
Despite these unprecedented times we are currently facing, may You continue to give our Council leaders wisdom and clarity of mind as they provide, protect and watch over the people of the Tweed Shire.
 
In Your mercy and steadfast love, we ask You to bless our Councillors as they meet and work together in unity seeking to make our community “Even better tomorrow than it is today”.
 
I pray this in the Name of Jesus
 
Amen."

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Katie Milne

RESOLVED that Council:

1.    Submits the attachment to this report on the Draft Far North Coast Regional Water Strategy to the Department of Primary Industry and Environment and includes the following:

  • Requests the Department removes a dam at Byrrill Creek from the long list of options due to the identified loss of significant and irreplaceable environment values.
  • Objects to further commercial groundwater extraction for bottling in the Tweed Shire.

2.    In the light of advice that the Department of Planning Industry and Environment, may not accept late submissions, submits the Draft TSC Water Strategies Review Project Reference Group Report with the current submission.

3.    Forwards the final report from the Water Strategies Review Project Reference Group to the Department of Primary Industry and Environment when it has been endorsed by Council.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Pryce Allsop

RESOLVED that Council extends business beyond 10.30pm.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Pryce Allsop

RESOLVED that Council:

1.    Urgently undertakes a drainage study of the Murwillumbah Leagues Club (MLC) site and surrounds, including hydraulic modelling of the contributing stormwater drainage network, surface water flows and interaction with flood mitigation devices. Particular focus needs to be given to providing recommendations to reduce flooding in the short term for the MLC site, including consideration of the installation of a flood pump and the optimal and most cost effective method to enclose the existing open stormwater channel. 

2.    Includes modelling consideration of the site in the long term in regards to climate change. 

3.    Requests of the General Manager that funding of this study be identified in the upcoming quarterly budget review.

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Warren PolglaseCr James Owen

PROPOSED that:

1. Council officers, in consultation with Murwillumbah Leagues Club representatives, monitor the performance of the current stormwater drainage, flood mitigation and sewerage management measures in and around the Murwillumbah Leagues Club land for 12 months.

2. A further report be provided detailing the outcomes of the monitoring period, any costs incurred by Council and the Murwillumbah Leagues Club for the period and recommending any further actions.

Amendment 1 was Lost

Cr James Owen
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

A.  Development Application DA18/0747.01 for amendment to Development Consent DA18/0747 for alterations and additions to existing Cabarita Surf Life Saving Club extending into Crown Reserve (Lot 7010 DP 1055324) and installation of two advertising signs be approved subject to the conditions being amended as follows:

1. Delete Condition No. 1 and replace with Condition No. 1A which reads as follows:

1A. The consent is issued for the following alterations and additions to the existing Cabarita Beach Surf Life Saving Club:

Ground floor
• Addition of a sealed undercover shaded area for Nippers training.
• Addition of a training gym;
• Addition of a cool room and freezer to kiosk;
• Internal modification to entry foyer/first aid room and stairs;
• Addition of wheelchair lift.

First floor
• Addition of a new observation deck;
• Addition of two training rooms/gyms;
• Addition of cold room;
• Internal modification to layout, bar, accommodate wheelchair lift and stairs;
• Addition of an archive/storage area;
• Addition of an office/additional storage area, and
• New awning in line with existing

Second floor
• An emergency control room.
• Addition of stair and wheelchair lift access; and
• Addition of plant deck and drone landing pad.

Roof Plan
• First floor roof extended to cover proposed training rooms and office area. 
• The ridge line of the first-floor roof to be adjusted on the western elevation.
• Additions of solar panels to all new roof areas.

Signage
This application also seeks approval for the installation of two signs on the facade upon the Eastern and Western elevations of the proposal.

The development shall be completed in accordance with the Statement of Environmental Effects and the following plans:

• General Arrangement Plan – Ground (Plan TP05 Rev 7) prepared by Plus Architecture and dated 10 November 2020;
• General Arrangement Plan – Level 1 (Plan TP06 Rev 7) prepared by Plus Architecture and dated 10 November 2020;
• General Arrangement Plan – Level 2 (Plan TP07 Rev 7) prepared by Plus Architecture and dated 10 November 2020;
• General Arrangement Plan – Roof (Plan TP08 Rev 7) prepared by Plus Architecture and dated 10 November 2020;
• North Elevation (Plan TP09 Rev 7) prepared by Plus Architecture and dated 10 November 2020;
• East Elevation (Plan TP10 Rev 7) prepared by Plus Architecture and dated 10 November 2020;
• South Elevation (Plan TP11 Rev 7) prepared by Plus Architecture and dated 10 November 2020; and
• West Elevation (Plan TP12 Rev 7) prepared by Plus Architecture and dated 10 November 2020,

except where varied by the conditions of this consent.

2. Delete Condition No. 8 and replace with Condition No. 8A which reads as follows:

8A. The existing building does not contain adequate measures to protect persons and facilitate egress in the event of fire.  Therefore the existing building and new building works are to satisfy the requirements of the BCA inclusive of Sections; C, D and E.

Further to the above fire upgrading, the option is available to submit a fire engineering report containing performance solutions addressing the Performance Requirements contained in Volume 1 of the Building Code of Australia relating to the BCA. This report is to be submitted to the appointed registered certifier for assessment and determination prior to issue of the Construction Certificate.

3. Insert new Condition No 9.1 which reads as follows:

9.1 A certificate of compliance (CC) under Sections 305, 306 and 307 of the Water Management Act 2000 is to be obtained from Council to verify that the necessary requirements for the supply of water and sewerage to the development have been made with the Tweed Shire Council.

Pursuant to Clause 146 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulations, 2000, a Construction Certificate shall NOT be issued by a Certifying Authority unless all Section 64 Contributions have been paid and the Certifying Authority has sighted Council's "Certificate of Compliance" signed by an authorised officer of Council. 

BELOW IS ADVICE ONLY

The Section 64 Contributions for this development at the date of this approval have been estimated as: 

Water: 1.04 ET @ $11,268.00 = $11,718.70
Sewer: 1.69 ET @ $7,288.00 = $12,316.70

4. Insert new Condition No. 45.1 which reads as follows:

45.1 The premises is to be utilised as a surf lifesaving club facility and any other use of the premises will require separate development consent. The Level 1 deck approved under DA08/1171 (as amended) is only to be used for a maximum of two functions each month and Sunday each week for Cabarita Beach Surf Life Saving Club events only.

5. Inclusion of a further condition to address the concerns regarding privacy and noise, which reads:

Prior to issue of a Construction Certificate, updated plans are to be submitted for approval of the Principal Certifying Authority demonstrating an acoustic barrier to the north elevation of the Level 1 observation deck.


B.  ATTACHMENT 4 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd.

"Thank you Madam Mayor

I am going to pray in the Christian tradition.  If you would like to join with me, please bow your head.

Gracious God,

Thank you for Council’s commitment to look after people and places.  We appreciate the beauty and abundant natural resources of our region, and acknowledge the many thousands of years of care for our region by the traditional owners and custodians of these lands.

With that history, we look forward and recognise the privilege of working together now for the sake of those who will follow us.  May tonight’s meeting express the wisdom to hear the diverse needs of our community and make good decisions for the future.

Help us as we work towards a community where we are truly one and free. 

Bless Council, both elected and staff, in their passionate approach to the pursuit of excellence.

We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

Cr Pryce Allsop
Cr James Owen

PROPOSED that Development Application DA20/0965 for earthworks and associated drainage at Lot 21 DP 1082482 Tweed Coast Road, Chinderah be approved subject to the conditions attached to this report.

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Katie Milne
Cr Ron Cooper

RECOMMENDEDthat Development Application DA20/0965 for earthworks and associated drainage at Lot 21 DP 1082482 Tweed Coast Road, Chinderah be deferred to conduct a workshop to discuss the following:
 
1.  The pros and cons of pumping of sand direct to the sites.
 
2.  The physical and psychological impacts on affected residents of truck and dog movements every two minutes for 6½ days per week for a minimum of 28 weeks.
 
3.  Seeking professional medical advice on the possible and physical and psychological impacts so many truck movements.
 
4.  Damage to residents properties.
 
5.  Damage to major roads in the area.
 
6.  Delays in commuter and tourist traffic.
 
7.  Impact on Kingscliff businesses over the 28 weeks minimum of traffic disruption.
 
9.  The effectiveness of compliance enforcement in the light of the problems of managing dust and traffic movements as per the approval for Kings Coast.
 
10. The impacts of introducing foreign fill material into the area including the potential of introduction of weeds and fire ants.
 
11. The requirement for orderly economic development as a key consideration in State Government Planning legislation over the aspirations for profits at the expense of the community’s health and amenity.

12. Constraining retail, tourism and commercial activity in the Covid aftermath. 

13. Potential impacts on flooding.

14. Invites the proponent and representative of the Kingscliff Ratepayers & Progress Association.

The Amendment 1 was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST -  None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase

ALTERNATE MOTION:

Cr Ron Cooper
Cr Katie Milne

RECOMMENDED that Council defers the decision on DA20/0860 for a new haulage road and acoustic wall and use of the haul road to transport fill associated with DA05/0004 (as amended) at Lot 4 DP 727425 Chinderah Road, Chinderah; Lot 26C DP 10715 Quigan Street, Kingscliff; Road 2301 Tweed Coast Road, Chinderah to conduct a workshop to discuss the following:

1.  The pumping of sand direct to the sites with the necessary protections for the wetlands.

2.  The physical and psychological impacts on affected residents of truck and dog movements every two minutes for 6½ days per week for a minimum of 44 weeks.

3.  Seeking professional medical advice on the possible physical and psychological impacts of 90,000 truck movements for a minimum of 44 weeks.

4.  Damage to residents properties.

5.  Damage to major roads in the area.

6.  Delays in commuter and tourist traffic.

7.  Impact on Kingscliff businesses over the 44 weeks minimum of traffic disruption.

8.  The impact on insurance premiums for structures built on the old 1:100 fill level.

9.  The effectiveness of compliance enforcement in the light of the difficulty of managing dust and traffic movements as per the approval for Kings Coast.

10.  The impacts on an identified significant wetland of introducing foreign fill material into a deep sand environment.  This will also address the introduction of weeds and fire ants.

11.  The impact on the community's confidence that Council is acting appropriately by increasing a developers financial return at the expense of their health and amenity.

12.  Impact on retail, tourism and commercial activity in the Covid aftermath.

13.  The impact of fill on flood behaviour and particularly with the alternative proposed fill source.

14.  The impact on threatened species and biodiversity including but not limited to the Wallum Froglet, Mitchell's Rainforest Snail and the Bush Stone Curlew.

15.  Invites the developer, a representative from the Kingscliff Ratepayers & Progress Association and up to 5 community representatives from the submitters. 


The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase

Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Pryce Allsop

RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 10 December 2020 be received and noted; and

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1 National Road Series & Championships Cup from Saturday 28 November 2020 until Sunday 7 December 2020

That the proposed National Road Series & Champions Cup from Saturday 28 November 2020 until Sunday 7 December 2020 to be held in the Tweed Valley be supported subject to current COVID-19 restrictions at the time of the event and the following conditions:

1. NSW Police approval being obtained.

2. Endorsement of the event by Cycling Queensland.

3. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 1 week before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.

4. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.

5. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.

6. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.

7. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.

8. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.

9. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.

10. That the applicant visit  www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.

11. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.

12. The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.

13. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.

14. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose, particularly Numinbah and Limpinwood/Zara Road that have repairs scheduled for after the event.



6.2 Changes to Bus Zone in Murwillumbah Street, Murwillumbah

That:

1.  The Bus Zone in Murwillumbah Street, Murwillumbah, be changed to 'Bus Zone 9:30am-4:30pm' and 'Loading Zone 4:30pm-9:30am'.

2.  That the parking zones in the vicinity of Murwillumbah Street and Queen Street, Murwillumbah be reviewed in consultation with the businesses and community and be brought back to the Committee in early 2021. 

3.  That the loading zones in Queen Street and Murwillumbah Street, Murwillumbah be sign-posted with a 20 minute limit.


6.3 Barnby Street and William Street, Murwillumbah

That a give way sign be installed on Barnby Street on the southern approach to William Street, Murwillumbah.


7.1 Tweed Coast Road, Cabarita Footpath - Skateboards and Bikes

That:

1.  That "No Bicycle/Skateboarding" signage be installed on the footpath area between 51 Tweed Coast Road, Cabarita (north) to the end of the Woolworths site.

2.  That "No Bicycle/Skateboarding" signage be installed on the footpath area at Marine Parade, Kingscliff, between Turnock Street and 20 Marine Parade, Kingscliff.

3.  That Council investigates the provision of pavement stencils to reinforce the regulatory "No Bicycle/Skateboarding".


7.2 Gold Coast Open Surfing 2021 - Change of Date

That the proposed change of date for the Gold Coast Open Surfing event from 17-23 March 2021 to 2-13 May 2021 is supported.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Mike Boyd from Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church:

"Gracious God, 

We are grateful for the privilege of meaningful work, for our colleagues, for the sense of purpose and joy in sharing common goals.

This makes us mindful of those in our community who are isolated due to age, ill health, limited work opportunities, homelessness, domestic and family violence, subtle or unsubtle discrimination, or who do not feel welcomed in our community.

We’re grateful that Council is committed to enabling people to be connected in many ways and to foster a welcoming, integrated community.  Please bless Council as they work towards this common goal through diverse means, so our community may be strengthened as a result of tonight’s meeting.

We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr Pryce Allsop

PROPOSED that:

1.    The tree be removed.

2.     Freckles Early Learning Centre be required to pay for the removal of the tree and pay for compensatory planting of 5 mature trees at the direction of council officers.


AMENDMENT 1

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that Council:

1.    Investigate the use of lighting and/or wind spinners to deter the roosting ibises in the mature Eucalyptus tereticornis (Forest Red Gum) tree adjoining Freckles Early Childhood Learning Centre, if it is deemed there is reasonable chance of success and it is permissible in the flight path, then proceed with the installation of the appropriate lighting as soon as possible.

2.    In the event that lighting the tree is not found to be an appropriate tool to reduce the ibis roosting population then:

a)       Council investigate options to plant some mature stock trees in the vicinity to offset any potential tree removal, and allow to establish over an 18-24 month period. During this time, Council to manage the Ibis issue on-site periodically or an as-needed basis.

b)       The intent being that periodic dispersal of the Ibis population reduces their numbers to a manageable level, and periodic audit and risk management of the tree itself to minimise any risk associated with branch drop.

c)        The cost estimate of approximately $8,000 over 2 years for the management program be allocated through Council’s budget process. The program will include a 4 week dispersal program every 2-3 months to manage the Ibis roosting within the tree plus costs for additional tree maintenance from Council’s tree unit. 

d)       If Ibis remain after the 18-24 month period, Council can reconsider removing the tree. If not required, Council has retained a critical natural asset, as well as inheriting additional tree assets in the vicinity via the off-setting and planting of additional trees.


The Amendment 1 was Carried

VOTE AGAINST - Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Warren Polglase

Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Tweed Coast and Waterways Committee Meeting held Wednesday 9 December 2020 be received and noted.

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be endorsed as follows:

A3. Hastings Point Headland Management Plan

That Council:

1. Commits to preparing a Hastings Point Management Plan and that it be incorporated into the Tweed Coastline Coastal Management program.

2. Requests the Sustainability & Environment Unit to prepare draft Terms of Reference and cost estimate to complete the works.

A4. Fingal Headland Access and Erosion Management

That Council notes, in relation to the Fingal Headland Access and Erosion Management project, that the Tweed Coast & Waterways Committee:

1. Is aware of and endorses the project.

2. Recommends that Council considers the project for funding opportunities.

3. Supports Council working with the Aboriginal community and Crown Lands regarding the approval and implementation process.

GB3. Cobaki seagrass / saltmarsh 

That Council sends a letter to Department of Primary Industry and Environment (DPIE) regarding the Cobaki Saltmarsh, requesting an update, expressing its concern and interest due to the water quality, and seeking an expedited resolution.

The Motion was Carried

Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Katie Milne

RESOLVED that:


1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 4 February 2021 be received and noted and

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations (via email) be adopted as follows:

7.1 Hastings Road, Bogangar

That:
1. A short length of double centre line be installed on Hastings Road on the approaches to Reef Water Circuit and a 5m no stopping edge line be installed on Hastings Road on the east side just south of the pedestrian crossing point.
2. No prohibitive parking be placed on Hastings Road near Cooley Street and this area be monitored and brought back to the Committee if considered necessary.

7.2 Kingscliff Public School - School Zone Safety Upgrades

That:
1. The bus zone in Orient Street, Kingscliff be removed and the pick-up/drop off zone be extended to replace the existing bus zone and Surfside Buslines be notified that the changes will be effective from Term 2 2021. 
2. The bus zone in Sutherland Street, Kingscliff be extended north to replace the existing "No Parking" zone and Surfside Buslines be notified that the changes will be effective from Term 2 2021.
3. The installation of a right turn lane from Sutherland Street into Orient Street, Kingscliff be reviewed to reduce the impact on residents.
4. The installation of the shared user path and associated crossing point on Sutherland Street, Kingscliff is supported.
5. The installation of the new school crossing on Orient Street just north of Omar Street is supported.
6.  Council officers consult with impacted residents about proposed changes.
7.  The school be requested to notify the school community about the upgrades

7.3 Adelaide Street, Tweed Heads

That a:
1. 10m section of yellow no stopping line be installed on the inside of the curve on Adelaide Street at No. 63 
2. Short length of double centre lines be placed on Adelaide Street on the approach to Charles Street and a a continuity line be placed at Charles Street on Adelaide Street.
3. "Give Way" sign be placed on Adelaide Street on the approaches to Charles Street.

7.4 Letitia Road, Fingal Head

That, while the Committee does not support the ongoing closure of Letitia Road, Fingal Head on traffic management purposes, there are no objections to Council extending the time period of the temporary closure.
1.   Council Writes to the NSW Police, Transport for NSW and the representatives on the Local Traffic Committee to advise of Council's intention to maintain the road closure at Letitia Road, Fingal Head until 27 May 2021 due to heightened concerns to protect the Aboriginal Elders and residents particularly vulnerable to COVID-19.
2.   Maintains the road closure at Letitia Road, Fingal Head until 27 May 2021 ensuring that the road is still open to pedestrians and cyclists.
3.   Seeks the advice of the Aboriginal Advisory Committee for any further extensions to the closure.

7.5 Coronation Avenue, Pottsville

That the:
1. "No Skateboarders and Cyclists" signs and pavement stencils on both sides of Coronation Avenue between the two Berkleys Lane accesses be installed.
2. Road Safety Officer provide information to schools regarding cyclists dismounting on marked pedestrian crossings.

7.6 Tweed Heads Parking Limits

That the following parking zones be installed:
1. Tweed Terrace between Boundary Street  and Boundary Lane, Point Danger  -  3 hour (3P) parking "5 am - 11pm"
2. Off road parking area between Eden Street and Hill Street, Tweed Heads - 3 hour (3P) parking "5 am - 11pm"
3. Boundary Street  from Coral Street to Twin Towns and car park adjacent to Twin Towns Services Club - 3 hour (3P) parking "5 am – 11 pm" and "No Parking 11 pm – 5 am" 
4. Bay Street parking on Chris Cunningham Park - 3 hour (3P) parking from "5 am to 11 pm"
5. End of Bay Street, Tweed Heads - as this is a residential area the installation of timed parking during the day was not supported, however this should be monitored and referred back to the Committee if required.

 The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Ron Cooper
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

PROPOSED that the following Policy in regard to Delegation of Power to Determine Development Applications be adopted by Council: 

"The EP&A Act 1979 appoints Council as the Determining Authority for certain types of Development Applications; such determinations requiring a Meeting of the full Council. In accordance with S.377 of the LG Act 1993, this authority is delegated to the General Manager (GM) by Council subject to Parts A, B, & C below: 

A.  A delegation of the  Power to determine complying Development Applications without the need to report to a Council meeting can be assumed by the General Manager under the following circumstances:

i.   The estimated cost of the proposed development is less than $1 million, or
ii.  The estimated cost of the proposed development is between $1 million and $10 million; and
iii.  Councillors have been given at least two weeks' prior notice of the General Manager's intention to determine the Application under Delegated Authority, and
iv.  No Councillor has made a written request for the application to be determined by Council, and
v.  The Director of Planning and Regulation (DPR) has advised the General Manager that in his/her professional judgement (a) the Application meets the Compliance Criteria in Part B, and (b) issues raised by public submissions received during its exhibition are adequately dealt with, and (c) any proposed relaxations of requirements of the Tweed DCP does not diminish the desired future character and amenity of the neighbourhood.

B.  Compliance Criteria:

The Development Application does not propose a relaxation of more than 10% of any numerical development standards contained in the Tweed DCP and other adopted planning policies and is otherwise substantially compliant with these policies.

C.  Access to Internal Reports:

When a Development Application is determined under Delegated Authority, internal Assessment Reports underpinning such determinations will be made available to Councillors on individual request."

Cr Warren Polglase

REASON FOR CONFIDENTIALITY

Local Government Act

This report is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, which permits the meeting to be closed to the public for business relating to the following: 

(g)     advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege

ALTERNATE MOTION

RECOMMENDED that:
1.  Council undertakes a review and prepares an amendment to the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008, to ensure the currency of its provisions as they relate to the Seabreeze Estate Pottsville 'Potential School Site', including but not limited to the insertion of an express objective for clause 3.5 of Section B21 and validation of the forecasts substantiating the need for a school at the site. The Development Control Plan amendment, once prepared, is reported back to Council prior to public exhibition. 
2.  Council makes representations to the local State Members and the Minister for Planning with regards to the difficulties and the financial disadvantage caused to Council in regard to NSW State Government position on school zonings and the potential for these problems to continue into the future. 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen
ABSTAINED - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins from Murwillumbah Church of Christ.

"Dear Father,

I thank and pray for all the men and women You have placed in Council to watch and serve over the Tweed Shire.   Whether it be from the staff who work on the front desk to all those who mow the grass and maintain our roads, each one is a valuable team member and I pray for Your goodness and safety over each and every one of them.

Father, You have promised to give generously to anyone who asks for wisdom. I pray that You will give Council wisdom, understanding and clarity of mind, as they come together tonight.  Direct them in the things that are important and may the outcomes be fair and right, not only for the now, but also for the future of others to come. 

May everyone be heard and no-one misunderstood.  That all be treated mindfully and with respect.

Father, continue to help and guide us, to live and practice the values we know to be true ... that our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.

Amen"

Cr Katie Milne
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council endorses the following motion be submitted to the Australian Local Government Association for the National General Assembly 2021:
 

Motion: Economic Stimulus for Regenerative Landscape Management

"The National General Assembly calls on the Federal Government to provide a significant and transformational funding stream for regenerative landscape management as an economic stimulus and job creator, that is easily accessible for rural landholders (including consideration of US and EU models of farm payments) to maintain and restore rural lands and provide the large scale change that is required to mitigate the increasing natural disasters that Australia is experiencing with Climate Change."

Background

Regenerative Landscape Management has the potential to create thousands of jobs, mitigate the impact of natural disasters, enhance town water supply, assist farmers, capture carbon, and transform Australia’s degraded landscapes.

Australia is in dire need of transformational change to address these issues.  Landholders are keen to make changes but they need significant financial and technical support to implement these practices. 

This COVID-19 crisis is an opportune time to kick start Australia on a path to building back better, reconnecting our communities to the land and keeping our communities safe.  

Young people are keen to assist with this change but at the moment there are few job opportunities or career prospects in this area.  Until research and investment in this space is activated these opportunities will not be realised.  The Australian landscape is important for our national psyche and sense of well being.  Regenerative Landscape Management is a way to reinvigorate that pride and be a transformative change that will secure Australia’s future into the 21st Century.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

PROPOSED that:


1. Council receives the Water Strategies Review Project Reference Group (PRG) Report to Council prepared by Workplace Edge in December 2020.

2. Council adopts the recommendations of the Water Strategies Review PRG as listed in the PRG report prepared by Workplace Edge, with the exception of recommendation 3, the recommendations being:

1.   Integrated water management with adaptive pathways – Council adopts an integrated water management approach with adaptive pathways in the development of its future water strategies.

2.   Clarrie Hall Dam – Council proceeds with the raising of the Clarrie Hall Dam; and continues the work on planning and land acquisition, in accordance with the existing project schedule for this work which is consistent with Council’s resolution. Concurrently, Council further investigates other options as recommended in this report that may be able to diversify water supply, be less reliant on rainfall dependent sources, and improve the security and longevity of the yield.

4.   Mini-link - Council continues with the upgrade of the mini-link between the City of Gold Coast and Tweed Shire to provide some contingency supply in the event of a failure of the Tweed District Water supply.

5.   Desalination – As a priority, Council commissions investigation and feasibility into the options of accessing the desalination plant at Tugun or purchasing a desalination plant in its own name or in conjunction with other regional councils.

6.   Recycled water non-potable – In the short-term, Council considers engaging with developers for existing developments such as Kings Forest and Cobaki regarding the possibility of implementing a residential recycled water scheme for the existing approved developments.

7.   Managed aquifer recharge – Council investigates the reuse of stormwater, with aquifer recharge storage, to be incorporated into a locally integrated water management scheme.

8.   Community/precinct water recycling schemes - In addition, Council reviews planning requirements to ensure the implementation of community/precinct recycled water schemes for future development applications.

9.   Recycled water potable – Council considers development and implementation of an appropriate education campaign to address the community concerns regarding recycled potable water in the short term, with a view to medium/long-term implementation of recycled potable water.
     
      Council considers approaching the NSW Government regarding the possible easing of restrictions and associated legislation and policy on the use of recycled potable water.

10.  Land management practices – Council considers detailed investigation, promotion and development of programs for landscape rehydration works and regenerative landscape management.

11.  Commercial extraction for bottling water – Council considers restricting the removal of groundwater for drinking purposes for crisis/drought management rather than a permanent/regular source for bottled water.

12.  Groundwater alluvium and coastal sands aquifers – Council considers further research regarding the quantity of water that is available and the environmental impacts of using alluvial and coastal sands aquifer sources of water.

13.  Underground pipe grid – Council considers further research to confirm the costs and volume of water that could be stored in particular geographic area as a supplement to other water supply options.

14.  Long-term urban water strategy – Council considers inclusion of the results of future research and development and hydrological (surface water and groundwater) investigations into a long-term urban water strategy.

15.  Water Demand Strategies - Council considers the recommendations by the PRG as listed in Table 6 of the PRG Report, with a focus on the following high-priority options:implementing enhanced leak detection and correction system and processes improving data collection as part of a shift towards digitisation of data collection with the introduction of smart metering enhance incentive programs as listed in Table 5, especially with the introduction of a hardship program for those who are disadvantaged.

16.  In light of the recent experience with drought conditions in the Tweed and application of drought water restrictions for the first time (under the current policy), and the projected impact of global warming, Council revises the text in the Policy to reflect the new triggers and water use targets (e.g. 5/10/25).

17.  Council considers triggers for focused community and business water use education programs and campaigns.

18.  Council considers the use of recycled water for firefighting and dust suppression.

19. Council considers a program for growing shade trees around the edges of the Dam and Weirs and applying regenerative landscape management practices.

3. Council amends and adopts the amended recommendation 3 of the Water Strategies Review PRG, the amended recommendation being:

3.    Byrrill Creek Dam – The option of a large or small dam at Byrrill Creek is not preferred due to the reliance on rainfall, the inundation of areas of land which will not be useable in future for this highly significant environment, for either agriculture or available as natural environment, and the likely impact on productivity and wellbeing of the community as a result of this option.

4. Council proceeds with the implementation of the PRG recommendations as outlined in the Overarching Implementation Steps attached to this Council report.

5. The recommendations of the Water Strategies Review PRG inform the review of Council’s Integrated Water Cycle Management Strategy.

6. Council thanks the Water Strategies Review PRG for its work.


AMENDMENT 1

Cr Katie Milne
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that :

1.   Council adopts the Water Strategies review Project Reference Group (PRG) recommendations as described in this report and the PRG report prepared by the facilitator, Workplace Edge.

2.   Council proceeds with the implementation of the PRG recommendations as outlined in the Overarching Implementation Steps attached to this Council report with the modification to recommendation 3 to be in line with the PRG recommendations.

3.   The recommendations of the Water Strategies Review PRG inform the review of Council’s Integrated Water Cycle Management Strategy.

4.   Council thanks the Water Strategies Review PRG for its work.

Cr Ron Cooper
Cr Katie Milne

RESOLVED that Council, in respect to Contract RFO2020132 Concept Design and Planning Approval Documentation for Hinged Barrier at the Bray Park Weir:

1. Declines to accept any of the Offers, and by resolution, in accordance with Regulation 178(3)(e) of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2005: "(e)  enter into negotiations with any person (whether or not the person was a tenderer) with a view to entering into a contract in relation to the subject matter of the tender", noting the reasons for doing so and granting the General Manager delegated authority to award the contract and approve appropriately deemed variations to the contract and those variations be reported to Council at finalisation of the contract.

2.  Notes the reasons for declining to accept any of the offers are that the price of the offer from the capable organisation was well above budget estimates.

3.  Notes the reasons for not declining to invite fresh tenders as referred to in subclause (3)(b)-(d) are that the matter is urgent as the frequency of overtopping of the weir and the risk of salt water contamination of the water supply is increasing.  It is considered a better result for the project, in terms of implementable concept designs and cost, will be achieved by working with a consultant and determining what work would best be done by Council and what would be best done by the consultant, and in doing so allocating risk to where it can be managed best.  Both these activities require negotiation with the nominated consultant and should result in a better outcome for the project at an acceptable cost.

4.  Notes the reasons for determining to enter into negotiations with the preferred bidder in accordance with subclause (3)(e) is that they have demonstrated suitable experience, expertise and methodology to undertake the engagement and have a good understanding of risks to be addressed in any concept design and environmental impact assessment.


5.     ATTACHMENTS 1 and 2 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(c)     information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business

(d)     commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
 (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
 (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or
 (iii) reveal a trade secret


The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Katie Milne
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RECOMMENDED that Council:

1.    Endorses the waiver of an architectural design competition in lieu of an architectural design review process as endorsed by the NSW Government Architect over both the Tweed Mall Shopping Centre and Tweed Heads Bowls Club sites and that written correspondence confirming Council’s endorsement of the waiver be forwarded to the NSW Government Architects;

2.    Nominates Council’s Senior Urban Designer to represent Council on the architectural design review panels which will also be made up of a NSW Government Architect representative and a proponent nominated architect representative;

3.    Advises the landowner proponents of Council’s likely fees and charges based on an hourly rate as specified within Fees and Charges 2020/2021 Revenue Policy;

4.    Advises the landowner proponents to engaging in Council’s development assessment panel process to ensure statutory planning considerations and relevant development control, standards and guidelines are being appropriately considered as part of the design review process;

5.   Requires both sites through the design review process to demonstrate a high standard of design excellence that provides significant improvement to the streetscape and building design through:

  • Building, urban design and landscape design which pays homage to Tweed Shire’s internationally significant environment and significant Aboriginal Cultural heritage;
  • Buildings achieve high standards of sustainable design to carry us into the future and include where practical green walls, green roof areas and zero / low carbon operations;
  • Preparation of an integrated landscape design concept that demonstrates generous landscape planting areas and substantial areas of landscaped front setbacks, particularly for the Tweed Mall site, to improve the visual and health amenity, reduce urban heat island effect, noise and pollution impacts; and
  • Activated uses to the ground level and public accessibility of the street interface designed to achieve a high level of pedestrian amenity such as shady seating and comfort befitting of the 'key site' locations.

6.    Considers a further report at the conclusion of the architecture design review panel process to inform Council of the design review panel recommendations and outcomes over both sites.

Amendment 1 was Carried

Cr Katie Milne
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:

1. Notes the significance of the environment in the Tweed Shire being identified as one of Australia’s eight National Iconic Landscapes, having the third highest biodiversity in Australia and the most diverse range of species of Australia’s ancient Gondwana rainforests.

2. Notes the threat that natural disasters pose for this internationally significant environment and the Tweed community, particularly the previous bushfire season that could have resulted in catastrophic loss for our community and our rainforests or many species within them.

3. Notes that one of the most effective ways to alleviate the worst impacts of natural disasters is to make the landscape healthier and more resilient by restoring ecosystems and soil health through large scale regenerative landscape management.

4. Acknowledges the work undertaken by governments and volunteers to restore the environment but the mammoth task involved.

5. Notes the obligation of all levels of government to protect this community and this precious environment but the difficulty in doing so with limited funds or landholder incentives.

6. Recognises that government funding is unlikely to increase to any significant degree in the near future and that impacts to Council, the community and the environment will increase with climate change unless large scale restoration efforts are undertaken.

7. Notes the appreciation people express for Tweed’s beautiful environment and the incredible generosity of people all over the world in response to Australia’s recent bushfires.

8. Brings forward a report on the potential for Council to establish a mechanism, such as a trust, to campaign locally, nationally and internationally to raise funds to assist in large scale transformational Regenerative Landscape Management to preserve and restore the Tweed’s internationally significant environment.

9. Requests a meeting with Federal and State Environment Ministers and Local Members to seek special status for Tweed Shire to protect and restore this internationally significant environment and recognise the added pressures of population growth in such important and sensitive areas.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

Councillor Katie Milne asked:

From preliminary estimates of information currently available, what would be the maximum potential environmental offset value that could be realised from the 330 hectare Tanglewood property that is currently on the market for sale?


The Director Sustainable Communities and Environment responded as follows:

  • The Tanglewood property is 311 ha with approximately 80 ha of existing high use koala habitat, potential for an additional 70 ha of primary koala habitat and a further 160 ha of secondary koala habitat.
  • All areas have potential to generate biodiversity credits under the NSW Biodiversity Offset Scheme.
  • Assessment of biodiversity credits under the scheme is required to be undertaken by an accredited assessor in accordance with the Biodiversity Assessment Method.
  • The amount of credits generated is variable across the site based on vegetation classification, vegetation condition, ecosystem classification and the presence of species that may also generate credits.
  • The financial value of these credits is also variable based on the specific credit value and the supply and demand on the credit trading market.
  • Engagement of an accredited assessor is required to determine an estimate of the financial value of any biodiversity credits that could be generated from the site, noting that realisation of this financial potential remains subject to the sale of these credits on the trading market.
  • Further to the above, Councillors were advised by the General Manager on 22 February 2021 that Tangelwood is under contact in a due diligence stage until 30 June 2021. The potential purchasers ae currently undertaking necessary due diligence before the contract is finalised and this includes attending Council Development Assessment Panel meetings.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that Council: 

1. Writes to Mr Geoff Provest MP expressing Council’s appreciation for his advocacy for the approval of the Tweed Coast Koala Plan of Management and other measures to improve the prospects for koalas on the Tweed Coast.

2. Requests the Tweed Shire and other councils with significant koala populations (e.g. Byron, Lismore, Port Macquarie and Gunnedah) be treated in the same manner as the Central Coast Council where Koala SEPP 21 applies to all zones including rural zones.

3.  Seeks an urgent meeting with the State members for Tweed and Lismore, Mr Geoff Provest MP, and Ms Janelle Saffin MP respectively, and the Minister for Planning and Public Places, the Hon. Rob Stokes to discuss the following issues:

a) potential amendments to the Koala SEPP 2021 to permit the preparation of koala plan of management under the Koala SEPP to apply to all land, including rural zoned land.

b) the proposed removal council’s consent role in relation to forestry.

c) environmental planning measures to ensure that koala habitat is appropriately zoned in Council LEPs.

d) further consultation with stakeholders including councils, researchers and practitioners to ensure the Koala SEPP 2021 meets the needs and aspirations of local communities.

e) further investment in hardwood plantations instead of harvesting native forest.


4. In accordance with the mandatory requirement of Clause 16 of the Koala SEPP 2020, resolves to:

a) commence work on surveying land within the Shire (excepting National Parks and land covered by the Tweed Coast Comprehensive Koala Plan of Management) to identify koala habitat; and 

b) on completion of this work advises Council of its outcomes and brings forward a report on appropriate environmental planning measures to protect and manage koalas and their habitat in those areas. 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Pryce Allsop
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that, in respect to Contract RFO2020139 Air-conditioning Systems Maintenance for Tweed Shire Council:


1. Council awards a 2 year contract to LEN Enterprises Pty Ltd ABN 27 000 724 809 for the amount of $257,887.85  (exclusive of GST) and $283,676.64 (inclusive of GST).

2.     The Director Sustainable Communities and Environment be given delegated authority to approve a 2 year contract extension should it be required.

3. The General Manager be granted delegated authority to approve appropriately deemed variations to the contract and those variations be reported to Council at finalisation of the contract.

4. ATTACHMENTS 1 and 2 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:-

(d)  commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:

(i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
(ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or
(iii) reveal a trade secret

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins.

Dear Father, 

I thank you for the Tweed Shire Councillors that You have appointed over us. I pray for Your blessing & guidance on everyone here today, to be faithful & trusted leaders in all of their duties.

In particular, I pray for our Mayor Chris Cherry & the wonderful job she has been doing over the Tweed Shire. Father, I ask You to give our Mayor clarity of mind & a discerning heart. May her thoughts & words be fair & true. Father, we know her job is challenging & demands much from her, but may You continue to give our Mayor wisdom & understanding as she leads & guides Council in our meeting tonight. 

Father, there is much to discuss & go over tonight. But may we be reminded that You are our Invisible Guest…our silent listener… who is welcome & always seeks the very best for us.

So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.     

Thank You, Father
Amen

RESOLVED that:

1. The following tabled Petition(s) be received and noted.

• Petitions received on 16 March 2021 and containing 32 valid signatories in relation to "Sacred Park, Cnr Banner and Murwillumbah Streets, Murwillumbah" advising as follows:

"The undersigned residents are concerned at the neglect of this culturally significant landmark in our street The issues are:
  • The roof tiles, brick walls and concrete floor are covered in moss and mould;

ALTERNATE MOTION


Cr Ron Cooper
Cr Katie Milne

PROPOSED that:

1.    a.     Review and modify the existing Concept Plan guided by the permissability of the current zoning of the site with a view to reducing costs while retaining liveability and social objectives and planning requirements.

       b.     Confirm the principle that Wardrop Village will remain rental only and will remain in public ownership.  This will avoid the market driving up village house prices and to avoid the potential for division in the community.

2.    a.     Consult with people in rental stress to confirm the acceptability of living in the Wardrop Village model.

       b.     This conversation should include local representative of Community Housing Options who have offices in the Tweed and who are in continual contact with people in rental stress in the Tweed.

3.    Proceed to develop the Business case and the Shire wide Affordable Housing Strategy.

4.    a.    Seek to re-engage with Landcom.

       b.    Using the first stage of Wardrop Village as a base, compare the cost/benefit of Landcom’s model and the private sector model for Affordable Housing.
       
       c.    Council notes the likely continuing increase in property prices in the Tweed – the investment swing to Short Term Holiday Lettings – the impact of the State Government’s 10 year leasing model on long-term availability of affordable rental – the Tweed’s growing dependence on the tourism, retail and hospitality sectors – the fact that these sectors rely on low wage employees who are often required to accept part time and causal employment.  These people are becoming homeless or leaving the Tweed.

5.   a.     Contact National Housing Finance and Investment Corporation regarding grant parameters.

      b.     Proceed to prepare a business plan if all of the above indicate possible viability.

6.    Progressively update the Audit Committee on the required procedures.

7.    Ensure that councillors have the opportunity to participate in this process at every stage.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that Standing Orders be resumed.

Cr James Owen
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that:


A. Development Application DA19/0802 for the demolition of existing dwelling and construction of a caravan park in 4 stages including a bore for water – Stage 1 for 8 short term sites, 62 long term sites, community centre, swimming pool, amenities, men’s shed, managers dwelling, on-site detention pond and effluent treatment system; Stage 2 for 40 long term sites; Stage 3 for 41 long term sites and Stage 4 for 21 long term sites at Lot 2 DP 803636 No. 355 Tomewin Road, Dungay be refused for the following reasons:

1.     Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the likely impacts of that development, including environmental impacts on both the natural and built environment, and social economic impacts on the locality.

(i)    The development is likely to have adverse impact on the existing built environment as a result of the proposed density of development occurring on the land in an area which comprises of vast rural landscapes and a character which is inconsistent with the proposed development as well as the impact on existing residences as a result of the increase in population;
(ii)    The development is likely to have adverse impact on the existing community as a result of a sudden increase in population in an area which is otherwise sparsely populated and the demand the development will put on local infrastructure and services;
(iii)    The development is likely to have adverse impact on existing agricultural land uses due to the potential conflicts between the proposed residential development occurring in a rural zone which forms part of an area which is considered to be Farmland of Regional Significance.

2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) ) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 in relation to site suitability; an isolated rural lot with little access to public transport and services, forms a flood island during storm events and cannot be accessed by car or foot in emergencies, containing 164 long term sites (manufactured homes), 8 short term caravan sites with a potential population of 344 – 516 people is not a suitable location for the development. The proposal is not in accordance with the principles of Tweed DCP Section A3, the Tweed Local Environment Plan and the NSW Floodplain Development Manual;

3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the development is not considered to adequately satisfy the provisions of The Tweed LEP 2014 including the objectives of the plan, the zone objectives, and Part 7 (Additional Local Provisions);

4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 Council is not satisfied (as per section 7.10 of the Tweed LEP 2014) that suitable essential services (the supply of water and the disposal and management of sewage) are available to the proposed development;

5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the proposed development does not satisfy the provisions of SEPP 21 Caravan Parks

(i)    The application fails to satisfy the aims and objectives outlined in Clause 3 of SEPP 21 – Caravan Parks.
(ii)   The application fails to satisfy the matters to be considered by Council outlined in Clause 10 of SEPP 21 – Caravan Parks.

6.    Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the application has failed to adequately satisfy the Tweed DCP Section A13 – Socio Economic Impact Assessment;

7.    Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(d) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 consideration of the submissions made in accordance with the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act from both public authorities and local residents indicate that the proposed development is not worthy of support; and;

8.    Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the proposed development was originally exhibited for a period of 30 days and additional information was further notified to objectors for a period of 14 days which raised several concerns over the development proposal and the social, environmental, economic and built environmental impacts. Based on the other listed reasons for refusal and having regard to the extent of concern raised by the public, it is considered that the proposed development is not in the public interest.

B.     ATTACHMENTS 7 and 8 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

RESOLVED that Development Application DA20/0965 for earthworks and associated drainage at Lot 21 DP 1082482 Tweed Coast Road, Chinderah be approved subject to the conditions attached to this report.

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Ron Cooper

PROPOSED that Development Application DA20/0965 for earthworks and associated drainage at Lot 21 DP 1082482 Tweed Coast Road, Chinderah be refused for the following reasons:

1.    Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the proposed development does not give effect to the adopted Kingscliff Locality Plan.

2.    Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the proposed development does not promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed’s natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways.

3.    Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the proposed development does not promote development that is consistent with the principles of ecologically sustainable development and to implement appropriate action on climate change

4.    Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the likely impacts of that development, including environmental impacts on both the natural and built environment, and social economic impacts on the locality.

5.    Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 in relation to site suitability the proposed development proposes filling of a site where it has not been demonstrated filling is required for this site.

6.    Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 in relation to site suitability, the proposed development does not satisfy the Objects of the Act s1.3(c) to promote the orderly and economic use and development of the land as it proposes filling of a site where it has not been demonstrated filling is required for this site. 

The Amendment 1 was Lost

VOTE AGAINST - Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

Cr Ron Cooper
Cr Katie Milne

PROPOSED that Council defers this item to:

VOTE AGAINST - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper

Cr Pryce Allsop
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 1 April 2021 be received and noted and

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1  Murwillumbah Cycle Club 2021 Season

That:

1.    A revised Traffic Management Plan that is in PDF format and legible, with the correct event dates be submitted to Council officers for support before the event commences and in compliance with the current COVID-19 requirements. 

2.    The proposed Murwillumbah Cycle Club Events from March to October 2021 be supported, subject to:

a.      NSW Police approval being obtained.
b.      Endorsement of the event by Cycling Queensland.
c.      Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
d.      Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
e.      The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
f.      Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.
g.     All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
h.     Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
i.      Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
j.     That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
k.    The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
l.    The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
m.  The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

6.2  Broadway Burringbar

That concept designs be developed for entry treatments to Broadway, Burringbar with the intention of applying to Transport for NSW for a high pedestrian activity zone for 40km/h speed limit and the designs be distributed for community consultation.

7.1 Wharf Street, Tweed Heads - Proposed bus zone removal adjacent the library

That the southbound and northbound bus zones in Wharf Street, Tweed Heads adjacent to the Tweed Library be removed and replaced with '2P-9am-5pm Mon-Fri and 9am-12pm Saturdays'.  

7.2  Terranora Road - Vehicle Activated Signs for Koalas

That to support the koala zone, the installation of two vehicle activated signs and pavement stenciling on Terranora Road on the section between Fraser Drive and Corkwood Road is supported subject to a site suitability assessment. 

7.3  Kirkwood Road, Tweed Heads South

That:

1.    The previous Recommendation from meeting held 8 October 2020 to install no stopping yellow edge lines and guide posts be on Kirkwood Road, Tweed Heads South, to prevent motorists parking to access Arkinstall Park is supported.  Signage to include a temporary "This is no longer a parking area, please use alternative sites".

2.    Lindisfarne School be advised accordingly.

7.4  Terranora Road 'No Stopping Zone'

That:

1.    A 'No Stopping' zone be installed on Terranora Road from 40m east of Shamara Road to 70m west of Shamara Road, to reinforce existing road rules that would prevent queuing through this section.

2.    The school be notified of the changes and the road safety issues associated with queuing on Terranora Road at least 2 weeks prior to implementation. .

7.5  Philip Street, Pottsville

That the Committee endorses the installation of a yellow edgeline between the last two driveways on Philip Street, Pottsville to improve the ability of large vehicles to turn around at the end of the street.

CONFIDENTIAL ITEM:

10.1  Proposed Event

See Confidential Minutes attached.

LATE ITEM:

11.1  Kellehers Road / Tweed Coast Road Intersection

That guide posts be installed on the west side of Tweed Coast Road 25m south of its intersection with Kellehers Road.


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

Cr Pryce Allsop
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

1.       The Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards Selection Panel (comprising all Councillors) and the current Awardees, consider Tweed Shire Australia Day Award nominations for the following categories:

•  Citizen of the Year
•  Arts and Culture
•  Volunteer of the Year (individual)
•  Volunteer of the Year (group)
•  Sporting Achievement (individual) 
•  Sporting Achievement (group)
•  Community Event of the Year 
•  Young Achiever in Community Service,

with the option to make an ‘Honourable Mention’ to a nominee who deserves recognition for their efforts.


2.       Council supports the changes to the nomination categories and the eligibility criteria for the Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards as outlined in the report.

3.       Council continues to support, from the Australia Day budget, applications for financial assistance from non-profit organisations and community groups for hosting small community Australia Day events for up to $300.

4.       Council notes that the awards and ceremony held in 2021 was funded by an existing budget of $9,721 and a one-off $20,000 grant due to COVID-19. 
 
5.      Council notes that the 2022 awards and ceremony will revert to the existing budget of $9.721, and the format as held in 2020, and elements of the 2021 ceremony such as videography and lunch packs which were only possible due to grant funding, will not fall within the scope of that budget.

6.      Council supports:

a)  Venue Option 1 - approach suitable venues in the Tweed Shire to apply for club grant opportunities and authorises the General Manager to evaluate the venues offering club grants and determine the venue to hold the 2021 Tweed Shire Australia Day Citizenship Ceremony a
b)  Venue Option 2 - hold the 2021 Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards and Citizenship Ceremony at the Murwillumbah or Tweed Heads Auditorium should the club grant applications not be successful.
c)  While Council’s preferred approach is a physical ceremony, if required by COVID-19 conditions, the General Manager may implement alternative options to deliver the ceremony in a COVIDSafe way.


7.     Council supports the rollover of funds from the 2020/2021 Australia Day events budget, as well as the 2020-2021 Civic Business - Civic Ceremonies budget.

8.     Council continues to explore gift ideas from local Aboriginal organisations/individuals for Award recipients.

9.    Council invites the 2021 Tweed Shire Australia Day Sporting Achievement winner, Gemma Eaton, to be the 2022 Tweed Shire Australia Day Ambassador.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd from Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church.

"Gracious God, 

We thank you for the hard work of Councillors and staff in preparation for tonight.  Please grant them wisdom and good outcomes in all their deliberations this evening.  

We pray for Council, and all tiers of government, as they work together to ensure that people are healthy, homed, educated, and employed, consistent with your character of justice and mercy.

As we approach the twentieth anniversary of National Reconciliation Week, we pray for Council’s work in taking action to achieve reconciliation locally.  We are deeply thankful for the people of the Bundjalung nation and other First Nations peoples in our community, and pray that they will see real progress towards true reconciliation.

We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen. "
