ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr Pryce Allsop

PROPOSED that, in the event that Council considers that the proposal is substantially the same, that the determination of Development Application DA06/0413.14 for an amendment to Development Consent DA06/0413 for a staged seniors living development under SEPP (HSPD) 2004 comprising 91 independent living units, 94 supported living units and 67 beds within a high care facility at Lot 1 DP 786570; No. 87-89 Tweed Coast Road HASTINGS POINT be deferred and the applicant afforded an opportunity to submit the outstanding information requested by Council officers.  


AMENDMENT 1

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Katie Milne

PROPOSED that:

A. Development Application DA06/0413.14 for an amendment to Development Consent DA06/0413 for a staged seniors living development under SEPP (HSPD) 2004 comprising 91 independent living units, 94 supported living units and 67 beds within a high care facility at Lot 1 DP 786570 No. 87-89 Tweed Coast Road, Hastings Point be refused for the following reasons: 

1. Pursuant to Section 4.55(2) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, Council is not it is satisfied that the development to which the modification relates is substantially the same development as the development for which consent was originally granted and before that consent as originally granted was modified, having regard to: 

(a) the proposed changes from three (3) distinct types of seniors living approved on the site and the reduction in the number of units/beds; 
(b) encroachment of the perimeter road and hardstand elements in the Cudgera Creek outer buffer and the potential environmental impacts associated with same; and
(c) increase in number of car parking spaces on site and associated increase in traffic movements.

2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal, which seeks to construct an access road and other impermeable structures within the Cudgera Creek outer buffer, and to extend the development footprint further west towards Cudgera Creek, is contrary to the aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014: 

(a) as set out in Clause 1.2(c) ‘to promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed’s natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways, visual amenity and scenic routes, built environment, and cultural heritage’.
(b) as set out in Clause 1.2(g) ‘to conserve or enhance the biological diversity, scenic quality and geological and ecological integrity of Tweed’.
(c) as set out in Clause 1.2(i) ‘to conserve or enhance areas of defined high ecological value.’
(d) as set out in Clause 1.2(j) ‘to provide special protection and suitable habitat for the recovery of the Tweed coastal Koala.’

3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal, which seeks to construct an access road and other impermeable structures within the buffer, and to extend the development footprint further west towards Cudgera Creek, is contrary to the aims of the State Environmental Planning Policy (Coastal Management) 2018 as set out in Clause 3(a) to manage development in the coastal zone and protect the environmental assets of the coast. 

Further, it is contrary to requirements in Clause 11(1)(a) of the SEPP, that development consent not be granted to development on land identified as “proximity area for coastal wetlands” or “proximity area for littoral rainforest” on the Coastal Wetlands and Littoral Rainforests Area Map unless the consent authority is satisfied that the proposed development will not significantly impact on  the biophysical, hydrological or ecological integrity of the adjacent coastal wetland or littoral rainforest. 

4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal, which seeks to include basement car parking is contrary to the objective of Clause 7.3(a) of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 ‘to minimise the flood risk to life and property associated with the use of land’.  

Further in accordance with Clause 7.3(3)(e), the consent authority is not satisfied that the development is not likely to result in unsustainable social and economic costs to the community as a consequence of flooding.

5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1) (b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal, which seeks to amend the development within the approved buffer, and is contrary to the objective of Clause 1.7 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act, as Council cannot be satisfied that the proposed modifications will not increase the impact on biodiversity values under s7.17 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016. In this regard the application has failed to satisfy Part 7 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016.

6. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the proposal, which seeks to amend the development within the approved buffer, and include additional basement car parking is contrary to the objective of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section B23 Hastings Point as set out in section 4.4.2.1:

(a) ‘to implement a continuous creek buffer, 
(b) ‘to ensure that the Cudgera Creek foreshore protects the integrity of the estuary ecology’.

7. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the proposal, involving repositioning of the development footprint further to the west of the approved building footprint fails to satisfy the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan Section A19 Biodiversity & Habitat Management, having regard to the relevant various environmental and ecological controls applicable to the subject site considered necessary to avoid and minimise cumulative direct and indirect impacts upon the adjacent Cudgera Creek and associated riparian habitat. 

8. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the applicant has not demonstrated to the satisfaction of the consent authority that the proposed basement car parking of the site will not negatively impact the adjacent wetlands. 

9. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the proposed development, is not considered to be in the public interest having regard to:

(a) the potential loss of public access to the Cudgera Creek foreshore; 
(b) the potential impact on the Cudgera Creek foreshore as a result of encroachment of roads and hardsurfaced areas in the Cudgera Creek outer buffer; 
(c) the reasonable expectations of residents/owners in Stage 1 of the development who understood that they were buying into a transitional seniors living development that would allow them to age in place.

B.     ATTACHMENTS 4 and 5 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

Amendment 1 was Lost

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

ALTERNATE MOTION 

 

Cr Katie Milne
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RECOMMENDED that:

1.    Council endorses the comments contained within this report and the draft submission in Attachment 1 of this report with the following points:
*   Due to the close proximity of highly populated areas a risk analysis and management plan should be provided to consider the potential for catastrophic failure for all risk scenarios, such as significant drain blockage, weir or bund failure that may suddenly redirect waters to sensitive populated areas.

*   Due to the close proximity of highly populated areas and important farmlands, worst case scenarios should be considered for joint probability analysis of combined events for all potential flooding and storm water impacts, including with stormtides, wind driven waves, meteotsunamis and seiches.

*   Potential impacts on the Chinderah village should be examined in detail in regard to increased velocities in this area, and for the potential of waters and / or debris being redirected towards the northern side of the Tweed River to the Oxley Cove residential areas.

*   Further investigation and assessment should be undertaken in regard to the impact of the proposal on the marine ecology of the Tweed estuary from increased flows, increased velocity, poor or contaminated water quality, including on any key fish habitats associated with the drainage system, Boyds channel and the significant Lillies Island seagrass beds that are downstream and are the largest seagrass bed in the Tweed River.

*  Due to the close proximity of highly populated areas a geotechnical analysis should be undertaken on the ability of the landscape to withstand such large scale changes in structural forces and in light of the ongoing erosion processes of the Tweed Caldera.

*  Analysis should be undertaken by a suitably qualified expert on the significance of the site for the Tweed in regard to the wider geological landscape and in light of the Tweed being identified as a National Iconic Landscape, and any potential geological attributes that may be affected including ecosystem services.

*  As the water bodies and surrounding environment will require ongoing management at the end of life of the sand quarry operation that consideration be given to applying a royalty or some other form of arrangement to fund this work in perpetuity, if approved; and

2. The endorsed submission be forwarded to the Department of Planning, Industry and Environment with regard to the proposed Hanson Tweed Sand Plant Expansion – State Significant Development (SSD-10398).
 
The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

Cr Ron Cooper
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RECOMMENDED that Council endorse the following revised practices of the call up of applications for determination at a Council or Planning Committee Meeting, within Council’s current adopted delegations to Council officers:

1. For all Development Applications and Modifications with a building cost estimate between $1 Million and $10 Million, the Director Planning and Regulation will send a standard format email to all Councillors at the end of the officers’ assessment of these applications, containing the following:

  • a summary of the main elements and description of the proposal;
  • identification of any significant variations to Council’s Development Control Plan (DCP) controls (noting that any variations to Local Environmental Plan development standards greater than 10% are required to be reported to Council);
  • the number and key issues of any public submissions received; and
  • an indication of whether the officers are recommending approval/refusal.

2. Councillors will be provided with 5 business days to provide written advice to the Director Planning and Regulation as to whether they wish to call up these applications for Council determination;

3. Councillors can ask for clarification of any technical requirements for these applications, but it is not intended for Councillors to be engaging with the officers on any debate on the merits of the application, or negotiating any conditions of consent to influence a decision not to call up an application for Council determination;

4. The Councillors shall provide their reasons for the call up, so that these can be relayed to the proponents or any other interested parties;

5. In accordance with the current Code of Meeting Practice, any request for call up of an application, must be made by at least two Councillors; 

6. If no request is received, the officers will proceed to determine the DA under delegated authority;

7. The same Code of Meeting Practice call up provision is still available to any development application lodged with Council; and

8. When a Development Application or Modification Application is determined under Delegated Authority, internal Assessment Reports underpinning such determinations will be made available to Councillors on individual request.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 6 May 2021 be received and noted and

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1  Tweed Valley Triathletes Season 2021/22

That the proposed Tweed Valley Triathletes Season from 18 September 2021 to 19 March 2022 be supported, subject to current COVID-19 restrictions at the time of the event and the following conditions:

1.   NSW Police approval being obtained.
2.   Endorsement of the event by Triathlon Australian and Triathlon NSW.
3.   Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
4.   Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
5.   The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
6.   Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.
7.   All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
8.   Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
9.   Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
10. That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
11. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
12. The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
13. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

7.2  Overall Drive, Pottsville

That:

1.  A length of double centre line be installed on Overall Drive, Pottsville on the curve between numbers 201 and 211.

2.  50km/h repeater signs be installed on Overall Drive, Pottsville.

3.  A No Through Road sign be placed on Overall Drive, Pottsville near the roundabout at Kellehers Road, Pottsville.

4.  That Council's advisory radar to be placed on Overall Drive, Pottsville (south of Kellehers Road) when available.

7.3  Dulguigan Road / Hogans Road intersection

That a Stop sign and associated linemarking is not supported on Hogans Road at the Dulguigan Road, Dulguigan intersection as sight distance is available.  Minor trimming of trees should be considered which would further improve sight distance.  

The Motion was Carried

RESOLVED that the Minutes of the Tweed Coast and Waterways Committee Meeting held Wednesday 14 April 2021 be received and noted and the following be included in the minutes to be endorsed by Council:
A3. Ecological Impact of Proposed Fishing Competition

1.     That Council notes the potential ecological impacts of the proposed recreational fishing competition could include:

  • waste & litter
  • sea bird entanglement and injury
  • fish mortality
  • pressure on boating facilities
  • that while the event is promoted as catch and release, there may be no practical means of ensuring that this occurs.

2.     The Tweed Coast and Waterways Committee recommends that Council does not allocate sponsorship funding to the proposed recreational fishing competition.

3.     That Council notes that the Tweed Coast Waterways Committee does not support the proposed recreational fishing competition.

The Motion was Carried

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins from the Murwillumbah Church of Christ.

"Dear Father,
I ask You to be present tonight as Council meets together. We know this is not always an easy task, but may You to watch & direct over all that needs to be discussed.
Father, may You give Your help, support & strength for all those here, that the outcomes will be as You want them to be.
I pray that You may grant what is best for the Tweed Shire Council – that the shire will be blessed – people may be kept safe & provided for and that Your plans be fulfilled.
We thank You for Your many blessings. Your goodness is new every day, with opportunities that allow us to fulfil what You have called us to do. 
Father, I pray for all our councillors. Put aside their distractions of the day and focus their minds and hearts upon the work that is before them.
Bless our Mayor Chris Cherry as it is You who appointed her to this position. Father, I pray that You will enlighten her mind with all wisdom, that she may lead and watch over the Tweed Shire Council with virtue and uprightness.
Father I give thanks tonight and may Your blessing be upon Council for every good gift and every perfect gift is from You. 
May You answer us in the day we call.
Amen"

Cr Katie Milne
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:

1.     Adopts the draft Cool Towns – Tweed Shire Urban Forest Program and incorporates actions into existing operations with the following highlighted amendments to Section 4.4 of the Program:

4.4 Planning and regulation review
Council will revise controls within the existing legislative framework focused on the expansion of healthy tree canopy and biophillic plantings within urban areas to maximise the environmental, economic, social and public health benefits of locally appropriate native trees and multi-strata vegetation in urban areas to both present and future generations.

The review will include:

  • Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 with regard to:

– vegetation removal controls and permit requirements to protect existing trees
– landscaping and streetscaping controls and specifications within residential, commercial and subdivision developments to ensure future developments provide for local native urban mature trees and biophillic plantings.

  • Council protocols and procedures regarding Council works to ensure operations across Council are in alignment
    with the objectives of this program.
  • Council policy regarding regulation and compliance of vegetation vandalism or unauthorised removal.
  • State, regional and other local planning documents to ensure best practice is undertaken and all opportunities for
    funding are pursued.


2.     Consider an annual recurring allocation of $120,000 in future budget deliberations to deliver the program.

3.     In accordance with Section 160 of the Local Government Act 1993, the draft Road Reserve Vegetation in Urban Areas Policy be placed on public exhibition for a period of 28 days, with submissions being received for a period of 42 days.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins:

"Dear Father,

I thank You for this opportunity that we can come together despite the many obstacles & challenges we are facing at the moment. 

May we use this time wisely, being reminded of the responsibility we have been given to do. Father, help us to put aside any distractions, weariness & anxiety we may be feeling to focus on the task before us. 

Father, I pray that You will give strength, wisdom & insight to all here tonight. Our Mayor, Counsellors & the Tweed people. 

I thank You that You give power when we are weak and strength when we are powerless. We know that if we lack wisdom, we can come to You, who gives generously without finding fault, and it will be given to us. 

Father, You are our unseen Guest tonight, silently listening in all that will be said & done. May everyone be heard and no-one misunderstood.  That all will be treated mindfully and with respect.

So, Father, continue to help and guide us, that we may live to practice the values we know to be true. That Council be transparent in all its dealings tonight. Treating the people of the Tweed with fairness, commitment, planning for their future…with everyone involved:

So that our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.

May You answer us in the day we call.

Amen"

Cr Katie Milne

RECOMMENDED that:


A. Development Application DA20/0530 for a five lot subdivision and road reserve at Lot 832 DP 1144994 No. 2-4 Watego Drive, Pottsville be refused for the following reasons:

1. The application has not satisfied Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 and the requirements of Clause 1.2 Aims of the Plan, in that the proposal does not give effect to Sections B15 and B21 of the Tweed Shire Council Development Control Plan 2008, contrary to aim (a) of this clause - EPA Act s4.15 (1)(a)(i).

2. The application has not satisfied Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 and the requirements of Clause 2.3 Zone Objectives and Land Use Table, in that the proposal will undermine the ability of the site to provide a range of small scale retail, business and community uses contrary to the objectives of the B1 Neighbourhood Centre zone - EPA Act  s4.15 (1)(a)(i).

3. The application has not satisfied Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 and the requirements of Clause 7.10 Essential Services, in that the proposed location of Council sewer infrastructure is not in accordance with Council’s Development Design Specification D12 or Standard Drawing SD006 - EPA Act s4.15 (1)(a)(i).

4. The application has not satisfied the requirements of Tweed Shire Council Development Control Plan (DCP) 2008 Section A5 - Subdivision Manual with respect to the proposed dedicated laneway and the absence of the provision of public benefit by way of a much needed thoroughfare or provision of services; and the absence of a reciprocal Right of Way - EPA Act s4.15 (1)(a)(iii).

5. The application has not satisfied the intent, objectives and requirements of Tweed Shire Council Development Control Plan (DCP) 2008 Section B15  - Seabreeze Estate, with respect to the proposed fragmentation of the site and the resulting undermining of the site’s potential to provide for future local, retail, commercial and civic uses across the site, and its ability to meet the day to day neighbourhood service needs of the Seabreeze Estate - EPA Act s4.15 (1)(a)(iii).

6. The application is contrary the intent, objectives and requirements of Tweed Shire Council Development Control Plan (DCP) 2008 Section B15  - Seabreeze Estate in that the fragmentation of the site will not result in an appropriate overall integrated and cohesive development - EPA Act s4.15 (1)(a)(iii).

7. The application is contrary to the intent, objectives and requirements of Tweed Shire Council Development Control Plan (DCP) 2008 Section B15 - Seabreeze Estate with respect to the proposed laneway and the resulting reduction in the potential developable area and the resulting reduction in potential for an appropriately integrate and cohesive development - EPA Act s4.15 (1)(a)(iii).

8. The application is contrary to the intent, objectives and requirements of Tweed Shire Council Development Control Plan (DCP) 2008 Section B21  -  Pottsville Locality Based Development Code, in that the fragmentation of the site will not result in an appropriately integrated and cohesive development - EPA Act s4.15 (1)(a)(iii).

9. The application has not demonstrated the suitability of the site for development in the manner proposed - EPA Act s4.15 (1) (c).

10. The application is contrary to the requirements of Tweed Shire Council Development Control Plan (DCP) 2008 Section A5 Subdivision Manual, in that the proposed public road reserve does not comply with Design Specification D1- Road Design – Section D.17, 7(d) - EPA Act s4.15 (1)(a)(iii).

11. The application does not promote the orderly and economic use and development of the site - EPA Act s1.3(c).

12. The application is not in the public interest because of the range and extent of issues identified – EPA Act s4.15 (1) (e).

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Katie Milne

RECOMMENDED that:

A. Development Application DA19/0562.03 for an amendment to Development Consent DA19/0562 for alterations and additions to an attached dual occupancy in two (2) stages, including construction of carports, reconstruction of ground floor balcony, construction of first floor balcony and use of converted garages and subfloor area at Lot 17 DP 28471 No. 4 Anthony Avenue, Banora Point be approved subject to the consent being amended as follows:

1. Delete Condition No. 1 and replace it with Condition No. 1A which reads as follows:

1A.   A consolidated set of amended plans are to be submitted for the approval of the General Manager or his delegate demonstrating the following: 

a)       The proposed ground floor level and first floor level balconies of both units are to be set back a minimum of 3m from the rear boundary; 
 
b)       The proposed ground floor level balconies of both units are to be enclosed by opaque balustrades (minimum 1m high) on the external side elevations;
 
c)        The proposed first floor level balconies of both units are to be enclosed by opaque balustrades (minimum 0.5m high) on the external side elevations;
 
d)       The proposed ground floor level and first floor level balconies of both units are to be fitted with a privacy screen for the length of the external side elevations.

The privacy screen should be designed to provide adequate privacy between the subject property and adjoining properties and incorporate the following: 

i.        has no individual opening more than 30mm wide, and 
ii.       has a total area of all openings that is no more than 30% of the surface area of the screen or barrier, and
iii.      with a height between 1.7m and 2.2m.

e)      Provision of a bathroom (shower/handbasin/WC) on the lower ground floor of one (1) unit only - only one (1) sink is to be included in the other unit; and
 
f)       Details of the colorbond fencing as constructed to be shown.

RECOMMENDED that:

A. Development Application DA19/0346 for alterations and additions to an existing water bottling facility at Lot 1 DP 883113 & Lot 2 DP 883113 No. 2574 Kyogle Road, Kunghur be refused for the following reasons:

1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 1.2 Aims of the Plan section a), b), c), d), e), f), g), and i) in that it has not been adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling is a sustainable use of this resource, or that it will not have an adverse impact on natural water systems or the potential agricultural use of the land, the environment, or other groundwater or surface users.

2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 2.3 RU2 Zone Objectives in that it has not been adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling is a sustainable use of this resource, or that it will not have an adverse impact on the environment, agricultural uses, or other groundwater or surface users, or that it maintains the rural landscape character of the land.

3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 7.7 Drinking Water Catchments in that it has not been adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling will not have an adverse impact on the quality of drinking water storage. 

4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 7.15 Water Bottling Facility in that it has not been adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling will not have an adverse impact on natural water systems or the potential agricultural use of the land in regard to the sustainable use of this resource.

5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 the application has not satisfied SEPP (Primary Production and Rural Development) 2019 in regard to the Aims of the Policy in that it has not been adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling is a sustainable use of this resource, or that it will not impact on the environment, agricultural uses, or other groundwater or surface users.

6. Pursuant Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 in regard to the Objects of the Act parts a), b), c), or e) in that it has not been adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling is a sustainable use of this resource, or that it will not impact on the environment, agricultural uses, or other groundwater or surface users.

7. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 the application has not adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling will not impact on the environment, agricultural uses, or other groundwater or surface users, and that the rural character and amenity of the area will not be adversely affected.

8. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 in regard to Suitability of the Site - the application has not adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling is a sustainable use of this resource, or that it will not impact on the environment, or other groundwater or surface users, and that the rural character and amenity of the area will not be adversely affected.

9. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(d) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 there have been numerous submissions made in regard to the application that the application has not adequately established that the commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling is a sustainable use of this resource, or that it will not impact on the environment, agricultural uses, or other groundwater or surface users, and that the rural character and amenity of the area will not be adversely affected.

10. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 in terms of public interest, the application has not adequately established that the additional commercial extraction of groundwater for water bottling is a sustainable use of this resource, or that it will not impact on the environment, agricultural uses, or other groundwater or surface users, and that the rural character and amenity of the area will not be adversely affected.

B. (i) Council allocates $50,000 to resource an investigation into allegations that the existing water extraction and bottling activity is not operating in accordance with the relevant existing approvals, and

(ii) If the investigation reveals that relevant approvals are being breached or have been breached then appropriate regulatory action is to be undertaken in accordance with advice from Council's solicitors.

C. ATTACHMENTS 5-15 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

Cr Pryce Allsop
Cr Warren Polglase

PROPOSED that:

2. Council defers investigation of alleged non compliance with existing development consents until determination or withdrawal of DA19/0346.

3.     This further information be provided within 60 days and is subject to obtaining feedback from the Department of Primary Industries.

RECOMMENDED that:

A. Development Application DA06/0413.14 for an amendment to Development Consent DA06/0413 for a staged seniors living development under SEPP (HSPD) 2004 comprising 91 independent living units, 94 supported living units and 67 beds within a high care facility at Lot 1 DP 786570 No. 87-89 Tweed Coast Road, Hastings Point be refused for the following reasons: 

1. Pursuant to Section 4.55(2) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, Council is not it is satisfied that the development to which the modification relates is substantially the same development as the development for which consent was originally granted and before that consent as originally granted was modified, having regard to: 

(a) the proposed changes from three (3) distinct types of seniors living approved on the site and the reduction in the number of units/beds; 
(b) encroachment of the perimeter road and hardstand elements in the Cudgera Creek outer buffer and the potential environmental impacts associated with same; and
(c) increase in number of car parking spaces on site and associated increase in traffic movements.

2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal, which seeks to construct an access road and other impermeable structures within the Cudgera Creek outer buffer, and to extend the development footprint further west towards Cudgera Creek, is contrary to the aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014: 

(a) as set out in Clause 1.2(c) ‘to promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed’s natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways, visual amenity and scenic routes, built environment, and cultural heritage’.
(b) as set out in Clause 1.2(g) ‘to conserve or enhance the biological diversity, scenic quality and geological and ecological integrity of Tweed’.
(c) as set out in Clause 1.2(i) ‘to conserve or enhance areas of defined high ecological value.’
(d) as set out in Clause 1.2(j) ‘to provide special protection and suitable habitat for the recovery of the Tweed coastal Koala.’

3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal, which seeks to construct an access road and other impermeable structures within the buffer, and to extend the development footprint further west towards Cudgera Creek, is contrary to the aims of the State Environmental Planning Policy (Coastal Management) 2018 as set out in Clause 3(a) to manage development in the coastal zone and protect the environmental assets of the coast. 

Further, it is contrary to requirements in Clause 11(1)(a) of the SEPP, that development consent not be granted to development on land identified as “proximity area for coastal wetlands” or “proximity area for littoral rainforest” on the Coastal Wetlands and Littoral Rainforests Area Map unless the consent authority is satisfied that the proposed development will not significantly impact on  the biophysical, hydrological or ecological integrity of the adjacent coastal wetland or littoral rainforest. 

4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal, which seeks to include basement car parking is contrary to the objective of Clause 7.3(a) of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 ‘to minimise the flood risk to life and property associated with the use of land’.  

Further in accordance with Clause 7.3(3)(e), the consent authority is not satisfied that the development is not likely to result in unsustainable social and economic costs to the community as a consequence of flooding.

5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1) (b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal, which seeks to amend the development within the approved buffer, and is contrary to the objective of Clause 1.7 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act, as Council cannot be satisfied that the proposed modifications will not increase the impact on biodiversity values under s7.17 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016. In this regard the application has failed to satisfy Part 7 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016.

6. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the proposal, which seeks to amend the development within the approved buffer, and include additional basement car parking is contrary to the objective of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section B23 Hastings Point as set out in section 4.4.2.1:

(a) ‘to implement a continuous creek buffer, 
(b) ‘to ensure that the Cudgera Creek foreshore protects the integrity of the estuary ecology’.

7. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the proposal, involving repositioning of the development footprint further to the west of the approved building footprint fails to satisfy the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan Section A19 Biodiversity & Habitat Management, having regard to the relevant various environmental and ecological controls applicable to the subject site considered necessary to avoid and minimise cumulative direct and indirect impacts upon the adjacent Cudgera Creek and associated riparian habitat. 

8. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the applicant has not demonstrated to the satisfaction of the consent authority that the proposed basement car parking of the site will not negatively impact the adjacent wetlands. 

9. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the proposed development, is not considered to be in the public interest having regard to:

(a) the potential loss of public access to the Cudgera Creek foreshore;

Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)
Cr James Owen

PROPOSED that Council, in respect of the alleged unauthorised works relating to the premises, No. 217 Sleepy Hollow Road, Sleepy Hollow (Lot 1 DP 740293):

1. Engages Council’s Solicitors to commence Class 4 proceedings in the NSW Land and Environment Court seeking orders and costs (if successful) to have the unauthorised dwelling demolished; and

2. Engages Councils Solicitors to assist with obtaining a warrant to undertake an inspection of the alleged unauthorised building works to determine what further action is necessary, if any.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RECOMMENDED that Council engages Council’s Solicitors to assist with obtaining a warrant to undertake an inspection of the alleged unauthorised building works to determine what further action is necessary, if any.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 3 June 2021 be received and noted and

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1 Murwillumbah Street, Murwillumbah - Loading Zone

The request to modify the existing "No Parking 8:30am - 6:00pm Mon - Fri, 8:30am - 12:30pm Sat" zone on Murwillumbah Street, Murwillumbah adjacent to the Tweed Fruit Exchange to "Loading Zone 8:30am - 6:00pm Mon - Fri, 8:30am - 12:30pm Sat".
 
6.3 Battle on the Border, Tweed Valley: 6 - 8 August 2021

That the proposed Battle on the Border, Tweed Valley on 6 - 8 August 2021 be supported subject to standard conditions of approval and current COVID-19 restrictions at the time of the event.

1.   That the residents and businesses directly affected by the Sunday criterion and time trial be consulted with by the Event Organiser and their responses assessed. If there is not general support for the event the criterion and/or time trial should be relocated to the routes used in most recent years- the Lundberg Circuit for the criterion and the Tumbulgum/Racecourse Road for the time trial.

2.   NSW Police approval being obtained.

3.   Endorsement of the event by Cycling Queensland.

4.   Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.

5.   Community and affected business consultation (including the Murwillumbah Business District Chamber) addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.

6.   The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.

7.   Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.

8.   All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.

9.   Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.

10.  Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.

11.  That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.

12.  The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.

13.  The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.

14.  A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.

15.  The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
 
7.1 Durigan Place, Banora Point

That a section of yellow 'no stopping' line be installed at the end of the cul-de-sac between the driveways of numbers 31 and 36 Durigan Place, Banora Point.

That Council's Road Safety Officer prepare  information about safe practices in Durigan Place, Banora Point for the school to communicate to parents.

That a footpath be installed from the school's back entrance to the stairs that connect to Cominan Street, Banora Point subject to funding.
 
7.2 Blue Horizon Drive, Casuarina

That the double centre line on Blue Horizon Drive at the intersection of Casuarina Way, Casuarina, be extended by 16m and the adjacent residents be advised of the road rule in relation to parking within 3m of an unbroken line.
 
7.3 Accessible Parking Space, Fingal Beach

That an accessible parking space be installed in the first angled parking space adjacent the Surf Club in Marine Parade, Fingal Beach.
 
7.4 Cycle for Life, Salt Village, Sunday 1 August 2021

That the proposed Cycle for Life event on Sunday 1 August 2021 be supported, subject to current COVID-19 restrictions at the time of the event:

1.      NSW Police approval being obtained.

2.      Endorsement of the event by Cycling Queensland or NSW.

3.      Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.

4.      Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.

5.      The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.

6.      Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.

7.      All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.

8.      Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.

9.      Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.

10.    That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.

11.    The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.

12.    The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.

13.    A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.

14.    The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

RESOLVED that:


1. The Minutes of the Tweed Coast Koala Management Committee Meeting held Tuesday 11 May 2021 be received and noted; and

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

BA3. Preparation of a map of paper roads on the Tweed Coast

That the Road Closures and Private Purchase Policy be reviewed and amended if required to consider environmental values and the potential use of these lands for wildlife habitat.  Further, that an analysis of the existing paper roads and other vacant crown land be undertaken to identify opportunities for habitat improvement. 

A2. Council resolution of Thursday 18th March regarding NSW Koala SEPP 2021

1. That the committee notes that DCPA19 needs to be updated in response to the introduction of NSW Koala SEPP 2021 due to the need to address references to the superseded SEPP 44 and the adoption of the Tweed Coast KPOM.

2. That the Chair follows up on behalf of the committee seeking to ensure the requested meetings occur as a matter of urgency.

3. That the Chair write on behalf of the committee to Team Koala thanking the members for their efforts in advocating for better protections for the Tweed Coast koalas.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Paster Chris Jenkins.


"Let’s us pray
Father, I thank You for knowing that You are here amongst us. You are our unseen Guest, silently listening & watching in all that will be said & done.
You are our good & mighty Councillor whose ways are good & right. I pray that You, will provide guidance for our mayor & every councillor here tonight, that they also may have in mind to do what is good & right. 
I pray that You will give each one of them wisdom, discernment & humility. Help them know what needs to be discussed & accomplished as they provide & protect over the Tweed Shire. 
I pray that every councillor gives careful consideration & attention to those they have been given charge over, and that the relationship between Council & the people of the Tweed will continue to grow in trust & respect. 
Father, I would also like to pray in appreciation of each one of our councillors, for the service they provide and the accountability each of them carries.  It is not an easy task, especially with all that we are facing at the moment. May You continue to provide and protect over each of our council members, their families & their loved ones in these days. 
So Father, continue to help and guide us, that we may live to practice the values we know to be true. That Council be transparent in all its dealings tonight. Treating the people of the Tweed with fairness, commitment, planning for their future…with everyone involved:
So that our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.
May You answer us in the day we call…
Amen"

RESOLVED that Council, in respect to Contract RFO2020100 Barry Sheppard Oval Amenities Building:

Cr Katie Milne

RESOLVED that:

1. Council amends the Code of Meeting Practice to establish livestreaming as its formal means of webcast by amending clause 5.19A to read as follows: 

“5.19A  For the purposes of clause 5.18, a webcast will comprise an audio and visual or audio livestream of the meeting, with audio recording or an audio and visual recording of the meeting to be uploaded on Council’s website on the next business day following the meeting (note if technical challenges occur the upload will occur as soon as practicable after the meeting).  If due to technical challenges, a livestream is not possible, a webcast will comprise an audio recording or an audio and visual recording of the meeting to be uploaded on Council’s website on the next business day following the meeting.” 

2. The amended Code of Meeting Practice be placed on public exhibition for 28 days with submission to be received for 42 days.

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr Pryce Allsop

PROPOSED that Council, in respect land described as Lot 11 DP 125420830, 30 Fraser Drive, Tweed Heads South:

1. Supports the Section 82 application and allows the manufactured homes to be erected progressively within the manufactured home estate subject to the following:

a) Council informs the applicant that sites 39, 40 and 85 to 96 are not supported to be built on-site;
b) On completion of civil works, Council issues the Section 68 Approval to Operate and include a condition excluding sites 39, 40 and 85 to 96 from being built on-site;
c) The appeal and Council resolution are forwarded to the Department of Planning, Industry and Environment for concurrence of the Departmental Chief Executive, in accordance with Section 82(3) of the Local Government Act 1993.


AMENDMENT 1

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Katie Milne

PROPOSED that Council refuses the objection and requires the manufactured homes to be constructed off site and transported to the manufactured home estate as this is what is required by law and the variation is not sufficiently justified.

Amendment 1 was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil


AMENDMENT 2

Cr Pryce Allsop
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

1. Council defers this item and seeks further advice on the justification to build on-site including but not limited to comparative analysis for on-site/off-site build in regards to the following issues:

a. The size of the trucks that would be used for the manufactured homes?
b. Would a crane be required?
c. Where the manufactured homes may be purchased and supplied from?
d. If built on-site would homes be built on one location and moved to independent sites?
e. The number of vehicle movements for built on or built off locations? 
f. If employment for construction would be sourced locally. 
g. The estimated time for on-site construction. 

2. This matter be brought back to the 5 August 2021 Council meeting. 


Amendment 2 was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Ron Cooper
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

Cr Katie Milne
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

1.   The Minutes of the Floodplain Management Committee Meeting held 4 June 2021 be received and noted; and

2.   The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

4. Early Warning Network General Tweed Warning Service

That Council Officers further investigate, and if appropriate implement, provision of a General Tweed Warning Service to improve the dissemination of Bureau of Meteorology warnings in the community.

5. Gales Kingscliff Masterplan

That Council notes the concerns of the Floodplain Management Committee in relation to the proposals for urban land release and widescale filling of the floodplain in West Kingscliff due to the following issues:

  • Impacts on existing urban and rural areas upstream and downstream of West Kingscliff
  • Limitations on the capacity to upgrade drainage systems to offset the loss of floodplain storage
  • The impacts of drainage upgrades on Chinderah, including adjoining residents and the environment
  • The ability to maintain drainage and flood mitigation systems in perpetuity, where they pass through environmental areas, and
  • The ongoing flood risk to residents of the future subdivisions.

8. Flood Prone Land Package

That Council advises the Department of Planning Industry and Environment that it will opt in to the “Special Flood Considerations” Clause in the Local Environmental Plan.
That a detailed report be provided to Council outlining the content of the Flood Prone Land Package and the implications for Council’s floodplain management approach and planning instruments. 

10. Mooball Designated Flood Level

The process commence to amend Development Control Plan Section A3 - Development of Flood Liable Land to apply a Designated Flood Level to Mooball Village that is consistent with other “Area Behind Levee” approaches.

11. Flood Mounds

Council provides in-principle support for “flood mounds” (fill pads) on rural agricultural properties, subject to DCP and LEP permissibility advice available from Council Staff, to minimise agricultural losses from future floods.

15. Post 2017 Flood Efforts

The Committee extends their congratulations to Council and Council staff on the various flood mitigation initiatives and actions since the March 2017 flood disaster.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Cr Katie Milne
Cr Ron Cooper

RESOLVED that Council:

1. Notes the potential for major flooding and dangerous flash flooding in the Tweed Shire with these risks expected to become more severe with climate change.

2. Notes the analysis done by the award winning organisation ‘Climate Risk’ highlighting that many more addresses in the Tweed Shire may become uninsurable in the future, and the implications this may have for the community and Council if homes or whole areas have to be abandoned:

2050

2100

Tweed Heads South

21.5%

36.9%

Tweed Heads West

25.7%

47.9%

Chinderah

25.7%

44.3%

Kingscliff

10.3%

18.7%
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2019-10-23/the-suburbs-facing-rising-insurance-costs-from-climate-risk/11624108?nw=0#suburbsearch

3. Notes that our current planning controls for new greenfield developments require flood planning levels to accommodate the 1% ARI flood with a 10% increased rainfall intensity for climate change and a 500mm freeboard, and consideration of evacuation routes for floods up to the probable maximum flood, but that 0.2% ARI floods (1 in 500 chance) have already been experienced in this Shire and other areas around Australia, so that while our controls aim to protect life, they only protect property to a limited extent, and in fact will make some other areas more flood prone. 

4. Notes the intense and long term emotional and financial trauma that floods cause to our community and to Council.

5. Notes the planning consideration for the Hawkesbury/Nepean area that at least requires not only evacuation routes but also analysis of the capacity of the road network to evacuate the community within the time required to escape rising flood waters. 

6. Seeks urgent advice from the NSW Minister for Planning, the State Emergency Service, Council’s insurers and Council’s Flood Plain Committee in regard to whether new developments should still be allowed in Tweed’s floodplain considering Tweed is also classified as a high risk area with flash flooding, and if so, how these risks can be better mitigated.

7. Highlights these concerns to the Northern Region Planning Panel for their consideration. 

8. Brings back a report to the Floodplain Management Committee and subsequently to Council, on potential options to further mitigate the risks for life and property for existing and new development for the Tweed Shire, including but not limited to, consideration of limiting or restricting new development in the floodplain, undertaking analysis to ensure evacuation can be achieved in a timely manner, increasing the Flood Planning Levels for new developments, requiring the use of flood resilient buildings materials, mezzanines and roof refuges, planned retreat, maximizing pervious surfaces such as sand as fill material, and providing further information on floods greater than the 1% ARI such as the 1 in 200, 1 in 500 and 1 in 2,000 chance floods.

9. Includes in the report advice on at what stage in the future areas of the Tweed may become nonviable due to increased risk and how Council can manage such abandoned infrastructure.

The Motion was Carried on the Casting Vote of the Mayor.

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

Councillor Reece Byrnes joined the meeting at 6.34 pm.

Cr Katie Milne
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

1. Council notes the 2017 United Nations Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons is the first treaty to comprehensively outlaw nuclear weapons and provide a pathway for their elimination.  This Treaty entered into force on 22 January 2021. All national governments are invited to sign and ratify the treaty but Australia is yet to become a party to this treaty.

2.  Notes the Australian Local Government Association National General Assembly 2021 a resolution was unanimously passed by all 537 Councils of Australia to support the treaty and call on the Government to become a signatory to the Treaty.

3.  Entry into force is an important milestone on the path to a nuclear weapon free world.  It makes concrete the standard that nuclear weapons are illegal and illegitimate for all states, and a permanent part of international law.

4.  To commemorate this UN achievement of global diplomacy, our council endorses the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons ‘Cities Appeal’, which reads:

"Our city/town is deeply concerned about the grave threat that nuclear weapons pose to communities throughout the world. We firmly believe that our residents have the right to live in a world free from this threat. Any use of nuclear weapons, whether deliberate or accidental, would have catastrophic, far-reaching and long-lasting consequences for people and the environment."

5. The Mayor writes to the Federal Government and local Federal Member requesting they join the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons without delay.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd, Presbyterian Church.

"Gracious God,

We acknowledge our own grief and the grief in our community over plans changed, border closures, lockdowns, and the increased danger of COVID. Please give wisdom to state governments and their Health ministers, and grace to us all as we respond to these challenges. We pray especially for vulnerable people in lockdown and for those isolated from family, friends, and the community.

We pray for Councillors and Council candidates in yet another deferred election. Thank you for Councillors willing to extend their service, and please give them endurance and strength as they continue to work on behalf of our community. Be with staff as they adjust to the changes, and we pray for a return to normality before the elections.

Grant peace and satisfaction in their work to everyone involved in tonight’s meeting.

We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen. "

Cr Warren Polglase

RECOMMENDED that:

A. Development Application DA20/0466 for a staged development comprising of multi dwelling housing (37 townhouses), 11 swimming pools, 33 lot community title subdivision, and associated works at Lot 169 DP 1075495 & Lot 930 DP 1079118 No. 4-8 Bells Boulevard, Kingscliff be approved by way of deferred commencement subject to the conditions attached to the report for this item and as amended below:

1. Update the description of works as follows:

Development Application DA20/0466 - staged development comprising of multi dwelling housing (37 townhouses), 11 swimming pools, 33 lot community title subdivision, and associated works at Lot 169 DP 1075495 & Lot 930 DP 1079118; No. 4-8 Bells Boulevard Kingscliff

2. Update Condition A to state the following:

A. A consolidated set of amended plans are to be submitted for the approval of the General Manager or his delegate demonstrating the following:

Setbacks
(a) A front building line of no less than 6m to Gunnamatta Avenue for dwellings on Lots 6-13;
(b) A setback of no less than 4.1m to Gunnamatta Avenue for Lot 14;
(c) A front building line of no less than 5.27m to Barrel Street for dwellings on Lots 1-5;
(d) A setback of no less than 3m to Barrel Street for dwelling on Lots 6 and 32;

Fencing
(a) Front fencing to Gunnamatta Avenue and Barrel Street to a maximum height of 1.5m high with a maximum solid fence height of 600mm, above the solid wall the fence is to have a min. openness ratio of 60%.
(b) No pools in the setback to Lots 1-13, or Lot 32;
(c) Fencing details for Lots 4-7 (prior to and during any use for car parking);

Building Design
(a) A mixture of dwelling designs throughout the development scheme, in particular on street facing lots by incorporating different external material and roof typologies;
(b) Gable roofs to be provided for dwellings on on Lots 3, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 19, 21, 32;
(c) Detached dwellings to be provided on Lots 1 and 5;
(d) The floor plans for dwelling types D1, D4 and D6 are to be amended so that the study is not enclosed and cannot be adapted for use as a second bedroom;

Staging
(a) Staging Plan for discrete stages that includes road construction and civil works, dwelling construction and associated community title subdivision for each stage;

Draft Community Management Statement
(a) Draft Community Management Statement.

3. Update Condition 14 to state the following:

14. The developer shall provide 78 parking spaces including nine (9) visitor parking spaces and parking for the disabled (as required) in accordance with Tweed Shire Council Development Control Plan Part A2 - Site Access and Parking Code.
Full design detail of the proposed parking and manoeuvring areas including integrated landscaping shall be submitted to the Certifier (Council or a Registered Certifier) with the Construction Certificate for Building/Subdivision Works.

4. Update Condition 17 to state the following:

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:


1. Approves the establishment and timeframes of alcohol-free zones in accordance with Section 644B of the Local Government Act 1993, within Tweed Heads, Tweed Heads South, Kingscliff, Salt, Cabarita Beach, and Murwillumbah areas over roads, footpaths, and public carparks  for a maximum period of four years commencing 2 December 2021 and expiring no later than 1 December 2025 as outlined in Alcohol Free Zones within Tweed Shire (2021- 2025): and as follows;

 

Tweed Heads (24 hours per day, all days)

  • Boundary Street between Wharf Street and Coral Street;
  •  Public car park adjoining Twin Towns Services Club;
  • Wharf Street between Kennedy Drive and the Queensland border;
  • Bay Street, east of Wharf Street to John Follent Park;
  • Chris Cunningham Park public carpark; 
  • River Terrace;
  • Terranora Terrace and
  • Razorback Road carpark between water tower and lookout area.

Tweed Heads South (24 hours per day, all days)

  • Public car park adjoining Tweed Regional Aquatic Centre (TRAC) Tweed Heads South, Home and Community Care (HACC), and South Tweed Skate Park

Kingscliff  (24 hours per day, all days)

  • Cudgen Creek Carpark, between Casuarina Way and Cudgen Creek.
  •  Marine Parade between Turnock Street and Cudgen Creek;
  • Turnock Street between Marine Parade and Pearl Street;
  • Pearl Street between Turnock Street and Seaview Street;
  • Seaview Street between Pearl Street and Marine Parade and
  • Lions Park and Faulks Park public carparks and the public carpark adjoining Kingscliff Memorial Park.

Salt (24 hours per day, all days)

  • Bells Boulevard

Cabarita Beach (24 hours per day, all days) 

  • Pandanus Parade; and
  •  Public carpark between Palm Avenue and Pandanus Parade.
  • 24 hours per day, all days

Murwillumbah (24 hours per day, all days)

  • Queensland Road between 'Harry Williams Gate' of the Murwillumbah Showgrounds and Murwillumbah Street;
  •  Public car park area near Mount Saint Patrick's School on Queensland Road;
  • Bent Street between Queensland Road and Church Street;
  • Church Street between Bent Street and Queen Street;
  • Alice Street between Queen Street and Church Street; 
  • Church Lane;
  • Police Lane;
  • Bruce Lane;
  • Queen Street between Murwillumbah Street and Church Street;
  • Murwillumbah Street between Nullum Street and Queen Street;
  • Wharf Street between Queen Street and Tumbulgum Road;
  • Proudfoots Lane;
  • Public carparks between Wollumbin Street and Proudfoots Lane;
  • Commercial Road between Wharf Street and King Street;
  • King Street between Commercial Road and Brisbane Street;
  • Public carpark between Lavender Lane and King Street;
  • Lavender Lane;
  • Brisbane Street between Murwillumbah Street and Condong Street;
  • Condong Street between Brisbane Street and Nullum Street;
  • Nullum Street between Condong Street and Murwillumbah Street;
  • Wollumbin Street between Nullum Lane and Commercial Road;
  • Nullum Lane between Wollumbin Street and Byangum Road;
  • Byangum Road between Nullum Lane and Murwillumbah Street;
  • Alma Street between Commercial Road and Tweed Valley Road;
  • Tumbulgum Road between Wharf Street and Racecourse Road;
  • Public carparks adjoining Tweed Shire Council Civic Centre and Tweed Regional Aquatic Centre (TRAC) Murwillumbah;
  • Sunnyside Lane;
  • Factory Lane between King Street and Wollumbin Street;
  • Budd Park public carpark;
  • Knox Park public carpark; and
  • Red Cross Hall public carpark.

Excluding those businesses approved by Council for the purposes of footpath dining whilst those businesses are trading.


2. Delegates to the General Manager authority to vary or suspend the alcohol free zones for special circumstances.


3. Notifies prescribed interested parties including NSW Police Local Area Commander and officers in charge of Tweed Heads, Kingscliff, and Murwillumbah Police Stations and any liquor licenses and secretaries of registered clubs whose premises are adjacent to any Alcohol Free Zones within Tweed Shire.


4. Erect new signs in existing and proposed locations with the Alcohol-free Zone commencing 2 December 2021 and expiring 1 December 2025.

The Motion was Carried

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Katie Milne
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:

1. Notes the significant action being taken across the organisation in response to climate change and the vast effort required by all departments of Council whilst in an extremely constrained budget environment, but the significant savings to the organisation from renewable energy and the lost opportunity costs if action is not fully embraced.

2. Requests a report back by the end of 2021 on the costs and staff resourcing required to describe community emissions reduction scenarios, in the interests of commencing this work as soon as possible. The review of community emissions reduction options is to consider actions that benefit low income households and enable land managers to access carbon markets. The review also needs to consider how the actions can be paid for.

3. Notes plans to establish a climate change reference panel to assist with stakeholder and community engagement, following the risk assessment. 

The Motion was Carried

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that the Mayor:

1. Writes to the Minister for Planning and Pubic Spaces to express Council’s extreme disappointment at the lack of genuine consultation with affected councils and their representatives in its recent decision to make the Environmental Planning and Assessment Amendment (Compliance Fees) Regulation 2021, with the effect of prohibiting councils from collecting existing compliance levies after 31 December 2021, noting that Tweed Council will now be forced to revise the extent of its current compliance services, much to the detriment of our community and environment, and will also restrict Council’s capacity to assist State Government compliance agencies in their investigations and enforcement within the Tweed Shire; 

2. Writes to the Chair of the Northern Rivers Joint Organisation seeking an urgent collective action among its members to advocate against the latest State Government Regulation on compliance levies, with a view to seeking an urgent meeting with the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces.  Councillor representatives for the meeting will be the Mayor and Councillor Polglase; and

3. Writes to both its State and Federal Members seeking their urgent support and assistance for an immediate review and further pausing of recent State legislation to provide affected councils with additional to investigate alternative funding services to continue its current compliance services. 

The Motion was Carried

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins.

"Dear Father,
I give thanks for all those You have placed in Council to watch and serve over the Tweed Shire.
I pray for our Mayor and Counsellors, and all who are in positions of authority, that Your Spirit may rest upon them and enlighten their minds as they seek to guide the people of the Tweed with all skill, wisdom and understanding. 
Father, may the heart of our leaders be in Your hands and their decisions divinely engaged by You.  Help and direct them in the things that are important, that their outcomes be fair and right, not only for the now but also for the future of others to come.
Father, we are facing interesting and challenging times, but You are our refuge and stronghold in times of trouble. May we not waver or grow weary. May we continue to do what we have been called to do with courage and strength. Watch over and protect us I pray. May Your Will be done.
So, Father, continue to help and guide us, that we may live to practice the values we know to be true. That Council is transparent in all its dealings tonight. Treating the people of the Tweed with fairness, commitment and truth, planning for their future…with everyone involved.  So that our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today. 
May You answer us on the day we call.
Amen"

Local Government Act
This report is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, which permits the meeting to be closed to the public for business relating to the following: 

(a)     personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors).


COMMENTS FROM THE MAYOR MADE IN OPEN COUNCIL

Council’s General Manager is employed under a Contract of Employment, which is in the standard format required by the Office of Local Government.

A requirement of that contract is for reviews to be undertaken of the General Managers performance.

Council appointed a Performance Review Panel to undertake these reviews – I am on that Panel, together with all Councillors.

Council undertook a detailed review of the General Managers performance for the 2020/21 financial year, based on his Performance Agreement with Council. That review was held on Wednesday 7 July.

In accordance with Guidelines issued by the Department of Premier and Cabinet, the details of this review are to be reported to Council in Closed session, and all associated documents are to remain confidential.

The outcome of that review was an overall rating of more than satisfactory performance over the year by our General Manager.

Under the General Managers contract of employment, which is in the same format of all General Managers in NSW Councils, Council is contractually required to review the General Managers Remuneration as part of the review process and using review outcomes. 

It was noted by the Panel that the General Manager has not had his Remuneration increased under this requirement in the past 2 years despite above satisfactory performance outcomes in each of those years.

In undertaking this review the Panel noted that the Office of Local Government had recently released a consultation paper on General Manager remuneration. That paper included a table for GM remuneration in NSW with Tweed being placed in the Regional Centre category. The table indicates that the Tweed GM was on the average TRP of the other 24 General Managers in the category – and confirms that Tweed has the highest population in that grouping. Tweed also has very significant growth and environmental matters to prioritise and address, and the Council has a proactive agenda of items that it continues to deal with – all of this requires extra expertise and commitment from the General Manager.

The Panel also noted that the General Manager did not receive a remuneration increase at his last 2 reviews, but rather the Council supported a leadership professional development activity for him. This was postponed due to Covid. Council encouraged the General Manager to undertake this course when it was re-offered and that it would pick up any additional costs should such be required.

Based on the high level of performance evidenced by the review outcomes in 2020/21, and in acknowledgement of Troy’s outstanding Leadership in very challenging times over the past 12 months, the Panel has recommended a 2.5% increase in the General Managers Total Remuneration Package. 

Follow up areas requiring the General Managers attention were identified and conveyed to him as part of this process.

The Performance Review Panel has also prepared the General Managers Performance Agreement for 2021/22 and this is presented for endorsement.

On behalf of all Councillors, I wish to thank Troy for his efforts and support, which are very much valued by Council, Councillors and staff. 

It is not an easy job, and we appreciate the contributions Troy has made to better our Region and the local government industry generally, and the Leadership he provides in our community and to our Councillors and staff.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RECOMMEndED that:

1. The report from the Performance Review Panel, which comprises the Mayor and all Councillors, on the outcomes of the annual review of the General Manager’s 2020/21 performance against his Performance Agreement be received and noted.

2. In acknowledgement of the high level of performance as evidenced in the Performance Review outcomes and consistent with Clause 8.3 of the General Managers Contract of Employment, the General Managers Total Remuneration Package be increased by 2.5% effective from the date of this meeting. 

3. The General Managers 2021/22 Performance Agreement be endorsed.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  Nil.

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 1 July 2021 be received and noted and

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1 Festival of Speed on Tweed 7, 8 and 9 January 2022
That the Committee provides in-principle support of the Speed on Tweed event on 6, 7 and 8 January 2022, subject to:

The appropriate car racing approval process is being followed.

That a Traffic Management Plan and Traffic Control Plans be submitted to Council at least four months before the event.

7.1 Letitia Road Parking adjacent Caravan Park
That restricted parking signage along Letitia Road, Fingal Head is not supported given the slow speed environment and the difficulty in enforcing signage in an informal parking situation. 

7.2 Greenway Drive, Tweed Heads South
That a yellow no stopping line be installed around the curve on Greenway Drive opposite Enterprise Avenue.  This should extend from the driveway of the childcare centre at 53 Greenway Drive south for 75 metres.

That longitudinal line marking be installed on Greenway Drive at the intersection of Enterprise Avenue for north-bound traffic to improve recognition of the intersection. 

That the length of the bus zone adjacent to the child care centre at 53 Greenway Drive to be reduced to enable on street parking.

That marking individual parking spaces and timed-parking on Enterprise Avenue is not supported as this is an industrial area that the demand for on-street parking is generally not for customers who require a turnover of parking spaces.  Individual parking bays often result in reduced parking space availability.  

Prohibitive parking on Greenway Drive adjacent Carey Cottages is not supported as there is enough width to park on-road without impacting on through traffic and vehicles can partially park on the nature strip without obstructing the formed footpath.

That extending the yellow no stopping line on the eastern side of Greenway Drive to the south of Corporation Circuit is not supported as there is adequate sight distance at the intersection.

That the installation of additional pedestrian refuges on Greenway Drive be considered as part of the Pedestrian and Bike Plan.

The Motion was Carried
