Cr Katie Milne
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:
 
1.     Notes that there is new technology being developed for roadside litter management and weed management.  Unfortunately, there is very limited capacity for Council to fund roadside maintenance for litter collection or more environmentally sensitive vegetation management as budget priorities have had to shift to respond to the NSW ‘Fit for the Future’ benchmarks which do not include environmental considerations in these built assets and financial management targets.
 
2.     Notes the NSW Premier’s Priority to reduce litter by 40% and the NSW Litter Prevention Strategy that states: 
 
“Why is clean up important? As well as bins, we must keep sites clean to reduce litter. This is vital for sending the message that litter doesn’t belong. Sites that are clean stay cleaner, while littered sites signal that littering is the norm.”
 
3.     Writes to the Premier and responsible Ministers for Waste, Pollution, Fisheries, Environment and Infrastructure to request that a fixed percentage of the Waste Levy be returned to Council to enable regular litter collection from roadsides and waterways, highlighting that Tweed Shire is the highest biodiversity hotspot of NSW and an internationally significant environment, including marine environment, that warrants special consideration.
 
4.     Includes consideration of increased litter collection and roadside weed management in future budgets to ensure that Councillors can consider this against competing priorities as this environmental impact should not just be ignored.
 
5.     Requests the North East Waste group undertake a campaign with messaging about the impact of litter to our wildlife and providing incentives such as support, training, insurance and/or prizes for community groups or individuals that assist with litter collection.
 
6.     Considers undertaking a trial of the Transport for NSW Slasherteck guidepost mower.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd:

"Thank you Madam Mayor

I am going to pray in the Christian tradition.  If you would like to join with me, please bow your head.

Gracious God, 

We are grateful for the relative safety we are enjoying in our region in the pandemic.  Our hearts are with the Local Government Areas that are deeply affected, and for families who are grieving and fearful.

And yet our community carries its own grief, with border closures affecting our ability to work, go to school, get medical treatment, and be with family.  Be with us in our distress.  May state leaders on both sides of the border recognise our particular circumstances, and provide compassionate, wise, and good solutions to our needs.  Thank you for the work of Council in making our needs known and advocating for us.  We pray also for other border communities in similar circumstances.

Many of us are fatigued and frustrated.  Please grant Council, both elected and staff, daily strength for the work.  Help each one to meet work and personal challenges in your ongoing grace and peace.

May the hard work of tonight’s meeting, and all its preparation, result in blessing to our community and satisfaction for each one here.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

The current 15 minute timed parking in front of 33 Ewing Street, Murwillumbah be removed.

7.1 Overall Drive, Pottsville, Bus Zone
That a bus shelter and bus zone be installed on Overall Drive, Pottsville (south of Hampton Court) adjacent No.6 Overall Drive, Pottsville.  

That a 'No Stopping' line be installed on Overall Drive from Hampton Court, north for 35 metres to the crossing. 

7.2 Tweed Valley Way, Tumbulgum - Overtaking Lane
That the southbound overtaking lane on Tweed Valley Way, Tumbulgum (near house number 8581) be reduced by 300m in length at the northern end.

A copy of the plans be circulated to the members of the committee before installation.

7.3 Kent Street, Tweed Heads
That the existing double centre line be removed and replaced with a broken centre line on Kent Street, 60m from Murraba Crescent to 10m from the Quarterdeck service lane, and this be monitored.

7.4 Twin Towns Triathlon Season 2021/22
That the proposed Twin Towns Triathlon Club 2021-22 Season events be supported, including the Club Championship event in March 2022, subject to current COVID-19 restrictions at the time of the event, and:

1.      NSW Police approval being obtained for the conduct of the race event in March 2022. 

2.      Endorsement of the events by Bicycle NSW or Cycling QLD. 

3.      Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.

4.      Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.

5.      The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.

6.      Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.

7.      All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.

8.      Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.

9.      Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the events.

10.    That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.

11.    The events be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.

12.    The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins, Murwillumbah Church of Christ:

"Let’s us pray
Father, I thank You for knowing that You are here amongst us. You are the Head of our meeting tonight, our unseen Guest, silently listening and watching over all that will be said and done. You are our good and mighty Counsellor whose ways are always good and right. 
I pray for our team: that Your blessings and goodness will be upon each and every one them.
Mayor Chris Cherry, Deputy Mayor Reece Byrnes, Councillor Pryce Allsop, Councillor Ron Cooper, Councillor Katie Milne, Councillor James Owen and Councillor Warren Polglase.
Helping them know what needs to be discussed and accomplished with all wisdom, as they seek to provide and watch over the Tweed Shire. 
I also pray for the up and coming Council elections in December. 
Father, I acknowledge that the Tweed Shire Council has been put in place by You, for there is no authority except that which You have established.  
Lord, may each person that is voted and elected for, be the ones that You have chosen. That they may also do what is good and right and be commended by You. That the people of the Tweed may give respect and honour, acknowledging that our authorities are Your servants, who give their skills and time to govern and watch over us.
So Father, continue to help and guide us, that we may live to practice the values we know to be true. That Council be transparent in all its dealings tonight. Treating the people of the Tweed with fairness, commitment, planning for their future with everyone involved.
So that our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.
May You answer us in the day we call.
Amen"

The General Manager advised that the Manager Corporate Governance, Ms Stephanie Papadopoulos, has been appointed as Returning Officer for the election of the Deputy Mayor for the period ending 4 December 2021.

The Returning Officer advised that two nominations have been received for Deputy Mayor:

  • Cr Pryce Allsop was nominated by himself and Cr Warren Polglase and has accepted the nomination.
  • Cr Reece Byrnes was nominated by himself and Cr Ron Cooper and has accepted the nomination.

The result of the Ordinary Ballot by way of show of hands for Deputy Mayor was as follows:

·  Voting for Cr Pryce Allsop

FOR VOTE - Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Warren Polglase

·  Voting for Cr Reece Byrnes

FOR VOTE - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr James Owen, Cr Ron Cooper and Cr Katie Milne.

The Returning Officer declared that Cr Reece Byrnes received the majority of votes and is elected as Deputy Mayor of Tweed Shire Council for the period ending 4 December 2021.

Cr Pryce Allsop
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that, based on the above voting for the position of Deputy Mayor, the Returning Officer declared that Cr Reece Byrnes is the Deputy Mayor for the period ending 4 December 2021.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

3.    The road closure shall not be finalised until the new access road from Tweed Coast Road is constructed by the applicant in accordance with the conditions of consolidated consent (MP08_0194), specifically points 29 and 93 listed below:
Depot Road Access and Services.

29.  1)   Closure of the Depot Road road reserve and the existing access to the Depot Road sports fields site shall not occur until an alternative access road capable of supporting the continued development and future use of the sports fields is provided, and the road reserve is dedicated to Council. The alignment of the access to the Depot Road sports fields site shall be compatible with the concept layout for the proposed sports fields, taking into account boundary constraints, vegetation mapping, current consents and future infrastructure servicing needs, including water, sewerage, telecommunications, and electricity, to the satisfaction of council.

        2)   The design of the Kings Forest water, sewerage, electricity and telecommunications networks adjacent to the Depot Road sports fields must provide adequate capacity for the future connection of this site by council.


Depot Road

93. Uninterrupted all weather vehicular access to the Depot Road sports fields site shall be maintained for the duration of works.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Warren Polglase

RESOLVED that Council submits the following motions to the LGNSW Annual conference:

Councillor's Remuneration
That Local Government NSW write to the Honourable Shelley Hancock MP, Minister for Local Government to request that NSW Local Government Councillor’s be fairly remunerated based on the fiscal, legal and community responsibilities of their roles and the time required for representation of the relevant population base.

Regenerative Landscape Management
That LGNSW write to the NSW Premier and the NSW Minister for Agriculture to request significant investment in research and development of regenerative agriculture to position NSW to become a world leader in best practice landscape management to sustain future food security and farm viability, and to harness the vast potential for economy recovery through our regional areas.

Local Government election -  electronic voting 
That LGNSW write to the Honourable Shelley Hancock MP, Minister for Local Government to request that electronic voting (iVote) be introduced for Local Government elections, with eligibility criteria to include allowing voters to use iVote if they reasonably believe attending a polling place on election day will pose a risk to their health or safety of themselves or those around them, because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Funding for Environmental Protection
That Local Government NSW requests the NSW Government to dramatically increase funding for environmental protection to at least 5% of the State Budget in light of current funding levels of $1,497 million, which equates to only 1.53% of the $98,133 million 2020/21 operating budget.


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd.

"Gracious God,

With world mental health day coming this Sunday, we acknowledge the extraordinary stresses we are under at the moment. The inability to get away for meaningful breaks, separation from family, and increased stresses at work have left us all vulnerable. In our frustration at things beyond our control, we feel the temptation to express our anger at the people close to us.

We lose sight of the beauty around us, so we stop now and say thank you for the beautiful beaches and ocean lying in front of us, the river running through the heart of our Shire, and Wollumbin standing tall behind us. We are grateful for the gracious welcome to country we have received from the people of Bundjalung Nation, and their generous sharing of the land with us all.

And even in the business of tonight we will see things to celebrate: the professionalism and capability of Council staff; the passion and dedication of Councillors; the leadership and wisdom of our Mayor, and the involvement and concern of the public.

One of your greatest gifts is peace of mind and heart. May we know that peace tonight, and be able to speak peace to one another as we respond to the demands of our times.

We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen. "

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Pryce Allsop

RESOLVED that:

1.   The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 2 September 2021 be received and noted, and 

2.   The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1 Prospero Street, South Murwillumbah

A survey be conducted with adjacent business operators in Prospero Street, South Murwillumbah, to determine the most suitable time limit and that this matter be brought back to the committee.

7.1 Water Street, Tweed Heads South and River Terrace, Tweed Heads 

The Committee had concerns with the impact of the proposed signage on adjacent residences, boaters and business operators. Installing such signage may lead to campers moving to the adjacent streets and therefore not addressing the issue. Current COVID restrictions impact campers’ access to caravan parks and to Queensland. The installation of No Parking 11pm-5am in Water Street and River Terrace, Tweed Heads, is therefore not supported at this stage.

7.2 Kingscliff Triathlon - 14 November 2021 and 27 March 2022
That the proposed Kingscliff Triathlons on 14 November 2021 and 27 March 2022 be supported, subject to standard conditions of approval and current COVID19 restrictions at the time of the event:

1.  NSW Police approval being obtained.
2.  Endorsement of the event by the Kingscliff Business Chamber and Bicycle NSW.
3.  Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
4.  Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
5.  The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
6.  Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
7.  All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.  Approval from Transport for NSW is required for any signage / variable message boards placed on state controlled roads.
8.  Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
9.  Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
10.  That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
11. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
12. The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
13. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
14. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

7.3 Tweed Coast Enduro, February 2022

That the proposed Tweed Enduro on 26 and 27 February 2022 be supported, including temporary closure of Tweed Coast Road, Wooyung Road, Overall Drive and Kellehers Road subject to current COVID-19 restrictions at the time of the event:
 
1.  NSW Police approval being obtained.
2.  Endorsement of the event by Triathlon Australia.
3.  Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
4.  Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
5.  The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
6.  Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser be provided to Council at least 2 weeks prior to the event.
7.  All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
8.  Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
9.  Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
10. That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
11. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
12. The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
13. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
14. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

7.4 Leeward Terrace, Tweed Heads

That the installation of temporary 'No Stopping' signs on Leeward Terrace, Tweed Heads at the road closure barrier, is supported while the road is closed due to the COVID restrictions.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Nil.
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Katie Milne, Cr Warren Polglase

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins. 

"Let’s Pray,
Our Father in Heaven, You are the blessed God, our source of life, wisdom & goodness. 
Despite the many obstacles & difficulties we are facing at the moment, You have also provided us with so many other good things for which I am truly grateful.
I am grateful for bringing us together for the task that You have called us to do. 
I am grateful for the staff & Councillors within the Tweed Shire Council. 
So many talented & dedicated people that You have put in charge over us to help provide a beautiful & safe place to live & enjoy. Thank You Father.
May our Councillors never be satisfied with a project that is not well done or properly throughout. Father, I pray that with all that is said & done tonight, it will be done in a professional & thoughtful manner, providing the best possible result.
Father, keep us working steadfast & true for the Tweed Shire Council. 
Support & encourage each of our Councillors - that they may not grow weary or fall short of the task that You have given them to do. Give each one of them strength & wisdom to complete a job well done!
Father, You already know the outcome of this meeting… So may everyone who is involved, every Councillor, be led by Your Wisdom & Guidance.
So, Father, continue to help and guide us, that we may live to practice the values we know to be true. That Council be transparent in all its dealings tonight. Treating the people of the Tweed with fairness, commitment, planning for their future…with everyone involved: 
So that our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.
May You answer us in the day we call.
Amen"

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

1. The following tabled Petitions be received and noted.

• Petition containing 103 signatures of which 72 are valid signatories and received on 28 September 2021 entitled "Make Koala Beach Roads Safe for Children & Wildlife" advising as follows:

"Over 20 years has elapsed since the establishment of the Koala Beach Estate and the town of Pottsville has undergone significant changes and population increases. Effective Traffic management is a core requirement in preserving the conservation values of Koala Beach Estate and accordingly a Traffic Management Plan and controls were devised at the onset and require periodical review.

It has become more apparent as the Estate has filled, Tom Merchant Drive established and the population in Koala Beach Estate and the Pottsville surrounds has significantly increased, wildlife are increasingly falling victims to motor vehicle strike on Koala Beach roads.

The Koala Beach Estate is built within an area of high biodiversity and conservation value supporting threatened species, and sensitive ecosystems. The land is a critical and strategic link within the Tweed Coast Koala and Wildlife corridor.

The community in Koala Beach are confronted regularly with wildlife fatalities on their road and are feeling sad, angry and frustrated. They are desperately trying to raise awareness to motorists to Slow Down and have more wildlife awareness."

(More details are contained within the Confidential attachment.)

• Petition containing 139 signatures received on 6 October 2021 entitled "Telstra Tower 5807 Tweed Valley Way Mooball NSW" advising predominantly as follows:

"I object to the proposed mobile phone tower clt 5807 Tweed Valley Way Mooball, and I request Tweed Shire Council not approve the DA for the following reasons:

1. In August 2020 the U.S Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit ruled that the reliance on the current radio frequency electromagnetic radiation (RF EMR) exposure guidelines failed to consider the non-cancer evidence regarding adverse health effects of wireless technology, when it decided its 1996 emission guidelines (these outdated guidelines are the same as what the Australian regulatory body ARPANSA rely on to protect the public's health)

2. It is unsafe and unsound to rely on the ARPANSA Standard wheel installing mobile phone telecommunications infrastructure. There are thousands of peer-reviewed scientific studies evidencing harm from RF EMR well below the standards set by ARPANSA (www.biointiative.org).

3. The ARPANSA Standard has been strongly criticised by independent scientists worldwide as unscientific and inadequate for the protection of human safety. Authorities in other countries have adopted standards 10 to 10,000+ times more rigorous than the ARPANSA Standard. In February 2021 the ARPANSA Standard increased the general public exposure limit by 400%. This increase in exposure levels is alarming and not proven to be safe by any governing bodies.

4. More than 250 scientists have signed the International EMF Scientist Appeal, which calls for stronger exposure limits These scientists have published more than 2000 peer-reviewed papers on EMF in professional journals and arguably constitute the majority of experts on the effects of non-ionizing radiation.

5. No long-term prospective studies have been completed proving the safety of RF EMR levels under the ARPANSA Standard for children. The proposed site is 200m from where children live

6. In 2011, the International Agency on Research on Cancer (IARC) listed non-ionizing radio frequency radiation from cell phones and other wireless devices in Group 2B: Possibly carcinogenic to humans(in the same group as DDT and lead)

7. World renowned EMF scientists have since argued that the evidence that wireless is carcinogenic has increased and IARC should upgrade the listing to Group 2A: probably carcinogenic to humans or Group 1: carcinogenic to humans classification(www.emfscientist.org).

8. The views of ICNIRP (on whose guidelines the ARPANSA Standard is based) and ARPANSA are not in line with the opinions of the larger, independent scientific community who have published thousands of peer-reviewed studies on the biological effects of RF EMR. ICNIRP is not independent of industry and has had numerous conflicts of interest Identified over the years

9. Scientific literature on the health risks of RF EMR identifies detrimental skin and ocular effects and profound effects on all biological systems including cells, bacteria, yeast, animals and humans, including hear rate variability; at field Intensities comparable to(or below) what persons living within 500 meters of a mobile phone base station tower will be subjected to on a continual basis.

10. Persons living in proximity to the proposed tower would be exposed without consent to RF EMR, classified as a possible carcinogen" by the World Health Organisation.

11. Simultaneous, cumulative exposure from all sources (such as towers, small cells, public WiFI, smart city infrastructure smart street lighting and loT devices) is not or monitored or regulated by Australian government or industry.

12. Professor Martin Pall (Emeritus of Biochemistry and Basic Medical Sciences, Washington State University) has warned that EMF exposures make plants much more flammable, and may therefore cause and contribute to bushfires. There is an urgent need for more research into the bushfire risk cell towers pose to rural (and even urban) Australia

13. According to published real estate reports and advice from local agents, the proposed tower would directly affect the value and saleability of nearby properties by up to 50%.  This in effect imposes financial loss upon the  owners of said properties without fair and just compensation. The proposed site is in direct view of neighbouring homes."
 
 
2. ATTACHMENT 1 and 2 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:
(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

3. Petition 1 "Make Koala Beach Roads Safe for Children & Wildlife" be referred to the Local Traffic Committee to give regard to potential traffic calming and driver awareness tools that could be implemented at this locality.

Councillor Ron Cooper asks:

With reference to the proposed purchase of land at Byangum (Confidential Item 29.1 from Council Meeting held 16 September 2021), how much of that land is suitable for compensatory planting? Do we have to compensate with the same species, genus or would the most suitable native be acceptable?


The Acting Director Sustainable Communities and Environment responded that subject to the extent and location of any proposed land uses associated with the purchase of the land, a significant proportion of the land appears suitable for use as compensatory planting or offsetting based on: 

  • Current rural zoning – any protective mechanisms (covenants, voluntary conservation agreements) would meet additionality requirements.
  • Current land use – given the land is currently cleared, any revegetation also provides additionality.
  • Vegetation communities – based on location in the landscape, including the topographical variation, river frontage and alluvial areas, several key ecosystems (lowland rainforest, swamp sclerophyll, freshwater wetland) may be able to be compensated for through revegetation.

The specifications for compensatory plantings or offsets are determined by the values that are impacted at the development site. Therefore, the first consideration is that all measures are taken to avoid or mitigate impact. This site could then be suitable as a receiving site for the residual impacts of proposed development, where those impacts are on the vegetation communities associated with the ecosystems identified above.

Cr Katie Milne

RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Minutes of the Tweed Coast and Waterways Committee Meeting held Wednesday 25 August 2021 be received and noted; and

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

A1 - Tweed Estuary Coastal Management Program update

RECOMMEND that Council writes to Geoff Provest  with a request for further information from Transport for NSW - Maritime concerning its plans for review of the Tweed River Boating Plan, and comment on Coastal Management Program actions.

A4. Cudgen / Chinderah drainage

RECOMMEND that Council:

  1.  Supports the concerns raised by the Tweed Coast and Waterways Committee about the potential environmental impact of Council’s West Kingscliff Catchment and Drainage Management Plan 2000.
  2.  Supports consideration of the longer term viability of this development post 2100 in regard the further potential clearing or other environmental impacts that may be required to address sea level rise and increased flood and storm events.
  3.  Supports limits on the development to avoid significant environmental impacts including clearing of native vegetation.
  4.  Consults further with this Committee to consider alternative, more environmentally sensitive proposals for drainage and drain management.


A5. Beach access way upgrade works

RECOMMEND that Council writes to the Crown Lands Commissioner, Professor Richard Bush, highlighting the impact that significant delays in processing of Crown Land licence applications is having on Council’s program of waterways management works, particularly grant funded projects where delivery timing is critical. 


The Motion was Carried

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr James Owen

Cr Polglase temporarily left the meeting at 6.23pm.

RESOLVED that Council:

1.   Notes that since 1990, NSW koala populations have declined by between 20% and 50%, to be in the range of 15,000 to 25,000 remaining. Local extinctions have already occurred and the species is projected to become extinct in the wild in NSW within 30 years. Urgent action is needed to ensure future generations can see these iconic species in the wild. 

2.   Writes to the Premier, Minister for Planning & Public Spaces, Minister for Energy and Environment, and Minister for Agriculture urging them to: 

a.    Maintain Council dual consent provisions for Forestry, including Private Native Forestry in Local Environmental Plans, to account for the variability within regions, zoning objectives, site survey needs, traffic and infrastructure limitations, and consultation with adjoining land holders; 

b.     Enable Council to opt in to Schedule 1 of the NSW Koala SEPP 2021 and apply the policy in all zones as per the precedent established for the Central Coast and eight Greater Sydney local government areas;

c.    Maintain Council’s ability to regulate environmental zones to protect, manage and restore lands of high ecological, scientific, cultural or aesthetic values, particularly for the protection of core koala habitat; 

d.    Provide planning certainty, resources and support for identifying core koala habitat and the development of Koala Plans of Management; and 

e.     Allow for departures by the consent authority from the SEPP Guidelines based on existing surveys, local circumstances or emerging technology where this is agreed to by the Department. 

Cr Polglase returned to the meeting at 6.29 pm.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR -Cr Katie Milne, Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Ron Cooper, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST -None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -Nil.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd:

"I am going to pray in the Christian tradition.  I invite you to join with me.

Gracious God, 

We are grateful for the work of all our Councillors, who were willing to extend their term to continue serving our community through the pandemic.  It’s been a difficult and tiring time, and we are thankful for their willingness to serve and their resilience.

For those choosing not to stand at the election, we pray that this month may be an opportunity to reflect on good work done and friendships made.  Please bless them as they move into another phase of their life and service.  We appreciate their work for our community, and thank both them and you for their leadership.

For those who will stand again, we pray for fresh energy and renewed joy in their work.  Please grant them everything they need through the election process and for their future service.

We thank you for the leadership of our Mayor through a very difficult year, and for her advocacy on our behalf.

For the new Council to be elected, we pray for a smooth transition for both Councillors and staff, and for positive, effective working relationships that will benefit our community.

Please grant your grace, mercy, and peace to all here tonight.

 We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

RECOMMENDED that Development Application DA21/0052 for a 3 lot subdivision at Lot 3 Section 14 DP 758739 No. 39 Mooball Street, Murwillumbah be refused for the following reasons:

1. The development does not satisfy Section 4.15(1) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, particularly Section (a)(i) – the provisions of any Environmental Planning Instruments in that the application is not considered to meet the zone objectives of the R3 Medium Density Residential Zone of the Tweed LEP 2014.

2. The development does not satisfy Section 4.15(1) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, particularly Section (a)(iii) – the provisions of any Development Control Plan in that the development is inconsistent with the Development Control Plan Section A5 – Subdivision Manual as:

a) There is no garbage service available to proposed Lots 31 and 32 (Banner Lane).

3. The development does not satisfy Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act, particularly Section 1(c) - the suitability of the site for the development, in that the site is not considered suitable for the proposed development.

4. The development does not satisfy Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act, particularly Section 1(e) - the public interest in that the development is not considered to be in the public interest. 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Katie Milne, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RECOMMENDED that:

1. Development Application DA12/0215.02 for an amendment to Development Consent DA12/0215 for change of use to daytime respite care centre with associated signage, car parking and landscaping at Lot 23 DP 8100 No. 9 Boyd Street, Tweed Heads be approved subject to the conditions of consent being amended as follows:

1. Insert new condition 1.1 which reads as follows:

1.1. An updated Plan of Management shall be submitted to Council within 28 days of the date of this approval.  The updated Plan of Management shall include detail on the monitoring and control of noise and other anti-social behaviour during normal and any out of hours uses so as not to adversely affect the amenity of the surrounding residences and businesses, and to include “events” and “emergency client needs” and the aims, procedures and rules of each.  The updated Plan of Management is to be submitted to Council to the satisfaction of the Council’s General Manager or delegate.

2. Delete condition 74 and replace with new condition 74A which reads as follows:

74A. The LAeq, 15 min noise level emitted from the premises shall not exceed the background noise level (LA90) in any Octave Band centre frequency (31.5 Hz - 8KHz inclusive) by more than 5dB(A) between 7am and 12 midnight, at the boundary of any affected residence.  Notwithstanding the above, noise from the use of the premises shall not be audible within any habitable room in any residential premises between the hours of 12 midnight and 7am weekdays and 12 midnight and 8am weekends.

3. Delete condition 75A and replace with new condition 75B which reads as follows:

75B. Hours of operation of the business are restricted to the following hours:

* Mondays to Fridays: 8am to 5pm (staff access); 8.30am to 4.00pm (client access), except for a maximum 12 emergency client needs on a one-to-one basis, which are not to include a general opening of the Centre;
* Weekends and Public Holidays: 8am to 5pm (staff access); 9.00am to 2.00pm (client access), except for 12 emergency client needs on a one-to-one basis, which are not to include a general opening of the Centre; and 
* Maximum 6 ‘events’ per year permitted to operate anytime between 8am and 5.30pm, or between 8am and 6.00pm during Daylight Savings Time.

4. Delete Condition 76 and replace with new condition 76A which reads as follows:

76A. All externally mounted artificial lighting, including security lighting, shall comply with AS4282:1997 Control of the Obtrusive Effects of Outdoor Lighting and be shielded to the satisfaction of Council’s General Manager or delegate where necessary or required so as to prevent the spill of light or glare creating a nuisance to neighbouring or adjacent premises. External mounted lighting must not spill beyond the boundaries of the site.

5. Delete condition 77 and replace with new condition 77A which reads as follows:

77A. Upon receipt of a noise complaint that Council deems to be reasonable, the operator/owner must submit a Noise Impact Study (NIS). The NIS must be prepared by a suitably qualified and practicing acoustic consultant and must be to the satisfaction of the General Manager or his delegate. The NIS must identify noise sensitive receivers, provide a representative background noise measurement (LA90, 15 minutes) and provide a prediction as to the level of noise impact likely to affect noise sensitive receivers from the approved use of the premises. If necessary, the NIS must include recommendations to ensure that that noise complies with the noise criteria identified under Condition 74A. The operator/owner must implement any recommendations of the NIS within a timeframe specified by Council's authorised officer.

6. Insert new condition 83 which reads as follows:

83. The use must always be operated / managed in accordance with the approved Plan of Management.  In the event of any inconsistency, the conditions of this consent will prevail over the Plan of Management.

7. Insert new condition 84 which reads as follows:

84. The occupier of the premises must ensure that the behaviour of patrons entering and leaving the premises does not detrimentally affect the amenity of the neighbourhood. In this regard, the occupier must be responsible for the control of noise and litter generated by users of the premises and must ensure that users leave the vicinity of the premises in a manner that is to the satisfaction of Council’s General Manager or delegate.

8. Insert new condition 85 which reads as follows:

85. A contact telephone number for the purpose of receiving complaints must be available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. This contact telephone number must be provided in writing to Council’s General Manager or delegate, NSW Police and nearby residents within five working days of the date of this approval. Any subsequent changes to this telephone number must be notified in accordance with the above requirements and within five days of the change being made. All complaints must be responded to and documented within a written complaint register that must be made available to Council or NSW Police when requested.

9. Insert new condition 86 which reads as follows:

86. Speakers and/or noise amplification equipment must not be installed and music must not be played in any of the outdoor areas associated with the premises.

10. Insert new condition 87 which reads as follows:

87. A register is to be kept by the owner or proprietors to record the emergency client access and events.  The register shall be made available to Council at the end of each quarter of the calendar year.

11. Insert new condition 88 which reads as follows:

88. Notice of scheduled ‘events’ shall be provided to all properties within a 100m radius no less than 5 days prior to the event.  A copy of the letter shall also be provided to Council for records.

2.     ATTACHMENT 3 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Katie Milne, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Ron Cooper

(Sec 3.40, 13.9 to 13.17 Model Code of Meeting Practice)

Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.

Nil.

RESOLVED that:

1.   The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 7 October 2021 be received and noted, and 

2.   The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1 Wharf Park, Murwillumbah
That the request for additional four 15 minute parking spaces on Tumbulgum Road,
Murwillumbah (adjacent to the toilet block, extending to the driveway of Southern
Cross Credit Union) is supported.

7.1 Gold Coast Challenger Series Surfing Event - Duranbah
That the proposed use of the roads associated with the Gold Coast Challenger Series
Surfing events on 4 to 15 May 2022 be supported, subject to conditions of approval
and current COVID-19 restrictions at the time of the event.
1. NSW Police approval being obtained.
2. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control
Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and
controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
3. That the proposed signs, lines and devices necessary to effect the proposed
road closures be approved.
4. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns
including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
5. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by
advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the
operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name,
specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route
arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for
all event related enquiries or complaints.
6. $20milion public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a
current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
7. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or
pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
8. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
9. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the
Local Traffic Committee: Thursday, October 7, 2021
Page 3
event.
10. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event
application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
11. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of
conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
12. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for
the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Katie Milne, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Ron Cooper

Local Government Act
This report is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, which permits the meeting to be closed to the public for business relating to the following: 

(a)     personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors)

(b)     the personal hardship of any resident or ratepayer

Cr Cherry declared a Non-Significant, Non-Pecuniary Interest in this item.  The nature of the interest is that Cr Cherry's family own and operate a caravan park in the Shire.  Cr Cherry will manage the Interest by remaining in the Chamber for discussion and voting on the merits of the item.

Cr Pryce Allsop
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RECOMMENDED that Council:


1. Receives and notes this report, and endorses the actions as outlined in the report pertaining to Pottsville North Holiday Park.

2. In relation to each of Fingal Head, Tweed Heads, Kingscliff North and Pottsville North Holiday Park Managers, notes the General Manager has offered a withdrawal of the termination notice issued 3 August 2021, and if withdrawal is accepted, notes the General Manager will write to the relevant Managers confirming withdrawal of the termination notice.

3. Notes that for the park managers who do accept the withdrawal of termination and who have exercised the option to renew their Deed, they will have the option of continuing to manage their park until 30 September 2024 or to seek to assign their Deed.

4. Notes that for the park managers who do not accept the withdrawal of termination, the expiry of their 180 day notice period will be 31 January 2022, and authorises the General Manager to appoint temporary park managers until 30 June 2022 to allow a tender process to be undertaken with a revised Deed, for those holiday parks, having regard to the extenuating circumstances identified in 7 below. Council resolves not to tender for the appointment of temporary mangers given the exemption in s.55 (3)(n) of the Local Government Act 1993.

5. In relation to Pottsville South and Kingscliff Beach Park Managers, notes the General Manager has sought to obtain the agreement of the relevant managers to extend, and give effect to any such agreement to extend on terms the General Manager considers appropriate, the current term of the Pottsville South and Kingscliff Beach Holiday Park Deeds to 30 June 2022, to allow a tender process to be undertaken with a revised Deed, and if accepted, authorises the General Manager to execute all necessary documentation to effect the extension. Council resolves not to tender for the appointment of temporary mangers given the exemption in s.55 (3)(n)of the Local Government Act 1993 and having regard to the extenuating circumstances identified in 7 below.

6. To the extent it is needed, delegates authority to the General Manager to make all other necessary decisions and execute all necessary documentation to bring these matters to a satisfactory conclusion.

7. Determines that, pursuant to section 55 (3)(i) of the Local Government Act 1993, there are extenuating circumstances which warrant seeking to extend the term of current Holiday Park Management Deeds of Agreement for Kingscliff Beach and Pottsville South and to appoint temporary managers to manager such parks to 30 June 2022. These include:

a. the need to prepare revised Deeds of Agreement reflecting the changes to the legislative framework and legal identify of the entity responsible for management of Crown Land on the coming into force of relevant provisions of the Crown Land Management Act 2016 and following the transitional regulation period;
b. the need for ongoing communications with Crown Lands concerning the initial categorisations for each Council managed Crown reserve including Tweed Holiday Parks;
c. consideration of appropriate commercial terms to include in revised draft deeds.
d. constraints on timeframes to conduct a tender process, following the preparation of revised draft Deeds;
e. the need to ensure appropriate interim management of the Holiday Parks is or remains in place during the summer holiday period and until a tender process is completed and new Deeds of Agreement are entered into;
f. the limited pool of suitably experienced Park Managers available in the region and difficulties in securing temporary managers for short term relief periods;
g. that a Council is unlikely to be able to obtain competitive tenders for temporary management for the time period and in the time frame required; and
h. that the local government elections are scheduled for 4 December 2021 and there is no scheduled meeting of the new Council until February 2022, which postdates the expiry of  existing arrangements.

8. Receives, notes and endorses the temporary contract between MSI Products Pty Ltd ACN 130 864 176 and Tweed Shire Council Tweed Holiday Parks (ABN 90 178 732 496 / 008) that was entered on 6 April 2021, appointing MSI Products Pty Ltd as caretaker of the Hastings Point Holiday Park until 31 October 2021.

9. Receives, notes and endorses the extension of the temporary contract with MSI Products Pty Ltd in connection with the Hastings Point Holiday Park for a six month period expiring on 30 April 2022, being an exercise of the 6 month option period within the temporary contract.

10. Notes that pursuant to section 55(3)(n) of the Local Government Act 1993, the temporary contract was exempt from tendering requirements as it involved an estimated expenditure of an amount less than $250,000.

11. Notes that pursuant to section 55(3)(i) of the Local Government Act 1993, there are in any event extenuating circumstances which warranted the entering and extension of the temporary contract for the Hastings Point Holiday Park to 30 April 2022. These include:

(a) On 28 February 2021, the previous park managers of the Hastings Point Holiday Park terminated their contract on short notice;
(b) An extensive search for replacement park managers was carried out by Council. A suitable candidate was not identified for a variety of circumstance specific reasons.
(c) As an interim measure, an interim park manager was put in place until the temporary contract was entered into;
(d) The directors of MSI Products Pty Ltd are individuals known by Council to be experienced in Park management, and who as at April 2021 and at the present date, are also responsible for management of the Pottsville South Holiday Park under a separate agreement;
(e) Management of Crown land reserves, including the Hastings Point Holiday Park, is in a state of flux as a result of the changes introduced by the Crown Land Management Act 2016 giving rise to an overhaul of Council's internal processes and procedure and intentions to prepare a revised Deed of Agreement and undertake a tender process, which will take time;
(f) Council need to ensure daily management of the holiday parks continues, especially over the upcoming holiday season, while it prepares new management deeds and undertakes an intended tender process (including after 30 April 2022 in respect of the Hastings Point Holiday Park and other parks).

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Pryce Allsop, Cr Katie Milne, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Ron Cooper

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins from the Murwillumbah Church of Christ.

"Dear Father,
I thank you for the men & women You have chosen for the task that is ahead of them. Each one of them is unique, bringing a variety of experiences, skills & knowledge that will be valued & appreciated. 

I pray that You will give each & every one of them strength, wisdom & humility to complete the work that You have entrusted them to do. 

Thank you for bringing us here despite the many obstacles & difficulties we have encountered in the last couple of years. However, Father, bless our counsellors with strength, wisdom, courage & determination, that they may press on, serving & providing for the people of the Tweed Shire. 

May our counsellors also encourage & build one another up in their various areas of responsibilities.  Help each one of them to plan & carry out their various tasks with clear lines of communication, harmony, respect & integrity. May they be united in one mind & spirit that all they seek to do will be achieved with great success.

Father, we don’t know the future or what it holds for us, so I pray for our counsellors that You may watch over them & their families, protecting & keeping each one of them safe in the days to come. May Your Will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

Thank you again for Your many blessings. We look forward to the contributions & gifts of service our counsellors will bring to the Tweed Shire. Bless each one of them I pray.

So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 

That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.   
  
Thank You Father… Amen."

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RESOLVED that Council submits the following motions to the LGNSW Annual conference:

Councillor's Remuneration
That Local Government NSW write to the Honourable Wendy Tuckerman MP, Minister for Local Government to request that NSW Local Government Councillor’s be fairly remunerated based on the fiscal, legal and community responsibilities of their roles and the time required for representation of the relevant population base.


Regenerative Landscape Management
That LGNSW write to the NSW Premier and the NSW Minister for Agriculture to request significant investment in research and development of regenerative agriculture to position NSW to become a world leader in best practice landscape management to sustain future food security and farm viability, and to harness the vast potential for economy recovery through our regional areas.


Local Government election - electronic voting 
That LGNSW write to the Honourable Wendy Tuckerman MP, Minister for Local Government to request consideration of the expansion of criteria for electronic voting (iVote) and postal voting for Local Government elections.


The Motion was Carried

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins:

"Dear heavenly Father, 

Thank you for the gift of a new year. 

I pray for your goodness & mercy as we prepare & plan for what is ahead of us. I confess our need of Your presence and Your guidance as we face the future.

Father, I pray for our Mayor & Councillors… for the awesome responsibility they have been elected to do. You alone know what it holds for them, and only You can give them the strength and the wisdom they will need to meet its challenges. 

Father, help them to humbly look towards You, to trust and seek Your wisdom & strength during this coming year.

In the midst of life’s uncertainties in the days ahead, assure council of the certainty of Your unchanging love. You are always there to help when we call upon Your name.

Father, I pray for the people of the Tweed Shire. For all those who live & work in the Northern Rivers. I pray especially for Your love & protection over our essential workers, truck drivers, healthcare workers, nurses, doctors, police officers, emergency services & etc… who provide us with the things we need & to keep us safe. Be with their families also, and assure them of Your love and concern for them.

So, Father, continue to help and guide us, that we may live to practice the values we know to be true. That Council be transparent in all its dealings tonight. Treating the people of the Tweed with all wisdom & love, planning for their future…with everyone involved:

So that our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.

May You answer us in the day we call.

Amen."

RECOMMENDED that:

A.   Development Application DA20/1033 for a food and drink premises (pub) including associated bottle shop, drive-thru and signage at Lot 10 DP 1254208 No. 14 Fraser Drive, Tweed Heads South be approved subject to the conditions attached to the report for this item with the following amendment to Condition No. 44 to read as follows:

44. A detailed landscape plan shall be submitted and approved by Council's General Manager or delegate prior to the earlier of issue of the first of any construction certificate or commencement of works onsite.  The detailed landscape plan shall:

a. Provide details of littoral/intertidal zone rehabilitation involving assisted restoration and revegetation of the entire area depicted as  ‘Lake edge planting’ on Detail Plan 1 and Detail Plan 2 in Landscape Concept Plan Issue B dated 12 August 2020 prepared by Plummer & Smith to include: 

i. Plant schedule to include scientific names, plant quantities and pot sizes comprising 100% local native species suitable to the site;
ii. Environmental weed species to be treated and treatment method consistent with Chenoweth EPLA and Bushland Restoration Services (2012) South East Queensland Ecological Restoration Framework; 
iii. A minimum average of one (1) local native plant per square metre to apply across the nominated area;
iv. A statement of commitment that all plants are to be installed and environmental weeds are to be treated and controlled prior to issue of occupation certificate.

b. Details of landscaping for all areas on-site beyond the ‘Lake edge planting’ area to include:

i. A plant schedule consistent with the following:

A. Minimum of 80% locally occurring Australian native species and maximum of 20% non-locally occurring Australian native species to apply to all trees. 
B. Minimum of 80% locally occurring Australian native species and maximum of 20% Australian native or exotic species to apply to other plants (shrubs, ground cover and similar). 
C. No noxious or environmental weed species

ii. The plant schedule is to include plant numbers and stock sizes. 
iii. A statement indicating that all landscape areas the subject of the detailed landscape plan are to be afforded a minimum twelve month active maintenance period.
iv. The surface currently marked as 'synthetic turf area' on the submitted Landscape Concept plans to be of a variety of synthetic turf that has at least 60% renewable resources.

B. ATTACHMENTS 11-13 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law
(g)    advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege

RESOLVED that:

1.    The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 4 November 2021 be received and noted and

2.    The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

7.1  Terranora Road, Banora Point

That the installation of No Stopping signage or lines, on Terranora Road opposite Old Ferry Road, are not supported at this stage given the good sight distance availability, and no crash history at the intersection.  The area will be monitored by Council officers and brought back to the committee if considered a safety issue is present.

7.2  Tweed Coast Road, Hastings Point
That the installation of No Stopping signs be supported on the eastern side of Tweed Coast Road, Hastings Point from 40m south of Yugari Drive extending 250m south to the Slow Point adjacent to number 37 Tweed Coast Road, in accordance with the Tweed Shire Council Aboriginal Cultural Heritage Management  Plan - TSC standard procedure for ACH impact mitigation: maintenance and emergency works. 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

RESOLVED that:

1.    The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 2 December 2021 be received and noted; and

2.    The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

7.1  Collier Street, Cudgen
That a Children's Crossing be approved on Collier Street, Cudgen (adjacent to the Primary School) subject to a detail design and funding being sought.

7.3  Grand Parade, Casuarina
That the on-street angled parking on Grand Parade, Casuarina - between Casuarina Way and Tweed Coast Road, be signposted as 2P 8am - 6pm.

3.    The Executive Leadership Team's recommendation 7.2  Letitia Road, Fingal Head be received and noted.

The Committee did not support the temporary closure of Letitia Road as put forward.  The Committee considered that the proposed closure of Letitia Road, Fingal Head for health reasons was not appropriate as the proposal is not for road safety or traffic concerns and the health concerns raised are addressed by other means and strategies.

The Motion was Carried

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins.

"Dear Loving and Gracious God:

May we be thankful; for You are indeed the giver of every good and perfect gift. 
Your goodness & mercy never fails us. 
Father, we come together this day to seek your wisdom, guidance, courage and strength. 
Be with us in our discussions and help us to be wise in the decisions we make for the people of the Tweed and the good of all those who have placed their trust and confidence in our leadership. 
Give us insight to lead with integrity that our decisions may reflect what is right and good. 
Keep us from not just focusing on the present, but give us insight to plan for the days ahead. 
Father, grant us the humility to always seek your will in all that we do and speak. 
May we be mindful of each other, being respectful & honouring one another in our thoughts & discussions tonight.
So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 
That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.     
May You answer us in the day we call: 
Amen."

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that: 

1.      The below five (5) motions be submitted to the Australian Local Government Association for the National General Assembly 2022.

2.      The General Manager arrange staff to draft key arguments Motion 4 -  "ALGA requests that the federal government allocate additional funding to councils to enable additional resources to ensure the timely delivery of infrastructure and regulatory services" prior to lodgement.


MOTION 1

Motion: Advocacy for A Substantive Increase in Commonwealth Funded and Managed Permanent Rental Housing

That the National General Assembly continues to advocate to the Federal Government to undertake a major program of construction and management of permanent rental social housing.

National Objective:

Why is this a national issue and why should this be debated at the NGA? (Maximum 250 words)

For a number of decades, the Australian Housing and Urban Research Institute (AHURI) has conducted extensive research that has informed and driven the public debate and actions by different levels of government on housing policy.

As highlighted in a post on the ALGA web site on 30 April 2021, AHURI has more recently been examining the consequences of Covid-19 for households in regional Australia, using Tasmania as a case study. 

Key findings from this study were that Increased demand for housing in the regions during the Covid-19 pandemic has exacerbated social and economic disadvantage, and In places where social and affordable housing is in short supply, lower-income tenants, including students and young unemployed people, are now at increased risk of experiencing more housing stress and precarity.

From the Tweed Shire’s perspective as a major growth area, these increasing social and economic impacts for both regional/rural areas and major cities warrants an urgent, national based response, best coordinated and funded by the Federal Government, aided by close consultation and partnerships with state and local governments.

Summary of Key Arguments:

Background information and supporting arguments (Maximum 500 words)

As identified in a web site article published for The Conversation on 15 November 2018: https://theconversation.com/australia-needs-to-triple-its-social-housing-by-2036-this-is-the-best-way-to-do-it-105960 , earlier AHURI research on the housing infrastructure needs of low-income earners estimated that following 25 years of inadequate investment,  Australia was facing a shortfall of 433,000 social housing dwellings. The current construction rate at that time was little more than 3,000 dwellings a year, not even keeping pace with rising need, let alone making inroads into the current backlog.

The AHURI report identified this historical neglect:

• From 1945, state and territory governments, financially supported by Canberra, maintained public programs that built 8,000-14,000 dwellings a year for half a century.

• From 1996, however, social housing largely slipped from the Australian government agenda. Dedicated ongoing funding to states and territories was at “starvation levels”. Public house building plunged to today’s residual output, except for a short-lived GFC-stimulus-funded recovery from 2008-11.


AHURI estimates that Australia needs to expand the national social housing stock to nearly three times its 2016 size by 2036.

To eliminate the both the backlog and service newly emerging need, an annual program of social housing construction averaging 36,000 units is needed.

Put into perspective, that output would equate to a 14% public housing share of Australia’s total house building, similar to that undertaken in the decade to 1955.

For comparison, housing providers with a social purpose today account for 20-31% of all house building in the UK, Finland, France and Austria, and much more in some Asian countries such as Singapore. England’s not-for-profit housing associations, for example, completed some 42,000 homes in 2017-18, out of 161,000 homes built in total.


MOTION 2


Motion: Advocacy for the continued development of National Recycling Initiatives

National General Assembly continues to advocate to the Federal Government to develop National Recycling Initiatives

National Objective:

Why is this a national issue and why should this be debated at the NGA? (Maximum 250 words)

The development of National Recycling Initiatives in Australia will reduce red tape, remove inconsistent waste policies from state to state and provide greater transparency to the waste sector.  

For the past two decades, Australian State Governments have introduced recycling initiatives that vary from state to state. For example, Tweed residents currently pay a landfill levy of approximately $85 per tonne for the landfilling of waste within Tweed, compared to approximately $140 per tonne in Sydney, and $0 in central NSW. Until recently, QLD did not have a waste levy, resulting in cheaper access to landfill within QLD. This resulted in waste being transported interstate, where industry would identify and access the cheapest landfill. It was estimated that over One Million tonnes of landfill was being transported from the Sydney Metropolitan region to QLD each year. QLD have recently proposed to increase their waste levy by $50 per tonne over the next 5 years, which is likely to see waste transported interstate from QLD to NSW as QLD waste levy reaches $130 to $140 per tonne. 

National Product Stewardship Programs that have been implemented by the Federal Government offer Local Government and the Waste/Recycling sector a greater understanding and transparency of recycling initiatives. National Recycling Initiatives provide industry with consistent policy frameworks that do not vary from state to state. 

Tweed Shire Council has recently adopted a Towards Zero Waste Strategy that will transition Council to a more Circular Economy and reduce the waste that it sends to landfill. National Waste Initiatives that support a circular economy and achieve less waste going to landfill will facilitate Council’s objectives of its Towards Zero Waste Strategy, which has been modelled the Federal Government’s National Waste Policy.

Summary of Key Arguments:

Background information and supporting arguments (Maximum 500 words)

Local Government is well positioned to support a national framework for waste and resource recovery in Australia that aligns with the National Waste Policy. 

State Based recycling initiatives that vary from state to state provide inconsistency in the industry and frustrate effective recycling initiatives.  

The success of Product Stewardship programs demonstrates that a National approach to recycling in Australia is effective. 

Product Stewardship programs apply the cost of recycling a product on the consumer at the point of purchase, which reduces the cost of recycling a product away from the recycling processor, which has historically seen a cost placed on Councils who operate waste facilities throughout NSW.   

By comparison, in New Zealand, and European Countries, there is a consistent approach to Waste and Recycling initiatives. There are national waste levies that do not differ from State to State within a Country or region. 


MOTION 3


Motion: ALGA calls upon the Federal Government to significantly increase the roads component to an acceptable percentage of the councils cost of maintaining the local road network.

National Objective:

Why is this a national issue and why should this be debated at the NGA? (Maximum 250 words)

Australian residents across the country rely on local Councils to provide safe well-maintained roads. The issue of funding these repairs is often greater for rural and regional councils that have large land areas with a low rate base. This is a national issue as the road component of the Financial Assistance Grant is insignificant compared to the asset value and responsibilities of councils for the nation’s local road network. 
Recent climatic and natural disaster events have accelerated the decline in the condition of this asset class that is pivotal for the distribution of goods and services throughout the economy.

Summary of Key Arguments:

• Currently the Financial Assistance Grants provide a very low percentage of the actual roads asset value – for Tweed this is 0.4%. There is an increased need due to increasing natural disasters and high rainfall to ensure our road network is safe not only for general use but also for emergency evacuations. An injection of funds is needed to be able to complete higher quality repairs to withstand heavy rainfall and extreme heat. 


MOTION 4


Motion: ALGA requests that the federal government allocate additional funding to councils to enable additional resources to ensure the timely delivery of infrastructure and regulatory services. 

National Objective:

Why is this a national issue and why should this be debated at the NGA? (Maximum 250 words)

There is little doubt that the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic has had a significant impact on the delivery of local government services. 
Whilst the federal and state governments focus on the economic recovery from the COVID pandemic, the historically low interest rates coupled with large government incentives/grants has resulted in a development boom. 
Councils do not have the capacity to deal with the heightened investment in infrastructure projects, the unprecedented increase in developments and the significant increase in the number of development assessments. This has led to a number of impacts such as delivery issues. This has also led to the outsourcing of projects to the private sector and resulting in inflated prices across the country.
Additionally, the ability of councils to service the regulatory requirements of developments has created a bottle neck in the timely approvals process.


MOTION 5


Motion: Advocacy for a substantive increase in Commonwealth Funded programs to assist local communities address climate change risk and adaptation.

That the National General Assembly continues to advocate to the Federal Government for provision of funding for Local Government Authorities to prepare climate change risk assessments and adaptation plans to inform Federal resilience funding priorities.

National Objective:

Why is this a national issue and why should this be debated at the NGA? (Maximum 250 words)

Reducing community carbon emissions sources, grid electricity use and transport fuels, rely on state and federal policy and investment to deliver cost effective action. Consistency across Australia would greatly assist in ensuring a diligent and strategic approach for LGAs in developing responsible decision-making in response to climate change.

Summary of Key Arguments:

Background information and supporting arguments (Maximum 500 words)

Thirty four cities and shires in Australia have signed to the GLOBAL COVENANT of MAYORS for CLIMATE & ENERGY, the world’s largest cooperative effort among mayors and city leaders to reduce greenhouse gas emission, track progress, and prepare for the impacts of climate change (https://www.globalcovenantofmayors.org/). One of the benefits of joining this cooperative is the benefit of benchmarking Council’s efforts against a common standard, and having clear guidance about what best-practice responses to climate change involve.

Consistency in climate risk assessments and adaptation pathways for LGAs across Australia would ensure efficient and equitable approaches to: 

• Preparation of detailed risk assessments: comprehensive understanding of very high and high ranked risks, quantitative analysis, ranking importance
• Benchmarking LGAs current and future adaptation responses against relevant industries. 
• Facilitate multi criteria analyses of adaptation options to describe recommended priorities taking into consideration:

o Council’s own institutional and administrative capacity
o Costs
o Adverse impacts
o Benefits
o Co benefits
o Subsequent risks

• Cross dependency analysis.
• Consideration and funding for short term and long term options in response to high and very high risks.
• Highlight interim steps needed to progress, scoping work needed and implications.
• Describe consistent targets/indicators, and assign responsibilities.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR -Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen

1.     Endorses the following eight (8) Advisory Committees for the current Council term and accepts the recommended minor amendments outlined in the report:

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

1.   The Minutes of the Floodplain Management Committee Meeting held 8 December 2021 be received and noted; and

2.   The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

1. Murwillumbah CBD Levee Spillway and Rehabilitation
That the “Murwillumbah CBD Levee Spillway Modelling” document is reported to Council with a recommendation for it to be placed on public exhibition. 

2. Mooball Designated Flood Level(s)
That the “Mooball Village Flood Risk Assessment” document, and proposed changes to DCP-A3 in line with its recommendations, are reported to Council with a recommendation for it to be placed on public exhibition. 

5. Wardrop Valley Future Urban Land Release Area
That the committee supports in principle the development of a contemporary Growth Management and Housing Strategy, and recommends that Council strongly considers options for alternate land release areas, if needed, to be flood free. 

3.  That the “Murwillumbah CBD Levee Spillway Modelling” and “Mooball Village Flood Risk Assessment” reports be reported to Council at a future Council meeting for them to be considered for exhibition.

4.  That Council holds an on-site workshop on the Mooball Village Flood Risk Assessment to understand the implications for flood planning on new and existing residential development in Mooball prior to any public exhibition of this document.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR -Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST -None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -Cr Warren Polglase
