RESOLVED that the Mayor urgently write to the Minister for Planning and Housing in respect of the “Cudgen Connections” redevelopment proposal and planning proposal (seeking to create a private hospital, medi-hotel, allied healthcare, rehab pool, gym, aged care facilities, essential worker housing, community hub, farmers’ market, eateries and an amphitheatre set in parklands on 5.7 hectares) on the site known as No. 741 Cudgen Road Cudgen, and currently in a pre-lodgement consultation phase with Council, identifying these critical concerns:

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd from Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church:

"Gracious God,

We are being pushed from one crisis into the next and we have no chance to rest, recover, or process what we are going through. It is hard not to be overwhelmed. We are burdened by layers of grief. Have mercy.

Our hearts are broken over the floods that have afflicted our community and manyother local government areas.  We feel so powerless against these forces of nature, despite our best efforts to prepare and respond.

We pray for those who have lost loved ones, homes, and businesses. Be with us in our deep sadness. We are grateful for the expressions of care we see, despite our community being under strain for so long.

Please grant both Councillors and staff strength and resilience in yet another period of uncertainty and complexity. We pray for all those who go into dangerous situations to make them safer for others. We ask for appropriate and timely assistance from other levels of government.  Guide Council and our community in the hard work of recovery.

Thank you for Jesus' invitation to find rest for our souls when we are weary and burdened.

Please grant your grace, mercy, and peace to all here tonight."

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RECOMMENDED that:


1. Development Application DA20/0443 for alterations and additions to an existing shopping centre (Banora Shopping Village) including signage at Lot 1 DP 848125 No. 59 Darlington Drive, Banora Point be approved subject to the conditions attached the report for this item.

2.     Amendment to Consent Condition 11 as highlighted in red below:

11.          A detailed Plan of Landscaping containing no priority weed species and with a minimum 80% of total plant numbers comprised of local native species to the Tweed Shire is to be submitted that ensures areas for tree canopy species in the carpark areas are large enough to sustain mature trees and approved by Council's General Manager or his delegate prior to the issue of a Construction Certificate.  Local native species are to comprise appropriate species selected from the Tweed Shire Native Species Planting Guide available online at: <http://www.tweed.nsw.gov.au/Controls/NativeSpeciesPlanting/Landing.aspx>

The plan of landscaping must also include a replacement planting (ratio of 1:1) of an advanced specimen (45 Litre stock size) along the Darlington Drive Road Reserve in the proximity of the Poinciana (Delonix regia) which is to be removed under this consent.


3.    ATTACHMENT 4 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e) information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law


Cr Reece Byrnes attended the meeting at 6.12PM.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

Cr James Owen
Cr Warren Polglase

RECOMMENDED that:

A. Development Application DA20/0965.01 for an amendment to Development Consent DA20/0965 for the filling of land and associated drainage works of Lot 21 DP 1082482 Tweed Coast Road, Chinderah be approved subject to the following changes being made to the consent conditions:

1. Delete Condition No. 1 and replace with new Condition No. 1A which reads as follows:

1A. The development shall be completed in accordance with the Statement of Environmental Effects, except where modified by this application, and Plans Nos 020 rev D, 030 rev B, 031 rev C, 040 rev D, 041 rev C, 042 rev B, 043 rev C, 044 rev B, 045 rev C, 046 rev E, 050 rev C, 051 rev B, 052 rev B, 072 rev E, 073 rev G, 090 rev C, 091 rev C, 092 rev C, 093 rev C, 094 rev D, 095 rev C, 096 rev D, 100 rev E prepared by Mortons Urban Solutions and dated 13.10.20.

2. Insert new Condition No. 1.1 which reads as follows:

1.1 The filling works associated with this development are to carried out in the following phases:

Phase I - A maximum of 24,000m3 of material to be transported to the Altona fill site (Lot 21 DP 1082482) from the adjacent Kings Coast development site.

Phase II - As a combined total, not more than 12 trucks per hour inbound and 12 trucks per hour  outbound (total 24 movements per hour) is permitted to access / egress the:

• Altona fill site (Lot 21 DP 1082482);
• Sand extraction facility, approved under Project Approval MP05_0103B; and
• Phase II works shall not proceed until the passing bay extension at the Altona Road access is completed to Council’s satisfaction.

3. Insert new Condition No. 1.2 which reads as follows:

1.2 A maximum of 24,000m3 of fill may be sourced from the adjoining Kings Coast development provided the works are undertaken under a Traffic Control Plan utilising Traffic Controllers at the intersection of Crescent Street and Altona Road, prepared by an RMS accredited person and submitted to and endorsed by the Principal Certifier prior to such works commencing.

Additional Traffic Controllers are required at the site access should the delivery of material proceed prior to the passing bay being extended.

A log book is to be kept of the Phase I daily truck movements as evidence of the progress and the log book is to be submitted to Council at the completion of Phase I works.

4. Insert new Condition No. 1.3 which reads as follows:

1.3 A combined total of not more than 12 trucks per hour inbound and 12 trucks per hour outbound (totalling 24 movements per hour) is permitted to access / egress the Altona fill site (Lot 21 DP 1082482) and the Cudgen Lakes Sand Quarry (approved under Project Approval MP05_0103B).

In this regard, a log is to be kept of the daily truck movements at each operation and be submitted to Council every two weeks to Council's General Manager or delegate.

5. Insert new Condition No. 8.1 which reads as follows:

8.1 Prior to the importation of any waste (including fill or soil) from the south-east Queensland fire ant biosecurity zone, the supplier of the waste must demonstrate that a current biosecurity instrument permit issued by the Qld Department of Agriculture and Fisheries is in place.

6. Insert new Condition No. 8.2 which reads as follows:

8.2 Any importation of waste (including fill or soil) from the south-east Queensland fire ant biosecurity zone must be in accordance with a current biosecurity instrument permit issued by the Qld Department of Agriculture and Fisheries.

7. Insert new Condition No. 8.3 which reads as follows:

8.3 Any importation of waste (including fill or soil) from the south-east Queensland fire ant biosecurity zone must be in accordance with NSW Department of Primary Industries requirements.

8. Delete Condition No. 14 and replace with new Condition No. 14A which reads as follows:

14A Application shall be made to Tweed Shire Council under Section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 for works pursuant to this consent located within the road reserve. Application shall include (but not limited to) engineering plans and specifications undertaken in accordance with Councils Development Design and Construction Specifications for the following required works:

(a) Construct the access and extended passing bay in accordance with Plan Na. 27305-ALTBE-100 rev E prepared by Mortons Urban Solutions dated 13.10.21, unless agreed otherwise by Tweed Shire Council.
(b) Provide a bitumen sealed pavement, min 22m long between the edge of existing road pavement and entry gates.
(c) The access is to be of sufficient width to allow two heavy vehicles to pass.
(d) The access is to incorporate a 375dia RCP within the existing table drain in accordance with Tweed Shire Council Standards.
(e) A shake down area is to be provide immediately inside the site access gates.

The above mentioned engineering plan submission must include copies of compliance certificates relied upon and details relevant ta but not limited to the following:
• Road works/furnishings
• Stormwater drainage
• Water and sewerage works
• Sediment and erosion control plans
• Location of all services/conduits
• Traffic Control Plan (as applicable)

Where Council is requested to issue a Construction Certificate for works associated with this consent, the abovementioned works can be incorporated as part of the Construction Certificate application, to enable one single approval to be issued. Separate approval under Section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 will then NOT be required.

9. Delete Condition No. 18 and replace with new Condition No. 18A which reads as follows:

18A Prior to commencement of any works onsite associated with this development consent or prior to issue of construction certificate whichever occurs first, the following amended development layout plans shall be submitted to Council and approved by Council's General Manager or delegate to show the following:

a. Submit an amended staging plan which has the areas identified as 'Offset planting areas' shown on Figure 2.25 Cudgen Village Indicative Structure Plan in Tweed Development Control Plan Part B26 – Kingscliff Development Control Plan Version 2.1 adopted 04.06.2020, to be assigned to the final stages of filling. This condition shall not in any way preclude achievement of the required maximum five (5) year time frame for removal of fill within this area.

10. Delete Condition No. 23 and replace with new Condition No. 23A which reads as follows:

23A Notwithstanding the issue of this development consent, separate consent from Council under Section 138 of the Roads Act 1993, must be obtained prior to any works taking place on a public road including the construction of a new (or modification of the existing) driveway access (or modification of access).

Applications for consent under Section 138 must be submitted on Council's standard application form and be accompanied by the required attachments and prescribed fee.

NOTE: The site access for delivery vehicles shall be restricted to the nominated location within Altona Road.

11. Delete Condition No. 33.

12. Delete Condition No. 48.

B.     ATTACHMENT 3 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

PROPOSED that Council endorse:

1.   The draft submission (Attachment 4) which outlines Council’s preferred zoning and additions for Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to the Department’s  proposed new ’Opt In’ LEP Clauses identified in the Draft Standard Instrument (Local Environmental Plans) Amendment (Agritourism) Order 2021, subject to a qualification that:

a)    the proposed newly permitted with consent uses of “Agritourism”, “Farm experience premises”, “Farm gate premises”, and “Farm Stay Accommodation”, only be permitted in the RUI Primary Production and RU2 Rural Landscape zones of the Tweed LEP, and on sites greater than 10 hectares in size; and

b)   to add the new optional Clauses 5.23 Farm stay accommodation and 5.24 Farm gate premises in the LEP, retaining the numerical threshold capacities and objectives recommended by the Department in the Draft Order, with the exception of Clause 5.23 2(d), which it is requested that the clause should read “the maximum number of moveable dwellings used for accommodation of guests will be no more than 3” (instead of 6); and

2.   The draft submission be amended in accordance with Point 1, and the required on-line nomination form be completed and a copy of Council’s endorsed submission be forwarded to the Department of Planning and Environment.

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RECOMMENDED that Council:

1.   Writes to the Tweed Shire rural industry groups and places the proposed amended submission on public exhibition for a period of 28 days for seeking their feedback.

2.   Seeks an extension of 12 months for a submission from the Department of Planning and if successful requests a further report to the May 2022 Council meeting.

Amendment 1 was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

RESOLVED that, in respect to Contract RFO2021131 Anchorage Island Canal Estate Revetment Renewal:


1. Council awards the offer to Envirostruct Services Pty Ltd (ABN 98 093 452 325) for the amount of $1,498,800.00 (exclusive of GST) and $1,648,680.00 (inclusive of GST)

2. The General Manager be granted delegated authority to approve appropriately deemed variations to the contract and those variations be reported to Council at finalisation of the contract.

3. ATTACHMENTS 1 and 2 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:-

(d)  commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
(i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
(ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or
(iii) reveal a trade secret

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  Nil

RESOLVED that the recommendations of the Ordinary Planning Committee Meeting held Thursday 3 March 2022 be adopted.

8.1       Development Application DA20/0443 for alterations and additions to an existing shopping centre (Banora Shopping Village) including signage at Lot 1 DP 848125 No.59 Darlington Drive, Banora Point

 

RECOMMENDED that:

1.     Development Application DA20/0443 for alterations and additions to an existing shopping centre (Banora Shopping Village) including signage at Lot 1 DP 848125 No. 59 Darlington Drive, Banora Point be approved subject to the conditions attached the report for this item.

2.     Amendment to Consent Condition 11 as highlighted in red below:

11.          A detailed Plan of Landscaping containing no priority weed species and with a minimum 80% of total plant numbers comprised of local native species to the Tweed Shire is to be submitted that ensures areas for tree canopy species in the carpark areas are large enough to sustain mature trees and approved by Council's General Manager or his delegate prior to the issue of a Construction Certificate.  Local native species are to comprise appropriate species selected from the Tweed Shire Native Species Planting Guide available online at: <http://www.tweed.nsw.gov.au/Controls/NativeSpeciesPlanting/Landing.aspx>

The plan of landscaping must also include a replacement planting (ratio of 1:1) of an advanced specimen (45 Litre stock size) along the Darlington Drive Road Reserve in the proximity of the Poinciana (Delonix regia) which is to be removed under this consent.

3.    ATTACHMENT 4 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e) information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

 

8.2       Development Application DA20/0965.01 for amendment to Development Consent DA20/0965 for earthworks and associated drainage at Lot 21 DP 1082482 Tweed Coast Road Chinderah

 

RECOMMENDED that:

A. Development Application DA20/0965.01 for an amendment to Development Consent DA20/0965 for the filling of land and associated drainage works of Lot 21 DP 1082482 Tweed Coast Road, Chinderah be approved subject to the following changes being made to the consent conditions:

1. Delete Condition No. 1 and replace with new Condition No. 1A which reads as follows:

1A. The development shall be completed in accordance with the Statement of Environmental Effects, except where modified by this application, and Plans Nos 020 rev D, 030 rev B, 031 rev C, 040 rev D, 041 rev C, 042 rev B, 043 rev C, 044 rev B, 045 rev C, 046 rev E, 050 rev C, 051 rev B, 052 rev B, 072 rev E, 073 rev G, 090 rev C, 091 rev C, 092 rev C, 093 rev C, 094 rev D, 095 rev C, 096 rev D, 100 rev E prepared by Mortons Urban Solutions and dated 13.10.20.

2. Insert new Condition No. 1.1 which reads as follows:

1.1 The filling works associated with this development are to carried out in the following phases:

Phase I - A maximum of 24,000m3 of material to be transported to the Altona fill site (Lot 21 DP 1082482) from the adjacent Kings Coast development site.

Phase II - As a combined total, not more than 12 trucks per hour inbound and 12 trucks per hour  outbound (total 24 movements per hour) is permitted to access / egress the:

• Altona fill site (Lot 21 DP 1082482);
• Sand extraction facility, approved under Project Approval MP05_0103B; and
• Phase II works shall not proceed until the passing bay extension at the Altona Road access is completed to Council’s satisfaction.

3. Insert new Condition No. 1.2 which reads as follows:

1.2 A maximum of 24,000m3 of fill may be sourced from the adjoining Kings Coast development provided the works are undertaken under a Traffic Control Plan utilising Traffic Controllers at the intersection of Crescent Street and Altona Road, prepared by an RMS accredited person and submitted to and endorsed by the Principal Certifier prior to such works commencing.

Additional Traffic Controllers are required at the site access should the delivery of material proceed prior to the passing bay being extended.

A log book is to be kept of the Phase I daily truck movements as evidence of the progress and the log book is to be submitted to Council at the completion of Phase I works.

4. Insert new Condition No. 1.3 which reads as follows:

1.3 A combined total of not more than 12 trucks per hour inbound and 12 trucks per hour outbound (totalling 24 movements per hour) is permitted to access / egress the Altona fill site (Lot 21 DP 1082482) and the Cudgen Lakes Sand Quarry (approved under Project Approval MP05_0103B).

In this regard, a log is to be kept of the daily truck movements at each operation and be submitted to Council every two weeks to Council's General Manager or delegate.

5. Insert new Condition No. 8.1 which reads as follows:

8.1 Prior to the importation of any waste (including fill or soil) from the south-east Queensland fire ant biosecurity zone, the supplier of the waste must demonstrate that a current biosecurity instrument permit issued by the Qld Department of Agriculture and Fisheries is in place.

6. Insert new Condition No. 8.2 which reads as follows:

8.2 Any importation of waste (including fill or soil) from the south-east Queensland fire ant biosecurity zone must be in accordance with a current biosecurity instrument permit issued by the Qld Department of Agriculture and Fisheries.

7. Insert new Condition No. 8.3 which reads as follows:

8.3 Any importation of waste (including fill or soil) from the south-east Queensland fire ant biosecurity zone must be in accordance with NSW Department of Primary Industries requirements.

8. Delete Condition No. 14 and replace with new Condition No. 14A which reads as follows:

14A Application shall be made to Tweed Shire Council under Section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 for works pursuant to this consent located within the road reserve. Application shall include (but not limited to) engineering plans and specifications undertaken in accordance with Councils Development Design and Construction Specifications for the following required works:

(a)    Construct the access and extended passing bay in accordance with Plan Na. 27305-ALTBE-100 rev E prepared by Mortons Urban Solutions dated 13.10.21, unless agreed otherwise by Tweed Shire Council.
(b)    Provide a bitumen sealed pavement, min 22m long between the edge of existing road pavement and entry gates.
(c)    The access is to be of sufficient width to allow two heavy vehicles to pass.
(d)    The access is to incorporate a 375dia RCP within the existing table drain in accordance with Tweed Shire Council Standards.
(e)    A shake down area is to be provide immediately inside the site access gates.

The above mentioned engineering plan submission must include copies of compliance certificates relied upon and details relevant ta but not limited to the following:
• Road works/furnishings
• Stormwater drainage
• Water and sewerage works
• Sediment and erosion control plans
• Location of all services/conduits
• Traffic Control Plan (as applicable)

Where Council is requested to issue a Construction Certificate for works associated with this consent, the abovementioned works can be incorporated as part of the Construction Certificate application, to enable one single approval to be issued. Separate approval under Section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 will then NOT be required.

9. Delete Condition No. 18 and replace with new Condition No. 18A which reads as follows:

18A Prior to commencement of any works onsite associated with this development consent or prior to issue of construction certificate whichever occurs first, the following amended development layout plans shall be submitted to Council and approved by Council's General Manager or delegate to show the following:

a. Submit an amended staging plan which has the areas identified as 'Offset planting areas' shown on Figure 2.25 Cudgen Village Indicative Structure Plan in Tweed Development Control Plan Part B26 – Kingscliff Development Control Plan Version 2.1 adopted 04.06.2020, to be assigned to the final stages of filling. This condition shall not in any way preclude achievement of the required maximum five (5) year time frame for removal of fill within this area.

10. Delete Condition No. 23 and replace with new Condition No. 23A which reads as follows:

23A Notwithstanding the issue of this development consent, separate consent from Council under Section 138 of the Roads Act 1993, must be obtained prior to any works taking place on a public road including the construction of a new (or modification of the existing) driveway access (or modification of access).

Applications for consent under Section 138 must be submitted on Council's standard application form and be accompanied by the required attachments and prescribed fee.

NOTE: The site access for delivery vehicles shall be restricted to the nominated location within Altona Road.

11. Delete Condition No. 33.

12. Delete Condition No. 48.

B.     ATTACHMENT 3 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

 

8.3       Briefing Paper on Employment Zones Reform

 

RECOMMENDED that Council receives and notes the Return Translation Details provided as an attachment to this report relating to the NSW Department of Planning and Environment “Employment Zones Reform”.

 

8.4       Briefing on a New Approach to Rezoning in NSW Discussion Paper

 

RECOMMENDED that Council:

1.    Endorses the staff submission provided as an attachment to this report relating to the NSW Department of Planning and Environment “A new approach to rezonings Discussion paper”.

2.   Does not support the 7 day acceptance period for new planning proposal as it is unworkable and supports at least a 21 day acceptance period.

3.   Has concerns about the reduction in weight placed on community submissions for planning proposals.

4.   Does not support the penalties proposed for Council in the timeframes for the assessment of planning proposals.

8.5       Agritourism and Small-Scale Agriculture Development - Proposed 'Opt In' Clauses to Amend Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014

 

RECOMMENDED that Council:

1.   Writes to the Tweed Shire rural industry groups and places the proposed amended submission on public exhibition for a period of 28 days for seeking their feedback.

2.   Seeks an extension of 12 months for a submission from the Department of Planning and if successful requests a further report to the May 2022 Council meeting.

 

8.6       Tweed Shire Council Submission on the draft SEPP Design and Place Exhibition Documents

 

RECOMMENDED that:

1. Council endorses the Council officers draft submission related to the draft State Environmental Planning Policy Design and Place (D&P SEPP) and associated guidelines.

2. Any amendments or inclusions resolved by Council be included as an addendum in the final submission to be forwarded to the Department of Planning and Environment by 25 March 2022.

3.    Council requests that Tweed Shire is included in the new BASIX requirements proposed to be applied to the rest of NSW.


The Motion was Carried

VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd.


"Gracious God, 

We struggle to comprehend the extent of the devastation our community has suffered in such a short time.  For those who have lost their lives, we mourn them and ask for your peace and comfort to their families and friends.

We acknowledge the members of staff who worked so hard re-establishing essential services, even while many of them were personally affected by the flood.  We pray for their safety and renewed strength as they continue to rebuild and enable us to recover.
We are deeply thankful for the many volunteers from the SES, individuals, and members of Defence who have come into our community to help.  We are so encouraged by the generosity of local friends and strangers giving time, donations, and care.  

For those rebuilding their lives and businesses, please grant renewed hope and resilience, and reminders that they are not alone.

Thank you for Council’s leadership, their advocacy on our behalf with other tiers of government, and the good work being done in the Recovery Centre.  Please give wisdom as they coordinate repairs and rebuilding.

Help us to be able to grieve appropriately, and to find rest for our souls and bodies in this demanding time.  
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:

1.     Approves the procurement of Large-scale Generation Certificates (LGCs) not from wood or waste burning at an estimated cost of $110,000/year including GST for 2021-22 to meet the electricity-related carbon reduction target of 25% less electricity-related carbon emissions (as tonnes CO2-e) than 2016-17 by 2022 funded from existing electricity budgets excluding the Streetlight Electricity and be pro-rated based on electricity usage between the General, Sewer and Water Funds.

2.     Includes in its Long Term Financial Plan an allowance from the existing electricity budgets for the purchase of Large Scale Generation Certificates (LGCs) not from wood or waste burning of $20,000/year for 2022-23 and 2023-24 to meet the electricity-related carbon reduction target of 25% less electricity-related carbon emissions (as tonnes CO2-e) than 2016-17 by 2022, and $110,000/year including GST for the period 2024-25 to 2029/30 to meet the electricity-related carbon reduction target of 50% less electricity-related carbon emissions (as tonnes CO2-e) than 2016-17 by 2025 and that actual costs be pro-rated based on electricity usage between the General, Sewer and Water Funds.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins from the Murwillumbah Church of Christ:

"Dear Loving and Gracious God:

You promise to be here when we call upon You… and there is certainly much upon our hearts & minds. 

Bush fires, Covid, Housing shortages, the rise in the cost of living, unemployment, uncertainty in World affairs & now these recent events of flooding have left so many with nothing except a feeling of destitution & hopelessness. People’s homes, possessions, memories, livelihoods, lives… have been destroyed & washed away.

Father, it is during these times that we are simply lost in what to say or think. Our thoughts & emotions become so overwhelmed with it all that we struggle to know how to put our grief & pain into words. 

So may my prayer simply be… Please help us Lord… for we are in great need & now asking You for Your help & assistance. May You give council wisdom & understanding in how to approach & address each problem as You would… being a shining light of hope & blessings for all those who are in need.

So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 

That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.     

May You answer us in the day we call:         Amen."

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RECOMMENDED that Development Application DA21/0261 for multi dwelling housing comprising 6 x 3 bedroom units and 1 x 4 bed unit, including tree removal at Lot 619 DP 508200 No. 10 Willow Avenue and Lot 632 DP 216389 No. 12 Willow Avenue, Bogangar be deferred:

1. To enable Council officers to prepare a response to questions raised by Councillors and further public submissions in respect of the Business Paper report, addressing the following issues:

a. Flood risk
b. Loss of vegetation
c. Internal design layout of proposed dwellings
d. Adequacy of side setbacks
e. Impacts on privacy and views of adjoining neighbours
f. Other planning and site constraint issues
g. Cultural Heritage consultation that has occurred to date
h. Stepping back from the front boundary
i. The lack of water retention required on site;

2. For the proponent be asked to provide more plan detail and information relating to the deferred commencement condition relating to the retention of Tree No. 7; and

3. A further report be submitted to the May Planning Committee Meeting.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE AGAINST - None

Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.

Nil.

RESOLVED that, in respect to augmenting RFO2021110 to provide full service cement stabilisation works for the 21/21 program, Council resolves:


1. That a satisfactory result would not be achieved by inviting tenders due to the lack of competitive or reliable Bidders following the natural disaster event on 28 February 2022 and approves the use of a selective tender process. 

2.     Awards the amended offer from Ellis Profiling Pty Ltd ABN 96144885334, which includes the full service, for the amount of $761,871.97  (exclusive of GST) and $881,020.47  (inclusive of GST)

3. The General Manager be granted delegated authority to approve appropriately deemed variations to the contract and those variations be reported to Council at finalisation of the contract.

4. ATTACHMENTS 1, 2 and 3 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:-

(d)  commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
(i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
(ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or
(iii) reveal a trade secret

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins


Dear Father,
Thank you for being here for us in this time of need. 
It’s wonderful to know that You are always there to take the time to listen & care about the things we have to say.
Father, I thank You for our councillors:
Chris Cherry, Reece Byrnes, James Owen, Meredith Dennis, Rhiannon Brinsmead, Warren Polglase, Nola Firth, And our Director: Troy Green
Father, bless these people as they seek to make the Tweed a shire where people love to live. That our councillors will look after our people and places, exploring all opportunities and making them proud of their passionate approach.
May our councillors tonight also care about each other, choosing to be here, and knowing that we are all in this together… having conversations where everyone can contribute and everyone is willing to have a go.
We also look forward to the contributions & gifts of service our councillors will bring to the Tweed Shire. Again, bless each one of them I pray.
So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 
That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.     
Thank You, Father… Amen.

Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that Council determines to implement the following flood assistance measures:

1.     The deferral of up to two quarters (6 months) of rate instalments with zero interest, to be repaid over a two (2) year period from 28 February 2022 where impact or hardship from flooding can be demonstrated.

2.     Reducing user-pay water notices, where water usage is abnormally high due to having to wash out premises following flood inundation, to the average of the previous 3 years property consumption as opposed to the actual consumption.

3.     For lessee's or licensees of Council land and/or buildings, provide a rent/license fee-free period, where the lessee/licensee is not able to utilise the premises due to the recent floods, from the time of the first flood event until re-occupation of the land/building.


The Motion was Carried

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Nola Firth

RESOLVED that:

1.     Council adopts the Road Reserve Vegetation in Urban Areas Policy with the following amendments:


In the ‘Road Reserve Landscaping Requirements’ section the sentence:
 
a)      Generally, the nature strip landscaping should feature mowable grass, free from rocks and loose stones and graded to even running contours
 
Be replaced with:
 
Generally, the nature strip landscaping should feature a mowable or hard surface footpath at least 1.2m wide which may be edged house-side with low plants such as native shrubs or grasses free from rocks and loose stones and graded to even running contours
 
b)      As Council acknowledges the value of vegetation within the nature strip and the benefits mature trees, in particular, bring to the community, landscaping beyond the standard grassed roadside nature strip is supported in principle.
 
Be replaced with:
 
As Council acknowledges the value of vegetation within the nature strip and the benefits mature trees and biodiversity, in particular, bring to the community, landscaping beyond the standard grassed roadside nature strip is supported in principle.


2.     Add in the definition of a description of an urban environment to which this policy applies.

3.     Add in a statement that Council encourages increasing the urban shade canopy in road verges and support our residents to be inspiring in their care for our environment and pockets of diversity without compromising public safety or the provision of our infrastructure.

  [OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL] [AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that Council:

1. Writes to the NSW Premier, Minister for Environment and Heritage, Minister for Regional NSW and Minister for Agriculture identifying that:

a.   Council requests that the NSW state government reconsiders the proposed exclusion of private native forestry from the operation of the NSW Koala SEPP 2021. This request is made on the basis of the following:

i. Recent assessment and mapping of koala habitat completed through a joint project of the University of Queensland, Southern Cross University, University of Sydney, Friends of the Koala and 4 northern rivers councils have identified significant and critical areas of koala habitat that would be able to be logged without assessment, consent or controls under this proposal.

ii. In the Tweed, and many other areas of the state, the target tree species and size class for forestry are the same trees most critical to koala habitat conservation.

b.   Council further requests that the proposed removal of council's consent role in relation to forestry is also reconsidered. In addition to removing council’s role in land use decision making in relation to environmental impacts, this also excludes council from being able to assess broader impacts including noise, threatened species (including koalas) dust, traffic, amenity (particularly in more closely settled areas such as the Tweed) and local infrastructure impacts. It is also noted that this aspect of the proposed changes goes well beyond the management of koalas and affects all forestry operations.

c.   Council notes that it is working collaboratively and positively with the NSW state government on a range of initiatives, especially through our regional partnerships and projects. The following key issues are identified and recommended for further consideration:

i. Land acquisition is a key strategy that requires further consideration to respond to the varying regional situations, especially in regard to prioritisation based on land value and parcel size.

ii. Management of the impact of the Pacific Motorway on koalas requires further consideration and actions where the current and projected high risk of koala road kill remains unaddressed.

iii. The absence of any specific legislative protection for koala habitat in NSW is highly significant and undermines the value of many of the conservation and recovery actions and investments.

d.    Requests that Schedule 1 of the NSW Koala SEPP 2021 be amended so that the SEPP applies to the whole of Tweed Shire including land zoned rural. Noting that Council has requested this amendment via several submissions on the SEPP and has yet to receive a response, and that precedence has been set with Sydney and Central Coast Councils.

2.     Officers investigate and prepare preliminary concepts and cost estimates and consult with the community on the installation of traffic calming devices along the 3km section of Clothiers Creek Road West of Bogangar with the aim of mitigating the ongoing issue of Koalas being hit by vehicles along this section of road.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd of the Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church:

"Gracious God, 

We stop at this time before you to acknowledge the many expressions of community we have experienced in these hard times.  Thank you for the many formal and informal structures that exist to help us and give us opportunities to care for others.

Thank you for the ongoing work of Council, and we pray for continued strength, wisdom, and resilience in their vital work for our region.  Please bless all the deliberations of this meeting and may it result in an even stronger community into the future, where people and places are well cared for.  Thank you for the committed, qualified, and highly capable staff of Council.

We recognise the contribution and potential of our youth.  Thank you for the many ways they are involved, and their passionate approach.  May we be able to work with them for an ongoing legacy where the vulnerable are protected and each person is able to reach their full potential.  Help us to build strong foundations for an even better future.

 We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis

PROPOSED that Council:


1.     Opts-in to the optional clauses of the State Government's Draft Amendment to the Standard LEP Instrument, adopting the default objectives with the addition of the objectives outlined below and numerical controls, and lodge an online Agritourism Nomination Form for the same purpose:

5.23 Farm Stay Accommodation

c)  to enhance the viability and capacity of the land for primary production purposes

d)  to provide for low scale, low impact, unobtrusive and sustainable uses of the land

e)  to enhance the environment, restore wildlife corridors and waterways, and ensure no adverse environmental impacts

f) to ensure that agritourism uses are secondary to the primary use of primary production

g) to ensure State Significant and Regionally Significant farmlands continue to be utilised primarily for primary production.

5.24  Farm Experiences

c)  to enhance the viability and capacity of the land for primary production purposes

d)  to provide small scale, low impact, unobtrusive and sustainable uses of the land

e)  to enhance the environment, restore wildlife corridors and waterways, and ensure no adverse environmental impacts

f) to ensure that agritourism uses are secondary to the primary use of primary production

g) to ensure State Significant and Regionally Significant farmlands continue to be utilised primarily for primary production.

2.    Advises the Department that ‘agritourism’ and its subsets of ‘farm gate premises’ and ‘farm experience premises’: a) Only applies to the RU1 & RU2 zones, and b) Nominates these uses as ‘permitted with consent’ in these zones

3.    Advises the Department of Planning and Environment of its resolution to ‘opt-in’ to the optional clauses, adopting the specified objectives and numerical controls, and lodge an online Agritourism Nomination Form for the same purpose;

4.    Advises the Department of Planning and Environment that Council does not support the proposed Exempt and Complying code as put forward in the Explanation of Intended Effects and would not support its application to the Tweed Shire and requests an exclusion from this process.

5.    Urgently advances the Rural Land Strategy Action 18 to conduct a rating review as an incentive to ensure that farmland is utilised for productive agricultural purposes.

6.    Council writes to the Department of Planning and Environment and seek an urgent written confirmation that the proposed exempt and complying development controls will be publicly exhibited and community input sought prior to the introduction of those controls.

SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDERS

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RECOMMENDED that Standing Orders be suspended to discuss the alternate motion.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)


RESUMPTION OF STANDING ORDERS

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RECOMMENDED that Standing Orders be resumed.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Warren Polglase

PROPOSED that Council ‘opt-out’ and not support inclusion of optional clauses.

The Amendment 1 was Lost

VOTE FOR - Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

AMENDMENT 2

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis

RECOMMENDED that Council in respect of the State Government's Draft Amendment to the Standard LEP Instrument, relating to agritourism controls:

1.    Writes to the Department of Planning and Environment and seek an urgent meeting to clarify the State Governments intent as to whether they will publicly exhibit the proposed exempt and complying development provisions.

2.    Identify that Council is extremely concerned about the advancement of these draft provisions without further public exhibition and community input.

3.    That Council seeks to defer its decision of whether to opt-in to the current LEP clauses and permissibility until clearer direction is provided by the Department in respect of points 2 and 3.

The Amendment 2 was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

Local Government Act

(d)     commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
(i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
(ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or
(iii) reveal a trade secret


ALTERNATE MOTION


Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr James Owen

RECOMMENDED that Council:

1.    Endorses the waiver of an architectural design competition in lieu of an architectural design review process as endorsed by the NSW Government Architect over the Tweed Mall Shopping Centre site relating to a master-plan/concept development application process and proposed commercial building in the south-west corner of the site and that written correspondence confirming Council’s endorsement of the waiver be forwarded to the NSW Government Architect.  This is subject to GANSW in co-ordination with Council and the proponents facilitating the design review process including establishing, administering, and hosting the design review sessions, appointment and composition of panel members and taking of minutes and distribution of design advice from the panel meetings;

2.    Delegates the selection of Council’s design representative on the architectural design review panel to the General Manager;

3.    Advises the landowner proponents of Council’s likely fees and charges based on an hourly rate as specified within Council's Fees and Charges 2021/2022 Revenue Policy;

4.    Advises the landowner proponents who are engaging in Council’s development assessment panel process to ensure statutory planning considerations and relevant development control, standards and guidelines are being appropriately considered as part of the design review process;

5.    Requires the design review process to demonstrate a high standard of design excellence that provides significant improvement to the streetscape and building design through:

  • Building, urban design and landscape design which pays homage to Tweed Shire’s internationally significant environment and significant Aboriginal Cultural heritage;
  • Buildings achieve high standards of sustainable and biophhillic design to carry us into the future and include where practical green walls, green roof areas and zero / low carbon operations;
  • Preparation of an integrated landscape design concept that demonstrates generous landscape planting areas and substantial areas of landscaped front setbacks, to improve the visual and health amenity, reduce urban heat island effect, noise and pollution impacts, whilst not compromising the functioning of a future light rail station, and which maintain the visual access to the street frontages of any future Tweed Mall redevelopment; and
  • Activated uses to the ground level and public accessibility of the Bay and Wharf Street interfaces, and designed to achieve a high level of pedestrian amenity such as shady seating and comfort befitting of the 'key site' locations.

6.    Considers a further report at the conclusion of the architecture design review panel process to inform Council of the design review panel recommendations and outcomes over the site; and

7.    ATTACHMENTS 1-5 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(d)     commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
 (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
 (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or
 (iii) reveal a trade secret


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Nola Firth
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd of Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church:

"Gracious God, 

Our hearts are with those who continue to grieve as a result of the floods.  Many have been re-traumatised by the recent rains and are still suffering as they rebuild their lives.  Your word calls us to bear one another’s burdens and we thank you for the many ways this is happening.  Please grant us endurance, patience, and grace as we deal kindly with others and are mindful of their struggles.  

We pray that the state and federal response to our local crisis will not be distracted but will be timely, appropriate, equitable, and compassionate.  Thank you for the advocacy of Council on our behalf and may they be encouraged by an appropriate response from other tiers of government.  Continue to be with Council staff as they work hard to restore infrastructure and serve our region in so many ways.

Please be with each Councillor and our Mayor as they bear a heavy burden through this time.  Thank you for their commitment to our community and please grant them all they need, even to find joy in their service in this time of trial.
  
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen. "

RESOLVED that:


1. The following tabled Petition(s) be received and noted.


• Petition containing  2281 signatories, of which 1443 were valid signatures, and received on 3 May 2022 entitled "Concerned Citizens of Bogangar, Cabarita Beach & Tweed Shire Assoc.  COMMUNITY AND QUALITY SURVEY Norries Headland Upper Carpark" advising as follows:

"I Do Not agree with the proposed parking changes at the Northern end of the Carpark."

2.     Council notes the petition  entitled "Petition from the Residents of Ridgeback Road Leeward Terrace and Charles Street - Tweed Conservation Zone Review" containing 58 signatories received on 17 May 2022 advising as follows:

"I refer to the proposed rezoning of C2 land in the Razorback Ridge area to R5 under the auspices of "environmental protection".

Currently the vegetation in the C2 zoned land and the rear of 18 residential blocks with steep rear bush (largely unbuildable) boundaries provide several important ecological benefits including:
  • huge attraction to birds resting and nesting (at least 9 species identified by residents)
  • cooling effects of forest in summer and to protection of a wind break in stormy weather
  • environmental beauty in an area with already diminishing native bush attributes
  • protection of the Minjungbal people's bird legend site

If rezoned to R5 as proposed, as access is from Charles Street, there will be increased traffic along the already busy Charles Street.

Any reduction of or infringement into this already fragile ecological area would most certainly be detrimental and I/we strongly object to the proposed R5 rezoning of C2 land on Razorback Ridge."


was considered at a meeting held with key staff and councillors in attendance at the first Community Strategic Plan workshop with a large group of Razorback property owners. The meeting was productive and allayed most concerns.

3.     A workshop be scheduled to address the petition from the Cabarita Residents relating to the Norries Headland Master Plan.

RESOLVED that:


1.   The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 7 April 2022 be received and noted, and

2.   The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1 Commercial Road, Murwillumbah
The 'no stopping' zone on Commercial Road, Murwillumbah, approaching Wharf Street be extended to 20 metres from the marked pedestrian crossing and Council officers contact Australia Post to request a relocation of the post box.
 
6.2 Nullum Street, Murwillumbah
That Council approves the upgrading of the Children's Crossing on Nullum Street, Murwillumbah adjacent to the Sathya Sai School to a raised wombat crossing in principle, and a detailed design be provided to Transport for NSW for comment.
 
6.3 Murwillumbah Cycle Club, 2022 Race Events
That the proposed Murwillumbah Cycle Club Events from March to October 2022 be supported, subject to:
a.   NSW Police approval being obtained.
b.   Endorsement of the event by Cycling Queensland.
c.   Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
d.   The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
e.   Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.
f.   All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
g.   Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
h.   Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
i.   That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
j.   The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
k.   The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
 
7.1 Keith Compton Drive, Tweed Heads
That the existing No Stopping length on Keith Compton Drive, Tweed Heads in front of no. 64-66 be reduced by 18m towards the roundabout.  
 
7.2 First Avenue, Tweed Heads
The installation of "No Stopping 6am -12 Midday Tuesday Only" signage be installed on First Avenue, Tweed Heads be supported.
 
7.4 Pedestrian Facilities - Kingscliff and Bogangar
That the installation of pedestrian refuges on Kingscliff Street near Wommin Bay Road, Kingscliff; Sutherland Street near Orient Street, Kingscliff; and on Hastings Road near Towners Avenue, Bogangar is supported in principle and a detailed design be provided to Transport for NSW for comment.
 
7.5 Enid Street, Tweed Heads
The installation of a convex safety mirror within the road reserves are not supported by Transport for NSW.  The request for a convex mirror on Enid Street, Tweed Heads opposite the driveway of 11 Enid Street, Tweed Heads is therefore not supported.  The Body Corporate is requested to manage the placement of its garbage bins to minimise their impact on road users.  As previously advised it is recommended that a 'speed hump' be installed within the driveway on private property to improve safety for pedestrians on Enid Street.  The body corporate should also consider the installation of a 'stop sign' on their property before entering Enid Street. 
 
7.6 Terranora Road, Terranora
That a "No Right Turn 8:00am to 9:30am, 2:30pm to 4:00pm School Days" sign be installed on the eastern approach to the school drop off / pick up zone in Terranora Road, Terranora.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis

PROPOSED that Council:

1.   Does not Opt-in to nominating permissible uses or adopting the optional clauses of the State Government's Draft Amendment to the Standard LEP Instrument, relating to new Agritourism use and activities;

2.   Advise the Department of Planning and Environment of this decision;

3.   A further report be brought back to Council that outlines the process involved in advancing a new Planning Proposal containing Tweed Council specific Agritourism controls, including the community consultation processes involved with this action.

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:
 
1.    Does not Opt-in to nominating permissible uses or adopting the optional clauses of the State Government's Draft Amendment to the Standard LEP Instrument, relating to new Agritourism use and activities, unless the State Government can guarantee that they are willing to incorporate all of the following Opt-in request:

PREFERRED OPT-IN REQUIREMENTS

A.    Opts-in to the optional clauses of the State Government's Draft Amendment to the Standard LEP Instrument, adopting the default objectives with the addition of the objectives outlined below and numerical controls:

5.23 Farm Stay Accommodation
c)    to enhance the viability and capacity of the land for primary production purposes
d)    to provide for low scale, low impact, unobtrusive and sustainable uses of the land
e)    to enhance the environment, restore wildlife corridors and waterways, and ensure no adverse environmental impacts
f)     to ensure that agritourism uses are secondary to the primary use of primary production
g)    to ensure State Significant and Regionally Significant farmlands continue to be utilised primarily for primary production.

5.24 Farm Experiences
c)    to enhance the viability and capacity of the land for primary production purposes
d)    to provide small scale, low impact, unobtrusive and sustainable uses of the land
e)    to enhance the environment, restore wildlife corridors and waterways, and ensure no adverse environmental impacts
f)     to ensure that agritourism uses are secondary to the primary use of primary production
g)    to ensure State Significant and Regionally Significant farmlands continue to be utilised primarily for primary production.

B.    The new definitions of ‘agritourism’ and its subsets of ‘farm gate premises’ and ‘farm experience premises’ only apply to the RU1 & RU2 zones, and are nominated as ‘permitted with consent’ in these zones.

C.    The proposed Code's SEPP relating to exempt and complying development provisions to be excluded from State Significant farmland.

2.    Advise the Department of Planning and Environment of this decision; and

3.    In the event that the State Government does not support Council’s requested Opt-in requirements, a further report be brought back to Council that outlines the process involved in advancing a new Planning Proposal containing Tweed Council specific agritourism controls, including the community consultation processes involved with this action.

Mr Troy Green (General Manager) attended at 4.04PM.

Amendment 1 was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins, Murwillumbah Church of Christ

"Dear Father,

Father, bless our Counsellors with favour this day as they gather together to guide, provide & watch over the Northern Rivers. That they may know and fulfill Your purposes. It’s not always an easy task, but You promise to give strength & wisdom to those who ask.

We ask You to bless all who have been appointed to serve as government leaders & our new Prime Minister Anthony Albanese with all wisdom, that they will be steadfast in what is upright for Australia and seeking to do every good work.

Father, thank you for the Tweed Shire Council leadership you have entrusted to us. Help them to be faithful in all of roles they have been given. In particular, I ask that they might be counsellors of truth, humility, and fairness. May our counsellors be focused on what is important for the people of the Tweed Shire. May they be servant leaders of all you have given into their care.

Father, I ask during this time today, that our councillors be mindful of each other, caring for one another and knowing that we are all in this together. Having conversations where everyone can contribute and everybody is willing to have a go.

So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true.

That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today. 

Thank You Father… Amen."

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr James Owen

PROPOSED that Council defer Development Application DA21/0989 for a recreation facility (outdoor) at Lot 2 DP 121377 No. 271 Carool Road, Carool to allow the applicant an opportunity to submit information to address all outstanding issues and deficiencies with application in the form of a comprehensive Request for Further Information Letter including but not limited to: 

• Traffic Impact Assessment Report
• Acoustic Assessment Report
• Stormwater Management Plan
• Bushfire Assessment Report 
• Habitat Restoration Plan
• Tree survey
• Ecological Constraints Analysis 
• Baseline Ecological Assessment (if required)
• Cut and fill Plan
• Stormwater Management Plan
• Details regarding erosion and sedimentation management 
• Details regarding potable water
• Details regarding public access to the facility 
• Further details regarding events including management of these events 
• Visual Impact Analysis 
• A Clause 4.6 Variation to Building Standards to Clause 4.3 Building Height for Shed 2 or amended plans lower height 
• Detailed plans for Concrete skate park, Asphalt Pump track, Dirt Jumps Zone, BMX Competition Jumps, Slopestyle Course, additional roads and car parking areas.
• Details to demonstrate that the proposal is compliant with DCP A2 with regard to access and car parking. 

The applicant would need to demonstrate that: 

• The indoor elements of the development are permissible with consent. 
• The application is consistent with the aims of the plan (Tweed LEP 2014) and Objectives of the RU2 Zone (Tweed LEP 2014). 
• Amenity impacts have been adequately addressed (including noise, light, traffic, stormwater).  
• Matters raised by Essential Energy have been addressed. 

The application would require referral/re-referral to:
• Council’s internal units including Development Engineering Unit, Building Unit, Environmental Health Section, Traffic Engineering Section, Sustainability and Environment Unit;
• Rural Fire Service;
• TBLALC (if required following consultation);
• Essential Energy; and
• Gold Coast Airport Authority.  

AMENDMENT 1


Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RECOMMENDED that:

A. Development Application DA21/0989 for a recreation facility (outdoor) at Lot 2 DP 121377 No. 271 Carool Road, Carool be refused for the following reasons:

1. The development proposal is not consistent with the Aims of Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed’s natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways, visual amenity and scenic routes, built environment, and cultural heritage.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

2. The development proposal is not consistent with RU2 Rural Landscape Zone objectives of Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014, specifically: 

a. to maintain the rural landscape character of the land;
b. to provide for a range of tourist and visitor accommodation-based land uses, including agri-tourism, eco-tourism and any other like tourism that is linked to an environmental, agricultural or rural industry use of the land.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.


3. The development proposal has not demonstrated that significant elements of the proposal (being the indoor recreation facilities) are permissible with consent in RU2 Rural Landscape Zone of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 -  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

4. The proposal exceeds the Maximum Building Height Development standard for the site set out in Clause 4.3 of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 and the application has not been accompanied by a request under Clause 4.6 of the Plan demonstrating that a variation can be supported.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

5. The development proposal has not demonstrated due consideration or compliance with Tweed Shire Development Control Plan 2008 Section A2 Car Parking and Access Code.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

6. The development proposal has not demonstrated that the proposed development, which is located on an elevated sloping site, will not result in adverse visual impacts or detract from the rural character of the area.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

7. The development proposal has not demonstrated due consideration of impacts associated with traffic volumes, traffic noise, stormwater / erosion or impacts on the natural environment.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979,

8 From the limited information provided with the application, it is considered that development proposal, as a result of its scale, design, operation is not suitable for the site.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

9. The development proposal has not demonstrated that the bushfire risk to the proposal has been appropriately addressed and that the site is suitable for the proposed development.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

10. The development proposal has not demonstrated that the risks from electricity infrastructure to the proposal has been appropriately addressed and that the site is suitable for the proposed development.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

11. On the basis of the information submitted, the development proposal, is not considered to be in the public interest.  Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

B. ATTACHMENTS 7 and 8 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

The Amendment was Carried

VOTE AGAINST - Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RECOMMENDED that:

1.  Council endorses the following strategies to be put into place by 1 July 2022 and reviewed before the end of 2022, to assist in reducing the current DA backlog and processing times:

THE ORGANISATION (Council Staff)

Development Assessment Panel (DAP) Meetings

  • DAP meetings to be retained but fewer meetings until end of 2022, then reviewed.
  • Meetings proposed to be held 1 day per fortnight, 2 appointments (vs currently 2 days per week, one appointment on each day), and that these appointments be allocated for the most complex of proposals. All other enquiries can be via duty officer, in consultation with senior staff, if needed.
  • Increased fees for DAP meetings have been included in Council’s draft 2022/23 budget.

Officer Contact

Direct officer contact retained, but minimised through:

  • Enhanced DA Tracker as the first point of call for the progress of DAs- the Industry and members of the public should refer to this rather than calling/emailing DA assessment officers.
  • Officers will be available for other calls; staff will return calls within 5 business days (not the current 48 hours) and are only available for example Thursday afternoon 1.00pm-4.30pm.
  • The Industry need to have one point of contact only, not multiple people contacting staff, Management, Councillors.

(Requests For Further Information) RFIs

  • One consolidated RFI/One Applicant response to be commenced from 1 July 2022 for new DAs.

Prioritisation/Finalisation of Current DAs and New Applications for Flood Affected Residents and Businesses

  • Senior Council Staff to meet to review every single DA and see whether the outstanding referrals are really needed, whether any existing DA’s be fast-tracked with conditions or just refused if multiple RFI’s have already been issued. All existing DA’s will get one final RFI giving them the last chance to respond.
  • Where appropriate and practical, Council staff to consider opportunities to give priority to the determination of new applications for flood affected residents and businesses.

TWEED COUNCILLORS

  • Adjust the current call up procedure to be limited to Development Applications with cost estimate $2.5M to $10M until the end of 2022.
  • Continue to consider the most appropriate actions with regards to Land and Environment Court Appeals and negotiate outcomes where possible.

THE INDUSTRY

  • Commit to better supporting information with applications.
  • Avoid unnecessary contact with staff, and lobbying of multiple levels of management and Councillors

2.  Writes to the Minister for Planning and Homes to request an immediate increase to the deemed refusal timeframe for Development Applications of 120 days.

3.  The Mayor writes to all NSW Council Mayors and Local Government NSW and requests support in writing to the Minister for Planning and Homes as set out in part 2.

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

REPRESENTATIONS FOR ITEMS CONSIDERED IN COMMITTEE
(Sec 3.40, 13.9 to 13.17 Model Code of Meeting Practice)

Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.
 
EXCLUSION OF PRESS AND PUBLIC

Cr James Owen
Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that Council moves itself into a Confidential Committee in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993 and that the press and public be excluded from the whole of the Committee Meeting, because, in the opinion of the Committee, publicity of the proceedings of the Committee would be prejudicial to the public interest, by reasons of the confidential nature of the business to be transacted.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins.

"Dear Father,

As we prepare to begin our meeting, we acknowledge Your promise to be here as You are our Almighty Counsellor, Head of Council, the Unseen Host at this meeting, the silent Listener in all our conversations.

Father, I thank you for our councillors:

Chris Cherry
Reece Byrnes
James Owen
Meredith Dennis
Rhiannon Brinsmead
Warren Polglase
Nola Firth
And our Director: Troy Green

Father, inspire each & every one of them with Your wisdom, understanding & the ability to do what they have been called to do. Grant each one of them the willingness to be open to each other, to respect each, to be honest with each other, to be supportive of each other as they work together to serve the Tweed Shire.

Father, may You bless & keep each of our councillors. May Your face shine and be gracious. Turn Your face towards them & give them peace.

So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 

That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.     

We pray… Amen."

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Nola Firth

RESOLVED that the proposed amendments within the attached Draft Community Strategic Plan 2022-2032  be endorsed with the following additional changes and the updated Community Strategic Plan 2022 - 2032 be adopted: 

• P3, P37 and P38 – Change the ‘Preserving’ stream to ‘Protecting’ stream
• P42 – Change Goal 2.2 to “Deliver a safe and connected local road and active transport network that can accommodate increased traffic as our shire grows and connects people, places and businesses to each other”

The Motion was Carried.
