ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that Council:


1.     Endorses that the requirements for tendering does not apply to a contract with a value of $1,000,000 and under, pursuant to Section 55(3)(i) of the Local Government Act 1993 (the Act), where the following extenuating circumstances apply for a period of 12 months:

1.1    Significant scale of restoration works to be undertaken in relation to the 2022 flood event; and
1.2    Need to restore flood affected infrastructure in a timely manner, where the loss of infrastructure is having a significant detrimental impact on the local community; and  
1.3    Local market conditions, where there is a combination of high demand for and/or shortage of construction related contractors and materials.

2.     Endorses the following functions are delegated to the General Manager:

2.1    Acceptance of Tenders

Authority to accept a tender in accordance with clause 178 of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2005 but not in respect of tenders to provide services currently provided by members of staff of the Council (s.377(1)(i)) Local Government Act 1993).

Conditions / Limitations: Authority is limited to tenders with a maximum value of $3,000,000 excluding GST for flood restoration related tenders and $1,000,000 excluding GST for all other tenders.

2.2    Write off rates, charges and accrued interest

Authority to write off rates, charges and accrued interest on rates and charges in accordance with section 567 of the Local Government Act 1993 and clause 130 and 131 of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2005

Conditions / Limitations: Authority to write off write off rates, charges and accrued interest on rates and charges is limited to amounts $10,000 and below.  Rates, charges and accrued interest can only be written off where the General Manager believes on reasonable grounds that an attempt to recover the amount would not be cost effective.

2.3    Write off debts

Authority to write off debts, including accrued interest in accordance with section 213 of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021

Conditions / Limitations: Authority to write off debts is limited amounts of $10,000 excl. GST and below.  Debts can only be written off where the General Manager believes on reasonable grounds that an attempt to recover the debt would not be cost effective.

2.4    Extenuating Circumstances

Authority to accept a contract with a value of $1,000,000 and under, pursuant to Section 55(3)(i) of the Local Government Act 1993 (the Act), where the following extenuating circumstances apply:

1. Significant scale of restoration works to be undertaken in relation to the 2022 flood event; and

2. Need to restore flood affected infrastructure in a timely manner, where the loss of infrastructure is having a significant detrimental impact on the local community; and 

3.  Local market conditions, where there is a combination of high demand for and/or shortage of construction related contractors and materials.

Conditions / Limitations: This authority applies for a period of 12 months, expiring on 15 June 2023.

3.     Endorses the following functions being revoked from the General Manager delegations:

3.1     Appoint Acting General Manager

To appoint an Acting General Manager due to the absence of the General Manager on Council activities or leave.

3.2     Finance - GM - Tenders up to $250,000 (excl GST)

Council extends to the General Manager the following additional delegation under Section 377(1)(i) of the Local Government Act 1993:

The acceptance of tenders to provide services currently not provided by members of staff of the council to a maximum value of $250,000 excluding GST.

3.3    General Manager Acceptance of Tenders

Council extends to the General Manager the following additional delegation under Section 377(1)(i) of the Local Government Act 1993:

The acceptance of tenders to provide services currently not provided by members of staff of the council to a maximum value of $400,000 excluding GST.

4.     Endorses the following functions are delegated to the Mayor.

4.1    Temporary appointments

Authority to appoint a person to a position temporarily pursuant to Section 351 of the Local Government Act 1993.

Conditions / Limitations: Limited to temporary appointments of 3 months or less to the general manager position in accordance with section 351(1)(a) of the Local Government Act.

4.2     Expenditure - $3,000

Authorise expenditure for goods and services for Council of not more than $3000 (including GST) in accordance with relevant Policies, Protocols and Procedures.

5.     Confirms the delegation to Rous County Council for the control of noxious weeds in Tweed Shire: 

Being a local control authority under the Noxious Weeds Act 1993 (the Act) and pursuant to Section 68 of that Act:

  • Delegates to Rous County Council the functions of Tweed Shire Council, as a local control authority, that are capable of being delegated under the Act.
  • Delegates to the position of General Manager, Rous County Council the functions of Tweed Shire Council, as a local control authority, that are capable of being delegated under the Act.
  • Delegates to the position of Manager Operations, Rous County Council the functions of Tweed Shire Council, as a local control authority, under Sections 12, 18, 18A, 20, 36A, 41, 45 and 64 of the Act.
  • Delegates to the position of Manager Weeds Services, Rous County Council the functions of Tweed Shire Council, as a local control authority, under Sections 12, 18, 18A, 20(3), 36A, 45 and 64 of the Act.
  • Delegates to the positions of Senior Noxious Weeds Officer and Noxious Weeds Officer Rous County Council the functions of Tweed Shire Council, as a local control authority, under Section 45 (excluding Section 45(2)(b)) of the Act.
The Motion was Carried.

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.

Cr R Brinsmead, Cr J Owen and Cr W Polglase temporarily left the meeting at 4.05pm  due to a non-pecuniaryno-significant Conflict of Interest in this item.

DECLARATION OF INTEREST

The nature of the interest is that Cr Brinsmead is a committee member of the Kingscliff Chamber. Cr Brinsmead will manage the Interest by vacating the Chamber for discussion and not voting on the item. 

The nature of the interest is that Cr Owen is the President of the Kingscliff Chamber. Cr Owen will manage the Interest by vacating the Chamber for discussion and not voting on the item. 

The nature of the interest is that Cr Polglase is the President of the Tweed Heads Chamber of Commerce. Cr Polglase will manage the Interest by vacating the Chamber for discussion and not voting on the item.



Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis
 
 RESOLVED that Council:

1.     Receives and notes this report. 

2.     In order to resolve ongoing issues with the Kingscliff & District Business Chamber in relation to their contribution to the purchase of the Christmas tree in 2015:

a)    Returns the contribution of $11,700 to the Kingscliff & District Business Chamber with the understanding the funds will be directed towards their own initiatives to promote Christmas initiatives in the Kingscliff CBD and localities.

b)  Enters into a Deed of Settlement and Release with Kingscliff & District Business Chamber.

3.     Writes to the Tweed Chamber of Commerce and Twin Towns Services Club to advise that the contribution towards the purchase of the Christmas trees in 2015 is being returned to the Kingscliff & District Business Chamber for them to promote Christmas initiatives in their CBD and offers them the same opportunity. 

The Motion was Carried.

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  Cr Brinsmead, Cr Owen, Cr Polglase


Cr Brinsmead and Cr Polglase returned to the meeting at 4.08 pm.

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

1.     The Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards Selection Panel (comprising all Councillors) and the current Awardees, consider the 2022 Tweed Shire Australia Day Award nominations for the following categories:

  • Citizen of the Year
  • Arts and Culture
  • Volunteer of the Year (individual)
  • Volunteer of the Year (group)
  • Sporting Achievement (individual) 
  • Sporting Achievement (group)
  • Community Event of the Year 
  • Young Achiever in Community Service

with the option to make an ‘Honourable Mention’ to a nominee who deserves recognition for their efforts.

2.      Council continues to support, from the Australia Day budget, applications for financial assistance from non-profit organisations and community groups for hosting small community Australia Day events.

3.      Council notes that the awards and ceremony held in 2022 was funded by an existing budget of $9,896. 

4.      Council notes that the 2023 awards ceremony will be organised based on the 2022/2023 Australia Day budget allocation. 

5.      Council supports:

a)     The 2023 Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards and Citizenship Ceremony being held in the Murwillumbah Auditorium.
b)     A physical ceremony, however if required by NSW Public Health Orders, the General Manager may implement alternative options to deliver the ceremony in a COVIDSafe way.

6.      Council supports the rollover of funds from the 2021/2022 Australia Day events budget, as well as the 2021/2022 Civic Business - Civic Ceremonies budget.

7.      Council continues to explore gift ideas from local Aboriginal organisations/individuals for Award recipients.

8.      On the basis that Council nominates its next Tweed Shire Australia Day Ambassador from within the past year's recipients, Council invites (subject to their acceptance), Grant ‘Jack’ Frost (2021 Volunteer of the Year Individual), and if Grant is unavailable, Sven Loemker (2021 Young Achiever in Community Service). 

9.      Council invites the 2021 Citizen of the Year, Amanda Philp to be the 2023 Tweed Shire Australia Day Community Event representative. 

10.    Additional budget be sought in the next Quarterly Budget Review for funding a videographer for the 2023 ceremony.

11.    If the Australia Day Council of NSW and/or National Australia Day Council advise a name change to Tweed Shire Council Awards is permissible, that the proposal for such a name change be put on public exhibition for 28 days.

7.2 Battle on the Border on 5-7 August 2022 (Event)
That the proposed Battle on the Border Racing event 5 - 7 August 2022 be supported,
subject to current COVID-19 restrictions at the time of the event and suitability of the
road network and subject to the following conditions:

1.      NSW Police approval being obtained.
2.      Endorsement of the event by Bicycle NSW and/or Bicycle QLD.
3.      Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
4.      Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
5.      The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
6.      Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event. 
7.      All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
8.      Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
9.      Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
10.    That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed. The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources. If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
11.     The event be conducted and signposted in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
12.     A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions. 
13.     The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

The Motion was Carried.

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  Nil.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd, Presbyterian Church, Tweed Heads.

"Gracious God, 
 
We’re grateful as a community during Local Government Week to have opportunities to gain a greater awareness of Council’s work on our behalf.  Thank you for the team of over 750 dedicated, professional, skilled, and creative staff and Councillors providing essential services to us.  May this week be an encouragement to all in Council as they are recognised and appreciated for their important, yet often unseen work.  May it be refreshing after such a hard and heartbreaking year so far.  Please continue to grow a deepening sense of cooperation between our community and Council as we work together for an even better tomorrow.
 
We also acknowledge Homelessness Week.  We pray for those in our Shire who are currently homeless; that you would protect them and comfort them in their distress.  Thank you for the work of organisations like Momentum Collective and Fred’s Place and the opportunities they provide to care for the members of our community who are in crisis.  Thank you for the compassion and efforts of Council to address this complex issue.  Please grant wisdom so that equitable and appropriate solutions can be found.
 
We continue to pray for resilience, renewed strength, peace, and grace for all members of Council, and for good outcomes of the meeting this evening.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

Cr Meredith Dennis
 
RECOMMENDED that:

A.  Development Application DA20/0712 for a staged Development: demolition of existing educational establishment, two (2) lot subdivision, and seniors housing including three (3) signs at Lot 61 DP 1194165 No. 58-78 Caloola Drive, Tweed Heads be refused for the following reasons:
 
1.  Pursuant to Clause 4.46 of NSW EP&A Act 1979 the applicant has not supplied sufficient information to satisfy relevant provisions of the Water Management Act 2000 as regulated by NSW Resource Access Regulator (NRAR). 

2.  Pursuant to Clause 4.47 of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 Concurrence and General Terms of Approval (GTA) by NSW Resource Access Regulator (NRAR) have not been granted for the development. 

3.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 1.2 Aims of the Plan in that the proposed Seniors Living (Residential Care Facility) in an area affected by flooding and being isolated in a flood event with no option for evacuation is not conducive to a sustainable form of housing that promotes sustainable management of the built environment.  

4.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 1.2 Aims of the Plan in that the development fails to address Visual Impact concerns. 

5.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 1.2 Aims of the Plan given the lack of detail available to address stormwater drainage provision and required channel upgrade to suitably protect environmental impact on natural waterways. 

6.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 2.3 Zone objectives given the exceedance in height and the failed attempt to justify the contravention in building height. The proposed building height poses potential impact on the low density residential zone. 

7.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 4.3 Height of Building in that the development exceeds the maximum building height permitted under this Clause and fails to meet the development standard and objectives under this Clause.  

8.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 4.6(3)(a) and (b) in that the written request seeking exception to the development standard prescribed under Clause 4.3 does not adequately address that compliance with the development standard is unreasonable or unnecessary in the circumstance of the case and that there is sufficient environmental planning grounds to justify contravening the development standard.  

9.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 4.6(4)(a) in that the written request seeking exception to the development standard prescribed under Clause 4.3 adequately addresses matters required to be addressed under Clause 4.6(3) and demonstrate that the proposal will be in the public interest because it is consistent with the objectives of that particular standard and the objectives within the zone. 
  
10.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 7.3 Flood Planning in that the consent authority cannot be satisfied that the development is compatible with the flood hazard of the land. 

11.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 7.4 Floodplain Risk Management in that the consent authority cannot be satisfied that the Residential Care Facility will not, in flood events exceeding the flood planning level, affect the safe occupation of, ad evacuation from the land.  

12.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed LEP 2014 in regard to Clause 7.9 Development in areas subject to aircraft noise in that the consent authority cannot be satisfied that the number of people occupying the facility combined with the design and location of outdoor living spaces are conducive to the acoustic environment in terms of aircraft noise.  

13.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied SEPP (Housing For Seniors or people with a Disability) 2004 in regard to Clause 26 Location and Access to facilities given there is insufficient information to demonstrate that access to appropriate services and facilities can be provided in accordance with trip times prescribed in 26(2)(c). 

14.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied SEPP (Housing For Seniors or people with a Disability) 2004 in regard to Clause 34 Visual and Acoustic Privacy having regard to the proposed location and design of balconies in response to aircraft noise.  

15.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied SEPP (Housing For Seniors or people with a Disability) 2004 in regard to Clause 40(4) Development Standards – minimum sizes and building height given the development exceeds the 8m height limitation prescribed under this Clause and the building located in the rear 25% area of the site exceeds 1 storey in height. 

16.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(a)(iii) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied Tweed DCP 2008 in regard to compliance with Section A3 (Development of Flood Liable Land) due to the Flood Response Assessment and Action Plan not demonstrating facility management and operations are capable of making appropriate provisions for staff and residents to cohabitate in limited capacity for an extended period of time and the likely impacts to emergency services  during a flood event.  

17.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(c) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the site is not considered to be suitable for the development on grounds of flooding impacts, amenity impacts to the proposed residents and the developments ability to achieve desired outcomes in terms of height without exceeding the maximum permitted building height. 

18.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(d) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the development is not satisfactory having regard to the public submissions and external agency submission from NSW Natural Resource Access Regulator (NRAR) and the outstanding information to respond to their submission. 

19.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(e) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the development is not in the public interest given the developments failed performance against statutory planning instruments and development control plans publicly exhibited and adopted by Council.

B.  ATTACHMENT 6 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase

RECOMMENDED that:
 
 A.  Development Application DA21/0517 for the demolition of existing structures and construction of a four storey residential flat building with basement car parking at Lot 26 DP 1253093 No. 2-6 Tweed Coast Road, Cabarita Beach be refused for the following reasons:
 
1.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application is not consistent with Tweed DCP 2008 A1 Residential and Tourist development Code in that the development is not consistent with the Objective to ensure that the development is compatible with the local natural and built character, scale and amenity. 

2.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application is not consistent with Tweed DCP 2008 A1 Residential and Tourist development Code Section 4.1 Streetscapes Objectives in that the development does not ensure new development is compatible with, and complements the positive characteristics of the existing built, landscape and topographic elements of the streetscape  

3.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application is not consistent with Tweed DCP 2008 A1 Residential and Tourist development Code Section 4.1 Streetscapes Control C2 in that the development is not compatible with other buildings and sites along the street, particularly those that are older and more established.
  
4.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application is not consistent with Tweed DCP 2008 A1 Residential and Tourist development Code Part C Control 1a in that the development does not comply with building length standard and objective of this control is not met. 

5.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application is not consistent with Tweed DCP 2008 A1 Residential and Tourist development Code Part C Control 2g in that the development does not comply with the impermeable surfaces standards and the objective of this control is not met. 

6.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application is not consistent with Tweed DCP 2008 A1 Residential and Tourist development Code Part C Control 6d in that the development does not comply with the wall plate height standards and the objective of this control is not met. 

7.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application is not consistent with Tweed DCP 2008 B19 Bogangar/Cabarita Locality Plan Objective B19.8.2 in that the development does not ensure that an appropriate density of development is retained, which reflects the existing development in the precinct and surrounding residential areas. 

8.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application is not consistent with Tweed DCP 2008 B19 Bogangar/Cabarita Locality Plan Preferred Outcomes B19.8.4 in that the development is not consistent with the development design guidelines stipulated within Clauses B19.14, B19.15 and B19.16 of this Section with regards to wall length and 3 storey structure. 

9.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application is not consistent with Tweed DCP 2008 B19 Bogangar/Cabarita Locality Plan in that the development is not consistent with the vision of B19 that new buildings will respect the streetscape and the amenity and character of adjoining developments 

10.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application has not satisfied the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 A1 Residential and Tourist development Code in that the development does not meet the standards in wall length, wall plate height, deep soil zone, impermeable area, setbacks and the variations do not satisfy the objectives.
 
11.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application does not have acceptable impacts on the surrounding natural and built environment in being inconsistent with the character of the surrounding streetscape. 

12.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 the application is not found to be in the public interest due to the visual impact and incompatibility with the surrounding character. 

13.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979, and Clause 28 of SEPP No. 65 the application has not satisfied Apartment Design Guidelines Principle 1 in that the development is not consistent with the local context and character. 

14.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979, and Clause 28 of SEPP No. 65 the application has not satisfied Apartment Design Guidelines Principle 2 in that the development is not consistent with the bulk, size and scale of the existing or future desired character of the area.

B.  ATTACHMENT 6 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:
(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd from the Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church.


"Gracious God, 
 
Today on Vietnam Veterans’ Day, we stop to acknowledge the service of the veterans of that conflict.   We are deeply grateful for them, and pray for them and their families still living with the physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual wounds inflicted in their service.  May today be a special day of recognition, remembrance, and renewed friendships.  We also value the service of other ex- and currently serving members of the Australian Defence Force who live in our community.   Watch over them, preserve them in these uncertain times, and be with the many organisations who support them.  
 
This makes us conscious of the sacrifice and hard work of those who have come before us; military and civilian, the Bundjalung Nation and later arrivals, who have shaped our Shire into the beautiful place we enjoy today.  Help us to take their legacy and hand it on to those who follow as an even stronger community with wider opportunities for all residents.  Please grant Council all they need to fulfil their vision, and give both Councillors and Staff a deep satisfaction as they work to that end on our behalf.  We recognise the hard work already invested into today’s meeting, so may our Shire be strengthened and blessed through its decisions.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that Council submits the following motions to the 2022 Local Government NSW Annual Conference:

1.  That Local Government NSW  requests that the Department of Planning and Environment reinstates community services facilities, including buildings, to the list of essential works list that may be subject to Section 7.11 Developer Contributions Plan reviews by Integrated Planning and Reporting Tribunal (IPART) under the Local Infrastructure Contributions Practice Notes.
 
2.  That Local Government NSW  requests the NSW Government to review the deemed refusal timeframes under the NSW Environmental Planning and Assessment Act for Class 1 appeals. The 40 day and 60 day timeframe for an applicant to commence proceedings in the NSW Land and Environment Court for a deemed refusal determination has been part of the NSW Environmental Planning & Assessment (EP&A) Act since inception and does not reflect current assessment demands  or the variation of complexity of development proposals.
 
3.  That Local Government NSW advocates to the NSW Government on prioritising immediate provision of social housing for homeless and flood affected communities.
 
4.  That Local Government NSW  advocates to State and Commonwealth Government for an immediate, significant and sustained increase in funding for councils for Voluntary House Purchase schemes to allow councils to help the community move out of high flood hazard areas, and for Voluntary House Raising schemes to reduce personal losses due to flooding and increase community resilience.
 
5.  That Local Government NSW  requests that Department of Planning and Environment perform an audit of the operation of the Planning Portal to improve workability, with particular focus on the length of time the portal is adding to assessment timeframes.
 
6.  That Local Government NSW  calls upon the NSW State Government for the immediate implementation of a flying planning team that can be sent to localities after a natural disaster to help affected residents negotiate the planning system in repairs of their homes and businesses caused by the natural disaster event.
 
7.  That Local Government NSW  calls on the State Government to introduce a Shire wide opt-in 90 day limit on all non-hosted Short Term Rental Accommodation to elicit an immediate increase in the supply of homes for long term rental to alleviate housing crisis being experienced in many regional shires.


8.  That Local Government NSW advocates to the State Government to ensure that councils retain a role as consent authority in relation to forestry, including private native forestry.
 

9.  That Local Government NSW advocates to the State and Commonwealth Governments to release criteria for eligibility and current and future budgets for Voluntary House Purchase Programs as an immediate priority to give disaster affected residents certainty.


Cr Polglase temporarily left the meeting at 4.42pm.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr James Owen
 
RESOLVED that:

1.    Council revises its existing policies relating to Council licensed events on public land and at Council-owned facilities so that they:  

  • prohibit the release of helium balloons (effective immediately); and  
  • from 1 January 2023, prohibits the use or supply of all types of balloons, where all, or part, of the event occurs outside. 

2.   These changes are to be accompanied by an extended public education campaign using both print and social media to educate residents about the damage caused by plastic balloons, including to marine life.

3.   Council writes to the Federal and NSW Environment ministers outlining Tweed's outdoor balloon ban.

4.   Council requests the State and Federal governments ‘review the regulations on the sale and use of helium, especially relating to balloons; for them to educate the community on the harm of helium balloon releases; and ban on the use of gas filled balloons on government-controlled land’. 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
 
RESOLVED that:

1.     The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 9 June 2022 be received and noted, and

2.     The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

4.1 Water Street, Tweed Heads South
Pedestrian and traffic counts have been provided to Transport for NSW.
That this matter be deferred, pending further investigation by Transport for NSW.

7.1 Cycle for Life (Bicycle Event)
There are no objections to conduct off the Cycle for Life events, Sunday 31 July 2022 and the proposed temporary closure Bells Boulevard, subject to the below conditions. 
 
1. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) designed and implemented by suitably trained and accredited persons.
2. That the signs and devices deemed necessary to effect the traffic management arrangements necessary for the events be approved, subject to the TCP’s being deemed suitable for the event.
3. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
4. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
5. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
6. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
7. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
8. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
9. That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed. The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources. If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
10. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of completion of the event, confirming compliance with the above conditions and to permit a review of the conditions of approval for future events.
11. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose

7.2 Jack Evans Boat Harbour, accessible parking
The installation of 3 Designated Accessible Parking Bays in the car park adjacent to Jack Evans Boat Harbour and Twin Towns Club are supported subject to compliance AS2890.6 Off Street Parking for People with Disabilities.

7.3 Ourimbah Road, Tweed Heads street parking
The installation of 8P on Ourimbah Road, Tweed Heads to be trialled for 6 months
 
7.4 Splendour in the Grass (Music Event)
The installation of signage for Splendour in the Grass 22-24 July 2022 is supported, subject to:
  
1. Conformance with the approved Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans, designed and implemented by suitably trained and accredited persons.
2. The signs and devices deemed necessary to effect the traffic management arrangements necessary for the events be approved, subject to the Traffic Control Plans being deemed suitable for the event.
3. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
4. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
5. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
6. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
7. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
8. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
9. That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed. The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources. If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
10. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of completion of the event, confirming compliance with the above conditions and to permit a review of the conditions of approval for future events.
11. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
12. Submission to Council, 2 weeks prior to the event, proposed bus routes within the Tweed (extending to Coolangatta) identifying pick up locations, potential parking issues, and rubbish removal procedures.  
 
7.5 Eviron Road, dividing lines
The installation of dividing (barrier) lines on Eviron Road is supported in compliance to the RTA Longitudinal Markings Delineation guides.

Transport for NSW to review the existing speed limit on Eviron Road.   
 
7.6 Marine Parade, Kingscliff
That the Committee support the removal of the "Give Way" sign and linemarking on Moss Street entering Marine Parade.
 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that:

A.  The applicant be advised in writing that the Review of Determination has been undertaken and Council confirms the refusal of Development Application DA21/0034 for the use of a roofed deck at Lot 2 SP 42690 No. 2/36 Leeward Terrace, Tweed Heads for the following reasons:


1.   Pursuant to The Environmental Planning and Assessment Act, Section 4.15 (1) (a)(iii) the proposed development is contrary to the provisions of the Tweed Shire Council Development Control Plan Section A1, in respect to the following:

 

  1. The proposal does not satisfy Preliminaries Objective 1 (3.1 Streetscape) in deck is not compatible with, or compliment the positive characteristics of the existing built elements of the streetscape.
  2. The constructed deck does not satisfy Preliminaries Control 2 (3.1 Streetscape) in that the front setback is not compatible with that of other buildings along the street.
  3. The constructed deck does not satisfy Part A Objective 1 (3.1 Setbacks) in that the proposed front setback does not achieve the desired spatial framing of the street.
  4. The constructed deck does not satisfy Part A Control 1 (3.1 Setbacks) in that the upper storey addition is setback within 6m of the front boundary.
  5. The constructed deck does not satisfy Part A Control 2 (3.1 Setbacks) in that the proposal is not consistent with the front setback distance of neighbouring dwellings.
  6. The constructed deck does not satisfy Part A Control 3 (3.1 Setbacks) in that the front deck intrudes more than 1.5m into the front setback and exceeds 25% of the frontage width.
  7. The constructed deck does not satisfy Part A Control 4 (3.1 Setbacks) in that the deck is setback a minimum of 1.9m from the front boundary with a portion of the structure located on common land.
  8. The constructed deck does not satisfy Part A Control 1 (4.4 Built Form) in that the reduced front setback does not relate to surrounding development. 

2.   Pursuant to the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act, Section 4.15 (1) (b), the proposed development is considered contrary in respect to the following: 

  1. The proposal does not maintain the desired context and setting of the locality with respect to the streetscape. The proposed front setback sets an unwarranted precedent and results in an undesirable outcome with significant potential to detract on the streetscape of the locality. 

 

3.  Pursuant to the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act, Section 4.15(1)(e), the proposal is considered contrary to the public interest in that it would create an undesirable structure with an unwarranted front setback precedent, which would be incompatible with the desired spatial framing of the streetscape. The proposal would also result in a front setback which is inconsistent with surrounding development.

 

AND

 

That Council gives the applicant 3 months from the determination of the Review of Determination to lodge a new DA for an alternative designed deck that is wholly outside common property and achieves a minimum setback of 3.5m from the front property boundary. 


Failure to lodge a DA within 3 months will result in Council seeking legal advice as necessary to commence the process to have the unauthorised deck removed (this could involve demolition orders). 


B.   ATTACHMENT 1 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(d)     commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: 
          (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
          (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or 
          (iii) reveal a trade secret

 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that:

1.     The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 14 July 2022 be received and noted, and

2.     The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

4.1 Water Street, Tweed Heads South
That this matter be deferred, pending further investigation by Transport for NSW.

Site observation data be forwarded to Transport for NSW. .

6.1 Banner Street, Murwillumbah
That an 10 metre length of yellow no stopping line (C3) be placed at the end of Banner Street, Murwillumbah to limit vehicles obstructing access to the childcare centre.

6.2 Mooball Street, Murwillumbah
The replacement of the existing ‘Give Way’ signs on Mooball Street at Queensland Road with ‘Stop’ signs was not supported given the adequate sight distance and expected non-compliance.
Officers to consider intersection upgrades under the Black Spot Program or Safer Roads Program and may involve seeking funding for a proactive proposal accompanied by a road safety audit.

7.1 Twin Towns Triathlon Club
There are no objections to Twin Towns Triathlon Club conducting events throughout the season on local roads within Banora Point subject to:

1. Compliance with the NSW Road Rules for all activities
2. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
3. Marshalls are not to direct traffic in any way.
4. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
5. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
6. Police approval and control is given for the conduct of the March 18 event.

7.2 Elrond Drive, Kingscliff
That:

1. The installation of a Give Way sign and associated linemarking on Beach Street at Elrond Drive be installed.
2. The existing 60km/h signs approaching the intersection from Beach Street be removed.
 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins:

"Dear Father,

We thank You for the many blessings that You pour upon us moment by moment.

Your steadfast love never ceases; Your mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning and great is your faithfulness.

Father, I thank you for our councillors:

Chris Cherry

Reece Byrnes

James Owen

Meredith Dennis

Rhiannon Brinsmead

Warren Polglase

Nola Firth

And our Director: Troy Green

I pray for Your blessings upon them… that they make wise and straight decisions which are in the best interest for the people of the Tweed Shire. May You also bless them with good health, clarity of mind & watch over their families & loved ones.

Father, as this meeting proceeds, may we trust in You with all our heart, and do not lean on our own understanding… but in all our ways acknowledge You, and You will make our paths straight. May Your face shine upon us with favour, and be gracious to us, surrounding us with Your loving-kindness.

So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 

That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.     

I pray in Jesus Name: 

Amen."

Feedback:

P. 29    Strategy 3.1. Add in an additional point: Prioritising restoration, including pest and weed eradication, on high environmental value land (HEV).

 

P.37     Strategy 5.4.

 

Point 1- query as to why forest products are specifically listed as resilient and sustainable when they are fire hazard. Use of mud brick would be better?

 

Point 2. Insert ‘Plantation’ after Sustainable. ( ie no more forestry from native forests!)

 

P.40     Exclude wood and contaminated waste from Biowaste. Wood is precious and small pieces of so called waste need to be used as engineered wood for flooring etc. Contaminated urban waste burning causes serious air pollution problems.

 

P. 42    Remove reference to wood pellets from native trees (re Grafton trial p. 42). Native trees are needed for habitat and carbon storage and should not be thought (re circular economy) as  waste. See also the point above.

 

P. 47    The 2036 Plan acknowledges the value of smaller parcels of agricultural land for boutique local production, we need to retain 3 levels of significance for farmland rather than the opaque “important” farmland, with its non-searchable mapping.

 

P. 53    Talk of forestry should mention protection of biodiversity and habitat and particularly protection of old growth forests

 

P. 57    Under key challenges created by tourism, list impact on housing availability and affordability through STRA 

 

P. 61    Empowerment of LALC's should include an action to enable LALC's to provide housing for Aboriginal communities on LALC lands

 

P. 70    Strategy 16.1 re active transport should include that all new residential developments have mandatory connected bike paths and pedestrian pathway networks to facilitate active transport, maybe include Action to ensure region wide delivery climate change: Tweed Valley has been identified as one of the top 5 most vulnerable regions in Australia in terms of economic cost in a high emissions climate change scenario by Deloitte access Economics in 2022, we need this to be front and centre.

 

P. 90    Include a point 10:  Increased resources for environmental protection and restoration.

 

P. 135  Regional Priorities.

 

Point 1 Add in after LGA ‘in a way that protects our internationally significant environment’

 

Add in a new point: Continue to promote the region as an area of clean, green food bowl that utilises regenerative agriculture.

 

Point 3. Add ‘environmentally sustainable’ before ‘nature based’.

 

P. 135  In support of suggestions 83 and 84 from the staff submission it is suggested to provide the Tweed Narrative that is consistent with our Community Strategic Plan and LSPS rather than simply telling them that it is not.

 

Replace Tweed Narrative on p135 with the below:

 

Regional Priorities

 

Facilitate delivery of a diverse mix of affordable housing in existing residential zoned land

 

Deliver social housing to a minimum level of the state average

 

Coordinate delivery of natural disaster resilience measures including Voluntary House purchase, voluntary house raising, land swaps and flood resilient build-backs

 

Ensure protection of world-heritage and internationally significant natural environment

 

Facilitate productive use of agricultural lands to encourage a thriving agricultural sector

 

Liveable and Resilient

 

Ensure all new residential development has a clear and connected dedicated bike/pedestrian network

 

Increase shade canopy in Urban areas to combat future urban heat health impacts

 

Review planning legislation to ensure future development is climate change resistant and resilient

 

Support local and regional net-zero emissions and circular economy initiatives 

 

Facilitate renewable energy production in regional areas (excluding energy from wood burning and waste)

 

Productive and Connected

 

Facilitate transport corridors for energy efficient transport eg electric bus dedicated corridor for fast public transport

 

Ensure M1 is flood free and not contributing to flood flow impediments

 

Remove impediments to Cross Border economic trade and service provision 

 

Housing and Place

 

Deliver a diverse range of housing options that facilitates planned growth

 

Increase provision of homelessness services and crisis accommodation

 

Introduce levers to get existing residential zoned land to market to improve delivery of housing in a strategic and coordinated way that matches provision of infrastructure

 

Protect unique character and sense of place in existing towns and villages

 

Facilitate Open Space improvements in urban centres to improve quality of life

 

Ensure green belts continue to be maintained in the Coastal strip to ensure character and fragile ecosystems are protected.

 

Smart, Connected and Accessible (Infrastructure) 


  • Foster stronger alignment and integration with the Southern Gateway Economic Cluster in South East Queensland and the Northern Rivers subregion. 

 

  • Collaborate with South East Queensland on the Gold Coast Airport precinct masterplan. 

 

  • Identify barriers to economic growth and essential infrastructure delivery between South East Queensland and Northern NSW.

and

  • That the Department of Planning and Environment be requested to provide a response to the final submission.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

RECOMMENDED that Council:

1.   Endorses the waiver of an architectural design competition in lieu of an architectural design review process on the Nos. 3-7 River Terrace Tweed Heads site relating to the development of a multi-storey mixed-use development scheme and that written correspondence confirming Council’s endorsement of the waiver be forwarded to the NSW Government Architects.


2.   Delegates the selection of Council’s design representative(s) on the architectural design review panel to the General Manager to be undertaken in consultation with the NSW Government Architects.


3.   Advises the applicant of Council’s fees and charges which will be based on a cost recovery basis to be established via an endorsed Design Review Process and Fee Agreement where the rates for design panel members will be in alignment with the State Design Review.


4.   Considers a further report at the conclusion of the architecture design review panel process to inform Council of the design review panel recommendations and outcomes over both sites.

ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF THE PASSING OF HER MAJESTY QUEEN ELIZABETH II
On behalf of the people of the Tweed Shire, I would like to take a moment to acknowledge the passing last Friday of Her Majesty, Queen Elizabeth II. We express our deepest sympathies to members of the Royal family.

It truly is the end of an era. She was Britain’s longest-serving monarch with an unmatched 70 years at the helm. Such was her longevity and dedication to public service, many of us would never have known another monarch in our lifetimes.

Queen Elizabeth II ruled during challenging times and various significant world events. She swore in multiple prime ministers and has been a rock of stability in world leadership.

She had a special relationship with Australia and its people, visiting 16 times between 1954 and 2011 and was always greeted very warmly by people across the nation.

Above all, she was an incredible example of service and loyalty and an inspiration for both Councillors and staff who are working to serve our community in local government.

Tweed Shire Council is joining the community in the National Day of Mourning on Thursday 22 September.

As further marks of respect, the Border Marker has been lit up each night with a special In Memoriam photo display and the lights on the Murwillumbah Bridge have glowed purple each evening. These displays will continue until after the evening of 22 September.

Please join me in a minute’s silence as a mark of respect for Her Majesty, Queen Elizabeth II.


The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd from the Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church.

Gracious God, 
 
We pause to acknowledge the passing of Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth.  We thank you for her many years of service, and for her example of the difference an individual can make in their role of responsibility.  We pray for her family who have to grieve while performing such public roles.  Please give wisdom and grace to King Charles as he assumes his new responsibilities.
We also recognise the complex relationship that the monarchy has with Australia.  We pray for those in our community for whom this week has reopened grief over trauma inflicted on families in the name of the Crown.  We long for true reconciliation and healing.
 
And we are reminded of our own calling in this time and place.  We recognise that the decisions of this meeting make history and will affect the lives of individuals, families, and our community.  Thank you for each person present here, and the wisdom, experience, and individual gifts they bring to the decision-making process.  As each one fulfills their responsibility, may the outcomes of today even exceed our positive expectations and shape the future in a way that is a true blessing for everyone in our Shire.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen.

RESOLVED that 
1. The following tabled Petition(s) be received and noted.

 • Petition containing 20 valid signatories and received on 24 August 2022 entitled "DA22/0431 - Submission - 2-4 Commercial Road Murwillumbah " advising as follows:

"Re: Development Application DA22/0431 for the installation of a relocatable "Food & Drinks Premises (Cafe) at 2-4- Commercial Road Murwillumbah (Lot I DP 395360 and Lon DP 780240)

We, the undersigned state that this proposal is not in character with Murwillumbah's historic town heritage We, the undersigned disagree that such a cafe is a welcome addition to the Murwillumbah centre as stated in the proposal. The proposal listed above takes up already limited car park space and will create congestion to the existing open-air car park at the rear of the building on the eastern corner of the rear car park, in the area bounded by the retaining wall to Wharf Street and the revetment wall adjacent to the Tweed River.

Murwillumbah has already an abundance of coffee shops."

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.

RESOLVED that

1.   Adopts the amended Councillor and Staff  Interaction Policy, noting receipt of the two public submissions (refer to attachment #30 and confidential attachment #31) with the following amendment:

  • That in 5.7 the following sentence be included after the first sentence: This time frame may need variation where late reports are added to the Council Agenda or where Councillors urgently need information prior to the Council meeting in order to be fully informed in their decision making.
  • Clause 8.1 be amended to remove points (h) and (i) and that these be added to 8.2 as points (k) and (l)
2.     Re-adopts the 11 policies in (attachment #29) that do not require amendment at this time.

3.     Adopts the 22 draft amended policies that have minor/ moderate amendments as follows:

  • Access and Inclusion Policy
  • Asbestos Management Policy
  • Backflow Prevention and Cross Connection Control Policy
  • Business Continuity Management Policy
  • Discharge of Liquid Trade Waste to the Sewerage System Policy
  • Disposal of Surplus Goods, Materials and Portable Assets Policy
  • Driveway Access to Property - Design Specification Policy
  • Driveway Access to Property - Construction Specification Policy
  • Community Facility Hire and Use Policy
  • Flood Controls for Caravan Park Accommodation Guidelines
  • Flood Risk Management Policy
  • Footpath Trading Policy
  • Fraud and Corruption Control Policy
  • Graffiti Vandalism Management Policy
  • Naming of Buildings and Facilities on Council Sportsfields Policy
  • Naming of Council Public Parks and Sportsfields Policy
  • Cemeteries and Burials Policy
  • Procurement Policy
  • Reduction of Water Related charges due to Undetectable Leakage Policy
  • Roadside Tributes Policy
  • Vending of Food on Public Reserves Policy
  • Volunteers Policy 
4.     Approves public exhibition from 20 September to 2 November 2022 of the 3 attached policies (attachments #26, 27 and 28) with major amendments:

  • Youth Policy
  • Community Halls Policy
  • Markets Policy
5.     Revokes the following 3 policies:

  • Financial Assistance to Licensed not for Profit Native Animal Welfare Groups Policy (and the removal of reference to this policy in the Community Sponsorship Policy)
  • Community Options Contributions Policy
  • Open Space infrastructure Policy
6. In relation to the following policies, that staff consider the following:
 
  • Private Cemeteries and Burials Policy - burials definitions 
  • Market Management Plan Guidelines - the list of unforeseen circumstances should specifically mention flood
  • Business Ethics Policy - management of confidential Council and a commitment to reducing our carbon emissions footprint and reaching zero waste targets outlined in x policy and minimising or avoiding harm to the environment

7.     ATTACHMENT 31 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:
(a)     personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors)

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins from Murwillumbah Church of Christ:


"Dear Father,

Lord, we thank You for Your goodness and many blessings that you pour upon us day by day… for Your love endures forever. But unfortunately, it’s easy to get distracted by the world events around us and be overwhelmed with anxiety and worry. 

But Lord, Your thoughts are higher than our thoughts, and Your ways are better than ours. You give hope to the hopeless, and strength to the weak. You alone are able to refresh our minds and remind us of what we have been called to do.

Today, may You help each one of our councillors take every thought captive as they give You their concerns. 

  • Chris Cherry
  • Reece Byrnes
  • James Owen
  • Meredith Dennis
  • Rhiannon Brinsmead
  • Warren Polglase
  • Nola Firth
  • and our General Manager, Troy Green.

Remind them that You are with them, and that You will continue to instruct and lead them as they seek to serve and guide the people of the Tweed Shire.

So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the people of the Tweed and beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 

That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.     

I pray in Jesus Name: 

Amen."

RECOMMENDED that:
 
1. Council receives and notes the progress to date of informal landowner consultation on the Tweed Conservation Zone Review methodology and draft mapping.

2. The planning responses and mapping corrections arising from landowner consultation to date, as outlined in this report, are received and noted. 

3. Land zoned 7(f) Environmental Protection (Coastal Hazard) zone under the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2000 remain deferred from the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 pending re-evaluation on progression of the Tweed Coastal Zone Management Plan.     

4. The C Zone Review progresses to drafting of a planning proposal, noting that informal landowner consultation is ongoing across several sites. 

5. Options and recommendations on how to progress with any outstanding matters be presented in a report to Council accompanying a draft planning proposal.

6. A minimum of two Councillor workshops be scheduled prior to reporting to Council with a draft planning proposal for endorsement to submit to the Minister for Planning for Gateway Determination. 

7.  A formal response be sent to all submitters as to where this decision fits in the process and opportunities for further consultation in the future on individual landowner needs.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins from Murwillumbah Church of Christ.


"Dear Father, 

Thank You for this day & for the many blessings we have received. Your goodness endures forever. 

I thank You for each of our Councillors that You have entrusted with this tremendous task of watching, guiding & providing over the Tweed Shire. I pray for: 

  • Cr Chris Cherry;
  • Cr  Reece Byrnes;
  • Cr  James Owen;
  • Cr  Meredith Dennis;
  • Cr  Rhiannon Brinsmead;
  • Cr  Warren Polglase;
  • Cr  Nola Firth; and
  • General Manager, Troy Green

I pray that You would do a mighty work in each of their hearts & minds, giving them wisdom & understanding as they gather together today. 

Father, help them to make the very most of this time with thoughts & words that are wise & intelligent – making this a productive, caring & fruitful meeting.

For our Councillors I pray “The Lord bless you and keep you: The Lord make his face to shine upon you, and be gracious to you: The Lord lift up his face upon you, and give you peace.”

So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 

That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.     

I pray in Jesus Name:  Amen."

Cr Meredith Dennis
 
RESOLVED that:

1.  The General Manager or delegate commence the statutory procedures for amending the relevant sections of the Tweed DCP pertaining to carparking for residential development, to provide better clarity and remove any anomalies in regards to carparking rates including visitor parking and two bedroom units. 

2.  Council, in the interim period prior to amendments to the Tweed DCP, and also post amendments to the Tweed DCP support the imposition of conditions of consent for development applications under assessment, and future development applications, that differentiate the allocation of car parking spaces on a dwelling basis in accordance with Council's DCP, where subdivision is proposed or intended for the car park. 

3.  The General Manager or delegate cease the practice of providing draft conditions of consent to development applicants prior to the report being reviewed and finalised for determination.

The Motion was Carried

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that:

1.     The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 8 September 2022 be received and noted, and

2.     The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:


7.1  Signage at Terranora Public School, Terranora Road, Terranora
That the signs on Terranora Road prohibiting right turns into the primary school drop off/pick up zone be modified to only prohibit the movement 2:30pm-4pm on school days.

7.2 Reconnect Regional NSW Event - "Reconnect at the Junction" Street Party in Tumbulgum
That the Committee supports this event, subject to:
  
c.     Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
d.     Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents. 
e.     The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
f.      Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser. 
g.     All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.  
h.     Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed. 
i.      Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
j.     That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
k.    The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
l.     The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines to ensure consistency across e network.
m.   The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr James Owen
 
RESOLVED that Council:

1. Writes to the Secretary for Planning and the Independent Planning Commission as the declared consent authority that approved the development application (SSD 8169) for the North Byron Parklands site (applicant Billinudgel Property P/L) seeking an Independent Audit of SITG 2022 as provided for in Condition E10 of the 2019 approval.

2. Requests that the Planning Secretary also consider impacts to both Tweed and Byron Shire residents and businesses, particularly in relation to:

  1. Traffic queues onto the site extending for several kilometres onto the M1. 
  2. Traffic delays of several hours impacted people who had to reach other destinations.
  3. Social amenity, particularly noise to adjoining residents.

3. In the light of point 2 above:

  1. Requests that the Planning Secretary also require a Performance Evaluation Report as described in Condition D17 for this event. 
  2. Expresses our concerns with the time taken to provide safe egress from the site in wet conditions and the impact on the local road network and request a copy of the Traffic Monitoring Report for this event as detailed in Condition D27(e).
  3. Expresses our concern that noise related conditions D30 and D31 may not be complied with and request that a Noise Impact Report for this event be required by the Planning Secretary as allowed for under Condition D46.
  4. Requests the Planning Secretary request a review under Condition A3(a) including reviewing the increase to 50,000 patrons and request a reduction in capacity to 42,500 as allowed for under Condition A2(b) as this appears to be the capacity of the road network.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Rhiannon Brinsmead asks:
Can the General Manager advise what is Tweed Shire Council doing to prepare ahead of next flood or the predicted 3rd La Niña event?


The General Manager responded that effectively since the February/ March 2022 flood event, Council has been preparing for the next event by repairing our damaged infrastructure and building back better where possible. Our primary focus has been to respond to the aftermath of the 2022 event. In this vain to date, at a very high level we have:
  
  • Assessed the overall damage to Council infrastructure at around $100 million;
  • Assessed the damage to our roads network and logged more than 2,900 repair jobs (not including potholes). It is estimated this will cost up to $80 million and take more than 2 years to repair;
  • 90 Council buildings were inundated in the flood, each of which has had to be cleaned and repaired. This includes the 50m outdoor swimming pool at our Tweed Regional Aquatic Centre at Murwillumbah;
  • Forthcoming workshop with Councillors to understand flood related risks to existing buildings in flood prone areas and possible options to reduce risk; 
  • Collected more than 26,000 tonnes of flood waste from residential and business properties in the aftermath of the flood. This includes making special arrangements to deal with the collection of more than 1,440 tonnes of asbestos, including from neighbouring LGAs unable to cope with this demand.
  • More than 75,000 tonnes of mud debris has been collected to date from roads and public property, with this figure continuing to rise;
  • Established a Mayoral Flood Appeal which raised more than $80,230 in donations from the community to distribute to worthy resilience projects in the community;
  • Established a flood recovery team who are working together with State and Federal Government agencies and the local community to address community needs such as with the flood recovery centres;
  • Council continues to be an active member in the Local Emergency Management Committee (LEMC) comprising of NSW Police, SES, Fire, Ambos, etc to ensure we are participating in flood preparedness. Currently the Committee meets monthly to monitor seasonal weather predictions from the BOM and short term weather events;
  • I table some key flood 2022 statistics as an infographic for the Minutes and public record which will also be attached to these minutes.
  • Submission to the NSW Parliamentary Flood Inquiry.
  • Worked with the State to identify locations for temporary housing, including at Pottsville North Caravan Park.
  • Finalising our internal debrief and development of improvement plan to improve Council’s business continuity processes;
  • Finalising the Climate Change risk assessments for Council operations.
Looking forward below are some of the things we are doing to help better prepare the Tweed community for the next wet season/ flood:

  • Launched a new Flood Alert system at Burringbar, Mooball and Crabbes Creek on Thursday 14 October;
  • Organising a new Tweed Eco Festival to prepare residents to be climate ready. This will be held in Knox Park, Murwillumbah on Sunday 13 November;
  • Prepared a draft Flood Camera Monitoring Policy which will proceed to Council for recommendation to go on exhibition.  This is with a view to putting in place governance for flood camera footage to be made accessible on Council's website.
  • $20,000 in funding raised through the Tweed Mayoral Flood Appeal will be used to purchase VHF radios for remote communities so they are not isolated by floodwaters again;
  • The remaining $60,000 of Tweed Mayoral Appeal distributed to Murwillumbah Community Centre, Family Centre, SES and Northern Rivers Community Foundation for future flood resilience programs;
  • The road network is being fixed as rapidly as possible, with one lane of access on the major landslip of Scenic Drive now restored. Geotechnical reports have been received to fix the remaining significant landslips at Tyalgum Road, Limpinwood Road and Reserve Creek Road with short-listed construction contractors pricing up concept designs with the aim of having designs and tender pricing to Council by late November;
  • Ongoing rebuild efforts (roads, buildings, waterway assets, etc) are continually looking for opportunities to avoid building back in harm’s way or building back better. Council will be applying for funding under the Build Back Better program to upgrade Blacks Drain at South Murwillumbah;
  • Consultants have prepared a drainage study for the area around the Murwillumbah Leagues Club (Brothers) which floods regularly from water behind the Dorothy Street levee. The study looks at various options to try and limit the impacts of flooding on the club and surrounding properties. The report will be provided to the October Council meeting where options such as installing a new flood pump will be considered;
  • Council is still awaiting the formal announcement from the NSW Government about a $120,000 grant for a new Murwillumbah CBD Levee and Drainage Study Review and Pump Station Investigation;
  • Work is continuing on our first and second Industrial Land Swaps – with the second round of our Expression of Interest recently completed and over-subscribed;
  • Council has been working closely with the Northern Rivers Reconstruction Commission on providing a list of properties suitable for the adopted Voluntary House Purchase and Voluntary House Raising schemes, as well as providing a list of properties as part of the NRRC’s EOI process for suitable land for potential residential land swaps;
  • Working with the NSW SES and the NSW Government to secure a new site for a new SES building in Murwillumbah and then construct that site;
  • Working with the NSW SES to advance a Development Application for a new SES building in Banora Point on 5 acres of land that Council has acquired for this purpose;
  • Acquired a property at 91-95 River St, Murwillumbah; adjacent to the existing flood pump, to allow for an upgraded and larger pump station;
  • A Community Resilience Officer position has been created until March 2024 - officer commencing 1 November 2022
  • LEMC supporting Red Cross and SES to build and strengthen the community resilience network program as part of the Local Recovery Plan arrangements;
  • Review of the Local EMPLAN and Recovery Plan and Community Resilience Network governance arrangements;
  • Regularly conducting Community Resilience Network Group meetings to strengthen networks;
  • Delivering on the Bushfire Recovery Grants (inclusive of Flood Camera installation) to improve evacuation centres, fire mitigation, community safety and better understanding of illegal/unlawful occupancy issues;
  • Finalising enhancements to the Emergency Operations Centre (EOC) at the Tweed Heads Police Station (grant funded);
  • Improved telecommunications to 4, Council owned, nominated evacuation centres through the Govt funded STAND project – NBN Skymuster Plus Satellite service with a Wireless Access Point (WAP).

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd of the Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church:


"Gracious God, 
 
We continue to remember those affected by the floods.  We’re grateful for the many services being provided, and for Council’s advocacy with other tiers of government to enable current and future support.  We’re conscious of the new trauma that came with recent rains and the forecast for another wet summer.  Please grant continuing strength and grace to many still working on repairs and for those rebuilding their lives.  Please spare our shire from further damage in the coming months.

We appreciate the current community engagement with the Council’s Growth Management and Housing Strategy.  We recognise the diverse and sometimes competing issues this involves, and our inability to accurately see the future.  May Council and community be united in a wise response to these challenges.  Guide us as we work to make our region fit for sustainable growth and resilient in a changing climate, while remaining good stewards of its natural beauty and resources.  

Please bless both the decisions of this meeting, and the way in which those decisions are made.

We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."
