AMENDMENT 1

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis

RECOMMENDED that:

1.       Development Application DA22/0325 for a change of use to dual use (Serviced Apartments and Shop Top Housing) of units 215 - 218, 333, 334, 335 & 338 at Lot 14 SP 69243; No. 14/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; Lot 15 SP 69243; No. 15/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; Lot 16 SP 69243; No. 16/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; Lot 17 SP 69243; No. 17/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; Lot 32 SP 69243; No. 32/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; Lot 33 SP 69243; No. 33/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; Lot 34 SP 69243; No. 34/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; Lot 37 SP 69243; No. 37/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; SP 69243; No. 78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF be refused for the following reasons:

1.       In accordance with s4.15 1(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the development is not considered to meet objective s1.3(c) of the Act to promote the orderly and economic use and development of the land as there are limited tourist dwellings of this nature in a single location in this key tourist locality, and reducing the number of dedicated tourist dwellings in this centrally located complex has the potential to reduce the towns ability to function as an economic driver for tourism, particularly impacting on the capacity for large group bookings needed for business conferences and events.

2.       In accordance with s4.15 1(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the development is not considered to be in the public interest as there is limited tourist accommodation in this coastal location that is highly popular and should be available to be shared and enjoyed to meet a wide diversity of tourism and business needs.

2.       ATTACHMENTS 6, 7 and 8 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law
 
The Amendment 1 was Carried

VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd. 


"Gracious God, 
 
Our state is being plunged into one trouble after another.  Our hearts are with the residents and Councils in the west of our state and Victoria in their current flood crisis.  We pray for all those who go into dangerous situations to make them safer for others.  For those who are overwhelmed, bereft, grieving, losing hope, grant your comfort and peace.  Help our communities across the state to continue to care for one another in exhausting circumstances.  Give our State government the wisdom and resources to bring timely and effective assistance in these new areas of need while remembering the continuing needs in our own Shire.
 
As we draw closer to the end of the year, we reflect on a series of such trying years it’s hard to remember what a ‘normal’ year feels like.  We join our voices with many in the Bible who cry out to you, ‘How long?’  We’re mindful of the tiredness of many in this room and our community, worn down by the cares they carry.  Yet we are also heartened by their extraordinary resilience, and the many expressions of true community we have experienced.  Grant each one the times of rest and refreshment they need.  Please grant your grace, mercy, and peace to all here tonight.  
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that Council:

1.   Notes this report on the potential for establishment of a funding mechanism for large scale regenerative landscape management by Council.

2.    a)    Notes the recommendations made by the NSW Flood Inquiry Report 2022 that relates to improved floodplain management and the NSW Government's support of these recommendations and monitors any future opportunities to participate in and promote grants and initiatives.
       b)    Continue to leverage existing farm plans developed with local landholders by encouraging submission of grant applications for implementation of these plans;  and use future grant and other opportunities to assist landholders develop project plans that would be suitable as potential applications for grant funding opportunities. 

3.   Promotes existing and future Federal and State Government opportunities for rural landholders to apply for grant funds and other assistance to improve land management practices.

4.   Continues to support landholders through private land conservation programs.  
   
5.   Notes the positive response from the Hon Dugald Saunders MP Minister for Agriculture in regard to the Local Land Services similar interest in public - private funding partnerships and offer of further discussions on this matter with the General Manager North Coast Local Land Services and State Director NRM Louise Orr.  
  
      a)   Seeks further information and advice from Local Land Services on their time frame for this work and if/ how Tweed Council may be involved to assist in expediting these mechanisms.  
      b)   Requests Local Land Services to also include consideration of benevolent donations in their deliberations.  
      c)   Highlight the significance of the Tweed as the primary biodiversity hotspot of NSW and the imperative to protect this area.  
   
6.   Provide a further report to Council on the outcome of discussions with Local Land Services and the development of projects for forthcoming grant opportunities.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Warren Polglase

Tweed Shire Council’s Annual Report 1 July 2021 – 30 June 2022

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
 
RESOLVED that:

1.     The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 13 October 2022 be received and noted, and

2.     The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:


6.1Murwillumbah Farmers' Market - Queensland Road, Murwillumbah

 
Council reiterates to the Market Manager that they can only operate when onsite parking is provided.
 And that:
  • The existing No Stopping zone around the Harry Williams Gate be further reinforced by the installation of witches' hats.
  • The Harry Williams Gate be closed to pedestrians and vehicles.
  • If further use of Gate 8 is proposed then an internal connection is required to the Markets.
 
7.1Falls Festival - North Byron Parklands
 
The conduct of the Falls Festival 31/12/22 to 02/01/23 is supported subject to:

  1. Conformance with the approved Traffic Management Plan and associated TCPs, designed and implemented by suitably trained and accredited persons.
  2. Gate (E) on Wooyung Road only to be used as left out only egress and under traffic control
  3. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox to drop to directly affected residents
  4. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to council at least 2 weeks prior to the event.
  5. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
  6. A report be provided to Council within 2 weeks of completion of the event confirming compliance with the above conditions.

7.2.Bolwarra Place, Bilambil Heights 
 
That:
“No Parking Authorised Vehicles Excepted” signage be installed on Bolwarra Place at the cul-de-sac end including the turning bay and prior to installation adjacent residents are to be advised.
 
7.3.NX Sports Community Foundation Events :  Kingscliff Triathlons - 20 November 2022 and 19 March 2023
 
That the proposed triathlon events to be held on 20 November 2022 and 19 March 2023 be supported, subject to:

1. NSW Police approval being obtained.
2. Endorsement of the event by the Kingscliff Business Chamber and Bicycle NSW. 
3. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons. 
4. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents. 
5. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints. 
6. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser. 
7. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event. 
8. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed. 
9. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event. 
10. That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed. The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources. If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval. 
11. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein. 
12. The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network. 
13. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions. 
14. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose. 
15. Any signage, or Variable Message Signs installed on the Pacific Motorway are to be approved by Transport for NSW.
16. The application of all signs and devices necessary to effect the changed traffic management conditions and temporary road closures for the events, also being approved as part of the event approval.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

"that:

1.  Development Application DA22/0325 for a change of use to dual use (Serviced Apartments and Shop Top Housing) of units 215 - 218, 333, 334, 335 & 338 at Lot 14 SP 69243; No. 14/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; Lot 15 SP 69243; No. 15/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; Lot 16 SP 69243; No. 16/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; Lot 17 SP 69243; No. 17/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; Lot 32 SP 69243; No. 32/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; Lot 33 SP 69243; No. 33/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; Lot 34 SP 69243; No. 34/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; Lot 37 SP 69243; No. 37/78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF; SP 69243; No. 78-80 Marine Parade KINGSCLIFF be refused for the following reasons:

1.  In accordance with s4.15 1(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the development is not considered to meet objective s1.3(c) of the Act to promote the orderly and economic use and development of the land as there are limited tourist dwellings of this nature in a single location in this key tourist locality, and reducing the number of dedicated tourist dwellings in this centrally located complex has the potential to reduce the towns ability to function as an economic driver for tourism, particularly impacting on the capacity for large group bookings needed for business conferences and events.
 
2.  In accordance with s4.15 1(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the development is not considered to be in the public interest as there is limited tourist accommodation in this coastal location that is highly popular and should be available to be shared and enjoyed to meet a wide diversity of tourism and business needs.

2.  ATTACHMENTS 6, 7 and 8 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:

(e) information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law"


be rescinded.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins Murwillumbah Church of Christ 

"Dear Father,

We thank You for this day & for the many blessings that You pour upon us moment by moment. Your love endures forever.
Father, bless our councillors:

  • Chris Cherry
  • Reece Byrnes
  • James Owen
  • Meredith Dennis
  • Rhiannon Brinsmead
  • Warren Polglase
  • Nola Firth

Father, I thank You that we are able to come to You, seeking your help, as You made the heavens & the earth. Noting is too impossible for You. You promise that You will not let us fall as You never sleep and always watching over us.

May You watch over the Tweed Shire Council. Guard & protect over each of our counsellors as they seek to also watch, provide & keep the people of the Tweed safe & cared for.

Father, I pray that this meeting will not only be pleasing to Council, but also pleasing to You. That we may see Your mighty hand at work.

So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 

That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today. 

I pray in Jesus Name:

RECOMMENDED that:

1.  Development Application DA21/0021 for demolition and construction of a residential flat building comprising 2 x 1-bedroom units, 24 x 2-bedroom units, 2 x 3-bedroom units at Lot 2 DP 360543; No. 1 Brett Street Tweed Heads; Lot 1 DP 360543; No. 26 Recreation Street Tweed Heads be refused based on the following reasons:

1.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 and Clause 6.10 of the TCCLEP 2012, the application has not satisfactorily exhibited design excellence having regard to the suitability of the land for the development, the relationship of the development with the neighbouring site in terms of setbacks and amenity, solar access, and the achievement of the principles of ecological sustainable development.
 
2.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 and Clause 2.48 of SEPP (Transport and Infrastructure) 2021, the application has not satisfied safety concerns raised by Essential Energy by demonstrating compliance with ISSC 20 Guideline for the Management of Activities within Electricity Easements and Close to Infrastructure.
 
3.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 and Clause 28 of SEPP 65, the application has not satisfied Design Quality Principle 3 and 6 in that the design does not achieve a high level of amenity for residents and each apartment, resulting in a density appropriate to the site and its context.
 
4.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 and Clause 28 of SEPP 65, the application has not satisfied Design Quality Principle 4 in that good sustainable design including the use of natural sunlight, passive thermal design, and sufficient deep soil zones are not adopted and maximised to achieve a positive social, economic, and environmental outcome.
 
5.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979 and Clause 28 of SEPP 65, the application has not satisfied NSW Apartment Design Guidelines Objectives 3F, 4A, 4B, 4C, 4D, 4E, 4U, 4V, and 4W to achieve the design quality required to satisfy the principles relating to density, sustainability, and amenity. 

6.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979, the application is not consistent with Tweed DCP Section B2 in terms of setbacks, internal building amenity, communal open space, housing choice and mix, shading, and balconies.
 
7.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979, the application is not consistent with DCP Section A1, Part C in terms of minimum lot size, maximum impervious area, visual privacy, sunlight access, balcony depth, landscaping, minimum setbacks, ceiling height, passive solar design, internal corridors, and side fences.

8.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) and (e) of the NSW EP&A Act 1979, the application is not in the public interest based on the number of proposed variations to SEPP 65, DCP Section B2, and DCP Section A1 to accommodate the proposal of a 28-unit development, indicating that the proposal is an overdevelopment.

2.  ATTACHMENT 4 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

The Motion was Carried

  
VOTE FOR - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins, Murwillumbah Church of Christ


Dear Father,

We thank You for this day and for the many blessings that You pour upon us moment by moment. Your love endures forever.

Father, bless our Councillors:

Chris Cherry
Reece Byrnes
James Owen
Meredith Dennis
Rhiannon Brinsmead
Warren Polglase
Nola Firth
and our General Manager, Troy Green

Father, I pray that You will enlighten each of our Councillors with all wisdom, knowledge and understanding as they come together. May we always remember that You are a God of miracles, able to perform the impossible, able to provide all the answers to the obstacles and struggles we face in life when we call out to You.

I would also like to pray and give thanks for our Senior Administration Officer - Maree Morgan who has worked tirelessly over the years, working for the good of others, and now ready to look forward to her years of retirement. I pray that Maree will enjoy her new chapter in life and that You will continue to bless her with good health, joy in abundance, giving her peace of heart and mind, from this day forward and each day that follows.  

So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed and beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 

That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.     

I pray in Jesus Name,  Amen.

 • Petition containing 56 valid signatories and received on 1 December 2022 concerning "50 Main Road, Fingal Head" advising as follows:

  "...In regards to 50 Main Road Fingal Head.  Previously known as Fingal Head General Store and Cellars.  Any proposed to various hours of operation and/or use of site.

We petition the Tweed Shire Council (TSC) to maintain the currently approved use for 50 Main Road Fingal Head as a general store and to maintain the currently approved hours of operation to between 7 am and 7 pm.
We would strongly object to any business other than a general store, café, newsagency and / or post office.
Any other use including a bakery would have a major negative impact on the amenity of Fingal Head.
It would further reduce services and would compound the pressures on the environment including traffic, noise and parking.
Our objection also applies to any future proposals to operate outside current approvals.
We would like to be informed of any such proposal.
The restrictions and provisions we are requesting are in keeping with the objectives of the R2 Low Density Residential Zone:
to provide for the housing needs of the community within a low density residential zone and to enable other land uses that provide facilities or services to meet the day to day needs of residents.

We, the undersigned, are ratepayers and/ or residents of Fingal Head.
We object to any proposal to vary hours of operation and/or use of site
It would be incompatible with the quiet village amenity of Fingal Head.
It would increase parking problems.
It would cause unacceptable noise levels and impact Fingal Head including residents living within a few metres of the site.
It would mean further loss of services meeting residents' day to day needs."

RESOLVED that Council:

1.   The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 17 November 2022 be received and noted, and

2.   The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1.    Murwillumbah Cycle Club 2023 Events
That the proposed Murwillumbah Cycle Club events for 2023 be supported, subject to ;
  1. NSW Police approval being obtained.
  2. Endorsement of the event by Bicycle NSW.
  3. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
  4. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
  5. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts, road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
  6. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
  7. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
  8. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
  9. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
  10. That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
  11. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
  12. The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
  13. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
  14. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
  15. The application of all signs and devices necessary to effect the changed traffic management conditions and temporary road closures for the events, also being approved as part of the event approval.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that Council:

1.   Endorses proceeding to the preparation of the Growth Management and Housing Strategy - Options Paper.
 
2.  Receives and notes the attached Growth Management and Housing Strategy - Issues Paper and request the following revisions to the document:

  1. Removal of identification and note: “Potential opportunities to accommodate future employment land along the M1 corridor “ on page 43; Employment Land Issues-Map 2;  as the land identified at the top of the map on Gold Coast Airport (GCA) west of the M1 has not been previously identified as such in any State/Local plan/strategy, and has been identified in Gold Coast Airport’s previous and current Master Plans as Environmentally Significant Areas and National Estate. This area adjoining the Cobaki Broadwater (lower Tweed River Estuary) includes environmental species/habitat/communities and indigenous cultural heritage values of National significance. Further, such development of this area is at the extreme end of any sense of resilience and sustainability.
  2. Removal of the note on page 43; Employment Land Issues-Map 2, “potential opportunities to accommodate future employment land at the southern end of the Gold Coast Hwy within Cobaki Lakes” as the land identified is the Sewer Treatment Plant (STP) site within 2 adjoining parcels of employment lands with the STP not previously identified as employment land.
  3. Correction of mapping anomaly on Pg.49; Protection of productive agricultural and rural land values-Issues Map 1; at the top of the map the land on the north side of the Cobaki Broadwater is identified as State and Regionally Significant Farmland, however it is environmental land and identified as such in the Tweed LEPs.
  4. Add the NSW Department of Planning projected population figures for 2041 (an increase of 15.093) on page 5.
  5. Add in the protection of the Natural Environment into Key Themes under the Planning and Policy Framework.

3.  Notes that the population outlook prepared by PSA Consulting (Australia) Pty Ltd in their draft Issues Paper is more than double that of the population projections published by the NSW Department of Planning and Environment and NSW Department of Health and progresses the Options Paper on the basis that the variation in populations forecasting between these two measures be adequately explained and justified in the Options Paper.

4.  Includes in the Options Paper flood mapping that is at least 1 in 500 year in addition to the current 1 in 100 year measure.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase

Dear Father

We thank You for the many blessings You pour upon us. 

We thank You for your steadfast love that never ceases; Your mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness. 

Father, as this year is nearly coming to an end, we thank You for all You’ve done for us. 

Our Mayor, Councillors, Directors, Manager, Secretaries, Administrators and all other areas of Council have worked hard over this past year, with so much being achieved and yet there is still much to do. Bless each one of them I pray. 
However, may we all now enjoy a much-deserved rest over this Christmas break.  

Father, thank you for your Son, Jesus, the entire reason for we are celebrating Christmas. Thank You for each member of our beautiful families and friends. 
May we cherish this time together with giving, laughter and joy, making precious memories for years to come.

Please watch over each and every one of us, keeping us safe over this Christmas period and bring us all back in good spirits into the new year.

Thank You Father… You are our Shepherd; we have everything we need. 

You let us rest in fields of green grass and lead us to quiet pools of fresh water. 

You give new strength. Guiding us in the right paths, as You have promised. We thank You.

So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed and beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Warren Polglase
 
RESOLVED that

That, in respect to Contract RFO2022142 Portion 1 - Design and Construction - Restoration of Major Landslips, Tyalgum Road and Reserve Creek Road (conditional to approval through Disaster Recovery Funding Arrangements and positive financial assessment of the Bidders):

1. Council awards the offer for Reserve Creek Road (DM 00089) to SEE Civil Pty Ltd ABN 88 115 963 427 for the amount of $5,978,367.19 incl GST ($5,434,879.26 excl GST) conditional to further scope definition during the completion of the design stage; and
 
2. The General Manager be granted delegated authority to approve appropriately deemed variations to the above contract and those variations be reported to Council at finalisation of the contract; and

3. Council declines to accept any of the offers received for Tyalgum Road (DM00280) and by resolution, in accordance with Regulation 178 (e) of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, enter into negotiations with Bidders and any person (whether or not the person was a tenderer) with a view to entering into a contract in relation to the subject matter of the tender and granting the General Manager delegated authority to award the contract and approve appropriately deemed variations to the contract and those variations be reported to Council at finalisation of the contract; and

4. Council notes the reasons for declining in item three (3): 

-  There is significant divergence in cost between bids which prevents Council from establishing that value for money has been achieved; and
-  The proposed design models contain unresolved matters; and 
-  The value of the bids value exceed Transport for NSW standard funding authority which would result in an extended approval process.

The reasons for not inviting fresh tenders in item three (3) are noted as: 
-  Value for money is unlikely to be achieved given current market conditions; and
-  Existing bidders have extensive knowledge of the site, character of the damage and retain geotechnical information required to complete design; and
-  A process delay would extend the significant adverse impacts already experienced by the community.

5. ATTACHMENTS 1, 2 and 3 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:
(d)  commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
      (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
      (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or
      (iii) reveal a trade secret

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
 
RESOLVED that Council, in relation to increased requirements for quarried material from High-tec Quarry at Dulguigan Road Tumbulgum following the 2022 floods:

1. Resolves to not take enforcement action for laden truck movements up to a maximum of 15,600 in the 2022/23 reporting year and 16,250 in the 2023/24 reporting year, subject to the quarry:
  • meeting all other existing conditions of consent
  • submitting quarterly reports to Council advising of the total number of laden truck movements and material leaving the quarry per month

2. Informs Hy-tec of this exemption and that Council reserves the right to review the situation and withdraw its assurance that it will not take enforcement action, should the quarry operator not comply with these requirements or for other reasons

3.  Notes that this increase is strictly for the specified reporting periods due to the exceptional circumstances regarding flood repair works and no increase of truck movements for other reporting periods is permitted by this resolution.

4.  ATTACHMENTS 2 to 5 CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
(a)     personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors)
(c)     information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business
(d)     commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: 
          (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
          (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd


Gracious God, 
 
We’re grateful for the opportunities last week and this week to celebrate the many people who contribute to the diversity and strength of our Shire.  

For our newest citizens, the winners of the Australia Day awards, and our robust volunteering community, we give you thanks and acknowledge their hard work that blesses and inspires us.  

We are thankful for the opportunities Tweed Seniors’ Festival provides to celebrate the contribution older people make to our community.  

We deeply appreciate the welcome by, and shared work with, the generations of the Bundjalung Nation and other Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
 
We recognise the hard work of Council, both elected and staff, to foster an interdependent and cohesive community.   Grant them every grace to meet the opportunities and challenges of the coming year.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen.

Cr James Owen
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that Development Application DA22/0765 for an expansion of existing restaurant and use of works undertaken without consent including earthworks at Lot 1 DP 1240727 & Lot 3 DP 582718 No. 47 Hindmarsh Road, Nunderi, be refused for the following reasons:

 1.     Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) - The proposal, which seeks to substantially intensify the use of a restaurant on a rural zoned site to accommodate up to 153 guests and which fails to demonstrate that the impacts associated with same is acceptable, is contrary to the aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in clause 1.2(b) to encourage a sustainable local economy and small business, employment, agriculture, affordable housing, recreational, arts, social, cultural, tourism and sustainable industry opportunities appropriate to Tweed.

 2.     Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) - The proposal is contrary to the objectives of Zone RU2 Rural Landscape as set out in clause 2.3 the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to maintain the rural landscape character of the land, to provide for compatible land uses, and to   provide for a range of tourist and visitor accommodation-based land uses, including agri-tourism, eco-tourism and any other like tourism that is linked to an environmental, agricultural or rural industry use of the land.

 It is considered that the scale of the development is inconsistent with the rural nature of the area, and the application fails to demonstrate that the impacts associated with the operation of the premises will not have an adverse impact on the amenity of neighbouring properties.

 The proposal is similar in scale and operations to a function centre which is prohibited in Zone RU2.

 3.    Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(b) - The application has not demonstrated to the satisfaction of the consent authority that the operation of the premises will not negatively impact neighbouring properties, particularly in relation to internal and external sources of noise, including but not limited to, noise associated with operation of the restaurant/café and associated outdoor dining areas, traffic noise, and operation of plant and/or machinery.

 4.     Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(b) - The applicant has not demonstrated to the satisfaction of the consent authority that the proposed Sewage Treatment Plant and associated effluent Land Application Area(s) will not prejudice ground water quality, or create a public health hazard.

 5.     Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(c) - The premises is not considered suitable for the proposed development, as evidenced by the non-compliances with Building Code of Australia and the National Construction Code.

 6.      Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(e) - The proposed operation of a ‘restaurant’ with a patronage capacity of up to 153 guests in a rural zone, which has a history of operating as a wedding venue/function centre which is prohibited in the zone and ongoing complaints in relation to noise is not considered to be in the public interest.

7.       ATTACHMENT 5 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)          information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law


The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd from the Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church.


Gracious God

As we approach the anniversary of last year’s floods here and across our region we pause to remember and reflect.  
We remember those who lost their lives, and their families who still grieve.  
We remember those who remain homeless, or are still rebuilding.  
We remember those who lost jobs, businesses, and all those uprooted from what seemed stable and secure beforehand.  
We remember and acknowledge our shared trauma as we sought to bear one another’s burdens.  
And we will not forget the many acts of kindness and self-sacrifice.
 
As we reflect on the year since, many of us are still so tired.  
We carry a deep sadness.  
Recent storms bring back memories that haven’t healed.  
We recognise the increased, sustained demands on the whole of Council and the toll that brings.  
Grant rest to all those weary and burdened.  
Comfort those who sorrow.  
Have mercy on troubled hearts.
 
We pray for the many ways Council and other tiers of government continue to help our community recover.  
May they remain appropriate, effective, and equitable.  
Bless each one delivering those services, and grant Council sustained grace in this long-term work.  

We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen.

REASON FOR CONFIDENTIALITY

Local Government Act
This report is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, which permits the meeting to be closed to the public for business relating to the following: 

(a)     personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors)


DECLARATION OF INTEREST
The General Manager, Mr Troy Green declared a Pecuniary Interest in Item 24.1 - Mayoral Minute for Renewal of Appointment of General Manager.  The nature of the interest is that it deals with his employment contract.  Mr Green advised he will manage the Interest by vacating the Chamber and taking no part in the discussion or voting on the matter.

Mr Green, General Manager temporarily left the meeting at 5.26 pm due to a pecuniary Conflict of Interest in this item. 

Cr Polglase returned to the meeting at 5.28 pm.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that:

1.     Council renews the appointment of Mr. Troy Green as its General Manager under a 5-year contract of employment commencing on 23 December 2023, in the standard format required by the Department of Local Government.

2.     The Mayor be authorised to execute the renewal of appointment contract as detailed in clause 1 above as soon as is practicably possible for the benefit of all parties.

3.     ATTACHMENTS 1-3 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contains :

(a)     personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors)

 

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

MAYOR'S COMMENT 
Council’s General Manager, Mr. Troy Green, is currently employed under a Contract of Employment which is outlined in the standard format then required by the Department of Premier and Cabinet. This contract is due to expire on 22 December 2023.
 
Under Clause 5 of the current contract, Mr Green is required to advise Council at least 9 months before the termination date of his contract if he seeking re-appointment to the position of General Manager.
 
Mr Green advised the Mayor by email dated 10 November 2022 that he was seeking re-appointment to the position of General Manager for a five-year period  with Council under the terms of the new Standard Contract of Employment for General Managers as at June 2022. Mr Green subsequently provided a copy of that CONFIDENTIAL email to all Councillors. Mr Green noted that the contract details have changed from his existing contract and a summary of those changes are outlined in the reports attachment circular No 22-25/31 August 2022 from the Office of Local Government titled “GM Contract Changes Explained. Mr Green also provided a copy of the new template Standard Contract of Employment for General Managers.
 
Council’s Performance Review Committee (PRC), which comprises the Mayor and all Councillors met on 11 August 2022 for the purpose of undertaking the annual performance review of the General Manager. The Mayor and all Councillors were present for this meeting. The outcome of the review was a rating of “better than satisfactory”. The performance review outcomes were tabled at the Council meeting on 27 October 2022 with Council approving Mr Green’s remuneration increase of 3% from date of endorsement ie 27 October 2022.
 
Following endorsement by Council, the PRC recommends the Mayor execute the new contract for renewal of appointment of Mr Green to the position of General Manager to take effect on 23 December 2023.
 
The Council would like to take this opportunity to commend Mr Green on his exemplary service to Council. His passion and dedication for serving the Council and the Tweed community make him a great asset for local government.","isPublic":false,"isPublished":false,"isCurrentItem":false,"meeting":null,"reports":[{"id":12030,"name":"Public Confidential Report","isUploaded":0,"reportTemplateId":4,"wordTemplateId":8,"pdfMediaFullPath":"stream/TWEED/tmp_277c50be20.pdf","token":"6fbcbc09-21f6-4e9f-8243-2e8846c3a078","isPublic":true}],"attachments":[],"actionSheets":[],"bookmarks":[],"minutes":[]},{"id":17182,"name":"Innovation Solutions Grant Fund Application","parentId":15121,"sortOrder":48,"minutesSortOrder":48,"minutesParentId":15121,"outlineNumber":"3","fullOutlineNumber":"17.3.","htmlContent":"

23.    Prior to issue of Subdivision Works Certificate a Detailed Plan of Landscaping (DPoL) shall be submitted to Council and approved by Council's General Manager or delegate. The DPoL shall include the following:
a.      Plant selection criteria for all areas of the site other than the area denoted as ‘Littoral Forest Setback’ in Ground Floor (Overall) Plan, Drawing No. SD 02 Issue 04 (dated 16/12/2022) prepared by C2 Architecture shall comply with the following:
i.        A minimum of 80% locally occurring Australian native species and maximum of 20% non-locally occurring Australian native species to apply to all trees
ii.       A minimum of 80% locally occurring Australian native species and maximum of 20% Australian native or exotic species to apply to other plants (shrubs, ground cover and similar)
iii.      No noxious or environmental weed species
b.      A deep planting landscape zone component for the nominated ‘Littoral Forest Setback’ area shall comply with the following:
i.        100% local native littoral rainforest species incorporating a minimum of nine (9) local native coastal trees of advanced stock size class (minimum 45 litre) comprising Cupaniopsis anacardioides (Tuckeroo) and Syzygium hemilampra (Blue Satinash) species.
ii.       Comprises 100% local native littoral rainforest species in the shrub and understorey layer of minimum tube-stock size
iii.      Excludes any turfgrass, noxious or environmental weed species
iv.      Satisfies the NSW Rural Fire Service Standards for Asset Protection Zones
                             v.       Consideration also be given to include an additional four (4) trees in the rear littoral rainforest setback of the same species identified in 23(b)(i). 
c.      Five (5) advanced stock street tree plantings comprising coastal local native species including (but not limited to) Cupanipsis anacardioides (Tuckeroo) and Syzygium hemilampra (Blue Satinash) in accordance with Council’s Development Design Specification D14.08.03C Tree Planting and Location and Standard Drawing ‘Tree and Shrub Planting Details’ Dwg. No. SD701.
d.      Landscaping must comply with any RFS requirements.
     ii.  Receipt of amended Bushfire Safety Authority from the NSW Rural Fire Service.
3. The applicant be invited to discontinue the proceedings.
4.  ATTACHMENTS 1-5 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
 (g)    advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd

"Gracious God, 
 
We are grateful for the opportunities this week to remember, reflect, and come together as a community on the anniversary of last year’s flood.  We remember before you those grieving as they rebuild, or still wait for certainty about housing.  We pray for ongoing healing for all those living with trauma that persists today.  We bring before you our frustrations, our tiredness, our unease, our vulnerability in living in this beautiful yet dangerous world.
 
We remember the efforts of Council staff who worked so hard re-establishing essential services, even while many of them were personally affected by the flood.  We remember Council’s leadership and advocacy on behalf of our Shire.  We remain deeply thankful for the many volunteer organisations, individuals, and members of Defence who came into our community to help.  We pray for the continuing hard work of recovery, and for the particular burden that has placed on Council.
 
We ask that the decisions of this meeting today may foster an ever deepening experience of community.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd.


"Gracious God, 
 
We are grateful for the privilege of meaningful work, for our colleagues, for the sense of purpose and satisfaction in sharing common goals.
 
Thank you for Council’s commitment to look after people and places.    We acknowledge the hard work required to provide us with a quality of life we often take for granted.  As Council works for the sake of our current community and of those who will follow us, grant wisdom to understand the diverse needs of our region and make good decisions.  
 
May the incoming State government also understand those needs and partner well with Council to meet the opportunities and challenges of the future.
 
Please bless Council in its decision making today.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

Cr Reece Byrnes
Cr James Owen
 
 RESOLVED that:

 1.      The Affordable Housing Strategy Fee Proposal prepared by Urbis Pty Ltd of 25 November 2022 is accepted.

2.      Urbis Pty Ltd is awarded the service contract for the preparation of the Tweed’s Affordable Housing Strategy.

3.      The amount of $218,500 be reallocated from the current Murwillumbah Regional Locality Plan budget to the Affordable Housing Strategy budget within the Strategic Planning and Urban Design group budget, noting that a currently submitted State grant funding program has indicated in-principal support of Tweed’s application in the amount of $137.000 and if approved will reduce Council’s contribution to $81,500.

4.      The amount of funding reallocated under Resolution 3 to this report, is to be allocated to the Murwillumbah Regional Locality Plan budget within the Strategic Planning and Urban Design group budget, at the next budget opportunity.

5.      ATTACHMENT 1 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(c)     information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business
(d)     commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: 
          (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
          (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or 
          (iii) reveal a trade secret
(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

Cr Reece Byrnes
Cr James Owen
 
RESOLVED that in respect to Contract RFO2023026 Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Solution:

1.     Council enters into negotiations with TechnologyOne Limited ABN: 84 010 487 180 with a view to entering into a contract for the OneCouncil ERP.

2.     Council notes that a market scan has been undertaken which did not identify a suitable alternative ERP supplier. 

3.     Council grant the General Manager delegated authority to award the contract, within the limits as outlined in the Unsolicited Proposal from Technology One (attached), under section 55 (3)(i) of the Local Government Act 1993because a satisfactory result would not be achieved by inviting tenders due to:
  • The relatively short timeframe that Council's existing core software will remain supported.
  • The risk associated with Council using unsupported core software.
  • The uniqueness of the unsolicited proposal to meet Council requirements (including cyber security, ERP and support requirements) and to minimise change management costs and impacts to Council. 
4.     The General Manager be granted delegated authority to approve appropriately deemed variations to the contract and those variations be reported to Council at finalisation of the contract.

5.     ATTACHMENTS 1, 2, 3 and 4 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contains:

    (c)  information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business. 
  
    (d)  commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
           (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
          (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or
         (iii) reveal a trade secret


The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council endorses the following motion to be submitted to the Australian Local Government Association for the National General Assembly 2023.

1.     Motion:  That the National General Assembly calls on the Australian Government to: 
  • establish mandatory soft plastic recycling targets
  • place a levy on production and consumption of polymer plastic made from fossil fuel and particularly for single use and packaging 
  • use of the levy to support urgent establishment of plastic recycling research and facilities 
  • mandate government institution use of recycled plastic procurement for any single use plastics and plastic packaging.

Background:
The use of single use plastics between 2018 and 2021 increased by 1 kg per person on the planet. By 2050 it is estimated that at current rates there will be more plastic in the sea than fish. Fish, native birds and animals are at risk due to ingestion of plastic in the environment.  Microplastics are already throughout the food chain.  We urgently need the above incentives and government mandates to change this shocking situation.

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  Cr Reece Byrnes 


Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that Council endorses the following motion to be submitted to the Australian Local Government Association for the National General Assembly 2023.

2.     Motion: The National General Assembly calls on the Australian Government to reduce the impact on housing affordability and housing availability attributable to the commercialisation of housing by way of short-term holiday letting (STHL):

  • Reviews tax laws to ensure that taxation of commercialised tourism housing is transparent and enforceable on the property owner;
  • Reviews tax laws to ensure that taxation on commercial platforms operating as booking agents for property owners is transparent and enforceable, so that the cost of combating the impacts on housing affordability and accessibility arising from STHL, at a State and local government level, is offset by those providing the STHL services;
  • Allocates appropriate resources to tackle the spatial land distribution and permissibility of STHL at a local government level to reduce the incidence and severity of STHL impacts in vulnerable housing areas or markets where housing affordability and accessibility is at a critical level. 
 
Background:
Tourists holidaying in Australian cities and regions increasingly choose to stay in short-term holiday letting.  The supply side of the property market is responding by a rapid growth of dwellings advertised online for short-term holiday stays.  Longer term, short-term holiday rental has the potential to impact on local neighbourhoods if not adequately managed through increased noise levels, traffic and parking, safety and security, but most importantly, through cumulative impacts on housing affordability. Whilst Australian states and territories undertake efforts to manage short-term holiday letting through planning-based policy mechanisms, there is also an opportunity to explore scenarios for regulating the issue through changes to the tax laws and spatial distribution control measures.

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  Cr Reece Byrnes


Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RESOLVED that Council endorses the following motion to be submitted to the Australian Local Government Association for the National General Assembly 2023.

3.   Motion:  That the Federal Government review the taxation system to incentivise the use of untapped existing accommodation within homes. For example, consideration be given to allowing owner of a Principal Place of Residence to nominate a bedroom for Board rental to individuals who qualify for rental assistance and in return that portion of their home remains exempt from Capital Gains Tax and does not effect their pension should they be a pensioner provided they register their bedroom for accommodation with CentreLink at a discount of 20% to market rent.

 

Background: 

Homelessness and Affordable housing are impacting negatively right across Australia and currently there is a disincentive for homeowners to share their traditional 3 bedroom homes with people outside their immediate family due to the negative impacts that this may have on capital gains tax. Removing this disincentive would enable more people to open their home to renting rooms or parts of their home to those most disadvantaged. This would provide the potential for an immediate accommodation supply in already existing housing stock.

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  Cr Reece Byrnes

RESOLVED that

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

7.1. Wharf Street, Tweed Heads
The request to modify the 2P parking on Wharf Street, Tweed Heads, adjacent to no.117 is not supported as this may set an undesirable precedent in the CBD area. Council officers are to liaise with Kinetic Bus Lines to ascertain whether or not the bus zone on Wharf Street adjacent to no.117 is currently used and if not, the signage and infrastructure be removed and replaced with 2 hour parking 9am-5pm Mon-Fri, and 9am-12 noon. Saturday.

7.2. Greenway Drive, Tweed Heads South
The installation of a yellow no stopping line (C3) on Greenway Drive from Corporation Circuit, Tweed Heads South, to the driveway of no.47 is not supported. Council officers will continue to monitor the site and resubmit to the Local Traffic Committee if required.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins:

"Dear Father,

Father, bless our Councillors with favour this day as they gather together to guide, provide & watch over the Northern Rivers. Where there is no guidance, the people fall, but in an abundance of councillors there is safety. It’s not always an easy task, but You promise to give strength & wisdom to those who ask. 

Father, thank you for the Tweed Shire Council leadership you have entrusted to us.

Help them to be faithful in all of the roles they have been given. In particular, I ask that they might be councillors of truth, humility, and fairness. 

May our councillors be focused on what is important for the people of the Tweed Shire. 

May they be servant leaders of all you have given into their care.

Father, I also ask during this time today, that our councillors be mindful of each other, knowing that we are all in this together. Having conversations where everyone can contribute and everybody is willing to have a go.

So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 

That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.     

Thank You Father… Amen."

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RECOMMENDED that Council:
1.   Await further information on the industry nomination pilot to consider implications of the Rezoning Pathways Program on the established evidence based and community supported approach to strategic planning in the Shire;
2.   Refrains from participating in the NSW Planning Rezoning Pathways program due to the lack of transparency provided to our community and the inconsistency of the Program with our strategic planning documents;
3.   Writes to the State Members for Tweed and Lismore requesting their advocacy in abandoning the Rezoning Pathways Program in its current form to allow appropriate transparency and democracy in any future Planning Proposals in the state; and
4.   ATTACHMENTS are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RECOMMENDED that Council:

1.       Seeks legal advice on any and all potential non-compliances carried out at 60 Tringa Street, Tweed Heads to date in relation to the existing current approvals for this development and the recommended legal options to remedy any non-compliance.

2.       Notes that the 2015 Construction Certificate for this land parcel defined tree clearing and grubbing works as earthworks and as such works that have occurred on site to date are not contained to site preparatory works.

3.       Notes that the environmental protection buffer zones have been compromised by the temporary Tringa Street access, which appears to contravene the existing Approval and Construction Certificate.

4.       Notes that the large trees cleared on site were chipped, which appears to contravene the approved Vegetation Management Plan.

5.       Notes that the Controlled Activity Approval required erosion and sediment controls to be in place before works occurred and that appears not to have occurred.

6.       Writes to the landowner seeking that further operations on site cease until the Plans of Management required under Condition 66 are produced and approved for the reported EEC’s observed on site during clearing activities.

7.       Requires any request for landowners consent for future access to this site to be referred to a full Council decision.

8.       Holds a Councillor Workshop to discuss options to require this development to adhere to current environmental, aboriginal heritage, and flood risk expectations. The workshop to be based on legal advice obtained in point 1 and take account of insurance issues.

9.       Notes that Resolution 175 from Council Meeting 02/05/2019 is still outstanding (copied below).

RESOLVED that Council:

1.       Defers granting of a temporary licence to Feitelson Holdings Pty Ltd and Garbind Pty Ltd over Lot 1 DP 1011625 until such time as the consent condition for allowing access through Council's property is amended.

2.       Writes a letter to applicant seeking advice if the subject access road is intended to be the permanent access.

3.            Seeks further details on the removal of major electricity infrastructure.

4.       Seeks detailed specifications of the access road construction between the water quality control ponds on the development site and immediately adjacent tidal channel eg. width of road access/buffer area, extent of excavation and maintaining tidal regime and stormwater flow.

5.       Requests that an Acid Sulfate Soil investigation be undertaken and management provisions be included in any works required for the access road that occur below ground level.

6.       Requires the provision of above information to be considered with any approval of the license extension.

7.       Advises the applicants that as per Condition 26A(f) a table identifying compliance with the conditions of consent will be required for consideration of an extension of the temporary access.

8.       As part of the modification application seeks to negotiate improved environmental outcomes in accordance with the Coastal Management State Environmental Planning Policy.

10.     ATTACHMENTS 1-11 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:

(g)     advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege

 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase

RESOLVED that:

1.     The Minutes of the Floodplain Management Committee Meeting held Friday 3 March 2023 be received and noted, and

2.     The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

2.    Minimising Current and Future Flood Risk in the Tweed Shire 

That the draft Council report ‘Minimising Current and Future Flood Risk in the Tweed Shire’ be submitted to a Council meeting.   

 3.    CSIRO Northern Rivers Resilience Initiative

That the Floodplain Management Committee:

1.    Supports the continuation and completion of the Tweed Valley Flood Study Update and Expansion project, which is fully funded and well advanced, to provide a complete hydrologic/hydraulic flood model for the Tweed Valley floodplain.

2.    Recommends to Council that Council writes the following request to the CSIRO Northern Rivers Resilience Initiative (NRRI):

a.    That the NRRI provides a technical peer review of the draft Tweed Valley Flood Study Update and Expansion report, to allay community concerns that it is fit for purpose and provides the best available information on flood risk in the Tweed Valley.

b.    That the NRRI utilises the updated Tweed Valley flood model to be provided by Council, to test:

       i.    The potential effectiveness of dredging activities as a flood mitigation measure at various reaches of the Tweed River and its tributaries.
      ii.    The effect that the Pacific Motorway has on flood behaviour, including the Barney’s Point Bridge approach, on the floodplain for all villages and determine any necessary measures to mitigate adverse impacts. 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle from Living Waters Church, Tumbulgum.


1 Timothy 2:1-4 (NKJV)
Therefore I exhort first of all that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks be made for all men, 2 for kings and all who are in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and reverence. 3 For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour, 4 who desires all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
 
Dear Lord
 
Today as decisions are being made as to direction of our shire, according to your word, we pray and give thanks for those you have placed in authority to govern our shire. We thank you that the decisions they make, in godly reverence, will cause us to live in peace. 

May they be led by your Holy Spirit especially in the tough decisions and help them to find the truth of each situation so they can govern well.
 
We ask that your peace will reign over their personal lives and families and thank you for the personal sacrifice they have each given to represent us in Council.
 
We ask this in Jesus name

Local Government Act
This report is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, which permits the meeting to be closed to the public for business relating to the following: 

(d)     commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: 

 (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or 
 (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or 
 (iii) reveal a trade secret


Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that:

  1. Council approves the General Manager negotiating with each interest holder of part 83 Fraser Drive Terranora, Lot 1 DP798632 (property), to endeavour to reach agreement to Council's acquisition of the property.

  2. If agreement is reached, Council will acquire the property, provided that such agreement will be subject to a further resolution of Council.

  3. If no such agreement is reached within a reasonable period of time:
    • The acquisition of the property be carried out by compulsory process in accordance with Part 1 of Chapter 8 of the Local Government Act 1993 and the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991;
    • Council seeks approval from the Minister for Local Government in accordance with section 187 of the Local Government Act 1993 to give all necessary Proposed Acquisition Notices (PAN) in accordance with the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991;
    • Council takes further steps as is necessary to obtain approval from the Minister, the Governor or any public authority as may be necessary, and take all actions as may be necessary, to give notices and otherwise carry out the acquisitions by means of compulsory acquisition;
    • Following receipt of the Minister's approval, Council serves each PAN and takes each other action necessary to carry out the acquisition;
    • Following receipt of the Governor's approval, Council gives effect to the acquisition by publication of an Acquisition Notice in the NSW Government Gazette and such other publication as may be required by law;
    • Council pays compensation to all interest holders entitled to compensation by virtue of the compulsory acquisition on the terms set out in the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991.

  4. Council authorises the General Manager to complete and execute all documentation necessary to finalise and bring into force Council’s acquisition of the Property, including use of the Common Seal of Council (if necessary) for any applications to the Minister, the Governor, the Register General or any public authority for the compulsory acquisition.

  5. Upon acquisition, Council intends to dedicate the acquired land as road. 

  6.  ATTACHMENTS 1 to 7 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
    (a)     personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors)
    (d)     commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: 
              (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
              (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or 
              (iii) reveal a trade secret

The Motion was Carried
 
VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Holds a combined Australia Day Award ceremony and Citizenship ceremony on the afternoon of 25 January 2024 at the Tweed Heads Auditorium.
     
  2. The Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards Selection Panel (comprising all Councillors) and the current Awardees, consider the 2024 Tweed Shire Australia Day Award nominations for the following categories:
    • Citizen of the Year
    • Arts and Culture
    • Volunteer of the Year (individual)
    • Volunteer of the Year (group)
    • Sporting Achievement (individual) 
    • Sporting Achievement (group)
    • Community Event of the Year 
    • Young Achiever in Community Service

        with the option to make an ‘Honourable Mention’ to a nominee who deserves recognition for their efforts.

  3. Support, from the Australia Day Awards budget, conforming applications for financial assistance from non-profit organisations and community groups for hosting small community Australia Day events for 2024.

  4. Acknowledges that the awards and ceremony held in 2023 was funded by an existing budget of $10,094, in addition to grant funding and the 2024 awards and ceremony will be organised based on the 2023/2024 Australia Day budget allocation.
     
  5. Supports the rollover of funds from the 2022/2023 Australia Day events budget, as well as the 2022/2023 Civic Business - Civic Ceremonies budget.
     
  6. Supports the introduction of absentee voting for awardees that cannot attend the Tweed Shire Australia Day Selection Panel.

  7. On the basis that Council nominates its next Tweed Shire Australia Day Ambassador from within the past year's recipients, Council invites (subject to their acceptance), 2023 Arts and Culture awardee, Allira Cornell.  If Allira is unavailable, the invitation be extended to the 2023 Citizen of the Year Joan Henderson.

  8. Invites the 2023 Citizen of the Year, Joan Henderson to be the 2024 Tweed Shire Australia Day Community Event representative. If Joan is unavailable, the invitation be extended to the co-winners of the 2023 Sporting Achievement - Individual award category.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase

Local Government Act
This report is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, which permits the meeting to be closed to the public for business relating to the following: 

(d)     commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: 

 (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or 
 (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or 
 (iii) reveal a trade secret


Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that:

  1. Council approves the General Manager negotiating with each interest holder of Fraser Drive, Terranora, Lot 227 in DP755740, to endeavour to reach agreement to Council's acquisition of the Property;
      
  2. If agreement is reached, Council will acquire the Property, provided that such agreement will be subject to a further resolution of Council.
      
  3. If no such agreement is reached within a reasonable period of time:
    • the acquisition of the Property be carried out by compulsory process in accordance with Part 1 of Chapter 8 of the Local Government Act 1993 and the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991;
    • Council seeks approval from the Minister for Local Government in accordance with section 187 of the Local Government Act 1993 to give all necessary Proposed Acquisition Notices (PAN) in accordance with the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991;
    • Council takes each further steps as is necessary to obtain approval from the Minister, the Governor or any public authority as may be necessary, and take all actions as may be necessary, to give notices and otherwise carry out the acquisitions by means of compulsory acquisition;
    • Following receipt of the Minister's approval, Council serves each PAN and takes each other action necessary to carry out the acquisition;
    • Following receipt of the Governor's approval, Council gives effect to the acquisition by publication of an Acquisition Notice in the NSW Government Gazette and such other publication as may be required by law;
    • Council pays compensation to all interest holders entitled to compensation by virtue of the compulsory acquisition on the terms set out in the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991.

  4. Council authorises the General Manager to complete and execute all documentation necessary to finalise and bring into force Council’s acquisition of the Property, including use of the Common Seal of Council (if necessary) for any applications to the Minister, the Governor, the Register General or any public authority for the compulsory acquisition.

  5. Upon acquisition, Council intends to resolve to classify the acquired land as ‘operational’ land (following a 28-day public submission period) pursuant to section 31 of the Local Government Act 1993 and a further report will be brought back to Council.

  6. ATTACHMENTS 1 - 4 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:

(d)     commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: 
             (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
             (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or 
             (iii) reveal a trade secret


The Motion was Carried
 
VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Writes to the Minister for Local Government Mr Ron Hoenig and the Minister for North Coast Ms Rose Jackson to advise the costs that Council have been quoted for the upcoming 2024 Local Government elections and request a 40% reduction in fees for all flood impacted Councils on the North Coast due to the huge flood recovery costs we are currently facing.  Letter to include: 

    1. an estimate of the likely gap in Disaster Recovery Funding Arrangements and the cost to Council of the 2022 flood

    2. a request for an explanation of State Government's contribution to the costs

  2. Writes to the NSW Electoral Commission:

    1.  noting that during the recent State Government elections prepoll occurred for only 6 days and reminding them of their commitment to provide the same level of service to voters at the Local Government elections as at the State elections and asking if the quoted costs would now be reduced due to a more than halving of time required for manning prepoll locations.

    2. requests a review of the number of polling booths and the removal of polling booths that are within 5km of each other in order to reduce costs.

  3. Writes to the Northern Rivers Joint Organisation to join Council in writing to the new Minister for Local Government to request a 40% subsidy for the 2024 Local Government Election costs for all North Coast effected Councils due to the extreme costs being incurred in flood recovery.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that:

  1. The Mayoral Minute for March 2023 be received. 

  2. Attendance of Councillors at the following conferences be determined and authorised:

    • 23-26 May Floodplain Management Conference - Sydney :Cr Cherry
    • 31 May - 1 June Local Government Conference Expanding The Possibilities - Sydney : nil.
    • 7-9 September National Tree Symposium - Adelaide : Cr Firth

    • In accordance with clause 6.37 of the Councillor Expenses and Facilities Policy, Council has considered factors including the:
      • relevance of the topics and presenters to current council priorities and business and the exercise of the councillors civic duties 
      • cost of the conference or seminar in relation to the total remaining budget.

  3. Council noted the upcoming retirement of the Acting Director for Sustainable Communities and the Environment and thanked Mr Stewart Brawley for his 33 years of service to Council and the community. 

    It was noted that Stewart had joined Council in 1990 as a gardener and worked his way up to Acting Director for Sustainable Communities and the Environment. 

    He has been responsible for the public face of Council in the Parks and Recreation unit for 23 years and was praised for his ability to find solutions to contentious issues and finding a great balance in getting the best outcome for the community while making sure the services provided were fair to all. 

    His steady guidance and even-handedness in dealing with community issues has been an incredible asset to Council and he will be sorely missed. 

    Council wished him well in his next adventure and would like to particularly thank Stewart for staying an extra 6 months in his role when Council needed his expertise and experience.

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase
