Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

 

RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 9 March 2023 be received and noted and 

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:
6.1  Rail Trail, signage
The signage as shown in Plan INF10 Rail Trail Murwillumbah Station line marking and signage, be supported. A designated space be signed in close proximity to the Murwillumbah Rail Trail entry "No Parking, authorised vehicles excepted." A No Stopping zone be installed on the east side of Tweed Valley Way, opposite Crabbes Creek Road, to prevent vehicles stopping on the road shoulder.

6.2  Murwillumbah Street, Murwillumbah - bus zone
The existing No Parking 8am - 9:30am signage on Murwillumbah Street, Murwillumbah east of the marked pedestrian crossing, be modified to include Bus Zone 2:30pm - 4pm on School Days (adjacent to the church). Prior to installation, officers are to communicate the proposed changes to the school and the church.

7.1  Ozone Street, Chinderah
A yellow unbroken (C3) line be installed on the cul-de-sac bulb of Ozone Street, Chinderah.

7.2  Heffron Street, Tweed Heads South
The proposed works on Heffron Street, Tweed Heads South, to upgrade pedestrian facilities are supported subject to:
• Installation of the regulatory pedestrian crossing signage R3-1
• Replacement of the proposed No Standing signs with yellow edgeline (C3)
The proposed installation of No Stopping signs on Heffron Street, west of the proposed marked pedestrian crossing (adjacent to the school), should only be implemented after the Oxley Street parent pick-up area has been constructed in Arkinstall Park.

7.3.  Gold Coast Challenger Event - surfing
The proposed Gold Coast Challenger Event (Surfing) in May 2023 be supported, subject to current COVID-19 restrictions at the time of the event:
1. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted and approved by Council and Police at least 2 weeks before the event).
2. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
3. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
4. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
5. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
6. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
7. Council approves the installation of signage and devices to effect the proposed closure of Coral Street, Tweed Heads. 


The Motion was Carried
 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen

VOTE AGAINST - None

ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase

RESOLVED that:
 
1.  Council writes to:
  • The Honourable Daniel Mookhey MLC, Treasurer
  • The Honourable Jihad Dib MP Minister for Customer Service and Digital Government, Minister for Emergency Services, and Minister for Youth Justice
  • The Honourable Ron Hoenig MP Minister for Local Government
  • cc Federal and State Members for Tweed and Lismore

    Requesting immediate reinstatement of the subsidy for the Emergency Services Contributions, including this year’s increase above the rate peg and to work with LGNSW on a more appropriate funding model and/or transparent and sustainable collection methodology.

2.  Council requests the Northern Rivers Joint Organisation make a similar request. 

3.  The Mayor makes representations to all interested Government representatives on this issue.

4. The following background be noted:

Council has in the last week of April been informed that the NSW Government’s Emergency Services Contribution payable by Council for the next financial year will be increased to $1,476, 236.21. This is a 24.28% increase on previous years charges; combined with a decision by the state government to no longer provide a subsidy for these charges and means that although Council budgeted a 4% increase in the funds remitted to the State on the previous years into the budget, the actual cost will be $540,000 more than has been budgeted for.

In effect this means that paying this cost would take up one third of the proposed special rate increase and leave Council in a situation where it would have to proceed with both the special rate variation to continue providing the community with the same level of service AND introduce service level cuts in order to fund the state government levy.
 
This year (2022-23) Council had budgeted for an Emergency Services Contribution increase of 2.25% as well as a continuation of the assistance provided by the State. 
For next year we had originally allowed for an increase of 2% in the long term financial plan. This was increased to 4% as a result of the announced rate peg and we also, like most other councils had allowed for the continuation of assistance in the absence of advice to the contrary. 
 
Council had received no advice that either the assistance would stop or that the Emergency Services Levy Contributions increase would be in the vicinity of 25%. It is apparent that most other councils are in the same position. Some councils such as Tenterfield will have 119% of their rate peg increase eaten up by the increase to the state government levy.
 
To have councils confronted with this increase in charges when we have already gone to the community with a proposed budget and rate variation means Councils has no opportunity to fund the contributions except to reduce services provided by Council.
 
The Emergency Services Levy is a state government levy imposed on all ratepayers but collected by councils on behalf of the state. This situation needs to change as it is supposed to be independent of Council but has huge impacts on the financial planning and budgeting of councils. This charge should be collected either as a separate bill sent to the ratepayer directly or as a Federal levy added to taxation bills like the Medicare Levy is. This would result in a fair and equitable contribution to the provision of Emergency Services for disasters but keep the collection of these funds as the responsibility of those tasked with its distribution.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd:

"Gracious God, 
 
The events of Youth Week reminded us of the contribution young people are making to our Shire.  Thank you for their energy and passion to make an impact on the world.  We’re grateful for parents, teachers, coaches, community leaders and elders, and volunteer organisations who work hard for our youth to reach their potential.  Please continue to bless the Council as it works with youth today so our community is even better tomorrow.
 
We also acknowledge the coronation of King Charles this Saturday.  Please give him wisdom to fulfil his duties well, and a strong commitment to justice and the needs of the vulnerable.  We pray for those in our community for whom this event will reopen grief over trauma inflicted in the name of the Crown.  We long for true reconciliation and healing.
 
As Council considers today the varied and sometimes competing needs within our Shire, grant both Councillors and staff a deep satisfaction as they do this important work on our behalf.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that:
 
1.  Development Application DA21/0830.02 for an amendment to Development Consent DA21/0830 for a 2 lot subdivision at Lot 30 DP 1092500 No. 6 Sunnycrest Drive, Terranora be approved subject to the consent being amended as per the conditions attached to the report for this item; and

2.  Adds a new PSC Condition No. 35 which reads as follows:

35.    Prior to issue of Subdivision Certificate, fourteen (14) compensatory local native plants being seven (7) trees Cupaniopsis anacardioides (Tuckeroo) and seven (7) complementary local native plants shall be installed in the location of T35 to T41 (inclusive) as shown on Plan of Trees on Site - Plan No. 21101-4 - Issue D - Sheet 1 of 1 - Prepared by Michel Group Services dated 19 April 2023 (as amended in red by Council), to the satisfaction of Council’s General Manager or delegate. All compensatory trees shall be of minimum 25 Litre stock size and of minimum tube stock size for other native plants, installed in accordance with Tweed Shire Council Landscaping Standards Dwg. No. S.D.701 Issue C Tree and Shrub Planting Details – Advanced Tree Planting in Turf.

3.  Council approves the variation of Restriction on the Use of Land seventeenthly referred to in DP 1092500 over Lot 30 in DP 1092500 so that it burdens each lot except Lot 30 and 32; and
 
4.  Council executes all necessary documentation in relation to this matter under the Common Seal of Council.  In this regard, the revised restriction for the proposed lots is to be finalised prior to the variation of existing restriction seventeenthly referred to in DP 1092500; and

5.  A Penalty Infringement Notice (PIN) be issued to the owner of the subject property for breach of Condition 7A of Development Consent DA21/0830 (as amended).

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd. 


Gracious God, 
 
In National Volunteer Week we are grateful for the many individuals and organisations who strengthen our community through their volunteer service. For those who put themselves in harm’s way for the sake of others, please keep them safe.  For those who work with people who are vulnerable and in distress, may their compassion never fail.  For those who advocate on behalf of others, bless their commitment to justice and equity.  We thank you for the many ways Council facilitates the work of volunteer organisations.
 
And as Reconciliation Week approaches we remember Council’s commitment to reconciliation in action.  We recognise the valuable contribution the Tweed Aboriginal community make to the shire, and their voice for, and care for the Country we all share.  Please bless all efforts to build strong and respectful relationships so we will move further towards the true reconciliation that is your intention for all humanity.
 
May your grace, mercy, and peace be our experience throughout this meeting.  
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen.

ALTERNATE MOTION


Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that:

  1. The following tabled Petition be received. 

    Petition containing 45 signatories of which 44 are valid (with 1 being invalid due to lack of address details) was received on 26 April 2023 entitled "Pedestrian safety and speeding vehicles in Burringbar".

    "We the residents of Tweed Valley Way, Cudgera Creek Road, Howards Road and Wallaroo Drive in Burringbar are petitioning Tweed Shire Council and Transport for NSW to assess the increased traffic conditions and exceedance of safe vehicle speeds on these roadways. We would like to see the speed limit on Tweed Valley Way at the village boundary reduced to 50km and the speed limit beyond the village residential area signposted at a reduced limit for the extent of Howards Road and Cudgera Creek Road; where there is currently no speed limit applied. There are many blind corners on these narrow rural roads, limited or non-existent road verges and often steep gullies and precipitous drop offs at the road edge. With many vehicles - be they delivery trucks vans or people travelling to/from work, traveling at speed - we are fearful of our safety and that of our children who join us riding bikes, horses and walking their dogs along these roads."

  2. Council notes that the petition has been referred to the Local Traffic Committee for advice regarding implementation of this request. 

  3. ATTACHMENTS 1 and 2 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contains:
    (e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.

The Motion was Carried

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins


"Dear Father,
 
I thank you for the men & women You have chosen for the task that is ahead of them. 
 
Each one of them is unique, bringing a variety of experiences, skills & knowledge that is valued & appreciated. 
 
I pray that You will give each & every one of them strength, wisdom & humility to press on, serving & providing for the people of the Tweed Shire. 
 
May our counsellors also encourage & build one another up in their various areas of responsibilities.  
 
Help each one of them to plan & carry out their various tasks with clear lines of communication, harmony, respect & integrity. May they be united in one mind & spirit that all they seek to do will be achieved with great success.
 
Father, we don’t know the future or what it holds for us, so I pray for our counsellors that You may watch over them & their families. Protecting & keeping each one of them safe in the days to come. May Your Will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
 
Thank you again for Your many blessings. We look forward to the contributions & gifts of service our counsellors will bring to the Tweed Shire. 
 
Bless each one of them I pray.
 
So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 
 
That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.
 
Thank You Father… Amen."

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that:

1.      Development Application DA22/0088 for a telecommunications facility at Lot 2 DP 815370 No. 1126 Pottsville Road, Pottsville be refused for the following reasons:

 

a.     The consent authority cannot be satisfied that the Development is not likely to significantly affect threatened species pursuant to section 7.2 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016 and that no Biodiversity Development Assessment Report was required to accompany the DA.

 

b.     The consent authority cannot be satisfied that the Development is consistent with the approved koala plan of management that applies to the Site, as required by section 4.8(2) of State Environmental Planning Policy (Biodiversity and Conservation) 2021.

 

c.    The DA has not demonstrated that the Development has been designed to minimise and mitigate impacts on the environmental values of the Site. The DA has not demonstrated that there will not be a significant or unacceptable impact on ecological values of the Site. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

 

d.     The proposal does not provide adequate evidence that it will not significantly impact on the following attributes listed under clause 2.8(1) of State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021 in particular: 


(a) the biophysical, hydrological or ecological integrity of the adjacent coastal wetland, or

(b) the quantity and quality of surface and ground water flows to and from the adjacent coastal wetland.

 

e.     The application fails to adequately respond to Clause 25 of Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2000 Development in Zone 7 (a) Environmental Protection (Wetlands and Littoral Rainforests) and on adjacent land, including the provision of a Plan of Management. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

 

f.     The development is not consistent with the Aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed’s natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways, visual amenity and scenic routes, built environment, and cultural heritage. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979. 

 

g.     The development is not consistent with the Aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to conserve or enhance the biological diversity, scenic quality and geological and ecological integrity of Tweed. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979. 

 

h.      The development is not consistent with the Aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to conserve or enhance areas of defined high ecological value. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979. 

 

i.    The development is not consistent with the Aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to provide special protection and suitable habitat for the recovery of the Tweed coastal Koala. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979. 

 

j.   The development proposal has not demonstrated due compliance and consideration of The Tweed development Control Plan 2008 Section A19 – Biodiversity and Habitat Management. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

 

k.    On the basis of the information submitted, the development proposal, is not considered to be in the public interest. Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

 

2.       Council works with the proponent to investigate alternate sites to service the Pottsville community with the aim to achieve an agreed site within 6 months.


3.      ATTACHMENT 10 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

 

(e)          information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Reece Byrnes
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle.


Reading from Matthew chapter 6 verses 9-13 (King James Version)
 
The Lord’s Prayer
 9 After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. 10 Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
 11 Give us this day our daily bread. 
12 And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. 
13 And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, 
     and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen. 
 
As we open this meeting with prayer, let us follow the model that our Lord Jesus gave us.
 
Oh Lord our God, we honour you as Lord of this earth, Lord of this nation and Lord of this shire. We pray that your will be done, not the will of any man, but that your will, will be accomplished through your servants on this council. We pray that every person in this shire will be fed & not go hungry, and we thank you for the bountiful provision you bring through this shire. We ask for your forgiveness for the times we have strayed from your commands and ask that you help us to remain in a spirit of forgiveness toward our fellow man. I pray that you would protect us & deliver us from any & all evil, for your Kingdom, Power & Glory are from everlasting to everlasting.
 
In Christ we pray, Amen.

The Mayor paid tribute to Vince Connell Director Planning and Regulation who has resigned from Council:
 
On behalf of Council, I would like to take this opportunity to thank our Planning Director, Mr Vince Connell. As many of you know he is leaving us today for further opportunities and I want to acknowledge the many years he has provided a guiding hand to the last three iterations of Councillors on the Tweed. Vince has been Planning Director for the Tweed Shire for the last 15 years but has worked in local government for another 12 years before that so he has certainly built an incredible wealth of knowledge that as Councillors we have relied on. It is a sad day today for us as we say goodbye, you are certainly leaving incredibly big shoes to fill. I know from my 6 and a half years here at Council that you have been able to provide a steady hand, a patient voice of reason. You have been able to find that right balance of walking the line between the legislative requirements your staff follow and the pressures of community sentiment and expectation that Councillors will always be wanting to consider.
 
 In those times when Council have all of the background and information provided and yet still needed to choose an outcome different to the staff recommendation, you have always respected the Councils need to represent the views of the community and helped us find a way forward, so I thank you for your professionalism, your understanding and your help. I have never met anyone who works as tirelessly as you and provides feedback so quickly, constructively and efficiently. You will be sorely missed. The legacy you leave in the Tweed is clear for all to see, we have a fast-growing Shire that is still managing to keep a very high level of community satisfaction and that, more than anything, is due to our planning controls matching the expectation of our residents. You have worked hard to protect our natural environment that our community so strongly values, while ensuring that what is built here is high quality and protects the amenity of our shire. I know that you are incredibly well respected in the Planning Industry, and you have led Council to win many accolades and awards for excellence in planning. You will be very sought after in the industry going forward.  
 
 We wish you every success in this new chapter of your life. We hope that it allows you to put your wealth of knowledge and experience to work in a way that is fulfilling and rewarding. Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that Council undertakes the following steps to address ongoing koala mortality due to a vehicle strike on Clothiers Creek Road between North Hill Court and Rosewood Avenue, Bogangar:

  1. Notes the recent decision by Gold Coast City Council to reduce the speed of Tallebudgera Rd to 50kph in order to reduce risk of koala strike.

  2. Immediately request urgent consideration by NSW Roads and Maritime Services to reduce the speed limit on Clothiers Creek Road to 50kph in the section that intersects with Cudgen Creek Nature Reserve.  In the request Council includes both the accident records for Clothiers Creek and the history of fatal wildlife strike that we have for this road and a reasoned justification for the speed reduction based on risk reduction for both people and wildlife.

  3. Consults with the Department of Planning and Environment to confirm the planning approval pathway for road works / environmental protection works on Clothiers Creek Road within coastal wetland areas.

  4. Determines the viability of solar power for the lighting of chicanes and/or vehicle-activated signage.

  5. Engages a Traffic Engineering Consultant to prepare a traffic assessment considering all proposed design options, and their impacts on traffic behaviour and distribution on the network.

  6. Commissions an additional survey to enable a more detailed design and a better understanding of the footprint and potential impacts associated with each design option.

  7. Prepares a cost analysis of the preferred options.

  8. Develops a community consultation plan in collaboration with community engagement, traffic, and biodiversity staff as well as the Local Traffic Committee, Transport for NSW, Tweed Coast Koala Advisory Committee, and Aboriginal Advisory Committee.

  9. Consults with the community. 

  10. Selects a preferred design option based on ecological, traffic, community, and financial impacts and benefits associated with each option.

  11. Reports the outcome of the above steps to the Local Traffic Committee (LTC).

  12. Reports the recommendations of LTC to Council for endorsement and consideration of funding for the preferred option.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 11 May 2023 be received and 

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1   Mooball Street, George Street, Mayal Street Intersection - Murwillumbah
That a Stop sign and associated line-marking be installed on Mayal Street, Murwillumbah, at the intersection with George and Mooball Streets. Short lengths (10m) of (BB) double centre lines be installed on George and Mooball Streets, on the approaches to Mayal Street.

6.2  Crabbes Creek, Mooball, timed parking
That signage be installed as per the below:

Crabbes Creek
“1P:  Mon-Fri 7am – 6pm,  Sat-Sun 7:30am-5pm”
On Crabbes Creek Road, Crabbes Creek, opposite the General Store, between Bluegum Court and the power pole with the streetlight opposite the fuel pumps.
 
Mooball
“15 minute:  Mon-Thu 7am-1pm,  Fri 7am – 12 Midday”
On Tweed Valley Way in front of Post Office between the refuge island and the yellow line, approximately 18m.

6.3  Proudfoots Lane, Murwillumbah
That:
1.   The existing stencils be repainted on Proudfoots Lane, Murwillumbah.
2.   Two rubber [ 1.6m(w) x 2m(L) ]  speed humps be installed at locations adjacent to streetlights, subject to available funding.

6.4  Broadway, Burringbar
Council to develop a Concept Design for a potential 40km/h high pedestrian activity zone on Broadway, Burringbar, for submission to Transport for NSW for review and consideration of funding.

7.1  Tweed Coast Road, Pottsville - Pedestrian Crossings
Officers conduct pedestrian observations on Tweed Coast Road near the Pottsville Oval and provide advice back to the Local Traffic Committee on the findings. The second nominated location on the northern end of Tweed Coast Road for a marked pedestrian crossing, is not supported, as adequate facilities are provided in close proximity to the roundabout.

7.2  Northern Rivers Rail Trail
The Committee discussed that issues have been raised in relation to the interaction of Cyclists at road crossing points along the trail.
That an audit be conducted of the road crossing points along the Trail and brought back to the Committee for consideration.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

1.  The following tabled Petition be received. 

Petition containing 300 signatories of which 254 are valid (with 41 being invalid due to lack of address details and 5 being invalid due to no signature) was received on 6 June 2023 entitled "Review of Funding for Banora Point Community Centre Project Officer's Position and Continuing Support for the Fun Activities for Banora Seniors (FABS) Programme".
 
 "The Tweed Council meeting on 16 March 2023 voted to discontinue the federal funds CHSP (Commonwealth Home Support Program) that currently funds the Project Support Officer's position that initiates and supports a wide range of programmes for Seniors (FABS) at the Banora Point Community Centre. These programmes are open to all and contribute significantly to the health and wellbeing of Seniors in the Community.
  
 The under-signed members of the community are very concerned that without support for this position the future of FABS is uncertain.
 
 We petition Tweed Shire Council to:
 
 1. Ensure that funding for the Banora Point Community Centre's Project Officer position is continued
 2. Ensure the wide range of programmes for Seniors (FABS) is maintained and allowed to expand."

2.  That in recognition of the importance of the FABS program to the community, Council requests the General Manager to provide a report to Council following the upcoming community consultation process on ways in which Council can facilitate the program continuing.

3. ATTACHMENT 1 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle from the Living Waters Church, Tumbulgum.

Exodus 33: 13-14 New King James Version (NKJV)


The Promise of God’s Presence


13 Now therefore, I pray, if I have found grace in Your sight, show me now Your way, that I may know You and that I may find grace in Your sight. And consider that this nation is Your people.”

 14 And He said, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
  
 Prayer
  
 Dear Lord, 
  
 As council sits today to preside over matters concerning the Tweed Shire, we seek your guidance, your direction and your favour. 
 
 I thank you Lord that you know every person by name and your Goodness & Kindness is displayed towards the people of this beautiful land that we live in. 
  
 As Moses asked of you, so do we. We want to know your ways, know your presence, and find Grace in Your sight. Guide every decision made here today so that we are being directed by the will of Almighty God. 
  
 In Jesus name we Pray
  
 Amen.

REASON FOR CONFIDENTIALITY

Local Government Act
This report is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, which permits the meeting to be closed to the public for business relating to the following: 

(c)     information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business 


Cr Warren Polglase
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that:

  1. Council approves the General Manager negotiating the acquisition by private agreement of the whole of Lot 21 DP331993, 39 West End Street, Murwillumbah (Property), for wastewater, sewerage infrastructure and road purposes.

  2. Council executes the Contract of Sale with the landowner for the acquisition of the Property.

  3. Council pays the landowner compensation for up to an amount as detailed in the valuation report attached to this report.

  4. Upon acquisition, Council intends to resolve to classify the acquired Property as 'operational' land (following a 28-day public submission period) pursuant to section 31 of the Local Government Act 1993 and a further report will be brought back to Council.

  5. All necessary documentation in relation to this matter to be executed under the Common Seal of Council.

  6. ATTACHMENTS 1-6 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:

(c)     information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business.


The Motion was Carried

CONFIDENTIAL COMMITTEE

REPRESENTATIONS FOR ITEMS CONSIDERED IN COMMITTEE
(Sec 3.40, 13.9 to 13.17 Model Code of Meeting Practice)

Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.
 
EXCLUSION OF PRESS AND PUBLIC

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that, in regards to DA13/0712 at 67 Howards Road, Burringbar and the ongoing noise compliance matters Council:

1.  Continues to seek legal advice on DA Compliance as required noting that the ATP Acoustic Report submitted March 2023 detailed potential non-compliance with consent conditions 54.5A and 55; and

2.  Accepts the Scope 1 quote from PKA Acoustic Consulting to peer review the applicants ATP report for compliance against DA13/0712.02 with the following additional questions:

a.  The ATP report has put forward using a background value obtained at 41 Howards Road as a suitable background value for 74 and 75 Howards Road, even though previous court appointed consultants measured the background at 74 and 75 Howards Road as lower than that at 41 Howards Road. Previous proponent employed consultants measured the background at 74 and 75 Howards Road as lower than that presently being put forward. 41 Howards Road is approximately 220 m closer to Tweed Valley Way (main arterial road) than the residence on 75 Howards Road and this may have a significant impact on background noise levels and the validity of using such a background level.

b.  Although not specifically required by Condition 54.5A, it would assist for the acoustic report to report on noise emanating from the Birchmeier mister machine as this is relevant to Condition 55.

c.  Condition 55 requires measurement of all noise from the site, which includes the Birchmeier mister and requires adjustments for annoying noise to be made if required. Previous acoustic reports have measured the noise emanating from the Birchmeier Mister to require adjustments for tonality. It would assist for the acoustic report to report on this.

d.  The site used for measuring the noise at 75 Howards Road was possibly located in the noise shadow of the acoustic wall and may not accurately represent noise received at the residence at 75 Howards Road. Advice is sought on this matter.

e.  The consultant used is registered in Queensland. Advice is sought on whether the methodology used aligns with by New South Wales noise measurement standards and policies; and

3.  Prioritise replacing the unattended noise monitors back at the neighbour's property.

4.  ATTACHMENTS 1-4 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
(g)    advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins, Murwillumbah Church of Christ


"Let’s pray:

Father, I thank You for knowing that You are here amongst us. 

You are our unseen Guest, silently listening & watching in all that will be said & done.

You are our good & mighty Counsellor whose ways are good & right. 

I pray that You, will provide guidance for our mayor & every counsellor here, that they also may have in mind to do what is good & right. 

I pray that You will give each one of them wisdom, discernment & humility. Help them know what needs to be discussed & accomplished as they provide & protect over the Tweed Shire. 

I pray that every counsellor gives careful consideration & attention to those they have been given charge over, and that the relationship between Council & the people of the Tweed will continue to grow in trust & respect. 

Father, I would also like to pray in appreciation of each one of our counsellors, for the service they provide and the accountability each of them carries.  

May You also continue to provide and protect over each of our council members, their families & their loved ones. 

So, Father, continue to help and guide us, that we may live to practice the values we know to be true. 

That Council be transparent in all its dealings. Treating the people of the Tweed with fairness, commitment, planning for their future…with everyone involved:

So that our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.

May You answer us in the day we call… Amen."

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RECOMMENDED that: 

A.  Development Application DA20/0386 for a 13 lot subdivision (11 residential lots, 1 drainage lot and 1 residual dedicated riparian lot) at Lot 156 DP 628026 No. 40 Creek Street, Hastings Point be refused for the following reasons:
 
1.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal does not comply with Clause 1.2 Aims of the Tweed LEP 2014 as the development does not:
 
i. give effect to the desired outcomes, strategic principles, policies and actions contained in the Council’s adopted strategic planning documents, including, but not limited to, consistency with local indigenous cultural values, and the national and international significance of the Tweed Caldera as required by subclause (a), 
 
ii. promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed’s natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways, visual amenity and scenic routes, built environment, and cultural heritage as required by subclause (c), 
 
iii. promote development that is consistent with the principles of ecologically sustainable development and to implement appropriate action on climate change as required by subclause (d), 
 
iv. conserve or enhance the biological diversity, scenic quality and geological and ecological integrity of Tweed as required by subclause (g), 
 
v. conserve or enhance areas of defined high ecological value as required by subclause (i), 
 
2.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal does not comply with Clause 5.21(1) Flood Planning of the Tweed LEP 2014 as the development is not consistent with objectives of this Clause, in particular this development:

 (a)  does not minimise the flood risk to life and property associated with the use of the land
 
(b)  is not compatible with the flood function and behaviour on the land, taking into account projected changes as a result of climate change
 
(c)  does not avoid adverse or cumulative impacts on flood behaviour and the environment and
 
(d)  does not enable the safe occupation and efficient evacuation of people in the event of a flood. 

3.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal does not comply with Clause 5.21(2) of the TLEP 2014 therefore consent cannot be granted to the development for the purpose of a residential subdivision as the application has not satisfied the following clauses:

(a)  The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that the development is compatible with the flood function and behaviour on the land, and  

(b)  The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that the development will not adversely affect flood behaviour in a way that results in detrimental increases in the potential flood affectation of other development or properties, and 

(c)  The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that the development will not adversely affect the safe occupation and efficient evacuation of people or exceed the capacity of existing evacuation routes for the surrounding area in the event of a flood, and 

(d)  The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that the development incorporates appropriate measures to manage risk to life in the event of a flood, and 

(e)  The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that the development will not adversely affect the environment or cause avoidable erosion, siltation, destruction of riparian vegetation or a reduction in the stability of river banks or watercourses. 

4.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal does not comply with Clause 5.21(3) of the TLEP 2014 as the application has not demonstrated adequate consideration of:

(a)  Projected changes to flood behaviour as a result of climate change and,

(b)  whether the development incorporates measures to minimise the risk to life and ensure the safe evacuation of people in the event of a flood. 

5.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal does not comply with Clause 7.2 Earthworks of the TLEP 2014 as the application has not demonstrated the development will not have a detrimental impact on environmental functions and processes, neighbouring uses, cultural or heritage items or features of the surrounding land. 

6.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal does not comply with Clause 7.4 Flood Risk Management of the TLEP 2014 as the application has not demonstrated the development will appropriately respond to the evacuation or emergency response issues, and enable evacuation of land subject to flooding in events exceeding the flood planning level and protect the operational capacity of emergency response facilities and critical infrastructure during extreme flood events.

7.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal does not comply with Clause 5 of the TLEP 2000 as the application has not satisfied the Objectives of this Clause as the proposal does not follow precautionary principles and is not consistent with the conservation of biological diversity and ecological integrity in that the development footprint extends into the 75m and 50m ecological buffer zones of the Coastal Wetlands and removes 340m2 of koala habitat. 

8.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal does not comply with Clause 8 Consent Considerations of the TLEP 2000 as the application has not demonstrated the development will not have an unacceptable cumulative impact on the community, locality or catchment. 

9.   Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal does not comply with Clause 20 Subdivision in Zone 7(a) of the TLEP 2000 as the application has not demonstrated the development will not protect the ecological or scenic values of the land. 

10. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal does not comply with Clause 25(3) of the TLEP 2000 therefore consent cannot be granted to the development for the purpose of a residential subdivision as the application has not properly considered the following clauses:

(a)  The likely effects of the development on the flora and fauna found in the wetlands or littoral rainforest and, 

(b)  The potential for disturbance of native flora and fauna as a result of intrusion by humans and domestic and feral animals, increased fire risk, rubbish dumping, weed invasion and vegetation clearing and, 

(e)  The effect on the wetlands or littoral rainforest of any   proposed clearing, draining, excavating or filling.
 
in particular the cumulative impacts of the development, the location of sediment ponds, lots and APZ in 75m ecological buffer zones and the lack of enforceability of dog and cat bans.

11.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal does not comply with Clause 31(3) Development adjoining Waterbodies of the TLEP 2000 therefore consent cannot be granted to the development for the purpose of a residential subdivision as the application has not satisfied the following clauses: 

(a)  The development will not have a significant adverse effect on scenic quality, water quality, marine ecosystems, or the bio-diversity of the riverine or estuarine area or its function as a wildlife corridor or habitat, and 

e)  The development addresses the likely impact of biting midge and mosquitoes on residents and tourists and the measures to be used to ameliorate the identified impact in particular the creation of a drainage swale the intercepts with the water table creating stagnant water bodies.

12.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal is not consistent with the goals and objectives of the North Coast Regional Plan 2041 in that it does not provide “liveable, sustainable and resilient development” as it proposes residential dwellings on an estuarine location subject to sea-level rise and storm surge impacts. 

13.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal is not consistent with State Environmental Planning Policy (SEPP) (Resilience and Hazards) 2021 Clause 2.7(4): the development cannot be granted consent as it has not demonstrated that sufficient measures have, or will be, taken to protect, and where possible enhance, the biophysical, hydrological and ecological integrity of the coastal wetland or littoral rainforest. 

14.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal is not consistent with State Environmental Planning Policy (SEPP) (Resilience and Hazards) 2021 Clause 2.8: the development cannot be granted consent as it has not demonstrated satisfaction of clause a) or b). 

15.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal is not consistent with State Environmental Planning Policy (SEPP) (Resilience and Hazards) 2021 Clause 2.10 and as such the development cannot be granted consent. 

16.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal is not consistent with State Environmental Planning Policy (SEPP) (Biodiversity and Conservation) 2021 Section 3.8 Tweed Coast Comprehensive Koala Plan of Management in that it removes 340m2 of core koala habitat. 

17.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A3 – Development of Flood Liable Land 

18.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A5 – Subdivision Manual 
 
19.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section B23 – Hastings Point Locality Based Development Code in particular Strategy 2 and Strategy 3.
 
20.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section B23 - Hastings Point Locality Based Development Code in particular Section 4.2.3.3 Controls in particular the minimisation of site fill. 

21.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) the proposal has failed to demonstrate the development will not have a negative impact on the natural and built environment. 

22.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) the proposal has failed to demonstrate suitability of the site for the development in particular the flooding constraints of the site have not been sufficiently addressed. 

23.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(d) the proposal has failed to adequately address the flooding and drainage issues raised in public submissions 

24.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) the proposal is not in the public interest.

B.  ATTACHMENT 7 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

    (g)  information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

The Motion was Carried

VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

RECOMMENDED that

2.  The Growth Management and Housing Strategy have strong regard for the building heights and density controls within the Kingscliff Locality Plan and Tweed Development Control Plan Section B26 - Kingscliff given the extent of community consultation undertaken on these matters.

Cr James Owen
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
 
RECOMMENDED that:

1.  Further work on a planning proposal to prohibit caravan parks on land zoned RU2 Rural Landscape be continued and not wait until finalisation of the Growth and Housing Management Strategy;

2.  The Mayor writes to the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces, the Hon. Paul Scully MP, detailing the issues and concerns with current legislative scheme and planning system, and requesting urgent action by the Minister to review both; and

3.  The Mayor advocates through the Minister for a State-wide response to affordable housing by way of regular housing that is close to services, within walkable catchments, and unaffected by natural hazards such as flooding, bushfire, or spatial segregation.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins, Murwillumbah Church of Christ


Let us pray
 
Heavenly Father, today we come asking for You to fill this place with Your blessings. You have placed us & many others in council because You know we can bring positivity & growth. 
You have shown us what it means to serve others, and today we need You to help us be a role model to everyone we seek to serve. Help us to see the greatness You see in all of us.

Father, it’s not always easy to work in a place where so much is expected from us; as the resources to succeed are not always available. So, we ask that You will give us what we need, to take care of those we are called to serve.
Lord, I also ask that You bring joy to our Mayor & Counsellors. 

Give everyone that refreshing sense of hope & wisdom. I ask that You show us today, that You are here amongst us. Please show us favour in all the works we do, doing Your Will, for the Tweed Shire.
 
So, Father, continue to help and guide us, that we may live to practice the values we know to be true. That Council be transparent in all its dealings today. Treating the people of the Tweed with fairness, commitment, planning for their future…with everyone involved:
So that our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.

May You answer us in the day we call…

ALTERNATE MOTION 
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council submits the following motions to the 2023 Local Government NSW (LGNSW) Annual Conference:

Motion 1 - Caravan Parks
That LGNSW write to the Honourable Minister Scully and request:

  • support to prohibit caravan parks in rural zones with other forms of tourist accommodation still permissible on merit
  • implementing a state government body to help overhaul the caravan park industry similar to NSW Food Authority or NSW Health. A government body is also needed for Moveable Dwellings Outside of Caravan Parks, and Manufactured Home Estates
  • an overhaul of the Local Government (Manufactured Home Estates, Caravan Parks, Camping Grounds and Moveable Dwellings) Regulation 2021, with different requirements  for 'permanent living' caravan parks versus 'tourist  accommodation' caravan parks.

Background information
Tweed like most Councils has problems with the Local Government (Manufactured Home Estate, Caravan Parks, Camping Grounds and Moveable Dwellings) Regulation 2021 (the ‘Regulation’). It is no longer fit for purpose.
Tweed and the Northern Rivers is currently experiencing a problem with either existing traditional caravan parks or new caravan parks being developed into unapproved housing estates under the Regulation.
People are using exemptions under the Regulation to live in caravans and other moveable dwellings on private properties with few or no options to assess bushfire, flood, public health air pollution from airports, or pollution risks.
Manufactured home estates that are akin to residential subdivisions are being developed under the Regulation, which was not created for that purpose.
Caravan Parks were once used predominantly for tourist accommodation, with some longer-term living. With housing affordability and shortage challenges over the past two decades, many caravan parks have evolved from tourist accommodation into permanent living locations. Some caravan parks in highly sought after locations continue to operate as tourist accommodation, and these are generally well run and not part of the current concern.
Tweed currently has 35 active caravan parks with some 4% of our population now residing in these parks. Fewer and fewer are being utilised for tourism. Most are legacy developments that sit within the floodplain and the most affected and displaced persons from the 2022 floods were from these sites.
The eight caravan parks in flood prone Chinderah are examples of caravan parks evolving into permanent living locations. The general change has been gradual over time and has not been approved under the Regulation or the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 (the 'EPAA’).
There may be a stigma with permanent living in a caravan park. There is a high proportion of permanent occupants who wish to change the look of their caravan into a home. Common changes include removing drawbars and wheels, and building structures over and around the caravan to make it look like a home. There is a high proportion of non-compliance at sites in caravan parks in Chinderah, including short term sites being used for long term occupation, unapproved structures, and greater than 65% roof structure site coverage
There is interest in the development industry to create or expand caravan parks to fill the housing affordability and housing shortage gap. Council currently has: A Development Application (DA23/0302) for a caravan park with 112 long-term site at 1126 Pottsville Road, Pottsville.
In the last year Council had a pre DA lodgment meeting (Development Assessment Panel meeting) for alterations and additions including expansion of The Palms caravan park at Dry Dock Road (approved as 240 long term and 10 short term sites) from a residential land-lease community with the intent of targeting the over 50s market, and a proposed caravan park (264 long term and 30 short term sites) to the north of Pottsville on RU2 (Rural Landscape) zoned land.
The Regulation has changed very little over the past 28 years (from the Regulation 1995) when it largely regulated tourist accommodation. It is not an effective tool for regulating predominately permanent living to fill the housing affordability and shortage gap
Caselaw has determined that a caravan park by definition can comprise of (for example) 300 manufactured homes provided there are 8 caravans on site. This can result in developers lodging DA’s for a 'caravan park' on rural land comprising of 300 manufactured homes and 8 caravans on site, where manufactured homes are prohibited. The sites are often not serviced by water or sewer, affected by bushfire, and affected by flooding. Having caravan parks permissible in rural zones gives false hope to developers and can result in long lengthy appeals in the NSW Land & Environment Court.
The Regulation is written for short term accommodation (for example it requires the provision of ironing boards, irons etc.). Over time historic caravan parks have been unlawfully occupied by permanent residents due to the housing affordability and shortage crisis.
There is no Government body to oversee the industry

Motion 2 - Moveable Dwellings Outside Caravan Parks
That LGNSW write to the Honourable Minister Scully and request circulars to assist with interpretation of the Local Government (Manufactured Home Estates, Caravan Parks, Camping Grounds and Moveable Dwellings) Regulation 2021.

Background information
While Council is supportive of Section 77 of the Local Government (Manufactured Home Estate, Caravan Parks, Camping Grounds and Moveable Dwellings) Regulation 2021, it is poorly understood by Councils, and with no expertise in the NSW State Government to technically advise, Councils are struggling to understand and regulate the explosion of caravans and other moveable dwellings and ‘tiny homes’ on private properties.
People are using exemptions under the Regulation to live in caravans and other moveable dwellings (very broad definition) on private properties with few or no options to assess bushfire, flood, public health, aircraft noise and pollution risks. This matter is getting a lot of media coverage at present, with a lot of negativity directed at Councils 'evicting’ people from what they regard as their homes on private properties. All Councils working independently to manage this matter and related challenges is irrational.
An example of where an interpretation is required is under Section 77(b) of the Regulation the owner of a property with a dwelling on it can have caravan if the caravan is occupied by the owner in connection with owners dwelling. The caravan must be occupied in a safe and health condition. What does ‘in connection’ mean? Is this immediately next to the house, or can it be 200 m away? How does Council practically determine ‘members of the owner’s household’? What about a tiny homes, same day granny flats and similar structures? Can they be brought onto a site and left there forever under Section 77(1)(b). Can a landowner use all the provisions under Section 77 concurrently to have multiple caravans/moveable dwellings on the property at the same time? Make it clear that 77(d) can only be used for registerable moveable dwellings (for example a caravan) and provide certification from Service NSW of this, including chassis number or similar.

Motion 3 - Manufactured Home Estates
That LGNSW write to the Honourable Minister Scully and request:

  • a review of the Local Government (Manufactured Home Estates, Caravan Parks, Camping Grounds and Moveable Dwellings) Regulation 2021 to remove the loopholes that allow permanent manufactured homes in areas where they are otherwise prohibited
  • a review of the Local Government (Manufactured Home Estates, Caravan Parks, Camping Grounds and Moveable Dwellings) Regulation 2021 and work with industry and councils to develop small village controls where land tenure exists and national construction standards can be enforced while meeting contemporary manufactured home estate living
  • a review of the SEPP Housing 2021 provisions for caravan parks with a view to properly distinguish a caravan park from a manufactured housing estate.

Background information
Tweed like most Councils has problems with the Local Government (Manufactured Home Estate, Caravan Parks, Camping Grounds and Moveable Dwellings) Regulation 2021 (the ‘Regulation’). It is no longer fit for purpose.
Tweed and the Northern Rivers is currently experiencing a problem with either existing traditional caravan parks or new caravan parks being developed into unapproved housing estates under the Regulation.
People are using exemptions under the Regulation to live in caravans and other moveable dwellings on private properties with few or no options to assess bushfire, flood, public health air pollution from airports, or pollution risks.
Manufactured home estates that are akin to residential subdivisions are being developed under the Regulation, which was not created for that purpose.
Manufactured home estates have changed significantly since the 1995 Regulation. In 1995 they were actual manufactured homes (built in factories, transported to sites), which were affordable. Advanced, modern and efficient construction methods and techniques have enabled the manufactured home to resemble a standard dwelling house. The development industry is now using the Regulation to deliver manufactured homes that are in effect houses, at costs similar to house and land packages on freehold land. The development industry pressures Councils to support the variation to the Regulation 'build on-site’ via the Section 82 Local Government Act 1993 objection/concurrence process. Further evidence that these structures are houses. The State Government provides no direction or opinion regarding such proposals.
A manufactured home is defined under the Local Government Act as:
“A manufactured home means a self-contained dwelling (that is, a dwelling that includes at least one kitchen, bathroom, bedroom and living area and that also includes toilet and laundry facilities), being a dwelling -
  1. that comprises one or more major sections, and
  2. that is not a motor vehicle, trailer or other registrable vehicle within the meaning of the Road Transport Act 2013, and includes any associated structures that form part of the building.”
The only differentiation between a manufactured home and the in situ standard construction of a dwelling is part a) of the definition that requires the manufactured home to comprise at least one major section. To give practical meaning to this, it means that the dwelling has to have a major part of it constructed/assembled prior to it being placed on its final site.
Another issue is that the manufactured home estates are being constructed outside of the standard construction certification process under the EPAA that is in place for standard subdivision development for housing and infrastructure. There is a certification void for internal infrastructure provision.
Council currently has:
  • GemLife (a manufactured home estate with 110 site) under construction
  • Up and coming DAP meetings include a proposal for a MHE at 117-147 Tweed Coast Road, Cudgen (approximately 33 ha).
The development industry pressures Councils to support other variations from the Regulation via the Section 82 objection/concurrence process. These include lesser/no setbacks, and greater site coverage. The State Government provides no direction or opinion regarding such variations.

Motion 4 - Correct Use of Recycling Bins
That, as a matter of urgency, the state government implements an education program aimed at building public awareness on the importance of the correct use of recycling bins in public places.

Background information
Australia has one of the highest waste generation per capita rates in the world.  If waste is not disposed of and recycled properly, it can end up in landfill, causing detrimental damage to the environment.  There is a lack of general knowledge of the proper use of recycling bins in public places, especially at events.  While many public parks have implemented recycling bins, the lack of understanding of the importance of this system is apparent.  This results in many recyclables ending up in landfill, and contamination of recycled products by general waste.  A public campaign will promote, educate, and build awareness of the importance of recycling and assist in reducing national waste generation.

Motion 5 - NSW Local Government Grants Agency
That LGNSW write to the NSW Premier and the NSW Minister for Local Government requesting the establishment of a NSW Local Government Grants Agency to coordinate all the state and federal grants programs through one central agency. This would provide a single point of contact for councils and establish consistent grant application, reporting  and acquittal arrangements.

Background information
In the 2022/23 financial year Tweed Shire Council interacted, reported and acquitted $65,479,143 in grant funds across 43 different agencies (Federal, State, quasi Govt, NGO, Private) covering 230 grant programs. The costs to Councils in coordinating such efforts diminishes the resources available to undertake the grant program of works.
The central agency could provide;
  1. Funding for feasibility studies to get projects “shovel ready” (concept design, development approval, detailed design etc) for grant requirements
  2. A consistent online grants portal for;
    1. Grant guidelines / criteria
    2. Deed 
    3. Applications,
    4. Amendments 
    5. Reporting
    6. Acquittals
  3. Better remittance reporting to Councils.

Motion 6 - Safe Cat, Safe Wildlife
That LGNSW write to the Minister and Shadow Ministers for Local Government, Environment and Animal Welfare and our local Member of Parliament requesting the following reforms to better manage the highly negative impact of roaming domestic cats on wildlife and improve the health and welfare of companion animals:

  • Amend the Companion Animals Act 1998 and associated Companion Animals Regulation 2018 to enable local governments to enforce the containment of pet cats in NSW. The introduction of these containment laws to include phase-in periods and community support and monitoring frameworks.   
  • Develop, and allocate funding towards, a state-wide program to support local governments to enforce compliance with the Companion Animals Act 1998. This funding to include increasing the number of rangers available to undertake such compliance.  
  • Streamline pet identification and registration processes into one process managed by Service NSW and accessible through self service functions within the Service NSW app.   
  • Transition to mandatory desexing laws that align with existing state approaches in Western Australia, Tasmania, Australian Capital Territory, South Australia and Victoria. 
  • Establish a $10 million, three-year state-wide grant program to support councils to implement domestic cat containment policies and associated responsible cat ownership programs. The program to include: identification and registration measures, large scale desexing and microchipping programs and effective education programs to support people to keep their cats contained.  
  • Implement a state-wide 'Safe cat, safe wildlife' campaign that includes the development of a central, state-wide online platform, in consultation with councils, relevant agencies and animal welfare bodies to make responsible pet ownership information easily accessible. 

Background Information
The NSW Companion Animals Act 1998 does not currently include requirements for cats to be secured at home and prevented from roaming. NSW and WA are the only States in Australia that do not have such legislation 
Cat containment requires cat owners to keep their pet within the bounds of their property, as is currently the case for dogs, livestock and other pets. Cats that are kept safely at home live up to 10 years longer. According to the RSPCA NSW, two in three cat owners have lost a cat to a roaming-related incident and one in three to a car accident. 
Pet cats allowed to freely roam outside kill an estimated 323 million native Australian animals and an additional 223 non-native animals annually. Feral animal predation, along with weed invasion, are the second major causes (after habitat removal) of biodiversity loss in NSW (NSW State of the Environment report 2021). 
In our shire, with its special responsibility to protect our environment it is urgent that this situation is remedied by a change in our state legislation. Our wildlife, our cats, and our precious local environment will be the beneficiaries.


Motion 7 - Street trees as essential community infrastructure in New South Wales
That LGNSW advocates that the NSW Government :
  • Reintroduces street trees as eligible community asset through the Section 7.11 Contributions Plan.
  • Investigate and implement a suitable mechanism and governance structure that would enable councils to introduce a fee for compensatory  tree planning.
Background Information
Point 1:
Street trees were removed from Tweed Shire Council’s Section 7.11 Contributions Plan (formerly s94 Contributions Plan No. 6) at the direction of the NSW Minister for Planning on 10 July 2009. Contributions for library book stock and surf lifesaving facilities were removed in the same manner at this time. These items were identified to not be appropriate pieces of infrastructure for which contributions should be required. A Ministerial Direction under s94E was issued specifying that council must no longer require monetary section 94 contributions for this purpose.
As recognised through an increasing number of urban tree canopy programs throughout Australia, including the Tweed Shire Cool Towns program, trees provide significant benefits to the environment, local climate, economy, and to social and public health outcomes. Trees are widely recognised as an integral and essential component of urban infrastructure. Urban trees are a key asset that contribute directly to improving the liveability of urban areas in a changing climate.
Section 7.11 of the NSW Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 provides for a consent authority to require the dedication of land, the payment of a monetary contribution (or both) where a development proposal is likely to require the provision of or increase demand for public amenities and services within the area.
It is recommended that councils have the option to consider the use of contributions plans for street trees due to the essential services they provide to the public. While it is reasonable to require developers to install street trees as consent conditions, our Council’s experience in larger subdivision development is that the trees installed in conjunction with civil works are often damaged or removed by subsequent lot development such as houses. By collecting a contribution from the subdivision developer instead, these funds can be used later by Council once houses are established to achieve a consistent, high-quality streetscape, at a cheaper overall cost due to economies of scale and reduced tree loss.
The earlier Tweed Shire Councils Contributions Plan No. 6 - Street Trees in Residential Areas required a contribution of $297 per lot towards the planting and maintenance of two street trees per allotment, together with developer contributions towards the embellishment of public reserves (including the planting of trees), walkways and other public areas within a new subdivision.
The first element of this motion thus seeks support from the NSW Department of Planning and Environment under which councils can reintroduce street trees as a community asset through a Section 7.11 Contributions Plan.
Point 2:
As a consent authority, council assesses applications for the removal of trees. This can be in association with a development application or a permit for tree removal. When a tree removal approval is issued, council seeks to achieve at least a no net loss outcome and requires compensatory planting as a condition of the development or permit approval.
As compensatory plantings aim to achieve a ‘like for like’ species outcome, some sites are unsuitable for compensatory planting. This is most often when the site is not suitable for a large tree to be planted due to the presence and position of dwellings or other infrastructure.
Council currently has limited options to achieve the compensatory outcomes when the development site is unsuitable. It is possible to use a voluntary planning agreement, but this is a costly and complicated approach to simple situations involving replacement plantings for a small number of trees.
Larger development proposals may trigger the Biodiversity Offset Scheme and have the option of meeting biodiversity credit obligations for any residual impact through making a payment to the Biodiversity Offset Fund. The proposed compensatory planting fee would not apply to developments that trigger the biodiversity offset scheme.
Council can impose fees and charges under the Local Government Act 1993 (LG Act). The revenue raised from fees and charges is used to provide specific services or facilities for which they are charged on a user pays basis. Subject to further investigation of the suitability of this mechanism, including in relation to the provisions of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 (EP&A Act), council could identify a compensatory planting fee per tree.
The revenue from this charge could be used to fund street tree plantings through the Tweed Shire Cool Towns program as it may provide a suitable implementation and governance framework. This program provides the opportunity to include large trees of a range of species and so more likely to achieve like for like outcomes. It would hopefully also provide an appropriate mechanism to provide transparency and accountability for both the financial management and on-ground outcomes.

Motion 8 - The Minister for Local Government and the NSW Electoral Commission to address the exponentially rising costs of holding Local Government elections
That LGNSW advocate to the Minister for Local Government and the NSW Electoral Commission to address the exponentially rising costs of holding Local Government elections, requesting a review be undertaken:
  1. of the time allocated for prepolling, noting that during the recent State Government elections, prepoll occurred for only 6 days.
  2. of the number of polling booths and the removal of polling booths that are within 5km of each other in order to reduce election costs.
  3. That the General Manager prepares background information for this motion.

The Motion was Carried

Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
 
RESOLVED that:

1. The following tabled Petitions be received.

Petition 1:
Petition containing 35 signatories of which 20 are valid (with 11 being invalid due to signatories are from out of the shire and 4 being invalid due to incomplete details) was received on 15 June 2023 entitled "Halt Koala Deaths by Vehicle Strike, on Clothiers Creek Road".

"Reason - The iconic Australian koala it now at a tipping point it has been listed as "Endangered" the situation is grim. The opportunity to assist them to survive in the wild is slipping away very quickly unless there is more sincere and science appreciated action taken. The latest Koala SEPP21 ( State Environmental Planning Policy) haphazardly tabled by the State government and by some ministers who no longer are in government is a watered down version doomed to fail because it does not follow the science and does not include 
control/protection for all habitat in particular on Private Native Forests. Logging in these areas will hasten the koalas extinction in the wild. Removing koala habitat means no koala, quite simple. 

Team Koala always stands up to protect the koalas. Closer to home, once again we highlight the danger of Clothiers Creek Rd. Since the creation of the Ml, Clothiers Creek Rd has become a busy connection road between Murwillumbah and the Tweed Coast. This road is notorious for road deaths of humans and koalas. We are focused on the 3km stretch from Cabarita, start of Koala zone marked by the electronic sign, travelling west to the end of the Koala Zone also marked by the electronic sign; this is well before the highway. This 3kms uniquely cuts through the very centre of core koala habitat much to the horror of all koala lovers. The traffic speed at present is 70km/h yet the speed day or night on this stretch of road averages 70- 90km/h by both cars and trucks. We do not want any more preventable koala or human deaths on this road. 


Request - Team Koala are proposing a reduction of the speed limit from 70km to 50 kms for this 3km stretch of Clothiers Creek Rd, through the use of traffic calming devices such as those used in Coronation Ave Pottsville before the New Ambulance Station. There are several sections that could provide the width of road for such devices. We urge the Tweed Shire Council along with the Road and Transport department to address these issues before it really is too late. These are the wishes of Team Koala Inc and the signatories below ...."


Petition 2: 
Petition containing 50 signatories of which 28 are valid (with 15 being invalid due to signatories are from out of the shire and 7 being invalid due to incomplete details) was received on 15 June 2023 entitled "Halt Koala Deaths on Clothiers Creek Road".

"The iconic Australian koala is now at tipping point it has been listed as 'Endangered' the situation is urgent.

Help Team Koala save koalas here and now!

The latest Koala SEPP21 (State Environmental Planning Policy) tabled by the State Government will fail to protect koalas because it does not follow the science and allows clearing and logging in koala habitat areas in privately held native forests.

When habitat is cleared for roads and housing estates, cars and dogs become a serious threat to Koalas.

Over 4000 Koalas are killed in Australia each year by cars and dogs.

https://www.savethekoala.com/about-koalas/interesting-facts/

This petition concerns the 3 km marked koala zone on Clothiers Creek Road from Cabarita going west, right through the heart of koala habitat. This section is well clear of the highway.

This petition requests:
That the Tweed Shire Council  along with the NSW Road and Transport department reduce the speed limit through this koala habitat from 70 kph to 50 kph, and enforce the limit through the use of traffic calming devices such as signs and chicanes similar to those used in Coronation Ave Pottsville, on the approach to the Ambulance Station.
There are several  areas in the danger section of Clothiers Creek Road wide enough for such devices. 

These measures to protect koalas are supported by Team Koala Inc and the signatories below."


2. ATTACHMENTS 1 and 2 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law


The Motion was Carried

Council approves the General Manager negotiating with each interest holder of the Property, to endeavour to reach agreement to Council's acquisition of the Property; being an acquisition of land for road purposes on the Property's downslope from Tyalgum Road, and an acquisition of an easement for support on the Property's upslope from Tyalgum Road.

  3. If agreement is reached, Council will acquire the Property, provided that such agreement will be subject to a further resolution of Council.
    1. If no such agreement is reached within a reasonable period of time: 
    2. the acquisition of the Property be carried out by compulsory process in accordance with Part 1 of Chapter 8 of the Local Government Act 1993 and the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991;
    3. Council seek approval from the Minister for Local Government in accordance with section 187 of the Local Government Act 1993 to give all necessary Proposed Acquisition Notices (PAN) in accordance with the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991;
    4. Council take each further steps as is necessary to obtain approval from the Minister, the Governor or any public authority as may be necessary, and take all actions as may be necessary, to give notices and otherwise carry out the acquisitions by means of compulsory acquisition; 
    5. following receipt of the Minister's approval, Council serves each PAN and takes each other action necessary to carry out the acquisition.
    6. following receipt of the Governor's approval, Council give effect to the acquisition by publication of an Acquisition Notice in the NSW Government Gazette and such other publication as may be required by law;
    7. Council pay compensation to all interest holders entitled to compensation by virtue of the compulsory acquisition on the terms set out in the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991.

  4. Council authorises the General Manager to complete and execute all documentation necessary to finalise and bring into force Council’s acquisition of the Property and if necessary to fix the Council seal to the application to the Minister, the Governor, the Register General or any public authority for the compulsory acquisition.

  5. That upon acquisition, Council intends to dedicate the land acquired on the downslope of the Property as road reserve (noting that no dedication of land is required for the acquisition of an easement).

  6. ATTACHMENTS 1 to 5 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
     (e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law
