ALTERNATE MOTION
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr James Owen
 
RESOLVED that
 
  1. Council notes that the NSW government has introduced movement restrictions on high-risk materials after fire ants were found north of the Queensland and NSW border, at Tallebudgera. People who breach the control order may face court-imposed fines of up to $1.1 million or three-years imprisonment for individuals, or $2.2 million for corporations. The control order prevents high-risk materials such as mulch, woodchip, soil, compost, sand, gravel, baled hay, and turf being moved from within a five-kilometre radius of a site where fire ants were found unless inspected and issued with a certificate by the Queensland Agriculture Department.
  1. Council notes the establishment of a cross-border task force that has been undertaking training and education campaigns, and that could move to enforcement if necessary. They will be using automatic number plate recognition systems and different types of technology to make sure that they can monitor movements between Queensland and NSW. 
  1. The Mayor write to Senator Murray Watt, Minister for Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry acknowledging the current increased commitment of $60 million this year to assist NSW & QLD combat Fire Ants and request, given the impending and increasing threat to agriculture, tourism, livestock and native fauna, that the Commonwealth further assist both the NSW and QLD Governments with additional funding and Federal Departmental assistance to eradicate Fire Ants.
  1. The Mayor write to the Hon. Tara Moriarty MLC, Minister for Agriculture requesting an increase in funding to NSW Department of Primary Industries to fund:
    1. NSW DPI Officers to investigate creating check points in the border region for all tippers, trailers, etc bringing material across the border that could contain fire ants. These check points to include technology such as cameras and sniffer dogs to quickly check the material as well as ensuring the correct paperwork from source.
    2. Noting the announcement of 16 August 2023, for an education campaign in the border region, including road signage, TV, radio, newspapers, and social media to alert people to the threat of fire ants and what to do if suspected nests are found. This campaign should also target markets, landscape supplies, nurseries and primary producers.
  1. Should Fire Ants enter New South Wales, that Council will work closely with the NSW Department of Primary Industries to undertake early identification of any infestations, prevent infestations, and have a rapid response with the aim being eradication of Fire Ants from the Tweed Shire.

Cr Polglase left the meeting at 4.43pm.

The Motion was Carried

Cr James Owen
 
RESOLVED that Council writes to the Minister and Shadow Ministers for Local Government, Environment and Animal Welfare, and our local Member of Parliament requesting the NSW Government to make the following reforms to better manage the highly negative impact of roaming domestic cats on wildlife and improve the health and welfare of companion animals:

  1. Amends the Companion Animals Act 1998 and associated Companion Animals Regulation 2018 to enable local governments to enforce the containment of pet cats in NSW. The introduction of these containment laws to include phase-in periods and community support and monitoring frameworks. 

  2. Develops, and allocate funding towards, a state-wide program to support local governments to enforce compliance with the Companion Animals Act 1998. This funding to include increasing the number of rangers available to undertake such compliance.

  3. Streamlines pet identification and registration processes into one process managed by Service NSW and accessible through self service functions within the Service NSW app. 

  4. Transitions to mandatory desexing laws that align with existing state approaches in Western Australia, Tasmania, Australian Capital Territory, South Australia and Victoria.

  5. Establishes a $10 million, three-year state-wide grant program to support councils to implement domestic cat containment policies and associated responsible cat ownership programs. The program to include: identification and registration measures, large scale desexing and microchipping programs and effective education programs to support people to keep their cats contained.

  6. Implements a state-wide 'Safe Cat, Safe Wildlife' campaign that includes the development of a central, state-wide online platform, in consultation with councils, relevant agencies and animal welfare bodies to make responsible pet ownership information easily accessible.

The Motion was Carried

Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 20 July 2023 be received; and 

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1.    Tweed Valley Triathletes 2023-24
That the proposed Tweed Valley Triathletes Season commencing Saturday 16 September 2023 and concluding Saturday 16 March 2024 be supported, subject to the following conditions:
1.      Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.
2.      All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
3.    The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

6.3.    Stokers Road, Stokers Siding
That 45 degree angle parking be installed on Stokers Road, Stokers Siding (opposite Stokers Pottery).

7.1.    Kingscliff Triathlon 26 November 2023 and 24 March 2024
That the proposed Kingscliff Triathlons on Kingscliff Triathlon 26 November 2023 and 24 March 2024 be supported, subject to standard conditions of approval:
1.  NSW Police approval being obtained.
2.  Endorsement of the event by Triathlon NSW.
3.  Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
4.  Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
5.  The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts, road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints.
6.  Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
7.  All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
8.  Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
9.  Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
10.That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
11. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
12. The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
13. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
14. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
15. The application of all signs and devices necessary to effect the changed traffic management conditions and temporary road closures for the events, also being approved as part of the event approval. 

7.2.    Darlington Drive, Banora Point
That the request for a pedestrian crossing at Darlington Drive, Banora Point is not supported.

7.3.    Stanley Street, Tweed Heads
That the installation of unbroken yellow edge lines be installed on Stanley Street, Tweed Heads, adjacent to the existing double centre lines, extending 10 metres into Norman Street

7.4.    Turnock Street, Tweed Heads
1.  The installation of timed parking on Turnock Street, Tweed Heads to address potential illegal activities is not supported.
2.  The unapproved yellow markings adjacent to the driveway on Turnock Street be removed. 
3.  That No stopping signs be installed on Pearl Street, north of the driveway at no.39 Pearl Street, to prohibit parking south of the driveway and the pedestrian crossing point.

7.5.    Island Drive, Tweed Heads
That 6-hour parking signage be installed on Island Drive at the 2 on-road carparks between Harbour Drive and Keith Compton Drive, Tweed Heads.

7.6    Broadway, Burringbar
That 1hr parking be installed adjacent to 27 Broadway, Burringbar and council officers consult with adjacent businesses to determine whether or not extending the 1hr parking zone would be supported.

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Polglase

Cr Brinsmead declared a Non-Pecuniary/Non-Significant Interest in Item 23.1.1 LATE Expression of Interest - North Star Holiday Resort, 1-3 Tweed Coast Road, Hastings Point.  The nature of the interest is that Cr Brinsmead declared the vendor provided a political donation to the campaign of the ticket I was on for the 2021 local government election.  Cr Brinsmead will manage the Interest by vacating the Chamber for discussion and not voting on the item.
 
Cr Owen declared a Non-Pecuniary/Non-Significant Interest in Item 23.1.1 LATE Expression of Interest - North Star Holiday Resort, 1-3 Tweed Coast Road, Hastings Point.  The nature of the interest is that Cr Owen declared the vendor provided a political donation to the campaign of the ticket I was on for the 2021 local government election.  Cr Owen will manage the Interest by vacating the Chamber for discussion and not voting on the item.

ALTERNATE MOTION:

Cr Reece Byrnes
Cr Warren Polglase

PROPOSED that Council, in relation to No. 16 Hovea Drive, Pottsville:

1.  Notes legal advice concerning the Disability Discrimination Act 1992 (Cth);

2.  Requests the General Manager to instruct Council’s solicitors to write to the owners of this property advising that Council will not enforce the property covenant in relation to dog ownership, or commence action in the NSW Supreme Court subject to:

a.  the General Manager negotiating and entering into an Agreement within one (1) month of the resolution with the property owners, outlining reasonable measures to accommodate the property, as summarised below:

  • evidence of the dog having undertaken accredited assistance training
  • receipt by the General Manager of advice/report from a registered psychologist/psychiatrist that the assistance dog is the best solution for the person's disability
  • evidence of a smaller fenced off area within the property, up to 64m2
  • approval by the General Manager of a management plan for the dog (the dog only to be permitted outside to toilet, fenced area to be swept for fauna prior to the dog entering the area, dog to be taken through the garage into the car when leaving the property)
  • agreed public communications between the property owner and the General Manager in respect to the circumstances under which the accommodation has been made
  • the dog be removed if the person with the disability no longer lives at the property
  • should the dog become deceased or removed then this agreement is terminated and an undertaking is provided by the property owner not to replace the dog with one that is prohibited under the covenant
  • should the dog become deceased or removed from the property or the person with the disability no longer lives at the property, the smaller fenced off area also be removed.
b.  the agreed measures be put into effect within six (6) weeks of the Agreement execution.

3.  ATTACHMENTS 1-3 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain: (e) information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law (g) advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege.

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RECOMMENDED that Council:

  1. In respect of No. 16 Hovea Drive, Pottsville, instructs Council’s solicitors to write to the Australian Human Rights Commission advising that Council intends to commence legal action in the NSW Supreme Court as previously resolved, should the unauthorised dog be remaining on the premises, as matters raised in the conciliation conference were not able to provide resolution of this issue. 

  2. ATTACHMENTS 1-3 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain: (e) information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law (g) advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  Cr James Owen

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd

Gracious God, 
 
We approach a Spring and Summer full of uncertainty.  We witnessed the northern hemisphere summer and have seen the warnings for dangerous weather to come.  We are grateful for Council’s efforts to repair the damage caused by recent disasters, and for their work to mitigate risks in the future.
 
And yet the future remains so unknown to us.  We pray for everyone in our community who are still recovering from trauma and are dreading  another summer.  Please grant wisdom, safety, and grace to all people, both paid and volunteer, who protect our Shire.  Guide all who have the responsibility to plan for the future to keep us safe.
 
May all Councillors and Staff find a deep satisfaction in their work on our behalf, and may we all experience true community as we live and work together.
 
May your grace, mercy, and peace be each one’s experience throughout this meeting.  
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen.

RECOMMENDED that item 10.1.1 - LATE DA18/0478.02 for an amendment to Development Consent DA18/0478 for demolition of existing structures, tree removal, earthworks, construction of dwelling and two swimming pools at Lot 1 DP 1273277 No. 20 Lagoon Road, Fingal Head, being a Late item, be dealt with and it is ruled by the Chair to be of great urgency.

The Motion was Carried
VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.


Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RECOMMENDED that Council 

A.  Refuse DA18/0478.02 for an amendment to Development Consent DA18/0478 for demolition of existing structures, tree removal, earthworks, construction of dwelling and two swimming pools at Lot 1 DP 1273277 No. 20 Lagoon Road, Fingal Head for the following reasons:
 
1.  Pursuant to Section 4.55(1A)(a) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979, the application has not demonstrated that the proposed modification is of minimal environmental impact, and that the modification powers of S4.55(1A) which rely on the consent authority being satisfied that the proposed modification is of minimal environmental impact, can be engaged.

2.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979, the modification application should be refused because insufficient information has been submitted to enable a proper assessment of the impacts that the development as proposed to be modified will have on the biophysical, hydrological or ecological integrity of the adjacent littoral rainforest.

a.  Under State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021, the subject site is mapped as being the Proximity Area to both Coastal Wetlands and Littoral Rainforest.

b.  Four of the trees proposed for removal occur within a candidate Littoral Rainforest EEC that forms a contiguous connection to the adjacent mapped Littoral Rainforest Area.

c.  No details have been provided of any vegetation to be removed to provide the access formation, or the materials to be used for same.

3.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979, the modification application should be refused because insufficient information has been submitted to enable a proper assessment of the impacts that the development as proposed to be modified will have on the Coastal Environment Area, and that the proposal has been designed to avoid an adverse impact, or where such an impact cannot be avoided, that it has been minimised.

a.  No details have been provided of alternative strategies which seek to minimise impacts upon the ecological environment, coastal environmental values and natural coastal processes.

4.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979, the proposed tree removal and access formation within the Littoral Rainforest Conservation Area, and the additional tree removal, is contrary to the provision of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A1 – Dwellings, Dual Occupancies, Secondary dwelling and Alterations and Additions to retain indigenous vegetation and mature trees, 

C4.  Existing landscape elements on sites such as natural rock outcrops, watercourses, dune vegetation, indigenous vegetation and mature trees should be retained and integrated with the design of the buildings.

5.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979, the proposed tree removal and access formation within the Littoral Rainforest Conservation Area, which is the subject of a s88B covenant under the Conveyancing Act 1919, and the additional tree removal is contrary to the objective of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A16 – Preservation of trees or vegetation, ‘(t)o minimize, and avoid where possible, unnecessary clearing of native trees and vegetation’.

a.  The proposal involves removal of six (6) trees that qualify as prescribed vegetation under DCP A16 Part 1.3. 

b.  Four (4) of the six (6) trees form part of a candidate Littoral Rainforest EEC.

c.  No details have been provided of any vegetation to be removed to provide the access formation, or the materials to be used for same. 

6.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979, the application has not demonstrated that the tree removal as proposed is essential to achieve the required Asset Protection Zones for bushfire protection, and that there is no alternative strategy which would meet the requirements for bushfire protection while minimising biodiversity impacts. 

7.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979, the application has not demonstrated that the proposed fire services access way and access gate identified on the Landscape Plans as being within the Littoral Rainforest Conservation Area, which is the subject of a s88B covenant under the Conveyancing Act 1919, is required for firefighting purposes.

The application has not demonstrated that where such firefighting measures are required that there is no alternative strategy which would minimise biodiversity impacts on the Littoral Rainforest.

Further, no details have been provided of any vegetation to be removed to provide the access formation. 

8.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979, the application has not be accompanied by an adequate Assessment of Significance [Five Part Test under Section 7.3 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016] that provides a quantified assessment of the cumulative impact of the development as proposed to be modified, and as such an informed decision regarding Section 7.3 (1)(b) and (c) of the Biodiversity Conservation Act2016 cannot be made. 

9.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the applicant has not demonstrated to the satisfaction of the consent authority that the proposed tree removal and disturbance will not negatively impact the adjacent Littoral Rainforest on public land, and as such is not considered to be in the public interest; and

B.  In relation to the Class 1 Appeal for the deemed refusal of DA18/0478.02 for an amendment to Development Consent DA18/0478 for demolition of existing structures, tree removal, earthworks, construction of dwelling and two swimming pools at Lot 1 DP 1273277 No. 20 Lagoon Road, Fingal Head determines to defend the Class 1 Appeal and engage any necessary experts.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that:
  
 A.  Development Application DA23/0302 for a caravan park (112 long term sites), reception, manager's residence and pool at Lot 2 DP 815370 No. 1126 Pottsville Road, Pottsville be refused for the following reasons:
 
  1. The consent authority cannot be satisfied that the Development is not likely to significantly affect threatened species pursuant to section 7.2 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016 and that no Biodiversity Development Assessment Report was required to accompany the DA.
     
  2. The consent authority cannot be satisfied that the Development is consistent with the approved koala plan of management that applies to the Site, as required by section 4.8(2) of State Environmental Planning Policy (Biodiversity and Conservation) 2021.
     
  3. Due to the inadequacy of the application and the material submitted, the consent authority cannot be satisfied that the Development is not designated development pursuant to Section 2.7(2) of the State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021.
     
  4. The proposal does not provide adequate evidence that it will not significantly impact on the following attributes listed under clause 2.8(1) of State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021 in particular:
    1. the biophysical, hydrological or ecological integrity of the adjacent coastal wetland, or
    2. the quantity and quality of surface and ground water flows to and from the adjacent coastal wetland.
       
  5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application fails to adequately respond to Clause 25 of Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2000 Development in Zone 7 (a) Environmental Protection (Wetlands and Littoral Rainforests) and on adjacent land, including the provision of a Plan of Management. 
     
  6. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development is not consistent with the Aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed's natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways, visual amenity and scenic routes, built environment, and cultural heritage. 
     
  7. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development is not consistent with the Aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to conserve or enhance the biological diversity, scenic quality and geological and ecological integrity of Tweed. 
     
  8. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development is not consistent with the Aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to conserve or enhance areas of defined high ecological value. 
     
  9. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development is not consistent with the Aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to provide special protection and suitable habitat for the recovery of the Tweed coastal Koala. 
     
  10. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied that adequate consideration of Heritage Conservation relating to known and predictive places of Aboriginal significance have occurred in accordance with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan. 
     
  11. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development proposal has not demonstrated it meets land use the definition of a 'caravan park' and therefore is a permissible land use in the RU2 Rural Landscape Zone. 
     
  12. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, a significant portion of the development extends into the 7(a) Environmental Protection (Wetlands and Littoral Rainforests) Zone under the Tweed LEP 2000, where caravan parks are a prohibited land use. 
     
  13. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development proposal is not consistent with the objectives of Zone 7(a) Environmental Protection (Wetlands and Littoral Rainforests) under the Tweed LEP 2000,
    1. Primary objectives
  • to identify, protect and conserve significant wetlands and littoral rainforests.
  • to prohibit development which could destroy or damage a wetland or littoral rainforest ecosystem.
    1. Secondary objectives
  • to protect the scenic values of wetlands and littoral rainforests.
  • to allow other development that is compatible with the primary function of the zone. 
     
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development proposal is not consistent with RU2 Rural Landscape Zone objectives of Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014, specifically:
    • to maintain the rural landscape character of the land.
    • to provide for a range of tourist and visitor accommodation-based land uses, including agri-tourism, eco-tourism and any other like tourism that is linked to an environmental, agricultural or rural industry use of the land.
        
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) and Section 4.15 (1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 and Clause 7.10 of Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014, the development has not demonstrated that services essential for the development can be adequately achieved including:
    • the disposal and management of sewage.
    • stormwater drainage or on-site conservation
    • suitable vehicular access.
        
  1. Pursuant to Clause 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the Flood Impact Assessment (FIA) prepared by Engeny dated 1 June 2023, submitted by the applicant is deficient as it is required to consider all flood mechanisms such as creek flooding, storm surge, local events and the interaction with the wetland. 
    • Only a single flood event has been analysed (1% AEP). The FIA is required to analyse a broader range of flood events to conclude the filled site will not cause flood impacts external to the site. 
    • The 24hr or 36hr events are likely to be the critical flood events, the applicant has not confirmed the developed model has also used the 24hr and 36hr events. 
    • The creek has been removed from the truncated model. This may be invalid unless an alternative boundary condition has been included. The wetland is inextricably linked with the creek. The applicant did not advise why the creek has been removed from the model or confirm the alternative boundary conditions. 
    • The development filling has been considered in isolation (not part of a cumulative filling development scenario as required by the Tweed Coastal Creeks Floodplain Risk Management Study 2015). 
       
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development proposal has not demonstrated due compliance with or consideration of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A19 – Biodiversity and Habitat Management. 
     
  2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the Development application has not demonstrated that the Development has been designed to minimise and mitigate impacts on the environmental values of the Site. The Application has also not demonstrated that there will not be a significant or unacceptable impact on ecological values of the Site.
     
  3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the applicant has not suitably demonstrated the site is suitable for the development in relation to potential land contamination as required by State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021 through provision of a preliminary site investigation prepared in accordance with NSW EPA guidelines by a suitably qualified contaminated land consultant. 
     
  4. Pursuant to Section 4.15 (1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, on the basis of the information submitted, the development proposal, is not considered to be in the public interest.
     
B. That Council, in relation to the Class 1 Appeal of Development Application DA23/0302 for a caravan park (112 long term sites), reception, manager's residence and pool at Lot 2 DP 815370 No. 1126 Pottsville Road, Pottsville determines to defend the Class 1 Appeal, engage any necessary experts and provide delegation under Section 377(1) of the Local Government Act 1993 to Council’s Officers to undertake negotiations as necessary, including at section 34 conciliation conferences, and to resolve any issues in the proceedings or enter into section 34 agreements to resolve the proceedings as necessary based on evidence. 

C.  ATTACHMENT 6 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:
(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd, Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church.


Gracious God, 
 
With National Police Remembrance Day coming next week we are grateful for those who serve in the Tweed-Byron Police District.  Comfort them as they remember colleagues who lost their lives in the line of duty.  Guard their hearts as they respond to traumatic events.  We are thankful for the work of Superintendent Roptell in command of a large and diverse District, and for all who work to make our community safe.
 
For the many important issues before Council today, we pray for wisdom and grace.  We are grateful for the privilege of meaningful work, for our colleagues, and for the sense of purpose in sharing common goals.  Bless their work as they give their time to care for, manage, and improve our region.  May our community be strengthened as a result of today’s meeting.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen.

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that:

  1. Council excludes the Trutes Terrace properties from this stage of the scheme.

  2. Council progresses the Parkes Lane Area Stage 3 Sewerage Scheme as a voluntary scheme, with a 50% Council contribution towards the estimated scheme cost being available to properties that connect within 5 years of completion of the scheme, with the Parkes Lane Area Stage 3 Sewer Levy contribution being $17,818 (2023-24) to be increased by CPI each year and with payment options being:

        (i) Property owners pay the full levy amount upfront to receive a 20% discount, or
        (ii) Property owners pay the levy in equal annual amounts for a 10 year period.

  3. Property owners within the Parkes Lane Area Stage 3 Sewerage Scheme who make application to connect to sewer more than 5 years after the completion of the scheme will be required to pay the estimated full cost of connection being $35,636 (2023-24) to be increased by CPI each year.

  4. For a period of 5 years after the completion of the Parkes Lane Area Stage 3 Sewerage Scheme, sewerage access charges will not be levied for properties that have not connected to sewer and after the expiration of this period, Council will levy sewerage access charges in accordance with Council’s fees and charges for all properties within the Parkes Lane Area Stage 3 Sewerage Scheme.

  5. Council further develops the detail design and documentation, costs estimate and call for tenders for the Parkes Lane Area Stage 3 Sewerage Scheme.

  6. In the implementation of the scheme consideration be given to prioritising connection of those properties which have On Site Sewage Systems that are most at risk of failure and impacting the environment.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that:

1. The following tabled Petitions be received.

Petition containing 55 signatories of which 55 are valid was received on 24 August 2023 entitled "Petition to improve pedestrian access within Frangela Drive Reserve Leash Free Dog Exercising Area".

"We the undersigned residents/ratepayers, request that the Council install a hand rail (or something similar) along the steep  slope on the western side of the Reserve so that pedestrians can move with greater safety between the upper and lower  sections of this popular public  space. There are no footpaths in Frangela Drive itself."

2.  Accepts the petition and requests a report in relation to the petition and its implications on Council’s adopted Integrated Planning Reporting Framework documents.

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Receives the Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 10 August 2023; and

  2. Adopts the Executive Leadership Team's recommendations as follows:
    7.1. Navigation Lane, Tweed Heads
    1. That the yellow no stopping line be extended on the east side of Navigation Lane, Tweed Heads, to opposite the ingress of the Ultima building underground car park. 
    2. That a yellow no stopping line be installed on Navigation Lane, Tweed Heads, on both sides of the curve around the Twin Towns Services Club garbage pick up area.

    7.2. Megan Street, Tweed Heads South
    That double centre lines be installed through the curve on Megan Street, Tweed Heads South.

    7.3. Kingscliff Lane, Kingscliff
    The installation of no parking signs on the west side of Kingscliff Lane, Kingscliff (between Ocean Street and Terrace Street) is not supported as observations indicate there is not a significant issue. Officers should continue to monitor the area and bring this back to the Committee if required.

    7.4. Bay Street, Tweed Heads
    That the proposed closure of Bay Street (from Wharf Street to east of Enid Street) Tweed Heads, for the Street Christmas Party on either Saturday 9 or 16 December from 10am - 9pm be supported subject to:
    1. NSW Police approval being obtained.
    2. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 4 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
    3. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
    4. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts. 
    5. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
    6. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
    7. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
    8. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
    9. That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed. The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources. If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website 
    for approval.
    10. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
    11. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
    12. The application of all signs and devices necessary to effect the changed traffic management conditions and temporary road closures for the events, also being approved as part of the event approval.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that Council resolves the Notice of Motion by Councillor Firth on 22 June 2023 entitled ageism, be amended to add part 3 below which was missed due to an administrative processing error: 

  1. Requests the General Manager to include consideration of ageism as a part of Seniors Week activity. Items might include seminars for the general public on addressing ageism, ageist language and on learning from indigenous elder regard. 

  2. That a new category of award be established for the 2023 Australia Day Awards called 'Senior Ambassador Award’, with the following criterion:
    1. The nominee must be at least 65 years (Note, this age is consistent with the Commonwealth award);
    2. The nominee has made a significant contribution in the Tweed Shire community, through voluntary or other contributions;
    3. The nominee must display strong communication skills and leadership to become the Tweed Shire Senior Ambassador for the 12 months following receipt of the award and be willing to take on voluntary promotion of awareness of seniors' positive contribution to the Tweed Shire community.

  3. Participates in Ageism Awareness Day in October.

The Motion was Carried

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins:

"Dear Father,

I ask You to be present today as Council meets together. 

We know this is not always an easy task, but may You watch & direct over all that needs to be discussed.

Father, I ask for Your help, support & strength for all those here, that the outcomes will be as You want them to be.

I pray that You may grant what is best for the Tweed Shire Council – that the shire will be blessed – people may be kept safe & provided for and that Your plans be fulfilled.

We thank You for Your many blessings. Your goodness is new every day, with opportunities that allow us to fulfill what You have called us to do. 

Father, I pray for all our councillors. 

May they put aside their distractions of the day & focus their minds & hearts upon the work that is before them.

Bless our Mayor Chris Cherry: as it is You who appointed her to this position. 

Father, I pray that You will enlighten her mind with all wisdom, that she may lead & watch over the Tweed Shire Council with virtue & uprightness.

Father I give thanks & may Your blessing be upon Council, for every good and perfect gift is from You.

 So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 

That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.     

May You answer us in the day we call.
 
Amen"

RECOMMENDED that:
 
A.      Development Application DA21/0757 for an eco-tourist facility comprising five cabins and ancillary infrastructure at Lot 333 DP 1001758 No. 84 Sleepy Hollow Road, Sleepy Hollow be refused for the following reasons:
 
1.       The consent authority cannot be satisfied that the Development is not likely to significantly affect threatened entities pursuant to section 7.2 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016 and that a Biodiversity Development Assessment Report was required to accompany the Development Application.
 
2.       Pursuant to Section 2.3 of TLEP 2014 the development is properly characterised as tourist and visitor accommodation which is a prohibited use in RU2 Rural Landscape zone. 
 
3.       Pursuant to Section 5.13(3) of TLEP 2014 consent cannot be granted to the development for the purpose of an eco-tourist facility as the application has not satisfied the following clauses: 
 
i.       The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that there is connection between the development and the ecological, environmental, and cultural values of the site or area as required by clause 5.13(3)(a).  
 
ii.      The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that development will be located, constructed, managed, and maintained so as to minimise any impact on, and to conserve, the natural environment as required by clause 5.13(3)(b).  
 
iii.     The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that development will enhance an appreciation of the environmental and cultural values of the site or area as required by clause 5.13(3)(c).  
 
iv.      The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that development will promote positive environmental outcomes and any impact on watercourses, soil quality, heritage and native flora and fauna will be minimal as required by clause 5.13(3)(d).  
 
v.       The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that development will be maintained (or regenerated where necessary) to ensure the continued protection of natural resources and enhancement of the natural environment as required by clause 5.13(3)(e).  
 
vi.     The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that power to the site will be provided through the use of renewable energy sources and as required by clause 5.13(3)(i). 
 
vii.    The application has not satisfactorily addressed or provided an appropriate management strategy for minimising any impact on the natural environment as required by clause 5.13(3)(k) including:  
 
(i)      The provision of appropriate measures to remove any threat of serious or irreversible environmental damage in accordance with clause 5.13(3)(k)(i); 
 
(ii)     Details regarding the maintenance (or regeneration where necessary) of habitats in accordance with clause 5.13(3)(k)(ii); 
 
(iii)    The provision of appropriate mechanisms for monitoring and reviewing the effect of the development on the natural environment in accordance with clause 5.13(3)(k)(iv); 
 
(iv)    Details regarding maintaining improvements on an on-going basis in accordance with relevant ISO 14000 standards relating to management and quality control in accordance with clause 5.13(3)(k)(v). 
 
4.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A3 – Development of Flood Liable Land.  
 
5.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A19 – Biodiversity and Habitat Management.
 
B.      ATTACHMENT 4 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contain:
(e)          information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.

 The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Nola Firth
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil



AMENDMENT 1

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

PROPOSED that:

A.  Development Application DA22/0304 for the demolition of existing dwelling, earthworks, tree removal and erection of multi dwelling housing at Lot 16 Section 8 DP 758571 No. 103 Kingscliff Street, Kingscliff be refused for the following reasons:
 
1.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal does not comply with Clause 1.2 Aims of the Tweed LEP 2014 as the development does not:
 
i.  give effect to the desired outcomes, strategic principles, policies and actions contained in the Council’s adopted strategic planning documents, including, but not limited to, consistency with local indigenous cultural values, and the national and international significance of the Tweed Caldera as required by subclause (a), in that it is not consistent with Tweed DCP Section A1 Part B – Town Houses & Row Houses 
 
ii.  promote development that is consistent with the principles of ecologically sustainable development and to implement appropriate action on climate change as required by subclause (d) in that sufficient deep soil zones have not been included to combat urban heat.
 
2.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal does not comply with Clause 2.3 Objectives and Land Use Tables of the R3 Zone of the Tweed LEP 2014 as the development does not:
 
i.  provide for the needs of the community within a medium density residential environment as it does not provide a mix of accommodation types.
 
3.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A1 – Residential and Tourist development Code (Part B Townhouses and Row Houses) Chapter 1, in that the townhouses are not provided on a lot minimum size 1000m2 as required in Control c.
 
4.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A1 – Residential and Tourist development Code (Part B Townhouses and Row Houses) Chapter 1, in that the townhouses do not all have a clearly identifiable entry from the street as required in Control f.
 
5.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A1 – Residential and Tourist development Code (Part B Townhouses and Row Houses) Chapter 1, in that the townhouse development does not provide a mix of dwelling sizes and a diversity in number of bedrooms as required in Control i.
 
6.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A1 – Residential and Tourist development Code (Part B Townhouses and Row Houses) Chapter 1 Rear Deep Soil Zone, in that the townhouse development does not provide a minimum depth of 5.5m as required in Control c.
 
7.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A1 – Residential and Tourist development Code (Part B Townhouses and Row Houses) Chapter 1 Impermeable Site Area, in that the townhouse development does not provide for the collection of rainwater in tanks as required in Control c.
 
8.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A1 – Residential and Tourist development Code (Part B Townhouses and Row Houses) Chapter 1 Topography Cut and Fill, in that the townhouse development exceeds the maximum allowable cut and fill of 1m as specified in Control f.
 
9.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A1 – Residential and Tourist development Code (Part B Townhouses and Row Houses) Chapter 1 Topography Cut and Fill, in that the townhouse development contains fill to the boundary contrary to Control h and m.
 
10.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A1 – Residential and Tourist development Code (Part B Townhouses and Row Houses) Chapter 1 Setbacks, in that the townhouse development does not provide a front setback consistent with the average setback of neighbouring dwellings as required in Control c.
 
11.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A1 – Residential and Tourist development Code (Part B Townhouses and Row Houses) Chapter 1 Sunlight Access, in that the townhouse development does not provide a minimum side setback of 4m as required in Control b.
 
12.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the proposal does not comply with the provisions of Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 Section A1 – Residential and Tourist development Code (Part B Townhouses and Row Houses) Chapter 1 External Building Elements, in that the townhouse development exceeds the maximum fence height as required in Control d and i.
 
13.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) the proposal is not considered suitable for the site given the view loss of the iconic Mt Warning (Wollumbin) as a result of the development for nearby properties.
 
14.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(d) the proposal has failed to adequately address the amenity issues raised in public submissions.
 
15.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) the proposal is not considered to be in the public interest as it does not comply with the adopted Policy position of Council’s Tweed DCP specifically Section A1 (Part B Townhouses and Row Houses).

B.  ATTACHMENT 5 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

VOTE AGAINST - Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

RECOMMENDED that:

A.  Development Application DA22/0431 for a café and signage at Lot 1 DP 395360 & Lot 1 DP 780240 Nos. 2-4 Commercial Road, Murwillumbah be refused for the following reasons:

1.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application which seeks approval to stack 2 shipping containers on the buried foundation of the Murwillumbah CBD Levee wall, to erect a deck overhanging the Murwillumbah CBD Levee wall, to support the deck with posts impacting a publicly used pedestrian footpath on the river-side of the Murwillumbah CBD Levee wall where insufficient information has been provided to confirm the posts will not impact a nearby Eucalyptus tree, impact river-bank stability or resist flood flow and debris impact, is contrary to the aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in:

(a)  Clause 1.2(2)(a): to give effect to the desired outcomes, strategic principles, policies and actions contained in the Council’s adopted strategic planning documents, including, but not limited to, consistency with local indigenous cultural values, and the national and international significance of the Tweed Caldera;

(b)  Clause 1.2(2)(c): to promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed’s natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways, visual amenity and scenic routes, built environment, and cultural heritage; and

(c)  Clause 1.2(2)(g): to conserve or enhance the biological diversity, scenic quality and geological and ecological integrity of Tweed.

2.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority cannot be satisfied of the matters set out in Clause 5.21(2) of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 for the following reasons:

(a)  insufficient information has been provided to confirm the location of the café will not adversely impact the Murwillumbah CBD Levee wall’s buried foundation;

(b)  insufficient information has been provided to confirm the deck posts will not impact river-bank stability (including with respect to any loss of integrity due to impact on a Eucalyptus Grandis tree), not impact or be impacted by erosion, will resist flood flow, will resist debris impact and will provide adequate structural support; and

(c)  the proposal restricts access to the Murwillumbah CBD Levee for maintenance, future upgrades and flood emergency operations.

3.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority cannot be satisfied of the matters set out in Clause 7.2(3) of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014. The application has not demonstrated that the proposed earthworks will not have a detrimental impact on the environmental functions and processes of the Tweed River riverbank and 2 x Eucalyptus grandis (Flooded Gum) trees, including the riverbank’s stability and the likely potential future use or redevelopment of the Murwillumbah CBD Levee for future flood works.

4.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate the proposal is not likely to cause an adverse impact on the matters set out in the the following clauses of State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience & Hazards) 2021:

(a)  Clause 2.10(1)(a) – the integrity and resilience of the biophysical, hydrological and ecological environment;

(b)  Clause 2.10(1)(b) – coastal environmental values and natural coastal processes; 

(c)  Clause 2.10(1)(d) – native vegetation; and

(d)  Clause 2.13 – native vegetation on the riverbank in an area designated high priority for riparian vegetation restoration in the Tweed River Estuary: Coastal Management Program 2022-2032.

5.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate the proposal complies with the following sections of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008.

(a)  Section A2 Site Access and Parking Code – the application has not demonstrated that the proposed parking layout is acceptable due to the required waiver of 2 x staff car parks which is not supported.

(b)  Section A3 Development of Flood Liable Land – the application has not demonstrated that the proposed location does not adversely impact the Murwillumbah CBD Levee and is adequately structurally supported within land mapped as a high flow area and high hazard flood storage area.

6.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority cannot be satisfied the likely impacts of the development, including environmental impacts on both the natural and built environments, and social and economic impacts in the locality are acceptable. The application has not demonstrated the proposal does not give rise to unacceptable risk to the Murwillumbah CBD Levee, the Tweed River and the public visiting the café or result in unacceptable impacts to vegetation and car parking.

7.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application has not provided adequate information to satisfy Council the site is suitable for the proposed development. For the reasons set out in the preceding reasons, the application has not provided adequate information to satisfy Council the site is suitable for the development.

8.Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, for the reasons set out in the preceding reasons and for the reason that insufficient information has been provided to justify the omission of acceptable disabled access, the application is not in the public interest.


B.   ATTACHMENT 3 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

PROPOSED that Council endorse the following 1-10 Development Application thresholds for reporting applications to Council:
 
1.  For all Development Applications that reach the following thresholds a report to Council will be prepared:

a)  Any Development Application with an estimated cost of development that exceeds $10M; and/or
b)  Any Development Application for subdivision of more than 50 lots; and/or
c)  Any Development Application where a 4.6 variation or a SEPP 1 variation seeks a variation of greater than 10% (as per DPE Ministerial Directions).
2.  For all modifications that seek to vary a condition originally deliberately imposed by Councillors (i.e. in addition to the staff recommendation) a report to Council will be prepared.

3.  For all Development Applications with a estimated cost of development between $2.5 Million and $10 Million, the Director Planning and Regulation will send a standard format email to all Councillors at the end of the officers’ assessment of these applications, containing the following:

a)  a summary of the main elements and description of the proposal;
b)  identification of any significant variations to Council’s Development Control Plan (DCP) controls (noting that any variations to Local Environmental Plan development standards greater than 10% are required to be reported to Council);
c)  the number and key issues of any public submissions received; and
d)  an indication of whether the officers are recommending approval/refusal.
4.  Councillors will be provided with 5 business days to provide written advice to the Director Planning and Regulation as to whether they wish to call up these applications for Council determination.

5.  In accordance with the current Code of Meeting Practice (s3.42), any request for call up of a development application, must be made by at least two Councillors and must be in writing. 

6.  Councillors can ask for clarification of any technical requirements for these applications, but it is not intended for Councillors to be engaging with the officers on any debate on the merits of the application, or negotiating any conditions of consent to influence a decision not to call up an application for Council determination.

7.  The Councillors shall provide their reasons for the call up, so that these can be relayed to the proponents or any other interested parties.

8.  If no request is received, the officers will proceed to determine the DA under delegated authority.

9.  The same Code of Meeting Practice call up provision is still available to any development application lodged with Council. and

10.  When a Development Application or Modification Application is determined under Delegated Authority, internal Assessment Reports underpinning such determinations will be made available to Councillors on individual request.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins. 


"Dear Loving and Gracious God:

May we be thankful; for You are indeed the giver of every good and perfect gift. Your goodness & mercy never fails us. 

Father, we come together this day to seek your wisdom, guidance, courage and strength. Be with us in our discussions and help us to be wise in the decisions we make for the people of the Tweed and the good of all those who have placed their trust and confidence in our leadership. Give us insight to lead with integrity that our decisions may reflect what is right and good. 

During our time together, help us from not being distracted by the current events that are happening in the world right now, but give us understanding & determination to plan for the days ahead. 

Father, grant us the humility to always seek Your will in all that we do and speak. May we be mindful of each other, being respectful & honouring one another in our thoughts, words & deeds… Not only in our place of work… but also to everyone You bring into our lives.

So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 

That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.     

May You answer us in the day we call.

Amen."

RESOLVED that Council:

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Adopts the alternate methodology of determining Water Access Charges and Sewerage Access Charges for non-residential properties which is based solely on the flows through the water meter, with Sewerage Access Charges further adjusted by the Sewerage Discharge Factor applicable to each non-residential property. 

  2. Drafts the 2024-25 Revenue Policy based on the methodology in 1.

  3. Stage the implementation of the alternate methodology of determining Water Access Charges and Sewerage Access Charges for non-residential properties over 4 years.

  4. Provides advice of the proposed change to all those provided with water supply and sewerage services by Council by inclusion of a general notice in all water bills.

  5. Informs the impacted non-residential water users of the proposed change.

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Receives the report into dredging as a flood mitigation option, 

  2. Supports ongoing dredging operations by the State Government in the Lower Tweed River to maintain safe navigation,

  3. Continues to perform ad hoc dredging activities as part of its responsibilities to maintain access to and operation of waterway, flood mitigation, and stormwater infrastructure, such as boat ramps, floodgates and drainage outlets, subject to environmental approvals and licences and available budget, and

RESOLVED that: 
  1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 14 September 2023 be received, and 

  2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

7.1.    Heffron Street, Tweed Heads South

  1. The relocation of the recently installed marked pedestrian crossing on Heffron Street, Tweed Heads South is not supported as its location was determined through the school's development assessment process.
  2. The reinstatement of 'on street parking' on Heffron Street adjacent to 5 Seymour Street, Tweed Heads South is not supported, as maximising sight distance and reducing vehicle movements is best practice on approaches to marked crossings, particularly around schools.

7.2.    Cowrie Lane, Casuarina

The request to install prohibitive parking at 6 Black Wattle Circuit, Casuarina (opposite of the garage at Cowrie Lane) is not supported, as the future development of the opposite site would include a driveway in that location.  However, should the applicant wish to fund the installation of no stopping signage this would be supported in the interim.  

7.3.    Twin Towns Triathlon Season 2023-24

There are no objections to Twin Towns Triathlon Club conducting events throughout the season on local roads within Banora Point subject to:

  1. Compliance with the NSW Road Rules for all activities.
  2. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
  3. Marshalls are not to direct traffic in any way.
  4. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
  5. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
  6. Police approval and control is to be sought for the conduct of the 24 March 2024 event.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr James Owen

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that in respect to RFO2023183 Expression of Interest for Conducting Community Markets:

1. Council delegates to the General Manager or his delegate to issue Section 68 approvals to operate a market for 3 years as follows:

a. Lions Club of Kingscliff Inc, Kingscliff (at Jack Bayliss Park), in accordance with the presented management plan.
b. Kraken Events, Kingscliff (Salt Central Park), subject to submission of additional information referred to within the market management plan and increase in Public Liability Insurance to $20million.
c. Curl Creative Events & Marketing (Knox Park), in accordance with the presented management plan and increase in Public Liability Insurance to $20million.
d. Pottsville Beach Neighbourhood Centre Inc, Pottsville (Philip Street), in accordance with the presented management plan.
e. Tweed Heads Community Men Shed Inc. Tweed Heads (Recreation Ground), subject to submission of a modified market management plan.
 
2. Council authorises the General Manager or their delegate to reissue an Expression of Interest for Conducting Community Markets at Kingscliff (Lions Park); and
 
3. Council authorises the General Manager or their delegate to:
a. Extend the current Section 68 approval to operate a market for Tweed Heads Jack Evans Boat Harbour until 30 June 2024 to allow a review of the fee structure to better accommodate markets with a small number of stallholders.
b. To reissue an Expression of Interest for Conducting Community Markets at Tweed Heads Jack Evans Boat Harbour; and
 
4. Council apply fees and charges as per current fees and charges $400 per event for small markets (less than 65 stalls) and $660 for large markets (more than 65 stalls); and
 
5. Council notes that the award of Salt Central Park tender is contrary to the Market Policy; and
 
6. ATTACHMENTS 1 and 2 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local
Government Act 1993, because it contains:
(c) information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business
(d) commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
(i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
(ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or
(iii) reveal a trade secret

ALTERNATE MOTION 

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

  1. A petition has been received which was conducted through the Change.org platform.  This platform does not provide sufficient information to meet the criteria of a petition under Council’s Code of Meeting Practice. While the petition comprises 553 signatories of those:
     
  • 29 signatories meet the criteria of a petition having provided, name, address and email address 
  • 344 signatories do not have a Tweed Shire Postcode 
  • The remaining signatories do not meet the petition criteria.
On the basis that 29 signatories meet the petition criteria, this petition is valid under the terms of Council’s Code of Meeting Practice. 

ACTION THAT WE WANT THE TWEED SHIRE COUNCIL TO TAKE:

  1. Stop all future works for construction of a 10 M stink pipe out the front of McAllisters Road and Buenavista Avenue. We want Tweed Shire Council, their engineering team and designers to go back to the drawing board to investigate and find alternative locations that is not out the front of someone's home and other homes where residents are affected by a stink pipe and major eyesore. 
  2. Bilambil Heights is a rural area with many open spaces and land available. Find another location.
  3. Since the upgrade is for future development, we want the council to consider putting the pipe in the new development areas if that is what the upgrade is intended for. 
  4. We insist that Tweed Shire Council reevaluate its approach to community engagement, starting with open and proactive communication with affected residents. A project of this nature, especially when it may encroach on the immediate surroundings of homes, should be conducted with the utmost consideration for the local community.
  5. We want a map available showing the locations of the 225 stink pipes in the Tweed Shire that you claim are out. 
  6. We want to know out of the 225 10m high sewage pipes, what number of these are out the front of privately owned homes (rate payers) and were the residents notified at all of the pipe that was to be constructed.
  7. We want to know how many of the 225 10 m high pipes are in parks and reserves in the Tweed Shire. 

 2. That Council receives the Petition and as it is an operational matter, refers it to the General Manager.

3.  ATTACHMENT 1 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:
(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

The Motion was Carried

PROPOSED that Council approves the tree permit removal application for the removal of 20 trees for construction of an industrial arts building at Lot 20 DP873920, No. 9-11 Hall Drive, Murwillumbah subject to the following conditions:

Vegetation Management

  1. Permitted vegetation management works are limited to the removal of the twenty (20) trees identified as ‘trees to remove’ in Table 2 of the Arboricultural Impact Assessment Report, Northern Tree Care, 27 September 2023 subject to approval of Complying Development, unless otherwise approved by Council.

  2. Permitted works must not commence until the following is provided to Council and written acceptance of the same issued by Council:

    1. Complying development certificate from certifier.
    2. Notice of appointment of principal certifying authority.
    3. Notice of commencement of works for the development.


  3. All vegetative material must be felled so as not to have any impact on neighbouring infrastructure or retained vegetation.

  4. Vegetation management works must be undertaken by an experienced local arborist who holds the Australian Qualification Framework (AQF) Level 3 in Arboriculture.

  5. All vegetative material removed must be either mulched and reused on-site, recovered for use as appropriate, or disposed of at an appropriate location e.g., authorised green waste facility.

  6. Retained vegetation must be protected during the construction phase in accordance with Section 9 (Tree Protection) of the Arboricultural Impact Assessment Report, Northern Tree Care, 27 September 2023.

  7. Retained vegetation must be protected and managed during the operational phase of the development in accordance with Section 8 (Recommendations) of the Arboricultural Impact Assessment Report, Northern Tree Care, 27 September 2023.

Compensatory Planting

  1. To compensate for the removal of 20 trees, compensatory planting, maintenance, monitoring and reporting as detailed in the Vegetation Management and Landscape Operational Works Plan, Outside Landscape Consultancy Issue A-E, as provided by ELKN Planning and Project Management 29 September 2023 is required.

  2. Compensatory planting is required to be completed within 3 months of the permitted vegetation works.

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

PROPOSED that Council refuses the tree permit removal application for the removal of 20 trees for construction of an industrial arts building at Lot 20 DP873920, No. 9-11 Hall Drive, Murwillumbah.
 
Pursuant to Clause 3.4 of the DCP Section A16 vegetation removal considerations, these twenty trees have characteristics that warrant refusal for their removal. They are locally indigenous, have significant ecological value and provide significant wildlife habitat, all being above 5 metres in height and some having considerable age and DBH over 700mm. These trees also provide significant amenity, aesthetic and scenic value.

The Mayor foreshadowed an amendment (Amendment 2) should Amendment 1 be carried and become the Motion.

AMENDMENT 2

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Warren Polglase

RESOLVED that Council defers the tree permit removal application to allow the proponent to produce evidence that:

a. this is the only site available that is flood free on the school land to construct the industrial arts building; and
b. the building kit purchased could not be modified to reduce the requirement for tree removal.

Cr Byrnes temporarily left the meeting at 05:00pm.
Cr Byrnes returned to the meeting at 05:01pm

The Amendment 1 was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

The Amendment 2 was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd:


"Gracious God, 
 
As Diwali commences we celebrate the beauty of cultural diversity and are thankful for the many ways people from South Asian communities strengthen and enrich our Shire.  We are grateful for days of joy and light, family and community, in times that often feel clouded by darkness.  
 
Our world often feels so uncertain, and with water restrictions commencing we face yet another difficult summer.  Give us wisdom to conserve our water well, and to steward it for those who follow us.  Thank you for Council’s leadership in this.  And yet we feel so vulnerable; we can’t produce this most essential resource.  So we ask you to send the rain we need as yet another expression of your goodness to us.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
 
PROPOSED that:

  1. Development Application DA22/0457 for farm stay accommodation (1 cabin) at Lot 10 DP 711758 No. 363 Cobaki Road, Cobaki be refused for the following reasons:

    1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is not inconsistent with the aim of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 1.2(2)(b) to encourage a sustainable local economy and small business, employment, agriculture, affordable housing, recreational, arts, social, cultural, tourism and sustainable industry opportunities appropriate to Tweed. The application which seeks approval for farm stay accommodation on agricultural land that does not meet the requirements to be defined as farm stay accommodation and is therefore prohibited tourist and visitor accommodation in a rural zone is not considered an appropriate tourist opportunity for the agricultural land.

    2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is for a permissible purpose of development in the RU2 Rural Landscape zone under the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014. The consent authority is not satisfied the proposed farm stay accommodation is on a commercial farm and ancillary to a commercial farm as required by the definition of farm stay accommodation.

    3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is not inconsistent with the objectives of the RU2 Rural Landscape zone pursuant to Clause 2.3(2) of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014. The consent authority is not satisfied the proposed tourist and visitor accommodation is suitably linked to an agricultural use of the land.

    4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, for the reasons set out in the preceding reasons, the application is not in the public interest.

  2. ATTACHMENTS 3 to 6 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:

(d)     commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: 
          (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
          (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or 
          (iii) reveal a trade secret


AMENDMENT 1

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr Reece Byrnes

RECOMMENDED that Development Application DA22/0457 for farm stay accommodation (1 cabin) at Lot 10 DP 711758 No. 363 Cobaki Road, Cobaki be deferred for five months to allow the applicant to provide evidence that he is a primary producer under the Income Tax Assessment Act and that the use is ancillary to the primary production business and that a report be brought back to Council for determination.

The Amendment 1 was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

VOTE FOR - Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
