[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RECOMMENDED that Council in response to the NSW Upper House Planning and Environment Portfolio Committee No. 7 - Planning & Environment Inquiry Into the Planning System and the impacts of climate change on the environments and communities:

  1. Edit Appendix 2 of the Draft Submission to include submission recommendations by the elected Tweed Shire Council which is detailed below; and
  2. Send the Draft Submission of this report titled "DRAFT Submission to the NSW Parliamentary Inquiry Committee No. 7 on Planning and Environment" with any submission recommendations from the elected Tweed Shire Council shown in Appendix 2 of the Draft Submission.

 Appendix 2: Recommendations:

  1. Prioritisation of green infrastructure to guard against urban heat is included in the body of this report. Specific and important measures would include mechanisms to allow offset payments and increased replacement tree fees and ratios by developers as well as substantially increased fees for illegal tree removal. Of relevance is the recent South Australian Urban Forest Report interim recommendation. The report has been established due to significant net loss of canopy e.g. 75,000 trees per year in Adelaide. Causes of such loss include infill housing development without urban greening being factored in. The interim report has 13 recommendations including the fee for illegal tree removal to be increased tenfold and offset planting to be strengthened to a ratio of 3:1 and with increased offset payment required. See:  https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5c57a2c2bfba3e5e4929ccf3/t/652f7247732256160550d9f7/1697608266562/ERDC+Urban+Forest+Report+No+1+signed.pdf
 
  1. Prioritisation of protection from the changes to the natural environment are also mentioned in the report. In particular this will entail urgent resourcing and requirement of conservation zones in all shires and that they be based on independent scientific assessments. 
 
  1. Climate change impacts are currently tracking at the high impact scenario according to the latest IPCC 2022 report. We can ignore this, or we can work with our communities to make some difficult choices now, to mitigate against the future impacts. Cost benefit analysis has consistently shown that investment in mitigation measures now with regards to coastal erosion and sea level rise will far outweigh the cost of not funding these adaptation measures. The planning system needs to consider no longer allowing people to build in the flood plain or have new residential uses of land in the coastal hazard zone. It is time for governments to pivot and make the change that councils cannot do at an individual level. Alternatively, government could consider allowing only tourist uses of areas at medium term risk such as coastal hazard zones, thereby allowing current owners of such land to retain an economic return and public to have use of this land in the period leading up to it being abandoned due to climate impacts in the future.
 
  1. In answering the inquiry question as to the adequacy of powers to revoke DA’s by Council, it is believed that in all of the years, this legislation s4.57 or its predecessor s96A of the EP&A Act 1979 have been in force, it has not been enacted by a Council as far as we are aware. This is because the legislation requires (under s4.57(7)) compensation to be paid by the regulatory authority that revokes the consent. This is cost prohibitive for local Councils and effectively means that there is no legal mechanism to revoke consents even in the face of known climate or environmental risks. There is currently $4BN federally dedicated to disaster mitigation. This needs to be used to take action now to remove people from hazardous risk areas. The government needs to make available a central fund, dedicated to compensation for approval revocations, to avoid disaster recovery funding being needed into the future.   Without this, or an alternative useable legislation, Councils will be forced to continue allowing legacy approvals to be acted on even in the face of known risk.
 
  1. No consideration of the adequacy of planning powers in the face of rapidly changing social, economic or environmental circumstances would be complete without the consideration of the introduction of zonings which are dependent on the subject development moving to construction within a defined period or an ability to rate a property according to its development potential if it has an approval in place. Both of these measures may create a way out of the current deadlock which sees land zoned for residential development in accordance with strategic growth plans and then no mechanism to force this land to be brought to market, creating an ability to landbank and disrupt the strategic planning for the provision of adequate housing.
The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd of the Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church.


'Gracious God, 

Thank you for the many joys of living in our Shire: for recent rain, for the amazing diversity of our flora and fauna.  We’re grateful for the many initiatives to value and protect native species in our region.  We pray for the ongoing work of Council to preserve these vital natural assets for this and future generations.
 
With White Ribbon Day tomorrow, we are aware that too many women in our community are vulnerable, in physical danger, or at risk for their lives. We pray for Police, refuges, the Purple Book, and other organisations who work to protect people from violence, including domestic and family violence. We pray for the protection of all who seek to escape that violence.  And we pray for the initiatives needed to change our culture to make it safe for all. 
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen.'

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
 
PROPOSED that Council:

  1. Notes that there is a severe shortage of affordable housing and rental accommodation in our shire which is contributing to highly stressful situations including homelessness and lack of worker accommodation.

  2. Begins the process towards enabling local control by council over short term housing by writing to the NSW Minister for Planning and Public Spaces, the Hon. Paul Scully MP requesting our shire to be considered for such control.

  3. When the NSW Government undertakes the review of short term rental accommodation Council actively participates in any review by responding to questions or writing submissions as required by the review.

AMENDMENT 1

Cr James Owen
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Notes that there is a severe shortage of affordable housing and rental accommodation in our shire which is contributing to highly stressful situations including homelessness and lack of worker accommodation.

  2. Begins the process towards enabling local control by council over short term housing by writing to the NSW Minister for Planning and Public Spaces, the Hon. Paul Scully MP requesting our shire to be considered for such control.

  3. Council notes that the State Government has indicated that it will undertake a review onto short term holiday letting and that it is anticipated the review will be announced prior to the end of 2023. When the NSW Government undertakes the review Council is to actively participate in any review by responding to questions or writing submissions as required by the review.

  4. Requests Council staff uses best endeavours to bring back a Report using publicly available data on short term holiday letting statistics and trends for the Tweed Shire.

  5. Once the review is announced and the terms of reference are known, that council begins the process for community consultation through Your Say Tweed to understand community views on short term holiday letting in Tweed Shire. 

Cr Warren Polglase temporarily left the meeting 4.37pm.
Cr Warren Polglase returned to the meeting at 4.40pm.

In accordance with 9.15 of the Code of Meeting Practice the amendment became the motion without debate or a vote as it was accepted by the Mover and the Seconder of the original motion.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

RESOLVED that:

 1. The following tabled Petition be received.

  • Petition containing 37 signatures, with 37 valid signatories was received on 31 October 2023 entitled "Fire Hazard Scenic Drive" advising as follows:

The roadside management and control of the overgrown trees and vegetation has been neglected along Scenic Drive for a very long time and is evident by the size of the Camphor Laurel trees that have grown. We would appreciate mitigating action by Council to remove all these large trees and overgrown vegetation to reduce the impact a fire in our area would have.

Given the proximity of the massive trees on council land to houses on the lower side of Karingal Avenue (some just metres away from existing structures), we would request Council to control and remove the overgrown vegetation that runs below our properties to Scenic Drive. Ironically, some of the largest trees on council land are Camphor Laurels that contain a volatile oil and are commune growing, and recognised as a weed in the Noxious Weed Act. We would appreciate it if all these trees were removed along with the other overgrown vegetation.
   
 2. Referred to the General Manager for consideration as the petition relates to an operational matter.

Cr James Owen
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Writes to the CEO of Surf Life Saving NSW, Mr Steven Pearce within 5 business days of this motion to determine Surf Life Saving NSW's support or otherwise for the installation of rescue tubes at the following locations based upon the Royal Life Saving Australia National Drowning Report and that he be requested to list the locations in priority order:

    1. Dreamtime Beach (attached to Emergency Beacon)
    2. North Kingscliff (attached to Emergency Beacon)
    3. Hastings Point River Mouth
    4. Pottsville River Mouth
    5. Kingscliff Surf Life Saving Club - in front of metal stairs near Kingscliff Bowls club
    6. Salt- attached to Salt Tower
    7. Fingal - at the Surf Life Saving Club
    8. Cabarita Beach - main access to the beach. 

  2. Upon affirmative receipt of written priority from Surf Life Saving Australia, that the Mayor writes to NSW Minister for Sport, Hon. Steve Kamper MP and the Member for Tweed, Geoff Provest MP within 5 business days of receipt of the letter, with a request for assistance in funding rescue tubes at the priority locations identified by Surf Life Saving NSW.

  3. Request the General Manager to monitor and if appropriate seek grant opportunities to fund rescue tubes at Surf Life Saving NSW priority locations within the Tweed Local Government Area is supported by Surf Life Saving NSW or alternatively fund through a quarterly budget review if savings are able to be achieved.

  4. Upon affirmative receipt of written priority from Surf Life Saving Australia, if all above funding avenues are exhausted and funds have not been sourced by June 2024, that council allocates funds in the 2025 budget to purchase and install the rescue tubes so that they can be operational by Sept 2024 - for the commencement of the 2024 surf lifesaving season.

Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Receives The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 12 October 2023.

  2. Adopts the Executive Leadership Team's recommendations as follows:

6.1 Wollumbin Street, Murwillumbah
That the installation of raised platforms (wombat crossing) should be pursued for the marked pedestrian crossings on Brisbane Street and Wollumbin Street, Murwillumbah.

6.2 Tweed Valley Way, Murwillumbah
On-street parking on Tweed Valley Way west between Prospero Street and Alma Street, Murwillumbah, be designated: 
2P 9am - 5pm Mon - Fri 
2P 9am - 12 noon Sat

7.1. Stuart Street, Tweed Heads
That the existing bus zone on Stuart Street, Tweed Heads, adjacent to the Twin Towns carpark, be converted to '15 minute parking 8am to 9:30am, 2:20pm to 4pm Monday to Friday, School days' and comment be sought from Twin Towns Services Club on whether a Bus Zone is required outside the times listed above.

7.2. Sutherland Street, Kingscliff
The installation of a marked pedestrian crossing on Sutherland Street, Kingscliff (between the Cudgen Creek Bridge and Viking Street) is not supported as the existing pedestrian refuge is considered the most suitable device.

7.3. Water Street, Tweed Heads
'No Parking 11pm – 5am' signage be installed along the length of the northern side of Water Street, Tweed Heads.

7.4. Limosa Road and Tringa Streets, Tweed Heads West
The installation of 4.5t weight limit on Limosa Road and Tringa Street, Tweed Heads West is not supported.

7.5. Phillip Street / Waugh Street, Chinderah
The installation of prohibitive ‘No Right Turn” signage be installed on Waugh Street, Chinderah to prevent vehicles entering Phillip Street for a period of 3 months. Traffic will be monitored and evaluated with feedback from the association included at the end of the trial and reported back to the committee.

7.6 LATE ITEM: Mahers Lane, Terranora
The relocation of the children’s crossing on Mahers Lane, Terranora and the installation of the associated linemarking and signage is supported subject to compliance with TfNSW guidelines and AS1742. It should be noted that the S/slash (no standing) signage is not supported in NSW and these should be replaced with the yellow unbroken kerb (C3) lines.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Warren Polglase
 
PROPOSED that Council approves the tree permit removal application for the removal of 20 trees for construction of an industrial arts building at Lot 20 DP873920, No. 9-11 Hall Drive, Murwillumbah subject to the following conditions:

Vegetation Management

  1. Permitted vegetation management works are limited to the removal of the twenty (20) trees identified as ‘trees to remove’ in Table 2 of the Arboricultural Impact Assessment Report, Northern Tree Care, 27 September 2023 subject to approval of Complying Development, unless otherwise approved by Council.

  2. Permitted works must not commence until the following is provided to Council and written acceptance of the same issued by Council:

    1. Complying development certificate from certifier.
    2. Notice of appointment of principal certifying authority.
    3. Notice of commencement of works for the development.


  3. All vegetative material must be felled so as not to have any impact on neighbouring infrastructure or retained vegetation.

  4. Vegetation management works must be undertaken by an experienced local arborist who holds the Australian Qualification Framework (AQF) Level 3 in Arboriculture.

  5. All vegetative material removed must be either mulched and reused on-site, recovered for use as appropriate, or disposed of at an appropriate location e.g., authorised green waste facility.

  6. Retained vegetation must be protected during the construction phase in accordance with Section 9 (Tree Protection) of the Arboricultural Impact Assessment Report, Northern Tree Care, 27 September 2023.

  7. Retained vegetation must be protected and managed during the operational phase of the development in accordance with Section 8 (Recommendations) of the Arboricultural Impact Assessment Report, Northern Tree Care, 27 September 2023.

Compensatory Planting

  1. To compensate for the removal of 20 trees, compensatory planting, maintenance, monitoring and reporting as detailed in the Vegetation Management and Landscape Operational Works Plan, Outside Landscape Consultancy Issue A-E, as provided by ELKN Planning and Project Management 29 September 2023 is required.

  2. Compensatory planting is required to be completed within 3 months of the permitted vegetation works. 

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

PROPOSED that Council refuses the tree permit removal application for the removal of 20 trees for construction of an industrial arts building at Lot 20 DP873920, No. 9-11 Hall Drive, Murwillumbah.

Pursuant to Clause 3.4 of the DCP Section A16 vegetation removal considerations, these twenty trees have characteristics that warrant refusal for their removal. They are locally indigenous, have significant ecological value and provide significant wildlife habitat, all being above 5 metres in height and some having considerable age and DBH over 700mm. These trees also provide significant amenity, aesthetic and scenic value.

The Amendment 1 was Lost

VOTE FOR - Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

AMENDMENT 2

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council approves the tree permit removal application for the removal of 20 trees for construction of an industrial arts building at Lot 20 DP873920, No. 9-11 Hall Drive, Murwillumbah subject to the following conditions:

Vegetation Management

  1. Permitted vegetation management works are limited to the removal of the twenty (20) trees identified as ‘trees to remove’ in Table 2 of the Arboricultural Impact Assessment Report, Northern Tree Care, 27 September 2023 subject to approval of Complying Development, unless otherwise approved by Council.

  2. Permitted works must not commence until the following is provided to Council and written acceptance of the same issued by Council:

    1. Complying development certificate from certifier.
    2. Notice of appointment of principal certifying authority.
    3. Notice of commencement of works for the development.


  3. All vegetative material must be felled so as not to have any impact on neighbouring infrastructure or retained vegetation.

  4. Vegetation management works must be undertaken by an experienced local arborist who holds the Australian Qualification Framework (AQF) Level 3 in Arboriculture.

  5. All vegetative material removed must be either mulched and reused on-site, recovered for use as appropriate, or disposed of at an appropriate location e.g., authorised green waste facility.

  6. Retained vegetation must be protected during the construction phase in accordance with Section 9 (Tree Protection) of the Arboricultural Impact Assessment Report, Northern Tree Care, 27 September 2023.

  7. Retained vegetation must be protected and managed during the operational phase of the development in accordance with Section 8 (Recommendations) of the Arboricultural Impact Assessment Report, Northern Tree Care, 27 September 2023.

Compensatory Planting

To compensate for the removal of the 20 trees, an amended Vegetation Management Plan detailing compensatory planting, maintenance, monitoring and reporting is to be submitted and approved by the General Manager or his delegate before vegetation works commence. The amended plan is to have a 3:1 local native tree replacement ratio, (i.e. 60 trees), using trees in 45 litre pots, and where possible, these trees are to be of the same species as those removed. Understory planting of 200 local indigenous species is to contain increased diversity, including at least 6 varieties of both grasses and shrubs.

Cr Owen left the meeting at 5.44pm

The Amendment 2 was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

The Amendment 2 on becoming the Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Nola Firth

Cr James Owen
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that:

  1. The amended application for the Review of Determination of the refusal of Development Application DA22/0022 for multi-dwelling housing comprising of 15 x 4 bedroom townhouses, demolition of existing structures, earthworks and tree removal (review of determination) at Lot 2 DP 516446 No. 1 Lalina Avenue, Tweed Heads West; Lot 1 DP 856963 No. 11 Lalina Avenue, Tweed Heads West be refused for the following reasons.

    1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate that the proposal is capable of meeting Essential Energy requirements pursuant to Clause 2.48 of SEPP (Transport and Infrastructure) 2021.

    2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate that the proposal is compliant with the provisions of Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014. The application has not demonstrated compliance with the following clauses:

      1. Clause 2.3 with regard to the development’s performance against zone objectives for R2-Low Density.

      2. Clause 7.2 with regard to the extent of cut and fill, the provision of retaining walls and the potential impact of the earthworks.

    3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the application fails to satisfy several aspects of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 (DCP). The application has not demonstrated compliance with the following Sections with the DCP:

      1. Section A1 - Preliminary Information - Chapter 4 Site Context and Analysis.

      2. Section A1 - Part B (Townhouses and Row Houses). The application proposes unacceptable variations to the following controls:

        1. Chapter 1: Building Types in terms of dwelling mix and building layout;
        2. Design Control 2: Site Configuration with regard to deep soil zones, external living areas, communal open space, cut and fill and retaining walls, and landscaping;
        3. Design Control 3: Side and rear setbacks;
        4. Design Control 5: Building orientation and separation;
        5. Design Control 7: Building amenity with respect to sunlight access, visual privacy and acoustic privacy.

      3. Section A15 - Waste Minimisation and Management. The application has not demonstrated adequate measures for operational waste storage.

    4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) the application is likely to have adverse impacts to the surrounding built environment and residents.

    5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate the site is suitable for the proposal with respect to surrounding land uses and the existing built form, proposed earthworks, construction noise, and vibration and noise impacts.

    6. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(d) the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate the issues raised in the submissions have been resolved.

    7. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) the application not considered to be in the public interest with regard to non-compliance with the LEP, Council’s DCP development controls, likely impacts and site suitability.

  2. ATTACHMENTS 3 and 4 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
 
RESOLVED that:

  1. The following tabled Petition(s) be received.

    Petition containing 167 signatures, with 150 valid signatories was received on 7 November 2023 entitled "Short Term Holiday Lets" advising as follows:

     

    The signatories of this petition call on Tweed Shire Council to support Councillor Nola Firth's November Notice of Motion on Short Term Letting that Council:

    • Notes that there is a severe shortage of affordable housing and rental accommodation in our shire including homelessness and lack of worker accommodation.   
    • Resolves to begin the process towards enabling local control by council over short term housing.
    • Writes to the Planning Minister requesting our shire be considered for such control.

    Tweed Shire has one of the highest levels of homelessness in NSW and a severe shortage of affordable housing and rental accommodation. Lack of secure housing causes severe human suffering and negative long term economic and social consequences. Currently many people in our shire are desperately in need of a home and unable to find one. We need to urgently do what we can within our role as a local government to address this situation.

     

    Within the shire there are over 900 non-hosted short term accommodation properties. These are free standing properties where the host does not reside on the property. These could potentially contribute to ameliorating this dire situation by becoming longer term rental homes rather than holiday accommodation.

     

    Our neighbouring shire of Byron has recently been granted a 60-day cap on such short term accommodation. It is timely that Tweed Shire Council is given control if short term holiday lets in the Shire.

  2.  ATTACHMENT 1 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Brenda Stuttle.


Dear Heavenly Father, 

Thank you for our beautiful area that we live in called the Tweed, we are so blessed by the richness and diversity this area has to offer, not only in landscape but in it’s people.  Thank you that you have called us to serve in this Community. Let us do it with integrity and enthusiasm, and as your word says not to grow weary doing good.

We pray for those in this time who are struggling. Those who are affected by the rental housing crisis and the homeless. Those who have been through the hardship of flood and the trauma associated by grief.  Give us wisdom and strategies to be a channel of blessing to those in need.

Let us not be overwhelmed by the task at hand, but to learn to give our cares over to you and trust you with the outcome, just one day at a time.

Thank you that every new day is a gift and never be ungrateful for each and every moment.

In Jesus name we pray Amen.

Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
PROPOSED that:
 
1.  Review of Determination of Development Application DA22/0088 for a telecommunications facility at Lot 2 DP 815370 No. 1126 Pottsville Road, Pottsville confirms the decision and be refused for the following reasons:
 
a.       The consent authority cannot be satisfied that the Development is not likely to significantly affect threatened species pursuant to section 7.2 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016 and that Biodiversity Development Assessment Report was not required to accompany the application.
 
b.      The consent authority cannot be satisfied that the Development is consistent with the approved koala plan of management that applies to the Site, as required by section 4.8(2) of State Environmental Planning Policy (Biodiversity and Conservation) 2021.
 
c.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application has not demonstrated that the Development has been designed to minimise and mitigate impacts on the environmental values of the Site. The application has not demonstrated that there will not be a significant or unacceptable impact on ecological values of the Site. 
 
d.      The proposal does not provide adequate evidence that it will not significantly impact on the following attributes listed under clause 2.8(1) of State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021, in particular: 
 
(a)     the biophysical, hydrological, or ecological integrity of the adjacent coastal wetland, or
 
(b)     the quantity and quality of surface and ground water flows to and from the adjacent coastal wetland.
 
e.      Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application fails to adequately respond to Clause 25 of Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2000 - Development in Zone 7 (a) Environmental Protection (Wetlands and Littoral Rainforests) and on adjacent land, including the provision of a Plan of Management. 
 
f.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development is not consistent with the Aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed’s natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways, visual amenity, and scenic routes, built environment, and cultural heritage. 
 
g.      Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development is not consistent with the Aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to conserve or enhance the biological diversity, scenic quality, and geological and ecological integrity of Tweed. 
 
h.      Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development is not consistent with the Aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to conserve or enhance areas of defined high ecological value.
 
i.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, The development is not consistent with the Aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to provide special protection and suitable habitat for the recovery of the Tweed coastal Koala.
 
j.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development proposal has not demonstrated due compliance and consideration of Section A19 – Biodiversity and Habitat Management of the Tweed development Control Plan 2008 and that adequate measures have been undertaken to avoid and minimise impact to ecologically sensitive habitats.
 
k.      Pursuant to Section 1.7 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, there is insufficient information to determine that the proposed development will not have a significant impact upon threatened species, or ecological community, or its habitat. The assessment of significance has not been prepared in accordance with the Threatened Species Test of Significance Guidelines.
 
l.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the likely impact of the proposed development, including environmental impacts on both the natural and built environments, are unacceptable.
 
m.     Pursuant to Sections 4.15(1)(d) and 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, having regard to the issues raised in the public submissions, and the adverse impacts of the proposed development, approval of the application is not considered to be in the interest of the public for the following reasons:
 
     i.        The application has not provided adequate information to satisfy Council that the development avoids and minimises significant impact upon threatened species, or ecological community, or its habitat.
 
     ii.       The application has not provided adequate information to satisfy Council that the proposed development is compatible with the flood function by virtue of the proposed platform level of 3.5m AHD. 
 
     iii.      The application has provided conflicting information between various reports/ documents/ plans with respect to the extent of the bushfire asset protection zone and the overall height of the development. 
 
     iv.      The application has not adequately demonstrated that there is no other alternate site that is more suitable for the proposed facility. 
 
 2.     ATTACHMENT 9 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:
 
        (e)          information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.

Cr Reece Byrnes
Cr James Owen

A.  Review of Determination of Development Application DA22/0088 for a telecommunications facility at Lot 2 DP 815370 No. 1126 Pottsville Road, Pottsville that Council has considered the following documents having regard to section 7.3(1)  and 7.3(2) of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016: 

  1. Tweed Shire Council Report 30 November 2023;
  2. DA22/0088 Site Plans
  3. DA22/0088 Development Plans
  4. DA22/0088 Statement of Environmental Effects
  5. DA22/0088 Acid Sulfate Soils Management Plan
  6. DA22/0088 Bushfire Protection Assessment
  7. DA22/0088 Flood Report
  8. DA22/0088 Sustainability and Environment Unit Comments
  9. DA22/0088 Resolution and Original Assessment Report to Council
  10. Confidential DA22/0088 Combined Submissions
In reviewing the above material and 7.3 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016 which states:
 
7.3   Test for determining whether proposed development or activity likely to significantly affect threatened species or ecological communities, or their habitats
(1)  The following is to be taken into account for the purposes of determining whether a proposed development or activity is likely to significantly affect threatened species or ecological communities, or their habitats—
 
(a)  in the case of a threatened species, whether the proposed development or activity is likely to have an adverse effect on the life cycle of the species such that a viable local population of the species is likely to be placed at risk of extinction,
(b)  in the case of an endangered ecological community or critically endangered ecological community, whether the proposed development or activity—
 
(i)  is likely to have an adverse effect on the extent of the ecological community such that its local occurrence is likely to be placed at risk of extinction, or
(ii)  is likely to substantially and adversely modify the composition of the ecological community such that its local occurrence is likely to be placed at risk of extinction,
(c)  in relation to the habitat of a threatened species or ecological community—
(i)  the extent to which habitat is likely to be removed or modified as a result of the proposed development or activity, and
(ii)  whether an area of habitat is likely to become fragmented or isolated from other areas of habitat as a result of the proposed development or activity, and
(iii)  the importance of the habitat to be removed, modified, fragmented or isolated to the long-term survival of the species or ecological community in the locality,
(d)  whether the proposed development or activity is likely to have an adverse effect on any declared area of outstanding biodiversity value (either directly or indirectly),
(e)  whether the proposed development or activity is or is part of a key threatening process or is likely to increase the impact of a key threatening process
(2)  The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette with the concurrence of the Minister for Planning, issue guidelines relating to the determination of whether a proposed development or activity is likely to significantly affect threatened species or ecological communities, or their habitats. Any such guidelines may include consideration of the implementation of strategies under the Biodiversity Conservation Program.

  4. The Height does not affect the setback provision;

  8. In relation to the habitat of a threatened species or ecological community the tower will not negatively impact habitat in a way that would affect the long term survival of the species or ecological community in the locality;
  9. The tower will not impact any declared area of outstanding biodiversity value (either directly or indirectly);
  10. The tower will not cause any key threatening process or increase the impact of a key threatening process;
  11. The reason the tower should be approved is because it will not significantly affect threatened species and will provide essential public infrastructure that is essential for public safety in emergencies and disasters; and

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that:

1.  Development Application DA23/0559 for use of unauthorised works consisting of two horse/cattle shelters, rural shed, entry gates, earthworks and internal driveway at Terranora Road, North Tumbulgum be refused for the following:

A.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the use of the structures is prohibited as the development application has not demonstrated permissibility with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 nor has the Development Application that the use of the structures would be a landuse which is permissible with consent under Clause 2.3, and as such the application cannot be approved

The development application is explicit that the proposed use of the structures are not for a commercial use, and that there is no commercial activity being undertaken on the site - which precludes the use of the structure for agriculture which is dependent on a commercial element.

B.       The application is made for the erection of a new structure. Given that the buildings have already been constructed, it is not lawful to give development consent for a building that has been built prior to development consent.

C.       The development application is substandard, and deficient in information: 

a)      The application type is specified as being for the erection of a new structure, though the structures have been constructed and approval for construction cannot be issued.  
b)      The driveway and entry gates are partial located in Council’s road reserve, and in accordance with Section 23(1) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2021, a development application requires the written consent of the owner of the land where the application is not made by the owner. No consent from Council was sought or obtained for these works. 
c)      The Information provided in the Development Application Form submitted via the NSW Planning Portal, the Statement of Environmental Effects and the Show Cause letter submitted with the Development Application is conflicting and lacking in detail. 
d)      The plans submitted with the application is limited to a site plan. There are no floor plans/elevations submitted as part of the Development application of the structures, and no details of the earthworks, driveway or entry gates.
 
D.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is consistent with the aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 1.2(2) subsections (a), (c), and (g):

(a)     to give effect to the desired outcomes, strategic principles, policies and actions contained in the Council’s adopted strategic planning documents, including, but not limited to, consistency with local indigenous cultural values, and the national and international significance of the Tweed Caldera,
(c)     to promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed’s natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways, visual amenity and scenic routes, built environment, and cultural heritage,
(g)     to conserve or enhance the biological diversity, scenic quality and geological and ecological integrity of Tweed.
 
The location of the shed is mapped as Predictive Aboriginal Cultural heritage, with the location of all the works mapped as being of high visual quality. The shed and concrete driveway are highly visible in the wider landscape and from scenic routes and do not represent responsible sustainable management of areas of visual amenity.
 
 
E.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is consistent with the provisions of Clause 7.2 of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 relating to earthworks, and in particular the likely disruption of, or any detrimental effect on, drainage patterns and soil stability in the locality of the development, and the likelihood of disturbing relics.

F.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is consistent with the provisions of Clause 7.10 of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as they relate to suitable vehicular access. There is no design for the driveway (dimensions, concrete strength or steel reinforcement used etc) and it is unknown in the driveway is compliant with Council’s standards, specifically S.D.011, or Planning for Bushfire Protection 2019.

G.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is consistent with the provisions of Clauses 2.10 and 2.11 of State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021 as they relate to designing and siting development to avoid an adverse impact on Aboriginal cultural heritage, the integrity and resilience of the biophysical, hydrological (surface and groundwater) and ecological environment, and the visual amenity and scenic qualities of the coast. It is considered that the bulk, scale and size of the large shed on an exposed ridgeline has an adverse visual impact on the surrounding coastal and built environment.

H.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development is contrary to the Objectives and Controls for Views and Vistas as set out in Part A - Preliminaries of Section A1 of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008:

O1.    To ensure existing public views and vistas particularly those of important natural features such as ridgelines, water or bushland, are retained in so far as it is practical to do so.
O2.    To ensure public view corridors, particularly those down streets and between buildings, are not unnecessarily reduced or obliterated.
O4.    To protect the iconic scenic landscapes of the Tweed.
O5.    To have regard to the “Tweed Scenic Landscape Evaluation”.
C1.    Building siting and height is, as far as it is practical, to be designed to minimise the impact on views from surrounding properties, and follow the Planning Principles of view sharing between properties.
C2.    The location and height of new development is not to significantly diminish the public views to heritage items, dominant landmarks, public buildings from public places or unreasonably obscure public district views of major natural features such as the water, ridgelines or bushland.
 
I.   Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development is contrary to the provisions of Section A19 Biodiversity and Habitat Management of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 to protect red-flagged value areas, with significant damage to both the upper limbs and structural woody roots of a White Mahogany (Eucalyptus acmenoides) which has significant biodiversity value being a mature remnant.

J. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority consider that the visual impact associated with the works, in particular the large shed, the concrete driveway and the associated earthworks constitutes a scar on the landscape and results in an unacceptable visual impact.

K. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority cannot be satisfied that due consideration was given to the Predictive Aboriginal Cultural Heritage mapping on the site, and that the extent of earthworks undertaken, in conjunction with the ongoing with of this area (including exposed and excavated areas) does not adequately protect Aboriginal Cultural Heritage potentially located on the site.

L. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, for the preceding reasons, the application is not considered to be in the public interest.

2.   ATTACHMENT 4 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.

 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase

The General Manager acknowledged the Bundjalung Aboriginal Nation with the following statement:

“We wish to acknowledge the Ngandowal and Minyungbal speaking people of the Bundjalung country in particular the Goodjinburra, Tul-gi-gin and Moorung - Moobah clans as being the traditional owners and custodians of the land and waters within the Tweed Shire boundaries. We also acknowledge and respect the Tweed Aboriginal community’s right to speak for its Country and to care for its traditional Country in accordance with its lore, customs and traditions.”

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins from the Murwillumbah Church of Christ.


Dear Father,

We thank You for the many blessings You pour upon us. 
We thank You for Your steadfast love that never ceases; Your mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness. 
Father, as this year is nearly coming to an end, we thank You for all You’ve done for us. 
Our Mayor, Councillor’s, Director, Managers, Secretaries, Administrators & all other areas of council have worked hard over this past year, with so much being achieved & yet there is still much to do. However, may they all now enjoy a much-deserved rest over this Christmas break.  Bless each one of them I pray.
Father, thank you for your Son, Jesus. The entire reason for we are celebrating Christmas. Thank You for the beautiful gift of family, loved ones and friends. 
May we cherish this time together with giving, laughter and joy, making precious memories for years to come.
Please watch over each and every one of us, keeping us safe over this Christmas period & bring us all back in good spirits with renewed strength into the new year.
Thank You Father… You are our Good Shepherd: Watching over us & providing everything we need. 
You let us rest in fields of green grass and lead us to quiet pools of fresh water. 
You give new strength. Guiding us in the right paths, as You have promised. We thank You.

  • So, Father, continue to help and guide all of us, our Mayor, our Councillors, the People of the Tweed & beyond, to live and practice the values we know to be true. 

That our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.     
I pray in Jesus Name:  Amen.

CONFIDENTIAL COMMITTEE

REPRESENTATIONS FOR ITEMS CONSIDERED IN COMMITTEE
(Sec 3.40, 13.9 to 13.17 Model Code of Meeting Practice)

Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.

REASON FOR CONFIDENTIALITY

Local Government Act
This report is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, which permits the meeting to be closed to the public for business relating to the following: 

(d)     commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: 

 (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or 
 (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or 
 (iii) reveal a trade secret


ALTERNATE MOTION  

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that Council defers consideration of this item for the General Manager to undertake consultation with all centre based childcare services in Council facilities based on the following proposed licence fee structure: 

  1. annual licence fee set at 4% of annual income, based on previous financial year, commencing 2026/27 for existing licences and immediately for new licences 
  2. annual licence fee to commence on the date of the new licence agreement for existing licences on the following phased-in licence fee rate:

    Year 1 (2023/24)

    Year 2 (2024/25)

    Year 3 (2025/26) and beyond

    1%

    2%

    3%

  3. annual licence fee to be reviewed every five (5) years and updated to reflect with the Australian Tax Office (ATO) benchmarks of the day


The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Warren Polglase

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 9 November 2023 be received and 

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

4.1.    Pottsville Pedestrian Counts (from 11 May 2023 LTC meeting)
The request for a pedestrian crossing on Tweed Coast Road near the Pottsville Oval is not supported as the minimum pedestrian crossing movements, in the TfNSW Guidelines are not met and the existing facilities near the Coronation Avenue, Pottsville, roundabout are adequate for the pedestrian movements in the vicinity. 

6.1.    Tweed Valley Way, South Murwillumbah
The installation of a childrens' crossing on Tweed Valley Way, adjacent to the driveway of the Murwillumbah South Infants school is supported subject to the submission of detailed design and approval under section 138 of the Roads Act.

7.1.    Pottsville Enduro Event, February 2024
The conduct of the Pottsville Enduro Event and the associated road closures on Saturday 24 February 2024 is supported subject to:
1.    NSW Police approval being obtained.
2.    Endorsement of the event by NX Sports.
3.    Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by SafeWork NSW accredited persons.
4.    Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
5.    The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or 
6.    Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
7.    All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
8.    Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
9.    Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
10.    That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
11.    The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
12.    The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
13.    A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
14.    The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
15.    The application of all signs and devices necessary to effect the changed traffic management conditions and temporary road closures for the events, also being approved as part of the event approval.


The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen

Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that the following Petition(s) be received :

  1. Petition containing 685 signatures of which 309 were valid (with 154 being invalid due to signatories are from out of the shire , 222 being invalid due to incomplete details) was received on 28 November 2023 entitled "Unrealistic Market Fee" advising as follows :

    To the Tweed Shire Council
    We the undersigned (stall holder/patron) strongly object to the unrealistic market fee imposed by your council on our Community Market run by the Tweed Heads Community Mens Shed.
    This is 500% increase is completely unjust and certainly not in the spirit of this Community run market and will eliminate a major funding source for the local charities by the Mens Shed.
    As all the profits form these markets go to the local charities this unrealistic action by the council will  ensure a bleak Christmas for many charities and individuals in the community.
    Under the new fee structure we feel the Mens Shed (as operator) may have no option but to raise fees which will make it uneconomical for the majority of stall holders with the market collapsing. 
    Surely this isn't the aim of your council.


  2. Petition containing 42 signatories of which 23 are valid (with 14 being invalid due to signatories are from out of the shire and 5 being invalid due to incomplete details) was received on 5 December 2023 entitled "Halt Koala Deaths by Vehicle Strike, on Clothiers Creek Road" advising as follows:

    "Reason - The iconic Australian koala it now at a tipping point it has been listed as "Endangered" the situation is grim. The opportunity to assist them to survive in the wild is slipping away very quickly unless there is more sincere and science appreciated action taken. The latest Koala SEPP21 ( State Environmental Planning Policy) haphazardly tabled by the State government and by some ministers who no longer are in government is a watered down version doomed to fail because it does not follow the science and does not include 
     control/protection for all habitat in particular on Private Native Forests. Logging in these areas will hasten the koalas extinction in the wild. Removing koala habitat means no koala, quite simple. 
     
    Team Koala always stands up to protect the koalas. Closer to home, once again we highlight the danger of Clothiers Creek Rd. Since the creation of the Ml, Clothiers Creek Rd has become a busy connection road between Murwillumbah and the Tweed Coast. This road is notorious for road deaths of humans and koalas. We are focused on the 3km stretch from Cabarita, start of Koala zone marked by the electronic sign, travelling west to the end of the Koala Zone also marked by the electronic sign; this is well before the highway. This 3kms uniquely cuts through the very centre of core koala habitat much to the horror of all koala lovers. The traffic speed at present is 70km/h yet the speed day or night on this stretch of road averages 70- 90km/h by both cars and trucks. We do not want any more preventable koala or human deaths on this road. 

    Request - Team Koala are proposing a reduction of the speed limit from 70km to 50 kms for this 3km stretch of Clothiers Creek Rd, through the use of traffic calming devices such as those used in Coronation Ave Pottsville before the New Ambulance Station. There are several sections that could provide the width of road for such devices. We urge the Tweed Shire Council along with the Road and Transport department to address these issues before it really is too late. These are the wishes of Team Koala Inc and the signatories below ....


  3. Petition containing 81 signatories of which 51 are valid (with 20 being invalid due to signatories are from out of the shire and 10 being invalid due to incomplete details) was received on 5 December 2023 entitled "Halt Koala Deaths on Clothiers Creek Road" advising as follows:

    The iconic Australian koala is now at tipping point it has been listed as 'Endangered' the situation is urgent.
     
    Help Team Koala save koalas here and now!
    The latest Koala SEPP21 (State Environmental Planning Policy) tabled by the State Government will fail to protect koalas because it does not follow the science and allows clearing and logging in koala habitat areas in privately held native forests.
    When habitat is cleared for roads and housing estates, cars and dogs become a serious threat to Koalas.
    Over 4000 Koalas are killed in Australia each year by cars and dogs.
     
     https://www.savethekoala.com/about-koalas/interesting-facts/
     
    This petition concerns the 3 km marked koala zone on Clothiers Creek Road from Cabarita going west, right through the heart of koala habitat. This section is well clear of the highway.
    This petition requests:
    That the Tweed Shire Council  along with the NSW Road and Transport department reduce the speed limit through this koala habitat from 70 kph to 50 kph, and enforce the limit through the use of traffic calming devices such as signs and chicanes similar to those used in Coronation Ave Pottsville, on the approach to the Ambulance Station.
    There are several  areas in the danger section of Clothiers Creek Road wide enough for such devices. 
    These measures to protect koalas are supported by Team Koala Inc and the signatories below.

  4. ATTACHMENTS 1-3 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

RESOLVED that the resolution for Item 8.4 of the Planning Committee meeting held on 13 December 2023 - Development Application S96/0049.12 for an amendment to Development Consent S96/0049 for a 37 lot industrial subdivision at Lot 2 DP 569304 No. Tringa Street, Tweed Heads, being:

"that:

1. Council refuses owners' consent for the lodgement of S96/0049.12 over Lot 1 DP1011625, with regard to temporary construction access through Lot 1; and

2. Development Application S96/0049.12 for an amendment to Development Consent S96/0049 for a 37 lot industrial subdivision at Lot 2 DP 569304, No. 60 Tringa Street, Tweed Heads West be refused for the following reasons:

a. Pursuant to Section 4.55(1A)(a) the proposal has not demonstrated that the proposed modification is of minimal environmental impact, specifically a detailed noise or dust assessment of the proposed changed haul route has not been provided.

b. Pursuant to Section 4.55(1A)(b) the proposal has not demonstrated that the proposed modification is substantially the same development as the development for which the consent was originally granted specifically no detailed assessment has been provided to compare the development to that originally approved in 1996.

c. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the proposal is not consistent with State Environmental Planning Policy (SEPP) (Resilience and Hazards) 2021 Clause 2.7(4): the development cannot be granted consent as it has not demonstrated that sufficient measures have, or will be, taken to protect, and where possible enhance, the biophysical, hydrological and ecological integrity of the coastal wetland.

d. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) the proposal has failed to demonstrate the development will not have a negative impact on the natural and built environment, in particular the protection of the tidal channel, impacts on Acid Sulphate Soils, impacts on migratory birds, ability to manage Occupational Health and Safety risks of transit through operational land during use of the temporary access have not been sufficiently addressed.

e. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) the proposal has failed to demonstrate suitability of the site for the development.

f. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(d) the proposal has failed to adequately address the environmental impact issues raised in public submissions.

g. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) the proposal is not in the public interest.

3. ATTACHMENTS 6 to 10 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
(e)    information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of the law
(g)    advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege.", 

be rescinded.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle from the Living Waters Church.

Genesis 1:29-31
29 And God said, “See, I have given you every herb that yields seed which is on the face of all the earth, and every tree whose fruit yields seed; to you it shall be for food. 30 Also, to every beast of the earth, to every bird of the air, and to everything that creeps on the earth, in which there is life, I have given every green herb for food”; and it was so. 31 Then God saw everything that He had made, and indeed it was very good. So the evening and the morning were the sixth day.

Prayer 
Our God and Father, we thank you for this Tweed Shire that we live in with it’s abundance of food that comes from your creative hand. According to the Genesis account, you have given this land to us to manage and nurture to produce food not only for us but other parts of Australia and the world. 

As this council sits today with task of managing what You have provided, I pray that they are guided by you in every decision they make so that they will help to bring about the plan and purpose you have for the Shire we live in.
 
In Jesus name we pray

RESOLVED that: 

  1. The minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held 14 December 2023 be received and 

  2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

4.1  Stuart Street, bus zone comments - from LTC 12 October 2023
That the existing bus zone on Stuart Street, Tweed Heads, adjacent to the Twin Towns carpark, be converted to '15 minute parking 8am to 9:30am, 2:30pm to 4pm Monday to Friday, School days. Buses excepted'.

4.2  Faulks Park, Kingscliff
That Council installs “No Stopping” signage (back of kerb) and a Yellow (C3) line 1m from the kerb, within the access aisle to Faulks Park, abutting the Cudgen Creek revetment wall and exclude the area adjacent to the fish cleaning station.

7.1  Kingscliff Street, Kingscliff - bus stop
That bus zone signage be installed adjacent to the bus shelter between the driveways of 105 and 103 Kingscliff Street, and between the driveway of 88 Kingscliff Street and the property fence on the northern side of 86 Kingscliff Street, Kingscliff.

7.2  Gold Coast Pro, Surf Event for 2024
The temporary closure of Coral Street, Tweed Heads for the Gold Coast Pro 2024 event is supported, subject to:
1. The submission of a Traffic Management Plan, and Traffic Control Plan approved by Council and NSW police, that are to be submitted at least 4 weeks prior to conduct of the Event.
2. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
3. The application of all signs and devices necessary to effect the changed traffic management conditions and temporary road closures for the events, also being approved as part of the event approval.

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

The General Manager (Troy Green) temporarily left the meeting at 4.14pm

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr James Owen
 
RESOLVED that:


  1. Notes that Wharf Street and Bay Street are the gateway entry statements from the Gold Coast (QLD) to Tweed Heads (NSW).

  2. Notes the opportunity for increased development and utilisation of the CBD.

  3. Notes the upgrades soon to be completed to the bus shelters in and around Wharf Street and Bay Street.

  4. Notes the upgrades to Jack Evans Boat Harbour that Council has invested in, in recent years.

  5. Notes that the Council has been working in collaboration with the Tweed and Murwillumbah Business Chambers on applications under the Community Infrastructure Development Program which will directly enhance Murwillumbah and the Tweed CBD.

  6. Notes the ongoing anti-social and graffiti issues that remain in and around Wharf Street, Bay Street and Jack Evans Boat Harbour. 

  7. Requests staff (through the Portfolio Board) to review and provide a report back to Council on the feasibility, options, costings, timing, prioritisation, and potential funding of a premier entrance statement for Tweed Shire which would encourage new development and activation of the Wharf Street precinct from Boundary Street to Bay Street by revitalising the current landscaped areas, additional and increased tree cover, and predominantly retaining the road and car parking configuration.

  8. Requests staff to further work with Police and the Tweed Mall to address the graffiti and abandoned shopping trolleys that plague the streets, including the impounding of trolleys outside of the shopping mall's property.

  9. Requests the General Manager to undertake an audit in the first half of 2024 of the Tweed CBD and surrounding streets (Wharf Street and Bay Street), and parks and infrastructure, to identify immediate and interim measures that can be undertaken for beautification of the area such as 

    - pressure cleaning council infrastructure including, but not limited to, bins, benches, seating, playgrounds, paths and walkways and bus stops; 
    - graffiti removal; 
    - revitalisation of the current landscaped areas; and 
    - consideration of options for festive and aesthetic lighting. 
     
  10. Conducts a new Community Safety Audit with the NSW Police for the precinct which can provide recommendations to address safety, homelessness, and other issues in this precinct, noting that the last audit was undertaken in 2016. 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil.

RESOLVED that:

  • Petition containing 63 signatories of which 53 were valid (with 7 being invalid due to incomplete details, and 3 signatories were from out of the shire) was received on 20 December 2023 entitled "Halt Koala Deaths on Clothiers Creek Road" advising as follows:

That the Tweed Shire Council  along with the NSW Road and Transport department reduce the speed limit through this koala habitat from 70 kph to 50 kph, and enforce the limit through the use of traffic calming devices such as signs and chicanes similar to those used in Coronation Ave Pottsville, on the approach to the Ambulance Station. There are several  areas in the danger section of Clothiers Creek Road wide enough for such devices.

  • Petition containing 54 signatories of which 33 are were valid (with 11 being invalid due to incomplete details, and 10 signatories were from out of the shire) was received on 20 December 2023 entitled "Halt Koala Deaths by Vehicle Strike on Clothiers Creek Road" advising as follows:

Team Koala are proposing a reduction of the speed limit from 70km to 50 kms for this 3km stretch of Clothiers Creek Rd, through the use of traffic calming devices such as those used in Coronation Ave Pottsville before the New Ambulance Station. There are several sections that could provide the width of road for such devices. We urge the Tweed Shire Council along with the Road and Transport department to address these issues before it really is too late. These are the wishes of Team Koala Inc and the signatories below.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Tay Lee,  Tweed Valley Uniting Church

"Gracious God,

We come before Your throne of grace with hearts full of gratitude for the community we are a part of in the Tweed Shire. We ask for your abundant blessings upon the Shire. Bless all its residents to access equal opportunities for prosperity and guide them to be a better community that helps and supports each other.

This time, we lift up the Tweed Shire Council into Your loving care and seek Your guidance, wisdom, and blessings. Lord, we thank You for the commitment and dedication of our Mayor, Councillors and Council staff. Bless them with discernment as they make decisions that impact the lives of the people of Tweed Shire. Grant them the wisdom to navigate challenges and the insight to pursue initiatives that promote the community's well-being, justice, peace, security and reconciliation so that they may contribute to the growth and flourishing of our community. May Your light guide their path and Your grace sustain them in their precious work.

 Loving God, we entrust the future of Tweed Shire into Your hands. May it be a place where love, justice, and harmony prevail. May it be a place where everyone satisfies to live. May it be a place where love, truth and compassion are alive.
In Jesus' name, we pray.

Amen."

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that:

A.      Development Application DA23/0632 for shop top housing comprising one (1) ground floor office premises and car parking and three levels of residential units at Lot 181 & 182 DP 259164; No 100 -102 Hastings Road, Bogangar, be refused for the following reasons: 

1.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate that the proposal is compliant with the National Construction Code.

2.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate that the proposal is compliant with the provisions of SEPP (Resilience and Hazards) 2021, Chapter 2 Coastal Management. 

3.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate that the proposal is compliant with the provisions of SEPP (Sustainable Buildings) 2022. 

4.       The proposed development is considered unacceptable pursuant to the provisions of s4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as the design quality of the proposal when evaluated in accordance with the design quality principles is unacceptable. Consent must not be granted as the proposal does not demonstrate that adequate regard has been given to the design quality principles. 

5.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate that the proposal is compliant with the provisions of Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014. The application has not demonstrated compliance with the following clauses:

a.      Clause 2.3 with regard to the development’s performance against zone objectives for E1-Local Centre
b.      Clause 4.3 in regard to amenity impact on the adjoining southern dwelling access to solar. 
c.      Clause 5.21 with regard to safe occupation and efficient evacuation in the event of flood.
d.      Clause 7.1 with regard to impacts of Acid Sulfate Soil disturbance and site management.
e.      Clause 7.2 with regard to the quality of soil to be excavated and the management of soil excavated. 
f.       Clause 7.6 with regard to stormwater management and the impact on adjoining sites.
g.      Clause 7.10 with regard to the adequate provision of stormwater drainage. 
h.      Clause 7.10 with regard to the adequate provision of vehicular access.
 
6.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) the application fails to satisfy several aspects of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 (DCP). The application has not demonstrated compliance with the following Sections within the DCP:

a.      Section A2 – Site Access and Parking. The application has not demonstrated adequate access requirements and insufficient car parking has been provided. 
b.      Section A15 – Waste Minimisation and Management. The application has not demonstrated adequate measures for construction and operational waste storage. 
c.      Section B19 – Bogangar / Cabarita Beach Locality Plan. The application has not demonstrated consistency with the design objectives of the identified precinct.

7.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate that the proposed earthworks will not impact the adjoining-built environment. 

8.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate that the proposed construction (ground vibration) works will impact on the adjoining-built environment.

9.     Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate that the proposed construction will not impact the amenity of the adjoining-built environment. 

10.     Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate that it will not adversely impact upon existing Council infrastructure (sewer).

11.     Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate the suitability of the site for the development. The application has not demonstrated compliance with respect to the existing built form, proposed earthworks, construction noise and vibration, noise impacts of the use, the relocation of the drainage easement and protection of Council’s sewer infrastructure.  

12.     Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) the application not considered to be in the public interest with regard to environmental impacts and non-compliance with Council’s controls and design standards.

B.      Council defends the Deemed Refusal in the Land & Environment Court.

C.     ATTACHMENT 4 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins from the Murwillumbah Church of Christ and the NSW Rural Fire Service Chaplain :


Let’s us pray.
 
Father, I thank You that You are here amongst us. 

You are our Almighty Counselor, silently listening and watching over all that will be said and done.
 
I pray for our leaders: that Your blessings, goodness & protection will be upon each and every one them: 
Mayor Chris Cherry, Deputy Meredith Dennis, Councillor Rhiannon Brinsmead, Councillor Reece Byrnes, Councillor Nola Firth, Councillor James Owen, Councillor Warren Polglase and our General Manager Troy Green.

Father, help and encourage our leaders to walk in humility and integrity. 

Guide them to put the needs of others before themselves and be true servant leaders. 

May they be open to the wisdom & counsel of others and know best where to use it. 

May they be authentic, morally upright, and have strong principles in line with Your standard of righteousness for the benefit of Your people. 

I pray that Your Will be done.

So Father, continue to help and guide us, that we may live to practice the values we know to be true. That Council be transparent in all its dealings today. 

Treating the people of the Tweed with fairness, commitment, planning for their future…with everyone involved:
So that our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.

May You answer us in the day we call…

Amen

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:

 

1. Receives the Minutes of the Aboriginal Advisory Committee Meeting held Friday 10 November; and

 

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

 

BA4. Fingal Holiday Park - Aboriginal Cultural Heritage Management Plan (ACHMP)

That the Coordinator Tweed Holiday Parks provide regular updates to the Aboriginal Advisory Committee on actions undertaken under the Aboriginal Cultural Heritage Management Plan for Fingal Holiday Park, subject to also keeping other project Registered Aboriginal Parties informed.

 

A4. Point Danger, Captain Cook Memorial works 

That the Aboriginal Advisory Committee endorses the following for Point Danger Cafe: 

 

1. Use of the following stories for the storyboards: 

 

Moy Ngagambi - Black Dingo 

Gamaygan Guyumgan - Morning Star 

Gerrah - White Cockatoo 

Booninybah - Place of the Echidna 

Jungarrabah - Place of the Pelican. 

 

2. The potential use of the name ‘Black Dingo Café’ by any new contractor for the Point Danger Café in accordance with the storylines. 

 

3. Receives the Minutes of the Aboriginal Advisory Committee Meeting held Friday 8 December 2023; and

 

4. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

 

BA1. Point Danger, Captain Cook Memorial works 

That the Aboriginal Advisory Committee is not in support of using the name ‘Black Dingo Café’ for the Point Danger café.



The Motion was Carried

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Notes the outcomes of the investigation into partnership opportunities to enable textile recycling.
     
  2. Requires the General Manager to conduct an expression of interest process from suitable textile recovery organisations with the aim of introducing a bin type textile collection within the Shire.

  3. Requires the General Manager to undertake a public education program to improve the quality and quantity of textile reuse in the Shire.

  4. Notifies all Not for Profits with subsidised waste collection that all waste must have textiles sorted separately for collection.

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Endorses the draft Sport and Active Recreation Strategy 2023-2033 as shown at attachment 1, with the following amendments: 
    1. on page 17, last paragraph to include 'microplastics',
    2. on page 61 add 'hiking and walking' to the list,
