Cr Brinsmead returned to the meeting at 6:18pm.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that Council prepares the following motions to be submitted to the Australian Local Government Association for the National General Assembly 2024:

  1. The National General Assembly calls on the Australian Government to provide local councils with funding to prepare climate change action plans.

  2. The National General Assembly calls on the Australian Government to allocate substantial increase funding for weed control given it is a major contributor to biodiversity loss. 

  3. That the Federal Government review the taxation system to incentivise the use of untapped existing accommodation within homes. For example, consideration be given to allowing owner of a Principal Place of Residence to nominate a bedroom for Board rental to individuals who qualify for rental assistance and in return that portion of their home remains exempt from Capital Gains Tax and does not effect their pension should they be a pensioner provided they register their bedroom for accommodation with CentreLink at a discount of 20% to market rent. 

SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDERS
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RECOMMENDED that Standing Orders be suspended to deal with Item 19.2 of the Agenda.

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None


RESUMPTION OF STANDING ORDERS
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor) 

RECOMMENDED that Standing Orders be resumed.

The Motion was Carried

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that:

  1. The following tabled Petition(s) be received.
    • Petition 1 - containing 27 signatories of which 27 were valid was received on 20 February 2024 entitled "Stop speeding/dangerous/noisy traffic - Banora Hills Drive, Banora Point" advising as follows:

      This petition is about safety which should be a fundamental right of residents living in the Tweed Shire be they ratepayer or renters.
      We would greatly appreciate if this petition was given consideration by the Council and that an investigation was conducted and appropriate action taken to ensure the safety of people living and using Banora Hills Drive, Banora Point.

    • Petition 2 - containing 45 signatories of which 39 were valid (with 1 being invalid due to incomplete details, and 5 signatories were from out of the shire) was received on 21 February 2024 entitled "Halt Koala Deaths on Clothiers Creek Rd" advising as follows:

      That the Tweed Shire Council along with NSW Roads and Transport department reduce the speed limit through the koala habitat to 50 kph, and enforce it through the use of traffic calming devices such as signs and chicanes similar to those used in Coronation Ave Pottsville, on the approach to the Ambulance Station. There are several in the danger section of Clothiers Creek Road wide enough for such devices.
      These measures to protect koalas are supported by Team Koala Inc and the signatories below.

    • Petition 3 - containing 56 signatories of which 40 were valid (with 4 being invalid due to incomplete details, and 11 signatories were from out of the shire) was received on 21 February 2024 entitled "Halt Koala Deaths By Vehicle Strike, On Clothiers Creek Rd" advising as follows:

      Team Koala are proposing a reduction of the speed limit from 70km to 50kms for this 3km stretch of Clothiers Creek Rd, through the use of traffic calming devices such as those used in Coronation Ave Pottsville before the new Ambulance Station. There are several sections that could provide the width of road for such devices. We urge the Tweed Shire Council along with the Roads and Transport department to address these issues before it is really too late,. These are the wishes of Team Koala Inc and the signatories below.

    • Petition 4 - containing 68 signatories of which 30 were valid (with 6 being invalid due to incomplete details, and 32 signatories were from out of the shire) was received on 28 February 2024 entitled "Halt Koala Deaths on Clothiers Creek Rd" advising as follows:

      That the Tweed Shire Council along with NSW Roads and Transport department reduce the speed limit through the koala habitat to 50 kph, and enforce it through the use of traffic calming devices such as signs and chicanes similar to those used in Coronation Ave Pottsville, on the approach to the Ambulance Station. There are several in the danger section of Clothiers Creek Road wide enough for such devices. 
      These measures to protect koalas are supported by Team Koala Inc and the signatories below.


  2. Council refer petition 1 entitled "Stop speeding/dangerous/noisy traffic - Banora Hills Drive, Banora Point" to the Tweed Byron Local Area Command for their attention.

  3. Council refer petition 1 entitled "Stop speeding/dangerous/noisy traffic - Banora Hills Drive, Banora Point" to the Local Traffic Committee to consider what Council can do to encourage lower speeds in the area.

  4. Council refer petition 2 entitled "Halt Koala Deaths on Clothiers Creek Rd", petition 3 entitled "Halt Koala Deaths By Vehicle Strike, On Clothiers Creek Rd" and petition 4 entitled "Halt Koala Deaths on Clothiers Creek Rd" to Transport for NSW for their attention and consideration in response to Council's request for a speed reduction on Clothiers Creek Road.

  5. ATTACHMENTS 1 - 4 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that The Mayoral Minute titled Time Capsule Letter from the then Mayor Clarrie Hall be received and noted.

The Chairman,
John Oxley Bi-Centenary Celebrations Committee 2023

Mr. Chairman,

May I extend my very best wishes for a happy and successful bi-centenary celebration. Even at this distance I would know such is assured.

Ours, back in the 1973 was, may I say, spectacular; it was really worth the effort of a dedicated Committee. For months we met on Monday nights at the Council Chambers, planning and organising; there were those times it seemed that things just wouldn't dove-tail, but we persevered and the outcome was most gratifying.

The popular State Governor, Sir Roden Cutler and his Lady paid their first visit to the Tweed for the occasion as our distinguished guests.

The Pioneers' Luncheon was a real winner; hundreds of old hands, men and women, attended from near and far. Old Tweed boys who returned for the function included The Hon. Sir Harry Budd, President of the Legislative Council of NSW and Sir Frank Nicklin, a past Premier of Queensland. Mr. Aub Budd chaired the Luncheon proceedings.

The re-enactment of Oxley's landing at Chinderah on 31st October 1823 was superbly done. The part of Oxley was played by Harry Smith who incidentally was a great-grandson of the late Pat Smith senr., first white child born on the Tweed - an appropriate choice to play the part, you will agree, Mr. Chairman?

The functions at Tweed Heads, Kingscliff and Uki were all done well. The laying of the foundation stone of the Murwillumbah Civic Centre by His Excellency marked another milestone in our history. The Vice Regal Ball, Civic Dinner, T.R.J.C. Races, the T.R. Agriculture Show were all remarkably well attended and lavishly enjoyed - and all in one week. People apparently just didn't tire; the spirit of celebrating the discovery was uppermost within everyone. We felt we owed a debt to John Oxley of 150 years, and everyone felt this was an occasion to show our appreciation of him and of the first settlers who followed later and pioneered the virgin land, as they did, into the greatest Valley on God's earth - this I believe; our river, our beaches, our hills and our pastures, all overlooked by Captain Cook's 4,000 ft. high Mt Warning, the peak of which is the first spot on our continent to receive the morning's sunshine; our regular seasons; our soft climate - all make us the envy of all others, and leave everything set up for a glorious future. Nothing can or will hold back the Tweed!

To date I have been 20 years a Tweed Shire Councillor and in that short space of time I have seen dramatic forward moves and having been Shire President for 12 of those years, may I say modestly that I was fortunately associated with a lot of change which we know rightly as progress.

Back to the purpose of my writing you - that there will be on record at least a distant association of the sesqui and the bi-centenary, 1973-2023.

On behalf of my Committee (Bob Whittle, Max Boyd, Bill Renehan, John Constable, Warren Judd, and others) I wish you well with your John Oxley Bi-Centenary Celebrations in 2023.

Sincerely yours,
C. H. HALL, CHAIRMAN
John Oxley Sesquicentenary Celebrations Committee. 1973


The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Councillor Owen asks for a brief (no more than 4 minutes) summary for the following.

What is Tweed Shire Council's succession plan for the following roles within Council:

General Manager
Director Sustainable Communities and Environment
Director Engineering
Director Planning and Regulation
Director Corporate Services


The General Manager replied:

Through you Madam Mayor. I thank Councillor Owen for the question. 

Regarding Council’s leadership succession plan, I provide the following as to what is already happening in this space. 

Given the dynamic and challenging environment we face, I'd like to start by highlighting the steps we've taken to ensure strong leadership stability at Council.

Chapter 11 of the Local Government Act 1993 prescribes “How are Councils staffed?”. The General Manager and other senior staff of a council are employed under contracts that are performance-based. This relates to me as the General Manager and the current four Directors referenced in the question. We are classified as senior staff as per the Act’s definition which states, “senior staff of a council means the general manager of the council and the holders of all other positions identified in the council’s organisation structure as senior staff positions”. 

As Councillors would be aware, I was recently reappointed to the General Manager role by way of Council resolution on 13 December 2023 for a period of five years, with a contract being signed to reflect this appointment. This was carried out pursuant to section 334 of the Local Government Act 1993. This extended term provides stability and continuity in leadership until at least December 2028. I am looking forward to working with the elected body to implement the strategic direction of Council for the period of my contract. 

We’ve also achieved significant stability at the Director level with five-year contracts recently being entered into by the Director Sustainable Communities and Environment and the Director Planning and Regulation. The Director Engineering and Director Corporate Services are further advanced in their contracts timing wise. This bodes well for continued stability in the coming years.

Now to succession planning relating to the General Manager position when I am on leave or should circumstances arise that I am no longer in the General Manager role. I have full confidence in our current Directors, their knowledge and experience after many years working in the local government sector. They are positioned well to act as the General Manager and indeed to apply for the position and be competitive in a merit selection process, if the need arises. You will note there are strict requirements in terms of the appointment of staff on merit under the Local Government Act which sets Council apart from private enterprise and limits what can and can’t be done in succession planning. 

We’re also fortunate to have a highly talented and committed Corporate Management Team. These individuals, who each report to one of the Directors identified in the question on notice, gain valuable experience through acting placements, including relieving Directors when they are on leave or acting for me as General Manager. Together, the Directors and I have full confidence in the Corporate Management Team's ability to step up and act as Directors whenever the need arises; or again to apply in a merit selection process should a Director position become vacant. The most recent appoint of the Director Planning & Regulation testifies to the strength of our management team in competing and succeeding in a competitive merit-based process. And the second most recent appointment of the Director Sustainable Communities and Environment shows that under a merit selection process, we will always employ the best person for the job.

I also recognise that succession planning goes beyond filling vacant roles. It’s a dynamic and ongoing process that aligns staff aspirations and talent with our evolving needs. It requires us to continuously plan to ensure we have the talent in place to meet future challenges and opportunities. This is reflected in Part 1 of Council’s Resource Strategy 2023-2033, which outlines our investment in our workforce, including offering professional learning and development opportunities to equip our staff with the skills and knowledge they need to grow their careers at Council, fostering a safe, positive and supportive work environment where staff can thrive and building a diverse and inclusive workforce.

For example, initiatives such as the ‘Great Managers’ training program, offered to all Corporate Management Team members, including Directors and myself, equip staff with the necessary skills and knowledge to excel in leadership roles at Council.

One of the most important benefits of succession planning is to improve employee retention, employee productivity and nurture future leaders. The last thing we want to do as a Council is to find and train a great staff member and then see them resign. To this end, I also thank and acknowledge this Council for the professional development opportunities it has afforded me. I was lucky enough to begin at this council and be mentored by former General Manager Mike Rayner, someone who had 30 years of experience at this Council. In my role I am passing on the combined experience of those that have gone before me and my own experiences to the Directors, Managers and senior staff to prepare them for future leadership opportunities.

It has also been professional development opportunities such as completing the Harvard Business School Leading Change and Organisational Renewal Leadership Program that ensures that I, as a leader remain energised, able to innovate and respond to emerging challenges. To this end I am proud that as a leader I have overseen some innovative change measures both locally here in Tweed and more broadly across the sector. And I must acknowledge that they at times faced resistance, but we pushed through to achieve great results. 

This innovation and willingness to change and respond to a growing community with new challenges is a culture that has been nurtured within our organisation. This week’s businesses paper is testament to that. Each of the Directors and their respective teams continue to innovate and put forward visionary ideas and projects for Council consideration. For that I am proud and have confidence in their ability to lead when I do step down from this role. 

The impressive achievements we have delivered as a collective body at this council, with elected officials and the staff working together are a testament to the value of having a long-tenured General Manager and experienced councillors. This continuity fosters strategic consistency, allowing for the execution of a long-term vision and the cultivation of strong relationships with Councillors, staff and other key stakeholders.

As a Council we also use talent identification and assessment tools including performance reviews and skills assessments to identify high-potential staff who have the necessary skills, experience and leadership qualities. We develop and train staff to address skill gaps and equip them with the necessary knowledge and experience. We utilise training programs, mentoring, coaching and project assignments to facilitate development and wherever possible, use retention strategies to recognise and retain our top talent, including leaders.  

The following observations need to be considered in relation to succession planning as well. The 2022 Local Government Workforce Skills and Capability Survey paints a clear picture of the challenges we face in succession planning, not just for the Tweed Shire, but across the entire local government sector. The survey highlights several longstanding issues including recruitment and retention struggles at all levels, including Director and General Manager level, a lack of skilled workers in key positions hindering productivity and service delivery, limited access to training and development opportunities to enhance workforce skills and capability and an ageing workforce. 

By way of example, just two weeks ago at the Regional Cities meeting, the Mayor and I heard how Albury is currently challenged with 100 out of 600 positions vacant.

The most common drivers hindering recruitment and retention at Tweed Shire and in local government are: market salaries and remuneration packages often surpass what we can offer, limiting our talent pool; the high cost of living and housing crisis in regional areas makes attracting qualified staff to the area challenging; the private sector increasingly offering flexible work arrangements and attractive perks, diminishing our advantage; and in local government there is a growing expectation that senior staff are to be available 24/7.

We’re actively tackling these challenges by improving our recruitment practices to attract and retain talent more easily, exploring ways to enhance our compensation and benefits offerings to better compete in the market and we’re developing a learning and development strategy that will focus on strengthening our apprenticeship and traineeship program, upskilling the existing workforce and succession planning, building a pipeline of future talent and leaders. In addition, we continue to look at ways we can enhance our workplace culture to improve staff wellbeing, job satisfaction and engagement to retain talent. 

While acknowledging these challenges, it’s important to recognise the skilled, capable and stable leadership team currently in place, especially at the executive level.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Owen asks for a brief (no more than 4 minutes) response to the following:


Is Council sufficiently resourced to manage the increase in vegetation maintenance during warmer and wetter months?
What other options are there and what is the potential cost and resource implications to Council?

The Director of Engineering replied:

Through you Madam Mayor.

The annual budget and long term financial plan for road maintenance does not cater for sudden increases in roadside vegetation growth during unusually hotter and wetter summers.

During growth season relatively more road maintenance resources are allocated to prioritise roadside vegetation management. However, due to the length of the road network we manage and unavoidable downtime during prolonged wet weather, it takes several months to carry out these activities on a rotational basis.

Over the years road maintenance budgets have been indexed at estimated inflation rates however this has been less than the actual increase in the costs of carrying out the work, meaning a reduction in funding in real terms. The mismatch of actual inflation rates and councils revenue raising ability was an issue highlighted in the recent IPART final report on the review of NSW rate peg methodology.

There has also been a corresponding increase in the community expectations on the level of service Council provides.

The control of roadside vegetation takes various forms including tree lopping, hand mowing, brush cutting, mowing with slashers and flails, and weed control. These activities are undertaken by a combination of Council employees, Council equipment and contractors. Expenditure last financial year on roadside vegetation management was $2.35 million and year to date expenditure is approximately $1.5 million. The nominal financial split being 45% Council and 55% contractors. During peak periods local contractors are fully utilised through our service contracts or are fully booked by other landowners, meaning there is no spare capacity in the current contractor market. 

Due to these limitations, it is unlikely in the current market that Council can improve the level of service for roadside vegetation maintenance in the peak growth season. Increases to the road maintenance program budget would enable additional internal and external vegetation management services to commence earlier in the year and extend further into the shoulder seasons. Previously staff and equipment resources were also made available from the Parks and Active Communities area to assist with peak demands, however as PAC has also inherited significant extra land to manage, they are now also fully allocated across their assets during high growth season.

It should be noted that Cr Firth has a notice of motion to consider an increase to roadside weed control in the 24/25 budget deliberations for an amount of $265,000. This is proposed to be allocated to Rous County Council and apply to all road reserve land and will not change Council’s roadside activities.

The options available to Council is to increase the budget/service levels for this program at the detriment of other programs and services or implement a special rate variation. Depending on the amount allocated, additional budget would be applied to additional staff or plant resources and/or contract resources when available through the year.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Owen asks for a brief (no more than 4 minute) response to the following:

  • What are the potential impacts to Tweed Shire Council of the Federal Government's proposed recycling levy?

The Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor. 

I can advise that the Federal Government is proposing a new levy to come into effect this year with the aim of helping the country manage waste within its national boundaries.  

If implemented, this proposal will see a fee of $4 on every tonne of recyclables exported overseas, and the progressive limiting of the allowable prohibited content in each export shipment.  The application of the levy is only where domestic use of recyclables is not occurring.

With regards to how this may impact Tweed Shire Council, Council has an agreed processing rate for recyclables within its current recycling collection contract.  Through this agreement the contractor is required to absorb costs associated with any change of legislation to a certain amount.

On this basis we are not anticipating any impact by this levy if introduced.  The contract Council has in place ends on 30 June 2032, some 8 years away, meaning it is unlikely to have any impact on Council’s cost to provide household recycling services. The government is investing into a Recycling Modernisation Fund to assist in transforming Australia’s waste and recycling capacity and ultimately reducing the amount that is exported.

It should be noted that this levy is only a proposal at this stage.

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr James Owen
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
 
RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Acknowledge the need to provide additional financial support to seniors and pensioners across the community, particularly during the cost of living challenge currently facing those across the Tweed Shire,

  2. Acknowledge local councils, including Tweed Shire Council, currently meet 45 percent of the total cost of pensioner concession rebates, but are financially constrained to provide any additional support;

  3. Acknowledge the New South Wales State Government has not increased its proportion of the Pensioner Concession Rebate for more than a decade;

  4. Recognises the significant funding that the current and previous State Governments has provided Tweed Shire Council for flood damage repair, write to the NSW Premier, the NSW Treasurer, the Minister for Local Government, the NSW Leader of the Opposition, the Shadow Treasurer, and the Shadow Minister for Local Government requesting their support for more permanent relief to pensioners by doubling the Pensioner Concession Rebate from $250 to $500 per annum, and increasing the annual water/sewer rates and charges rebate from $87.50 to $175, with the entire cost of the increase to be funded from NSW Treasury;

  5. Writes to the State Members for Tweed and Lismore seeking their support for the Council's position; and

  6. Requests the Mayor to raise this at Northern Rivers Joint Organisaton and requests the member councils to consider raising a similar motion at their Councils.

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd, Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church.


"Gracious God, 
 
With Youth Week approaching we celebrate the young people of our Shire.  We pray for them as they navigate a complex world, and thank you for the many elders, teachers, coaches, and community leaders both paid and volunteer who mentor them.  We are especially mindful of children who are in vulnerable circumstances and pray for the services in our community that keep them safe.  We are grateful for the commitment of Council over decades to create and maintain infrastructure and programs that enable young people to flourish.
 
Please bless the work of Council today and into the future.  Give Councillors and staff joy in their work, unity in the things that really matter, and courage to boldly address the needs of our community, especially those of our most vulnerable.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that:

  1. Development Application DA22/0457 for farm stay accommodation (1 cabin) at Lot 10 DP 711758 No. 363 Cobaki Road, Cobaki be refused for the following reasons:

    1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is not inconsistent with the aim of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 1.2(2)(b) to encourage a sustainable local economy and small business, employment, agriculture, affordable housing, recreational, arts, social, cultural, tourism and sustainable industry opportunities appropriate to Tweed. The application which seeks approval for farm stay accommodation on agricultural land that does not meet the requirements to be defined as farm stay accommodation and is therefore prohibited tourist and visitor accommodation in a rural zone is not considered an appropriate tourist opportunity for the agricultural land.

    2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is for a permissible purpose of development in the RU2 Rural Landscape zone under the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014. The consent authority is not satisfied the proposed farm stay accommodation is on a commercial farm and ancillary to a commercial farm as required by the definition of farm stay accommodation.

    3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is not inconsistent with the objectives of the RU2 Rural Landscape zone pursuant to Clause 2.3(2) of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014. The consent authority is not satisfied the proposed tourist and visitor accommodation is suitably linked to an agricultural use of the land.

    4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, for the reasons set out in the preceding reasons, the application is not in the public interest.

  2. The General Manager or delegate prepare a draft section for the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 for Council's consideration for agritourism and farm stay accommodation.

  3. ATTACHMENTS 3 to 6 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:

(d)     commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: 
          (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
          (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or 
          (iii) reveal a trade secret


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
PROPOSED that:

A. Development Application DA22/0160 for or multi-dwelling housing (13 townhouses), swimming pools, signage, earthworks and vegetation removal at Lot 5 DP 1030979; No. 18 Kildare Drive Banora Point be refused for the following reasons:

1.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the aim of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 1.2(2)(i) which is to conserve or enhance areas of defined high ecological value. The application which seeks approval for 13 townhouses does not meet the requirements of 1.2(2)(i) as there is insufficient setback to the Lowland Rainforest sufficient to enhance this threatened community.

2.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with Tweed DCP Section A19 Biodiversity & Habitat Management Clause 2.2 C1 as the application does not provide

a   sufficient buffer for the listed ecological community of Lowland Rainforest on the site and in the adjoining reserve. The buffer is 10m instead of the required 30m. 

b.  a sufficient buffer (10m instead of 20m) to protect the moderate to high likelihood of presence of the following threatened fauna:  Greyheaded Flying-fox, Wompoo Fruit dove, Rose-crowned Fruit dove, and White-eared Monarch. The buffer is 10m instead of the required 30m.

3.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with Tweed DCP Section A19 Biodiversity & Habitat Management Section 9 Principal 7 which states
 
P7. Small remnants – Small patches of habitat should be retained where possible and measures taken to mitigate edge effects and other relevant threats.
 
The site of this application adjoins a significant reserve and thus constitutes part of an important small remnant. The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that native vegetation loss is not occurring and does not involve negative edge effects.
4.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with Tweed DCP Section B3 Banora Point West – Tweed Heads South Section 13 Environment Section as:
 
a.  This application has not sufficiently demonstrated that the development protects the adjoining reserve in its natural state. The buffer from the listed ecological community of Lowland Rainforest is 10 m instead of the required 30 m (as per Tweed DCP Section A19). The reserve is of ‘Very High’ ecological status. (TVMS 2004 - Ecological Status, (Map 4 of 7) mapping, the 102 Sub-tropical / Warm Temperate Rainforest on Bedrock Substrates vegetation unit.). 
b.  The application fails to demonstrate that public access to the Lowland Rainforest on the site has sufficiently limited public access because the buffer is not the required 30 m as per Tweed DCP Section A19. 
c.  The application fails to retain existing stands of trees to enhance the visual appearance of the development. As well as trees under 5 metres and lower storey vegetation on 2421 square metres of vegetation removal, three substantial rainforest trees of 14m (Red Kamala), 10m (Lilly Pilly) and 16 m (Sandpaper Fig) will also be removed. 
5.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with Tweed DCP Section B3 Banora Point West – Tweed Heads South Section 13.2.b.ii which states: 
Existing trees should be preserved wherever possible. The siting and layout of a development at the initial design stage should consider the location of trees with a view to their preservation;
 
The siting and layout of the development at the design stage did not sufficiently consider the location of trees with a view to their preservation. Many trees under 5 metres will be removed and three tall rainforest trees (14m - Red Kamala, 10m - Lilly Pilly and 16 m –Sandpaper Fig) will also be removed.  A development that had a smaller footprint could have achieved retention of many more trees.

6.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as it relates to the likely impacts of the development,  the proposed development will have an unacceptable impact on the environment as it fails to sufficiently protect the threatened fauna ( Greyheaded Flying-fox, Wompoo Fruit dove, Rose-crowned Fruit dove, and White-eared Monarch) and flora (Lowland Rainforest).It also fails to sufficiently protect the adjoining reserve which is of ‘Very High ecological status’ (TVMS 2004 - Ecological Status, (Map 4 of 7) mapping, the 102 Sub-tropical / Warm Temperate Rainforest on Bedrock Substrates vegetation unit.).

7.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as it relates to suitability of the site, the proposed development is not suitable for the site as it is of a scale that does not allow sufficient buffer to sufficiently protect the threatened fauna ( Greyheaded Flying-fox, Wompoo Fruit dove, Rose-crowned Fruit dove, and White-eared Monarch) and flora (Lowland Rainforest). For the same reason it also fails to sufficiently protect the adjoining reserve which is of ‘Very High ecological status’ (TVMS 2004 - Ecological Status, (Map 4 of 7) mapping, the 102 Sub-tropical / Warm Temperate Rainforest on Bedrock Substrates vegetation unit.).

8.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(d) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as it relates to submission received, the proposed development has attracted 22 submissions, including a petition with 85 signatures opposed to the development.

9.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, for the reasons set out in the preceding reasons, the application is not in the public interest.
B.  ATTACHMENT 6 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law



AMENDMENT 1

Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RECOMMENDED that:

A. Development Application DA22/0160 for or multi-dwelling housing (13 townhouses), swimming pools, signage, earthworks and vegetation removal at Lot 5 DP 1030979; No. 18 Kildare Drive Banora Point be deferred for a site visit.

B.  ATTACHMENT 6 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law


Amendment 1 was Carried

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle from the Living Waters Church.



Dear Lord, 
 
It’s with heavy hearts that we reflect on the tragedies that have happened in our State in the past week. Our thoughts and prayers are with the victims and their families as they suffer the trauma of the recent events. Our hearts also go out to those who were directly affected by these atrocities and the resulting Trauma. 
 
As our council presides over the well-being of every citizen in the Tweed Shire Council, we ask for Your Wisdom to guide them in the decisions they make.
 
We thank you for the leadership of this council, and although appointed by men, the gifts they have to run this council are given by you.
 
Help our Councillors, Lord to continue to make this shire a safe and prosperous place to live.
 
We ask this in Jesus name.

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that Council:
 
  1. Determines that 2025 Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards and Citizenship ceremony be held on 24 January in the Murwillumbah Auditorium.

  2. The Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards Selection Panel (comprising all Councillors) and the current Awardees, consider the 2024 Tweed Shire Australia Day Award nominations for the following categories:
    • Arts and Culture
    • Citizen of the Year
    • Community Event of the Year 
    • Senior Ambassador
    • Sporting Achievement (Group and Individual)
    • Volunteer of the Year (Group and Individual)
    • Young Achiever in Community Service

      with the option to make an ‘Honourable Mention’ to nominees who deserves recognition for their efforts.

  3. Adopts the changes to the Australia Day Award nominations eligibility criteria.

  4. Selects the 2024 Australia Day Citizen of the Year, with the alternate of the Young Achiever in Community Service, to be invited to perform the role of 2025 Tweed Shire Australia Day Ambassador at the official Tweed Shire Australia Day Award and Citizenship Ceremony.


The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

Cr James Owen

  1. The setting of the date for the 2025 Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards and Citizenship Ceremony be deferred for consultation with the community about whether they wish to have the Australia Day Awards and Citizenship Ceremony on 24 January 2024 via Your Say Tweed. 

  2. The Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards Selection Panel (comprising all Councillors) and the current Awardees, consider the 2024 Tweed Shire Australia Day Award nominations for the following categories: 
    • Arts and Culture 
    • Citizen of the Year
    • Community Event of the Year 
    • Senior Ambassador
    • Sporting Achievement (Group and Individual)
    • Volunteer of the Year (Group and Individual)
    • Young Achiever in Community Service 

      with the option to make an ‘Honourable Mention’ to nominees who deserves recognition for their efforts. 

  3. Adopts the changes to the Australia Day Award nominations eligibility criteria. 

  4. Selects the 2024 Australia Day Citizen of the Year, with the alternate of the Young Achiever in Community Service, to be invited to perform the role of 2025 Tweed Shire Australia Day Ambassador at the official Tweed Shire Australia Day Award and Citizenship Ceremony.

The Amendment 1 was Lost

ALTERNATE MOTION 

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that:
 
  1. The minutes of the Tweed Coast Waterways Committee meeting held Wednesday 14 February 2024 be received.

  2. Council notes the recommendations of the Tweed Coast Waterways Committee as follows:

    1. That Council writes to NSW Crown Lands, highlighting the importance of the Jack Evans Boat Harbour training wall to foreshore stability and infrastructure within Tweed Heads, and its critical function in river navigation. Council requests that Crown Lands undertake all necessary engineering investigations into the condition, repair options and costs, and that works to repair the wall be funded and undertaken as a priority.

    2. That Council: Use the tidal inundation mapping to inform the Growth Management Housing Strategy, and that areas affected by future tidal inundation and flooding be discounted from further consideration for future urban development within the strategy. 

    3. That Council notes the Tweed Coast and Waterways Advisory Committee’s serious concerns in relation to environmental issues associated with a number of the areas identified for future urban development.

  3. In response, Council writes to NSW Crown Lands, highlighting the importance of the Jack Evans Boat Harbour training wall to foreshore stability and infrastructure within Tweed Heads, and its critical function in river navigation. Council requests that Crown Lands undertake all necessary engineering investigations into the condition, repair options and costs, and that works to repair the wall be funded and undertaken as a priority.

  4. In response to point 2ii) Council commits to using the tidal inundation mapping to inform the Growth Management Housing Strategy, and to giving serious consideration to areas affected by future tidal inundation and flooding being discounted from the Options being progressed for future urban development within the draft strategy.


The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

Submitted By: Councillor James Owen

COUNCILLOR QUESTION: Councillor Owen asks what is the process required for the Tweed Shire community to have the opportunity to choose how they elect their mayor? Noting that conversations about the 2024 local government elections are in full swing following the announcement by most of the current elected body that they intend to run again. People are contacting me to ask how they can vote for the Tweed Shire mayor in the September election.
 
RESPONSE
Through you Madam Mayor. The Local Government Act prescribes the two ways to choose a Mayor:
  1. By popular vote at an ordinary election; or
  2. By vote among the councillors.
 
The current method adopted by Council is the second method where the Mayor is elected by majority vote by Councillors. Section 228 of the Act gives Councils the power to change how they elect a mayor by seeking approval of its electors at a constitutional referendum.
 
If it’s decided by a constitutional referendum that the Mayor be elected by the electors, that decision takes effect in the next ordinary election after the decision is made.
 
I hope this information has been helpful. For more information Councillors may refer to the management comments of 17 August 2023 Council meeting which answered a previous item on this subject: 11.5 NOM - Cr Owen - Constitutional Referendum to Change Method of Electing Mayor. COUNCILLOR QUESTION: Councillor Owen asks in relation to the 4-laning of Tweed Coast Road from the M1 to Cudgen Road which will service Kings Forest, the new Tweed Valley Hospital and West Kingscliff lands: 1. Whose responsibility is it (local, state, federal) in terms of delivery & funding? 2. What is the current status and what are the next steps?
 
RESPONSE
Through you Madam Mayor. In response to part 1 concerning responsibility and funding, Tweed Coast Road is a local Council managed road. It has regional road status which provides us with annual grant funding from the State for maintenance activities. There is shared management of the interchange with the Pacific Motorway with the State. The proposed upgrading of Tweed Coast Road to 4 lanes from the Chinderah interchange to Grand Parade at Casuarina is a Council responsibility. It has been identified as a priority project in the Tweed Road Development Strategy and is funded in part by developer contributions collected under the Tweed Road Contribution Plan. Council has sought grant funding from State and Federal programs to co-fund the Tweed Coast Road upgrade. There have been various grants available for funding of infrastructure to unlock housing growth and employment, however Council has to date been unsuccessful, as these programs have been considerably oversubscribed. Council can pursue the project without external funding, however it would drain the contribution plan reserves considerably and limit our ability to provide further road upgrades in other areas.

In response to part 2 current status, the project has been split into a number of sections. Section 4 at the Cudgen Road intersection has been completed by the State along with the Tweed Valley Hospital development. Section 2 is the new intersection for Kings Forest Parkway, currently being constructed by Leda’s contractors and forecast to be complete around October this year. Council’s priority for delivery is Sections 5 and 6 between Cudgen Road and the M1, which we need to deliver before 2033 based on traffic modelling associated with the Hospital. Timing for the remaining sections to the south will depend on the progress of the Kings Forest land release and related population and traffic growth. With respect to next steps for Sections 5 and 6 Cudgen to Chinderah, Council is currently preparing detailed engineering designs, preparing consultant reports for aspects such as traffic, flooding, noise, biodiversity and cultural heritage to inform our Environmental Impact Statement and Development Application, we are managing minor road acquisitions along the route, and we are working with major adjacent landholders such as Gales Holdings to ensure compatibility of the project such as future intersections with future masterplanning for West Kingscliff.","isPublic":false,"isPublished":false,"isCurrentItem":false,"meeting":null,"reports":[{"id":17178,"name":"Question on Notice","isUploaded":0,"reportTemplateId":18,"wordTemplateId":8,"pdfMediaFullPath":"stream/TWEED/tmp_b628c41712.pdf","token":"e04dacf8-bee8-4929-bb39-45d4fb34d091","isPublic":true}],"attachments":[],"actionSheets":[],"bookmarks":[{"id":2588,"name":"16","eventId":993,"title":"QON - Cr Owen - Tweed Coast Road 4 Laning","text":"QON - Cr Owen - Tweed Coast Road 4 Laning","startTime":5464,"duration":null,"itemId":22803,"sortOrder":17,"minutesSortOrder":17,"parentId":-1,"additionalParentId":-1}],"minutes":[]},{"id":22804,"name":"QON - Cr Owen - Kirkwood Road and Kennedy Drive Intersections with M1","parentId":21066,"sortOrder":58,"minutesSortOrder":24,"minutesParentId":21066,"outlineNumber":"3","fullOutlineNumber":"12.3.","htmlContent":"

COUNCILLOR QUESTION: Councillor Owen asks: 1. Whose responsibility (local, state federal) are these roads (Kirkwood Road and Kennedy Drive) in in terms of delivery & funding? 2. What is the current status of each and what are the next steps? Noting the increasing frustration from significant delays being experienced by many Tweed Shire residents who have contacted Councillor Brinsmead and myself seeking information on the delivery of these important pieces of road infrastructure.
 
RESPONSE
Through you Madam Mayor. In response to Part 1 concerning responsibility and funding, Kennedy Drive and Kirkwood Road are both local Council managed roads. There is shared management of the interchanges with the Pacific Motorway with the State. The proposed upgrading of these roads is a Council responsibility.  Upgrades to the Kennedy Drive dog bone roundabout at the highway interchange and the western extension of Kirkwood Road have been identified as a priority project in the Tweed Road Development Strategy and are funded in part by developer contributions collected under the Tweed Road Contribution Plan. We intend to seek grant funding from State and Federal programs to co-fund these projects in the future when they are approaching delivery phase.

In response to part 2 current status, Council is currently in discussions with the highway authority Transport for NSW, regarding their masterplanning of the M1 south of the state border, in anticipation of the completion of the 6 laning project in Queensland and potential cross border traffic congestion. The configuration of the Terranora Creek crossing, which is currently limited by a 4 lane bridge is a key consideration for future transport planning, and this sits between our Kennedy Drive and Kirkwood Road projects. Modelling is underway to determine the best configuration and whether a new highway bridge or an additional service road bridge is the preferred approach for the State. COUNCILLOR QUESTION: Councillor Owen asks what is the process to allow secondary dwellings on RU1 & RU2 zoned land in the Tweed Shire? Noting that the Growth Management and Housing Strategy draft Options Paper consultation has recently closed and many residents have contacted Councillor Brinsmead and myself and provided us with feedback on the submission they made with respect to secondary dwellings on RU1 & RU2 zoned
land.
 
RESPONSE
Through you Madam Mayor. I thank Councillor Owen for the question which is what is the process to allow secondary dwellings on RU1 & RU2 zoned land in the Tweed Shire
 
Under the current Tweed LEP’s  2000 and 2014 detached secondary dwellings being a small 60m2 structure like a granny flat are prohibited in the RU1 and RU2 rural zones.
 
This means that at the moment you could not lodge a DA for a detached secondary dwelling on rural land as it would be a prohibited land use.
 
However, an attached dual occupancy of any size is allowed with consent in the rural zones. But the two dwellings have to be physically attached to one another by a common wall.
 
The Draft Options Paper for the Growth Management Housing Strategy canvasses a suggestion that an amendment to the 2000 and 2014 Local Environmental Plan to make Secondary Dwellings (detached) like small granny flats permissible with consent in the RU1 Primary Production and RU2 Rural Landscape zones, subject to meeting certain criteria.
 
Some of the possible controls listed in the Options Paper from page 39 include:
 
  1. The secondary dwelling and main house might have to share a single access point and shared driveway;
  2. 'Secondary Dwellings' would be limited in size to 60m2 (like a granny flat);
  3. The main house and 60m2 secondary dwelling would need to share a single On Site Sewerage Management (OSSM) system.
  4. The main house and 60m2 secondary dwelling would need to be close together to minimise site impacts.
 
If Council want to allow detached secondary dwellings in the rural zones as part of the endorsed actions of Growth Management Housing Strategy Options Paper this concept will advance through to the Growth Management Housing Strategy itself and then ultimately an LEP Amendments to allow detached 60m2 secondary dwellings in the rural zones.  Once the LEP’s are amended people would be able to lodge a DA for a 60m2 detached secondary dwelling which would be considered on its merits at each site.","isPublic":false,"isPublished":false,"isCurrentItem":false,"meeting":null,"reports":[{"id":17187,"name":"Question on Notice","isUploaded":0,"reportTemplateId":18,"wordTemplateId":8,"pdfMediaFullPath":"stream/TWEED/tmp_45242382c2.pdf","token":"269a7efa-bd84-4358-a419-25a48cdf388b","isPublic":true}],"attachments":[],"actionSheets":[],"bookmarks":[{"id":2591,"name":"19","eventId":993,"title":"QON - Cr Owen - Secondary Dwellings on Rural Properties","text":"QON - Cr Owen - Secondary Dwellings on Rural Properties","startTime":5926,"duration":null,"itemId":22806,"sortOrder":20,"minutesSortOrder":20,"parentId":-1,"additionalParentId":-1}],"minutes":[]},{"id":22807,"name":"NOM - Cr Owen - Better Phone Reception in Tweed Shire","parentId":21043,"sortOrder":62,"minutesSortOrder":19,"minutesParentId":21043,"outlineNumber":"2","fullOutlineNumber":"11.2.","htmlContent":"

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Notes the EPA’s Food Organics and Garden Organics (FOGO) position statement to help reduce PFAS chemicals in the environment by clarifying that potential sources, like fibre-based food contact materials, are not placed into FOGO bins.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Chris Jenkins:


"Let’s Pray,

Our Father in Heaven, You are the blessed God, our source of life, wisdom & goodness. 

Despite the many obstacles & difficulties Council often faces, You have also provided Council with so many other good things for which I am truly grateful.

I am grateful for bringing us together for the task that You have called us to do. 

I am grateful for the staff & counsellors within the Tweed Shire Council. 

So many talented & dedicated people that You have put in charge over us to help provide a beautiful & safe place to live & enjoy. Thank You Father.

May our counsellors never be satisfied with a project that is not well done or properly thought out. Father, I pray that with all that is said & done today, will be done in a professional & thoughtful manner, providing the best possible result.

Father, keep us working steadfast & true for the Northern Rivers. 

Support & encourage each of our counsellors, that they may not grow weary or fall short of the task that You have given them to do. 

Give each one of them strength & wisdom to complete a job well done!

Father, You already know the outcome of this meeting… 

So may everyone who is involved, every counsellor, be led by Your Goodness.

So, Father, continue to help and guide us, that we may live to practice the values we know to be true. That Council be transparent in all its dealings today. 

Treating the people of the Tweed with fairness, commitment, planning for their future…with everyone involved: 

So that our Tweed community is even better tomorrow than it is today.

May You answer us in the day we call.

Amen"

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
PROPOSED that: 
 

1.      Development Application DA22/0160 for or multi-dwelling housing (13 townhouses), swimming pools, signage, earthworks and vegetation removal at Lot 5 DP 1030979 No. 18 Kildare Drive, Banora Point be refused for the following reasons:


a.      Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the aim of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 1.2(2)(i) which is to conserve or enhance areas of defined high ecological value. The application which seeks approval for 13 townhouses does not meet the requirements of 1.2(2)(i) as there is insufficient setback to the Lowland Rainforest sufficient to enhance this threatened community.


b.      Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with Tweed DCP Section A19 Biodiversity & Habitat Management Clause 2.2 C1 as the application does not provide:


i.        a sufficient buffer for the listed ecological community of Lowland Rainforest on the site and in the adjoining reserve. The buffer is 10 m instead of the required 30m.

ii.       a sufficient buffer (10m instead of 20m) to protect the moderate to high likelihood of presence of the following threatened fauna:  Greyheaded Flying-fox, Wompoo Fruit dove, Rose-crowned Fruit dove, and White-eared Monarch. The buffer is 10 m instead of the required 20m.


c.      Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with Tweed DCP Section A19 Biodiversity & Habitat Management Section 9 Principal 7 which states:


P7. Small remnants – Small patches of habitat should be retained where possible and measures taken to mitigate edge effects and other relevant threats.

 

The site of this application adjoins a significant reserve and thus constitutes part of an important small remnant. The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that native vegetation loss is not occurring and does not involve negative edge effects.


d.      Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with Tweed DCP Section B3 Banora Point West – Tweed Heads South Section 13 Environment Section as:


i.        This application has not sufficiently demonstrated that the development protects the adjoining reserve in its natural state. The buffer from the listed ecological community of Lowland Rainforest is 10 m instead of the required 30 m (as per Tweed DCP Section A19). The reserve is of ‘Very High’ ecological status. (TVMS 2004 - Ecological Status, (Map 4 of 7) mapping, the 102 Sub-tropical / Warm Temperate Rainforest on Bedrock Substrates vegetation unit.).

ii.       The application fails to demonstrate that public access to the Lowland Rainforest on the site has sufficiently limited public access because the buffer is not the required 30 m as per Tweed DCP Section A19.

iii.      The application fails to retain existing stands of trees to enhance the visual appearance of the development. Over an area of 2,421 square metres lower storey vegetation and many substantial rainforest trees, both over and under 5 m in height, will be removed. These trees include a 14m Red Kamala, 10m Lilly Pilly, 16 m Sandpaper Fig, many Guioa and Macaranga trees(one 16 m high) many other tree species including Tallowwood, Bangalow palm, Native Elm, Silky Oak, Brown Pine, Banyan Fig.


e.      Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with Tweed DCP Section B3 Banora Point West – Tweed Heads South Section 13.2.b.ii which states:

Existing trees should be preserved wherever possible. The siting and layout of a development at the initial design stage should consider the location of trees with a view to their preservation;

The siting and layout of the development at the design stage did not sufficiently consider the location of trees with a view to their preservation. Many substantial rainforest trees both over and under 5 m in height will be removed. These trees include a 14m Red Kamala, 10m Lilly Pilly, 16 m Sandpaper Fig, many Guioa and Macaranga trees(one 16 m high) many other tree species including Tallowwood, Bangalow palm, Native Elm, Silky Oak, Brown Pine, Banyan Fig. A development that had a smaller footprint could have achieved retention of many more trees.


f.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as it relates to the likely impacts of the development, the proposed development will have an unacceptable impact on the environment as it fails to sufficiently protect the threatened fauna ( Greyheaded Flying-fox, Wompoo Fruit dove, Rose-crowned Fruit dove, and White-eared Monarch) and flora (Lowland Rainforest).It also fails to sufficiently protect the adjoining reserve which is of ‘Very High ecological status’ (TVMS 2004 - Ecological Status, (Map 4 of 7) mapping, the 102 Sub-tropical / Warm Temperate Rainforest on Bedrock Substrates vegetation unit.).


g.      Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as it relates to suitability of the site, the proposed development is not suitable for the site as it is of a scale that does not allow sufficient buffer to sufficiently protect the threatened fauna ( Greyheaded Flying-fox, Wompoo Fruit dove, Rose-crowned Fruit dove, and White-eared Monarch) and flora (Lowland Rainforest). For the same reason it also fails to sufficiently protect the adjoining reserve which is of ‘Very High ecological status’ (TVMS 2004 - Ecological Status, (Map 4 of 7) mapping, the 102 Sub-tropical / Warm Temperate Rainforest on Bedrock Substrates vegetation unit.).


h.      Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(d) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as it relates to submission received, the proposed development has attracted 23 submissions, including a petition with 80 signatures opposed to the development.


i.       Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, for the reasons set out in the preceding reasons, the application is not in the public interest.


2.       ATTACHMENT 8 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

 

Cr Byrnes returned to the meeting at 04:47pm.

VOTE AGAINST - Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

Cr James Owen
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
 
RECOMMENDED that Development Application DA22/0797 for alterations & additions to Fingal General Store & Restaurant at Lot 353 DP 755740 No. 50 Main Road, Fingal Head be deferred to enable:

  1. The applicant to discuss their options with staff going forward to see if the applicant is open to amending the current application to achieve the following outcomes:
    1. A compliant existing use rights scenario;
    2. A land use more reflective of a general store, small restaurant (33m2) and with a reduced scale to not be characterised as a type of food industry;
    3. Remove an ancillary development that would give rise to manufacturing of baked goods;
    4. Ensure compliant car parking is provided on site; and
    5. Reduce hours of operation (no early starts that impact neighbours)
It is noted any amended Development Application would require re-exhibition and would significantly affect Development Application assessment times.

The discussions and any amended application are to be lodged as soon as possible to enable the application to be reported back to Council as soon as possible, ideally on or fore the July Council meeting.

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

PROPOSED that Development Application DA22/0797 for alterations & additions to Fingal General Store & Restaurant at Lot 353 DP 755740 No. 50 Main Road, Fingal Head be refused for the following reasons:
 
  1. Pursuant to Division 4.11 of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 – The proposed change of use fails to satisfy Clause 163 of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Regulation 2021 having regard to the extent of intensification and expansion of the use(s).
  2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979  - The proposal, which seeks to expand and intensify existing uses that are otherwise prohibited in the zone, and, which fails to demonstrate that the impacts associated with use of the land will have no adverse amenity impact, is contrary to the aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in clause 1.2(a) effect to the desired outcomes, strategic principles, policies and actions contained in the Councils adopted strategy planning documents’ and Clause 1.2(b) to encourage a sustainable local economy and small business, employment, agriculture, affordable housing, recreational, arts, social, cultural, tourism and sustainable industry opportunities appropriate to Tweed.
  3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 - The proposal is contrary to the objectives of the R2 – Residential Low Density zone as set out in Clause 2.3 of Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 to enable other land uses that provide facilities or services to meet the day to day needs of residents.
  4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 - The proposal does not comply with the limitation under Clause 7, Schedule 1 of Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 given the dining area of the Restaurant exceeds 33sqm.
  5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 - The development fails to satisfy existing use provisions and includes aspects of land use that is characterised as a type of land use that is prohibited in the zone.
  6. Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 - The application has failed to demonstrate that the operation of the premises will not have adverse impact on the amenity of the neighbouring properties, particularly in relation to noise and carparking impacts.
  7. Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 - The extent of the alterations and additions and proposed use of the premises is not suitable for the subject site having regard to its proximity to residences, the zoning of the land and the likely amenity impacts resulting from both.
  8. Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 - The proposed alterations and additions to Fingal General Store are not enabled by any part of the statutory planning framework that applies to this site and the development poses unacceptable amenity impacts (noise and carparking). For these reasons, the proposal is not considered to be in the public interest.
  9. Pursuant to Clause 2.48 of SEPP (Transport and Infrastructure) 2021, agency referral comments have not been received by Essential Energy and therefore Council cannot be satisfied that the development satisfies these provisions.
  10. ATTACHMENT 7 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

 

The Amendment 1 was Lost

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
PROPOSED that:
 
  1. Development Application DA23/0438 for a change of use of fill material and delivery method on an approved fill site at Lots 1-9 DP 781714 and Lots 11-14 DP 871753 Turnock Street, Kingscliff be refused for the following reasons:
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the aim of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 1.2(2)(i) which is to conserve or enhance areas of defined high ecological value. The application which seeks approval for change of fill material does not meet the requirements of 1.2(2)(i) as there is insufficient information to adequately determine runoff impacts on the Wallum Froglet habitat and adjoining Coastal Wetlands.
  2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 1.2(2)(c) which is to promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed's natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways, visual amenity and scenic routes, built environment, and cultural heritage.
  3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 5.21(2)(a) Flood Planning. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it is compatible with the flood function and behaviour on the land.
  4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 5.21(2)(b) Flood Planning. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it will not adversely affect flood behaviour and result in detrimental impacts on external properties. 
  5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 5.21(2)(c) Flood Planning. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it will not affect the existing evacuation routes.
  6. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 5.21(2)(e) Flood Planning. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it will not adversely affect the environment or cause avoidable siltation or destruction of riparian vegetation.
  7. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 5.21(3)(a) Flood Planning. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that the development will not adversely affect flood behaviour in predicted climate change scenarios.
  8. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 7.2(3)(a) Earthworks. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it will not have a detrimental impact on drainage patterns and soil stability of the site.
  9. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 7.2(3)(c) Earthworks. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated the quality of the fill and the ability to ensure it is free of Red Imported Fire Ants.
  10. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 7.2(3)(d) Earthworks. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it will not have a detrimental impact on the existing and likely amenity of the adjoining properties.
  11. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 7.2(3)(e) Earthworks. The change of fill application has not sufficiently identified the source of the fill material.
  12. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 7.6(3)(a) Stormwater Management. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it maximises water permeable surfaces with regard to water infiltration.
  13. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 7.6(3)(c) Stormwater Management. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it avoids any significant adverse impacts from stormwater runoff on adjoining properties.
  14. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the SEPP Resilience and Hazards 2021 Chapter 2 Coastal Management 2.8. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it will not significantly impact on:
     (a)      the biophysical, hydrological or ecological integrity of the adjacent coastal wetland or littoral rainforest, or
     (b)      the quantity and quality of surface and ground water flows to and from the adjacent coastal wetland or littoral rainforest.
  15. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with Tweed DCP Section A3-Development of Flood Liable Land as the application does not sufficiently demonstrate it will not adversely impact on flood behaviour of surrounding properties.
  16. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with Tweed DCP Section A19 Biodiversity & Habitat Management Section 9. The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that additional sediment runoff caused by using clay based fill material will not adversely impact on protected vegetation.
  17. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the currently adopted Kingscliff Catchment and Drainage Management Plan in that it does not ensure that fill with an appropriate level of porosity is used throughout this development.
  18. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with Tweed DCP Section 26 Kingscliff as it does not protect and strengthen ecologically significant land. 
  19. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as it relates to the likely impacts of the development, the proposed development may have an unacceptable impact on the environment as it fails to sufficiently protect the threatened fauna, Wallum froglet, previously reported on the site.
  20. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as it relates to the likely impacts of the development and the environmental impacts on both the natural and built environments and social and economic impacts in the locality. The proposed development will have an unacceptable impact on the environment as it fails to sufficiently protect the amenity of the residents with regards to traffic impacts of the change in haul route.
  21. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as it relates to the suitability of the site for the change of fill and change of haul route development. The application has not sufficiently demonstrated that non-sand fill is suitable for this coastal environment.
  22. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(d) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as it relates to submissions received, the proposed development has attracted 25 submissions opposed to the development, raising concerns with flooding and amenity impacts on existing residents that have not been sufficiently addressed.
  23. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, for the reasons set out in the preceding reasons, the application is not in the public interest.
