[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RECOMMENDED that Council:
 

A.      Refuses the application to progress the planning proposal to the Gateway Determination for the following reasons:

 

1.      The proposal fails to meet the strategic merit assessment required by the Urban Growth Area Variation Principles in the following ways:

 

i.       It is inconsistent with the North Coast Regional Plan 2041(NCRP) which did not include this site in its mapping of urban boundaries AND is diametrically opposed to Objective 8 of this Strategy which is to “support the productivity of agricultural land AND is directly in opposition to strategy 8.1 which states “Local Planning should protect and maintain Agricultural productive capacity in the Region by directing urban, rural residential and other incompatible uses away from Important Farmland”.

 

ii.      The proposal is directly inconsistent with 9.1 Ministerial Direction 9.4 which specifically states that a Planning proposal must not rezone land identified as State or Regionally significant farmland for urban or rural residential purposes unless it is consistent with the NCRP or the Northern Rivers Farmland Protection Project 2005 (NRFPP). Consistency has failed to be demonstrated in both instances.

 

iii.     The proposal is directly inconsistent with the Tweed Local Strategic Planning Statement 2020 (LSPS) part 6.6 which requires that “Review land-use planning to support community access to educational and hospital or related health care services and to leverage economic benefits and new education or health sector business opportunities outside of the significant farmland areas.” The LSPS is consistent with the NCRP in protecting SSF and as such is a valid planning consideration.

 

iv.     The proposal is directly inconsistent with the Tweed DCP Section B26 Kingscliff Strategy 2.13(3) Reinforce the s.9.1 Ministerial Farmland Protection Direction by retain the rural zoning and agricultural primacy of these agricultural land holdings.

 

v.      The proposal is inconsistent with the strategies outlined in the Tweed Community Strategic Plan 2017-2027 (CSP) Section 1.4 Managing community growth to protect and enhance productive farmland.

 

vi.     The proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Sustainable Agriculture Strategy 2016 Objective 1 that “Prime agricultural land is preserved for sustainable primary production and land-use conflicts are avoided or managed” and actions including:

 

1.1.1            Ensure the on-going protection of prime agricultural land

1.1.2            Minimise land use conflicts between agriculture and other land uses

1.1.3            Increase utilisation of prime agricultural land for agricultural purposes

 

2.      The proposal fails to meet Important Farmland variation principle of Contiguity with Urban Land. Although the site is close to urban land, primarily to the west, the majority of the surrounding land is not classified as "urban land”. It is essential to emphasize that the SP2 zone, despite its proximity, does not fall under the category of an "urban zone”. The site is bounded by Important farmland to the north and south.

 

3.      The proposal has not demonstrated a sound evidence base addressing agricultural capability and sustainability. Specifically, the proposal has:

 

a.      Misrepresented the Agricultural Capability of the site with the Agricultural Land Assessment and Agricultural Capacity Report significantly underestimating the site's true agricultural capabilities and inconsistently reporting the arable land available on the site.

 

b.      Conducted only a limited crop assessment and fails to consider appropriate small scale agricultural uses such as intensive small cropping.

 

c.      Significantly underestimates economic potential.

 

d.      Overemphasises chemical usage constraints and fails to consider use of less restrictive chemical control methods.

 

e.      Failed to consider the precedent this parcel may create in eroding the protection of surrounding Important Farmland.

 

4.      The proposal fails to meet the site specific merit assessment in that it fails to consider the finite nature of Important Farmland as a resource.  Tweed has only 104ha of state significant farmland and this proposal would sterilise 5.6ha or 5%.

 

5.      The proposal fails to meet the site specific merit assessment in that it fails to provide appropriate Land Use Conflict buffers. The neighbouring special infrastructure development of the Tweed Valley Hospital provided a 30m buffer from Important farmland but the current proposal provides only 10m, which is inadequate for small crop uses.

 

6.      The proposal fails to meet the site specific merit assessment in that it fails to protect and provide the 30m buffer required for listed Ecologically Endangered Community Lowland Rainforest located on the north of the site and Coastal Wetland areas. It also fails to protect the Far North Floodplain Swamp Oak Paperbark forest remnant located on the east of the site.

 

7.      The proposal fails to give regard to the services or infrastructure that will be required to be available to meet the demand generated by this proposal. Specifically, water supply infrastructure requirements and traffic impacts have not been adequately assessed.

 

8.      The proposal fails to meet other strategic merit considerations in that it has not provided any strategic assessment to demonstrate need for a 119 bed private hospital in this location, nor has it considered or given regard to the impacts this proposal may have on the existing approved surrounding uses such as service providers, Tweed Valley Hospital, John Flynn private hospital 18kms to the north and Tweed Day Surgery.


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Cr Nola Firth

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle of the Living Waters Church, Tumbulgum:


"1 Timothy 2:1-4 (TPT)
Most of all, I’m writing to encourage you to pray with gratitude to God. Pray for all men with all forms of prayers and requests as you intercede with intense passion. And pray for every political leader and representative, so that we would be able to live tranquil, undisturbed lives, as we worship the awe-inspiring God with pure hearts. It is pleasing to our Saviour-God to pray for them. He longs for everyone to embrace his life and return to the full knowledge of the truth.
 
 
Dear Lord, 
 
Today as decisions are being made as to direction of our shire, according to your word, we pray and give thanks for those you have placed in authority to govern our shire. We thank you that the decisions they make, in godly reverence, will cause us to live in peace. 
May they be led by your Holy Spirit especially in the tough decisions and help them to find the truth of each situation so they can govern well.
 
We ask that your peace will reign over their personal lives and families and thank you for the personal sacrifice they have each given to represent us in Council.
 
We ask this in Jesus name 
 
Amen."

REASON FOR CONFIDENTIALITY

Local Government Act
This report is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, which permits the meeting to be closed to the public for business relating to the following: 

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law



Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that:

  1. Council notes that the Minister has not approved the proposed grant of a five (5) year lease to the Cabarita Beach Pony Club Grounds Committee Inc over Council-managed Crown Land at 12 Round Mountain Road, Bogangar, Lot 2 DP1254230 ("Property").

  2. Council notes that the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council has lodged an Aboriginal Land Claim pursuant to the Aboriginal Land Rights Act 1983 (NSW) over the Property. 

  3. Council responds to the Department's Aboriginal Land Claims Assessment Team providing documentary evidence that as at the date of the Aboriginal Land Claim the Property was lawfully used or occupied or needed or likely to be needed for an essential public purpose.

  4. Council seeks the New South Wales Local Aboriginal Land Council's written consent to grant the Cabarita Beach Pony Club Grounds Committee Inc a twelve (12) month short-term licence pursuant to s.2.20 of the Crown Land Management Act 2016 (NSW).  

  5. Should the New South Wales Local Aboriginal Land Council consent to the grant of the twelve (12) month short-term licence to the Cabarita Beach Pony Club Grounds Committee Inc, Council approves an authorised delegate to execute the proposed twelve (12) month short-term licence with Cabarita Beach Pony Club Grounds Committee Inc. 

  6. ATTACHMENTS 1-2 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

The Motion was Carried

ALTERNATE MOTION
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that Council submits a review request to the Geographical Naming Board in relation to the desired naming of the unnamed walkway next to 25 Viking Street, Kingscliff as Fay Walk. 
The review requested reconsideration to be on the basis that the NSW state government has classified the Tweed Shire as a Metropolitan area in their health and education systems under the Modified Monash Model and as such, there is an argument that the criteria for testing whether a street name is too similar to that in a neighbouring location should be limited to consideration of a 10km radius only. 
The nominated streets raised by the Geographical Naming Board are in very different geographical areas of the Shire and at Kay Street, Murwillumbah and Bay Street Tweed Heads, and as such there is no danger of confusion with Fay Walk.

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase

ALTERNATE MOTION 

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that:

  1. The Minutes of the Floodplain Management Advisory Committee Meeting held Friday 22 March 2024 be received by Council, and

  2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:
Agenda Item 1.  Tweed Valley Flood Study Update and Expansion
The Floodplain Management Advisory Committee RESOLVED that the outcomes from meeting with Rural Industries’ Stakeholders 20 March 2024 be actioned as follows:
  1. Ask CSIRO if they can resource a parallel study to their Richmond project for Tweed and confirm timeframes for their Richmond flood study project.
  2. Follow up with State and Federal MPs seeking NEMA funding through the responsible Minister for a Tweed CSIRO study.
  3. Pursue grant funding for sensitivity analysis of LiDAR and bathymetry datasets to be received from CSIRO, expected in July 2024.
  4. Move quickly to a risk management study (TVFRMS) following adoption of the TVFSU&E.
  5. Build transparency into the review of all options in TVFRMS, including discounted options or things previously considered unviable.
  6. Community participation in identifying and prioritising options in the TVFRMS be undertaken prior to the draft study formulation and exhibition.
  7. Follow up on request to Transport for NSW for a 2022 Flood Impact Review for the M1 Pacific Highway (Tumbulgum, Chinderah, Burringbar, Mooball, Crabbes Creek).
  8. Table State Government (‘Culleton’ and ‘MEMS’) reports on rural floodplain drainage to Floodplain Management Committee.
Agenda Item 4.  Grant Applications
The Floodplain Management Advisory Committee RESOLVED that the information provided about the grant applications be accepted.
  1. Flood Recovery and Resilience Grants Program (just closed): Murwillumbah CBD Levee Spillway Upgrade.
  2. 2024/25 Floodplain Management Program: Tweed Valley Floodplain Risk Management Study and Plan Update.
  3. Round 2 Disaster Resilience Fund: Tweed Valley Flood Study Update and Expansion Sensitivity Analysis – CSIRO LiDAR and Bathymetry Datasets. 

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

RECOMMENDED that:

b.   Notes the unanimous recommendation made to Council in the Floodplain Management Advisory Committee that: No more rezoning for residential purposes takes place in the Tweed Shire below the PMF (Probably Maximum Flood) level.

 

c.   Requests a workshop with the Floodplain Management Advisory Committee, staff and Councillors and an appropriate Department of Planning representative, on the possible ramifications of enacting the recommendation made by the Floodplain Management Advisory Committee to allow consideration of this as an option going forward in managing Tweed Shire Flooding risk.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Owen asks in relation to Council's legal services costs, per year, for the last two terms of Council:

  1. What was the budget for legal services?
  2. What is the annual spend on legal services?

The Director Corporate Services replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, in responding to the question, the following is provided as context in relation to this Question with Notice. Specifically, it provides context for Council’s budgeting process and more specifically the budget for legal expenses:

  • The annual budgeting and Long Term Financial Plan process determines the annual legal services budget based on the previous year’s original budget plus CPI rather than the actual expenditure at the end of the previous year. For legal expenses, past actual costs do not provide an accurate guide to future costs. As a result adjustments are made where expenses exceed the original budget during the year through Quarterly Budget Reviews.

  • There are a range of external or unknown factors which influence the risk of legal action. For example, the actions of applicants (for development applications) and the community (for compliance matters).

  • The annual original budget for legal expenses is similar to other services that are over or under expended at the end of the financial year, but remain within Council’s total original budget for the financial year. In accordance with our Integrated Planning and Reporting (IP&R) responsibilities and requirements of section 203 of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, Council undertakes quarterly budget reviews which are presented to Council for approval.

Legal Services Register Report

A ‘Legal Services Register Report’ is presented to Council on a quarterly basis. It provides the status of legal instructions for current or recently completed matters which have been issued to legal panel providers. Key financial information is included such as legal service provider expenditure and the budget for this expenditure.

I have gathered the information to respond to your question from these reports. I will provide a budget figure as at the beginning the financial year and at the end of the financial year as this figure is subject to change.

Points to note in these figures:

  • The last two terms of Council does not neatly fit into financial years. Figures for the 2016/17 financial year are therefore provided, where I note that the Council term started on 11 November 2016, when the election was declared.

  • There are years where the actual expenditure exceeded the budgeted expenditure. While the budget is an important aspect of financial management, a negative variation between actual and budget for one specific item is not necessarily a concern. It is one piece of financial information that needs to be considered with all other financial information to have an informed understanding of our organisation’s financial health.

  • Only the budget for the 2023/24 financial year is provided.

  • Council increased the legal services budget by $500k ongoing from 23/24.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Owen asks:

  1. What is the timeline for the feasibility study into the new indoor sports complex and 50 metre Olympic-sized pool?
  2. What progress has been made on it since the 21 March Council meeting?

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, with regards the timeline for the feasibility study, Officers are currently drafting the scope and brief for the site analysis, investigations, concept plans and feasibility study, which tenders will be called for. Officers are aiming to have the study delivered within 12-months, pending the response of the tender process. 
 
Since the March Council meeting, Officers have undertaken the following:
  • held internal meetings to preplan the project stages and next steps;

  • held preliminary meetings with potential external contractors and professional services to determine the appropriate scope of works to be tendered for;

  • held preliminary discussions with State Sporting Bodies (Basketball, Netball) to discuss support and advocacy; and

  • progressed with seeking legal advice on a potential ‘Public Private Partnership’.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Owen asks what are the future plans to address the traffic congestion at Kennedy Drive?

Director Engineering replied:

Through you Madam Mayor.
Kennedy Drive is a local Council managed road. As outlined at the April meeting, upgrades to signalise the Kennedy Drive dog bone roundabout at the Pacific Motorway interchange have been identified as a priority project in the Tweed Road Development Strategy, are part funded by the Tweed Road Contribution Plan, and we are currently in discussions with Transport for NSW to engage a traffic modeller to test the design and staging of the Kennedy Drive interchange. This work will need to be compatible with planned highway upgrades by the State in the future.

Council will note that the project to 4-lane Kennedy Drive west of the motorway was completed several years ago, however this does not alleviate peak hour congestion at the interchange. Both authorities are aware of the current extent of these queues in the morning and afternoon.

Stategically, the Tweed distributor road network relies on the future connection of Cobaki Parkway between Piggabeen Road and Boyd Street in Queensland as a western bypass and alternative to Kennedy Drive for West Tweed and Bilambil Heights traffic to access the Gold Coast. Unfortunately Council does not control the timing for delivery of this key piece of road infrastructure, and it is a considerable upfront cost to be borne by the developer.

Until Cobaki Parkway comes on line, Council has imposed a cap on traffic generating development in the catchment west of Cobaki Creek Bridge, to limit impacts of growth on Kennedy Drive. This has been in place for over 20 years, with the intent it should not be lifted until Cobaki Parkway is in place. This cap is currently under review due to growing pressures from landholders in this area, and will be presented to Council later in the year for further consideration.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Owen asks what is the process to move to a wards based system for the Tweed Shire Council?

Director Corporate Services replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, the process for a ward-based system is set out in the legislation.
 
The Local Government Act (Act) requires a constitutional referendum should Council wish to divide its area into wards. Specifically, section 16(a) of the Act states: 
 
'A council may not do any of the following unless approval to do so has been given at a constitutional referendum'.
      (a) divide its area into wards or abolish all wards in its area. This is reiterated in section 210(5) of the Act with regard to “Division of areas into wards”.
 
If Council resolves to conduct a constitutional referendum it must comply with the notification requirements contained in Schedule 10 of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 with regard to “Constitutional referendums and council polls”.
 
Councils are responsible for the preparation and publicity of the required explanatory material. Councils must ensure this material presents a balanced case both for and against any proposition to be put to a constitutional referendum.
 
Council resolved to engage the NSW Electoral Commission to administer the 14 September 2024 election. If a constitutional referendum or council poll is to be held in conjunction with an election of councillors, the general manager must notify the Electoral Commissioner of the question to be asked at the referendum or poll. The NSW Electoral Commission have advised that ‘should Council decide to proceed with a referendum, they would require a copy of the relevant resolution as soon as possible and then we would require the final question(s) by the end of June 2024’.
 
The current fee estimate from the NSW Electoral Commission does not include a provision for a constitutional referendum. The NSW Electoral Commission have advised that ‘to conduct a referendum in conjunction with the councillor elections there will be an approximate uplift of 10% in the total cost of the election.’ That would be approximately $88,797.
 
From a post-election standpoint, if elector approval was obtained from a constitutional referendum, and before dividing its area into wards, a council must undertake the consultation required by section 210A of the Act. This includes consulting with the Electoral Commissioner and the Australian Statistician together with public exhibition of the proposal. 
 
Changes to wards approved at a constitutional referendum conducted in September 2024 would come into effect for the electoral term commencing in September 2028.

Councillors, in considering the process to move to a ward system would need to take into account other requirements under the legislation and the impacts thereof.
 
There is a need to be mindful that moving to a ward system may necessitate consideration of an increase to the number of councillors as per section 224A(9) of the Local Government Act that states:
(9) A council for an area that is divided into wards may not make an application under this section for a decrease in the number of councillors that would result in the number of councillors for each ward being fewer than 3. 

For example, this may require consideration of 3 wards of 3 councillors each.
 
Alternatively, consideration could be given to moving to a popularly elected mayor and 2 wards of 3 councillors in each. 
 
Either approach would require additional referendum question as per sections 16(a),(b),(c); and Section 224 of the Local Government Act 1993 as well as budget allocation. If increasing the number of Councillors, additional recurring costs will need to be factored into the Long Term Financial Plan to account for Councillor allowances and expenses.
 
Further, Council needs to determine the method for electing Councillors in a ward system as per Section 16(d) of the Local Government Act. Sections 280 and 281 that prescribe the two methods available for consideration. These are method 1: Ward election of councillors, and method 2: Election of councillors partly by wards.
 
If Council were of the mind to pursue method 2, a further referendum would be required as per section 279 (2) of the Local Government Act 1993 (extract below). This would require additional funding for the electoral commission to undertake.

 
Cr Polglase temporarily left the meeting at 05:00pm.
Cr Polglase returned to the meeting at 05:03pm.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks can we please have a detailed update on the actions taken to date by Tweed Shire Council since the resolution of February 15, 2024, titled 'Tweed CBD'.

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, Officers across a number of business units have progressed a range of initiatives including:

Graffiti removal
Council increased the graffiti removal budget at the December quarterly budget review to fund a dedicated graffiti removal crew for six months. Equipment has been ordered to provide a modern and compact ute-based gurney system.  The team are expected to commence within the next couple of weeks.
 
Audit of Tweed CBD & Surrounding Streets (Wharf & Bay Streets), Parks and Infrastructure
An audit of the CBD was undertaken on the 28th March resulting in a number of actions to follow up.  In response to this immediate actions have been undertaken, including:
  1. The replacement of non-working street lights on Wharf Street
  2. Removal of various seats
  3. Regular weekday trolley collections with approximately 260 trollies collected within the first 4 weeks. 
Bus Shelter
A tender has been awarded for the demolition and replacement of the northbound and southbound bus shelters and nearby taxi shelter, all located at the northern end of Wharf St adjacent to Bay Street.  The scope of work also includes the replacement of various sections of footpath and lighting. The estimated contract commencement date is 29 May, and completion mid-late September 2024.
 
Safety Audit
Tweed Byron Police advised they do not have the capacity to undertake a review of the 2016 Jack Evans Boat Harbour safety audit, however suggested a walkthrough with staff similar to the CBD audit recently undertaken.
 
The Police and Council, through the Rangers team, recently undertook a joint operation to target and reduce anti-social behaviour in the Tweed CBD. 
 
A tender has also been awarded for the construction of the Jack Evans Boat Harbour Places to Swim project, and the Goorimahbah Stage 2 project was officially opened in March, both of which aim to beautify and activate the Tweed CBD.
 
In relation to the Community Infrastructure Development (CID) funding, Officers have been advised the Tweed Chamber of Commerce’s funding application was unsuccessful, however staff will continue to work on initiatives, such as tree light wrapping and banner signage, as funds allow.
 

Cr Byrnes temporarily left the meeting at 05:06pm.



","isPublic":false,"isPublished":false,"isCurrentItem":false,"meeting":null,"reports":[{"id":17495,"name":"Question on Notice","isUploaded":0,"reportTemplateId":18,"wordTemplateId":8,"pdfMediaFullPath":"stream/TWEED/tmp_f1fb228cfc.pdf","token":"0e04c070-20d2-49a6-bd48-4deca67495a5","isPublic":true}],"attachments":[],"actionSheets":[],"bookmarks":[{"id":2641,"name":"18","eventId":994,"title":"QON - Cr Brinsmead - Tweed CBD NOM Update","text":"QON - Cr Brinsmead - Tweed CBD NOM Update","startTime":5666,"duration":null,"itemId":22986,"sortOrder":22,"minutesSortOrder":22,"parentId":-1,"additionalParentId":-1}],"minutes":[]},{"id":22989,"name":"NOM - Cr Owen - Help for Giant Devil's Fig and Giant Parramatta Grass in Tweed Shire","parentId":21080,"sortOrder":61,"minutesSortOrder":61,"minutesParentId":21080,"outlineNumber":"2","fullOutlineNumber":"11.2.","htmlContent":"
  [OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL] [AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"
Cr James Owen
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
 
RESOLVED that Council:
  1. Notes:
    1. The significant impacts that Giant Devil's Fig and Giant Parramatta Grass are having on Tweed Shire farms and rural properties.
    2. The significant costs of trying to manage these weeds - in the tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars every year.
    3. That Giant Devil's Fig is listed in the North Coast Regional Strategic Weed Management Plan 2023-2027 in the 'Containment' management category.
    4. That Giant Parramatta Grass is not listed as a North Coast region priority weed.
    5. That there is naturally occurring biological control for Giant Parramatta Grass in the form of a fungi called 'nigrospora oryzae' that is recognised by the NSW Department of Primary Industries.

  2. Writes to:
    1. The following:
      • Minister for Agriculture and Minister for Regional New South Wales.
      • Shadow Minister for Agriculture and Minister for Regional New South Wales.
      • Shadow Minister for Agriculture.
      • Minister for Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry.
      • Member for Richmond.
      • Member for Lismore.
      • Member for Tweed.

    2. Asks them to:
      • Include Giant Parramatta Grass in the North Coast Regional Strategic Weed Management Plan 2023-2027 in the 'Containment/Eradication' management category.
      • Raise Giant Devil's Fig to the 'Eradication' category.
      • Provide additional funding for farmers, Council and rural landowners to contain and eradicate these weeds, and undertake local research and education.
      • Visit farmers and rural landowners in Tweed Shire affected by these weeds and understand the issues they are facing.
      • Urgently consider approving nigrospora oryzae as a biological control agent for Giant Parramatta Grass.

  3. That Council develop an appropriate communication campaign including, but not limited to inclusion in the rates notices to ensure that the message gets out to the community regarding these noxious weeds.

  4. That this issue be tabled at a forthcoming Northern Rivers Joint Organisation meeting.

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks what are the future plans for Tom Beaston Outlook commonly known as Razorback, including, but not limited to upkeep and maintenance, remedial works and vegetation repair/maintenance including weed management?

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, a habitat restoration plan has been drafted for the site.  Finalisation of which is pending consultation with the Tweed Byron Local Aboriginal Land Council.  The intention for working closely with Aboriginal Land Council is to ensure Council suitably addresses the cultural significance of the site as part of any habitat restoration works.  There is no funding for additional weed management works, however preparing the plan may assist Council in obtaining external funding.  The site is very steep, making access for bushland restoration difficult. In addition, the majority of the weed management required occurs on private land.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that Council requests an urgent meeting with the NSW Minister for Health, the NSW Minister for Lands and Property and our State member to discuss the future of the Tweed heads Hospital site including the need to:
 
  1. Retain a range of medical services and allied health services including Early Childhood Development, Mental Health Services and Community health at the Tweed Heads Hospital site

  2. Make part of the site available to a Common Ground, Housing first facility to ensure those on the lowest and medium low incomes in our Shire have access to safe and secure housing with wrap around support services.

  3. Make part of the site available for essential worker housing for the Tweed Valley Hospital and other essential services.

  4. Include Aged care facilities within the new development of this site.

The Motion was Carried

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr James Owen
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
 
RESOLVED that

A. That the Review of Determination confirms the reasons for refusal for the original Development Application No. DA22/0542 for extension to an existing storage premises. The reasons for refusal (including a new reason for refusal No. 2) are as follows: 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, storage premises are prohibited in Zone RU2 under Clause 2.3 of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014. Furthermore, pursuant to Division 4.11 Existing uses of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 and Clause 164 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2021 the land proposed under this application for use as an enlargement, expansion, or intensification of the storage premises as an ‘existing use’ is not considered to be land on which any existing storage premises use has been historically and lawfully carried out. 
  2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 – storage premises are prohibited in the RU2 Rural Landscape zone, under the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014. 
  3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 - The application has not provided adequate information to satisfy Council the application complies with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014. The application has not demonstrated compliance with the following clauses: a. Clause 1.2 - The proposed development is not considered to be in accordance with the aims of this plan. The proposed development would not give effect to the desired outcomes, strategic principles, policies, and actions contained in the Council’s adopted strategic planning documents. b. Clause 2.3 -The proposed development is not considered to be in accordance with the objectives of the RU2 Rural Landscape zone, as identified under the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014. c. Clause 5.21 - The application has not provided adequate information as to whether the development is compatible with the flood function and behaviour on the land and will not adversely affect flood behaviour in a way that results in detrimental increases in the potential flood affectation of other development or properties.
  4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 - The application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate the application complies with Section A2 – Site Access and Parking Code. The application has not demonstrated that adequate parking is provided on site or submitted swept path diagrams proving that there is sufficient space to safely manoeuvre vehicles through the site while vehicles are parked adjacent to storage units. 
  5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 - The application has not provided adequate information to satisfy Council the site is suitable for the proposed development. The application has not provided adequate information to satisfy Council as to the site’s suitability for the development with regards to land zoning, bushfire hazard and flooding. 
  6. Pursuant to Section 4.15C(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 - On the basis of the information submitted, the development proposal, is not considered to be in the public interest.

B. Council write to the applicant and suggest they consider lodging a Planning Proposal to enable “self storage facility” and/or  “storage facility” to be a permitted land use at Lot 2 DP 863736 No. 942 Cudgera Creek Road, Cudgera Creek, and Council will use its best endeavours to prioritise the assessment of such planning proposal. 

C.  ATTACHMENT 8 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:
(e) information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law     


The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None

CONFIDENTIAL COMMITTEE

REPRESENTATIONS FOR ITEMS CONSIDERED IN COMMITTEE
(Sec 3.40, 13.9 to 13.17 Model Code of Meeting Practice)

Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.
 
EXCLUSION OF PRESS AND PUBLIC

REASON FOR CONFIDENTIALITY

Local Government Act
This report is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, which permits the meeting to be closed to the public for business relating to the following: 

(g)     advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege


ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RECOMMENDED that Council:

  1. Acknowledge previous correspondence dated 20 April 1998 that development consent for Tanglewood Stage 5 (as amended) – S18F/624 remains in force;

  2. Acknowledge previous correspondence dated 3 August 1998 that development consent for Tanglewood Stage 5 (as amended) - S18F/624 relates to 19 lots, and that the relevant plan is OG134C titled Proposed Stage 5A prepared by John P Marendy & Associates (undated);

  3. Confirm that as a consent that is recognised and which has not lapsed that the lodgement of a future modification application to amend the consent (S18F/624) is a valid pathway forward;

  4. Request the Proponent to demonstrate the constructed infrastructure is fit for purpose (or how it will be made fit for purpose) including any additional works as deemed necessary by Council and is compliant with current engineering standards.

  5. Advise the Proponent that further approvals will be required if acting on the consent for vegetation removal where not already approved for infrastructure construction and further approvals for replacement of infrastructure will be required.

  6. Advise the proponent that existing vegetation, the existing fragmented zoning across the site and the proposed Conservation Zones on this property, as previously exhibited in 2021 may impact on the viability of any future lots being capable of accommodating a dwelling house even with the subdivision being acknowledged.

  7. ATTACHMENTS 1 to 8 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:

(g)    advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege


The Motion was Carried on the Casting Vote of the Mayor.

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

  [OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL] [AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that:
 
  1. Council acknowledges the impact the extended closure of the Murwillumbah CBD multistorey carpark is having on parking in the Murwillumbah CBD and the flow on impacts for businesses in our town.
 
  1. Council advises that we are working with the original builder of the carpark and our insurers to have some forensic engineering testing done to determine whether the structure can be repaired and we are hopeful that it will be.
 
  1. Council advises Council is currently working to get approval from our insurer to open up 70 additional carparking spaces plus two parking with disability bays that are not impacted by the structural damage.
 
  1. Council refers the matter to the Local Traffic Committee to consider the impact of releasing 72 additional parking bays in the multi-storey carpark and to assess other options to increase parking bays in the CBD and investigation of interim measures to relieve parking put forward by Murwillumbah businesses.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd of the Presbyterian Church in Tweed Heads.

Gracious God, 
 
World Environment Day yesterday reminded us again of the natural beauty that surrounds us.  We are thankful to live in such a wonderful part of the world, to be able to enjoy it every day, and to echo your exclamation of ‘very good!’.
We recognise the work and wisdom of the peoples of Bundjalung Country who have cared for this land for so long.  
We are also thankful for the many people in our community who have a passion to care for, restore, and protect our natural environment.  
 
And yet we also acknowledge its capacity to bring harm and grief through natural disasters.  We value the resilience of our Councillors and Council staff who have had to deal with a long series of traumatic events and be the centre of our community’s recovery.  Be with all those who continue to grieve or carry a weight of fatigue.
 
Bless Council as they navigate complex issues to make wise decisions that enable future generations to enjoy our natural environment even further.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RECOMMENDED that:
 
A.  Development Application DA23/0438 for a change of use of fill material and delivery method on an approved fill site at Lots 1-9 DP 781714 and Lots 11-14 DP 871753 Turnock Street, Kingscliff be refused for the following reasons:

  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the aim of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 1.2(2)(i) which is to conserve or enhance areas of defined high ecological value. The application which seeks approval for change of fill material does not meet the requirements of 1.2(2)(i) as there is insufficient information to adequately determine runoff impacts on the Wallum Froglet habitat and adjoining Coastal Wetlands.
  2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 1.2(2)(c) which is to promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed's natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways, visual amenity and scenic routes, built environment, and cultural heritage.
  3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 5.21(2)(a) Flood Planning. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it is compatible with the flood function and behaviour on the land.
  4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 5.21(2)(b) Flood Planning. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it will not adversely affect flood behaviour and result in detrimental impacts on external properties. 
  5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 5.21(2)(c) Flood Planning. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it will not affect the existing evacuation routes.
  6. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 5.21(2)(e) Flood Planning. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it will not adversely affect the environment or cause avoidable siltation or destruction of riparian vegetation.
  7. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 5.21(3)(a) Flood Planning. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that the development will not adversely affect flood behaviour in predicted climate change scenarios.
  8. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 7.2(3)(a) Earthworks. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it will not have a detrimental impact on drainage patterns and soil stability of the site.
  9. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 7.2(3)(c) Earthworks. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated the quality of the fill and the ability to ensure it is free of Red Imported Fire Ants.
  10. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 7.2(3)(d) Earthworks. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it will not have a detrimental impact on the existing and likely amenity of the adjoining properties.
  11. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 7.2(3)(e) Earthworks. The change of fill application has not sufficiently identified the source of the fill material.
  12. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 7.6(3)(a) Stormwater Management. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it maximises water permeable surfaces with regard to water infiltration.
  13. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 7.6(3)(c) Stormwater  Management. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it avoids any significant adverse impacts from stormwater runoff on adjoining properties.
  14. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the SEPP Resilience and Hazards 2021 Chapter 2 Coastal Management 2.8. The change of fill application has not sufficiently demonstrated that it will not significantly impact on:
      (a)      the biophysical, hydrological or ecological integrity of the adjacent coastal wetland or littoral rainforest, or
     (b)      the quantity and quality of surface and ground water flows to and from the adjacent coastal wetland or littoral rainforest.
  15. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with Tweed DCP Section A3-Development of Flood Liable Land as the application does not sufficiently demonstrate it will not adversely impact on flood behaviour of surrounding properties.
  16. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with Tweed DCP Section A19 Biodiversity & Habitat Management Section 9. The application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that additional sediment runoff caused by using clay based fill material will not adversely impact on protected vegetation.
  17. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with the currently adopted Kingscliff Catchment and Drainage Management Plan in that it does not ensure that fill with an appropriate level of porosity is used throughout this development.
  18. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is inconsistent with Tweed DCP Section 26 Kingscliff as it does not protect and strengthen ecologically significant land. 
  19. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as it relates to the likely impacts of the development, the proposed development may have an unacceptable impact on the environment as it fails to sufficiently protect the threatened fauna, Wallum froglet, previously reported on the site.
  20. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as it relates to the likely impacts of the development and the environmental impacts on both the natural and built environments and social and economic impacts in the locality. The proposed development will have an unacceptable impact on the environment as it fails to sufficiently protect the amenity of the residents with regards to traffic impacts of the change in haul route.
  21. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as it relates to the suitability of the site for the change of fill and change of haul route development. The application has not sufficiently demonstrated that non-sand fill is suitable for this coastal environment.
  22. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(d) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 as it relates to submissions received, the proposed development has attracted 25 submissions opposed to the development, raising concerns with flooding and amenity impacts on existing residents that have not been sufficiently addressed.
  23. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, for the reasons set out in the preceding reasons, the application is not in the public interest.
 
B. ATTACHMENT 5 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains: (e) information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Fr Paul McDonald of St Anthony's Catholic Church, Kingscliff

PRAYER FOR LIGHT AND GRACE

Look kindly Lord
On this group that trusts in You.
During this gathering as we discuss and reflect
On important issues
Help us to hear the voice of your Spirit
And receive your Word in faith.
Give us wisdom in discernment,
Prudence in judgement,
Firmness in decision
And wisdom in planning.
May diversity of views come together in common goals.
May we always act with due concern
For both the present and the future,
Respecting our traditions
But attentive to the signs of the time.
We ask this through Christ our Lord.

Amen.

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, yes when Council first considered the provision of bulky waste collection a number of options were considered including a voucher system.  I refer Councillors to Council Report dated 28 October 2021 for further details.

Currently residents with a red bin can call up a 2 cubic metre kerbside collection twice per year.  This collection option was preferred at the time as it was considered flexible and available to everyone.  A voucher system requires residents to have access to a ute or trailer to transport waste to the Resource Recovery Centre.  This option was also seen to reduce illegal dumping.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks can you please provide an overview of the structure Parks and Active Communities unit?

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, within the Parks and Active Communities Unit there are currently 121.33 full time equivalent staff employed across a number of teams including Aquatic Centres, Parks and Gardens Operations, Community Assets, Open Space Planning and Design, and Rangers.  There are also a number of casual staff who are contracted to Council’s Parks and Gardens Operations team through Spinifex Recruiting, however these numbers fluctuate as they are dependent upon seasonal demand and vacancies within our permanent workforce.  Generally, staff numbers across the Unit are considered to adequately resource Council’s service level requirements with the exception of the Parks and Gardens Operations team. RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 9 May 2024 be received and 

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

7.1.    Coronation Avenue, Pottsville
The removal of additional parking spaces around the existing marked pedestrian crossing was not supported given that the current sight distance of pedestrians with the kerb extensions is adequate. The existing bike/skateboard prohibitive signage for Coronation Avenue, Pottsville is to be upgraded to comply with the Road Regulations and NSW Police have advised that they will monitor enforcement during peak times. Council’s Road Safety Officer to investigate site specific educational signage to increase compliance with the prohibitive signage.

7.2.    Winders Place, Banora Point
That the installation of additional prohibitive signage/linemarking is not supported, however council officers to further monitor the site in consideration of the issues raised.

7.3.    Kennedy Drive, Tweed Heads
That the committee supports:
1. The installation of further physical barriers to prevent the turning from Kennedy Drive, Tweed Heads into the boat ramp carpark. 
2. The installation of bollards on the grassed median near McDonalds Street, Tweed Heads to prevent vehicles entering Kenndy Drive from the slip lane.

7.4.    LATE ITEM: Darlington Drive, Banora Point
This matter was discussed and there is no required action at this stage, to place a road barrier near the round about on Darlington Drive, Banora Point.

7.5.    LATE ITEM: EV Type 2 Destination - charge stations
The following sites for 22kW Type 2 Destination EV Charge stations are supported: 
- 10 Powell Street, Tweed Heads 
- 37 Commercial Road, Murwillumbah 
The proposed site at 1 Pearl Street, Kingscliff, was not supported given the high demand for on street parking and limited on-site parking provision for adjacent businesses. A more suitable location in this vicinity should be considered.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Note the findings and recommendations of the Plan C and UTS Northern Rivers Food Security Resilience Scoping Study, in particular the urgent need for coordinated food system governance, policies and planning in the region to build resilience to disasters and supply chain disruptions.

  2. Note the 'Food Production and Supply in NSW Inquiry and Report (November. 2022), particularly Recommendation 6: "that the NSW Government works with local councils to develop and implement strategies to improve local food systems, and provides appropriate funding as required".

  3. Write to the following NSW Government Ministers requesting the Government's response to the Inquiry and highlighting the importance of Recommendation 6 for communities recovering from disasters such as the Northern Rivers:
    1. NSW Premier the Hon Chris Minns MP;
    2. Minister for Agriculture the Hon Tara Moriarty MP;
    3. Minister for Local Government the Hon Ron Hoenig MP;
    4. Minister for Regional New South Wales and North Coast the Hon Rose Jackson MP;
    5. Minister for Health and Regional Health the Hon Ryan Park MP;
    6. Minister for Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Heritage the Hon Penny Sharpe MP; and
    7. Minister for Aboriginal Affairs and Treaty of New South Wales the Hon David Harris MP.

  4. Note the Northern Rivers Joint Organisation passed a similar motion at it's February meeting.

  5. Consult with the Tweed Rural Land Industry Management Committee and the Community Action Network on what mechanisms could be considered to enable and assist small scale agriculture in the Tweed LGA and how existing Council strategies or approaches are addressing food access, availability and utilisation to improve food security and resilience.

  6. Provide a report to Council outlining feedback from the above.

  7. Consult with the Reconstruction Authority about the potential use of land bought back through the Resilient Homes Program being used for future agricultural uses that could increase food production and access in the Shire.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Warren Polglase
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

ALTERNATE MOTION


Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that Council:

  1. In respect to RFO2023101 - Expressions of Interest Greenhills Lodge Repurpose notes the withdrawal of New South Wales Reconstruction Authority from the proposed use of the site for workers accommodation.

  2. Continues to explore options for future use of the facility with:
    a)  Homes NSW
    b)  Other government agencies and not-for-profit groups that were part of the previous tender process for provision of services at this site.

  3. Proceeds with the further geotechnical investigation of the landslip with a view to undertaking the remediation of the landslip if and when funding for the same become available, retaining the maximum number of rooms feasible during this process.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Owen asks has council investigated Artificial Intelligence to improve service delivery, communications and customer service? 

Director Corporate Services replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, 

Currently, a number of Council’s day-to-day tools, such as the Microsoft suite, already incorporate elements of AI that help streamline work processes and tasks. 

The public can already use AI to seek a range of Council information from our websites and communication information, highlighting the quality and importance of information we provide to the public through our communication channels.  
Our Contact Centre telephony solution utilises AI to automate caller IDs. Moving forward, it also provides options for us to improve direct customer experiences through SMS interactions and other AI options when on a live call with a customer.

Council has recently engaged a Microsoft partner to conduct a Microsoft CoPilot  workshop/s so that we can gain an understanding of the technology and implications for Council including use cases, risks, opportunities and governance requirements.  
 
Governance & Risk

Both the benefits and risks of AI are well summarised in the NSW Govt AI Strategy: “AI provides us with significant potential to transform society and the economy. ... However, because of the speed of technological evolution, the need to meet the highest privacy standards and to address ethical considerations, AI also presents new challenges .... AI needs to be developed responsibly and with clear outcomes focus so that the community has trust that the technology is being used appropriately, that any unintended consequences are avoided or remedied quickly and effectively.

With the growing number of data breaches and other risks in this space, we are adopting a good governance approach to ensure Council meets its obligations to protect our customer data and privacy. 
 
Potential Uses

Some potential uses include speeding up repetitive tasks, automated triaging of enquiries, process improvement and streamlining the preparation of some communications.

Our focus at present remains on implementing the new TechnologyOne cloud-based ERP which incorporates some AI functionality of the solutions such as many new customer service solutions, invoice recognition, and a new Customer Portal to support self-service.  

Given our experience to date with the Department of Planning’s ePlanning Portal, where Tweed was an early adopter, our preference is to continue to focus on working with the Department on delivering the basic functional requirements before venturing into AI for DA assessments.

While AI offers some improved efficiencies in preparing written content and information, it always requires a human review and editing to be relevant and suitable for public use or distribution, and to ensure Council or third parties do not breach copyright.

Cr Byrnes temporarily left the meeting at 4.34pm.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Owen asks in relation to the May Federal Budget, what announcements / funding commitments will Tweed Shire Council benefit from? 

General Manager replies.

Through you Madam Mayor,

Tweed Shire Council is a direct beneficiary of the Commonwealth Budget. In the 2024/2025 Draft Budget to be adopted by Council tonight at Item 19.1 it includes income directly from the Commonwealth by the way of the Financial Assistance Grants which Council utilises to assist fund its services to the community. In the 2024/2025 Draft Council Budget this comprises $8.5m General component +   $1.8m Roads component provided by way of Commonwealth FAG’s. 

In addition, Council is the recipient of other federal government grants such as Roads to Recovery and one-off grants such as the money for the Animal Rehoming Centre – it is also an item on tonight’s agenda, to Award the contract. 
Officers are working with the Federal Members Office and Commonwealth Agencies to arrange a sod turning in coming months. 

With respect to the broader question relating to the funding commitments in the Federal Budget that the Tweed Shire Council will benefit from, it includes items such as supporting Tweed residents with pensions (noting 13% of Council’s rate base are pensioners), health care, education, defence, housing, NDIS, and transport. 

As Tweed residents complete their tax returns for the 23/24 financial year they will receive a Tax Receipt which breaks down Commonwealth expenditure from the budget based on their tax paid which contributes to the broad categories of: Welfare, Health, Defence, Education, General public services, Interest on government debt, transportation and communication, industry assistance, fuel and energy, foreign affairs, economic aid, public order and safety, housing and community, recreation and culture, immigration, and other purposes. 

Councillors are referred to the Commonwealth budget for further detail which can be found at budget.gov.au and if any queries remain the Federal Member for Richmond has advised she is happy to respond directly to any questions from individual councillors.

For a more detailed analysis of the 2024 Federal Budget from a local government perspective refer to:
  • ALGA: https://alga.com.au/alga-analysis-of-2024-25-federal-budget/ or
  • Business NSW’s review from a business perspective: Federal Budget 2024-25 Business Analysis (businessnsw.com)

Council maintains an ongoing watch for new and renewed state and federal grants.  This includes ongoing contact with departments, direct notices and press releases, review of budgets and grant monitoring agencies.
As a closing remark I highlight to Councillors the importance of both State and Commonwealth grants to the Tweed Shire for the provision of infrastructure and services. By way of example Council this financial year secured 265 grants from 47 agencies totalling $195.6M. 

This is a great achievement and testament to the hard work and commitment of Council staff in preparing multiple quality grant submissions and the strong advocacy of management and councillors.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Owens asks what is the process to allow secondary dwellings and detached dual occupancy dwellings larger than 60m2 on RU1 & RU2 zoned land in Tweed Shire? 

Director Planning and Regulation replies.

Through you Madam Mayor

The permissibility of secondary dwellings and or detached dual occupancies in the rural areas has been discussed for many years with the community in The Tweed Rural Land Strategy and again more recently in the Growth Management Housing Strategy.  There were over 650 submissions to the Growth Management Housing Strategy, Options Paper and these submission are currently under review to determine the needs and preferences of the community. 

It is anticipated that the Growth Management Housing Strategy Options Paper will be reported back to Council in October or November 2024 and that such report will give consideration to the suitability of secondary dwellings and or detached dual occupancies in the rural areas. The future report will consider a needs analysis based on current available data and will review the impact of additional rural homes on the viability of farming going forward as well as the potential impact to council’s recurrent finances and ability to fund services and maintain assets. 

The Growth Management Housing Strategy Options Paper will be developed into a strategy with action items.

Upon receipt of the data in October or November 2024 if Council wish to support additional forms of secondary dwellings and or detached dual occupancies in the rural areas Council would need to ensure such wishes are reflected in the action items of the ultimate Growth Management Housing Strategy. 

Clause 5.4 of the Tweed LEP 2014 only entertains 60m2 secondary dwellings on urban land only (not rural land). Therefore, if Council wanted to support secondary dwellings on rural land an action in the Growth Management Housing Strategy may be to prepare a Planning Proposal to amend the Tweed LEP 2014 to include a new Clause 5.5 for secondary dwellings in the rural areas where Council specifies the maximum allowable square meters of the secondary dwelling, and the distance between the secondary dwelling and the principal dwelling. 

If Council wanted to support detached dual occupancies on rural land an action in the Growth Management Housing Strategy may be to prepare a Planning Proposal to amend Tweed LEP 2014 to include detached dual occupancies as permitted with consent in the rural land use tables.  

This will all be outlined in detail at the upcoming report to Council in October or November 2024.","isPublic":false,"isPublished":false,"isCurrentItem":false,"meeting":null,"reports":[{"id":18030,"name":"Question on Notice","isUploaded":0,"reportTemplateId":18,"wordTemplateId":8,"pdfMediaFullPath":"stream/TWEED/tmp_645f1a15b0.pdf","token":"a760660f-58d6-4478-9ed6-36626bbfadbe","isPublic":true}],"attachments":[],"actionSheets":[],"bookmarks":[{"id":2688,"name":"19","eventId":995,"title":"QON - Cr Owen - Secondary Dwellings","text":"QON - Cr Owen - Secondary Dwellings","startTime":0,"duration":null,"itemId":23252,"sortOrder":20,"minutesSortOrder":20,"parentId":-1,"additionalParentId":-1}],"minutes":[]},{"id":23253,"name":"QON - Cr Owen - Indoor Sporting Facility and 50m Pool Olympic Sized Swimming Pool Community Reference Group","parentId":21140,"sortOrder":81,"minutesSortOrder":81,"minutesParentId":21140,"outlineNumber":"10","fullOutlineNumber":"12.10.","htmlContent":"

Cr Reece Byrnes
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
 
RESOLVED that in respect to Contract Request for Offer RFO2024031 Design and Construct Animal Rehoming Facility South Murwillumbah: 

  1. Council awards the offer Alder Construction Pty Ltd ABN 31 106 657 470 for the amount of $6,192,042.29 (exclusive of GST) and $6,811,246.52 (inclusive of GST).

  2. The General Manager be granted delegated authority to approve appropriately deemed variations to the contract and those variations be reported to Council at finalisation of the contract.

  3. ATTACHMENTS 1 and 2 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain: 

(d)  commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:

 (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
 (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or
 (iii) reveal a trade secret

  1. ATTACHMENT 3 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains: 

(c)     information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business

 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Tay Lee:


"God Almighty,

We are here before You today with grateful hearts, thankful for the opportunity to serve our community, Tweed Shire. In this council meeting, we seek Your guidance and wisdom. May the discussions and decisions made today be guided by a spirit of fairness and justice. Let us consider the needs and concerns of all our community members, especially those who are most vulnerable and in need of support. Help us to work together in unity and respect, seeking the common good above all else.

Gracious God,

We ask for Your blessing upon the Mayor, each councillor and all the staff. Grant them the wisdom to lead with integrity, fairness, and justice. Help them to listen with open hearts and minds, and to speak with compassion and understanding. Bless their efforts to create a safe, healthy, and thriving environment for all who live and work here.

Also, we ask for Your Blessings and protection over our community. Bless all its residents to access equal opportunities for prosperity and guide us to be a better community that helps and supports each other.

We trust in Your perfect wisdom and guidance and place this meeting and all its agendas in Your mighty hands.

In Jesus' name, we pray.

Amen"

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle of the Living Waters Church in Tumbulgum.

O God, we come before you with gratitude, and thank you for being a God of love who is with us now in this very room. You never leave us or forsake us. By your grace You have brought us this far and You will continue to lead us and guide us.

I thank you for making each of us in this room, every person we meet, and every citizen of this shire, in your own image, with dignity and infinite worth. We thank you for the ability you have given every one of us, to be good stewards of your creation, to love our neighbours as ourselves.

I thank you for – our Mayor, our Councillors, and Tweed Shire Council staff. I give thanks for the life of service they have chosen to take up, on behalf of all of us here. We pray for their peace and safety in a world of unrest. We all come to this meeting as complex human beings, carrying burdens, carrying joy and hope, trusting that you alone can hold us together O God, in your love and peace. Help these Councillors to make God directed decisions that will benefit this Shire, both now and well into the Future.

We ask this in Jesus Name Amen

RESOLVED that the resolution at item 18.6 titled RFO2023101 - Expressions of Interest Greenhills Lodge Repurpose - Contract Termination from the meeting held Thursday 20 June 2024 being:
that Council:

  1. In respect to RFO2023101 - Expressions of Interest Greenhills Lodge Repurpose notes the withdrawal of New South Wales Reconstruction Authority from the proposed use of the site for workers accommodation.
  2. Continues to explore options for future use of the facility with:
     a)  Homes NSW
     b)  Other government agencies and not-for-profit groups that were part of the previous tender process for provision of services at this site.
  3. Proceeds with the further geotechnical investigation of the landslip with a view to undertaking the remediation of the landslip if and when funding for the same become available, retaining the maximum number of rooms feasible during this process.
  4. Investigate getting a not-for-profit tenant into the site to utilise part of the facility while the works are occurring to ensure no further degradation of the buildings occurs, and bring back a further report on this to Council.
be rescinded.

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. In respect to RFO2023101 - Expressions of Interest Greenhills Lodge Repurpose notes the withdrawal of New South Wales Reconstruction Authority from the proposed use of the site for workers accommodation.

  2. Continues to explore options for future use of the facility with:
    1. NSW Reconstruction Authority Resilient Lands Program (for an option providing reuse of as many of the existing structures/rooms as feasible);
    2. Homes NSW;
    3. Other government agencies and not-for-profit groups that were part of the previous tender process for provision of services at this site.

  3. Proceeds with the further geotechnical investigation of the landslip with a view to undertaking the remediation of the landslip if and when funding for the same become available, retaining the maximum number of rooms feasible during this process.

  4. In consultation with the NSW Reconstruction Authority, investigates getting a not-for-profit tenant into the site to utilise part of the facility while the works are occurring to ensure no further degradation of the buildings occurs.

  5. A further report is brought back to Council once the outcomes of conditions 2, 3 and 4 above can be determined by Council.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
RESOLVED that Council:

 

  1. Notes that emergency services are the responsibility of the NSW Government of which Council funds, through general fund rates, 11.7% of the service cost.

  2. Notes that the Tweed District Rescue Squad are currently the only State Rescue Board accredited agency for General Land Rescues and Vertical Rescues in the Tweed Shire and are identified by both the State Rescue Board and Local Rescue Committee as having primary responsibility for provision of these services in the Tweed Shire.

  3. Writes to the Minister for Emergency Services to request a meeting to discuss how Volunteer Rescue groups are funded.

  4. Resolves to increase its current funding to the Tweed District Rescue Squad on an ongoing basis to the total contribution value of $90,000 plus an annual indexation to the rate peg and this adjustment to funding support be allocated in the September 2024 Quarterly Budget Review.
