Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Submits the following motions to the 2024 Local Government NSW (LGNSW) Annual Conference:

Motion 1 - Rating of dual occupancy and secondary dwellings

That LGNSW calls on the NSW Government to amend the Local Government Act 1993 to:

  1. Provide a multiplying factor of 1.5x to the Ordinary Rate where a Primary Dwelling and Secondary Dwelling (granny flat) exists on residential or farmland rating categories.
  2. Provide a multiplying factor of 2x to the Ordinary Rate where Dual Occupancy (non-strata subdivision) exists on residential or farmland rating categories.
  3. The permissible income be increased annually based upon DA approvals to provide for the additional multiplying factor.

Background Information
As NSW is gripped with a Housing Crisis, and a deficit of low-cost dwellings for singles or couples, local government areas are experiencing an increase of properties with granny flats. This is a welcome trend and has the ability to fill a much needed housing topology gap whilst retaining the amenity of neighbourhoods. Likewise, some local government areas are facing pressure to permit dual occupancies on rural land (both residential and farmland categories). That is a second primary dwelling. 

The NSW Government, on 2 July 2024, introduced the low- and mid-rise housing reforms to create greater housing diversity on low-rise residential land to deliver more homes across NSW. The low- and mid-rise housing policy is expected to deliver 112,000 additional homes over the next 5 years, contributing significantly to the housing accord target of 377,000 new homes by July 2029. The Government states that the policy is a critical component of their planning strategy to address the urgent need for more housing across NSW. They state that it will unlock more diversity in housing to cater for more options for everyone – renters, families and empty nesters. 

Due to the NSW Rating system being based on unimproved land value, there is no mechanism for councils to seek a contribution towards the costs of services and facilities under the existing arrangement, and the reforms announced by the Government in July do not consider that the potential of the 112,000 additional properties will be unratable. Existing ratepayers will therefore continue to subsidise those with second dwellings on their property and this does not accord with the user pays system. By way of example, if Tweed were to permit dual occupancy on rural allotments (residential or farmland category) it could see up to 4,000 additional primary detached dwellings with no capacity to rate these homes. At an average rate of $1,694 this would result in lost recurrent revenue of $6.776M annually. Money much needed to provide the library, parks, sporting fields, pools, roads, etc. that the residents occupying these homes would expect and demand. Similarly, in Tweed’s case, if 36,000 residential properties all took advantage of a granny flat, there is likewise no provision to levy rates for the increase in population that will ultimately result in an increase to service provision. What is suggested therefore is a multiplying factor that recognises a granny flat will result in less population than a dual occupancy scenario and that the permissible income be increased annually based upon DA approvals.
 
This proposal is in addition to the population factor included in the current rate peg model. This proposal recognises, for example, if a 4000-lot greenfield development was to occur within a locality or if increased density were to occur through strata subdivision there would be a corresponding uplift to a council’s permissible income, whereas a similar increase in homes through non strata dual occupancy and secondary dwellings presently receives no corresponding uplift.

Motion 2 – Costs of assessing Development Applications 
 
That LGNSW calls on the NSW Government to:
 
  1. Engage IPART to measure the typical costs of assessing development applications and mods using three regional city councils, two rural councils and four metropolitan based councils as a valid audit sample.
  2. Re-assess the statutory fees in the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulations 2021, to achieve full cost recovery of the development application costs as the result of the IPART typical cost measurement.
  3. That the development application fees be indexed in line with the Local Government (State) Award.
 
Background information
 Councils' Development Assessment functions are an unsustainable business and financial model, subsidised by existing ratepayers and not reflective of a user pays principle.
 
The increasing expectations of both State and Federal Governments for local councils to perform at the highest levels of financial performance and provide an increasingly diverse range of community services and environmental stewardship, whilst at the same time reducing or limiting by regulation funding and income generating opportunities, is a totally unsustainable business model.
 
This is no more pronounced than in Council’s development assessment functions. Many of the complaints that Council has been receiving relating to DA assessment times is from private sector planning consultant and development firms.
 
Like most NSW councils, Tweed Shire Council is currently dealing with applications that don’t pay their way. In recent years, Council has been required to assess a number of State school, hospital and Part 3A legacy developments. Coupled with this, regulated fees and charges were non indexed for more than 20 years, before the current state government has thankfully started to index the fees as of 2023.
 
Council staff are providing extensive support and assessment services and are required to plan, design and build infrastructure to service those developments and yet they are exempt from developer contributions and the fees do not reflect the cost of assessment. When dealing with one such development it is a challenge but when you have multiple developments at the same time not paying their way, it becomes a real financial challenge.
 
Under the stress and demands of large workloads, Council staff are doing all within their powers (including working overtime) to work through each application in a fair and methodical manner, within the highly complex, litigious and politicised NSW Planning system. Excluding legal fees and referrals to other areas within Council, the ratepayers of the Tweed Shire have been subsidising the development assessment process in excess of $1m per year. Across an average of 1,000 applications per year, it currently represents a subsidy of around $1,000 per DA. If the regulated fees and charges were assessed and lifted to reflect the true cost of assessment local government would be in a position to hire on a recurrent basis the much needed additional resources to assist fund the development assessment process within the State and Commonwealth timeframes.

  1. Any further motions are submitted to the General Manager by 21 July 2024 for inclusion in the 1 August 2024 Council meeting business papers, noting that councillors may still raise motions for inclusion during the meeting.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 13 June 2024 be received and 

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1.    Alma Street, Murwillumbah
That:
1.  The installation of "no right turn between 8am and 6pm " signs at the exit from Hayes Lane onto Alma Street, Murwillumbah be supported.
2.  The installation of "no right turn between 8am and 6pm " signs into Hayes Lane from Alma Street, Murwillumbah not be supported.

6.2.    Carraboi Terrace, Tyalgum
That 'No Parking Area 11pm - 5am' signage be installed at the entrance to the Tyalgum Water Treatment Plant on Carraboi Terrace, Tyalgum.

6.3.    Temporary Road Closures for Open Streets Program, Tweed Shire
That the proposed temporary closures of streets within the Tweed Shire for the Open Streets Program, is supported in concept, subject to further information from the applicant identifying the proposed closure date and complying with Council's standard event conditions as follows:
1.    NSW Police approval being obtained.
2.    Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
3.    Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
4.    The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or 
5.    Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
6.    All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
7.    Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
8.    Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
9.    That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
10.    The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
11.    The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
12.    A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
13.    The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
14.    The application of all signs and devices necessary to effect the changed traffic management conditions and temporary road closures for the events, also being approved as part of the event approval.

6.4.    Multi-Level Carpark, Repairs
That:
1.  The taxi zone on Queen Street, Murwillumbah be replaced with 2 hour parking 9 - 5pm Mon- Fri, Sat 9am-12pm.
2.  The existing time limited parking within the Knox Park carpark, Murwillumbah be removed, and this be reviewed when the Multi-Level Carpark is fully operational.
3.  Tumbulgum Road (adjacent to Wharf Street Park) the existing 4 x 15 minute spaces be reduced to one.

6.5.    Pedestrian Refuge, Tweed Valley Way
That the proposed pedestrian refuge on Tweed Valley Way south of Prospero Street, Murwillumbah be supported subject to compliance with the appropriate Australian standards and detailed design.

7.1.    Piggabeen Road, Tweed Heads West 
That:
1.  Transport for New South Wales to provide criteria for a fixed speed camera installation for Council to include for a response to the customer.
2.  Council will install 2 speed zone repeater signs to reinforce the current 60km/h speed limit.

7.2.    Minjungbal Drive,Tweed Heads South
That:
1.   "No Stopping vehicles under 7m Excepted" be installed on Minjungbal Drive, Tweed Heads South, south of the existing No Parking extending approximately 170m to the south past the main entrance to the Ford dealership.
2.  The existing No Stopping be extended from Kirkwood Drive, Tweed Heads South, to the main driveway entrance for the Ford dealership.

7.3.    McKissock Drive, Kingscliff 
That a yellow no stopping line (C3) be installed on the inside of the curve at the intersection of Murphys Road and McKissock Drive, Kingscliff, for a length of approximately 40m to reinforce no stopping along the section of road where the verge narrows due to the bollards.

7.4.    Seaview Street, Kingscliff 
Any changes to existing line marking and signage on Seaview Street, Kingscliff, is not supported.

7.5.    Shearwater Parade, Tweed Heads
That the installation of no stopping (C3) yellow linemarking be installed at the end of Shearwater Parade, Tweed Heads at the driveway access to the park is supported.

7.6.    Tweed Coast Enduro 2025, Pottsville
That the proposed Tweed Enduro on Saturday 22 February 2025 be supported subject to: 
1. NSW Police approval being obtained. 
2. Endorsement of the event by Triathlon NSW. 
3. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons. 
4. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents. 
5. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts, road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints. 
6. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event. 
7. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event. 
8. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed. 
9. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event. 
10. That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed. The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources. If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval. 
11. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein. 
12. The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network. 
13. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions. 
14. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose. 
15. The application of all signs and devices necessary to effect the changed traffic management conditions and temporary road closures for the events, also being approved as part of the event approval. 

7.7.    Intersection Ocean Avenue/Marine Parade, Kingscliff
Drivers entering Ocean Street from Marine Parade, Kingscliff, need to take care when sight distance is limited by parked vehicles close to the intersection. No further prohibitive signage or line marking is warranted.

7.8.    Kingscliff Triathlon, December 2024 and March 2025
That the proposed Kingscliff Triathlon 1 December 2024 and 23 March 2025 be supported subject to: 
1. NSW Police approval being obtained. 
2. Endorsement of the event by Triathlon NSW. 
3. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons. 
4. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents. 
5. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts, road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related enquiries or complaints. 
6. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event. 
7. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event. 
8. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed. 
9. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event. 
10. That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed. The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources. If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval. 
11. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein. 
12. The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network. 
13. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions. 
14. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose. 
15. The application of all signs and devices necessary to effect the changed traffic management conditions and temporary road closures for the events, also being approved as part of the event approval.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Notes the works recommended in the Condong Creek Drainage Management Plan (2018) were adopted as a preferred option by Council as part of the South Murwillumbah Floodplain Risk Management Study and Plan (2019) for implementation.

  2. Notes the work already undertaken by the developer at the behest of the Drainage Union, with the help of Council, namely the creation of the maintenance bench along the drain on the western boundary of the Airfield. 

  3. Notes the work approved and funded for commencement in 2024 by the NSW Reconstruction Authority under the Northern Rivers Recovery and Resilience Program (NRRRP) on Lot 4 DP591604 and along Condong Creek from Quarry Road to the confluence of the Creek and the Blacks Swamp Drainage Union drain, and that funded under the Drainage Reset program that has not been able to be completed.

  4. As a priority, proceeds with the implementation of remaining recommended works from the Condong Creek Management Plan / South Murwillumbah Floodplain Risk Management Study and Plan.

  5. As a priority, continues to finalise the land tenure arrangements along Condong Creek with Crown Lands / Waterways and Duncan’s Holdings Limited (Pentarch). 

  6. Commences the process to conduct environmental assessment and obtain approvals where required, including obtaining relevant approvals from government agencies to undertake the above work (noting the CCCDMP 2018 indicates environmental approvals will be required for Acid Sulphate Soil interaction actions).

  7. As a priority, urgently pursues opportunities for grant funding from the State and Federal Government to implement the remaining work contained in the Condong Creek Drainage Management Plan / South Murwillumbah Floodplain Risk Management Study and Plan. 

The Motion was Carried

  [OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL] [AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks why does Council not use the Snap Send Solve app?

Acting Director Corporate Services replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, there are a number of applications that are available on the market to report an issue with Snap Send Solve (SSS) being one of those available.
A small number of residents, about 2 submissions per day, currently use the Snap Send Solve (SSS) app to report an issue to Council. These issues are all actioned. 
Council uses a web form solution, OpenForms, for managing Customer Service Requests (CSRs), which has broader capabilities to meet the range of customer service requirements. 
 
  • Council uses OpenForms for managing customer service requests via Report a Problem. Nearly 5,000 requests were submitted in the past 12 months. OpenForms also provides the ability for residents to self-service across the full range of Council’s 50+ services. 
  • We are currently replacing all remaining PDF forms on Council’s website with easy-to-use online fillable forms that uses the OpenForms technology. Some recent examples are plumbing and drainage work approval and application for road closure.
  • The format of information from SSS and the types of issues coming from these reports do not align with Council’s processes, leading to lengthier times for staff to log the CSR and to resolve the identified issue. 
  • Residents have to install the SSS app and create an account before they can start using it. 
  • Council has no control over how a third-party app, like SSS, manages or uses personal information, or where data is stored, etc.
  • SSS offers an ‘enterprise licence’ that gives Council’s greater control over the functionality and access to reports, etc. The cost ranges from approx. $30,000 - $60,000 per year, plus a one-off onboarding fee of $5,000. It would be difficult to justify this additional expense to ratepayers, which would be on top of our customer service solution, OpenForms. It could be seen as a charge for residents to report issues to Council, which they can already easily do using Report a Problem.
Finally, Technology One offers a paid connector for SSS, which would enable integration with our environment. However, Council is currently implementing the Technology One ERP ‘OneCouncil’ solution and will be implementing their new Request Management module in 2025/26. We will then likely be moving all CSRs into this direct Technology One interface.

Cr Byrnes returned to the meeting at 05:46pm. 

Acting Director Corporate Services replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, Council’s CCTV in Public Places Policy is available on the Tweed Shire Council website.

Information in relation to CCTV is also provided on the Community Safety page on our website: Community safety | Tweed Shire Council (nsw.gov.au). This page advises that:

Council operates a number of CCTV systems in public places within the Tweed to increase the level of safety for residents, businesses and tourists.

The CCTV cameras are located in sites across Kingscliff, Murwillumbah and Tweed Heads South.

CCTV in Public Places covers Murwillumbah CBD, Kingscliff CBD and Tweed Heads South Skate Park.

All CCTV cameras and recording systems are maintained by Council and have been refreshed within the last two (2) years.  Council uses the same technology as deployed at the new Tweed Valley Hospital. 
In addition to these fixed public CCTV systems, Council has purchased, using State Government election commitment grant funding, two mobile CCTV trailers and three semi fixed CCTV systems (pole mounted cameras) with the contract recently awarded. These mobile CCTV units will be used to:  

  • Assist in crime prevention.
  • Protect public assets.
  • Prevent anti-social behaviour.
  • Encourage public safety.
  • Assist in protecting the environment.
The new mobile CCTV equipment should be available for Council to deploy within the next few months.

In addition to the CCTV in Public Places, Council has a number of other cameras in place. The purposes of these cameras include:

  • Flood monitoring (comes under the Flood Monitoring Camera Policy). A report in relation to the current status and locations is included in the Council meeting agenda of 18 July.
  • Asset Protection/ Operational use, e.g. Stotts Creek Resource Recovery Centre.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Owen asks please provide an overview of the current backlog of development assessments and the effort to reduce them?

Cr Cherry returned to the meeting at 05:51pm.

Director Planning & Regulation replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, since Councillor Owen posed this question the State Government has published Statewide expectations for all Councils to meet certain targets around development applications and planning proposals. So, I will firstly explain the DA backlog and our efforts to address them as requested and then explain how this relates to the new expectation order.

In November 2022 there were 540 outstanding Development Applications in the system.
 
There are currently 284 outstanding applications. 
 
This represents a reduction of 256 outstanding applications since November 2022.
 
In December 2023 there was a conscious decision to target older applications to reduce the outstanding applications. In December 2023 there were 152 applications older than 180 days in the system. Since this time 114 of these applications have now been determined. Leaving 38 of the original older applications that are still being worked through. 
 
And today there are another 63 applications that have creeped back over the 180 days threshold, meaning 101 total outstanding applications over 180 days.
 
Simultaneously, staff have been targeting newer application to keep them moving through the system as quickly as possible cognisant of the quality of the application that has been lodged. 
 
Staff have also been stricter on DA lodgements to improve the quality of applications being lodged. 
 
The Development Assessment team that handle the more complex applications have a median assessment time of 106 days for applications lodged and determined in the last 12 months. 
 
However, due to the ongoing attempt to resolve historic applications the total median or average times can fluctuate regularly and over the past 12 months is approximately 189 average days for applications from Council.
 
The building unit have 112 of the current outstanding development applications.
 
The median time to assess a house in the past 12 months is 75 days (across 317 applications).
 
The median time to assess a pool in the past 12 months has been 49 days (across 115 applications).
 
Therefore overall, there has been great improvement in the number of our outstanding Development Applications and improvements to our DA Assessment times. 
 
So how do these assessment times relate to the new expectation order. 
 
The new order requires Council’s to lodge all applications from the NSW Planning Portal within 14 days. Currently Tweed averages 31 days as we have allowed applications to sit in the portal while we await additional information. This practice will cease, and applications lodged without all the necessary information will be rejected from the portal within 14 days wherever possible. We expect to see improvements with this statistic over the coming months.
 
The new order requires Council’s to assess DA’s within 115 days. Council’s cumulative average for the 2023 and 2024 financial year is 189 days. However as detailed earlier this is because we have determined 114 older applications in the last 8 months. These older determinations have and will continue to skew our average assessment times. 
 
If we had of just calculated the average assessment time for all DA’s lodged and determined in 23/24 our average assessment time would have been 93 days (well below the 115 days) – but determining older applications in the past 12 months has blown that statistic out to 189 days. 
 
The new order also requires planning proposals to be determined as per the LEP Making Guidelines within 115 days. Council is aware of this target and has been aiming for this wherever possible.
 
Overall, our DA backlog and improved assessment times are a work in progress and the team have great aspirations to keep improving every day. 
 
In addition to the Expectation Order the NSW Government has produced a DA League table that publishes statistics and compares Council’s against each other. Council will keep improving its turnaround times and monitor this against the league table however it is dangerous to compare Council’s in this manner as it is not a like for like comparison.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Owen asks what opportunities are there for Tweed Shire Council to improve, monitor and report on its customer service?

Acting Director Corporate Services replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, our Customer Service team handle a wide range of enquiries and requests across our 50+ services and via 4 different channels (face to face, phone, web chat and email). A range of self-service options are available 24/7, including Report a Problem.  We have an after-hours service that ensures emergencies are triaged promptly and directs any non-urgent enquiries to either self-service or a choice to call-back during working hours.

Improve
Continuous improvement is facilitated through regular reviews in line with industry trends, new technologies, changing community needs and expectations, and customer feedback. 
Council is a top performer in the customer service space and compares favourably against contact centre industry benchmarks. The 2024 Contact Centre Best Practice results were recently released, surveying more than 250 Australian contact centres across all sectors.

Our team exceeded the average/ benchmark performance across the key industry metrics:

  • ‘Average Speed of Answer’ benchmark was 115 seconds – Council’s was 74 seconds.
  • ‘Abandoned Call Rate’ benchmark was 8% of all incoming calls – Council’s was 3.4%.
  • ‘Average Handle Time’ benchmark was 543 seconds – Council’s was 393 seconds.

The Premier Contact Point (customer experience solution) is used to manage customer phone and web chat enquiries. It is one of the leading-edge contact centre solutions and continually brings technological advancements to the customer experience.

Importantly, Councillors can bring about a meaningful improvement by advising residents who contact them regarding a customer service issue that they should use our official report a problem online form for all non-urgent issues. Anything urgent should be immediately reported by calling 02 6670 2400 any time of day.

Monitor
Customer service (via our channels) is activity monitored to ensure it is within service levels. Real time task prioritisation and staff rostering is managed to meet demand.
Council captures the voice of the customer through feedback and complaints, post call surveys and call quality assurance. Information received is investigated and used to initiate improvement opportunities where required.
Report a Problem provides greater visibility of customer trends and activity.  Activity can be easily monitored and tracked for metrics such as volume of requests, trends or multiple requests for same issue, processing times and customer communication. 

Report 
Council has Service Experience Standards that sets the timeframes and service standards that customers can expect.

Publicly available customer experience performance measures are reported to the community every 6 months. 

In addition, the Customer Service team track daily, weekly and monthly stats in relation to customer experience and centre performance, which is used to prioritise operational tasks and resource allocation, identify improvement opportunities and track customer trends.

Examples of customer service information reported and performance measures published on Council’s website are:





It should be noted that we will be implementing a new Request Management system via the ERP Project in 2025. It is expected that this will further enhance customer user experience (both internal and external).

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by the Youth Pastor, Jessie Skelly Tweed Church.
 
Father God, let us pray, be peace come upon each of us.
In a tired and an anxious world, we pray your peace will come and fill our hearts.
Help us to be still before you.
We thank you for the great work that happens in this room, we thank you for the leaders in this room that you appointed.
We pray your blessing on them, and your peace on them, for all they do.
We pray your peace will be with them, as they go into the community and as they serve, as they lay down their lives for others, and this great region, we pray your blessing is on the Tweed Shire.
We thank you for the local government and what it represents.
Let us pray, Lord Jesus, that you will be with each person as they serve,  and care for this community.
 
We pray that you will unite the Tweed Shire, and you bring a oneness and a richness, and we thank you that we are so blessed, so prosperous in this nation, and we pray that we would not forget about the other.
Those that need our help, our care and our consideration and we pray for those that are homeless, those that are doing it tough, those that are struggling in our society.
We pray for the widow, for the poor, or for the single Mums struggling to pay rent. We pray for your blessing upon each and every person in our community. Thank you for the difference we can make here, and the lives we can change and touch.
 
We pray you will touch and change lives, Lord Jesus.
 
We thank you, that you love us and  you are with us.
 
I pray for each person in this room, as Number 7 says.
 
May the Lord bless you and keep you. May the Lord smile on you and be gracious to you, and may the Lord show you his  favour, and give you peace.
 
In the mighty name Jesus, 
Amen

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RECOMMENDED that 
 
1. Development Application DA21/0707 for a staged subdivision of two existing lots into seven lots at Lot 33 DP 1252272 No. 3 Murraya Way, Cudgen; Lot 34 DP 1252272 No. 9 Murraya Way, Cudgen be approved subject to the conditions attached to the report for this item except with the following change to Condition 24(c) which should read as follows:
 
24(c)     Revegetation detail for the entire balance area of the revegetation and rehabilitation area outside the zone shown as earthworks fill on Dwg. No. C2 Lot 33 Layout - Stage 1 Revision P5 dated 26 May 2023 prepared by Lucena Civil & Structural Engineers to include a schedule of mixed local lowland rainforest native shrub and small tree species to be used for planting at a minimum density of one (1) plant per two (2) square metres.  
 
2.           Council approves the variation of the covenant and restriction on the use of land being the “Terms of Positive Covenant numbered 6 in the plan” and “Terms of Restriction on the Use of Land numbered 9 in the plan” referred to in DP 1252272 to the effect that:  
  1. the “Terms of Positive Covenant numbered 6 in the plan” remains, subject to the requirements of a revegetation and rehabilitation program in accordance with a Revegetation and Rehabilitation Plan, and maintained in perpetuity, but is to ‘burden’ Part Lots 331, 332 and 333 and ‘benefit’ Tweed Shire Council;
  2. the “Terms of Restriction on the Use of Land numbered 9 in the plan” be varied to allow earthworks extending no more than 3.7m (maximum) into area G of DP 1252272, consisting of 1.2m (maximum) horizontally and 2.5m (maximum) battered at1:2 (v:h) (maximum); 
  3. an easement be created 4m wide and variable to provide for drainage of water and sewage on proposed Lots 331-337 inclusive; 
  4. a right of carriageway be created 3m wide and variable on proposed Lots 334-337 inclusive; 
  5. an easement be created 3m wide to drain water on proposed Lot 333; and 
3.         Council executes all necessary documentation under the Common Seal of Council. 
4.         ATTACHMENT 6 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains: (e) information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

RECOMMENDED that Council:

  1. Endorses the waiver of an architectural design competition in lieu of an architectural design review process on the Nos. 12-16 Florence Street Tweed Heads site relating to the development of a multi-storey residential flat building with affordable housing component and written correspondence confirming Council’s endorsement of the waiver be forwarded to the proponent;
  2. Delegates the selection of Council’s design representative(s) on the architectural design review panel to the General Manager (or his delegate) to be undertaken in consultation with the NSW Government Architects;
  3. Advises the applicant of Council’s fees and charges which will be based on a cost recovery basis to be established via an endorsed Design Review Process and Fee Agreement where the rates for design panel members will be in alignment with the State Design Review;
  4. Advises the applicant to attend a development assessment panel prior to the commencement of the design review panel to understand the key statutory considerations and relevant advice and commentary of the proposal against development control, standards and guidelines and infrastructure requirements;
  5. Advises the applicant to engage early with the Tweed Byron Aboriginal Land Council which may include undertake a cultural tour to better inform the Connecting with Country design approach; and
  6. Considers a further report related to the establishment of a permanent Tweed Design Review Panel.

The Motion was Carried

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd of the Presbyterian Church in Tweed Heads.


Gracious God
 
As Vietnam Veterans’ Day approaches, we stop to acknowledge the service of the veterans of that conflict.  We are deeply grateful for them and pray for them and their families still living with the physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual wounds inflicted in their service.  May Sunday be a special day of recognition, remembrance, and renewed friendships.  
 
As Local Government elections take place next month we reflect on the achievements of this term of Council.  We take a moment to remember before you a particular project or decision that gave us satisfaction or joy.  

For the new Council to be elected, we pray for a smooth transition for both Councillors and staff, and for positive, effective working relationships that will benefit our community.
 
Please grant your grace, mercy, and peace to all here today.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus

CONFIDENTIAL COMMITTEE

REPRESENTATIONS FOR ITEMS CONSIDERED IN COMMITTEE
(Sec 3.40, 13.9 to 13.17 Model Code of Meeting Practice)

Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.
 
EXCLUSION OF PRESS AND PUBLIC

Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
 
PROPOSED that Council endorses the Pottsville Open Space Masterplan as a guide for future planning with the following change:
 
  • Pg 30: remove ‘1. Tweed Coast Road – north of Cudgera Ave (further assessment in progress)’

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Warren Polglase
Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that Council endorses the Pottsville Open Space Masterplan and the proposed pilot bike skills facility and habitat restoration project at Lot 2 DP 1101923 and Lot 7015 DP 1068895 Tweed Coast Road, Pottsville, as a guide for future planning with the following conditions:

  1. In order to protect the sensitive environment beside the proposed pilot bike skills facility, fencing allowing wildlife to traverse and a ‘No Access’ notice be established between the facility and the buffer to the creek.

  2. Existing native vegetation on the site is incorporated into the design of the pump track where possible and appropriate in accordance with the Recommendations from the Environmental assessment.

  3. An education campaign with regards to the importance of protecting our bushland and riparian areas is carried out prior to the pump track opening.

The Motion was Carried


VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Nola Firth
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

Cr Warren Polglase

RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 11 July 2024 be received and 

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1.    Tweed Valley Triathletes 2024-25
That the proposed Tweed Valley Triathletes Season commencing Saturday 16 September 2024 and concluding Saturday 15 March 2025 be supported, subject to the following conditions:
1. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser. 
2. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event. 
3. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

7.1.    Tweed Heads Hospital, on-road timed parking
That:
1.  That Council officers seek further advice from NSW Health on the existing activities of the old hospital site and the provided parking provisions. There is currently parking provided off Florence Street that is limited to fleet vehicles only and clarification is to be sought whether this could be opened up to be available for customers and staff associated with the community health practice. There has also been a request for accessible parking provision on Keith Compton Drive and observations are that the building adjacent to this area is not currently being used.
2.  The 2P parking limits on Powell Street (between Brett Street and Florence Street) and on Solander Street, Tweed Heads be removed.

7.2.    Keith Compton Drive, Tweed Heads
The request for yellow line on Keith Compton Drive on the approach to the driveway for 1 Botany Crescent, Tweed Heads is not supported.  This property access is not dissimilar to other nearby driveways, and the driveway is wide enough for exiting drivers to exit with care.

7.3.    Sutherland Street, Kingscliff
That 10 minute timed parking on school days, during school zone times (8am - 9:30am and 2:30pm - 4pm) be installed on the 9 parking spaces on Sutherland Street adjacent to the Kingscliff Public School, Kingscliff.

7.4.    Kirkwood Road, Tweed Heads South 
That the yellow no stopping line on the south side of Kirkwood Road, be extended from the Minjungbal Drive intersection Tweed Heads South, to the driveway of no. 54 to ensure the turning lane is kept clear at all times.

7.5.    Panorama Drive, Tweed Heads West 
That yellow no stopping lines be placed at the cul-de-sac end of Panorama Drive, Tweed Heads West (above Scenic Drive), to facilitate heavy vehicle manoeuvering.

7.6.    Peninsula Drive, Bilambil Heights 
That:
1. The convex safety mirror currently within the road reserve outside 16 Peninsula Drive, Bilambil Heights be removed, as it is no longer supported to be in the road reserve by Transport for NSW. 
2. The installation of a double centre line be installed for a distance of approximately 55m between 14 and 24 Peninsula Drive, Bilambil Heights, be supported, to improve drivers' awareness of the curve.

7.7.    Scenic Drive, Spar Supermarket, Tweed Heads West 
That the request to modify the existing line marking and signage in relation to car park access to the Spar Supermarket on Scenic Drive, Tweed Heads West, is not supported, as the existing facilities support pedestrian movements and the car park egress sight distance is adequate.


The Motion was Carried



VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen, Cr Warren Polglase
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Nil

RESOLVED that Council:
 
  1. Notes that Share the Dignity is a national charity that promotes improved awareness of the economic, social, and cultural issues associated with period management, and which works with institutions, girls, and women to overcome them.

Councillor Brinsmead asks is there a correlation between the introduction of Council's on-call kerbside pickup and increased illegal dumping throughout the shire?

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replies. 

Through you Madam Mayor, Council’s kerbside bulk waste collection was introduced in 2008 with the dial-up service implemented in 2017 to allow residents within the shire to dispose of bulky items.  Residents with a red bin can book either two 2 cubic metres, or one four cubic metre collections per year.  Once booked, the waste is collected within 28 days, with the most collected within 2 weeks.
The original service which was a scheduled collection to all areas over a 6-week period, twice per year, led to the presentation and collection of between 3,000 and 3,300 tonnes of material each year. Under the current booking system between 1,100 and 1,200 tonnes of waste is collected on average per annum, with the same level of waste allowed to properties. The earlier system saw a lot of misuse with people dumping on other people’s piles. 
As the service has been established since 2008 it is difficult to show a correlation to the suggested increased illegal dumping throughout the Shire. The introduction of social media platforms to sell or donate items is likely to have impacted the amount of waste collected.  However, it can also be contended that there is not an increase, but rather a decrease with our surveillance and vigilance highlighting the practice of illegal dumping more.

Councillor Brinsmead asks will a return to weekly red bin collection be considered in the future, and if yes, what is the process?

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replies. 

Through you Madam Mayor, Council currently has a waste collection contract which expires in 8 years.  There are no plans to review the red bin collection during the contract term as it would have significant financial implications and would impact use of the organics bin which diverts nearly 30% of the domestic waste stream.   Further, Council has endorsed KPIs in its Delivery Program to divert waste from landfill and to increase recycling. Increasing the red bin collection to weekly would not align with this and would impact our ability to meet the State Government’s targets for household waste diversion as required through the Waste Avoidance and Resource Recovery legislation. It would also lead to an increase in organics to landfill which has environmental implications.

Councillor Owen asks what is the latest update on the Tyalgum Road landslip?

Director Engineering replies

Council’s contractor SEE Civil is progressing well with works at the Tyalgum Road landslip with the first row of piles having been completed.  This is a significant milestone.  
Pile tie-back anchor installation has also been completed on the lower side of the temporary access road through the slip site.  Following the completion of tieback work the contractor has now commenced footing and basket assembly of the gabion wall. 

The gabion basket retaining wall and backfilling will bring the eastbound lane up to the original road height. 
Works will then focus on the roadworks of the future eastbound lane. 

Once completed, traffic will then swap from the current temporary track to the eastbound lane to allow works on the upslope section of the slip to commence. During this time, access through the site will still remain as a single-lane with traffic lights either end. 

The completion of the lower row of piles has also changed conditions which trigger the closure of temporary access road gates at either side of the Tyalgum Road work zone. 
Previously, if the site was to receive more than 100 mm of rain in a 24-hour period or have 2 consecutive days of 50 mm of rain, the gates would close. Unexpected movement, measured on underground monitors, could also trigger closures. 

Now, the gates will only close if the site receives more than 125 mm in a 24-hour period, or if the underground monitors detect significant movements. This is likely to translate into fewer temporary road closures and less disruption for the local community. 

Council will still maintain an amber alert which is an advisory to commuters that the gates may close but this will only be initiated if the site receives more than 100 mm of rain. 
Monitoring of the site will continue while restoration work for the permanent fix continues, particularly in heavy rain events to ensure safety for motorists. The expected completion date for permanent works remains mid-2025.

Councillor Owen asks what are the options for Council to provide more rubbish bins in the commercial and retails areas of Marine Parade, Kingscliff?

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replies. 

Through you Madam Mayor, Council could provide additional bins in commercial and retail areas of Marine Parade, Kingcliff, however it comes at a cost.  The cost of servicing an individual bin is $3.95 per service which covers the supply of the bin.  Any stand or enclosure is an additional cost and the fee is adjusted quarterly based on CPI.  Bin locations are strategically identified based on pedestrian traffic flow and an assessment of potential waste generation and sources in the area.  It should be noted that Council does not provide public bins for commercial operators (shops and businesses) as they are required to supply their own waste disposal options.  Officers are looking into alternate technological solutions to service public waste collection, such as smart bin sensors, which attaches to the bin enclosure and provides data to assist staff in making informed decisions about waste levels and servicing needs.

The ongoing noise issues related to the operations of Pocket Herbs at 67 Howards rd, Burringbar are continuing to impact on the sensitive receivers at 74 and 75 Howards rd. The council noise monitors that have been installed, were required to be removed recently for recalibration and service. Direction is required as to replacement of the noise monitors. As the noise issues are ongoing and recent testing has indicated non-compliance with noise conditions of the consent, the noise monitors are required to be reinstalled as soon as possible.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council reinstall the noise monitors at 74 and 75 Howards Rd, Burringbar as soon as practical after the recalibration and service has been completed.

The Motion was Carried

RECOMMENDED that the resolution of Item 22.1 of the Planning Committee held on 1 August 2024 - Notice to Alter - Cr Polglase, Cr Brinsmead, Cr Owen - Appeal Management DA23/0438 being:

  1. The Mayor and the General Manager (or delegate) undertake Appeal Management of DA23/0438 by way of negotiated conditions for approval as per the attached confidential Notice to Alter.

be rescinded.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Brenda Stuttle of the Living Waters Church, Tumbulgum: 

Thank you once again for the Privilege of being able to Pray for you all in this next season that you are about to enter into. I would like to say it will be easy, but realistically, I think we’ve all been around the block a few times to know that Life happens” and some days are diamonds and some days are stones. I want to congratulate you all on being re elected and also welcome Kimberly Hone on her new appointment to Council. 

Dear Heavenly Father, 
Thankyou for the privilege of being able to serve in this amazing Community of the Tweed. 
We are thankful that it is such a rich area of fertile land and rivers that meet the sea. 
Give us wisdom as we make decisions for the Community that are in the best interests of those we serve and let our hearts be open to other cultures and opinions that may not reflect our own but make up such a rich, colourful tapestry of this local area.
We pray for those who are struggling in this time. The homeless, those who have been impacted by domestic violence, those who have been displaced by economic hardship and those who are impacted and struggling with the current world events of wars and rumours of wars and major weather events.    
Let us be mindful that we cannot fix every problem, but we can do good with the resources we have within our reach. 
As we continue on this journey of serving the Community, help us not to become weary doing good, even at times when those who should support us don’t. 
Help us Lord to keep short accounts and learn to forgive. 
Strengthen us daily and guide us continually we ask in Jesus precious  name. 
Amen

The Returning Officer advised that 2 nominations have been receive for Mayor:
  1. Cr Chris Cherry  was nominated by Cr Nola Firth and Cr Meredith Dennis and has accepted the nomination.
  2. Cr James Owen was nominated by Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead and Cr Reece Byrnes and has not accepted the nomination
The Returning Officer declared that as there was only one nominee for the role of Mayor, Cr Chris Cherry is elected as Mayor of Tweed Shire Council for a two year period ending September 2026.


The Returning Officer advised that 2 nominations have been receive for Deputy Mayor:
  1. Cr Meredith Dennis was nominated by Cr Chris Cherry and Cr Nola Firth and has accepted the nomination.
  2. Cr Reece Byrnes was nominated by Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead and Cr James Owen and has not accepted the nomination.
The Returning Officer declared that as there was only one nominee for the role of Deputy Mayor, Cr Meredith Dennis is elected as Deputy Mayor of Tweed Shire Council for the period of one year ending September 2025.

Cr Meredith Dennis

  1. Mayor for the period ending September 2026 - Cr Chris Cherry.

  2. Deputy Mayor for the period ending September 2025 - Cr Meredith Dennis.

“We wish to acknowledge the Ngandowal and Minyungbal speaking people of the Bundjalung country in particular the Goodjinburra, Tul-gi-gin and Moorung - Moobah clans as being the traditional owners and custodians of the land and waters within the Tweed Shire boundaries. The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle from The Living Waters Church, Tumbulgum

Exodus 33:12-14 New King James Version (NKJV)

The Promise of God’s Presence

12 Then Moses said to the Lord, “See, You say to me, ‘Bring up this people.’ But You have not let me know whom You will send with me. Yet You have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have also found grace in My sight.’ 13 Now therefore, I pray, if I have found grace in Your sight, show me now Your way, that I may know You and that I may find grace in Your sight. And consider that this nation is Your people.”
14 And He said, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
 
Prayer
 
Dear Lord, 
 
As council sits today to preside over matters concerning the Tweed Shire, we seek your guidance, your direction and your favour. I thank you Lord that you know every person by name and your Goodness & Kindness is displayed towards the people of this beautiful land that we live in. 
 
As Moses asked of you, so do we. We want to know your ways, know your presence and see Your glory. Guide every decision made here today so that we are being directed by the will of Almighty God. 
 
In Jesus name we Pray
 
Amen.

The Mayor took a moment to acknowledge and express appreciation and gratitude towards the former Director of Corporate Services, Warren van Wyk who is retiring from Local Government. The Mayor highlighted the Director’s exceptional dedication and hard work, which have significantly contributed to the Council’s success. Warren's efforts have made a big difference in the way Council interacts with the community and communicating Council's messages.

REPRESENTATIONS FOR ITEMS CONSIDERED IN COMMITTEE
(Sec 3.40, 13.9 to 13.17 Model Code of Meeting Practice)
 
Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.
 
EXCLUSION OF PRESS AND PUBLIC

Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor) 
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
   
RESOLVED that Council moves itself into a Confidential Committee in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993 and that the press and public be excluded from the whole of the Committee Meeting, because, in the opinion of the Committee, publicity of the proceedings of the Committee would be prejudicial to the public interest, by reasons of the confidential nature of the business to be transacted.   
   

The Motion was Carried

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that:

  1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 8 August 2024 be received 
    and

  2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:
6.1.    Barnby Street, Murwillumbah
Officers to further investigate the site at Barnby and William Street intersection, Murwillumbah, in relation to a Stop Sign request, and bring back the item to next available meeting.

7.1.    Wharf Street, Tweed Heads 
That in relation to vehicles parking on Wharf Street, Tweed Heads, Council's:  
  1. Parking rangers be requested to attend to unregistered vehicles within Terranora Terrace and around 112 Wharf Street, Tweed Heads.
  2. Compliance staff advice be sought as to development consent conditions applying to 112 Wharf Street, Tweed Heads.

7.2.    Enterprise Avenue, Tweed Heads South 
That the installation of prohibitive signage/linemarking on Enterprise Avenue, Tweed Heads South, on the cul-de-sac bulb, is not supported and will be further monitored by council officers.

7.3.    William Street, Tweed Heads South
That in relation for the request of prohibitive parking on both sides of the bend on William Street, Tweed Heads South:
  1. Double white centre lines been installed on the bend of William Street.
  2. Council Rangers be notified in relation to enforcement.


The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that:

  1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 12 September 2024 be received 
    and 

  2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:
4.1.    LATE ITEM: Phillip Street / Waugh Street, Chinderah
Considering that sufficient data to complete a report to Council has been received and given the high levels of non-compliance, it is recommended that the trial be ended ahead of schedule at Phillip Street / Waugh Street, Chinderah. The 'No Right Turn' signage installed for the trial should be removed, and the decision communicated to the community. 

6.1.    Installation of EVX
The installation of regulatory signage associated with future commercially funded EV charging stations at 22-24 Frances Street, Tweed Heads and at 115 Wollumbin Street, Murwillumbah be supported.

6.2.    Wollumbin Street, Murwillumbah
The conversion of the existing Taxi Zone on Wollumbin Street, Murwillumbah (adjacent to the Sunnyside Shopping Centre) to 5 minute loading zone is not supported. A taxi zone in this area has previously been removed and further reduction is not supported.

6.3.    William Street, Murwillumbah
The request for a ‘Yellow No Stopping’ line on William Street, Muwillumbah near the corner of Dorset Street, is not supported, given that traffic volumes are low, there is no recent crash history and the intersection can be navigated with caution. 

7.1.    Chinderah Bay Dive, Chinderah
The request for prohibitive parking at Homestead Holiday Park on Chinderah Bay Drive, Chinderah, is not supported. Parking demand in this vicinity is low and adequate sight distance is provided at the driveway exit.  

7.2.    Fraser Drive and Acacia Street, Tweed Heads
That Council supports the installation of a childrens' crossing on Acacia Street, Tweed Heads, in close proximity to the entrance to Pacific Christian College, subject to a complying design and a suitable funding source identified. 

7.3.    Limosa Drive, Tweed Heads West 
That the ‘Yellow No Stopping’ line on the east side of Limosa Drive be extended to meet the ingress driveway of 205 Kennedy Drive, Tweed Heads West, and that Rangers patrol the area to ensure compliance with parking regulations.

7.4.    Sunnycrest Drive, Terranora
That the request for a ‘Yellow No Stopping’ line on Sunnycrest Drive, Terranora (near Nassau Avenue) is not supported, given that construction works are temporary and that traffic volumes are very low.

7.5.    Florence Street, Tweed Heads 
Support for the installation of a ‘Yellow No Stopping’ line be installed on Florence Street, Tweed Heads:
  1. from the driveway access of 49 Beryl Street to Beryl Street.
  2. from the driveway access to 19 Florence Street to Enid Street.

7.6.    Leisure Drive/Greenway Drive, Banora Point
That:
  1. The Centre median on Leisure Drive be extended 20m from the Darlington Drive/Leisure Drive, South Tweed Heads roundabout and written advice be provided to impacted business operators.
  2. The ‘Yellow No Stopping’ line on the west side of Greenway Drive, South Tweed Heads be extended 3m to the north of the Childcare Centre driveway.

7.7.    Marine Parade, Fingal Head
That an additional designated accessible parking bay at Marine Parade, Fingal Head, be installed. Stencil markings to be applied to the new parking bay and signage be installed to incorporate both parking bays.

7.8.    LATE ITEM Turnock Street, Kingscliff
That two hour parking 9am – 5pm be installed on both sides of Turnock Street, Kingscliff (between Pearl Street and Marine Parade).



The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RESOLVED that: 
 
A.  Development Application DA24/0360 for an animal boarding and training establishment, use of unauthorised works consisting of a large stable and training complex and two animal shelters, internal driveway and entry gate and fence and fit-out and completion of the large stable and training complex at Lot 13 DP 755740; Dulguigan Road North Tumbulgum be refused for the following:  

  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is consistent with the aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as set out in Clause 1.2(2) subsections (a), (c), and (g):  
(a)     to give effect to the desired outcomes, strategic principles, policies and actions contained in the Council’s adopted strategic planning documents, including, but not limited to, consistency with local indigenous cultural values, and the national and international significance of the Tweed Caldera, 
(c)     to promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed’s natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways, visual amenity and scenic routes, built environment, and cultural heritage, 
(g)     to conserve or enhance the biological diversity, scenic quality and geological and ecological integrity of Tweed. 
 
The site is highly visible from Tweed Valley Way, Tumbulgum Village and the Tweed River frontage. Structure A: Large Stable and Training Complex has been erected along a ridgeline which is inconsistent with Council’s adopted Scenic Landscape Protection Policy. These structures significantly detract from the scenic quality of the area, and it is not considered that they can simply be mitigated with landscaping. The application does not represent responsible sustainable management of areas of visual amenity.
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development application has not demonstrated that it is permissible under Clause 11 The Zones of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2000. The application is seeking approval for the use of the land for animal boarding and training establishment.   Animal Establishments (similar definition to Animal Boarding and Training Establishment) is a prohibited landuse in the 7(d) zone.  

  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development application has not demonstrated that it is consistent with the zone objectives under Clause 2.3 of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014. This is due to the developments failure to maintain the rural character of the area as a result of to the visual impacts resulting from Structure A and the driveway.  

  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development application has not provided sufficient information to ensure that avoidable erosion and siltation will not adversely affect the environment or riparian vegetation in accordance with Clause 5.21 of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014.
  1.  The development application is substandard, and deficient in information:  
a)      The driveway and entry statement (gate and fence) are partially located in Council’s road reserve, and in accordance with Section 23(1) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2021, a development application requires the written consent of the owner of the land where the application is not made by the owner. No consent from Council was sought or obtained for these works. 
b)      The application does not contain sufficient operational information which has implications for onsite sewage management system and traffic management. 
c)      The entry walls contain signage which does not meet the exempt development requirements under the State Environmental Planning Policy (Exempt and Complying Development Codes) 2008. However, the application does not contain any information in respect to existing/proposed signage. 
d)      The development application does not include sufficient information to assess all elements specifically elevation plans for the front entry gate and fence.
e)      The development application does not address the additional front fencing which according to the survey plan submitted, falls within Council’s road reserve. 
f)       The development application does not include sufficient information to assess the whole driveway which traverses Lot 8 DP 113331 and Lot 61 DP 774633 and was erected at the same time. The application was not supported by a survey or engineering information in respect to the additional driveway.
g)      The development application has not been supported by any information in respect of the low brick retaining walls and black metal pool fencing which adjoins Structure A: Large Stable and Training Facility.
h)      The development application does not contain any information in respect to the extent of earthworks carried out without approval.
i)       The development application was not supported by a Detailed Visual Impact Assessment as required by the Tweed Scenic Landscape Protection Policy.
j)       The scale on the Driveway and Access Plans are incorrect. 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is consistent with the provisions of Clause 7.2 of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 relating to earthworks, and particularly the likely disruption of, or any detrimental effect on, drainage patterns and soil stability in the locality of the development, and potential for adverse impacts of any waterway. 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is consistent with the provisions of Clause 7.6 of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 relating to stormwater management. The application fails to satisfy the consent authority that the existing works and proposed works will not have a detrimental effect on the receiving waters of the site or area, including the Tweed River. Therefore, the application fails to demonstrate that it avoids significant adverse impacts from stormwater runoff. 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is consistent with the provisions of Clause 7.10 of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 as they relate to disposal and management of sewage, stormwater management and suitable vehicular access. The Onsite Sewer Management Assessment Report does not consider the additional load from the likely number of employees and from the horse washing bays. Therefore, the consent authority is not satisfied that adequate provision for the disposal and management of sewage could be achieved. The application fails to adequately address the matter of stormwater in respect of Structure A: Large Stable and Training Facility and associated hardstand areas. The application contains insufficient information to ensure that the driveway grade and width is acceptable for the likely vehicles that will access the site. The NSW Rural Fire Service in accordance with the Planning for Bushfire Protection 2019, require a 4m wide carriageway which has not been detailed on the application plans. The existing driveway is predominantly 3.5m wide. In addition, the application fails to address how during periods of no rain, how the rainwater tanks located at the rear of Structure A could be refilled. 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied the proposal is consistent with the provisions of Clauses 2.10 and 2.11 of State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021 as they relate to designing and siting development to avoid an adverse impact on the integrity and resilience of the biophysical, hydrological (surface and groundwater) and ecological environment, water quality, riparian vegetation, and the visual amenity and scenic qualities of the coast. It is considered that the bulk, scale and size of the large shed on an exposed ridgeline has an adverse visual impact on the surrounding coastal and built environment. In addition, the development is not consistent with the Tweed River Estuary Coastal Management Program as enlivened by Clause 2.13 – development in coastal zone generally – coastal management programs to be considered. 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development does not meet Essential Energy’s requirements pursuant to Clause 2.48 of State Environmental Planning Policy (Transport and Infrastructure) 2021. 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority is not satisfied that the application has addressed the requirements of the Water Management Act 2000 in relation to proposed/required works within 40m of waterway. 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application has not provided adequate information to satisfy Council that the application complies with the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008. The application has not demonstrated compliance with the following sections:
  1. Section A2 – Site Access and Parking Code – No landowners consent from Council has been sought or given in respect to works proposed in Council’s road reserve to relocate the entry statement (gate and fence) and remove excess concrete. Insufficient information has been provided with the application to determine the type of vehicles accessing the site, and whether the current grade or width of the driveway is compliant with AS2890. The application also fails to demonstrate that there is sufficient turn-around area for the expected heavy vehicles delivering or collecting livestock and parking for employees and visitors. 
  2. Section A15 – Waste Minimisation and Management – Insufficient information has been provided with the application to detail how operational waste and animal waste will be managed. 
  3. Section A16 – Preservation of Trees or Vegetation – Insufficient information has been provided to support the application to ensure the ongoing health and protection of two trees impacted by the construction of Structure A: Large Stable and Training Facility.
  4. Section A19 – Biodiversity and Habitat Management – The application does not address the significant encroachment of Structure C within the nominated watercourse buffer zone, or provide sufficient information to ensure that any cumulative adverse impacts on water quality and function of the watercourse/riparian zone are avoided and mitigated. Furthermore, the submitted Bushfire Assessment Report indicates the asset protection zone of Structure A is within an area of remnant vegetation to the east of the site. This remnant vegetation comprises mature native canopy trees including preferred Koala food trees species (Eucalyptus microcorys – Tallowwood) regarded as a red-flagged value. Council will not support an asset protection zone encroachment into the remanent vegetation unit.  

  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority considers that the visual impact associated with the works, in particular Structure A: Large Stable and Training Facility, the concrete driveway and the associated earthworks constitutes a scar on the landscape and results in an unacceptable visual impact. 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority cannot be satisfied that due consideration has been given to the proposed landscaping associated with Structure A: Large Stable and Training Facility in respect to bushfire hazard. 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the consent authority cannot be satisfied that this application represents a true reflection of the activities undertaken in relation to ‘Tumby Park’ holistically. The holding of ‘Tumby Park’ includes another two allotments (Lot 61 DP 774633 and Lot 8 DP 113331) and associated structures, facilities and access points, which have not been detailed or included in this application, and also required approval. 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, for the preceding reasons, the application is not considered to be in the public interest. 
B.  Council delegates to the General Manager the authority to conduct the appeals and instruct its’ solicitors on behalf of Council.

C.  ATTACHMENT 2 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr James Owen, Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Kimberly Hone
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Brenda Stuttle from the Living Waters Church, Tumbulgum.


Hi Everyone, 
its good to be back to pray for this Community and you all.   Running a small business and Church I have a saying “Team work makes the Dream work”, scripturally it says where there is unity God commands a blessing so it’s from this reference point I’d like to pray.

Dear Heavenly Father, 
Thankyou for your continued grace. We are blessed to live in this great Nation and especially the Tweed Shire. 
Help us to serve with a humble heart and think of our brothers and sisters who work alongside us. Let us be ever mindful of the needs of others and to put others before ourselves. 
Lord we pray for the hurting at this time, those who are displaced through financial and physical hardships. 
Give us wisdom to have strategies and practical ideas to help those in need. Help us to not be overwhelmed with the needs, but give us the strength to do good. 
Lord I pray a blessing over every household  and every person here or who is listening. 
The Lord bless you and keep you, the Lord make His face shine upon you and be gracious to you; 
The Lord lift up His countenance upon you and give you peace. 
In Jesus precious name.
Amen

CONFIDENTIAL COMMITTEE

REPRESENTATIONS FOR ITEMS CONSIDERED IN COMMITTEE
(Sec 3.40, 13.9 to 13.17 Model Code of Meeting Practice)
 
Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.
 
EXCLUSION OF PRESS AND PUBLIC

Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor) 
Cr Kimberly Hone
   
RESOLVED that Council moves itself into a Confidential Committee in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993 and that the press and public be excluded from the whole of the Committee Meeting, because, in the opinion of the Committee, publicity of the proceedings of the Committee would be prejudicial to the public interest, by reasons of the confidential nature of the business to be transacted.   
   
The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes.

AMENDMENT 1
Cr Nola Firth
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council endorses the attached submission in relation to Circular 24-17 Councillor conduct and meeting practices – a discussion paper for lodgement with the Office of Local Government with the following amendment:
