AMENDMENT 2
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council endorses the attached submission in relation to Circular 24-17 Councillor conduct and meeting practices – a discussion paper for lodgement with the Office of Local Government with the following amendments:

  1. Remove from Q6 the last paragraph: 'Similarly, a councillor engaged in property development outside of the local government area in which they serve should not be disqualified but they should be excluded from developing in the area whilst in office and for a period of ten years after serving in office.'
  1. Remove in Q6 the sentence: 'However, we do not believe the same level of risk applies to real estate agents, especially in more rural areas, including stock and station agents. Excluding them may unnecessarily disqualify potential candidates.'
 
The Amendment was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr James Owen.


AMENDMENT 3
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council endorses the attached submission in relation to Circular 24-17 Councillor conduct and meeting practices – a discussion paper for lodgement with the Office of Local Government with the following amendments:

  1. Remove from Q6 the last paragraph: 'Similarly, a councillor engaged in property development outside of the local government area in which they serve should not be disqualified but they should be excluded from developing in the area whilst in office and for a period of ten years after serving in office.'
  1. Remove in Q6 the sentence: 'However, we do not believe the same level of risk applies to real estate agents, especially in more rural areas, including stock and station agents. Excluding them may unnecessarily disqualify potential candidates.'

  2. Under Q7 re the Privileges Committee, include that Committee should be made up of past Mayors, rather than current ones. 
 
The Amendment was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr James Owen.


AMENDMENT 4
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council endorses the attached submission in relation to Circular 24-17 Councillor conduct and meeting practices – a discussion paper for lodgement with the Office of Local Government with the following amendments:

  1. Remove from Q6 the last paragraph: 'Similarly, a councillor engaged in property development outside of the local government area in which they serve should not be disqualified but they should be excluded from developing in the area whilst in office and for a period of ten years after serving in office.'
  1. Remove in Q6 the sentence: 'However, we do not believe the same level of risk applies to real estate agents, especially in more rural areas, including stock and station agents. Excluding them may unnecessarily disqualify potential candidates.'

  2. Under Q7 re the Privileges Committee, include that Committee should be made up of past Mayors, rather than current ones. 

  3. Add into the relevant section that we do not support the imposition of requiring Councillors to stand when the Mayor enters, or to stand when speaking in the chamber.
 
The Amendment was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr James Owen.


AMENDMENT 5
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council endorses the attached submission in relation to Circular 24-17 Councillor conduct and meeting practices – a discussion paper for lodgement with the Office of Local Government with the following amendments:

  1. Remove from Q6 the last paragraph: 'Similarly, a councillor engaged in property development outside of the local government area in which they serve should not be disqualified but they should be excluded from developing in the area whilst in office and for a period of ten years after serving in office.'
  1. Remove in Q6 the sentence: 'However, we do not believe the same level of risk applies to real estate agents, especially in more rural areas, including stock and station agents. Excluding them may unnecessarily disqualify potential candidates.'

  2. Under Q7 re the Privileges Committee, include that Committee should be made up of past Mayors, rather than current ones. 

  3. Add into the relevant section that we do not support the imposition of requiring Councillors to stand when the Mayor enters, or to stand when speaking in the chamber.

  4. Add in Suggest a requirement for elected Councillors to undergo Councillor inductions and mandatory training in each term and if that training is not undertaken and passed within 12 months then the Councillor is suspended until it is completed.  The role of Councillor needs to have a certain level of training to ensure each Councillor is operating to the best of their ability and has a basic understanding of the role and legislative requirements. 
 
The Amendment 5 was Carried on the Casting Vote of the Mayor.

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Kimberly Hone
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  Cr James Owen.


AMENDMENT 6
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council endorses the attached submission in relation to Circular 24-17 Councillor conduct and meeting practices – a discussion paper for lodgement with the Office of Local Government with the following amendments:

  1. Remove from Q6 the last paragraph: 'Similarly, a councillor engaged in property development outside of the local government area in which they serve should not be disqualified but they should be excluded from developing in the area whilst in office and for a period of ten years after serving in office.'
  1. Remove in Q6 the sentence: 'However, we do not believe the same level of risk applies to real estate agents, especially in more rural areas, including stock and station agents. Excluding them may unnecessarily disqualify potential candidates.'

  2. Under Q7 re the Privileges Committee, include that Committee should be made up of past Mayors, rather than current ones. 

  3. Add into the relevant section that we do not support the imposition of requiring Councillors to stand when the Mayor enters, or to stand when speaking in the chamber.

  4. Add in Suggest a requirement for elected Councillors to undergo Councillor inductions and mandatory training in each term and if that training is not undertaken and passed within 12 months then the Councillor is suspended until it is completed.  The role of Councillor needs to have a certain level of training to ensure each Councillor is operating to the best of their ability and has a basic understanding of the role and legislative requirements. 

  5. The Code be amended to include the ability for the OLG/Minister to issue a Performance Improvement Notice on one or more councillors as opposed to the whole council where warranted.
 
The Amendment was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Kimberly Hone

(g)    advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege
  

The Motion was Carried

VOTE AGAINST - Cr Kimberly Hone

Cr Kimberly Hone

The Mayor acknowledged the Bundjalung Aboriginal Nation with the following statement:

“We wish to acknowledge the Ngandowal and Minyungbal speaking people of the Bundjalung country in particular the Goodjinburra, Tul-gi-gin and Moorung - Moobah clans as being the traditional owners and custodians of the land and waters within the Tweed Shire boundaries. We also acknowledge and respect the Tweed Aboriginal community’s right to speak for its Country and to care for its traditional Country in accordance with its lore, customs and traditions.”

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Tay Lee of the Tweed Valley Uniting Church in Murwillumbah.

 
God, We bring you our gratitude today.
In this Bundjalung Country, we see your abundant blessing, and we are so grateful. 
For the diversity and wealth of this land and its people, for its beautiful mountains, valleys, creeks and forests, God, we thank you for your blessing and goodness. We ask that your blessing continually pour out this shire so that your ways may be known in our communities and all creation and people live in harmony, peace, abundance and care. 
 
God, we thank you for all our civil servants. 
Thank you for their hard work and sacrifice. God bless them. Give them wise and discerning hearts to govern the people in our shire skilfully. Give the mayor, councillors, and staff the wisdom they need today in this place to make better decisions, solve problems, distinguish between right and wrong, and bring order, stability, and prosperity to our community.
 
God, we entrust the future of Tweed Shire into Your loving and mighty hands. May this shire be where love, justice, and harmony prevail. May everyone love, help, and support one another here in your presence. 

In Jesus' name, we pray.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Hone asks can the General Manager or a delegate please advise Council of when we can expect construction to begin on the Tweed Coast Road from the freeway to Cudgen lights?

Director Engineering replies.

Land acquisitions, environmental assessments, community consultation and designs are in progress and the completion of detailed designs is programmed for Mid 2025.  It is therefore anticipated that construction will commence in April 2026 with completion in early 2028.

RESOLVED that:

  1. The following tabled Petitions be received.

    • Petition containing 21 signatories, of which 21 were valid received on 4 November 2024 entitled "Buried Whale at Pottsville " advising as follows:
      We the undersigned demand an urgent investigation into the decision making process which resulted in a juvenile humpback whale being buried in the beach 900m south of Black Rocks Pottsville NSW.

      We want to gain understanding by way of a written Statement as to why Tweed Shire Council in coordination with National Parks & Wildlife Service, picked up the deceased whale moving it 200m north and had it buried in Tweed Shire Council land. If it could be moved 200m why couldn't it be moved a further 700m to the all access vehicle track at South Black Rocks?

      We want to know why the position statement put out by NSW Department of Environment & Heritage 'review' into the management of deceased whales' was ignored given that the whale was in a location readily accessible by heavy earthworks equipment, in addition to the fact that the position statement expressly states no more burying deceased whales in urban or high visitation areas, which this location is. Review into the management of deceased whales - Environment and Heritage

      More importantly however we want to the whale removed as soon as possible with a Tweed Shire Council policy put in place in alignment with other local councils in our area, that whales be removed and disposed of off the beach permanently, so we the community don't have to address this again in the future.

    • Petition containing 1,699 signatories, of which 1,014 were valid (with 240 being invalid due to incomplete details, and 445 signatories were from out of the shire) received on 27 October 2024 entitled "Petition to Save Norries Headland" advising as follows:
      Norries Headland is cherished by locals and visitors alike and has been for generations. Its spectacular view of the ocean is invaluable 'blue space' for our community. Its accessibility by car is critical for our seniors, parents with young children and anyone that wishes to access the powerful mental health benefits 'blue space' provides.

      The Tweed Shire Council 'Norries Headland Masterplan' will close the carpark at great expense, destroying the Norries Headland we know and love.

      We the undersigned call on Tweed Shire Councillors to join Councillor Reece Byrnes to scrap the current 'Norries Headland Masterplan', to save rate payers money, retain the 'blue space' carpark and SAVE Norries Headland for generations to come!

    • Petition containing 46 signatories, of which 45 were valid (with 1 being invalid due to incomplete details) received on 31 October 2024 entitled "Regarding the Road Reserve Area at the end of Creek Street, Hastings Point" advising as follows:

      For some years, the traffic has been entering the reserve are at the end of Creek Street, Hastings Point. This no through road previously had a barrier to prevent traffic entering, eroding the track causing large pot holes, people getting bogged and for security and safety reasons by Tweed Shire Council, however there is no barrier now.

      There have been some problems including Police moving on an illegal camper who entered through resident's properties to access North Star Resort Facilities. Recently a resident had an incident of physical altercation by an illegal camper (photos and dates available)/ Residents are also concerned about fire hazards, hygiene and rubbish issues.

      Entering this track have been aggressive people getting bogged, others looking for places to camp and joy riding and hooning, this has happened often and very late at night. All these vehicles have contributed to the development of very large pot holes retaining water causing deterioration of the track and also contributing to the health hazards that result from mosquitoes and midges.

      Property owners are requesting that Council block off Creek Street Reserve road traffic and reinstate the barrier as it was previously. Council, fire and police to only have access.

      Residents who live at this community village in North Star Resort are very concerned for their safety and security.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Owen asks what progress has been made on the feasibility study for the Indoor Sporting Facility and 50m Olympic Sized Swimming Pool?

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, the following work has been undertaken in relation to this project:
  • a Request for Offer has been issued for the feasibility analysis 
  • a terms of reference for a Project Reference Group has been drafted, expressions of interest will be sought prior to the end of the year
  • as part of the Councillor induction, the General Manager of North Sydney Council provided a presentation on the North Sydney Olympic Pool redevelopment to inform the project
  • consultation has been undertaken with Logan City Council in relation to their indoor sports centre feasibility analysis, and
  • advice is being sought on potential partnership options.
It should be noted that this project is considered a medium-long term project as Council does not have the funds or resources to deliver it in the short term.  Council has over $1billion of capital works projects to be delivered over the next 4-5 years.  Should Council decide to proceed with this project, considerable funding will need to be secured, relevant approval sought, and resources allocated to deliver the project.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Owen asks what options are available to Council to address the homelessness, illegal parking, antisocial & criminal behaviour, littering, environmental damage, river pollution and community concerns occurring on Keith Compton Drive, Tweed Heads?

Cr Hone temporarily left the meeting at 05:59pm.

Through you Madam Mayor, the matter of homelessness, anti-social and criminal behaviour is the remit of the State Government, as such matters should be referred to the relevant agency such as Assertive Outreach for homelessness and the Police for anti-social and criminal behaviour.   Council’s role in this space is predominantly advocacy. 
 
In response to the illegal camping and parking on Keith Compton Drive, Council recently installed ‘no camping’ signs.  Council’s Rangers Team and the Police have recently undertaken joint patrols around the area targeting illegal camping and parking, and anti-social behaviour.  The patrols have been successful with tents and campers moved on and the area tidied up.   The neighbouring community have expressed their appreciation.  Patrols will continue. 
 
With regards to options for legally parked camper vans and cars, Council could request the Local Traffic Committee to consider a residents parking permit system or paid parking system.
 
With regards to littering and illegal dumping, this can be reported to the Environmental Protection Authority’s through ‘report a tosser’ and any illegal dumping should also be reported to the Environmental Protection Authority.  This can be done online through their website.  Similarly with environmental damage and river pollution.  There is also the option to report river pollution to NSW Fisheries.  Council’s role in this area is again, an advocacy role.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Owen asks what options are there to address the ibis poo problem adjacent to Freckles Kindy & Learning Centre on Limosa Road, Tweed Heads West?

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, on 18 February 2021 Council resolved to investigate the use of lighting or wind spinners to deter roosting ibises in the forest red gum, and in the event that lighting the tree is not found to be an appropriate tool to reduce the ibis roosting population then:

  • investigate options to plant mature stock trees in the vicinity to offset any potential tree removal, allowing the establishment over an 18/24 month period, and during this time manage the ibis issue on-site as needed, and
  • if Ibis remain – Council can consider removing the tree.
Since the resolution officers have managed the ibis and tree concerns by engaging an external service provider to implement an ibis management plan, and through regular tree inspections as needed in line with Council’s Tree Management Protocol. This approach was largely effective in managing the ibis roosting issues, noting that it was a seasonal problem and there was no guarantee the ibis would not return.   Since the completion of the management plan in 2021 no customer service requests were lodged by the Centre until July 2024.  In June 2024 Council’s qualified arborist inspected the tree who noted it to be in a sound and healthy condition.  Decisions regarding tree management are governed by Council’s Tree Management Protocol to ensure consistent decision-making.
  
The tree is a native forest red gum, approximately 20m in height and estimated to be greater than 80 years.   Given this and its condition, Officers do not recommend removal.

Ongoing management options investigated and/or trialled during this period also include:

  • up lighting, however this was not deemed suitable due to flight path issues, and the structure of the tree 
  • mature tree offsetting, however this was not deemed suitable or feasible due to the lack of space in the immediate area due to existing tree density and amenity impact on residents, and
  • further tree audits/assessments have been undertaken.
If the ibis continue to be an issue Council can revisit the ibis management plan for ongoing dispersal for a period of time and at a cost, or further pursue the tree removal option.  The latter could be pursued by a Councillor through a notice of motion.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks can we please have a detailed update on the actions taken to date by Tweed Shire Council since resolution of February 15, 2024 titled 'Tweed CBD'?

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, the following has been undertaken in relation to the resolution of 15 February:

  • Council increased the graffiti removal budget at the December quarterly budget review to fund a dedicated graffiti removal crew for six months. The team commenced in July and have been targeting graffiti removal in the Tweed CBD areas, cleaning of key CBD public furniture and other assets including bench seats, bin enclosures etc , cleaning/gerning of CBD pathways, streetscapes, landscaped areas, and bus shelters
  • The north and southbound bus shelters and nearby taxi shelters located at the northern end of Wharf St adjacent to Bay street have been replaced, along with various sections of footpath and lighting. 
  • An audit was undertaken of the Tweed CBD surrounding streets, parks and infrastructure in March.  Actions undertaken as a result of this includes:
  • cleaning of bins, benches, paths, walkways, gutters, sidewalk, and kerbs
  • removal of old business signs
  • graffiti removal
  • additional planting and landscaping in various areas
  • tree trimming near bus shelters and the visitor information centre to improve lines of sight
  • replacement of street lights on Wharf Street
  • removal of various seating, and
  • regular abandoned trolley collection.
  • Construction of the Jack Evans Boat Harbour Places to Swim project has been completed
  • The Police and Council’s Rangers team have undertaken a number of joint operations targeting anti-social behaviour and illegal camping in the Tweed CBD, and
  • A safety audit was recently undertaken by the Police and Council for the Tweed CBD.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks can we please have an update on the actions taken by Tweed Shire Council to date since July 18, 2024 NOM titled 'Pontoon for Kimberley Lake, Banora Point'?

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, Council staff have requested advice from the National Parks and Wildlife Service on issues to consider when assessing the feasibility of a potential floating wildlife refuge island on Lake Kimberley that is suitable to be used by black swans and other native birds for nesting.  Preliminary advice indicates expertise in artificial fauna habitat is required.  Funding will need to be considered following the feasibility assessment which will determine whether investment into a floating refuge island or other device is appropriate and effective.  If this is the course of action taken, relevant permits and approvals will be required.

The scope and methodology for consultation on issues facing Lake Kimberley and the surrounding area is being developed and coordinated with the organisation’s other consultation priorities.

Lastly, Ranger patrols have been increased around Lake Kimberley, noting that the issue is generally during the breeding season.

RESOLVED that: 
 
  1. Development Application DA24/0388 for a 20 lot community title subdivision comprising of 19 residential lots and 1 common property lot at Lot 3 DP 250581; No. 4A Boyle Avenue Banora Point be refused for the following reasons: 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application does not provide sufficient information to determine that the proposal complies with the following clauses of the State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021 – Chapter 2 Coastal Management:
    1. Section 2.8 regarding potential impacts to the coastal wetlands resulting from the proposed earthworks and proposed residential use of the site;
    2. Section 2.10 regarding potential impacts to the coastal environment area resulting from the proposed earthworks; 
    3. Section 2.11 regarding potential impacts on land within the coastal area resulting from the proposal.
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application does not provide sufficient information to determine that the proposal complies with the provisions of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014 (TLEP). Specifically, consent cannot be granted to the development unless the following clauses are satisfied: 
    1. Section 5.21 Flood Planning in that the proposal has not demonstrated that appropriate measures are incorporated into the development to manage the risk of life in the event of a flood; 
    2. Section 7.6 Stormwater Management regarding the avoidance and minimisation of stormwater runoff on adjoining properties, native bushland and receiving waters; 
    3. Section 7.10 Essential Services regarding appropriate stormwater management, suitable vehicle access to individual lots.  
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, insufficient information has been submitted to adequately consider the application with respect to the following clause of TLEP: 
    1. Section 5.10 Heritage Conservation in that an investigation of potential Aboriginal Cultural Heritage has not been submitted for the site; 
    2. Section 7.2 Earthworks in that sufficient information has been submitted to determine the impact of the proposed earthworks on the natural and built environment including heritage. 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application does not provide sufficient information to determine the proposal complies with the provisions of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 (DCP). Specifically, the following sections:
    1. Section A2 Site Access and Parking code with regard to compliant access to individual lots; 
    2. Section A5 Subdivision Manual  with regard to site constraints and impact on the natural and built environment;
    3. Section A16 Biting Midge and Mosquito Control regarding a biting insect management plan; 
    4. Section A15 Waste Minimisation and Management Plan regarding servicing of the community title development. 
    5. Section A19 Biodiversity and Habitat Management regarding setbacks of infrastructure to red flagged areas. 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application does not provide sufficient information to determine the likely   impacts of the proposal, specifically in relation to: 
    1. Impacts on ecological values of the site. The proposal has not provided an adequate assessment against the SEPP (Resilience and Hazards) 2021 and the Tweed Coast Comprehensive Koala Plan of Management or the impact of the proposed stormwater infrastructure on native vegetation; 
    2. Scenic Landscape Protection Policy. The proposal has not provided an assessment of this policy to determine if the visual impacts of the proposal are considered to be acceptable. 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application does not provide sufficient information to determine if the site is suitable for the proposal, specifically in relation to: 
    1. The bush fire hazard of the site. The RFS have noted that the provided slope assessment averaged out the slopes which ignored the variable nature of the topography of the site. 
    2. Topography. The proposal requires extensive earthworks, fill and retaining walls to facilitate the development. Insufficient geotechnical information has been submitted to determine of the proposed works are suitable to the topography and future residential use of the site.  
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(d) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, there is insufficient information in the application to enable to adequate consideration of the 31 submissions received in relation to the proposal. 
 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application is not considered to be in the public interest as Council is unable to determine if the proposal complies with the statutory controls and the DCP. The proposal as submitted would result in an unacceptable impact on the natural environment. 
 
  1. Council delegates the General Manager the authority to conduct the appeal and instructs its’ solicitors on behalf of Council and engage consultants to act as Council’s expert witnesses where required.
 
  1. ATTACHMENT 3 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:
    (e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law
 
The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Father Paul McDonald of St Anthony's Catholic Church in Kingscliff.


Loving God,

We gather here today at the conclusion of another year of service to our community.

We thank You for the opportunities we have had to work together for the good of all in the Tweed Shire.

As we come to this final meeting, we ask for Your guidance and wisdom.

Bless us with clarity and insight as we consider the important matters on our agenda.

Help us to discern what is best for the people we serve and to act with fairness, integrity, and compassion.

Lord, as we approach the season of Christmas, we pray for Your protection and blessing upon all Councillors, staff, and their families. Grant them a time of rest joy, and peace.

Keep them safe in their travels and bring them renewed strength for the year ahead.

We also lift up in prayer all those in our community.

May this Christmas be a time of hope and kindness for all, especially those who may be lonely, struggling, or in need.

Inspire us to continue working together in unity, building a community where everyone is valued and supported.

In your name, we pray. ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:
  1. adopts the Tweed Conservation Strategy 2025-2035, replacing the Tweed Vegetation Management Strategy 2004, as a guide for future planning with the following changes:
    1. p13, add another dot point under 'Through actions outlined in the strategy Council commits to': 
            minimise our impact on the environment, protect and improve the health of our land, waterways and native wildlife and mitigate the impacts of climate change.
    2. p. 28, 3.7 add 'while ensuring protection of the environment'.
  2. approves the transfer of the budget allocation from the Tweed Vegetation Management Strategy to the Tweed Conservation Strategy.
  3. retains reference to the Tweed Vegetation Management Strategy vegetation, ecological sensitivity, and ecological priority mapping until these are updated by completing the relevant actions within the Tweed Conservation Strategy 2025-2035.

Cr James Owen
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

RESOLVED that Development Application DA24/0445 for use of general industrial units and installation of signage at Lot 216 DP 1122768 No. 8-12 Honeyeater Circuit, South Murwillumbah be refused for the following reasons:

  1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development fails to satisfy the aims of Tweed Local Environmental Plan (TLEP) 2014 as far as it giving effect the desired outcome in accordance with Councils adopted strategic planning documents given that it forms a type of development that is prohibited in the zone.

  2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development fails to satisfy Clause 2.3 TLEP2014 as it is a type of Commercial Premises which is prohibited in the E4 – General Industrial zone.

  3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development is unlikely to provide the required onsite parking given the rates of parking for retail uses are far greater than general industrial land uses. Therefore, the development has failed to satisfy Section A2 of Tweed DCP 2008.

  4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development is likely to have adverse economic impacts due to the limited supply of General Industrial land that is suitable for industrial activities and the underutilisation of the subject site as a retail premises.

  5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the subject site is not suitable for the development given it forms a prohibited land use in the E4 General Industrial zone.

  6. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal is not considered to be in the public interest due it not being permissible in the E4 General Industrial zone.

  7. Pursuant to Clause 24 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation (2021), the application is insufficient to undertake a proper assessment in relation to carparking having regard to the format of the subject site and the proposed uses (i.e. site plan for the proposal relevant to all approved buildings on the site and the approved strata allocation).
 
The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Cr James Owen
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

RESOLVED that Council:

 

  1. Receives the Minutes of the Aboriginal Advisory Committee Meeting held Friday 1 March 2024.
      
  2. Adopts the Aboriginal Advisory Committee's recommendations of Friday 1 March 2024 as follows:
Item A3.    Request for Support and Collaboration on Dual Naming Initiative for Tweed Tourism Projects
That the Aboriginal Advisory Committee endorses the use of dual naming for the following locations: 
1. Joongurrabah - Cook Island 
2. Joongurrabah – Razorback Lookout
3. Wollumbin – Mt Warning
4. Booninybah – Fingal Headland
5. MyNgagambi – Point Danger
6. Bogangar / Bogangah – Cabarita
7. Cooloon – Tweed Heads.
 
  1. Receives the Minutes of the Aboriginal Advisory Committee Meeting held Friday 5 April 2024.

  2. Receives the Minutes of the Aboriginal Advisory Committee Meeting held Friday 7 June 2024.
      
  3. Adopts the Aboriginal Advisory Committee's recommendations of Friday 7 June 2024 as follows:
Item BA3.    Minutes from 1 March 2024 and 5 April 2024 meetings - Request for Support and Collaboration on Dual Naming Initiative for Tweed Tourism Projects (Sally Scott - The Tweed Tourism Co)
 
RECOMMENDATION: That the Aboriginal Advisory Committee: 
1. Does not support its recommendation from the minutes of Friday 1 March 2024 meeting “Agenda Item A3” and retracts the endorsement for the use of dual naming by Tweed Tourism Co (TTC) for the following locations:
  • Joongurrabah Ngarian - Cook Island 
  • Joongurrabah – Razorback Lookout
  • Wollumbin – Mt Warning
  • Booninybah – Fingal Headland
  • MyNgagambi – Point Danger
  • Bogangar - Cabarita. Request to ensure a clear distinction that Cabarita is the beach and Bogangar is the location.
  • Minjungbal – Tweed Heads.  Minjungbal to be changed to ‘Cooloon’ as Minjungbal is a language, and the place is Cooloon

2.  Supports the need for further consultation as discussed at its meeting on Friday 5 April 2024 at Business Arising - A3: “The AAC emphasised the need for further consideration and consultation with local Aboriginal communities before approval of the dual naming. The AAC stressed the importance of ensuring educational value, promoting truth-telling, and respecting Aboriginal culture and history.”
  
3.  Requests that staff from Tweed Tourism Co and other tourism operators that offer Aboriginal Cultural content participate in Cultural awareness training before any decisions are made regarding the Aboriginal Advisory Committee’s support of Tweed Tourism Co using dual naming.
 
4.  Requests Tweed Shire Council to write a formal letter to Tweed Tourism Co requesting that staff from Tweed Tourism Co and other tourism operators that offer Aboriginal Cultural content participate in Cultural awareness training to continue to foster respectful relationships between Tweed Tourism Co staff, Aboriginal Advisory Committee members and the broader Bundjalung Community. Letter to address the Aboriginal Advisory Committee’s concerns that the importance of ensuring educational value, promoting truth-telling, and respecting Aboriginal culture and history is not compromised and cultural integrity is upheld.
 
Item A2. Welcome to Country on Australia Day
 
RECOMMENDATION: That the Aboriginal Advisory Committee supports the Welcome to Country to take place at the Australia Day Ceremony for 2025, under the conditions:
  • That the Aboriginal Advisory Committee to nominate an individual from community to perform the Welcome each year.
  • That the nominated individual accepts the nominations and is comfortable to perform the Welcome to Country.
  • The Welcome to Country conversation to be re-visited annually with the Aboriginal Advisory Committee.
  • The Aboriginal Advisory Committee nominates Dedrie Currie to be consulted by Tweed Shire Council to perform Welcome to Country at 2025 Ceremony.

  1. Receives the Minutes of the Aboriginal Advisory Committee Meeting held Thursday 1 August 2024.
      
  2. Adopts the Aboriginal Advisory Committee's recommendation of Thursday 1 August 2024 as follows: 
Item BA1.    Request for Support and Collaboration on Dual Naming Initiative for Tweed Tourism Projects 
 Following adoption of the minutes of 7 June 2024, the AAC confirmed the following: 
 1.  Minjungbal – Tweed Heads to be changed to ‘Cooloon’ as Minjungbal is a language, and the place is Cooloon.
 2.  Approved the wording of the draft letter to Tweed Tourism Co.  
 
RECOMMENDATION: That the Aboriginal Advisory Committee approves the wording of the draft letter to Tweed Tourism Co and approves the sending of the letter.

8. Adopts the Executive Leadership Team's recommendation for the following item from Thursday 1 August 2024:

 Item BA4. CEO-Aboriginal to consult with Governance regarding the Committee's concerns of slander, resulting from the public display of Committee minutes on Council's website.

RECOMMENDATION: That Council notes the Aboriginal Advisory Committee’s safety concerns and take action to mitigate and address AAC member concerns by:

  1. Implementing changes to the format of Committee minutes that are compliant with relevant legislation.
  2. Introducing a process for members to report any safety incidents to Council so that appropriate action can be taken and support can be provided to Committee members. 
 
The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Councillor Brinsmead asks can we please receive an update on actions taken to date with respect to the NOM titled: Protecting Tweed Shire Animals Marine and Birdlife From Improperly Discarded Fishing Line and Gear?

Director Sustainable Communities & Environment replies.

Councillor Brinsmead asks can we please receive an update on actions taken to date with respect to the NOM titled: Short-term solution to desperate need for basketball courts in the Tweed?

Director Sustainable Communities & Environment replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, Council staff and Tweed Valley basketball representatives have made good progress in negotiating short and medium-term outcomes for basketball in the Tweed region resulting in the following:
  • Mount St Patricks College have commenced the process to obtain relevant reports and information to lodge a DA modification to utilise the school indoor sports centre for community use. Council staff have provided the school with preliminary advice on matters such as noise monitoring, parking, and consultation with local residents
  • Wollumbin High School will provide ongoing access to utilise the schools indoor sports centre, a single court timber floor facility suitable for training purposes
  • Kingscliff High School will provide access to the school indoor sports centre from late January 2025, a single court timber floor facility suitable for training purposes, and
  • Murwillumbah High School have indicated their in-principle support to utilise the school indoor sports centre following the completion of construction works anticipated post April/May 2025.

It should be noted that the ongoing issue of identifying a suitable facility for games and tournaments for the Association remains as all of the above facilities are only suitable for training purposes.

Councillor Brinsmead asks if there are plans to expand the current green bin service to units and rural areas? 

Director Sustainable Communities & Environment replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, Council currently offers an elective Food Organics and Garden Organics (FOGO) services to multi-unit developments and to rural properties that are on the connecting road to urban properties.  

In late November 2024 proposed amendments to the Protection of the Environment Operations Act (FOGO Recycling) Bill 2024 were released which are due to be discussed in Parliament on the first sitting day next year (11 Feb, 2025).
 
The overview states the object of the Bill is to amend the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997 to provide for mandates for the source-separated collection of food organics and garden organics (FOGO) waste from households and businesses, including by, amongst other things, requiring local councils to separately collect and transport FOGO waste from households that receive a residual waste collection service from 1 July 2030.

Based on this it is highly likely that the FOGO service will be expanded to service all multi-unit developments and rural properties, however consultation will need to occur prior to its implementation as it will have cost implications on ratepayers and will require a change in waste disposal behaviour.  Council’s recent waste audit will assist in informing Council of residents’ current waste behaviour and guide how the rollout of recycling and FOGO services more widely could occur.

Councillor Brinsmead asks what action has Council taken to date to address the protracted timeline of roadworks relates to the Kings Forest development on Tweed Coast Road?

General Manager replies.

Through Madam Mayor,

I thank the Councillor for the question with notice, as it places on public record that the road works occurring on Tweed Coast Road are not that of Council, but rather the private developer of the Kings Forest estate. The works are privately contracted, Further, this is the first major subdivision in the Shire to be fully privately certified. This means that all residential allotments created within Precinct 5 will be issued by a Private Certifier and not Council.

In essence these works, the delivery and timing of the works are an example of a fully privatised and commercial operation.

Council’s involvement has been to ensure that the infrastructure, ultimately to be dedicated to Council by the developer is of a standard that meets specifications and will be delivered without defect, so as to ensure that the Tweed ratepayer is not ultimately burdened.

Council officers have been aware that some in the community have wrongfully assumed that these works are Council and have been critical of Council for the time being taken to deliver the works and also critical of the condition of the road at times with potholes or other hazards. As such, Council officers have maintained regular inspections of the site and communication with the proponent, contractor, Consulting Engineer and Certifier. Further officers have reported defects outside of normal business hours when a safety hazard occurs. A recent example of such was two weekends ago when a pothole of significant size and safety risk was brought to Council’s attention by a Councillor. The proponent’s contractor was onsite within a matter of hours to affect the repair.

With specific reference to the representations made regarding the timing of the delivery, Council officers have maintained daily inspection reports which highlight defects that need to be addressed so as to ensure the delivery is not prolonged through infrastructure needing to be ripped up and rebuilt after construction. Officers have regularly liaised with the contractors in regard to dewatering, traffic management signage, temporary lane closures, sedimentation and erosion control, adequate night lighting and temporary line marking. The appropriate management of these matters results in impacted delivery times, however, ensures a safe workplace for both the public and contractors. 

Furthermore, the significant amount of wet weather that has occurred during the construction has had a significant impact on the delivery of the works on Tweed Coast Road.  

As the General Manager I have been in phone contact with the Chairman of Leda Holdings to express the community concerns regarding the timing of delivery and Leda have responded positively to those representations. Council officers at various levels within the organisation have met and corresponded with senior staff within Leda and their consultants about possible ways to fast track the completion.

Council officers have suggested at the highest level options to fast track the completion through night works under light. Effectively recommending two shifts within a 24 hour period. Council officers have however, not agreed to the complete closure of Tweed Coast Road with detour through Kingscliff as this would be unacceptable to the community. More recently the proponent has been challenged with timing of delivery by Essential Energy with the main electricity trunk under the road works and I have assisted Leda with this challenge through a formal written request to address the timing of delivery to both Leda and Essential Energy.

If Councillors are of the mind or desire to dig a little deeper and see all council records with respect to these works and the timing of such, I refer councillors to my emails copied to you all of 20 November at 5.05PM, 9.07PM and 21 November at 10.00AM which details the appropriate means of accessing this information.

I also take this opportunity to remind councillors and the community of Council’s Report a Problem system, accessible from the Home Page of Council’s website, which has recently been enhanced for councillors and the community to quickly and easily report problems such as potholes which may occur from time to time at this worksite or any other road in the shire. Further when this process is followed, none of the matters are added to the monthly quota of Councilor requests. https://www.tweed.nsw.gov.au/council/customer-service/report-problem ;

Councillor Brinsmead asks what plans or programs (if any) does Council have to celebrate Christmas 2024 in the Tweed Shire?

Director Corporate Services replies.

Through you Madam Mayor - Council has, along with other organisations, many planned programs to celebrate Christmas 2024 across the Tweed Shire:
Programs

  • The Tweed Festive Glow Guide is back again this year after the inaugural launch in 2023.  This interactive community map encourages residents/households that want to share their light displays with the public to submit details and a pic to be loaded onto an Interactive map that families and residents can use on their mobile devices to search great places near them or drive around to see the best displays in the region.  The interactive map and links can be found here: Christmas in the Tweed | Tweed Shire Council
  • The Tweed Festive Shopfronts Guide is a new initiative for 2024 in a collaboration with business chambers and the Tweed Valley Weekly. This year we have launched a Festive display campaign to encourage shopping locally and to recognise businesses with a winner in each region of Tweed Heads and Urban Surrounds; Tweed Coast; and Murwillumbah and Rural Villages.  Businesses can submit their details with a picture to be loaded onto an interactive map.  Competition info and entries can be found here: Christmas in the Tweed | Tweed Shire Council
  • The Tweed Tourism Company is coordinating and publishing the annual Tweed Gift Guide encouraging local gift ideas from a range of tourism and business operators.
  • The Shires three Business Chambers have also historically led activations or programs in their CBD areas. Council has on occasions supported the Business Chambers with specific requests of funding or activations within their areas.  This year the Tweed Heads chamber have already secured funding for Christmas on Bay Street through a Grant, and Murwillumbah Chamber recently also held the Making Tracks event.  We understand Business Kingscliff partnered with Lions for a Carols in the Park event held last night in Kingscliff which Council financially contributed towards. Last year Business Kingscliff requested funds for Christmas Activations were put towards the lighting of the Kingscliff Fig Tree which was delivered in October 2024. 
Public Lighting and Displays
  • The Tweed Border Marker has Christmas projections scheduled from Monday 2 December to Saturday 28 December 2024.  NYE projections are scheduled from Monday 30 January to Thursday 2 January 2025.
  • The Murwillumbah bridge lights changed to festive colours on Monday 2 December 2024.
  • The Kingscliff Fig Tree was lit in October in preparation for Christmas.
  • There was a public installation of Christmas decorations after hours on Monday 2 December 2024 in:
    • Wollumbin Street, Murwillumbah Street and Alma Street roundabout
    • Wharf Street to Florence Street, Tweed Heads
  • A small display of festive decorations is again being installed at the Murwillumbah Railway Station and Northern Rivers Rail Trail, with Santa doing some surprise runs and handing our merchandise on the Rail Trail to surprise and delight.
  • Council has approved requests from Pottsville Community Association for the installation of lighting in some trees within the CBD area, providing guidance and requirements to protect all trees.  Council has also collaborated with the Pottsville Community Association and Murwillumbah Chamber of Commerce to apply for grant funding for a more permanent opportunity.
Events
  • What’s On Tweed will continue to promote the wide range of events across the region with some feature and focused Christmas events.
  • Council has sponsored three community Christmas events under the 2024-2025 Events Sponsorship funding round:
1)    Lions Club of Kingscliff – Carols by the Coast ($2,300) Tuesday 10 December 2024
2)    Murwillumbah Rotary Club – Carols in the park ($2,300) Friday 13 December 2024
3)    Pottsville Beach Community Hall – Community Christmas Day lunch ($2,300) Wednesday 25 December 2024
  • Council was successful in receiving Transport NSW funding on behalf of Tweed Chamber of Commerce to host a Christmas on Bay Street event on Saturday 14 December 2024.
Council Communications
  • A Council Community Christmas Message, led by the Mayor and featuring other Councillors is being planned and aiming to publish the week prior to Christmas.  Both a digital video and a full-page print.
  • Tweed Shire Council’s regular community message banners will be up at Tweed Heads and Murwillumbah leading into Christmas.
  • Council’s social media content will also promote much of the above and focus on education around reducing waste and availability of services over the Christmas period.
  • Council’s two front counters at Tweed and Murwillumbah will be decorated accordingly and tastefully with a focus on nature, less plastic and festive well wishes for all denominations.

Councillor Owen asks what is Council doing in preparation for the holiday season to ensure that all public bins are proactively checked and emptied on a regular basis in order to minimise inconvenience and health risks to the community?

Director Sustainable Communities & Environment replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, Council increases its waste service schedules to public placed bins across the Shire during both the NSW and Queensland holiday seasons.  The schedule is based on previous seasons, and the experience of Council officers who service those areas. Service levels can be adjusted during the season based on observations of our Parks and Open Space staff, and through lodged customer service requests.  Council also has a Waste Compliance Officer who responds to illegal dumping as needed.

Councillor Owen asks what is Council doing in preparation for the holiday season to ensure that illegal camping is proactively managed and addressed?

Director Sustainable Communities & Environment replies.

Through you Madam Mayor, in early November Council’s Rangers team commenced group patrols of identified areas of concern.  An audit of regulatory signage has been completed resulting in additional signs installed in areas where enforcement of illegal camping had been identified as being hampered by inadequate signage, such as Keith Compton Drive and Murphy’s Lane, and further signage is to be installed in other locations such as Kingscliff North and Salt.  Further to this, a series of overnight patrols have been undertaken with the Police during November and December targeting illegal camping.

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

  1. Development Application DA24/0476 for use of unauthorised building alterations and additions and change of use to include glassing of surfboards at Lot 3 SP 77153 No. 3/64-66 Ourimbah Road, Tweed Heads be refused for the following reasons:
    1. The application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate that the proposal is compliant with the National Construction Code. 
    2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, insufficient information has been submitted to demonstrate that the proposal complies with the Objectives of the E4-General Industrial zone under section 2.3. Specifically, the application has not demonstrated that the proposal will minimise adverse impacts in adjacent residential land uses.
    3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application does not provide sufficient information to determine the proposal complies with the provisions of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 (DCP). Specifically, the following sections:
      1. Section A2 – Site Access and Parking. The application has not demonstrated adequate service arrangements for service vehicles. 
      2. Section A3 – Development of Flood Liable Land. Insufficient information has been provided to demonstrate flood free storage is provided.  
    4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application does not provide sufficient information to determine the likely impacts of the proposal on the amenity of the adjoining landuses. Specifically, the application has not adequately addressed the current noise, dust and odour impacts of site operations. 
    5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application does not provide sufficient information to determine if the site is suitable for the proposal. The applicant has not demonstrated the proposal is void of adverse amenity impacts to the adjoining residences.
    6. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application is not considered to be in the public interest. The proposal as submitted has note demonstrated the use will not result in an unacceptable impact to the locality.
  2. Council delegates the General Manager the authority to conduct the Class 1 appeal against the deemed refusal of DA24/0476 and instructs its’ solicitors on behalf of Council and engage consultants to act as Council’s expert witnesses where required.

  3. ATTACHMENT 3 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

    (e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Notes the essential role of creative arts and music in fostering the vibrancy, diversity, and resilience of the Northern Rivers region. Acknowledges the creative sector’s pivotal contribution to providing spaces for connection, expression, storytelling and healing during recovery from disasters and the pandemic. The loss of SCU’s Creative Arts programs risks severing a critical pipeline for training artists and musicians, ultimately limiting the region’s capacity to sustain these vital cultural and economic contributions.

  2. Writes to Southern Cross University (SCU) to reconsider its recent decision to discontinue its undergraduate programs in art and design, contemporary music and digital media from 2025. 

  3. Seeks an online meeting to better understand from SCU the factors contributing to this decision.

  4. Writes to the relevant Federal Ministers urging them to restore equity to the cost of Arts Degrees to ensure that young people can pursue training in music and the creative arts without financial barriers so as not to deter young people from pursuing creative arts education, 

  5. Writes to relevant State Ministers to take urgent action to increase funding and other support for regional arts and music events; and

  6. Seeks the advocacy of the Northern Rivers Joint Organisation on this matter.
 
The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

The Motion was Carried

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd of the Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church:

 
Gracious God, 
 
As we commence Council meetings for the year we are grateful for Council Staff, who work hard to protect and improve our Shire.  We recognise the experience, skills, and passion they bring.  We’re conscious of their difficult work in times of great need in our community, and of their daily work done so well we often take it for granted.
 
We pray for safety as they go about their work, a deep satisfaction in their career, and a harmonious workplace.  We pray especially for any member of Staff who carries out their duties even as they bear added burdens in their personal life.
 
Thank you for the Directors as they lead their teams.  In all the challenges and opportunities that will arise this year, encourage them in their important work.
 
Bless the Councillors as they consider and implement policies that will enhance our Shire now and into the future.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen.

RECOMMENDED that:
 
  1. Development Application DA24/0043 for a staged (2 stages) construction of a dual occupancy (detached) including two swimming pools, demolition and staged strata subdivision at Lot 14 Section 4 DP 9453 No. 14 Sutherland Street, Kingscliff be refused for the following reasons:

    1. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development is inconsistent with the following clauses of the State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021:
      1. Clause 2.10 - Insufficient information has been provided to demonstrate that the proposed Stormwater Management will not have adverse impact on the integrity and resilience of the hydrological (surface and groundwater) environment.
      2. Clause 2.11 - The proposed development has not been designed and sited to mitigate adverse impacts associated with the visual amenity and scenic qualities of the coast, with particular regard to the bulk, scale and view sharing.

    2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application has not provided adequate information to satisfy Council that the proposal complies with the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014. The application has not demonstrated compliance with the following clauses:

      1. Clause 1.2 - The proposed development is not considered to be in accordance with the aims of this plan. In particular, the development does not promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed’s natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways, visual amenity and scenic routes, built environment, and cultural heritage.
      2. Clause 4.3 - The application fails to demonstrate that the proposal is fully compliant with the Height of Buildings development standard, which establishes a maximum building height of 9m.
      3. Clause 7.6 - The application fails to provide an adequately sized on-site detention system as part of the Stormwater Management to the satisfaction of the consent authority to manage the stormwater runoff.

    3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development is inconsistent with the following Sections of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008:

      1. Section A1 (Part A) – with respect to site design, building envelope controls, and building design as these relate to view sharing, streetscape and landscaping.
      2. Section A2 – with respect to provision of adequate information to maintain functionality of the existing pedestrian refuge on Sutherland Street.
      3. Section B26 – with respect to provision of building design that is responsive to the sloping site conditions and allows view sharing.

    4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the likely impact of the proposed development in its current form on nearby properties and the locality with respect to view sharing is considered to be unacceptable.

    5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate that the likely impact of the proposed vehicular access, on functionality of the pedestrian refuge on Sutherland Street is acceptable.

    6. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application has not provided adequate information to demonstrate that the site is suitable for the proposed development with regards to the building design, pedestrian refuge, and view sharing concerns.

    7. Pursuant to Sections 4.15(1)(d) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, having regard to the matters set out in the submissions with respect to view sharing, streetscape, setbacks and potential impacts, the proposed development cannot be supported.

    8. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, having regard to the insufficient information contained in the application, and the non-compliances with Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014, Tweed Development Control Plan 2008, the approval of the proposal is not considered to be in the public interest. 

  2. ATTACHMENTS 7, 8 and 9 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:
 
(e)       information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.
 

The Motion was Carried on the Casting Vote of the Mayor.

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverent Tay Lee from Tweed Valley Uniting Church. 


We lift up Tweed Shire before You today, giving thanks for the beauty of this land, the richness of its community, and the people who call it home. We ask for Your abundant blessings to rest upon this region—upon its towns, its businesses, its families, and all who work tirelessly to build a thriving and caring community.

We ask for protection and provision over this land. May the rivers flow with life, the fields flourish, and the homes be filled with love and peace. May this community be united in kindness, generosity, and a spirit of neighbourly love.

Bless the children and young people with hope and opportunity, the elderly with honour and care, and every individual with a sense of belonging and purpose. May Tweed Shire be a place where Your presence is felt, where lives are enriched, and where people experience the depth of Your love and grace.

God of wisdom and courage,

We pray for this Council meeting today. We acknowledge Your wisdom and guidance, and we seek Your presence in this meeting.

Bless our leaders with discernment, clarity, and integrity as they make decisions that impact the lives of those they represent. May their discussions be filled with wisdom, respect, and a shared commitment to justice, fairness, and the common good.

God, grant them the patience to listen, the courage to act justly, and the compassion to serve with humility. Let their words and actions reflect unity, cooperation, and a vision for a brighter future for the Shire.

God, we commit this meeting into Your hands, trusting in Your goodness and faithfulness.

In Jesus' name, we pray. Cr Kimberly Hone 
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor) 

PROPOSED that in relation to Hastings Point Wastewater Treatment Plant Performance Upgrade Options Assessment: 

  1. Council selects Option 5 in the report (Convert to a continuous MBR process with the addition of a Contact Tank) as an alternate option for the performance upgrade of the Hastings Point Wastewater Treatment Plant and a report to come back to Council on the method of funding the additional cost of this alternate option.

  2. Council considers the outcomes of the odour and noise investigations and includes in the detailed design of the Hastings Point Wastewater Treatment Plant Performance Upgrade specific measures to mitigate noise and odour issues to ensure these meet all relevant legislative and regulatory requirements following the upgrade of the plant.

  3. Council continues to work with the community to develop future recycled water opportunities to increase reuse of recycled water and minimise discharge to the Hastings dunes. 

AMENDMENT 1 

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

RESOLVED that Council:
 
  1. Notes the community petition on the upgrade of the HPWWTP.

  2. Offers community representatives a tour of the Murwillumbah WWTP to demonstrate options being discussed.

  3. Receive the current loading and holiday loading figures recently measured and adjust scope of options 4 and 5 as required in response to questions raised in peer review point 1.

  4. Receive the criteria for ‘Environmental Impacts’ and ‘Operational Performance and Compliance’ as employed in the multi criteria analysis as suggested in peer review point 10 and 11.

  5. Request a meeting with the peer review consultant to discuss findings of the review.

  6. Conduct a capacity assessment of the current system including a review of the need for alkalinity correction and cause of poor nitrogen removal to further refine the scope of options 4 and 5 as recommended in points 1,2,4,5,7, 11 and 12.

  7. Conduct a new Odour model to check assumption made and adjust scope of Options 4 and 5 as necessary

  8. Advance option 4 and 5 to a more accurate estimate of cost.

  9. Pursues State or Federal funding for Option 5. 

  10. Include consideration of Option 5 in the upcoming budget documents.  

  11. Council considers the outcomes of the odour and noise investigations and includes in the detailed design of the Hastings Point Wastewater Treatment Plant Performance Upgrade specific measures to mitigate noise and odour issues to ensure these meet all relevant legislative and regulatory requirements following the upgrade of the plant.

  12. Council continues to work with the community to develop future recycled water opportunities to increase reuse of recycled water and minimise discharge to the Hastings dunes. 
  
The Amendment was Carried

VOTE AGAINST - Cr Kimberly Hone

Councillor Dennis asks how prepared are Tweed Shire Council and our community resilience groups for the upcoming high rainfall months?


Cr Firth temporarily left the meeting at 06:37pm.

Cr Firth returned to the meeting at 06:39pm.

Cr Brinsmead temporarily left the meeting at 06:44pm.

Cr Hone temporarily left the meeting at 06:44pm.

Director Corporate Services Replies 

Through you Madam Mayor

The Bureau of Meteorology's latest long-range forecast for February to April 2025 has predicted slightly above-average rainfall is likely for much of northern and eastern Australia. 
Tweed Shire Council has been actively working to prepare the community for seasonal events by updating flood risk maps, enhancing emergency preparedness resources, and partnering with emergency services to strengthen community resilience.

Since the February 2022 floods, Tweed Shire Council and local community resilience groups within the Tweed Community Resilience Network have taken proactive steps to enhance preparedness for future disasters, such as floods, storms and fires. The Community Resilience Network has expanded significantly. Since its initiation in 2019, and with the help of the Red Cross and SES, it now includes 30 community groups, 17 nonprofit and business organisations, and 7 government agencies. 

Under the State Emergency and Rescue Management Act 1989 (NSW), the NSW SES is the lead agency for responding to floods, storms, and tsunamis. NSW SES has adopted the nationwide Australian Warning System, ensuring real-time location-based alerts via the ‘Hazards Near Me’ app.

Ongoing NSW SES Initiatives for the Tweed are:
  • Providing free community training on flood preparedness
  • Pre-deploying resources to high-risk locations
  • Early briefings with partner agencies to ensure readiness
  • Training additional incident management personnel
  • Enhancing emergency response assets (vehicles, boats, ATVs, communication technology)
  • Expanding Community Action Teams (CATs) within the Tweed CRN
Residents are encouraged to visit the NSW SES website for preparation guides, safety tips, volunteer information, and weather updates.

Other Agencies 
In NSW, the lead agency for recovery is the NSW Reconstruction Authority (NSWRA). This agency is responsible for disaster recovery, resilience planning, and coordinating recovery efforts after natural disasters.
 
The Australian Red Cross has been a valued and reliable support agency for the Tweed Shire. With funding from the Australian Government, Red Cross has established Community-led Resilience Teams in Northern NSW to support local preparedness and recovery. Approximately 18 Community-led Resilience Teams have been established in the Tweed Shire and are being integrated into Councils Community-led Resilience Teams.   
 
Red Cross and Tweed Shire Council share a strong partnership, and the agency remains dedicated to supporting the Tweed region through planning, preparedness, and post-flood recovery efforts. 
 
Their ongoing commitment to the Tweed community this year includes: 
  • Continued training services such as First Aid and CPR
  • CPR Refresher Courses
  • Understanding Psychological first aid courses
  • Connecting with more community members to create more awareness and training with CRNs
  • Community gatherings and BBQs
  • Mentoring & Supporting CRT Working Groups to applying for Grant funding to build on CRT Resources and Community needs
  • Connecting community members with service
  • Pillowcase Presentations for youth
  • Continuing to support Community events to build resilience
  • Recruiting volunteers to support Emergency Services in Evacuation Centres & Outreach

In 2024, with grant funding from the Black Summer Bushfire Grants Program, Council achieved key milestones that delivered significant benefits to the community.
Key Achievements for 2024 are:
  • Audited 31 evacuation centres and implemented improvements, including:
    • Donating 11 AEDs, 10 solar power banks, Starlink equipment, and 3 generators.
    • Installing/upgrading air conditioning in community centres.
    • Preparing and delivering 31 evacuation centre kits.
  • Conducted a bushfire scenario exercise with the Local Emergency Management Committee, incorporating community participation
  • Drafted a Spontaneous Volunteer Framework
  • Strengthened relationships with community groups and emergency services, contributing to the growth of the Community-led Resilience Teams. Quarterly meetings and weekly informative newsletters led to further community engagement which promoted the work of the Emergency Services Organisations, which in turn allowed opportunities to build their volunteer base.  
The priorities for 2025 are:
  • As Council has been successful in obtaining a recent NSW Government grant, it will allow the Spontaneous Volunteer Framework Project to be finalised in 12 months
  • Organising the Emergency Expo Day (May 2025) - The Expo offers a unique chance for our Emergency Servies to engage with our local community, promote disaster preparedness and enhance community resilience volunteers.
  • Reviewing the Local Emergency Management and Recovery Plans. This is a State Government requirement and will take approximately 12 months to review and finalise, updates will include the Spontaneous Volunteer Framework and the inclusion of a new component relating to Discrete Aboriginal Communities 
  • Conducting emergency scenario exercises and annual evacuation centre audits
  • Strengthen and build the Community-led Resilience Teams. Quarterly meetings which will aim to provide the Community-led Resilience Team members with fresh ideas and informative information. The newsletter will continue on a fortnightly basis. Supporting communities in obtaining community grants. 
  • Linking community groups and Emergency Services together.  
 
Flood Risk Management & Mitigation Efforts 
Council’s flood risk management team is updating the Coastal Creeks Floodplain Risk Management Study and Plan (2015) and recently adopted the Tweed Valley Flood Study Update and Expansion (2024). The next step includes updating the Tweed Valley Floodplain Risk Management Study and Plan (2014).
Additionally, Council is working with NSW and Federal Government agencies on various flood mitigation projects, including:
  • Murwillumbah Pump Stations
  • Resilient Homes Program
  • Flood Levee Repair Program
  • Flood Warning Infrastructure Network Upgrades
  • Evacuation Route Assessments 
  • Drainage Reset Program
Council Preparations and Operational Procedures
Council continues to strengthen its internal procedural arrangements, in its role as a service provider, and in response to any flood emergency impacting the community including:
  •  OneRoad input, signage and communications
  • Provision of flood monitoring cameras
  • Emergency Dashboard and emergency information webpages
  • Business continuity planning and Crisis Management Group undertakings
  • Road Emergencies and Closure Procedure
  • Flood Triggered Relocation of Mobile Plant and Equipment Procedure
  • Maintenance of an Evacuation Centre resource list and Emergency Operation Centre readiness
Council maintains strong networks with emergency service organisations through the Tweed Byron Local Emergency Management Committee and agreed coordination and support efforts as formalised through the Tweed Byron Emergency Management and Recovery Plans with preparedness of these efforts practised through scenario testing.

Council is also finalising the compilation of a development application for a new SES facility for the Murwillumbah Unit and working with the SES to secure adequate funding for the project. Should the application be successful the new facility is hoped to be completed by mid-2026.
Important messages for our community:
  • Download the ‘Hazards Near Me’ app to stay informed of impending severe weather events 
  • Prepare an emergency plan for potential disaster events.

Councillor Brinsmead asks will Council consider entering into public-private partnerships for the management of local pools whereby delivery of the swimming program is undertaken alongside Council maintaining and facilitating public swimming?

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replies

Through you Madam Mayor, in 2015 Council resolved to develop an Aquatic Facilities Business Plan to direct the management of the Tweed Regional Aquatic Centres and in parallel, undertake industrial negotiations with a view to developing a separate enterprise agreement to the Local Government (State) Award 2023 to allow for the retention of pool management by Council in a more cost-efficient manner.  In 2016 Council resolved to enter into the enterprise agreement following the completion of the business plan. 
 
Subsequently, Council employs staff to operate the Centres and as part of this, deliver core programming such as swimming and other aquatic programs.  There are no plans at this point in time to outsource any of these functions to the private sector. Council’s team who service the aquatic centres are valued, high performing and are well respected in the community for the services and programs they provide.  This is reflected in swimming program enrolments.

Councillor Brinsmead asks what are the Council's current and future plans for the aquatic facilities in the Tweed shire, including those located in Tweed Heads, Kingscliff and Murwillumbah? Specifically, what considerations are being made for investment, refurbishment, heating and overall upgrades to ensure these facilities meet community needs?

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replies

Through you Madam Mayor, in 2025 the Parks and Active Communities Unit has a priority action to review the long-term strategic and business plans for Tweed Regional Aquatic Centres. This will guide the strategic direction and future priorities and investment of each centre.
 
However broadly:
  • The South Tweed facility is quickly approaching its end of useful life.  An assessment of this site will be undertaken as part of the feasibility assessment of a potential future 50-metre pool and indoor sports facility. Some minor upgrades to the heating system and plant equipment are scheduled to occur this year prior to winter to address the heating issues experienced last year. Staff are mindful of not overcapitalising on an asset that is reaching its end of useful life, as such staff are ensuring the facility any action meets the current demand requirements for the centre
  • The Kingscliff facility remains functional however some asset upgrades are required in the near future such as the roof replacement of the program pool. 
  • At the Murwillumbah facility mechanical heating of the 50m pool has been considered however the potential cost-benefit derived from the investment requires further investigation.  
 As mentioned, the development of strategic and business plans will address these matters.
 

Cr Brinsmead returned to the meeting at 06:46pm.

Cr Hone returned to the meeting at 06:48pm.
