Councillor Brinsmead asks can we please have an update on the comprehensive Community Safety Audit which was undertaken in the Tweed Heads CBD and at Jack Evans Boat Harbour by local police alongside Council staff and community representatives in September 2024.

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replies

Through you Madam Mayor, as a result of the safety audit undertaken late last year, a number of recommendations were made and various actions have been implemented including:
 
  • temporary mobile CCTV cameras were installed in December
  • investigation of permanent CCTV cameras in key hot spots has been undertaken
  • event organisers are being encouraged to book the new command bus with Tweed Byron Police for community events
  • an expression of interest process for the occupation of the former visitor information centre has progressed
  • additional bins at the new bus shelters have been investigated and modifications have been made to the shelters to prevent graffiti.
 
As with a lot of projects the lack of funding is a constraint to the full implementation of audit recommendations, however the recent announcement by the Member for Richmond of $1 million for crime prevention and community safety initiatives for the Tweed can assist with implementing the safety audit recommendations.

Councillor Brinsmead asks what measures and/or actions can be taken, or have been taken, to prevent the ongoing vandalism by way of graffiti to the newly built bus shelters and taxi rank in the Tweed CBD?

Director Engineering replies

Through you Madam Mayor 

Response to ongoing vandalism of the new public transport shelters in Wharf Street has been carried out by Roads and Stormwater maintenance staff as part of their operational activities. The two large bus shelters on the corner of Bay Street and in front of Tweed Mall have been the main targets, with the taxi rank experiencing less vandalism. Timely removal of graffiti when resources allow is an effective deterrent. 

Staff actioned graffiti removal for the shelters on 6 occasions during October 2024 and 3 times in November. Litter removal and repairs to damaged stormwater downpipes were also performed during this period.

On 11 December 2024, the large blank panels were removed from the partition walls of each bus shelter structure, and remaining graffiti also was removed from the structures. These infill panels were installed by the manufacturer for weather protection awaiting the provision of lit advertising panels by Council’s bus shelter maintenance contractor. Council has a long standing arrangement where this contractor obtains advertising rights in return for maintaining the shelters. Installation of these advertising panels was due this month, but the contractor appears to be experiencing further delays. In the meantime shelter maintenance remains with Council’s road maintenance team.

Since the panels have been removed, there have been only three further instances of reactive maintenance - litter removal in December, and graffiti removal of the Mall bus shelter in January and February.

Mobile CCTV cameras were also installed in the Jack Evans Boat Harbour precinct on 18 December 2024. These cameras provide surveillance of the northern bus shelter.

Councillor Owen asks what options does council have to reduce the number of duck and duckling fatalities in and around Market Parade Terranora?

Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replies 

Through you Madam Mayor, educating the local community during the breeding season is generally the preferred method in reducing duck fatalities.  Installation of wildlife warning signs is not recommended as there is no evidence available to demonstrate that warning signs are effective at reducing wildlife injury or mortality.  Signage proliferation is a major issue within the road environment and limiting signage to warn drivers to hazards and route management are Council’s priorities.   When signage is installed and motorists do not see the hazard, in this case ducks on the road, it may devalue other signage such as School Zones.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle of the Living Waters Church in Tumbulgum:


"Preparing for the worst outcome, praying and believing for the best. Wind speed and rainfall has not yet reached expectations yet, and we are believing for this to continue. Lord we pray for your mighty hand to calm the winds and the waves as you did when you were on a boat with your disciples. We pray for this cyclone to cease. We thank you for all the emergency services that are ready and waiting to assist. Give them & this council wisdom in knowing where to put their time & resources.

I pray for those who are suffering trauma & anxiety at present. May your peace be their portion. We pray for no devastation & no loss of life. Guide this council through this time to help make the right decisions in the days & weeks ahead.

In Jesus name we pray 

Amen"

Pastor Brenda Stuttle  - Living Waters Church, Tumbulgum 

Thankyou Lord that you hear our prayer. 

Thank you for the low impact of cyclone Alfred and for your protection during this time. I pray for those that have been affected, the businesses and those suffering stress and trauma from the event. Lord Send ministering Angels in their path, meet all their needs according to riches in glory. We lift up the homeless Lord and pray that you meet all their needs and change their circumstances. We lift up families in this time, the very core of society who are struggling to pay their bills or find rental accommodation. 

Give us realistic strategies to help them and alleviate their stress. Help us to remember the high calling you have placed on each and everyone as counsellors here. Let us not be overwhelmed by the needs but learn to trust in you and cast our cares daily upon you. Thankyou that you entrust us with this position and may we continually serve with a respect to culture and lifestyle differences in Jesus name we pray. 

Amen

REPRESENTATIONS FOR ITEMS CONSIDERED IN COMMITTEE
(Sec 3.40, 13.9 to 13.17 Model Code of Meeting Practice)
 
Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.

Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RESOLVED that: 

1. The Unconfirmed Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 13 February 2025 be received; and 

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

7.1.    Avondale Drive, Banora Point
Prohibitive parking signage is not supported along Avondale Drive, Banora Point. However, due to the matter involving behavioural issues rather than a vehicle safety issues, council officers will contact the nearby schools and childcare centre to communicate the resident's concerns.  

7.2.    Fingal Head Community Association, road matters
a.    The installation of Yellow Lines throughout Fingal Village on all intersections and across the roadway from the new boat ramp, is not supported, as current road rules are able to be enforced without additional treatments. However, to reinforce the rules in high parking demand areas, Yellow No Stopping Lines (C2) can be installed on Lighthouse Parade at Queen Street, Elizabeth Street.  Previous LTC support has already been given for the intersection at Healy Lane.
b.    TfNSW advice is sought on the request for a reduced speed limit for the Village. It should be noted that for a 30km/h posting the Speed Zoning Standard requires significant installation of engineering treatments to slow vehicles to that speed including traffic calming gateway treatments and vertical and horizontal deflection through the treatment area.
 
7.3.    Navigation Lane, Tweed Heads
To improve service vehicle accessibility in Navigation Lane, Tweed Heads, a Yellow Line (C2) will be installed on the west side of Navigation Lane adjacent to the planter boxes connecting to the existing yellow line towards Bay Street.

7.4.    Bay Street, Tweed Heads
The request for an additional pedestrian crossing on Bay Street, Tweed Heads (near Thomson Street) is not supported. Observations indicated that pedestrian activity was low and the proposed location would not be in a pedestrian desire line. Other pedestrian facilities will be investigated and then placed into council's Bike and Pedestrian Plans for priority assessment.

7.5.    Gold Coast Pro: 3 - 13 May 2025 
If required, the temporary closure of Coral Street, Tweed Heads for the Gold Coast Pro 2025 event is supported, subject to the submission of a Road Closure application (including Traffic Control Plans) at least 4 weeks prior to the event.  Separate approval from NSW Police should also be sought. 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE AGAINST - None

Councillor Brinsmead asks what is being done / has been done to remedy the ongoing IT issues experienced during Council meetings and workshops? 

The Director Corporate Services replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, there have been no recent significant issues that have prevented meetings from occurring or caused major disruptions. Minor issues such as software updates impacting sound recording, microphone feedback, and temporary freezing in full-screen mode are difficult to control as we use a cloud-based service. Whilst these issues are regrettable, they are to be expected when using technology. We continue to monitor, test and liaise with our vendors to address issues as soon as we are able. 

The Information Technology team are in the process of preparing a discussion paper to outline the current live streaming and recording methods and propose improvements to enhance system robustness, which includes the replacement of older hardware and proposing a number of different camera and minutes display layout options for the live stream.

Our council meeting software is a specialised solution with a relatively small user base. Among the available options, our current software, Resolve, is considered the best in its class. It is widely used by many 60 councils in New Zealand and Australia. In New South Wales, there are currently 15, soon to be 17, councils that utilise the Resolve software for their Council meetings. 

When Councillors log into Boardview after the meeting has started, it tends to cause more issues with voting and the overall running of the meeting in Resolve. At the February Council meeting, all Councillors who attended were logged in before the meeting started, resulting in a smoother voting process.

To further improve the efficiency of our meetings, we recommend that all Councillors log in well before the meeting starts. This will allow us to address any computer upgrades and test this approach further. Our experience since the upgrades during the caretaker period last year indicates that meetings run more smoothly and voting works better when Councillors are logged in before the meeting begins. It is also recommended that all users of Council equipment power on their computer for a least two hours per week to provide time for updates to install and security scans to run.

Councillor Brinsmead asks what are the future plans (if any) to address issues associated with the Knox Park pond including, but not limited to, safety, amenity, cleanliness and flora and fauna? 

The Acting Director of Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, the pond in Knox Park is a man-made feature that was constructed sometime between 1970 and 1987, primarily for amenity purposes. 
The Knox Park Masterplan, adopted by Council in 2014, proposed upgrades including connecting the island to the main park via bridge/boardwalks as well as the addition of seating and landscaping improvements. These were not included in the plan due to community and Councillor concerns. 

A further study and plan was undertaken by external consultants Australian Wetlands Consulting. Proposed options included: 
  • enhancing its stormwater treatment capacity, 
  • enhancing aesthetics, 
  • improving public safety, and 
  • maintaining the fauna habitat values at the site. 
Multiple options were considered including:
  • modifying the existing pond to create a wetland, 
  • converting it into a bioretention basin, or 
  • filling the pond in and returning it to turf. 

The recommendations of this report were considered but not implemented due to lack of funding and resources.

Ongoing management and maintenance of the pond requires periodic removal of water plants by external contractors at considerable cost.

There are no specific plans to upgrade the pond due to competing priorities and lack of funds and resources. The need to consider options to address safety concerns arising from the weed and plant material in the water body is acknowledged.

Quotes for fencing of the pond as a short to medium term solution to provide a physical barrier and deter accidental access to the pond ranges from $37,000 - $50,000. While no specific budget is available within existing budgets, this could be funded through Parks and Active Communities’ reserves in the 25/26 FY.

Councillor Brinsmead asks what is being done / can be done to address the ongoing issue of illegal camping in the Tweed Shire?

The Acting Director of Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, Council’s Rangers Unit is responsible for the patrolling and regulation of illegal camping in public spaces. The Unit currently undertakes regular patrols targeting illegal camping five mornings per week. Patrol locations vary each week in response to customer service requests but include both Tweed Heads and coastal village locations each week. When the Unit has a full complement of staff, illegal camping patrols would ordinarily be conducted 7 days per week.

The Natural Area Ranger, accompanied by user-pays police officers, conducts targeted illegal camping compliance patrols over holiday periods.

Ticketless penalty infringement notices are currently issued through a software application procured several years ago. That application has experienced significant functionality issues since the release of a new version of the application in November which remains unresolved to this date. As such, the issuing of fines has been limited and difficult throughout that period. 

Recently the State Government revised Council’s ability to issue ticketless parking fines. As a result, Council is in the process of procuring a new software system to meet the State Government’s requirement for fines to be physically issued. This new system, which is scheduled to be operational in May of this year, will allow the process to be undertaken in a more efficient manner and with the aim of reducing the number of illegal campers. 

Council does have the option to undertake patrols outside of the Rangers Unit standard operating hours (7.00 to 16.00), however this will require the diversion of resources during standard operating hours which will impact the Unit’s ability to respond to customer service requests and other priorities.

Councillor Owen asks what steps are being undertaken for the recovery of Tweed Shire after Cyclone Alfred?

The Director Engineering replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, Post Ex Cyclone Alfred Council Officers have compiled a list of actions which form the backbone of how Tweed Shire Council will recover from this disaster.   These actions include: 
  • Remove and cleanup green waste and other debris from open space, waterways, beaches, bushfire asset protection zones, roads, community buildings, the rail trail and other council land. 
  • Undertake kerbside collection of green waste and other flood effected hard waste from private residential property. 
  • Accept free drop-off of flood effected household goods and green waste at Councils Resource Recovery Centre. 
  • Assess beach erosion and take action to make safe and mitigate further erosion. 
  • Repair and reinstate beach accesses including emergency beach vehicle accesses. 
  • Replacement of beach emergency location signage. 
  • Advocate for additional funding to support the shortfall in cleanup and restoration costs for Council assets. 
  • Support the NSW Reconstruction Authority in the operation of Recovery Access Points and Mobile Outreach. 
  • Provide a Tweed Shire Council Information Desk at Recovery Access Points and Mobile Outreach. 
  • Update Tweed Shire Council Recovery Dashboard web site content. 
  • Attend and participate in DCJ and NSW RA Recovery briefings. 
  • Publish 'Share your ex Tropical Cyclone Alfred experience' on Your Say Tweed and associated comms. 
  • Facilitate Community Resilience Network meetings to discuss needs and analysis for our community. 
  • Compile Community Situation Reports for Council and the NSW RA. 
  • Assess damage to roads and commence process of reconstruction. 
  • Assess damage to parks, community buildings and other public assets and commence process of reconstruction. 
  • Undertake immediate repair of damaged to water and wastewater infrastructure. 
  • Proactively reach out to Hall Committees and licencees to seek out impacts to community buildings and facilities. 
  • Identify and pursue resilience and betterment initiatives for Council Services including the provision of additional generators, battery backup, and back up for critical communications systems. 
  • Identify and pursue resilience and betterment initiatives for the road network. 
  • Advocate for long term funding to develop and support the Community Resilience Networks, Red Cross Disaster Preparedness Funding and Assertive Outreach program. 
  • And finally, Council will also support the Regional Recovery Coordinator Superintendent Scott Tanner in undertaking regional recovery initiates including participation in the relevant Recovery Subcommittees.

Cr Firth asks what further steps can we take to secure broader koala protection in our shire given there is evidence of koalas beyond the coastal areas covered in Council’s Koala Plan of Management?

The Acting Director of Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, through the recently adopted Tweed Conservation Strategy, we are implementing a range of actions and projects that protect and improve koala habitat throughout the Shire.  

This includes our private land conservation programs (biodiversity, river health and sustainable agriculture grants and Land for Wildlife), vegetation and ecological prioritisation mapping review and the Stage 2 C-zone review.  

The strategy also includes an action to prepare a comprehensive koala plan of management for the whole shire, and a commitment to work with the Biodiversity Conservation Trust to increase the number of Voluntary Conservation Agreements. These agreements provide in perpetuity protection for koala habitat and access to financial resources for landholders to help them to manage these areas.

Council’s team is also continuing to work with neighbouring councils, research institutions and other stakeholders on regional koala conservation initiatives including implementing the Northern Rivers Regional Koala Conservation Strategy and the Australian Research Council Linkage Project researching koalas, climate change and private land conservation.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd from the Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church.


Gracious God, 
 
We are grateful for all the government and non-government agencies involved in the response to cyclone Alfred, especially for those who have come from other Shires and States to work with our local crews.  We commit to you those who have the responsibility for coordinating such a huge task; for wisdom, endurance, and satisfaction in work well done.  Give the crews strength and safety in their work.  And we pray for all those entrusted with the regular work of Council with this added layer of responsibility and complexity.
 
We are thankful that the storm was not as severe as predicted, but pray for those affected as they wait on repairs, live away from their home, and grieve over the trauma they experience.  As we enter the Easter season, remind us of your compassion and care for us and our world.  May we find our rest in you.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen.

RECOMMENDED that Council endorses the wording of the Draft Submission to the Department of Planning, Industry & Environment for the proposed Uniting Kingscliff Redevelopment (SSD-47105958) which is to be forwarded to the Department as a final submission with the following additional commentary:
 
Residents in Lorien Way raised concerns that Building A would overlook them being the southern neighbour. The State Design Review Panel process said “amendment adopted” with notes stating that “Single loaded corridor design outcome proposed. ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED That Council in review of community feedback received during the Options Paper exhibition period and further review of constraints as part of a multi criteria analysis of Change Options:
 
  1. Adopts the final Growth Management & Housing Options Paper as attached to this report (Attachment 11) to inform the future Strategy, subject to the following additional revisions (noting all endorsed options will be reviewed for their ability to be serviced with water & wastewater):  
a)  Amend Change 17, Building Rural Capacity (as per Attachment 12), which relates to rural housing opportunities and alternatively includes:

  • Allow detached secondary dwellings (granny flats) as permissible with consent in the RU1 Primary Production and RU2 Rural Landscape zones for those lots 10ha in size or over.
Note: this would mean landowners could choose between either the currently allowed attached dual occupancy or a detached secondary dwelling (granny flat) where the controls for such secondary dwellings would be established as part of the next phases within the Strategy and its implementation). The possible development controls could include consideration of:
 
  • Use of a single access for the main dwelling and secondary dwelling.
  • Size limit for ‘Secondary Dwellings’ (60m2, or other)
  • Potential to share a single On-Site Sewer Management (OSSM) system.
  • Maximum distance separation from main existing dwelling
  • Scenic impact.
  • Building materials (including colour and reflectivity).
  • Vegetation protection and setbacks to boundaries.
  • Setbacks from watercourses and water bodies.
  • Differing requirements for RU2 Rural Landscape, and/or RU1 Primary Production.
  • Option to review the Development Contribution waiver for Secondary Dwellings as specified in Tweed DCP A1.
  • Options to manage Short Term Rental Accommodation.
  • Support for rural workers by making it easier to obtain consent to build a rural workers’ dwelling, specifically by removing the 'isolation' requirement of clause 4.2C in the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014.
  • Opportunities to innovate, diversify, and add value, including agritourism opportunities.
  • Retain dual occupancy (attached) as an existing opportunity.
  • Allow dual occupancy (detached) on lots of at least 40ha.

b)  Retention of the Options Paper V2 Change 01, Tweed City Masterplan, to be renamed as the Tweed City LEP Review. The intent of the Tweed LEP review is to:

  • Review land uses and development standards in the context of potential uplift associated with housing diversity, affordable housing within Tweed Heads, and land use opportunities across the old Tweed Hospital site.
  • Review alignment between building height and FSR provisions.
  • Review minimum lot size requirements for residential flat buildings and shop-top housing buildings.
  • Review building height opportunities within the Tweed City Centre core area in alignment with Gold Coast airport obstacle limitation surface (OSL) requirements within the Commercial Centre, Mixed Use, and Medium Density zoned areas.
  • Review the design excellence clause.
  • Review the ability to service Tweed Heads with water and wastewater.
  • Review climate change flood impacts (inundation) expected as identified in the multi-criteria analysis.
  • Options Paper V1 Change 5 is to be removed from the Tweed City LEP Review.
 
c)  Deletion of the Options Paper V2 Change 23, Terranora R5 Minimum Lot Size Review, due to lack of infrastructure services.

 d)  Deletion of the Options Paper V2 Change 27, Chinderah Employment Land, due to flooding and environmental constraints.

 e)  Reduction of the Options Paper V2 Change 3, Banora Point Precinct Plan study area, to focus on uplift opportunities within the proximity catchment of the employment zone precinct rather than the entire locality. Review the ability to service Banora Point with water and wastewater.

 f)  Redefinition of the Options Paper V2 Change 14, Pottsville West Masterplan, to exclude land near the interchange of the M1 (as identified on Options Paper V1 Change 44) and to exclude land east of Pottsville Mooball Rd (as identified in Options Paper V1 Change 46) due to environmental constraints.

 g)  Remove Options Paper V2 Change 26 Tanglewood as the change itself states that it is highly constrained and will not be actioned within the timeframe of this strategy.

 h)  Remove the rural village expansion options as exhibited (Options Paper V2 Change 18 Tyalgum, Change 19 Uki, Change 20 Burringbar, Change 21 Crabbes Creek) in light of the community feedback and focus on developing a set of criteria which will guide future rural village expansion opportunities in alignment with Actions 20 and 95 of the Rural Land Strategy and Action 3.18 of the Rural Villages Strategy. Any expansion of Rural Village Areas to be the outcome of specific rural village locality plans based on an application of defined criteria and planning principles.

 i)  Further review the late submission made by Australian Bay Lobsters, which is seeking a review of opportunities to expand employment generation land uses and other ancillary land uses within the draft Strategy preparation stage.

 j)  Further review the late submission made by LEDA across lots, which is seeking the opportunity to consider a Land Lease Community at 436 Piggabeen Road (Lot 1 DP 874316 Holdings Pty Ltd), Lot 182 DP 755740, and Lot 470 DP 755740.

 k)  Remove Options Paper V2 Change 22 South Tweed Change Option 22 due to community opposition vulnerability to tidal inundation and flooding concerns (noting this will remove Options Paper V1 Changes 11,12 and 13 being increased density in South Tweed Heads).

l)  Remove Options Paper V2 Change 4 as this is not supported to advance within the strategy. Kingscliff Health and Education Precinct Plan is inconsistent with the Kingscliff Locality Plan. The changes in Options Paper V1 30, 31, 33, 35 and 36 have demonstrated lack of support from the community and have limited ability to be serviced by water or wastewater. Retain Options paper V1 Change 34 which relates to properties within Oxford and Yale St which are predominantly owned by the NSW State Government to investigate opportunities for more diverse housing.

m)  Amend Options Paper V2 Change 13 Mooball Village Expansion to the area already zoned for residential development noting the site constraints of steep landform vulnerable to landslips, soil contamination and the requirement for a private waste water supplier.  

n)  Amend Options Paper V2 Change 24 Innovation at Wardrop to exclude areas of high conservation value. 

o)  Remove Options Paper V2 Change 25 East Keilvale as the change itself states that it is highly constrained and will not be actioned within the timeframe of this strategy.

p)  Change 12 Bilambil Heights change option be amended to include the requirement to prepare a Council led development control plan and infrastructure contributions plan across the identified Bilambil Heights area to ensure holistic coordination between land use and required infrastructure on a cost recovery basis.

q)  Update all Options progressing to the strategy to include consideration of the upcoming Tweed Valley Flood Risk Management Plan, Coastal Creeks Flood Risk Management Study and Plan, Coastal Inundation and Tidal Inundation mapping and Conservation zone mapping and any modification required therefrom.

r)  Include the Conservation Strategy and the Sustainable Agriculture Strategy in the list of informing key policy documents listed in section 8.1 as per the Council resolution of 11/12/24. Also include in this section a point about how the Kingscliff Locality Plan and Tweed LEP’s will guide growth considerations.

s)  Ensure that the indicative area of Greenfield development sites (as shown in Fig 12 and 13in Options paper, page 34) are amended if included in the Strategy to not refer to Tweed City Centre as a greenfield site and match the resolved options going forward.

t)  Ensure that Change 6:  Review of Density in Proximity to Employment zones, includes maps of all areas affected by this change when included in the Strategy, so that people can visualise the impacts in their local area.

2.  Commences preparation of the Draft Tweed Housing and Employment Land Strategy, with a draft Strategy to be brought to Council for endorsement prior to public exhibition. This strategy should have a section acknowledging the impact of landbanking on Councils ability to deliver residential land strategically and include a section on what steps are needed by the state government to stop this practice further interfering with delivery of housing to provide Council with a clear advocacy position.

3.  Separate to the GMHS Review Council’s Dwelling Entitlement provisions with a view to allowing all blocks of land in RU1 and RU2 (excluding small slithers of land) a dwelling opportunity for DA’s to be lodged and assessed on their merits. This would avoid costly Planning Proposals.

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Michael Boyd, from the Presbyterian Church, Tweed Heads.

Gracious God, 
 
The events of Youth Week remind us of the contribution young people make to our Shire. We pray for them as they navigate a complex world, and thank you for the elders, parents, teachers, coaches, and community leaders who mentor them. We recognise the commitment of Council over decades to provide infrastructure and programs that enable young people to flourish. May the decisions of this meeting result in an even stronger community into the future, where people and places are well cared for.  
 
And with this Easter weekend we pray that after an exhausting start to the year, as many as possible will be able to enjoy needed rest. May we take time to reflect on Jesus’s words that he came to bring life in all its fullness.
 
May we find our rest in him.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen.

Cr James Owen returned to the meeting at 4:40pm.
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead returned to the meeting at 4:40pm.

AMENDMENT

Cr Kimberly Hone
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

PROPOSED that Council:

  1. Holds the 2026 Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards and Citizenship Ceremony on Monday 26 January in Murwillumbah Civic Centre.
      
  2. Supports the Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards Selection Panel (comprising all Councillors) and the current Awardees, considering the 2025 Tweed Shire Australia Day Award nominations for the following categories:

    • Arts and Culture
    • Citizen of the Year
    • Community Event of the Year
    • Senior Ambassador
    • Sporting Achievement (Group and Individual)
    • Volunteer of the Year (Group and Individual)
    • Young Achiever in Community Service
with the option to make an ‘Honourable Mention’ to a nominee who deserves recognition for their efforts.

  1. Adopts the changes to the Australia Day Award category descriptions.
      
  2. Selects the previous year's Citizen of the Year Awardee and as an alternate the Senior Ambassador Awardee to be invited to perform the role of 2026 Tweed Shire Australia Day Ambassador at the official Tweed Shire Australia Day Award and Citizenship Ceremony.

 The Amendment was Lost 

VOTE FOR - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

The Amendment was Lost on the Casting Vote of the Mayor. 


ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Holds the 2026 Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards and Citizenship Ceremony on Friday 23 January in Murwillumbah Civic Centre.
      
  2. Supports the Tweed Shire Australia Day Awards Selection Panel (comprising all Councillors) and the current Awardees, considering the 2025 Tweed Shire Australia Day Award nominations for the following categories:

    • Arts and Culture
    • Citizen of the Year
    • Community Event of the Year
    • Senior Ambassador
    • Sporting Achievement (Group and Individual)
    • Volunteer of the Year (Group and Individual)
    • Young Achiever in Community Service
with the option to make an ‘Honourable Mention’ to a nominee who deserves recognition for their efforts.

  1. Adopts the changes to the Australia Day Award category descriptions.
      
  2. Selects the previous year's Citizen of the Year Awardee and as an alternate the Senior Ambassador Awardee to be invited to perform the role of 2026 Tweed Shire Australia Day Ambassador at the official Tweed Shire Australia Day Award and Citizenship Ceremony.
 
The Alternate Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

RESOLVED that:

  1. The following tabled Petition(s) be received.

    • Petition containing 50 signatories, of which 23 were valid (with 27 being invalid due to incomplete details) received on 31 March 2025 entitled "Tweed Shire Whale Carcass Policy" advising as follows:
      We the undersigned being concerned local residents of Pottsville and the surrounding Tweed shire, request confirmation of the following by way of written statement issued to the Pottsville Community Association by way of email.

      1. When the policy on Whale Burials in the Tweed shire will be completed in draft form and presented to stakeholders and residents of the Tweed shire for review and comment. This being further to a motion being carried during Council meeting 21 November 2024 in relation to item 11.6 - NOM - Cr Cherry - Policy on Whale Burials in the Tweed Shire. It is not unreasonable that residents of Tweed shire concerns are suitably responded to once a motion has carried in such a manner. As such we require written response to the programme and timing of this policy being established by way of written correspondence issued to the Pottsville Community Associated by close of business Friday 4 April 2025.

      2. We also require that in said policy, all beaches in the Tweed shire will be deemed as urban or high visitation areas. With all future whale burials then being undertaken in accordance with the position statement put out by the NSW Department of Environment and Heritage 'Review into the Management of Deceased Whales, which expressly states 'no more burying deceased whales in urban or high visitation areas'.

  2. ATTACHMENT 1 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.

 
The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen

Councillor Brinsmead asks what can be done to better manage Cudgen Lake and the impact it has in respect to flooding of nearby residential streets during heavy rainfall and severe weather events?

The Director of Engineering replied:

Council has no direct role in managing Cudgen Lake. It is a natural waterway in a protected area managed by National Parks and Wildlife Service. Cudgen Creek is controlled by Crown Lands.

The lake is a large storage area located midway in the Cudgen Creek catchment. Upstream of the lake, the land is generally agricultural and storm and flood flows enter the lake via modified creek systems. Downstream of the lake, the creek maintains a natural form out to the ocean at Kingscliff.

During floods water levels in the lake are observed to rise slowly and then recede slowly. There is a history of flooding of the lower lying streets in Bogangar such as Tamarind and Rosewood Avenues due to backflows from the elevated lake. Lake levels also influence water levels in Friday Island canal and street stormwater systems. The flood of record occurred in 2022, with further over-floor flooding recorded during the Tropical Cyclone Alfred event in 2025.

Understandably the Cabarita-Bogangar community has long advocated for alternate management of the lake with an aim to reduce flood risk. The community has direct representation on the Floodplain Management Advisory Committee. Council has recently gained grant funding to commence an update of the existing Coastal Creeks Flood Study and associated Floodplain Risk Management Study and Plan. Initial consultation for this project has reinforced these concerns. Council officers through the committee have committed to reviewing community options for modification to the lake to determine whether engineering interventions such as changes to the lake outlet, high level diversion drains, or widening of downstream bridges and abutments would have a material outcome in reducing flood risk for Cabarita – Bogangar without worsening flooding for other areas. 

That assessment will include consideration of upfront and recurrent costs, approvals pathways, environmental impacts and ongoing maintenance requirements. National Parks and Crown Lands would need to support any initiatives prior to them being adopted by Council.

Any modifications of a scale that would change the hydrology of Cudgen Lake or Creek would have significant impacts on the waterway ecology.  This could affect water quality, vegetation distribution, Acid Sulphate Soils and flora/fauna.

The Floodplain Risk Management Study will also investigate improved flood warning systems, emergency management processes and land use planning controls as a package of measures to reduce flood risk to Cabarita – Bogangar.

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that Council notes:
 
  1. The interim report from the Parliamentary inquiry into local government sustainability.

  2. That the interim report from the Parliamentary inquiry into local government sustainability has confirmed the role of councils has evolved and grown over the past 30 years, and this is putting significant pressure on council budgets.

  3. The current federal funding system isn’t keeping up, and a new, more sustainable approach is needed. 

  4. The Committee is undertaking a thorough examination of all the evidence it received and will subsequently produce a final report. 

  5. ALGA's (Australian Local Government Association) media release (https://alga.com.au/no-new-funding-for-councils-in-federal-budget) dated 25/03/25 that states: Australia’s councils have been let down with no new local government programs announced in tonight’s 2025-26 Federal Budget. ALGA President Mayor Matt Burnett said a recent Parliamentary inquiry report confirmed many councils were at breaking point, after years of delivering more vital services to communities with less funding. Mayor Burnett said: “Once again, our councils – which are the most efficient level of government – and communities have been overlooked in the Budget with no new programs to address our financial sustainability emergency. “The current funding model for local government is badly broken, and we need significant long-term support to deliver local, place-based solutions to national challenges, including affordable housing, community infrastructure, road safety and natural disasters. “Increased funding to councils supports the delivery of free and low-cost facilities like local parks, events and libraries – which benefit our communities in this cost-of-living crisis.”

  6. The Tweed Shire Council submission to the inquiry into Local Government Sustainability, dated 31 May 2024.

  7. That the General Manager and the Director Corporate Services appeared before the parliamentary inquiry public hearing on 8 November 2024.
  
The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen

  1. The interim report from the Parliamentary inquiry into local government sustainability.

  2. That the interim report from the Parliamentary inquiry into local government sustainability has confirmed the role of councils has evolved and grown over the past 30 years, and this is putting significant pressure on council budgets.

  3. The current federal funding system isn’t keeping up, and a new, more sustainable approach is needed. 

  4. The Committee is undertaking a thorough examination of all the evidence it received and will subsequently produce a final report. 

  5. ALGA's (Australian Local Government Association) media release (https://alga.com.au/no-new-funding-for-councils-in-federal-budget) dated 25/03/25 that states: Australia’s councils have been let down with no new local government programs announced in tonight’s 2025-26 Federal Budget. ALGA President Mayor Matt Burnett said a recent Parliamentary inquiry report confirmed many councils were at breaking point, after years of delivering more vital services to communities with less funding. Mayor Burnett said: “Once again, our councils – which are the most efficient level of government – and communities have been overlooked in the Budget with no new programs to address our financial sustainability emergency. “The current funding model for local government is badly broken, and we need significant long-term support to deliver local, place-based solutions to national challenges, including affordable housing, community infrastructure, road safety and natural disasters. “Increased funding to councils supports the delivery of free and low-cost facilities like local parks, events and libraries – which benefit our communities in this cost-of-living crisis.”

  6. The Tweed Shire Council submission to the inquiry into Local Government Sustainability, dated 31 May 2024.

  7. That the General Manager and the Director Corporate Services appeared before the parliamentary inquiry public hearing on 8 November 2024.

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Requests the General Manager writes to the NSW Government advocating for the introduction of a consistent, state-regulated accreditation scheme for trainers of assistance animals, including the issuance of uniform identification markers for verified assistance animal teams.

  2. Requests the General Manager to prepare and lodge submissions to:

    1. The National Principles on the Regulation of Assistance Animals consultation paper, and
    2. The Review of the Companion Animals Act 1998

  3. Endorses the draft Assistance Animals in Council Places Policy, subject to the following amendment, being placed on public exhibition for a period 28 days with submissions to be received for a period of 42 days:

    1. amends Table 1 to read: “Trainee dog guides enrolled in assistance animal training” 
    2. adds into the Policy that Council is taking steps to ensure that registration of dogs and cats in areas of the Shire where restrictions apply is only possible where evidence of the need for an assistance animal and the animal's accreditation are provided.
  1. Notes that additional work is required and underway to address existing residential estates, including Koala Beach Estate, that have covenants and/or consent conditions that prohibit dogs and cats without appropriate reference to assistance animals, and that a policy position will be presented to Council for further consideration following the adoption of the draft Assistance Animals in Council Places Policy.

  2. ATTACHMENT 3 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains: 
     (d) commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: 
          (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it.

  3. ATTACHMENT 4 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains: 
     (g) advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege.
 
The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Receives the Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 13 March 2025; and 

  2. Adopts the Executive Leadership Team's recommendations as follows:
4.1.    Boyd Street, Tweed Heads (from LTC 12 December 2024)
That the existing 2P 9-5pm Mon-Fri and 9-12pm Saturday signage be removed from Boyd Street, between Florence and Brett Street, Tweed Heads, and brought back to the Committee, should issues arise.

7.1.    74 Greenway Drive, Banora Point
The installation of a yellow No Stopping line on the approaches to the driveway access at 74 Greenway Drive, Banora Point, is not supported given the low-speed environment, low on-street parking demand outside the school pick-up.

7.2.    Boundary Street, Tweed Heads
That:
1.    the installation of yellow No Stopping lines adjacent to the driveway of nos. 22-26 Boundary Street, Tweed Heads, is not supported as the driveway should be constructed for the contracted service vehicle.
2.    the installation of yellow No Stopping lines cannot be adequately enforced at Boundary Street, Tweed Heads, by existing parking officer resources.

7.3.    Martinelli Avenue, Banora Point
That the installation of "no parking 5am - 3pm Wednesdays" signage at 40 Martinelli Drive, Banora Point is not be supported due to the potential precedent for similar sites within the area and the limited council resources to enforce the signage.

7.4.    Ocean Avenue, Tweed Heads South
That the request for prohibitive parking in front of 22 Ocean Avenue, Tweed Heads South is not supported.
 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None

Councillor Owen asks how much do Tweed ratepayer contribute to running the Tweed Regional Aquatic Centres each year?

The Acting Director of Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, in the 2023/24 financial year the nett operational cost of the Centres was $1,447,846. At the end of March the 2024/25 costs were approximately $1.2m with 3 months remaining to the end of financial year.  Council is currently working off approximately 65% cost recovery basis from incoming revenues.   It should be noted that this is the operational costs only and do not include asset renewal and replacement.

Councillor Owen asks has Tweed Shire Council considered alternate models to provide world-class aquatic facilities at all its aquatic facilities (including existing and any potential new facilities) encompassing learn to swim to elite athlete swimming pathways?

The Acting Director of Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, Investigations and a tender process were undertaken in 2010 to consider alternative management models for Council’s Aquatic Facilities. At the time, the submitted costs from tenderers were considerably more than the cost for Council to continue running and managing the facilities. As such the decision was made to continue the current arrangements. 

Council currently employs staff who both run the operational aspects of the Aquatic facilities but also deliver core programming such as learn to swim and various aqua programs. These positions are under the current approved workforce and are governed via a separate Enterprise Bargaining Agreement to the Local Government Award. There are no plans currently to outsource any of these functions in our current facilities to the private sector.

Councillor Owen asks what alternate models or benchmarking of such programs has been conducted including any feasibility studies to understand the commercials of such a program (for all existing and any new potential facilities) and its ability to reduce of subsidies overall costs to the Tweed Shire ratepayers?

The Acting Director of Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, the last investigation, and subsequent development of business and strategic plans, was undertaken in 2017/18. A key project listed in Council’s delivery program in 2025/26 is the review of these business and strategic plans. This will include investigating options for various management models either across all venues or for certain aspects of TRAC operations.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Michael Boyd of the Tweed Heads Presbyterian Church:


"Gracious God, 
 
We are grateful for the many things we enjoy in our Shire that we often take for granted: safe drinking water; sewerage and waste services; infrastructure and services that many across the world do not have reliable access to.  We are thankful for all those who maintain these vital functions, and for their hard work in restoring them in times of natural disasters.
 
Your word calls us to bear one another’s burdens, and we thank you for the many ways we see this expressed in our Shire through paid and volunteer workers, and particularly by Council staff.
 
We pray for the federal election this Saturday, for a parliament that in Micah’s words, acts justly, loves mercy, and walks humbly with you.  We pray for a good relationship between all tiers of government that will deliver appropriate, effective, and equitable services for our community.
Bless each one delivering those services, and grant Council sustained grace in this long-term work.
 
We pray this in the name of Jesus, Amen."

Cr Chris Cherry has temporarily left the meeting at 3.36pm due to a non-pecuniary/non-significant Conflict of Interest in this item.

The nature of the interest is Cr Cherry's family owns a holiday park in the Tweed Shire which could be viewed as a direct competitor to the proposed holiday park at Dungay.  Cr Chris Cherry advised she will manage the conflict by vacating the Chamber for discussion and not voting on the item.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor) temporarily left the meeting at 03:36pm.


Cr Nola Firth
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

RECOMMENDED that:

A.  Development Application DA24/0546 for a caravan park providing for 262 short term sites (197 caravan sites, 29 camping, 36 cabins), managers residence, swimming pool, shop, reception, camp kitchens and associated amenities, bike trail, and demolition of existing residence (staged development) at Lot 2 DP 803636; No. 355 Tomewin Road Dungay be refused for the following reasons:

1.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 insufficient information has been provided to allow Council to be satisfied that the development is not likely to significantly affect threatened species pursuant to section 7.2 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016 (BC Act) and that a Biodiversity Development Assessment Report in accordance with Section 7.7 of the BC Act was not required to accompany the development application.

2.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the application does not provide adequate information to demonstrate that the proposal is compliant with the provisions of Local Government (Manufactured Home Estates, Caravan Parks, Camping Grounds and Moveable Dwellings) Regulation 2021.

3.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the Development Application does not provide adequate information to demonstrate that the Proposal will not result in adverse harm in the event of flooding. The Development Application is therefore to be refused under Clause 5.21 and Clause 5.22 of the Tweed LEP 2014 for the following reasons:

a.       The applicant’s consideration of flood risk is insufficient as it only considers the 1% AEP and PMF. No consideration of the Tweed Valley catchment flooding and resulting impacts to the safe evacuation of occupants have been included. 
b.       It is considered that the nature of flooding in the Tweed Valley (limited warning time, early closure of low-lying roads, landslips) make successful and safe evacuation of a large itinerant population, without local knowledge or flood experience, highly unlikely to be achievable in practice. 
c.       A shelter-in-place approach to flood risk at the site would expose residents/visitors and emergency services to an unacceptable residual risk. Dungay area is subjected to frequent, multi-day, isolation by road in even minor flood events. Normal support systems, supply lines, and services (e.g. medical) would not be available during flood isolation periods. 
d.       A shelter-in-place approach to flood risk at the site would not be able to comply with the NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure Shelter in Place Guideline for flash flooding.
e.       The proposal will transfer residual risk, in terms of emergency response activities, to NSW SES and increase capability requirements of the NSW SES through increased demand for rescue and resupply operations.

4.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 insufficient information has been provided regarding the importation of fill required to facilitate the development. As such a proper assessment cannot be undertaken to establish compliance with Clause 7.2 Earthworks of the Tweed LEP 2014.

5.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 insufficient information has been provided to determine that the proposal incorporates adequate arrangements for the provision of essential services in accordance with Clause 7.10 Essential Services. Specifically, in relation to the supply of water, the disposal and management of sewage and stormwater drainage or on-site conservation.

6.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application does not provide sufficient information to determine the proposal complies with the provisions of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 (DCP). Specifically, the following sections:

i.        The Applicant has not demonstrated compliant car parking spaces in accordance with Section A2-Site Access and Parking Code
ii.       The applicant has not provided a Flood Response Assessment Plan (FRAP) as required by Section A3 Development of Flood Liable Land.
iii.      The application has failed to adequately satisfy the provisions of Section A13 - Socio Economic Impact Assessment.
iv.      The Development Application has not provided sufficient information to demonstrate that all red-flagged biodiversity values on and adjacent to the subject site will be suitably avoided, managed and protected in accordance with Section A19 Biodiversity and Habitat Management.

7.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application does not provide sufficient information to determine the likely impacts of the proposal, specifically in relation to:

i.        Visual impacts of the proposal. The proposal has not provided an assessment of Council’s Scenic Landscape Strategy to determine if the visual impacts of the proposal are reasonable and acceptable.
ii.       Impacts on ecological values of the site and surrounds.
iii.      Potential noise impacts on the locality
iv.      Potential light pollution impacts on the locality 
v.       Potential land use conflicts with existing rural and residential uses.

8.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application does not provide sufficient information to establish that the site is suitable for the proposal. Specifically in relation to:
i.        The bush fire hazard of the site. The recommended Asset Protection Zones conflicts with ecological buffers to red-flagged biodiversity values. Therefore, Council cannot be satisfied that the Proposal complies with Planning for Bushfire 2019 requirements. 
ii.       Consideration of the existing rural character of the site. The density of the development and construction of a 2m high acoustic wall will result in a major impact to significant views from neighbouring properties of the Tweed Valley, and Mount Wollumbin. 
iii.      Land mapped as Regionally Significant Farmland and potential land use conflicts with existing rural and agricultural uses.
iv.      Access to services. The site is an isolated rural lot with little access to public transport and services. In a flood event, the site forms a flood island during storm events and cannot be accessed by car or foot in emergencies.

9.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(d) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the assessment of the proposal has had regard to the 133 community submissions objecting to the proposal and the submission received by the State Emergency Service. 

10.  Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the proposal is not considered to be suitable for the site and will result in adverse impact to the natural and built environment and thus is not in the Public Interest.

B.   ATTACHMENTS 7 and 8 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes

“We wish to acknowledge the Ngandowal and Minyungbal speaking people of the Bundjalung country in particular the Goodjinburra, Tul-gi-gin and Moorung - Moobah clans as being the traditional owners and custodians of the land and waters within the Tweed Shire boundaries. The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle of the Living Waters Church in Tumbulgum:


1 Timothy 2:1-4 (TPT)
Most of all, I’m writing to encourage you to pray with gratitude to God. Pray for all men with all forms of prayers and requests as you intercede with intense passion. And pray for every political leader and representative, so that we would be able to live tranquil, undisturbed lives, as we worship the awe-inspiring God with pure hearts. It is pleasing to our Saviour-God to pray for them. He longs for everyone to embrace his life and return to the full knowledge of the truth.
 
Dear Lord, 
 
Today as decisions are being made as to direction of our shire, according to your word, we pray and give thanks for those you have placed in authority to govern our shire. We thank you that the decisions they make, in godly reverence, will cause us to live in peace. 
May they be led by your Holy Spirit especially in the tough decisions and help them to find the truth of each situation so they can govern well.
 
We ask that your peace will reign over their personal lives and families and thank you for the personal sacrifice they have each given to represent us in Council.
 
We ask this in Jesus name 
 
Amen.

  [OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL] [AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Notes:
    1. the increased community concern about PFAS exposure levels due to possible links with cancer and thyroid issues.
    2. that PFAS is contained in synthetic grass regardless of infill used and that our holiday parks are near water. 
    3. that banning of synthetic grass is happening in countries such as The Netherlands (on sports fields) and in cities such as New York (sale prohibited).

  2. Receives this report with the following changes and incorporates the asset management plan for synthetic grass in holiday parks into the operational management of Tweed Holiday Parks:
    1. wherever possible, Council considers alternatives to synthetic grass in it's upgrages.
    2. as part of the implementation of the asset management plan, requests the General Manager to monitor and document the performance and wear of the synthetic grass assets that were installed from 2015 onwards in high-traffic and high-occupancy areas over the next two years to gather specific data on expected longevity in the Tweed Holiday Parks environment.
    3. requests the General Manager to schedule a Councillor Workshop following this monitoring period to review the data collected on synthetic grass longevity and discuss the long-term asset management strategy and appropriate replacement timeframes based on the performance observed in the holiday parks.
    4. that Council buys only synthetic grass which has low PFAS content ('PFAS free').
    5. that Council doesn't procure more synthetic grass until a recycling process is secured.
    6. that inspection of synthetic grass occurs monthly rather than daily.
    7. annual internal monitoring and implementation of evolving best practice risk management for PFAS and micro plastic.


The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr James Owen
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Kimberly Hone

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that:
  1. Council approves the granting of an easement to Essential Energy for access across Council-owned operational land at Holden Street, Tweed Heads South (Lot 6 in DP237093), subject to:

    1. approval of a new Development Application to be submitted by Essential Energy for this additional access
    2. the following restrictions on use:

      The owner of the lot benefited may - 
(a) by any reasonable means pass across the burdened lot, but only within the site of this easement, to get to or from the lot benefited, and
(b) only on weekdays during the hours of 7.30-9.30am and 2.00-4.00pm, and
(c) only twice per day,
(d) except in emergencies.


  1. Council delegates authority to the General Manager to negotiate an appropriate amount on compensation for the easement and to sign all necessary documentation in relation to this matter.

  1. ATTACHMENTS 7 and 8 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
(c) information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business
(e) information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr James Owen

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RESOLVED that: 

  1. Council approves the disposal of Council-owned operational land at 41 West End Street, Murwillumbah (Lot 6 in DP1303298) by public auction in accordance with Council’s Disposal of Land Policy. 
  1. Council engages local real estate agent Elders Murwillumbah to market and auction 41 West End Street, Murwillumbah (Lot 6 in DP1303298). 
  1. Council use the independent valuations obtained from JLL Valuers dated 4 March 2025 as a guide to set the reserve price for the disposal of 41 West End Street, Murwillumbah (Lot 6 in DP1303298) by public auction.
  1. Council approves the advertising of its intention to dispose of Council-owned operational land at 39 West End Street, Murwillumbah (Lot 5 in DP1303298) in special circumstances in accordance with Council’s Disposal of Land Policy by offering a selective tender to those persons within the Tweed Shire that were successful applicants in the NSW Government Reconstruction Authority’s Home Buyback or Home Relocation programs and invites written submissions on the proposal be made within 28 days from the date of advertisement.
  1. Following the conclusion of the 28 day public notification period a further report will be brough back to Council to consider any submissions received in response to the advertising of the proposed sale of 39 West End Street, Murwillumbah (Lot 5 in DP1303298) in special circumstances by selective tender. 
  1. Council will engage the services of an external probity consultant to prepare a probity plan in relation to the proposed sale of 39 West End Street, Murwillumbah (Lot 5 in DP1303298) in special circumstances by selective tender. The probity plan will need to: 
    1. set an acceptable minimum tender bid for the disposal of 39 West End Street, Murwillumbah (Lot 5 in DP1303298) by selective tender based on the independent valuation obtained from JLL Valuers dated 4 March 2025;  
    2. require tenderers to demonstrate to Council that any development proposed for the land is suitable for the site and adheres to the requirements of the current zoning and/or necessary rezoning applications will be pursued by the tenderer or at the tenderer’s expense before a Contract for the Sale of Land is entered into in accordance with Council’s Disposal of Land Policy;
    3. propose a process for disposal of the land should a selective tender not be awarded. 
  1. ATTACHMENTS 5-10 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
(c)     information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business
(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.
 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Kimberly Hone

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that in relation to initiating cleanup of the landslip near Illawong Crescent, Terranora, Council:
  1. Continues negotiations with the downslope owners for a further four (4) months to reach agreement to undertake Technical Solution 3, with Council contributing $1.55 million Community Assets Program (CAP) funding.

  2. Negotiates an extension of the Deed for the $1.55 million CAP funding.

  3. Engages the services of a Geotechnical Expert to provide a design for work so that site cleanup and revegetation works described in this report as Technical Solution 1 – Site cleanup and revegetation, can commence as soon as possible, noting that the work would also need to be undertaken on the adjoining private properties and agreement from the owners would be necessary to progress. The budget for this is to be considered for funding in the next budget review. 

  4. Should an agreement with the downslope owners not be reached within four (4) months, then this item is to be brought back to Council for further consideration. 

  5. ATTACHMENTS 2 and 3 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
(c) information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business
(e) information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law
(g) advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege
 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Kimberly Hone

RESOLVED that:

1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 10 April 2025 be received and 

2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1. Business Murwillumbah outdoor event - Proudfoots Lane, Murwillumbah
That the proposed temporary closure of Proudfoots Lane, Murwillumbah on 17 May 2025 be supported, subject to:
  1. NSW Police approval being obtained.
  2. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
  3. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
  4. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts.
  5. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
  6. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
  7. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
  8. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
  9. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
  10. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

6.2. Charles Street, Murwillumbah
That the request to shorten the existing school bus zone in Charles Street, Murwillumbah by 20m and terminate at the current repeater sign in front of no. 4 be supported leaving space for a car to park on street in front of the property.

7.1. Palm Avenue, Cabarita
That the request for prohibitive parking at the end of Palm Avenue, Cabarita, is not supported given that the applicant's driveway has adequate width to manoeuvre onto the road from the property.

7.2. Winders Place, Banora Point
That the request for prohibitive parking/line marking at Winders Place, Banora Point between (79 - 85) is not supported, given there are alternate options for vehicles to turn around on this road, to access parking adjacent to Lake Kimberley.

7.3. Kingscliff Lane, Kingscliff
Revision of existing signage (possible replacements) and an additional No Parking sign be installed on the eastern side of Kingscliff Lane at the intersection of Pearl Street.

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Kimberly Hone

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks what is the process for the Tweed Shire to move to a 60-day cap on STRA similar to the Byron Shire where non-hosted short-term rentals (like those offered on Airbnb or Stayz) are capped at 60 days per year, with some exceptions?

The Acting Director Planning and Regulation replied:
Through you Madam Mayor, The Byron Bay example led to a change in the NSW State Housing Policy, driven by robust economic analysis.

If Tweed Shire Council wants to introduce a 60-day cap on short-term rental accommodation, a similar approach would likely be necessary. This would involve preparing solid evidence, such as a social and economic impact assessment, and working closely with the Department of Planning to request an amendment to the State Housing Policy.

Council would need to carefully balance the social benefits of potentially increasing housing availability against the possible impacts on the tourism sector.

If Council chooses to pursue these changes, a thorough scoping of the project requirements would be essential and done in consultation with the Department of Planning.

We must also consider how to establish an efficient regulatory framework and allocate sufficient resources to manage a capped short-term rental system.

Importantly, prioritising this initiative could divert resources away from Development Application assessments and Planning Proposals, unless Council decides to outsource the work and votes to allocate funding accordingly.

The meeting opened with a Prayer prepared by Reverend Tay Lee and read by the General Manager:


God of grace,


We lift up the Tweed Shire before You today, giving thanks for the beauty of this land, the richness of its community, and the people who call it home.


We ask for Your abundant blessing to rest upon this region — upon its towns and villages, its businesses and services, its families and households, and all who work to build a thriving, caring community.


Protect and provide for this land, Lord. May the rivers flow with life, the fields flourish with abundance, and every home be filled with peace and love. Unite this community with kindness, generosity, and a spirit of true neighbourly care.


Bless the children and young people with hope and opportunity. Surround the elderly with honour and care. May each person in this Shire know they are valued and that they belong. Let Tweed Shire be a place where Your presence is known, where lives are enriched, and where Your love and grace are deeply felt.


God of wisdom and courage,


As we begin this Council meeting, we seek Your guidance and presence.


Bless our leaders with discernment, integrity, and clarity of thought. May their decisions be shaped by wisdom, compassion, and a shared vision for the good of all. Grant them the patience to listen well, the courage to act justly, and the humility to serve with care.


Let this meeting be marked by respectful dialogue, unity of purpose, and a commitment to the wellbeing of every person in this community.


As the psalmist prays, “May the favour of the Lord our God rest on us; establish the work of our hands for us — yes, establish the work of our hands” (Psalm 90:17).


So we commit this gathering into Your faithful hands.


In Jesus’ name we pray,


Amen.

    4. Easements be created over public authority reticulation services, if any. 
    5. All necessary documentation in relation to this matter to be executed under the Common Seal of Council. 
    6. If reasonable objections are received, a report will be brought back for further Council consideration.

  5. ATTACHMENTS 7-9 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:
(e)    information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of the law

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Brenda Stuttle of the Living Waters Church, Tumbulgum.

Dear Heavenly Father, we pray that in this time, we do not lose our peace. In our business, that we don’t lose sight of that which is important, our family, health and valuing those around us in our sphere of influence. As we hear of wars and rumours of wars and country’s we as a nation are aligned with, going to war, we ask for your continued guidance and direction in every aspect of governance. 

We lift up families in our region, bless them with finances and housing and communities around them to support them. 

We lift up the homeless who in winter are struggling more than usual, send help their way.

We pray for those struggling with mental illness and ask for more mental health facilities and workers to deal with this need. 

We lift up those who have been impacted by recent weather events. We pray that everything is restored including their mental health. 

Let us learn to love one another unconditionally as You love us and dwell with one another in peace.
