ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RECOMMENDED that:

A.  Development Application DA06/1334.05 for an amendment to Development Consent DA06/1334 for refurbishment of the Riverview Hotel at Lot 1 DP 1132797 No. 267 Tweed Valley Way, South Murwillumbah be approved subject to the amended conditions "DA06/1334.05 Recommended Conditions" attached to the report for this item except where varied as follows:

1.  Delete condition 1A and insert new condition 1B as follows:

1B.  The development shall be completed in accordance with the Statement of Environmental Effects and Plan No 2225DE/4 prepared by Nigel White and Associates dated 04/12/2008 and Plan Nos 1567 1 and 2 prepared by Ian Webb Building Design and dated Dec 08 and the plans marked Dwg Nos CC-01 to CC-06 (issue B) dated 24/10/2024 prepared by Ardill Payne & Partners under Job Number 10671, as annotated by Council except where varied by the conditions of this consent.

2.  Insert New Condition 1.1 as follows:
  1. Updated survey accurate carparking layout plans to be submitted prior to the commencement of any work approved under DA06/1334.05 to include the following details: 
  2. Retention of the existing mango tree at eastern end of carpark, 
  3. Deletion of Car Parking Space No 23,
  4. Demonstrate consistency with any landscape plan submitted for approval in terms of the potential for cars to overhang the kerb and adversely impact on the viability of the landscape strip – This may incorporate the provision of wheel stops to prohibit encroachment into the landscape while demonstrating sufficient length for a parked vehicle.
  5. Details of any car parking lighting to be provided or amended under this application. Car parking  shall not spill beyond the boundaries of the site. Lighting shall comply with AS 4282 and other relevant Australian Standards.

    The revised survey accurate car parking plan shall clearly identify the top of the river bank/armouring.

3.  Delete condition 8 and insert condition 8A as follows:

8A.  The developer shall provide twenty-two (22) off street car parking spaces and three (3) queued spaces along the driveway of the drive through bottle shop, including parking for the disabled in accordance with Tweed Shire Council Development Control Plan Part A2 - Site Access and Parking Code. Full design detail of the proposed parking and manoeuvring areas including integrated landscaping shall be submitted to and approved by the Council's General Manager or his delegate prior to the issue of a construction certificate.

4.  Insert a new condition 19.1 as follows:

19.1 Landscape Plan
Prior to the issue of a Construction Certificate a detailed plan of landscaping shall be submitted for the written satisfaction of Council's General Manager or delegate. The detailed plan of landscaping must satisfy the following criteria:

1. Landscaping plans are to feature landscaping along the northern length of the site that mitigates the visual amenity impacts of all development at the site.
2. The landscaping plan shall be consistent with any landscaping approved pursuant to DA22/0376 (or as amended) at the subject site and includes a construction management plan that retains and protects the mature mango tree during construction and into perpetuity.
3. Works are to be in accordance with Australian Standard AS4970 Protection of trees on development sites.
4. The landscaping design may include planter boxes where soil quality and depth cannot be achieved otherwise.
5. The landscaping design shall consider the length of the car parking spaces, and ensure that plants (having regard to the selected species, planting locations and potential use of planter boxes) are protected from parked vehicles.
6. A minimum of 80% local native species to the Tweed Shire and maximum of 20% Australian native or exotic species to apply to other plants (shrubs, ground cover and similar).
7. No declared weed species listed under the NSW Biosecurity Act 2016 (or as amended).
8. Provision must be made for a minimum 12-month maintenance period for all landscaping plantings.

5.     Delete condition 25 and insert condition 25A as follows

25A. 8. Provision must be made for a minimum 12-month maintenance period for all landscaping plantings.

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr James Owen

RECOMMENDED that:

  1. Development Application DA25/0126 for a staged residential development comprising of demolition of existing structures, nine (9) lot Torrens title subdivision and twenty (20) lot community title subdivision with a dwelling on each lot, vegetation removal and earthworks at Lot 1 DP 798632 & Lot 1 DP 798633 & Lot 39 DP 254416 No. 83 Fraser Drive, Terranora be refused for the following reasons:
    • Pursuant to Section 4.14(1) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application does not provide sufficient information to allow general terms of approval to be issued under s100b of the Rural Fire Services Act 1979.
    • Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application does not provide sufficient information to determine that the proposal complies with State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021 – Chapter 2 Coastal Management nor has the Development Application been supported with a Habitat Restoration plan. 
    • Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal has not adequately addressed the Tweed Coast Comprehensive Koala Plan of Management 2020 as required under the State Environmental Planning Policy (Biodiversity and Conservation) 2021. 
    • Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development application has failed to demonstrate consistency with the objectives of the following sections of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2000:
      • Section 25 Development in Zone 7(a) Environmental Protection (Wetlands and Littoral Rainforests) and on adjacent land
      • Section 31 Development adjoining waterbodies 
      • Section 39A Bushfire Protection
    • Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development application has failed to demonstrate consistency with the objectives of the following sections of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014: 
      • Section 1.2 Aims of the Plan 
      • Section 7.2 Earthworks
      • Section 7.6 Stormwater
      • Section 7.11 Essential Services
    • Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development application does not have sufficient information to determine the safety of the extension to Bartle Frere Close and the Private Road (Community title) in accordance with Tweed DCP Section A2 Site Access and Parking Code and AS2890.1.
    • Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development application has failed to justify the direct impact on biodiversity values and proposed variation to development envelope controls that seek establishment, management and protection of red-flagged ecological values and buffer zones in accordance with Tweed DCP Section A19 Biodiversity and Habitat Management.
    • Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development application has failed to adequately address and respond to the environmental and infrastructure constraints of the land in accordance with Tweed DCP Section A5 Subdivision Manual.  The development application has failed to respond to provisions of Tweed DCP Section A5 Subdivision Manual in relation to:
      • The environmental constraints of the land; and
      • Management and protection of environmental land. 
      • Geographic landforming.
      • Demonstrate suitable availability of infrastructure.
    • Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the development application has failed to adequately address and respond to provisions of Tweed DCP Section B24 Area E Urban Release Development Code Subdivision Manual in relation to:  
      • The environmental constraints of the land.
      • Management and protection of environmental land.
      • Provision of pedestrian movement network.
      • Protection of visual impact from identified viewfields.  
    • Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application has not included an appropriate level of ecological assessment detail for Council to be satisfied the development does not exceed the Biodiversity Offset Scheme threshold as determined under the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016. In this regard the application has failed to satisfy Part 7 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016.
    • Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(d) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the submissions received against the Development Application raised valid concerns in relation to traffic impact. 
    • Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development is not considered to be in public interest due to potential environmental factors and impact to the existing built form.

  2. ATTACHMENT 8 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

    (e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

     

 
The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Nola Firth

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Kimberly Hone
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

RECOMMENDED that: 
 
1. Development Application DA25/0296 for a Rolling Sets music festival on Saturday 29 November 2025. The proposed maximum capacity for the event is 12,000 people, with entertainment occurring from two (2) stages at Lot 448 DP 755740, Lot 653 DP 755740, Lot 702 DP 720453, Lot 7312 DP 1121225, Lot 7339 DP 1166191, Lot 7341 DP 1166191, Lot 7342 DP 1166191, Lot 7343 DP 1166191, Lot 7344 DP 1166191, Part Lot 7340 DP 1166191 & ROAD 1350 Coral Street, Tweed Heads; Lot 704 DP 877249 Eden Street, Tweed Heads and Part Lot 703 DP 877250 No. 18 Coral Street, Tweed Heads be approved subject to the conditions attached to the report with the following amendments: 
 
Amend Condition 22 to read as follows:
 
22.         Public Asset Protection
 
A minimum of two security personnel shall be provided by the event organisers to patrol the Jack Evans Boat Harbour Parklands around the children's playground and public toilets on the day of the festival between 10am 29 November 2025 and 12am 30 November 2025 to deter damage to public assets and vegetation in the area. Should any damage occur, all costs of the rectification works will be payable by the applicant/event organiser.
 
Amend Condition 26 to read as follows: 
 
26.         Fireworks
 
Use of fireworks is not permitted without the prior approval of Council’s General Manager or delegate and SafeWork NSW.
 
Amend Condition 38 to read as follows: 
 
38.         Potable Water Supply
 
The event organisers are responsible for supplying adequate water supply (not limited to but including drinking water). In the circumstances that a connection to town water cannot be provided onsite then a Quality Assurance Program prepared in accordance with NSW Private Water Supply Guidelines and Public Health Regulation 2022 shall be provided to Council and NSW Health at least 14 days prior to the event. All activities shall comply with the adopted QAP.
 
Amend Condition 42 to read as follows: 
 
42.         No temporary sewer connections to Council public infrastructure
 
No temporary sewer connections to Council's existing public infrastructure is permitted.
 
Amend Condition 43 to read as follows: 
 
43.         Temporary Penetration of OLS approval
 
Should any penetration of the OLS be required in association with the bump in or bump out processes, an application for airspace approval under the Airports (Protection of Airspace) Regulations is to be made via Gold Coast Airport Pty Ltd, for any proposed temporary penetration of the OLS by use of construction cranes or other equipment, with a minimum of 8 weeks' notice.
 
Add new Condition 58 to read as follows:
 
58.         Reticulated Water Supply 
 
Where water is to be drawn from Councils reticulated system, the proponent shall: 
 
  1. Make application (https://www.tweed.nsw.gov.au/Forms) for the hire of a Tweed Shire Council metered standpipe including Councils nomination of point of extraction. 
  2. Where a current standpipe approval has been issued application must be made for Councils nomination of a point of extraction specific to the development. 
  3. Payment of relevant fees in accordance with Councils adopted fees and charges.
 
2.  ATTACHMENT 7 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law


The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Nola Firth

RESUMPTION OF STANDING ORDERS
 
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RECOMMENDED that Standing Orders be resumed.


The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Nola Firth

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Tay Lee from the Tweed Valley Uniting Church.


I’ll be praying in the Christian tradition today. Whatever faith or reflection you hold, I invite you to join with me in heart and spirit.

Let us pray.

God of grace and wisdom,
We give thanks for the Tweed Shire — for its beauty, its diverse communities, and the people who call it home. We remember with gratitude the Traditional Custodians of this land and their deep care for Country through the generations.
Bless this region, Lord: its towns and villages, its rivers and coastline, its fields and mountains, its families and households. May the Tweed continue to flourish as a place of life, peace, and belonging, where people care for one another and where creation is respected and protected.

As this Council gathers, we seek Your wisdom and guidance. Strengthen these leaders with integrity, clarity, and compassion. May their decisions reflect a commitment to sustainable growth, good stewardship of resources, and the wellbeing of all who live here — now and for generations to come.

Inspire them to embody the values of this community: to look after people and places, to listen and work together, to act with courage and generosity, and to leave the Tweed even better tomorrow than it is today.

As the psalmist prayed in the Bible, “May the favour of the Lord our God rest on us; establish the work of our hands for us — yes, establish the work of our hands” (Psalm 90:17).

So, we commit this meeting, this Council, and this community into Your faithful hands.

In Jesus’ name we pray,

Amen.

Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"The Mayor advised that the Public Officer, Mathew Greenwood had been appointed as the Returning Officer for the election of the Deputy Mayor.
 
The Returning Officer advised that 2 nominations have been received for Deputy Mayor.

The order the voting was determined as:

Vote 2: Cr Kimberly Hone
 
The result of the ordinary ballot by way of open voting (show of hands) was as follows:
 
Voting for Cr Reece Byrnes
FOR VOTE: Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Meredith Dennis, C Nola Firth.
 
Voting for Cr Kimberly Hone
FOR VOTE: Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen.
 
The Returning Officer declared that Councillor Reece Byrnes is the Deputy Mayor until the next election to be held in September 2026.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that Councillor Reece Byrnes be declared Deputy Mayor until the next election which will be held in September 2026. 

The Motion was Carried

The draft Interim Flood Planning Levels Policy and draft Development Control Plan Section A3 - Development of Flood Liable Land Version 1.7 be placed on public exhibition for a period of 42 days, as supported by the Tweed Floodplain Management Advisory Committee with the following amendments prior to exhibition:
    1. Staff to review Section A3.1.4, page 2 and consider Step 1 should refer to all 3 Tweed LEP's
    2. Staff to review Section A3.1.5, page 3 and consider under "Flood hazard" replacing “and” with “or” between “injury” and “economic loss”

    5. Staff to review the document and consider deleting the non-standard term “moveable dwelling parks” and replacing with “caravan parks and manufactured home estates” as defined by the regulations
  1. Council notes that consideration of changing controls to manage risk for industrial and commercial development and the greater potential for loss that occurs in these businesses due to computerisation and mechanisation of industrial activities will occur in the upcoming Tweed Valley Flood Risk Management Study and Plan Update.
 

The Motion was Carried

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. That the draft Alcohol Free Zones 2025-29 Policy be placed on public exhibition for a period of 28 days with submissions to be received for 42 days. 
    1. Should no submissions be received, the draft policy be adopted at the conclusion of the exhibition period without a further report to Council.
    2. Should submissions be received, the draft policy be reported back to Council addressing any submissions received.

  2. Notifies prescribed interested parties including NSW Police, Local Area Commander, and officers in charge of Tweed Heads, Kingscliff, and Murwillumbah Police Stations, any liquor licenses and secretaries of registered clubs whose premises border on, or adjoin, or are adjacent to the zones, and the Tweed Byron Aboriginal Land Council of the proposal to establish the alcohol-free zones.

  3. Delegates to the General Manager Authority to vary or suspend the alcohol free zones for special circumstances.
 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

RESOLVED that Council adopts the Community Facility Hire and Use Policy with the follow sections included:
  1. Public Liability Insurance
    Incorporated hirers and others requiring their own insurance (where cover cannot be extended through Council’s PL cover) are required as part of the hire and use agreement to hold a minimum of $10M-$20M Public Liability Insurance for the duration of their hire, with a certificate of currency to be provided with the booking form to complete your booking.

    Council recognises that maintaining Public Liability Insurance can place a financial burden on small, incorporated resident associations representing their community and a member of REIGR. AMENDMENT 5

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RESOLVED that Council adopts the Homelessness Policy with the following included in the Policy Background section:
In addition, Council plays a leadership role in a ‘collaboration for impact’ project, Northern Rivers Zero. This project has the goal of making rough sleeping rare, brief, and non-recurring in the Northern Rivers region by 2034. The project brings together Local Government, State Government departments, NGOs and service providers to move from just responding to homelessness to changing underlying systems to improve outcomes. Participating service providers are also committed to the ’By name’ list which shares data, improves case coordination and increases continuity of care for individuals.
 
Council adopted the Tweed Shire Affordable Housing Strategy on 4 December 2024 Although the Strategy is not focused on homelessness specifically, it identifies that investment in affordable housing can help prevent homelessness and reduce housing stress. The Strategy includes a range of actions related to reducing homelessness including building internal capacity to facilitate more social and affordable housing delivery; advocacy and education to raise awareness of social and affordable housing issues and solutions; and monitoring and reporting to inform Strategy updates.

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that Council writes to the NSW Minister for Planning and the NSW Minister for Housing to:

  1. Express Council’s concern regarding the inconsistent use of the terms social housing and affordable housing during the assessment and consultation process for SSD-72700708 at 25–27 Boyd Street, Tweed Heads.

  2. Request that the State ensures all community consultation processes for housing developments are transparent and accurate, with clear definitions of housing types and eligibility criteria.

  3. Request that, where material changes to a project purpose are made (such as from “affordable housing” to 100% “social housing”), the proponent be required to re-engage with the community to allow fair and informed feedback.

  4. Investigate whether Homes NSW has misapplied the Housing SEPP provisions by using the terms affordable and social housing interchangeably, including any reliance on planning incentives that may not lawfully apply.

  5. Highlight the need for a balanced mix of housing types in Tweed Shire, including social housing, affordable housing, and essential worker housing, given the acute housing and homelessness pressures in the region.

 

The Motion was Carried

Cr James Owen
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

RESOLVED moves that Council:

  1. Acknowledges ongoing community concerns regarding the number of ducks, ducklings, and other wildlife being killed or injured on local roads across the Tweed Shire, particularly during breeding and migration seasons.

  2. Notes the specific example of Market Parade, Terranora, where residents have reported repeated duck fatalities and raised concerns about poor sightlines, traffic volumes, and the absence of measures to mitigate risks.

  3. Requests Council staff to investigate and report back on shire-wide options to reduce wildlife fatalities on roads, including, but not limited to:
    1. Identification of known or recurring wildlife crossing 'hotspots' across the Tweed.
    2. Seasonal or temporary traffic calming measures in priority areas.
    3. Targeted vegetation trimming to improve driver visibility.
    4. Community awareness and education initiatives during breeding/migration periods.
    5. Trial of innovative or low-cost measure (e.g. seasonal awareness signage, pavement markings, or speed monitoring) that balance effectiveness with overall road safety signage strategies.
    6. Receive the report back to Council with feasible and costed options prior to the commencement of the next duck breeding season.
 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone

Councillor Brinsmead asks how does the Tweed Shire Council Affordable Housing Strategy address short-term rental accommodation?


The Acting Director Planning and Regulation replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, Short-term rental accommodation presents both opportunity and challenge for our Shire. While it brings more diverse holiday accommodation and tourism income, it also has the effect of reducing the pool of long-term rental homes and drives up rents. While not unique amongst many coastal Councils, the effects are amplified within the Tweed given our existing shortfall in social and affordable housing supply. 

Although statistics and data in relation to short-term holiday accommodation varies, website ‘guest favorites’ (Airbnb Data in Tweed Shire Council, New South Wales | GuestFavorites) quotes the following Tweed Shire related statistics as of December 2024:
  • 1213 active short term holiday letting properties (Airbnb as of December 2024) or approximately 2.7% of Tweeds 44 000 dwellings. 
  • Average daily rate of $407
  • 55% occupancy rate
The Tweed Affordable Housing Strategy (AHS) recognises that housing pipeline supply limitations, significant increases in the market value and cost of housing, increased construction costs, long social housing waiting lists in addition to some supply taken up by STHL compound housing affordability across our Shire. Noting that Tweed currently has only 2.9% housing designated as social and affordable housing stock, but a short fall of 3783 social and affordable dwellings measured at the last census.

The specific action in relation to STHL is set out in Part E Advocacy and Education which states:
1.5 - Council to petition the State Government to include Tweed Shire LGA as a prescribed area in Division 2 (Exempt development), Part 6 (Short-term rental accommodation) of the Housing SEPP, and advocate to introduce ‘a 60-day cap on such short-term accommodation’. 
 
This action has been allocated a high priority. Council staff are currently devising an implementation plan which will prioritise actions such as this. This will include the preparation of a submission that documents the status and metrics of STHR within the Tweed and the above adopted policy position to advocate for a STHL cap.

Councillor Owen asks what steps can be taken to brief councillors on the options for future licence conditions, to allow broader community use for the Pottsville Beach Neighbourhood Centre, prior to issuing a new licence?


The Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, On the 21st November 2025 Council resolved, in part, to review the license arrangement for the Pottsville Beach Neighbourhood Centre upon the expiry of the current and consider inclusion of a requirement to provide room hire to local community organisations, including the Pottsville Community Association. 

The review process was shared with stakeholders including the Mayor and Cr Owen on 2nd July which outlined that officers would manage the process under the General Manager’s delegation.

As outlined in that email, officers have since undertaken consultation with stakeholders including the Neighbourhood Centre, Pottsville Community Association and a range of other user groups. Officers have also assessed community and operational needs and considered how the new licence conditions might align with Council’s policies and continue to deliver fair benefit to the community. This approach has maintained probity, consistency and transparency.

As part of the review, the Neighbourhood Centre demonstrated that it continues to deliver significant value to the community through the following:
  • Many private practitioners and service network partners share the Neighbourhood Centre’s building including: Pottsville Counselling; First Stop Child Assessment, Northern Rivers Community Legal Centre, Anglicare North Coast, Family Services Australia, Tweed Coast Tutoring, Consortium of Neighbourhood Centres (CONC) Staying Home Leaving Violence, CONC Regional Food Recovery Program, Services Australia, and Brighter Futures- NSW Government Early Intervention Initiative. 
  • The Neighbourhood Centre works with its community partners to provide a substantial community of practice for people to have easy access to specialist services, assessments, assistance and support. This includes: counselling, child assessments and early intervention programs, Community Legal Centre, disability employment services, tutoring, domestic violence outreach appointments and a food recovery program. The Neighbourhood Centre also hosts Toddler Tunes and Stories, Art and Play, Community Gardens as well as an Op Shop, markets, technology centre and a second-hand furniture store.
  • In addition, the Neighbourhood Centre has meeting room hire available within business hours. Many local community groups make use of the meeting rooms including Pottsville Community Association Committee meetings.
Staff determined that the Neighbourhood Centre’s current licence conditions already deliver ‘broad community use’ and significant community benefit.  Following the review, Officers made a recommendation that the licence be renewed which was supported by myself as the General Manager’s delegate. Therefore, the licence is currently being executed. Officers can provide Councillors with a briefing to outline the process and decision-making rationale including how stakeholder feedback was considered.

Councillor Owen asks can Council staff advise what is known about the extent of pasture dieback within Tweed Shire, and what measures (including advocacy, support programs, education, or land management initiatives) Council can take to assist local landholders in addressing this issue?


The Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, Pasture dieback is a condition that kills summer growing grass pastures. It starts as small patches and can spread rapidly to affect large areas. It is a relatively new phenomena in New South Wales having been first detected at Nobby’s Creek in March 2020. It is likely to have been introduced from Queensland where dieback has been present for many years. It has now spread thousands of hectares and extends west to Bogabilla and south as far as Coffs Harbour.
Dieback likely results from a complex interaction of factors including environmental stress, soil conditions, pests, and management practices. The pasture mealybug (Heliococcus summervillei) has been identified at affected sites and is now considered a potential agent. Grass death has resulted in the loss of ground cover, exposing soil to erosion and enabling broadleaf weed invasion.

North Coast Local Land Services and NSW Department of Primary Industries provide identification guides, webinars, and reporting pathways for pasture dieback. Local Land Services also provides pasture dieback management advice to landholders.

Council has been investigating the suitability of different grass species with resistance to dieback in collaboration with landholders. A number of trials have been conducted with support from Council’s Sustainable Agriculture Small Grants Program, investigating alternative pasture mixes. A field day is being planned with Local Land Services and Southern Cross University (SCU) for later in the year. The field day will look at a property where drone seeding has been used on dieback affected areas and consider the outcomes of an SCU pasture trial conducted in the locality. Council could increase advocacy, support programs, education, and other initiatives if additional resourcing or grant funding was available.

RESOLVED that:
  1. The Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 14 August 2025 be received and 
  2. The Executive Leadership Team's recommendations be adopted as follows:

6.1.    Tweed Valley Triathletes (September 2025 and March 2026)
That the proposed Tweed Valley Triathletes Season commencing Saturday 20 September 2025 and concluding 21 March 2026 be supported, subject to the following conditions: 
  1. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser. 
  2. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event. 
  3. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
 
7.1.    Dry Dock Road, Tweed Heads South
That the off-road delineated parking spaces adjacent to the Dry Dock boat ramp, Tweed Heads South, be signposted "No Parking - Vehicles with trailers Excepted" on the spaces marked as A, B C, F, G, H, J and K on the attached plan.

7.2.    Greenway Drive and Leisure Drive roundabout, Banora Point 
That the northbound linemarking on Darlington Drive when approaching the roundabout on Leisure Drive be modified to indicate the left lane be left turn only and the right lane be straight ahead and right turn.

7.3.    The Quarterdeck and Mugga Way, Tweed Heads 
That the installation of 'Buses Prohibited, School Buses excepted' signage be installed at the intersections of Ducat Street / Mugga Way and Kennedy Drive / Norman Street, Tweed Heads.

7.4.    Kingscliff Triathlon - November 2025
That the proposed Kingscliff Triathlon on 16 November 2025, 28 February 2026 and 1 March 2026 be supported, subject to: 
  1. NSW Police approval being obtained.
  2. Endorsement of the event by Triathlon NSW.
  3. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
  4. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
  5. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect.  
  6. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
  7. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
  8. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
  9. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
  10. That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
  11. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
  12. The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
  13.  A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
  14. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
  15. The application of all signs and devices necessary to effect the changed traffic management conditions and temporary road closures for the events, also being approved as part of the event approval.

7.5.    Marine Parade, Loading Zone
That a 12 metre loading zone 6am to 8am Monday to Friday, be installed on Marine Parade, Kingscliff, adjacent 32 Marine Parade, Kingscliff.

7.6.    Willow Avenue, Bogangar
That the installation of a yellow no stopping line is not supported, given traffic volumes and these conditions are typical of local residential streets and are not uncommon across the area. The existing yellow lines on the curve can be considered for removal when road resurfacing is planned for that road section.

7.7.    Morton Street, Chinderah
That yellow no stopping lines are installed at the cul-de-sac end of Morton Street, Chinderah, to facilitate heavy vehicle manoeuvring.

Councillor Hone asks how is the Federal and State Governments net zero and emission reduction target policies affecting the Tweed Shire's operational costs and how does this affect the rate payer?

The Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, State and Federal net zero and emissions reduction policies do not directly impact Council’s operational costs or the ratepayer, as these targets apply to their respective spheres of government, not local councils.
Indirect impacts include:
  • Electricity market: policy uncertainty at Federal and State levels can cause fluctuations in electricity costs, affecting Council’s operating expenses.
  • Transition plans: Federal and State decarbonisation initiatives help local government plan for community-level emissions reductions, such as increased renewable energy generation and incentives for electric vehicles, which lower the community’s emissions footprint.
  • Grant opportunities: Federal and State programs have reduced costs for Council, for example renewable energy credits making solar more affordable, and grants for electric vehicle chargers easing pressure on Council to meet community demand.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that in regard to Development Application DA22/0376.01 for an amendment to Development Consent DA22/0376 for stabilisation work on the bank of the Tweed River including the construction of rock revetment wall at Lot 1 DP 1132797 No. 267 Tweed Valley Way, South Murwillumbah:

  1. Council forms the view that the proposed Modification can be approved contrary to the officer recommendation as it is substantially the same development with minimal environmental impact AND the riverbank erosion that occurred made the approved plan unfeasible. Specifically, the proposal satisfies 4.55 1(A) of the EP&A Act 1979 as the modification:
  • Has no or minimal environmental impact as the alternative landscaping proposed in condition 33.1 will mitigate scenic impacts of the revetment works.
  • Is the same or substantially the same development as the development for which the consent was granted as it remains revetment works for the Riverview Hotel.
  • Is consistent with the original reasons for approval which stated:
    • The development proposal has been considered in accordance with the relevant provisions of the NSW Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 and on balance is suitable to be determined by way of approval.
    • Community views were considered as part of the assessment in accordance with Council’s Development Control Plan and the NSW Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 requirements for public notification
       as the proposed modification allows for alternative landscaping solutions in the circumstances where the land was eroded away and the protection works needed for the hotel no longer allowed the original landscaping plan to be completed.
           as the proposed modification is still considered to be the same development and of a minor nature that did not require public notification.
  • Has Considered 4.15 (1) evaluation matters in regard to the merits of the application and the modification specifically Council considered the environmental, ecological and visual aspects of the proposed modification and form the view the modification is minor   
  1. The modification DA22/0376.01 be approved as per the Draft Conditions of Consent attached to this report with an alteration to point 5 (Condition 33.1) e) to require the planter boxes, if used, to be a minimum size to cater for sufficient growth and to be worded: 
e. The landscaping design may include planter boxes where soil quality and depth cannot be achieved otherwise. The minimum planter box soil areas are to be of a sufficient size to support vegetation to soften the visual impact of the development.
 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr James Owen

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Tara Jones from The Gathering, Tweed Heads:

"I am going to pray in the Christian tradition today and I invite you to join me or take a moment for reflection.

Father, we thank you for the land of Tweed Shire - for its beauty, its people, and its purpose.

We ask for your wisdom to rest upon every councillor and leader - that righteousness, justice and truth would guide every decision. Let integrity be their foundation.

May this council be unified for the good of the community, stewarding resources with wisdom and vision. Let peace dwell in every meeting and may your hand establish what is right and good for the people of this land.

We declare that Tweed Shire will be known as a place of blessing, restoration, and flourishing - a region aligned with your heart and plans.

In Jesus' Name, Amen."

REPRESENTATIONS FOR ITEMS CONSIDERED IN COMMITTEE
(Sec 3.40, 13.9 to 13.17 Model Code of Meeting Practice)
 
Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.
 
EXCLUSION OF PRESS AND PUBLIC

Cr Meredith Dennis 
Cr Nola Firth

AMENDMENT 1

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

PROPOSED that Council make a submission to the NSW MLC Parliamentary inquiry into rural housing and second dwellings:
  1. Supporting second full-size detached dwellings on rural properties in excess of 10 hectares while limiting environmental and land-use conflict impacts.
  2. Requesting the ability to rate for a second dwelling in order to fund infrastructure requirements generated by second home.
 
The Motion was Lost 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Kimberly Hone
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

RESOLVED that Council make a submission to the NSW MLC Parliamentary inquiry into rural housing and second dwellings supporting second full-size detached dwellings on rural properties in excess of 10 hectares that:
  1. Council makes a submission to the MNSW MLC Parliamentary inquiry into rural housing and second dwellings supporting second full-sized detached dwellings on rural properties in excess of 10 ha; 
  2. This policy position of second dwellings being supported on rural lots in excess of 10ha be reflected within the draft Growth Management and Housing Strategy and Rural Land Strategy Implementation Plan to subsequently underpin any future rural housing amendments to the Tweed Local Environmental Plan;
  3. The drafting of a Rural Lands DCP that provides planning and design guidelines on rural housing be prioritised; and
  4. Investigate the ability to rate for a second dwelling in order to fund infrastructure requirements generated by second home.


The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

RESUMPTION OF STANDING ORDERS

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Nola Firth
 
RESOLVED that Standing Orders be resumed.

The Motion was Carried

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

PROPOSED that:
  1. Council approves the acquisition of a motel at 13 Minjungbal Drive, Tweed Heads South (Lot 4 DP23323) for the provision of facilities appropriate to the current needs of the local community and delegates authority to the General Manager to make an offer to purchase the property within the range as set out in the valuation report currently being prepared by independent valuers Herron Todd White.
  2. Should the proposed acquisition of the motel at 13 Minjungbal Drive, Tweed Heads South (Lot 4 DP23323) be successful, approves the advertising of its intention to dispose of the Council-owned operational land at 433-437 Tweed Valley Way, South Murwillumbah (Lots 19 & 20 DP9871) in special circumstances in accordance with Council's Policy on the Disposal of Land v1.3 via expression of interest for sale to community housing providers or other government authorities and invites written public submissions on the proposal be made within 28 days from the date of advertisement.
  3. Following the conclusion of the 28 day public notification period a further report will be brought back to Council to consider any public submissions received in response to the advertising of the proposed sale of 433-437 Tweed Valley Way, South Murwillumbah (Lots 19 & 20 DP9871) in special circumstances by expression of interest to community housing providers or other government authorities.
  4. Council will engage the services of an external probity consultant to prepare a probity plan in relation to the proposed sale of 433-437 Tweed Valley Way, South Murwillumbah (Lots 19 & 20 DP9871) in special circumstances by expression of interest to community housing providers or other government authorities. The probity plan will need to:
    1. set an acceptable minimum expression of interest bid for the disposal of 433-437 Tweed Valley Way, South Murwillumbah (Lots 19 & 20 DP9871) by expression of interest to community housing providers or other government authorities based on the independent valuation currently being prepared by Jones Lang LaSalle valuers dated 2 October 2025;
    2. require those submitting an expression of interest to demonstrate to Council that any development proposed for the land is suitable for the site and adheres to the requirements of the current zoning and/or necessary rezoning applications will be pursued by the tenderer at the tenderer’s expense;
    3. propose a process for disposal of the land by public auction should the expression of interest to community housing providers or other government authorities not be successful.
  5. Council commences discussions with Community Housing Providers to determine potential of developing an operational partnership model for 13 Minjungbal Drive, Tweed Heads South (Lot 4 DP23323).
  6. Council provides the General Manager with delegated authority to execute any relevant documentation to carry out this resolution.
  7. ATTACHMENTS 1-5 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
(d) commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
(i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
(ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or
(iii) reveal a trade secret

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Brenda Stuttle from the Living Waters Church, Tumbulgum.

Hi Friends, I hope you don’t mind me calling you friends, but my Granddaughter taught me a valuable lesson the other day. We were at an awards night for her Physical Culture and she was sitting with some girls, when they were about to eat, she asked them to say Grace with her and the Parents sitting by were quite touched by the gesture. Not all were of the faith, but when I asked her, did she say Grace with everyone ?, she said not everyone, just my friends.

So Friends, may we take a moment to reflect on the coming week and weeks and pray together as one. 

Dear Heavenly Father, Thankyou that we have this time together to reflect on what is happening not only in our sphere of influence but in the world. Thankyou that there has been peace made in Nations that have been fighting. Lord we pray for peace in other Nations and in our own Nation and Community. It is the one thing you asked us to strive for. May we be open to hear the heart of each other as we present our needs and desires for a better Community. We pray for Families that are struggling to meet every day needs. Give us wisdom to help them. We pray for those who are sleeping rough, may we find a way to not judge but love unconditionally. We pray for every Councillor and Community Member represented here today. Give them Wisdom to make sound judgements and decisions, keep them in perfect peace, realising the needs will always outweigh the resources, but they can make a difference and it started with saying yes to the position of serving in the Community, not for Selfish gain but to be a servant as Jesus You modelled Yourself by washing your disciples feet and reaching out to the lost and broken. Help us Lord and thankyou for the blessing of being in such an amazing area of the Tweed Shire. In Jesus name we pray, 

Amen.

CONFIDENTIAL COMMITTEE

REPRESENTATIONS FOR ITEMS CONSIDERED IN COMMITTEE
(Sec 3.40, 13.9 to 13.17 Model Code of Meeting Practice)
 
Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.
 
EXCLUSION OF PRESS AND PUBLIC

Cr Meredith Dennis 
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)
   
RESOLVED that Council moves itself into a Confidential Committee in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993 and that the press and public be excluded from the whole of the Committee Meeting, because, in the opinion of the Committee, publicity of the proceedings of the Committee would be prejudicial to the public interest, by reasons of the confidential nature of the business to be transacted.   
   
The Motion was Carried

RESOLVED that:

  2.  The installation of additional on-street parking bays in Ourimbah Road is not supported as it may result in reduced parking provision.

  3.  The reinstatement or further installation of Yellow No Stopping lines at driveway accesses in Ourimbah Road is not supported.

  7. It be noted that Council Rangers have installed a new parking management solution that will enhance the ability to conduct parking patrols in Ourimbah Road.

  8. Signage be installed along Ourimbah Road discouraging illegal dumping.

  9. All businesses in Ourimbah Road be informed of the outcomes of this report and recommend that all site owners review their approved on-site parking space arrangements and remove any obstructions to their use.

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Receives the Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 11 September 2025 and
     
  2. Adopts the Executive Leadership Team's recommendations as follows:

6.1  Sisters of the Saddle Charity Ride
That the proposed Sisters of the Saddle event on 24-26 October 2025 be supported, subject to the following conditions: 
  1. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.
  2. All cyclists and support vehicles abide by NSW Road Rules. 
  3. All signage erected for the event not to cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event. 
  4. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.

7.1  Tweed Coast Enduro 2026, Pottsville
That the proposed Tweed Coast Enduro on 14 February 2026 be supported, subject to:
  1. NSW Police approval being obtained.
  2. Endorsement of the event by Triathlon NSW.
  3. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
  4. Community and affected business consultation addressing raised concerns including a letterbox drop to directly affected residents.
  5. The event organiser notifies Tweed residents of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts, road closures and times, alternative route arrangements, event organiser, a personal contact name and a telephone number for all event related issues.
  6. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
  7. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
  8. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
  9. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
  10. That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
  11. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
  12. The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
  13. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
  14. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
  15. The application of all signs and devices necessary to effect the changed traffic management conditions and temporary road closures for the events, also being approved as part of the event approval.

7.2  Stanley Street, Tweed Heads
That a continuity centreline marking be installed along the curve on Stanley Street, Tweed Heads and the existing yellow no stopping line marking on the southern side of Stanley Street, Tweed Heads be extended by approximately 5 metres:
a.    To guide vehicle positioning on Stanley Street and improve sight distance for vehicles exiting McDonald Street.
b.    For Council's Rangers to be notified to include the corner of Stanley Street and McDonald Street, Tweed Heads, in their patrols.
 
The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen

Councillor Brinsmead asks what has been done / can be done / will be done to address community concerns with respect to the health of Pandanus trees along the Tweed Shire coastline?

Director Planning and Regulation replied:

The coastal Pandanus is one of the north coast’s iconic trees. After the tropical cyclone earlier in 2025 some local trees have been damaged or lost in the storm event. The more common cause to damage to the tree is from dieback, a disease caused by an insect known as the Pandanus plant hopper.
 
Leaf dieback often begins on the northern (warmer) side of the tree, or in trees on the northern edge of tree clumps. Planthoppers live between leaf sheaths and their egg cases are found under leaves of infested trees. Black sooty mould can usually be seen on the leaves and trunks of badly infested trees. Large amounts of dead leaf litter around the base of the leaf heads is also a sign of infestation.
 
Council’s Pest Management Team have an ongoing program to help save our Pandanus, staff regularly review the trees health and treat any infestations to ensure our most iconic coastal tree is protected.

Councillor Brinsmead asks can we please be advised what the cost of climate adaption for Tweed Shire Council has been to date?

Acting Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Council engaged Haskoning consultants to work with Council teams to develop a Climate Change Adaptation Plan at a cost of $89,676. This work identified best practice adaptation options to reduce climate change risk, included a multi criteria assessment system to prioritise adaptation options and community and stakeholder engagement. The draft plan will be presented to Council for review in early 2026. 
 
Many of Council’s other costed strategic priorities also support climate adaptation such as:

  • Delivery of the Community Assets Program projects to ensure public spaces can better withstand natural disasters
  • Clarrie Hall Dam raising
  • Bray Park Weir Tidal Protection Project
  • Tweed Heads South levee and drainage study
  • Cool Towns
  • Tweed’s Conservation Strategy
  • Coastal Management Program for Tweed Coast and Estuaries.

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Notes that ensuring that rubbish is properly removed, not mulched during maintenance activities (e.g. mowing, slashing, or similar) prevents pollution (microplastic and other) and its dispersal via wind etc and helps to protect local waterways and the environment.

  2. Provides a briefing to discuss:
    1. practical and cost-effective options to implement and/or improve rubbish removal prior to roadside and open-space maintenance activities (e.g. mowing, slashing, or similar) across the Tweed Shire.
    2. Identifying priority or high-impact locations - such as areas of higher population density, high visibility, known litter hotspots, or environmentally sensitive areas. 
    3. A range of options for implementation, (e.g. trial programs, integration with existing maintenance schedules, or potential collaboration with community and volunteer groups). 
    4. Indicative costs, potential efficiencies, and possible funding sources or potential partnerships.
    5. Community education campaigns.

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that:

  1. Council:

    1. Acknowledges the community’s ongoing concerns that facilities and services will be downgraded, closed, or reduced at Murwillumbah District Hospital. 
    2. Supports the community's campaign to retain all current facilities and services at Murwillumbah District Hospital. 
    3. Notes that in recent years the hospital has been downgraded without community and staff consultation, and the Local Health District have acknowledged that their approach to those events was unsatisfactory to all stakeholders involved.
    4. Recognises the vital role that Murwillumbah District Hospital plays in providing essential health services and facilities to the Murwillumbah, and surrounding, community as a much needed and highly valued health infrastructure asset. 
    5. Acknowledges that during severe weather events (flooding), the Murwillumbah District Hospital provides a vital service to surrounding villages and communities who are isolated from more eastern services and infrastructure. With the frequency of such weather events appearing to increase, it is vital that we identify the need of this facility for the people of Murwillumbah, the surrounding and western villages, and the broader population.
    6. Opposes any downgrading, closure, or reduction in facilities or services at Murwillumbah District Hospital. 
    7. Advocates for the retention and enhancement of current facilities and services at Murwillumbah District Hospital. 

  1. The Mayor writes to Janelle Saffin MP, Member for Lismore, Ryan Park MP, Minister for Health, and Tracey Maisey - Chief Executive Northern NSW Local Health District, calling for:

    • A clear commitment to maintain Murwillumbah District Hospital at the current level with no downgrading, closure, or reduction in facilities or services. 
    • The public release of any short or long-term plans for Murwillumbah District Hospital. 
    • A firm commitment to community consultation on any decisions made with respect to Murwillumbah District Hospital facilities and services. 
 
The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
 VOTE AGAINST - None

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Notes that the Environmental Planning and Assessment Amendment (Planning System Reforms) Bill 2025:

    1. makes sweeping changes to the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 

    2. introduces a new assessment category (“targeted development assessment”) that makes it unlawful to consider environmental impacts, site suitability, and public interest.

    3. restricts assessment of cumulative and indirect impacts of a development such as traffic and roads.

    4. removes the requirement to consult with the Environment Department before making an environmental planning instrument that would adversely affect critical habitat or threatened species, populations or ecological communities, or their habitats.

    5. requires only ‘significant’ impacts to be taken into account when the term ‘significant’ is not defined and therefore open to debate.

    6. centralises planning powers in new State-led authorities by: removing direct contact with state departments, abolishing regional panels and decreasing opportunity for community consultation and individualised conditions on development approvals. The change decreases transparency and opportunity for independent review and for adaptation to local conditions.

    7. requires councils to assess variations to complying developments within the extremely short time frame of 10 days after which time the variation will be automatically approved.

    8. requires councils to undertake significant planning previously undertaken by regional panels without guaranteeing increased resourcing of this work.

  1. Writes to the Premier, the Leader of the Opposition, the Minister and Shadow Ministers for Planning and Public Spaces, Local Government NSW, Minister for the North Coast and the Member for Tweed expressing these concerns. Writes to the Minister for the North Coast requesting a meeting to discuss these concerns.
 
The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Councillor Owen asks will the updated Tweed Regional Gallery Strategic Plan address plans for the future upgrading and expansion of the Gallery, the economic benefit of the Gallery to the Tweed Shire, and the need for increased staffing of the Gallery — and when will the Strategic Plan be released for community input prior to its adoption?

Acting Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

The updated Tweed Regional Gallery Strategic Plan is scheduled to be presented to Council on 20 November for a resolution to place it on public exhibition. The draft does not include reference to an upgrade or expansion of the Gallery for a number of reasons. The independent consultant did not report any expressed desire from the community nor stakeholders in the consultation phase of the development of the draft. The current service levels have achieved a 99% community satisfaction in Council’s 2024 Be Our Best Resident Survey and a 4.7/5 Google Rating, indicating extremely high satisfaction with the current Gallery levels of service. There are currently no resolved plans to upgrade or expand the Gallery, therefore it has not been specifically mentioned in the draft Strategy.

The draft Strategic Plan will include insights from a Visitor Experience Survey (funded by the Tweed Regional Gallery Foundation, delivered by external facilitator 'Destination Research') This research is essentially an economic impact survey.
 
Two streams in the draft Strategic Plan include reference to staff: ‘Growth and Sustainability’ and ‘Operating Environment’.
 
It is intended that the draft Strategic Plan will be placed on public exhibition in early December if Councillors decide to do so at their meeting in November.

Councillor Owen asks what is Council’s strategy and timeline for mosquito management this summer, including spraying operations, contingency planning if aircraft or contractors are unavailable, and measures to prevent a repeat of last year’s delays?

Director Planning and Regulation replied:

Council's Pest Management Team has commenced pre-treatment activities in line with seasonal plans. These early treatments focus on hard-to-reach areas or zones unsuitable for aerial application, using slow-release methods to maximise effectiveness.
 
In preparation for the treatment season, the Pest Management Coordinator has proactively engaged with all contracted service providers to confirm their availability. One contractor has indicated potential staffing challenges due to increased demand, and Council is working closely with this provider to monitor their capacity and ensure timely service delivery.
 
Council’s treatment approach uses a mix of aerial services - fixed-wing aircraft (Murwillumbah), drones (QLD), and helicopters (QLD) - based on site needs and cost-effectiveness. If one method is unavailable or unsuitable, alternatives are in place. For example, helicopters may be used in fixed-wing aircraft can't operate or when later-stage treatment is required.
 
It is important to note that mosquito treatment is highly dependent on environmental conditions, sampling availability and particularly the weather. The limited availability of specialised aerial services in the region also presents challenges. Council continues to manage these constraints through early planning and flexible treatment strategies to support public health and environmental outcomes.

Councillor Owen asks is the Stotts Creek Resource Recovery Centre adequately resourced to operate efficiently and effectively, and what actions is Council taking to ensure it continues to meet performance and service delivery standards?

Acting Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

The Stotts Creek Resource Recovery Centre and its services are resourced through a combination of permanent, temporary staff and casual staff, and contractors.  This structure allows Council to amend its services resource allocations as necessary.  Council has a schedule of services that is monitored by staff, its contractors, and through customer service requests. Should additional services, or service amendments be required, Council liaises with its contractors to ensure service requirements are met.

DISCLOSURE OF INTEREST IN COMMITTEE

Mr Tim Mackney (Director Engineering Services) declared a Non-Pecuniary/Non-Significant Interest in Item 22.5 Mobile Food and Drink Outlets operating under exempt development - legal advice.  The nature of the interest is that Mr Mackney knows socially the person who presented at Public Forum regarding item 22.5.  Mr Mackney will manage the Interest by remaining in the Chamber for discussion.  


Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor) temporarily left the meeting at 05:08pm.
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor) returned to the meeting at 05:09pm.

Cr James Owen temporarily left the meeting at 05:29pm.
Cr James Owen returned to the meeting at 05:29pm.


ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RECOMMENDED that Council:
 
  1.   Notes the differing legal advices received on the interpretation of the requirements for an exempt mobile food and drink outlet. 
  1.   Supports an interim broad interpretation of the requirements for an exempt mobile food and drink outlet. A broad interpretation of mobile food and drink outlets that meet all the relevant development standards would include a view that:
a.      mobile is considered to be Mobile Food and Drink Outlets (MFDO) that can be moved, whether self-propelled or not, and can be removed from a site within 24 hours; and
b.      MFDOs can remain in one location on a permanent basis; and
c.       MFDOs can be considered as exempt development, regardless of whether a food and drink premises is prohibited on that land.

  1.   Write to the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces (Mr Paul Scully) providing a copy of the confidential legal advices referred to above and asking the Minister how the provisions are meant to operate. If our interim broad interpretation is not how the Government intended for the provisions to operate then request the Minister to Amend the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act and the SEPP Exempt & Complying Code 2008 as necessary to reflect the State Governments intent.

4.  ATTACHMENT1 and 2 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
(g)     advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Pastor Rob Stuttle from the Living Waters Church, Tumbulgum  

Lord I thank you for every Councillor here, representing the Tweed Shire Council.

I Thank you for James Owen, I thank you for the godly principals he displays in standing up for Truth & Integrity for the sector of the community he represents.

I thank you for Rhiannon Brimsmead. Lord bless her family as they release her to bring her concerns for this Shire especially in the areas of Youth & employment.

Lord Thank you for Reece Byrnes and his 10yrs of service to this Shire. Bless him and his family as he continues to sacrifice his time & energy to serve this Shire, so that it will be a pleasure to live in for future generations.

I also Thank you Lord for Chris Cherry and her 10 years of Commitment to our Shire. With all the challenges that come with being Major, Lord Bless her with Wisdom beyond her years, to navigate every decision that needs to be made both now and into the future.

Lord I thank you for Kimberley Hone, as she represents us both Nationally and Locally. Bless her family as they release her as she passionately stands for Truth & Justice.

I thank you also for Meredith Dennis and especially her heart for the elderly and the ministry of palliative care. My own family were blessed with the care & support at Wedgetail and I want to personally thank you for that.

And Thank you Lord for the calibre of person we have in Nola Firth to represent us in council and the Wisdom she brings to this shire.

We are grateful for every councillor here representing us and want to Thank you & them for the tireless effort they bring to this shire.

We pray this in Jesus name.

Amen

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Father Paul McDonald from St Anthony’s Parish, Kingscliff. 

"Opening Prayer for Tweed Shire Council Meeting
 
Loving and provident God,
We gather today as servants of the people of the Tweed.
We ask your wisdom, guidance, and discernment as this Council meets.
 
Bless our Mayor as chair of this meeting.
Grant calm leadership, clarity of mind, and a spirit of respect and cooperation.
 
Guide our Councillors in their deliberations and decisions.
May their words be thoughtful, their actions just and their choices always reflect the wellbeing of the community they serve.
 
We give thanks for all who contribute to the life of this Shire—
its families, workers, volunteers, and leaders.
May we work together for the common good, seeking peace, fairness, and a hopeful future for all.
 
We ask this in your holy name. Amen"

RESOLVED that:

  1. Council adopts the Alcohol-Free Zones Policy 2025–2029 and approves the establishment of zones as outlined in the policy for a four-year period commencing 2 December 2025 and expiring 1 December 2029. 

  2. Council delegates authority to the General Manager to vary or suspend zones for special circumstances. 

  3. Council notifies prescribed stakeholders, including NSW Police, liquor license holders, and registered clubs adjoining or adjacent to the zones. 

  4. Council installs and maintains signage in accordance with legislative requirements, replacing damaged signs and erecting new signs where necessary.

  5. Council note that Alcohol-Free Zones’ shall continue to exclude those businesses approved by Council for the purposes of footpath (alfresco) dining whilst those businesses are trading.

  6. ATTACHMENT 4 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

Councillor Owen asks is Council’s Rangers Unit adequately resourced and staffed to operate efficiently and effectively, and what actions are being taken to ensure it continues to meet community expectations for compliance, safety, and service delivery?


 The Director Sustainable Communties and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, Council’s Rangers Unit is structured to deliver a broad range of compliance, safety, and community service functions. The Unit is currently resourced by 2 Field Rangers, 5 Rangers, 1 Rangers Operations Officer, administration support, and led by a Team Leader. In addition, the newly constructed Animal Management Facility is resourced with 2.5 Facility Assistants and 1 Facility Officer. These positions are a result of a restructure to the Unit and additional resources endorsed through the 2025/26 Council budget, ensuring the Unit is equipped to service the new facility.

The Unit’s operations are based around programmed services and patrols, as well as responses to both internal service requests and customer service requests. With the Unit tracking to receive in excess of 5,300 customer service requests this year, a risk-based approach is applied to prioritise and manage these requests, focusing on risks to people, animals, and the environment.

The Rangers Unit operates 7 days a week between 7am and 4pm, providing coverage across the community wherever possible. Council ultimately determines service levels and resources, and as with any service, the level of coverage is directly linked to the resources allocated, the more resources that are allocated, the more coverage the service will receive.

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. receives the Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 9 October 2025 and

  2. adopts the Executive Leadership Team's recommendations as follows:

    6.1.    Bakers Road, Dunbible
    In relation to Bakers Road, Dunbible, due to its condition, a 4.5-tonne load limit is to be imposed on the Kyogle Road access.

    6.2.    Stokers Road, Stokers Siding
    That the request to upgrade the existing 'Give Way' sign to a 'Stop' sign on Stokers Road, Stokers Siding, at its intersection with Tweed Valley Way, along with associated line marking, be supported. In addition, that a 'Stop Sign Ahead' warning sign be installed on Stokers Road on the approach to Tweed Valley Way, and a secondary 'Stop' sign be installed on the right-hand side of Blakeneys Road at its intersection with Tweed Valley Way.

    7.1.    Creek Street, Hastings Point
    In relation to Creek Street, Hastings Point, the request for a yellow no-stopping line on the northern side of Creek Street, Hastings Point, be supported. A 20 metre length of yellow no-stopping line, measured from the intersection with Tweed Coast Road and aligning with current yellow no stopping line marking, be installed to reinforce existing road rules, improve compliance, and enhance safety for both vehicles and pedestrians.

    7.2.    Philp Parade, Tweed Heads South
    In relation to Philp Parade, Tweed Heads South, the request for prohibitive parking is not supported, given adequate sight distance and traffic volumes, and the matter be referred to Council Rangers for enforcement.

    7.3.    Meridian Way, Tweed Heads
    In relation to Meridian Way, Tweed Heads, the request for the installation of convex mirror, no stopping line and roundabout upgrade, are not supported. Transport for NSW do not support convex mirrors in high volume environments, the existing line markings are adequate and the road reserve is insufficient for a roundabout.
 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  None

Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that Council write to the Federal Minister for the Environment and Water, the Minister for the Environment (NSW), Minister for Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (NSW), local state members, local federal member, the Australian Packaging Covenant Organisation and Soft Plastics Stewardship Australia:

  1. noting: 
    1. that each year approximately 320 tons of soft plastic are dumped into landfill in our shire; and
    2. the strong concern by many in our community at the difficulty of accessing and using soft plastic recycling despite the waste of precious finite resources and the danger, especially to our endangered wildlife species, when it is dumped into landfill

  2.  requesting the Government to: 
    1. increase producer responsibilities for soft plastics by mandating a percentage use of recycled plastic in new plastic products, mandating design standards on packaging and reforms/bans on certain types of packaging (e.g. plastic fish containers for soy sauce), requiring clear, consistent labelling, and establish mandatory soft plastic recycling targets;
    2. place a levy on production and consumption of polymer plastic made from fossil fuel and particularly for single use and packaging and use of the levy to support establishment of plastic recycling research and facilities; and
    3.  fund soft plastics collection recycling programs including financial support for councils undertaking collection for soft plastic recycling
 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None

Councillor Brinsmead asks can we please have an update on the Ed Parker Rotary car park upgrade and when it is expected to be finalised?


The Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, the project is not yet complete. While most contract deliverables were completed by 14 November 2025, turfing and topsoiling remains outstanding items. Council staff are liaising closely with the contractors to ensure the turf meets the contract specification. Final topsoiling will occur within the coming days. The contract includes a post completion period of 12-months. In addition, Council staff have prepared a landscape maintenance plan for the area.

The primary project objectives have been met, which are to protect the foreshore from further erosion through the removal of unapproved and dilapidated structures and the construction of a revetment wall. Other important features included access stairs and a pelican perch.
