Councillor Brinsmead asks what plans or programs does Council have planned to celebrate Christmas in 2025 in the Tweed Shire?


The Director Corporate Services replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, Council has, along with other organisations, various planned programs to celebrate Christmas 2025 across the Tweed Shire: 

For programs: 

  1. The Tweed Festive Glow Guide is back again. This interactive community map encourages residents/households that want to share their light displays with the public to submit details and a picture to be loaded onto an Interactive map that families and residents can use on their mobile devices to search great places near them or drive around to see the best displays in the region. The page includes information about Wildlife friendly festive lighting. The interactive map and links will be launched from 1 December and will be available on Council’s website soon.  

  2. The Tweed Festive Shopfront campaign will be on again following the inaugural one in 2024. This campaign is a collaboration with the three business chambers (Tweed Heads, Kingscliff and Murwillumbah) and the Tweed Valley Weekly. It encourages our businesses to get festive by creating vibrant and activated business precincts and our community to shop local. There will be a winner in each region of Tweed Heads and Urban Surrounds; Tweed Coast; and Murwillumbah and Rural Villages, with a prize pack for each winner valued at $1000. This includes 1 x $500 gift pay voucher for winners to choose their preferred voucher, ¼ page advertising space in the Tweed Valley Weekly and 1 x annual Chamber membership. Businesses can submit their details with a picture to be loaded onto an interactive map. Competition information and entries are available on Councils website. 

  3. The Tweed Tourism Company is coordinating and publishing the annual Tweed Gift Guide encouraging local gift ideas from a range of tourism and business operators. 

  4. The three Business Chambers have historically led activations or programs in their CBD areas. Council has on occasion supported the Business Chambers with specific requests of funding or activations within their areas. At this stage, there is minimal planned activations from the chambers this year. 
    • Tweed Business Chamber have confirmed no activations this year. 
    • Kingscliff Business Chamber is seeking to light a pine tree in Rowan Robinson Park. 
    • Murwillumbah Business Chamber have confirmed no activations for this year. 

For Public Lighting and Displays:

  • The Murwillumbah bridge lights will change to festive colours on Monday 1 December. 

  • The Kingscliff Fig Tree is lit all year round. 

  • Public installation of Christmas decorations will occur after hours from Monday 1 December 2025 in: 
    • Wollumbin Street, Murwillumbah Street and Alma Street roundabout 
    • Wharf Street to Florence Street, Tweed Heads 
    • A small display of festive decorations is again being installed at the Murwillumbah Railway Station and Northern Rivers Rail Trail, with Santa and helpers doing some surprise runs and handing out merchandise on the Rail Trail to surprise and delight. 

For Events: 

  • What’s On Tweed will continue to promote the wide range of events across the region with some feature and focused Christmas events. 

  • Council has sponsored three community Christmas events under the 2025-2026 Events Sponsorship funding round: 
    • Lions Club of Kingscliff – Carols by the Coast ($2,500) Tuesday 9 December 2025 
    • Murwillumbah Rotary Club – Carols in the park ($5,100) Friday 12 December 2025 
    • Lions Club Cabarita Beach and Pottsville – Community Christmas Party ($950) Saturday 13 December 2025 

For Council Communications:

A Council Community Christmas Message featuring Councillors who wish to participate is being planned and aiming to be published the week prior to Christmas. 

Tweed Shire Council’s regular community message banners will be up at Tweed Heads and Murwillumbah leading into Christmas. 

Council’s social media and Tweed Link content will also promote much of the above and focus on education around reducing waste and availability of Council services over the Christmas period. 

Council’s two front counters at Tweed and Murwillumbah will be decorated accordingly and tastefully with a focus on nature, no plastic and festive well wishes for all denominations. 

For Mayor’s Christmas Appeal:

The Mayor has chosen to focus on homelessness this year and will be encouraging those who wish to, and are able to give, to donate money directly to local services Fred’s Place and Agape Outreach Inc. This appeal will be promoted through the usual communication channels.

Councillor Owen asks how many homes in each suburb/locality of Tweed Shire will be impacted with new flood planning levels in the proposed 'Interim Flood Planning Levels Policy'?


The Director Engineering replied:

Through you Madam Mayor, there are approximately 9,200 potentially flood prone residential buildings in the Tweed Shire. Of these, approximately 3,300 already have floor levels that are non-compliant with (current) flood planning level. With the proposed Interim Flood Planning Levels Policy and associated DCP-A3 updates (currently on exhibition) this number will increase to approximately 4,900 houses (ie approximately 1600 additional houses becoming non-compliant with the proposed flood planning level).

Mapping is included in the public exhibition GIS package to define this: https://experience.arcgis.com/experience/654af0f409474618b01fca0baf09cd25/page/Floor-Levels-to-DFE.

The proposed updates will help ensure new homes and buildings are built above known flood levels, with a lower risk of flooding and greater resilience to climate change.

DCP-A3 includes an allowance for “minor additions” to existing dwellings with floor levels that do not comply with flood planning level (ie are lower). This allowance attempts to provide reasonable flexibility for minor additions to existing dwellings without permitting broadscale expansion of residential floor area at levels that would result in significant property losses during floods.

Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor) returned to the meeting at 07:58pm.

Cr James Owen
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

RESOLVED that: 

  1. Council notes its concern that the recent amendments to the Model Code of Meeting Practice for Local Councils in NSW are regressive and potentially discriminatory, particularly in relation to:
    1. restricting councillor remote attendance to instances of ill-health or caring responsibilities; and
    2. removing or limiting pre-meeting councillor briefings.

  2. Council recognises that these provisions discriminate against hardworking, community focussed councillors who juggle their public duties with employment, family, and other community obligations, and that they fail to reflect modern flexible work practices.

  3. that the Mayor writes to the Minister for Local Government, with copies to the Shadow Minister for Local Government, Local Government NSW, the Northern Rivers Joint Organisation and all NSW councils, outlining Council’s position and calling for a review and amendment of the Model Code of Meeting Practice consistent with this resolution. The letter to also include that the Minister for Local Government urgently amend the Model Code of Meeting Practice to:

    1. permit councillors to attend Council and Committee meetings remotely via audio-visual link for legitimate and reasonable reasons, including but not limited to:
      • when the councillor is outside the local government area due to work or business commitments.
      • when absent due to family or personal responsibilities;
      • when travelling or on personal leave/holidays, should the councillor choose to participate; and
      • when representing the Council at official events, conferences, or community engagements.

    2. ensure that councillors attending remotely under these circumstances retain full voting rights and are deemed present for quorum purposes, provided transparency and accessibility requirements are met.

    3. reinstate and protect pre-meeting councillor briefings as legitimate non-decision-making forums that enable councillors to obtain clarification and information from staff prior to formal meetings.

    4. requests that the Minister provide clear guidance confirming that councillors participating remotely have the same obligations and rights as those attending in person, with meetings to remain transparent via livestream or public recording.

    5. encourages other NSW councils to adopt similar resolutions to ensure that the Model Code supports effective representation, diversity, and modern governance practices across local government.


 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  None

AMENDMENT 

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that Council:
 
  1. notes the existing Psychosocial Safety Framework, whole-of-organisation and community approach aimed at preventing and managing psychosocial risks for staff and Councillors that has been in place in Tweed since January 2025.

  2. notes that Council has been recently nominated as a finalist in the 2025 Psychosocial Safety and Leadership awards in 2 categories: Outstanding Leadership and Best Team Collaboration for Psychosocial safety and commends staff on the proactive measures put in place.

  3. notes that Council has also this week been awarded Employer of Choice 2025 in the Local Government Engineers Association Awards with the Award particularly focussing on Tweed’s creation of a safe, inclusive and future focused workplace and congratulates staff on this achievement.

  4. notes that, in addition to this, councillors have, from time to time, expressed concerns that current local government processes and governance structures can make it difficult for elected representatives to fully and effectively perform their roles, with some feeling that the system can be overly weighted towards staff and executive functions, leaving councillors feeling insufficiently supported or valued, and some feeling there are insufficient mechanisms in place to protect both staff and themselves from bullying behaviour from their colleagues and the community.

  5. acknowledges that elected representatives face unique psychosocial risks arising from the responsibilities of public office, high levels of public scrutiny, complex decision-making, and interpersonal dynamics within the council environment.

  6. notes that Council provides free and confidential access to mental health professionals for Councillors and their families, has facilitated independent professionals to identify Councillor nominated psychosocial risks and has a confidential incident reporting mechanism specifically for Councillors to report psychosocial incidents and a protocol in place in order to try to address some of the above psychosocial risks faced by Councillors.

  7. recognises that a structured, proactive framework for councillor psychological safety and well-being is consistent with contemporary governance best-practice and is essential for fostering a respectful, high-performing, and resilient organisation.

  8. defers further consideration of potential actions to be taken to address Councillor Psychosocial safety and Well-being until the results of the Councillor Psychosocial Risk Assessment conducted in conjunction with Councillors in September this year are brought back to Council. 
 
The Amendment was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that Council: 

  1. notes the passing of the Planning Reform Bill through the NSW Parliament on Tuesday 11 November 2025. 

  1. writes to the Hon Chris Minns MP (NSW Premier), the Hon Paul Scully MP (Minister for Planning and Public Spaces), the Hon Ron Hoenig MP (Minister for Local Government), Mrs Janelle Saffin MP (Member for Lismore) and Mr Geoff Provest MP (Member for Tweed) to: 
    1. express Council’s deep disappointment that, as a result of the Planning Reform Bill, elected Councillors are proposed to be excluded from having any role in determining development assessments (DAs) in their Local Government Area (LGA) once a Local Planning Panel (LPP) has been established. Council notes that this exclusion was introduced without consultation with peak local government bodies such as Local Government NSW, the NSW Country Mayors Association, or Regional Cities of NSW.
    2. challenge the NSW Government’s decision to remove elected Councillors from involvement in local DA determination and call for the immediate retention of Councillors DA determination role as it existed prior to the Planning Reform Bill. 
    3. convey Council’s serious concern it was never advised that the planning reforms would remove the ability of elected Councillors to consider DAs within their LGA. 
    4. call upon the NSW Government to work with all NSW Councils and Local Government peak bodies to review this specific change, with the objective of retaining the current system that allows elected Councillors to fulfil their vital civic role of representing their communities through active involvement in DA decision-making. 

  1. writes to the Local Government NSW requesting the inclusion of the following urgent motion at the upcoming LGNSW conference:
"That Local Government NSW:
 
  1. acknowledges the passage of the NSW Government’s Planning System Reform Bill, recognises the scale and urgency of the housing crisis across New South Wales, and the intent of the reforms to improve the efficiency and clarity of development assessment.

  2. recognises the leadership shown by many councils to improve the efficiency of the development assessment process, including improvements in meeting assessment benchmarks and streamlined pathways.
     
  3. calls on the NSW Government to halt implementation and undertake genuine consultation with the local government sector before progressing these reforms, particularly regarding:
    1. the establishment and operation of Local Planning Panels where they don’t currently exist outside metropolitan Sydney (including joint panels)
    2. the transition from Regional Planning Panels
    3. resourcing, governance and administrative impacts on councils, and
    4. implications for local communities and for councils’ existing planning processes, including alignment with local strategic planning and community participation plans.
        
  4. notes concern about the removal of development assessment powers from democratically elected councils once Local Planning Panels are constituted, and:
    1. acknowledges the mixed community experience with panel models in metropolitan Sydney, and
    2. affirms the importance of elected councillors continuing to represent community views and provide local knowledge within the planning system.
       
  5. requests that the NSW Government:
    1. retains the ability for local democratically elected Councils to determine development applications to the same extent as is currently practiced.
    2. ensure clear mechanisms for local representation and input into Local Planning Panels and joint panels, noting that many regional/rural councils cover vast areas and do not have wards.
    3. provide adequate resourcing to councils to support new assessment, reporting and panel administration requirements, and
    4. maintain meaningful opportunities for councils and communities to participate in significant development assessment, including through transparent public processes, sufficient time for meaningful consultation and clear communication of decisions."
 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Tay Lee from the Tweed Valley Uniting Church:


"God of grace and wisdom,

We give thanks today for the Tweed Shire — for its natural beauty, its vibrant and diverse communities, and for all who call this place home. We honour the Traditional Custodians of this land and acknowledge their deep connection to Country and their faithful care for it across countless generations.

As this Council gathers, we seek Your wisdom and guidance.
Bless our Mayor as chair of this meeting with calm leadership, clear thinking, and a spirit of cooperation.
Grant each Councillor patience, respect, and a shared commitment to serving the common good.
We also pray for all Council staff — may their work be marked by peace, collaboration, and fairness.

As we approach the holiday season, we ask for Your protection over our community. Keep our roads, beaches, waterways, and gathering places safe. Watch over residents and visitors alike. May every household in the Shire enjoy this season with peace, joy, and an equal opportunity to rest, celebrate, and connect with those they love.

Lord, inspire us all to embody the values of this community — to care for people and places, to listen well, to work together, and to build a future where the Tweed Shire continues to flourish.

So we commit this meeting, this Council, and this Shire into Your faithful hands.

 In Jesus’ name we pray,

 Amen."

CONFIDENTIAL COMMITTEE

REPRESENTATIONS FOR ITEMS CONSIDERED IN COMMITTEE
(Sec 3.40, 13.9 to 13.17 Model Code of Meeting Practice)
 
EXCLUSION OF PRESS AND PUBLIC

Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor) 
Cr Nola Firth
   
RESOLVED that Council moves itself into a Confidential Committee in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993 and that the press and public be excluded from the whole of the Committee Meeting, because, in the opinion of the Committee, publicity of the proceedings of the Committee would be prejudicial to the public interest, by reasons of the confidential nature of the business to be transacted.   
  
Under Council’s Model Code of Meeting Practice, members of the public may make representations before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  If you wish to make any representations, you are invited to do so now.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr James Owen

Cr Brinsmead declared a Pecuniary Interest in Item 16.3 "Chamber Business Boost Program - a pilot for a new Council initiative". Cr Owen declared a Non-Pecuniary Significant Interest in Item 16.3 "Chamber Business Boost Program - a pilot for a new Council initiative". RESOLVED that Council:

      1. The Hon Julie Collins - Minister for Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry

  4. request the Ministers work collaboratively to guarantee long-term funding and support for eradication efforts outlined in the National Fire Ant Eradication Program Response Plan.

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

PROPOSED that Council: 

  1. notes the importance of native bees to the environment, recognising their critical role in pollination, biodiversity, and the health of local ecosystems,

  2. notes the priority actions in the Tweed Conservation Strategy 2025-35 contribute to increasing the native bee population, thereby supporting pollination, biodiversity, and the resilience of local ecosystems, 

  3. notes the review being undertaken on Council’s planting list for streets, parks, and other public areas will consider the habitat values of recommended species, alongside requirements for hardiness, low maintenance, and aesthetics,

  4. requests the General Manager to continue to promote community awareness on native bees and other species through Council’s Sustainability and Environment Unit’s newsletters by: 
    1. educating the community on the ecological role of native bees and other species 
    2. encouraging residents to adopt pollinator-friendly practices such as planting native flora and reducing pesticide use 
    3. supporting the objectives of the Tweed Conservation Strategy 

  5. requests the General Manager to consider additional actions regarding increasing the native bee population at the next review of the Tweed Conservation Strategy.
 
The Motion was Lost 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Meredith Dennis

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. develop a Native Bee Support and Habitat Enhancement Program aimed at improving habitat, food sources, and public awareness for native bee populations across the Tweed Shire.

  2. prepares a report to Council outlining:
    1. opportunities to expand native flowering vegetation within parks, road reserves, community gardens, and Council-managed lands.
    2. options for installing native bee hotels or nesting structures in appropriate public locations.
    3. guidelines and best-practice principles for creating pollinator-friendly landscaping in Council projects.
    4. educational programs to support community awareness of native bees, their ecological importance, and how residents can assist.
    5. opportunities to collaborate with local Landcare groups, schools, nurseries and beekeeping associations.
    6. funding options, including grants from state or federal biodiversity programs.

  3. incorporates native bee-friendly planting into Council’s ongoing revegetation, street-tree, and open-space management programs wherever feasible.

  4. promotes pesticide-free or reduced-pesticide management zones in selected parks or natural areas, based on ecological advice, to protect native pollinators.

  5. receives a progress report within 12 months on actions undertaken and measurable outcomes in improving native bee habitat and community engagement.
 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. undertakes a comprehensive audit of public bin provision across the Shire, including current bin locations, capacity, servicing schedules, and condition, with particular focus on:
    1. high-visitation coastal areas;
    2. areas serving tourist accommodation (caravan parks, holiday rentals, resort areas);
    3. commercial precincts and main street areas; and
    4. comparative analysis with bin provision in equivalent areas in neighbouring councils to establish best-practice benchmarks

  2. brings back a report that includes:
    1. recommendations for increased bin provision in high-visitation and high-impact areas, with specific locations and bin types (including options for secure/tamper-resistant designs to address misuse);
    2. cost estimates for implementation of recommended upgrades;
    3. enhanced servicing schedules (emptying and cleaning) for high-traffic areas to maintain bin capacity and visual amenity;
    4. integration with community masterplans to ensure bin infrastructure aligns with broader upgrade plans;
    5. develops a communication and education strategy to promote responsible bin use, clearly distinguishing between park use (picnic waste, recyclables) and residential waste disposal, to address ongoing issues with household rubbish in public bins; and
    6. recognises that enhanced public bin infrastructure supports visitor experience, tourism economic development, the viability of Council's own caravan park operations, and Council's commitment to consistent, equitable service delivery across all communities in the Shire.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RESOLVED that Council: 

  1. notes the increasing incidence of graffiti within the Shire and the limitations of Council’s current responsibilities under the Graffiti Vandalism Management Policy and allocated resources. 

  2. initiates formal discussions with relevant infrastructure owners to explore a coordinated graffiti management protocol. 

  3. shares information with Tweed Byron Police and relevant agencies on identified graffiti hotspots. 

  4. requests the General Manager to develop a public awareness campaign highlighting: 
    • that graffiti is a crime requiring police reporting; 
    • the amenity and financial impacts of graffiti on the Tweed community; 
    • how to report graffiti to the appropriate authority depending on asset ownership; and 
    • Council’s commitment to rapid remediation of graffiti on Council assets as a deterrent to offenders.

Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. initiates formal discussions with Transport for NSW, Essential Energy, Telstra, Australia Post, NBN Co, and other relevant infrastructure operators to establish a coordinated graffiti management protocol that clarifies responsibilities, response timeframes, and escalation procedures for infrastructure under their jurisdiction, with particular focus on high-visibility areas.

  2. undertakes a comprehensive audit of identified graffiti hotspots across the Shire to determine infrastructure ownership, responsible parties, and current remediation timeframes, with particular focus on locations where public amenity is significantly impacted and patterns suggest repeat offending.

  3. reviews the existing Graffiti Management Policy provision for cost-recovery removal of graffiti from private property and brings back a report outlining options for increasing Council's proactive engagement with private property owners in high-visibility areas, including potential partnership and subsidy models to address persistent graffiti on prominent private property that impacts community perception of local areas.

  4. brings back a report detailing options for implementing a proactive, rapid-response graffiti removal program on Council-managed assets, including evaluation of:
    1. establishing a dedicated mobile response team that identifies and removes graffiti within 48–72 hours of detection to disrupt offender motivation patterns and deter recurrence;
    2. strategic resourcing to expand the current Graffiti Management and Maintenance Crew to priority areas across the Shire, with particular attention to high-traffic public spaces; and
    3. community partnership models where residents can participate in low-risk graffiti removal activities under Council supervision and support.

  5. works with Tweed-Byron Police and relevant agencies to develop an intelligence-sharing protocol regarding recurrent graffiti offenders, noting that consistent tagging patterns across the Shire suggest a small number of repeat offenders who would benefit from targeted intervention.

  6. conducts a review of the 'Report a Problem' online portal to improve functionality, geolocation accuracy, and usability on mobile devices, removing barriers to community reporting.

    2. the amenity impact and financial cost of graffiti to the Tweed community;
    3. how to report graffiti to the appropriate authority (Council, Transport for NSW, Telstra, Essential Energy, etc.) depending on infrastructure ownership; and
    4. Council's commitment to rapid remediation of graffiti on Council assets as a deterrent to offenders.

Cr James Owen
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. immediately conducts a site assessment at Hastings Point, in consultation with local bird conservation experts and community members, to evaluate current fencing adequacy, habitat condition, and visitor disturbance patterns, and to identify specific areas requiring enhanced protection.

  2. brings back a report that includes recommendations for:
    1. extension of permanent fencing to encompass current resting and nesting areas, with particular attention to proximity to critical driftwood habitat and extension into water where necessary to create effective barriers to human disturbance
    2. enhancement and formalisation of secondary protected zones, particularly on the northern side of the creek, using permanent fencing to allow habitat recovery following cyclone damage and to provide alternative nesting and resting areas for pied oystercatchers, sooty oystercatchers, and beach stone curlews
    3. habitat enhancement measures to improve food availability in key feeding areas, including rock bed restoration and investigation of ecological management approaches to support natural prey populations
    4. dog management and visitor control protocols, including enhanced ranger patrols, improved signage clarity and placement, and evaluation of access restriction options to minimise human and canine disturbance during critical nesting and chick-rearing periods.
    5. cost estimates and funding sources for implementation, including exploration of grant funding from state and federal environmental agencies
    6. timeline for staged implementation prioritising immediate fencing extension and enforcement of dog-prohibited zones

  3. considers conducting similar site assessments in other Pied Oystercatcher populated areas in Tweed Shire. 

  4. works with state environmental agencies (NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy and Environment, and relevant fisheries authorities) to coordinate threatened species management, share conservation objectives, and align Council actions with broader recovery plans for pied oystercatchers, sooty oystercatchers, and beach stone curlews across Tweed Shire. 

  5. develops a community engagement and education strategy to build awareness of endangered species conservation needs, explain the importance of visitor distance and behaviour restrictions, and celebrate local conservation successes

  6. acknowledges the community's strong support for bird protection at Hastings Point and other areas within Tweed Shire, and commits to treating endangered species conservation as a priority that reflects Council's values and fulfils its obligation to protect the natural environment for current and future generations

AMENDMENT

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

PROPOSED that Council:

  1. notes that rainfall over the past five years has been significantly higher on average than historical records, and that floodplain drainage is influenced by rainfall, groundwater levels, tides, storm surge and floodplain characteristics. 

  2. notes that tidal inundation mapping has been completed for areas adjacent to the Tweed Coastal Creeks, and that drainage impacts will be extensive in future decades due to higher low tides.

  3. notes the complexity of management measures such as potential dredging of Tweed Coast estuary entrances, and that hydraulic impact assessment, cost-benefit analysis, environmental legislation and policy would likely not support the case for dredging to improve drainage in low-lying Acid Sulfate Soils (ASS) affected farmland. 

  4. notes that any modifications to estuary entrance channel depths would likely be quickly reversed due to natural shoaling processes at the creek mouth, and that short-term improvements to local drainage could be offset by increased tidal range and inundation of land in ocean-based events.

  5. notes that the significant Acid Sulfate Soils (ASS) issues affecting water quality in the Cudgen Lake and Cudgera Creek catchments have been well understood for many years and acknowledges the large body of research and remediation efforts that have been undertaken in these areas by both landowners and Council.

  6. notes that successful remediation of the two highest priority Acid Sulfate Soils (ASS) hotspots in the Cudgen and Cudgera Creek catchments would require significant funding, and potentially, both short and long-term land use change.

  7. writes to Sunshine Sugar and NSW Cane Growers (Tweed) highlighting its willingness to support and collaborate on projects that seek to mitigate the impact of Acid Sulfate Soils (ASS) and improve water quality.

  8. writes to the NSW Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development - Fisheries and Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water, highlighting its concern with known Acid Sulfate Soils (ASS) hotspots on the Tweed coastal floodplain, and urging that leadership and resources commensurate with the scale and costs of remediation works be provided, to re-commence efforts to undertake remediation of these areas.

Councillor Brinsmead asks, can you please advise what has been done / can be done / will be done to address the ongoing and increasing issue of illegal camping in Pottsville including along Tweed Coast Road to Wooyung?

The Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Current and ongoing actions include:
  • Patrol hours: Council Rangers are resourced to operate between 7:00am and 4:00pm, meaning all patrols along the Pottsville–Wooyung stretch are conducted during these hours.
  • Illegal camping patrols are conducted weekly and once over the weekend along the coastal strip.
  • Signage enforcement: "no camping / no parking 11pm–5am" signs have been installed across the coastal strip. Signage is regularly reviewed and replaced to ensure enforceability by Rangers and NSW Police
  • Council Ranger patrols address illegal camping, animal control, and littering offences simultaneously.
  • Police assistance is requested when campers refuse to provide details, ensuring compliance and safety.
  • Challenges with enforcement include:
  • Rough sleepers living in vehicles.
  • International visitors lacking enforceable identification (e.g., driver’s licence).
  • Overseas fine payment rates historically as low as 10%, creating financial/resource strain.
  • Unapproved events management: Rangers collaborate with NSW Police and NPWS. Recent deterrent measures include boulder placement to block vehicle access at known event sites.

Councillor Brinsmead asks can we please have an update on the newly established Tweed Shire CBD crews, including when it is expected that they will commence, what their tasks will be and their initial target areas?


The Director Engineering replied:

The available budget allocation will provide for a single 2 person crew and a utility work vehicle, reporting to the Roads and Stormwater Unit.  Recruitment has proved challenging and has delayed commencement, however this is expected to be finalised in January with the crew to start in late January or early February 2026.
 
Once operational, the CBD crew will focus on non-structural cleaning and tidying activities of road reserve areas, including rubbish and litter removal, leaf blowing, graffiti removal, guerneying footpaths and furnishings, storm clean up, and weed removal.  The crew will also help to proactively identify and report more significant maintenance issues outside of their capabilities that need the attention of roads or parks maintenance crews.  Initially the crew will focus on seven CBDs of Tweed Heads, Tweed Heads South, Murwillumbah, Kingscliff, Cabarita Beach, Pottsville and Burringbar, with activities limited to the core Main Street areas only.  Based on productivity, expenditure, demand and public feedback, the scope of these activities can be reviewed over time.
 
In the meantime while recruitment is underway, and to ensure areas are ready for the summer tourism influx, a number of CBD works are underway across the Shire.  Pedestrian crossings and road markings have recently been revitalised within the Murwillumbah town centre.  Further work under the “Border Beautiful” Tweed Heads CBD Revitalisation Project includes repainting of 6 pedestrian crossings (red and white) in Wharf, Bay, Stuart & Frances Streets carried out as night work this week – with the last occurring tonight (weather permitting).  A cleaning contractor has also been arranged to work during this same period to utilise the road closure and detour arrangements.  This cleaning work is to pressure wash road medians, islands and roundabouts between the Border and Frances Street with exact coverage to be determined subject to time and budget.

Councillor Owen asks what is the intent of the proposal to depoliticisatise the General Manager's role in the NSW Government's new Code of Meeting Practice and how will it impact civic business in Tweed Shire Council?

The Director Corporate Services replied:

The changes to the Model Code of Meeting Practice (both proposed and implemented) which were identified as depoliticising the role of the General Manager, are intended to protect the general manager from being brought into political arguments between councillors. The Office of Local Government confirmed this intent.

As noted in the explanatory paper issued with the consultation draft of the Model Meeting Code, “The changes will also reinforce the boundaries between councillors and general managers by depoliticising the role they play in council meetings. General managers will no longer need to provide advice on motions requiring the expenditure of funds. Disputes over the future direction of a council and the spending of ratepayer money should rightfully occur between elected councillors”.

The revised Model Code of Meeting Practice removes the non-mandatory provision allowing general managers to prepare reports for notices of motion. The Office of Local Government have advised that, “The Model Meeting Code is now silent on this and there is nothing to prevent councils from including a supplementary provision in their adopted meeting code based on the previous non-mandatory provision. Alternatively, in the absence of such a provision, there is nothing to prevent a general manager from providing a report in relation to a notice of motion where they consider that councillors would benefit from additional information about the proposed motion”.

Council has adopted the following supplementary provision in the new Code of Meeting Practice:
“If the notice of motion submitted by a councillor has significant legal, strategic, financial or policy implications which should be taken into consideration by the meeting, the notice of motion must call for a report to the Council, which if resolved, will consider those issues and be presented as an officer’s report at a future Ordinary Meeting of Council”.

This change is essentially a refinement of the previous approach. The impact on civic business will be minimal, but it achieves a better balance of protecting the General Manager while supporting informed decision-making.

Councillor Owen asks please provide an update on the Old Bogangar Road Light Spillage tree planting and report that was requested at the 19 June 2025 meeting?

The Director Engineering replied:

Council is still awaiting formal handover of the Tweed Coast Road intersection from the Kings Forest developer.
 
However, in the meantime Council staff have been investigating solutions to the light spillage complaints from Old Bogangar Road, including discussions between senior staff and impacted residents. The agreed approach is the replacement of several trees planted along the Old Bogangar Road noise wall with Eumundi Ash, which is a tall, fast growing native tree that is suitable for this constrained roadside environment.  Aeroscreens will also be fitted to the street lights on the western side of Tweed Coast Road to reduce light spill in the direction of the dwellings.  These amendments will be carried out at Council’s cost, as the developer implemented the intersection lighting in accordance with applicable Australian Standards.
 
The future report to Council will suggest changes to specifications to avoid such conflicts in the future.  However, issues of this nature are somewhat inevitable when a semi-rural area interfaces with a major land release area like Kings Forest.
 
Subject to other priorities, Council staff will aim to provide the additional report in March 2026, however this will not delay the above planned rectification works; pending handover of the infrastructure.

Councillor Owen asks please provide an update on the Draft Feasibility Study of the Indoor Sports Facility and 50m Pool, including the proposed location?


The Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replied: 
 
As per the Councillor workshop held on 27 November 2025, the feasibility study is nearing completion. Key components undertaken include:
  • Demand analysis
  • Masterplan development
  • Site section
  • Preliminary financial analysis
  • Benefit-cost analysis.

Preferred sites have been identified through a thorough site selection process.  These locations will be detailed in the forthcoming report to Council next year.  The sites were chosen based on accessibility, suitability for both the indoor sports facility and 50m pool, alignment with community need, and third-party funding considerations.

With regards to next steps, staff are aiming for a report to be presented to the February Council meeting with Council will determine whether to proceed in full (both sports facility and pool), in part (scaled or staged delivery), or not at all.
If Council resolves to proceed, the next stages will include:
  • Pursuing funding opportunities with State and Federal Governments and other third parties
  • Developing concept designs
  • Undertaking a detailed financial analysis of operating, maintaining, and renewing the project, including any capital and recurrent funds and depreciation that would need to be met by Council and the predicted effect on ratepayers, and
  • Community consultation to ensure local input informs the final decision-making process.

Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RESOLVED that Council:

1.  In regard to the Department of Planning, Housing & Infrastructure’s Expert Planner Final Report for Tweed Shire Council, receive and note this report. 
 
2. Endorse the following actions:
  • Update Development Application Guide – Council updates its Development Application Guide to reflect current environmental priorities and legislative requirements. An evaluation is made of the customer benefits of making the Guide a digital document that integrates with Council’s other digital customer service tools.
  • Continue industry information-sharing events – Council continues its program of information sharing events with industry.
  • Update website for variations register – The ‘variations to development standards’ subpage on the Tweed Council website is updated to include reference to the ‘variations register’ on the NSW planning portal, for information on Council’s recent variation determinations.
  • Evaluate methodology for DA Panel meetings – Pre-DA advice is simplified in terms of type and length, so that it focuses on providing direction on key and uncommon issues. Issues are categorised as: Determinative; Clarification required; Able to be conditioned.
  • Review GIS display and planning browser – Council reviews the display of GIS data on its website and evaluates creating a planning and development browser combining relevant layers to allow customers to overlay environmental layers.
  • Update consultant list wording – Update website to refer to consultants as ‘professionals to help’ rather than ‘qualified professionals to help’. Add text to identify: Consultants are not verified or endorsed by Council; Use of the consultant does not guarantee an approval.
  • Create internal referrals dashboard – Dashboard visible to all participants in DA process, recording lodgement date, referral issue date, and advice issue date.
  • Structure RFI letters for clarity – Categories: Determinative; Clarification required; Able to be conditioned.
  • Advocate to ePlanning for system improvements – Address system errors delaying assessment.
  • Review matters reported to Council based on Estimated Development Cost – Facilitate discussion on whether thresholds remain appropriate.
  • That Council recognise Planning focus meetings as being an important tool.  The Planning Manager may request experts to attend a meeting in 7 days, and the experts must make themselves available.  The experts will attend with sufficient knowledge to allow negotiations to occur to establish a whole of council position on issues. 
 
3. Receive and note the following suggested actions as being not endorsed at this stage (note the officers comments in the body of the report to demonstrate what actions are being taken to address these suggested actions):
  • KPIs for pre-lodgement services – 
  1. Planning and Building Appointment: Meeting held within 5 days of date of request; 
  2. Targeted advice: Advice provided within 7 days of request; 
  3. Development Assessment Panels: Meeting held within 21 days of request; Minutes issued within 5 days of meeting. 
  4. KPIs must be displayed on ‘Development and Business’ webpage.
  • Adequacy review and invoicing KPIs – Technical Officers complete pre-lodgement adequacy reviews within 4 days of submission; invoices issued within 4 days; applicant given 3 days to make payment.
  • Review Community Engagement Plan for reduced notification – Consider excluding small-scale residential developments from notification.
  • Fast-track referrals within 5 days – Technical Team Leaders review all referral requests within 1 day; simple matters identified for fast-track assessment and determined within 5 days.
  • KPI: 60 DA determinations per month – Planning and Regulation Division to determine 60 applications per month; review target every 6 months.
 4.  Continues to lobby for the NSW Department of Planning DA League Table to include the "median" statistic as another measure to inform proponents of the likely assessment time for an application. 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Meredith Dennis ​

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Nola Firth

RESOLVED that Council:
  1. notes trees in urban environments are considered an important adaptation strategy to respond to urban heat, increasing numbers of hot days and heat waves. Trees provide shade, reduce pollution and can lower air temperatures through transpiration. Trees promote active and health lifestyles and offer shade and cooling in areas with higher proportions of vulnerable populations. Trees and under storey vegetation provide urban local native wildlife habitat and corridors.
  1. receives the Canopy Audit Report and notes that although our targets are consistent with the NSW Greener Neighbourhood guide and other NSW Council programs, the first 2 years of the Cool Towns Program has failed to deliver more than a 2% increase in canopy cover in urban areas across Tweed. 

  2. notes that since Cyclone Alfred tree canopy will be further negatively affected.
  1. notes the report findings that the current barriers to increased tree canopy are staff resources, risk management concerns, availability of locations, funding for planting and maintenance, and planning to support the delivery of trees.
  1. notes the proposed Cool Towns Urban Forest Program Action Plan and amends this document to include amending the new Subdivision DCP to maximise planting potential including, where possible, colocation of grey infrastructure services so that suitable planting space is left for street trees and deep soil zones on public and private land.
  1. brings back a report on the changes made in the DCP and to the Cool Towns Urban Forest Action Plan to facilitate increased tree canopy cover in urban areas.
  1. in recognition of the above constraints and the implications of not achieving increased tree canopy, includes an increased allocation of $200,000 per year for urban tree planting and maintenance under the Cool Towns Program for consideration in the December Quarterly Budget Review. 
 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. adopts the following general order of business for Council meetings:
1. Opening Meeting
2.Acknowledgement of Country
3.Prayer
4.Apologies and applications for a leave of absence or attendance by audio-visual link by councillors
5.Confirmation of minutes
6.Disclosures of interests
7.Disclosure of Meeting Information Requests
8.Items to be moved from Confidential to Ordinary / Ordinary to Confidential
9.Schedule of Outstanding Resolutions
10.Mayoral minute(s)
11.Items by Exception
12.Reports to Council
13.Late Reports
14.Notices of Motion
15.Questions with Notice
16.Confidential Items for Consideration
17.Conclusion of Meeting

  1. determines that ordinary meetings of the council are to conclude at 9:00 pm on the day of the meeting.

  1. determines that the adopted order of business and meeting time limit be included in the Code of Meeting Practice (Model) Policy for ease of reference.

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Kimberly Hone
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead

RESOLVED that:

1.      Council delegates owners consent to the General Manager for the lodgement of the Hanson Tweed Sand Plant Expansion – State Significant Development (SSD-10398) application over the unnamed road adjacent to Lot 22 in DP1082435, Lot 1 in DP1250570 and Lot 2 in DP1192506 (Crescent Street, Cudgen) once the Commercial Agreement has been entered into between both parties; 

2.      Council endorses the comments contained within this report subject to the following edits being undertaken to the draft submission: 

Item 3.1 of the draft submission can be amended to state the following:

3.1 Haulage Route: 

It is noted that the haulage route being proposed appears to utilise the northern portion of the unnamed road reserve that is being excluded for the proposed development.

The recent Council decision to exhibit the possible road closure (approved 10 December 2025) identified the possible road closure area as that shown in Figure 1 below.

Figure 1: Proposed Road Closure Area (shown in orange)

Item 7.1 of the draft submission can be amended to state the following:

7.1 Unnamed Road Reserve

Council’s previous comments highlighted that owner's consent had not been obtained for the use of the unnamed road reserve, which is the subject of the latest amendment.  It is noted that the Department issued the proponent with a number of options:

1.      Provide owners consent and / or road closure application (in relation to the unnamed road reserve);

2.      Amend the proposal to remove the road reserve, thereby not requiring land owners consent from Council; or

3.      Modify the existing approval to extend the extraction area, while the issue of land owners consent is being resolved.

Separate to the latest amendment being proposed, the proponent lodged a new road closure application with Council.  Whilst the application was approved at the 10 December 2025 Council meeting, the approval is subject to a 28 day public consultation process which is currently occurring.  As per the resolution of Council, should no reasonable objections be received, the road closure and purchase of the unnamed road reserve is deemed to be approved.  However, should reasonable objections be received, the matter will need to be brought back to Council for a final decision.  In addition to the public consultation process, notification letters have also been sent to relevant authorities (including Crown Lands) requesting comment within a 28 day period.  If a report back to Council is required (due to submissions), the earliest Council meeting for a decision on the road closure / purchase application would be the 23 April 2026 Council meeting. If approved, the road closure / purchase is expected to take some time to process (anywhere from 6 months up to two years).  As a result, the proponent has separately requested owners’ consent from Council.  That matter is being dealt with separately to this submission.  It is expected that should owners’ consent be granted for the use of the unnamed road reserve, the proponent will not be relying upon the latest amendment to remove the unnamed road reserve from the SSD application.

The haulage route matters raised in Item 3.1are highlighted, in that the proposed amendment does not completely resolve owners consent issues; and 

3.       The endorsed submission be forwarded to the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure with regard to the proposed Hanson Tweed Sand Plant Expansion – State Significant Development (SSD-10398).

 
The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone

RESOLVED that Council submit motions to the Australian Local Government Association for the National General Assembly 2026 with the following topics

  1. Advocating to Minister Kristy McBain Minister for Regional Development, Local Government and Territories in relation to improving the NSW State Government's engagement with Local Government concerning changes to the Code of Meeting Practice and planning reforms. 

  2. Advocate to the Treasurer Jim Chalmers and the Minister for Finance, The Hon Katy Gallagher for a move back to a model of more direct funding to Local Government. 

  3. Federal action to ensure consistent regulation across all states with respect to weed and pest animal regulation and identification to avoid problematic border crossings.

Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor) temporarily left the meeting at 11:53am.

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Notes that rainfall over the past five years has been significantly higher on average than historical records, and that floodplain drainage is influenced by rainfall, groundwater levels, tides, storm surge and floodplain characteristics. 

  2. Notes that tidal inundation mapping has been completed for areas adjacent to the Tweed Coastal Creeks, and that drainage impacts will be extensive in future decades due to higher low tides.

  3. Notes the complexity of management measures such as potential dredging of Tweed Coast estuary entrances, and that hydraulic impact assessment, cost-benefit analysis, environmental legislation and policy would likely not support the case for dredging to improve drainage in low-lying Acid Sulfate Soils (ASS) affected farmland. 

  4. Notes that any modifications to estuary entrance channel depths would likely be quickly reversed due to natural shoaling processes at the creek mouth, and that short-term improvements to local drainage could be offset by increased tidal range and inundation of land in ocean-based events.

  5. Notes that the significant Acid Sulfate Soils (ASS) issues affecting water quality in the Cudgen Lake and Cudgera Creek catchments have been well understood for many years and acknowledges the large body of research and remediation efforts that have been undertaken in these areas by both landowners and Council.

  6. Notes that successful remediation of the two highest priority Acid Sulfate Soils (ASS) hotspots in the Cudgen and Cudgera Creek catchments would require significant funding, and potentially, both short and long-term land use change.

  7. Writes to Sunshine Sugar and NSW Cane Growers (Tweed) highlighting its willingness to support and collaborate on projects that seek to mitigate the impact of Acid Sulfate Soils (ASS) and improve water quality.

  8. Writes to the NSW Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development - Fisheries and Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water, highlighting its concern with known Acid Sulfate Soils (ASS) hotspots on the Tweed coastal floodplain, and urging that leadership and resources commensurate with the scale and costs of remediation works be provided, to re-commence efforts to undertake remediation of these areas.
 

The Motion was Carried on the Casting Vote of the Mayor.

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks could you please provide an update outlining the actions already undertaken, the measures available in the short to medium term, and the longer-term plans to address traffic congestion and ongoing issues on Kennedy Drive?

Council has been liaising with Transport for NSW for many years on the issues of traffic congestion on Kennedy Drive and the other interchanges along the Pacific Motorway.  There have been a number of studies undertaken by TfNSW over that time investigating various options and configurations for the M1 and the respective interchanges, river crossings and service roads.  More recently, TfNSW commenced a strategic planning process for the M1 south of the Queensland Border.

A joint traffic modelling project between Council and TfNSW (and funded by TfNSW) commenced in 2025 to investigate short, medium and long term upgrades for the existing double-roundabout on Kennedy Drive, which need to be compatible with future upgrades for the Pacific Motorway and the Terranora Creek bridge.  It is also considering the interaction of the Kennedy Drive interchange with a future extension of Kirkwood Road to the Motorway, consistent with the Tweed Road Development Strategy.  Councillors and community will be updated as the preferred options are developed and costed, in the first half of 2026.  Some of the options may include short-term improvements to the existing Kennedy Drive configuration, however any more substantial works (for instance alteration of ramps or structures) would be determined, funded and delivered by TfNSW.

The urgency of these works and need for collaboration were discussed with Minister for Regional Transport, Jenny Aitkinson, at Community Cabinet in mid 2025; as Council is unable to unilaterally undertake works in the area without state government coordination, designs and funding.

As a short term measure, Council has recently trimmed vegetation in the centre of the twin roundabouts and adjacent to the bridge abutments to improve visibility of turn movements for safety and to reduce delays.  Additional traffic counts and observations of turning movements have also been conducted to inform the modelling project.

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Acknowledges community concern regarding abandoned shopping trolleys across the Tweed Shire and the associated visual, safety and accessibility impacts within public spaces.

  2. Notes that under the Public Spaces (Unattended Property) Act 2021 (NSW), shopping trolleys are classified as shared service items and remain the responsibility of the owning supermarkets and operators, including their obligation to retrieve trolleys within the legislated timeframe once notified.

  3. Recognises that Council currently provides information to the community on how to report abandoned shopping trolleys, including referrals to Trolley Tracker and other retailer-operated retrieval systems and promotes this through Council's social media channels. 

  4. Acknowledges the consultation undertaken by Council officers since 2023 with all identified (trolley) shared service operators in the Tweed Heads area, particularly the Centre Manager for Tweed Mall and associated supermarkets, to improve responsiveness to shopping trolleys left unattended in public spaces.

  5. Acknowledges that Council implemented an impounding program following this consultation, but that ongoing impounding activities have been limited due to State-level changes to the Public Spaces (Unattended Property) Act 2021 (NSW).

  6. Notes the corresponding and significant reduction in Customer Service Requests relating to abandoned shopping trolleys over the past 12 months.

  7. Acknowledges that the Office of Local Government has completed a review of the Public Spaces (Unattended Property) Act 2021 (NSW), to which Tweed Shire Council has contributed.

  8. Requests that the General Manager write to the Office of Local Government seeking the expedited release of the review outcomes and any proposed legislative amendments that would better empower councils to implement a practical and sustainable approach to the impounding of, and issuing of fines for, abandoned shopping trolleys.

  9. Ensures that the letter referenced in point 8: - refers to the Notice of Motion resolution.

  10. Ensures that all Councillors are provided with a copy of the outgoing correspondence referenced in point 9, as well as any response received.
 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr James Owen

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Acknowledges the establishment of the NSW Women’s Safety Commissioner and Office of the Women’s Safety Commissioner and recognises this initiative as a state-level leadership and oversight mechanism to strengthen responses to domestic, family and sexual violence across NSW.

  2. Acknowledges the establishment by the NSW Women’s Safety Commissioner of the NSW Domestic, Family and Sexual Violence Lived Experience Advisory Group to provide strategic advice to the NSW Government from people with lived experience of domestic, family and sexual violence.

  3. Recognises that the Advisory Group is designed to amplify diverse victim-survivor voices and to ensure lived experience perspectives help shape government policy and programs aimed at improving responses to domestic, family and sexual violence across NSW.

  4. Recognises the importance of victim-survivor informed policy development in strengthening domestic, family and sexual violence prevention, response and support frameworks throughout NSW.

  5. Notes that the NSW Women’s Safety Commissioner Strategic Plan 2024–2027 - Working together to address domestic, family and sexual violence - provides a coordinated strategic framework focused on six priority areas including centring lived experience, enhancing oversight and accountability, promoting safe response systems, supporting primary prevention efforts, strengthening workforce capacity, and improving economic safety for women.

  6. Recognises the Commissioner’s role in amplifying the voices of people with lived experience of domestic, family and sexual violence to inform policy and program design, and in fostering collaboration across government, non-government sectors and community stakeholders to achieve improved safety outcomes.

  7. Notes that the Strategic Plan reinforces the centrality of evidence-informed policy and cross-sector engagement across specialist and mainstream services to support victim-survivors and address systemic barriers to safety.

  8. Supports the principles of the Strategic Plan, including its emphasis on integrated and accessible responses to violence, accountability for delivery of the NSW Domestic and Family Violence Plan 2022-27 and NSW Sexual Violence Plan 2022-27, and commitment to long-term cultural change.

  9. Requests the General Manager write to the NSW Women’s Safety Commissioner expressing Council’s support for the objectives of the Strategic Plan and the Lived Experience Advisory Group, seeking information on how local government and community stakeholders can engage with and benefit from the Commissioner’s work, strategic priorities and the outcomes of the Advisory Group, and identifying opportunities for Council to provide practical support and contribute to the delivery of these initiatives at a local level.

  10. Ensure that the letter referenced in point 9: - refers to the Notice of Motion resolution

  11. Ensures that all Councillors are provided with a copy of the outgoing correspondence referenced in point 9, as well as any response received. 
 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Tay Lee from the Tweed Valley Uniting Church


God of love and wisdom,
We give you thanks for the Tweed Shire - for its beauty, its rich diversity, and for all who live, work, and belong in this place.
We gather today mindful of your wisdom in Proverbs 3:5–6:
“Trust in the Lord with all your heart,
and do not depend on your own understanding.
In all your ways acknowledge him,
and he will make your paths straight.”
As this Council meets, we seek your guidance and insight.
Grant us wisdom, and lead us in the right paths.
 
Bless our Mayor with steady leadership, clarity of thought, and a spirit of unity.
Equip each Councillor with patience, integrity, and a genuine desire to serve the well-being of the whole community.
We also pray for all Council staff — may their work be marked by cooperation, fairness, and mutual respect.
 
As we journey through the season of Lent and approach Easter, we ask for your protection over our community.
Watch over all who live in this Shire, as well as those who are visiting or travelling through.
Keep our roads, beaches, waterways, and public spaces safe.
May all enjoy this Easter season with peace, joy, and a sense of renewal and say, "It is a happy Easter."
May this be a time of rest, reconnection, and shared life for all.
 
Lord, help us to listen with understanding, work together with purpose, and build a future where this community continues to grow and flourish.
We place this meeting, this Council, and this Shire into your faithful and loving care.
In Jesus’ name we pray.

Amen.

Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Receives the Minutes of the Local Traffic Committee Meeting held Thursday 5 February 2026 and

  2. Adopts the Executive Leadership Team's recommendations as follows:

6.1  McAuleys Road, North Tumbulgum
That the proposed temporary road closures for a filming sequence in North Tumbulgum, in two (2) nominated sites on McAuleys Road and one (1) nominated site on Terranora Road, for one day of filming between 13 February 2026 and 27 February 2026 be supported subject to: 
  1. NSW Police approval being obtained.
  2. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
  3. The Event organisers ensure that queue lengths on Riverside Drive do not extend to Tweed Valley Way.
  4. Affected residents and businesses are to be notified via letterbox drop to include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or expected interruptions, and event organiser contact details. Sufficient time is to be allowed for any identified issues to be addressed.
  5. The event organiser notifies Tweed Community of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or expected interruptions, and event organiser contact details.
  6. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
  7. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
  8. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
  9. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
  10. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
  11. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
  12. The application of all signs and devices necessary to affect the changed traffic management conditions and temporary road closures for the events, also being approved as part of the event approval.

7.1.    Tweed Coast Road, Pottsville - prohibitive parking
That the request for prohibitive parking on Tweed Coast Road, Pottsville be supported and "No Stopping" signage installed, to provide better access for pedestrians between Mooball Creek Bridge and Pottsville Beach, are endorsed.

7.2.    Solander Street, Tweed Heads
That the proposed temporary road closures near the former Tweed Hospital at Solander Street, Tweed Heads, for approximately 6 hours of filming during the period of 24 February 2026 - 26 February 2026 be supported subject to: 
  1. NSW Police approval being obtained.
  2. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
  3. Affected residents and businesses are to be notified via letterbox drop to include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or expected interruptions, and event organiser contact details. Sufficient time is to be allowed for any identified issues to be addressed.
  4. The event organiser notifies Tweed Community of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or expected interruptions, and event organiser contact details.
  5. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
  6. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
  7. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
  8. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
  9. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
  10. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
  11. The application of all signs and devices necessary to affect the changed traffic management conditions and temporary road closures for the events, also being approved as part of the event approval.

7.3.    Buchan Avenue, Tweed Heads 
In relation to Buchan Avenue, Tweed Heads, to improve compliance with the existing No Parking signs, 2 additional signs be installed.

7.4.    Tweed Coast Road, Pottsville - sight distance improvements
To improve sight distance when exiting the TriCare facility on Tweed Coast Road, Hastings Point, a 'yellow No Stopping line' be installed on the approach and departure side of the driveway for approximately 6 metres.

7.5.    Kingscliff Triathlon, 22 November 2026
That the proposed Kingscliff Triathlon on 22 November 2026 be supported, subject to: 
  1. NSW Police approval being obtained.
  2. Endorsement of the event by Triathlon NSW.
  3. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks before the event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
  4. Affected residents and businesses are to be notified via letterbox drop to include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or expected interruptions, and event organiser contact details. Sufficient time is to be allowed for any identified issues to be addressed.
  5. The event organiser notifies Tweed Community of the impact of their event by advertising in the Tweed Link at their expense a minimum of one week prior to the operational impacts taking effect. The advertising must include the event name, specifics of any traffic impacts or expected interruptions, and event organiser contact details.
  6. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
  7. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
  8. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
  9. Arrangements made for private property access and egress affected by the event.
  10. That the applicant visit www.whatsontweed.com.au and check if your event is listed.  The What’s On Tweed website automatically populates event listings from a range of sources.  If your event is not listed, create an account and submit your event directly to the website for approval.
  11. The submission and approval of a Community Event application/Major Event application and compliance with any conditions imposed therein.
  12. The event be conducted and signposted (where applicable this supersedes signposting in accordance with Transport for NSW Guide to Traffic Control at Worksites) in accordance with the current Transport for NSW Guidelines for Bicycle Road Races to ensure consistency across the network.
  13. A report be provided to Council, by the event organiser, within 2 weeks of conduct of the event, showing compliance with the above conditions.
  14. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
  15. The application of all signs and devices necessary to effect the changed traffic management conditions and temporary road closures for the events, also being approved as part of the event approval.

7.6.    2026 Gold Coast Pro surfing event
Subject to the submission of a Road Closure application the temporary closure of Coral Street, Tweed Heads for the Gold Coast Pro 2026 event is supported. The application is to be submitted at least 4 weeks prior to the event.

 The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Cr Chris Cherry declared a Non-Significant, Non-Pecuniary Interest in Item 14.3 Future Use of Former Temporary Housing Area - Tweed Holiday Parks Pottsville North.  The nature of the interest is that Cr Cherry's family owns and operates a holiday park which may be perceived to be in direct competition with the  caravan park that contains the land proposed for temporary housing and a decision to pursue transitional housing at this location may be perceived to impact on that caravan parks financial interests   Cr Cherry will manage the Interest by remaining in the Chamber for discussion and voting on the merits of the item.


Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)
Cr Meredith Dennis

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Notes the significant environmental, planning, operational, financial and Crown Land governance constraints that limit the suitability of the site for transitional accommodation.

  2. Does not proceed with the use of Tweed Holiday Parks Pottsville North for transitional accommodation for low to very low‑income earners.

  3. Advocates that transitional accommodation needs within the Tweed Shire be addressed through State-led solutions on appropriately zoned and serviced land, rather than through repurposing Tweed Holiday Parks Pottsville North.

  4. Notes that the site has historically operated as a caravan and camping facility prior to 2022, forming part of the Tweed Holiday Parks network and providing a long‑standing and reliable revenue stream for Council.

  5. Proceeds with reinstatement and redevelopment of the northern section of Tweed Holiday Parks Pottsville North in accordance with Council’s resolution of 18 July 2024 endorsing the Tweed Holiday Parks 2023–2034 Strategic Plan.

  6. Requests that NSW Government agencies complete all necessary remediation and negotiations to facilitate hand‑back of the site, enabling Council to progress with the approved and strategically endorsed redevelopment works.

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - None

Councillor Brinsmead asks could you please provide an update on any progress made in relation to a proposed skatepark in Kingscliff, including current status, next steps and anticipated timeframes, if available? 

The Youth Outdoor Recreation Action Plan adopted by Council, includes an action to develop a master plan and deliver a district level skate park in Kingscliff. The Walter Peate Sports Complex has been identified as the preferred location, subject to required approvals and land tenure arrangements. This project is listed as a Priority 1 action (to be progressed within 1–4 years).
 
Council has allocated $50,000 in the draft 2026/27 budget to commence master planning for the proposed facility. This funding will support early investigations and concept development only. At this stage, construction of the skate park is not funded. The planning process will also consider how a future skate facility will integrate with car parking needs for the adjacent sports fields and the broader active recreation precinct.
Proposed next steps include:
 
  1. Undertaking a detailed site assessment, including existing services, environmental constraints and suitability for skate infrastructure.
  2. Engaging with the Tweed Byron Aboriginal Land Council.
  3. Consulting with Cudgen Leagues Club to discuss land interfaces, access, use opportunities and any potential impacts.
  4. Completing a full site survey, including boundaries, drainage and geotechnical conditions.
  5. Conducting community engagement to identify preferred skate elements and facility style, consistent with Council’s adopted Youth Outdoor Recreation Action Plan.
  6. Preparing concept design options that consider skate elements, circulation, toilet access, shade, seating, lighting and other supporting infrastructure.
  7. Assessing car parking requirements, and
  8. Developing a cost estimate and funding strategy.
