[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks can we please receive a detailed overview of the street sweeping operations currently undertaken across the Tweed Shire, including where and when street sweeping is conducted and the frequency of those operations?

The Director Engineering replied:

"Through you Madam Mayor,

Council operates one street sweeper and one footpath sweeper - both out of our Tweed Depot. Both operate based on a fortnightly rotation through CBD and industrial areas, as well as reactive cleaning operations as required. Areas covered include Tweed Heads, Tweed Head Industrial Area, Murwillumbah, Murwillumbah Industrial Area, Kingscliff, Casuarina, Cabarita, and Pottsville. To minimise conflicts with parked cars, pedestrians and business owners such as cafes, the sweepers operate on an early morning shift, commencing at 3am.

Sweeping operations through the 25/26 financial year were interrupted due to operator availability. Measures were taken to replace normal activities with replacement Council or labour hire operators, additional day shifts, and use of contracted plant. However, these measures proved not to be wholly effective, and consistency of implementation was impacted - mainly due to the unusual shift times.

Staffing issues levels have recently returned to more normal operational capacity which has resulted in a noticeable increase in cleaning and maintenance around our CBDs. This has also coincided with the addition of the CBD Crew and some grant funded uplift programs already underway."

"Through you Madam Mayor,

During the 2024–25 financial year, Council received 693 customer service requests through Snap Send Solve and 4,288 through Council's Report a Problem platform. In the 2025-26 financial year, Council received 702 Snap Send Solve requests and 4,279 Report a Problem requests.

Overall, Council has not seen any notable increase in the use of either platform, with Report a Problem continuing to be the community's and council’s preferred digital reporting channel. 

Council's reasons for not adopting Snap Send Solve as its primary reporting platform remain largely unchanged from those previously reported to Council. Council's existing Report a Problem platform is integrated with broader customer service processes and supports a wider range of services. 

Given the relatively low volume of reports received through Snap Send Solve and the additional costs and system impacts associated with a transition, Council's current Report a Problem platform continues to represent the most suitable solution for managing customer requests and its use should be encouraged to ensure timely responses and integrated workflow."

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks what are Council's reasons for not adopting Snap Send Solve as its primary platform for customer service requests, and what would be the estimated cost and implications of transitioning from Council's current Report a Problem platform to Snap Send Solve?

The Director Corporate Services replied:
"Through you Madam Mayor,

Council previously responded to a similar question at the Council Meeting of 18 July 2024, and I would refer Council to the Minutes of that meeting for a more detailed response.  

In summary that response detailed that Council had previously considered the use of a dedicated Snap Send Solve enterprise arrangement, however this would involve additional licensing and implementation costs while largely duplicating functionality already available through Council's existing systems. Based on previous discussions, the cost of an enterprise licence was estimated at approximately $30,000 to $60,000 per year, plus implementation costs. While these figures may have changed, Council has not received updated pricing information. It is not considered efficient to implement systems that duplicate our existing solution and do not integrate with our systems.  

To note whilst Council's primary customer request platform is its online Report a Problem service, which forms part of Council's broader customer service system and supports a wider range of Council services and requests than that available on Snap, Send Solve, Council still receives and actions reports submitted via the Snap Send Solve application.,  

Council continues to review customer service technologies and invest in the upgrade of its enterprise software as part of ongoing improvements to its service request management and digital service delivery platforms."

The meeting commenced at 11.00 am.

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Reverend Mandy Larkin from the Anglican Parish of Murwillumbah.


I invite you to join with me as we pray or to take a moment for reflection.

Loving Father,
We bring our prayers to you for our local community and its varied needs.  We pray for those who live and work here in the Tweed Shire, for any who are struggling at this time, for all who are seeking work but have not yet found it, for those who live in poverty or on the streets alone.

We bring our prayers to you for our Tweed Shire Council as it meets today.  We pray for your guidance and wisdom to be with each person here, that in their deliberations and decisions, may they seek the common good for this community, that all who live and work here would be led towards a future of greater equality, prosperity and unity.

We give your thanks for our mayor and councillors and their willingness to step forward into leadership in our community.   Strengthen them with grace, patience and good will and grant them the wisdom and discernment they need to carry out their roles to the best of their abilities, as they make crucial decision about our shared future.

We ask all these things through Jesus Christ our Lord.   Amen.

Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)


RESOLVED that Council notes the Minutes of the Local Transport Forum Meeting held Tuesday 30 June 2026. Items endorsed by the Executive Leadership Team are: 

OPTIONAL ITEMS

5.1.    Hillcrest Avenue, Tweed Heads South
That the extension of double unbroken centreline markings on Hillcrest Avenue, Tweed Heads South, is not supported, as the available sight distance is considered adequate and does not justify installation. Where parking occurs adjacent to existing double centrelines and the minimum 3 metre clearance is not met, community may report any suspected non-compliance through Council’s “Report a Problem” portal.

5.2.    Thomson Street, Tweed Heads
The installation of time limited signage or prohibitive parking signage on Thomson Street, Tweed Heads is not supported, as the reported issues are not parking demand or safety related. Residents are encouraged to report anti-social behaviour to NSW Police who can then consider whether there are grounds to move people on from the area. Council Rangers are to continue to address unattended vehicles. 

5.3.    Ballymore Court, Banora Point
That Council staff conduct the onsite meeting with Bupa representatives and local residents to further discuss parking behaviours. Should no additional risks or measures be identified, Council will proceed with the implementation of a 'No stopping' yellow line within the south side of the axe handle turnaround area on Ballymore Court, to enable heavy vehicles to turn around and leave the road in a forward direction.

5.4.    Tweed Valley Triathletes 2026 - 2027
That the proposed Tweed Valley Triathletes Season commencing Saturday 19 September 2026 and concluding Saturday 21 March 2027 be supported, subject to the following conditions: 
  1. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser. 
  2. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event. 
  3. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
5.5.    Terranora Road, Terranora
To encourage parents to use the appropriate on-site parking facilities and to improve sight distance when exiting the driveway, an additional 10 metre 'No stopping restriction 8am - 9:30am and 2:30pm - 4pm' be installed west of the proposed driveway at 647 Terranora Road, Terranora.
  
5.6.    Kingscliff Lane, Kingscliff
That 6 metres of yellow ‘No Stopping’ line marking be installed on both sides of all ingress and egress intersections along Kingscliff Lane, Kingscliff at Pacific Street, Zephyr Street, Beach Street and Pearl Street, focusing on these higher-risk southern intersections. The effectiveness of these measures will be monitored following installation, with the northern intersections be reviewed based on observed outcomes. Consideration may also be given to additional regulatory signage or line marking, such as ‘Give Way’ controls, if warranted.

5.7.    Charles Street, Tweed Heads
To support vehicles exiting the laneway off Charles Street,Tweed Heads West, sight distance can be improved by: 
  • Installing 10 metres of double unbroken centre line marking on both approaches to the laneway on Charles Street.
  • Installing a continuity edge line across the laneway on Charles Street.
  • Undertaking vegetation trimming on the laneway median to improve visibility.
5.8.    Tour de Cure Charity Ride
That the proposed Tour de Cure ride through Tweed Shire Council on Sunday 13 and Monday 14 September 2026 be supported, subject to: 
  1. NSW Police approval being obtained.
  2. Riders obey NSW Road Rules. 
  3. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
  4. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser and a current certificate provided to Council at least two weeks prior to the event.
  5. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
  6. Consultation with emergency services and any identified issues addressed.
  7. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
  8. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
5.9.    Twin Towns Triathlon 2026 - 2027
That the proposed Twin Towns Triathlon Club scheduled events beginning 26 September 2026 concluding 27 March 2027 be supported, subject to the following conditions:
  1. Adequate public liability insurance being held by the event organiser.
  2. All signage erected for the event to not cause a hazard for motorists or pedestrians and be removed immediately following the completion of the event.
  3. The event organiser is to ensure that any proposed roads or pathways used for the event have been assessed and are fit for purpose.
  4. Conformance with a Traffic Management Plan and associated Traffic Control Plans (submitted to Council at least 2 weeks prior to the racing event) implemented and controlled by Transport for NSW accredited persons.
  5. NSW Police approval being obtained for the race event.

The Motion was Carried

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  None

RESOLVED that Council submits the following motions to the 2026 Local Government NSW (LGNSW) Annual Conference:

Motion 1 - Gambling

That LGNSW advocates to the NSW Government for additional poker machine harm reduction reforms, including:
  1. A statewide shutdown period for poker machines between midnight and 10am as it is known to be the period of greatest gambling harm. 
  2. An independently managed statewide self-exclusion register covering all venues with poker machines; and
  3. Publication of venue level poker machine data, including machine numbers and losses, to improve transparency and support local harm prevention responses.

Background
Poker machine gambling continues to cause significant harm across New South Wales communities causing financial stress, negative relationship and mental health impacts and increased demand on local community services. NSW residents lost $2.37 billion on poker machines in the first three months of 2026, an increase of 9.4 per cent compared with the same quarter in 2025, equivalent to approximately $26.4 million per day or $1.1 million per hour. 

Poker machine losses are a statewide issue affecting metropolitan, regional and rural communities. Local governments are often required to respond to the social consequences of gambling harm despite having limited direct regulatory powers over poker machine numbers, density and operating conditions. Tweed Shire poker machine players lost $33,000,000 over the first quarter of 2026 highlighting the local impact of gambling harm on individuals, families and the broader community. Tweed Shire Council has previously passed a motion recognising gambling harm, supporting stronger gambling reform and noting Wesley Mission’s Put Pokies in Their Place campaign.  

Motion 2 - Water Quality NSW

That LGNSW advocate to the NSW and Australian Governments to:
  1. Re-establish a coordinated catchment management framework in NSW, with clear responsibility for improving river health and water quality.
  2. Provide increased and ongoing funding to local government for riparian restoration, riverbank stabilisation, soil health improvement and catchment rehabilitation projects.
  3. Recognise that water quality and aquatic ecosystem improvement requires long-term investment and support funding programs that operate over decades rather than short-term grant cycles.
  4. Strengthen policy settings and incentives to guide and support landholders in protecting waterways and establishing effective vegetated riparian buffers.
  5. Reduce barriers to accessing State and Federal grants, including matching-funding and onerous reporting requirements that limit the scale of local government projects.
  6. Support partnerships between local government, landholders, industry and government agencies to deliver catchment-scale improvements in water quality and ecosystem health.


Motion 3

That LGNSW advocate to the NSW Government to investigate and address barriers preventing approved residential development from progressing to construction and occupation, including:

a) infrastructure funding constraints;
b) escalating construction costs and financing challenges;
c) delays associated with post-consent approvals and management plan requirements;
d) workforce shortages;
e) State agency approval processes; and
f) circumstances where approved development is unreasonably delayed without genuine delivery impediments (land banking).

Background 

NSW housing policy has largely focused on increasing planning approvals. However, a significant proportion of approved housing has not progressed to construction.

Tweed Shire Council's experience demonstrates that approval is often only the first step in delivering housing.
For example, the Kings Forest State Significant Development Concept Plan and Project Application were approved more than ten years before the first residential lots were released in January 2026. During that period, substantial post-approval obligations were required, including environmental management plans, infrastructure delivery, biodiversity works, water and sewer servicing, road construction and compliance with numerous approval conditions.

The cost of delivering the first lot release exceeded tens of millions of dollars before any development revenue could be realised. Such infrastructure is generally forward funded by the developer and is highly sensitive to market conditions, financing costs and construction cost escalation.

Regional councils are also experiencing increasing infrastructure constraints, particularly relating to water, sewer and transport infrastructure capacity. In many areas, these constraints can limit housing delivery regardless of the existence of planning approvals.
While genuine land banking may occur in some circumstances, a considerable proportion of delayed housing supply reflects broader economic, infrastructure and regulatory barriers rather than a deliberate decision not to develop.
Accordingly, reforms should focus on removing impediments to housing delivery and improving infrastructure funding arrangements while distinguishing these situations from speculative land banking. 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  None

ALTERNATE MOTION

Cr James Owen
Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
 
PROPOSED that Council:

  1. Receives the outcomes of the Tweed Indoor Sports and Aquatic Centre Analysis and Feasibility Study (the Study) noting the demonstrated and urgent shortfall in indoor sporting courts across the Tweed Local Government Area (LGA), and that existing aquatic facilities are not fit for purpose to meet the community's current and future needs.

  2. Adopts the integrated delivery approach for an indoor sports and aquatic centre at Recreation Park, Tweed Heads.

  3. Commences the next phase of work, including preparation of a detailed business case and concept design for a Council owned indoor sports and aquatic centre at Recreation Park, Tweed Heads. This is to include investigation of staged construction, funding opportunities (including State and Federal funding and other partnership contributions), and specialist operating models to improve affordability and deliverability, alongside consideration of asset rationalisation as new aquatic infrastructure is introduced. 

  4. Endorses the engagement of a legal service provider to prepare a Probity Advisory Plan and provide probity advice as per the requirements of Office of Local Government’s Public Private Partnerships Guidelines for significant capital works projects.

  5. Receives a further report on completion of the detailed business case and concept design to determine whether to proceed with the project.

AMENDMENT

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)
Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Receives the outcomes of the Tweed Indoor Sports and Aquatic Centre Analysis and Feasibility Study (the Study) noting the recommendation to construct the Indoor sports facility first to address the demonstrated and urgent shortfall in indoor sporting courts across the Tweed Local Government Area (LGA).

  2. Adopts a staged delivery approach, whereby:
    1. Council notes that the Study identifies an integrated indoor sports and aquatic centre at Recreation Park, Tweed Heads as the preferred long-term configuration for a co-located regional facility, and 
    2. Prioritises delivery of an indoor sports centre at Recreation Park, Tweed Heads, with the aquatic centre to be progressed as capacity and funding allow.

  3. Commences the next phase of work, including preparation of a detailed business case and concept design for a Council owned indoor sports centre at Recreation Park, Tweed Heads. This is to include investigation of staged construction, funding opportunities (including State and Federal funding and other partnership contributions), and specialist operating models to improve affordability and deliverability.

  4. Notes views expressed in the Project Reference Group that the aquatic centre could be grant funded and operated by a third-party at profit.  In order to achieve an aquatic centre as soon as possible for the Tweed community Council authorises the General Manager to undertake an Expression of Interest (EOI) process to identify suitably qualified private sector proponents interested in funding, delivering, operating and maintaining an aquatic centre within the Tweed LGA.

  5. Notes that the EOI process may include consideration of alternative delivery models, including Council leasing suitable land to a third-party operator at a nominal (peppercorn) rate, with the operator responsible for securing project funding, detailed design, construction, operation and ongoing maintenance of the aquatic centre.

  6. Receives a further report on the outcomes of the EOI process and any proposed delivery model prior to making a commitment to the project or entering into any binding agreement.

  7. Continues strategic planning and high-level feasibility investigations for a future aquatic facility as part of a broader aquatic facility network strategic plan, incorporating asset rationalisation as new aquatic infrastructure is introduced.

  8. Endorses the engagement of a legal service provider to prepare a Probity Advisory Plan and provide probity advice as per the requirements of Office of Local Government’s Public Private Partnerships Guidelines for significant capital works projects.

The Amendment was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  None

The Amendment on becoming the Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone, Cr James Owen

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead returned to the meeting at 04:57pm.

Cr James Owen
Cr Kimberly Hone

RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Notes that a meeting between Council staff, Councillors and Transport for NSW was held on 23 July 2026, at which TfNSW advised that the maintenance budget for the road network, including the M1, has not increased in line with the significant growth in workload.

  2. Notes the ongoing and increasing volume of community correspondence received by Councillors regarding the maintenance and presentation of M1 on- and off-ramps within Tweed Shire.

  3. Notes that this funding shortfall is not unique to Tweed Shire, and reflects a broader pattern in which population and traffic growth across regional New South Wales has consistently outpaced growth in state infrastructure funding.

  4. Request the Mayor to write to the Member for Tweed, the Minister for the North Coast, the Minister for Roads and the Minister for Transport, requesting an increase in the maintenance budget allocated to motorway infrastructure within Tweed Shire, commensurate with the growth in workload and population identified by TfNSW.
 

The Motion was Carried

VOTE AGAINST - Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor)

Councillor Owen asks, please advise the current budgeted (establishment) number of Ranger positions, the number of those positions currently filled, and the average length of service and turnover rate for Rangers over each of the past three financial years.
 
I can advise that the current Ranger establishment comprises 11 positions, consisting of a Team Leader, Ranger Operations Officer, 1 Ranger – Natural Areas, 5 Rangers and 3 Field Rangers, noting that one Field Ranger position is a temporary 12-month budget-funded position. At present there are 2 Field Ranger positions vacant.
 
In relation to workforce tenure and turnover, the average length of service and turnover rate for Rangers over the past three financial years is as follows
  • In 2023-24, the average length of service was 3.49 years, with a turnover rate of 31.58 per cent
  • In 2024-25, the average length of service was 5.54 years, with a turnover rate of 35.29 per cent
  • In 2025-26, the average length of service was 4.33 years, with a turnover rate of 53.33 per cent
 
These figures are based on those staff who perform ranger duties only and do not include periods of service staff may have completed in other Council roles prior to joining the unit. 
 
It is also worth noting that Ranger roles involve regular interactions with members of the public in compliance and enforcement situations, including occasions where staff are required to deal with unreasonable, aggressive or challenging behaviour. [IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks can Council identify any locations within the Tweed Shire that may be suitable for the establishment of an ocean pool, and advise what process would be required to investigate and ultimately establish such a facility?
 
At a preliminary level, Jack Evans Boat Harbour appears to be the most suitable location within the Tweed Shire for further investigation as a potential ocean pool site, given its existing recreational use, public amenities, accessibility and relative protection from ocean swell.
 
However, Council has not undertaken a detailed assessment of site suitability, and further work would be required to determine environmental, engineering, operational and financial feasibility. Other coastal locations may also warrant consideration as part of that assessment process.
 
Should Council wish to pursue the concept, the appropriate first step would be to assess the resource requirements, costs and organisational impacts associated with undertaking a detailed investigation, including consideration of consultant studies, staff resources and project priorities.
 
Subject to that assessment and allocation of resources, the next step would be a feasibility study to examine community demand, alternative sites, environmental impacts, engineering requirements, costs, operational considerations, concept design, community consultation and regulatory approval pathways.
 
Any proposal found to be feasible would then require detailed design, funding and construction before an ocean pool could be established.","isPublic":false,"isPublished":false,"isCurrentItem":false,"meeting":null,"reports":[{"id":27386,"name":"Question With Notice","isUploaded":0,"reportTemplateId":18,"wordTemplateId":8,"pdfMediaFullPath":"stream/TWEED/tmp_606db2336f.pdf","token":"266b2815-fa98-457f-a6e6-4a87441638ef","isPublic":false}],"attachments":[],"actionSheets":[],"bookmarks":[{"id":3735,"name":"31","eventId":1841,"title":"QWN - Cr Brinsmead - Tweed Shire Ocean Pool","text":"QWN - Cr Brinsmead - Tweed Shire Ocean Pool","startTime":22196,"duration":null,"itemId":32278,"sortOrder":32,"minutesSortOrder":32,"parentId":-1,"additionalParentId":-1}],"minutes":[]},{"id":32283,"name":"QWN - Cr Brinsmead - Murwillumbah Multi-Level Car Park Protracted Works","parentId":30508,"sortOrder":84,"minutesSortOrder":67,"minutesParentId":30508,"outlineNumber":"5","fullOutlineNumber":"21.5.","htmlContent":"

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks can you please provide an update on the ongoing and protracted works associated with the reopening of the Murwillumbah Multi-Level Car Park, noting that the community has been inconvenienced since December 2023? In particular, what works remain outstanding, what has caused the extended timeframe for completion, and what is the anticipated date for the full and final reopening the facility?
 
I can advise that the Occupation Certificate has now been received and the Murwillumbah Multi-Level Car Park has reopened to the public.
 
The only remaining works relate to three parking bays that remain temporarily unavailable while recently completed concrete repairs achieve the required curing strength. These bays are expected to be reopened within the next two weeks, at which point the facility will be fully operational.
 
The project took considerably longer than a typical building repair because it involved far more than repairing visible fire damage. Extensive engineering investigations were required to assess the impact of the fire on the structural integrity of the building, including detailed testing of concrete, structural steel, waterproofing systems and fire-affected areas. As investigations progressed, additional issues were identified that required further assessment and changes to the repair methodology. The works also needed to satisfy building certification requirements and be coordinated through a complex insurance process involving engineers, specialist consultants, certifiers, contractors, loss adjusters and the insurer.
 
Despite these challenges, the project has now reached practical completion and the community can once again use the facility. I acknowledge the patience of residents, businesses and visitors throughout this complex remediation process.","isPublic":false,"isPublished":false,"isCurrentItem":false,"meeting":null,"reports":[{"id":27397,"name":"Question With Notice","isUploaded":0,"reportTemplateId":18,"wordTemplateId":8,"pdfMediaFullPath":"stream/TWEED/tmp_7d2260f77b.pdf","token":"c30708b6-2677-44fc-9517-1dbe995a8e8c","isPublic":false}],"attachments":[],"actionSheets":[],"bookmarks":[{"id":3736,"name":"32","eventId":1841,"title":"QWN - Cr Brinsmead - Murwillumbah Multi-Level Car Park Protracted Works","text":"QWN - Cr Brinsmead - Murwillumbah Multi-Level Car Park Protracted Works","startTime":22301,"duration":null,"itemId":32283,"sortOrder":33,"minutesSortOrder":33,"parentId":-1,"additionalParentId":-1}],"minutes":[]},{"id":32284,"name":"PAN000019 Panel of Providers for Make Safe of Flood Damaged Building Assets","parentId":30503,"sortOrder":85,"minutesSortOrder":43,"minutesParentId":30503,"outlineNumber":"8","fullOutlineNumber":"16.8.","htmlContent":"

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks has there been any progress towards the establishment of a district skate facility at the Kingscliff Sports Complex (adjacent to Walter Peate Sports Field), as identified in the Youth Outdoor Recreation Action Plan 2025–2035? If so, what progress has been made? If not, why not?
 
I can advise that only limited progress has been made towards the establishment of a district skate facility at the Kingscliff Sports Complex. The project remains a Priority 1 action in the adopted Youth Outdoor Recreation Action Plan 2025–2035 and Council remains committed to its delivery.
 
Council was advised in March 2026 that funding would be allocated in the 2026/27 budget to commence master planning investigations, with the work scheduled to begin in the second half of the financial year. However, following the completion of the $15.5 million Community Assets Program, which funded 57 projects across the Tweed, Council undertook a review of the Parks and Active Communities program of works to ensure available resources were focused on projects with secured funding, strong alignment to emerging grant opportunities, and the greatest likelihood of delivery within established timeframes. As a result, a number of projects, including the Kingscliff skate facility, were rescheduled while funded and time-sensitive projects were progressed.
 
Council is currently progressing several major recreation and community infrastructure projects, including:
 
  • Jack Evans Boat Harbour improvements, including the recently funded tessellated stairs project
  • Depot Road Sports Fields Stage 1 delivery and funding applications for Stage 2
  • Greenway Drive Oval lighting upgrade
  • Norries Headland Car Park Review
  • Planning for the Indoor Sports and Aquatic Centre
  • Black Rocks Sports Field lighting (awaiting funding announcement)
  • Les Burger transformer upgrade
  • Kingscliff Men's Shed proposal (draft and adoption of Elrond Drive Plan of Management)
  • Knox Park Pond Investigations - stormwater function and environmental assessment
  • Pottsville High School partnership opportunities assessment: Sports fields and skate park planning, and
  • Community building leases and licence review 
 
These projects have been prioritised to maximise available external funding opportunities, leverage time-sensitive grant programs, and address ageing assets that are approaching the end of their service life.
 
Importantly, the Kingscliff Skate Park remains a priority project and work is continuing to support its future delivery. Delivery of this priority action is influenced by land tenure considerations at the preferred site, including an Aboriginal Land Claim and Native Title matters affecting the Crown land on which the facility is proposed. These factors create uncertainty around project timing and delivery and are being actively considered as part of Parks and Active Communities' program planning, project prioritisation and resource allocation processes.
 
Further, Council is currently engaging with the Department of Education regarding opportunities associated with the future Pottsville High School development, including the potential provision of sports fields and a skate facility. The timing and delivery of these recreation facilities are yet to be confirmed. As part of this process, the Parks and Active Communities unit will explore the benefits and feasibility of planning and designing the Pottsville and Kingscliff skatepark facilities concurrently to achieve efficiencies in design, procurement and community engagement. This approach may also provide opportunities to better understand community needs and emerging trends in skatepark design, while ensuring any future district-level skatepark in Kingscliff has a distinct identity, unique features and points of difference that complement the broader network of skate facilities across the Tweed.
 
Notwithstanding these challenges, Council remains committed to the project and intends to revisit the master planning process towards the end of the financial year as resources become available and greater certainty is achieved regarding the future use of the site, land tenure matters, and the provision of recreation facilities associated with the future Pottsville High School development.

RESOLVED that:

  1. The following tabled Petition be received and noted:

    Petition containing 83 signatures (of which 31 were valid and 52 were invalid due to incomplete information) and received 7 July 2026, entitled 'Make Big Polluters Pay Their Fair Share: Tweed Shire' advising as follows:

    "We support big coal, oil and gas corporations paying their fair share for the costs of climate change. Local councils and residents shouldn't be left holding the bill while corporations pocket the profits.

    We call on Tweed Shire to pass a Polluter Pays motion to support a Climate Compensation Fund which would help protect local services, strengthen and repair infrastructure and fund disaster response and preparedness - ensuring our community can stay safe and thrive.

    Council should formally call on the Australian Federal Government to: 

    - Establish a Climate Compensation Fund, paid for by a levy on major coal, oil and gas export corporations - not ratepayers and taxpayers;
    - Earmark funds for local councils to cover the rising costs of climate adaptation, disaster recovery and resilience; 
    - Provide sustained, legislated funding so councils can plan for the future with certainty; and 
    - Prioritise protecting ratepayers and taxpayers from bearing the escalating costs of climate damage."

  2.   ATTACHMENT 1 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:

Cr Kimberly Hone temporarily left the meeting at 12:24pm.

Cr Meredith Dennis
Cr Nola Firth

RESOLVED that:

  1. The following tabled Petition be received and noted, and considered in conjunction with item 15.3 on the agenda:

    Petition containing 424 signatures of which 354 were valid (with 68 being invalid due to incomplete details and 2 signatories being from outside of the shire), was received 5 August 2026, entitled 'Staged Delivery of Indoor Sports and Aquatic Facilities' advising as follows:

    "I support the development of both indoor sports and aquatic facilities for the Tweed community. However, I urge Council to 
    deliver these projects in stages. With no existing indoor sporting facilities in our region, delivering it first must be the top priority! Specifically, I support:
    Building the new indoor sports facility as the first priority.
    Keeping the aquatic centre as the next stage of the overall plan.
    Following the recommendations of the independent feasibility study and Council staff.
    Taking a practical approach that delivers benefits to the community sooner rather than later.
    In addition, the lack of indoor sporting facilities is having a direct impact on local clubs, schools, competitions and community participation. Delivering an indoor sports facility will help meet this immediate and growing need. I want to see both projects become a reality and believe that with a staged approach, Council can focus on getting the indoor sports facility built while continuing to plan for the future aquatic centre. Trying to deliver both major projects at the same time could create funding challenges, increased costs and delay progress on both facilities. Our community already has aquatic facilities, but currently has no indoor sports infrastructure. I urge Council to adopt a staged delivery model and make the indoor sports facility the immediate priority    "

  2.    ATTACHMENT 1 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains:
       (e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

     

 The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - None
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE -  Cr Kimberly Hone

Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor)


RESOLVED that Council:

  1. Welcomes the Federal Government’s recent announcement recognising the very real challenge of financial sustainability impacting the Local Government sector and committing to a meaningful, ongoing, annual increases in the level of Financial Assistance Grants;

  2. Welcomes the announcement of the intended Federation Compact with Local Government that commits to:
    1. Ongoing annual increases to Financial Assistance Grants to return them to historic levels;
    2. Ensure Roads to Recovery funding can be used to purchase plant and equipment to enable councils to carry out their own road maintenance with their own trained workers, to the extent possible;
    3. Support and increase the availability of apprenticeships in local government, as well as other employment programs in a local government context;
    4. Deliver new capabilities to improve outcomes in housing, planning, emergency management and aged care; and
    5. Ensure the Government publishes an annual summary of funding for Local Government.

  3. Commits the Mayor to write to the Prime Minister and Local Government Minister Catherine King welcoming their commitment to address the crisis in local government financial sustainability and urging them to work with the local government sector to urgently progress the Federation Compact with Local Government. 
 

The Motion was Carried 

VOTE FOR - Cr Chris Cherry (Mayor), Cr Reece Byrnes (Deputy Mayor), Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth, Cr James Owen
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Kimberly Hone

RESOLVED Councillor Owen, Councillor Brinsmead and Councillor Hone move that the Decision of Council at the 20 August 2026 Council Meeting for Item 15.3: Tweed Regional Indoor Sports and Aquatic Centre - Analysis and Feasibility Study Report be altered to:

that Council:

  1. Receives the outcomes of the Tweed Indoor Sports and Aquatic Centre Analysis and Feasibility Study (the Study) noting the demonstrated and urgent shortfall in indoor sporting courts across the Tweed Local Government Area (LGA), and that existing aquatic facilities are not fit for purpose to meet the community's current and future needs.

  2. Adopts the integrated delivery approach for an indoor sports and aquatic centre at Recreation Park, Tweed Heads.

  3. Commences the next phase of work, including preparation of a detailed business case and concept design for a Council owned indoor sports and aquatic centre at Recreation Park, Tweed Heads. This is to include investigation of staged construction, funding opportunities (including State and Federal funding and other partnership contributions), and specialist operating models to improve affordability and deliverability, alongside consideration of asset rationalisation as new aquatic infrastructure is introduced. 

  4. Endorses the engagement of a legal service provider to prepare a Probity Advisory Plan and provide probity advice as per the requirements of Office of Local Government’s Public Private Partnerships Guidelines for significant capital works projects.

  5. Receives a further report on completion of the detailed business case and concept design to determine whether to proceed with the project.
 

The Motion was Lost 

VOTE FOR - None

The meeting opened with a Prayer read by Senior Pastor Tara Jones from The Gathering, Tweed Heads.

​
Heavenly Father

We thank You for the privilege of gathering here today, and for the beautiful Tweed region that we are blessed to call home. Thank You for its people, its families, its communities, and the natural beauty that surrounds us.

Today, we lift up our Mayor, councillors, council staff, and every person carrying the responsibility of leadership in our region. We ask that You grant them wisdom, discernment, integrity, and courage as they consider the matters before them.

Help them to listen carefully, speak respectfully, and make decisions with compassion and understanding. May every discussion be guided by truth, and may every decision seek the wellbeing of our whole community—not only for today, but also for the generations who will come after us.

Give our leaders insight for the complex challenges facing our region. Help them to steward our finances, land, resources, and opportunities wisely. May they protect the vulnerable, strengthen families, support local businesses, and work toward a community where every person can flourish.

Where there are differences of opinion, give grace and humility. Where there is division, bring unity and mutual respect. Where there are difficult decisions, bring clarity and peace.

We also pray for the people of the Tweed. May our neighbourhoods be safe, our families strengthened, and our communities marked by generosity, compassion, and care for one another.

Let Your peace and protection rest upon this region. Bless the work of this council, and may all that is accomplished here ultimately serve the good of our community and bring honour to You.

In Jesus’ name

Amen.

AMENDMENT

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead
Cr Kimberly Hone

PROPOSED that Council:
 
  1. Approves an additional loan facility of $225,000 to Salt Surf Life Saving Club Inc. for the purpose of undertaking works and meeting obligations associated with Development Consent DA25/0243 PAN-535309.

  2. Requires the additional loan facility to be incorporated into a revised repayment schedule which:

    1. Maintains the Club's current monthly repayment commitment under the existing loan arrangements until the expiry of the current facility in 2031;

    2. Acknowledges that the original 10-year loan term has been extended by approximately three years through Council approved repayment deferrals as a result of deferrals associated with occupation certificate delays, COVID-19 assistance measures and subsequent repayment relief arrangements; and

    3. Commencing following the expiry of the current loan facility in 2031, requires repayment of the additional $225,000 loan advance over a period of not more than ten years, together with any additional repayments generated through the Club's proposed contribution of 25% of annual EBITDA, subject to verification through audited financial statements.
  1. Authorises the amendment or replacement of the existing Deed of Grant and associated loan documentation to incorporate the additional funding, revised repayment arrangements and reporting requirements.

  2. Requires Salt Surf Life Saving Club Inc. to continue providing annual audited financial statements to Council and to apply any project surplus funds toward repayment of the loan facility.

  3. Authorises the execution of all necessary documentation under the Common Seal of Council.
 
The Motion was Lost 

VOTE FOR - Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone
VOTE AGAINST - Cr Reece Byrnes (Mayor), Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor), Cr Chris Cherry, Cr Nola Firth
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr James Owen

Cr Chris Cherry
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that Council:
 
  1. Approves an additional loan facility of $225,000 to Salt Surf Life Saving Club Inc. for the purpose of undertaking works and meeting obligations associated with Development Consent DA25/0243 PAN-535309.

    1. Maintains the Club's current monthly repayment commitment under the existing loan arrangements until the expiry of the current facility in 2031;

    2. Acknowledges that the original 10-year loan term has been extended by approximately three years through Council approved repayment deferrals as a result of deferrals associated with occupation certificate delays, COVID-19 assistance measures and subsequent repayment relief arrangements; and

    3. Commencing following the expiry of the current loan facility in 2031, requires repayment of the additional $225,000 loan advance over a period of not more than ten years, together with any additional repayments generated through the Club's proposed contribution of 25% of annual EBITDA, subject to verification through audited financial statements.

The Acting General Manager advised that the Public Officer, Mathew Greenwood has been appointed as the Returning Officer for the election of Mayor and Deputy Mayor.

The Returning Officer advised that 2 nominations have been received for Mayor:
  1. Cr Reece Byrnes was nominated by Cr Chris Cherry and Cr Meredith Dennis and has accepted the nomination.
  2. Cr Kimberly Hone was nominated by Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead and Cr Kimberly Hone and has accepted the nomination

The order of the voting was determined as:

Vote 1: Cr Kimberly Hone
Vote 2: Cr Reece Byrnes

The result of the ordinary ballot by way of open voting (show of hands) was as follows:

Voting for Cr Kimberly Hone
FOR VOTE: Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead, Cr Kimberly Hone

Voting for Cr Reece Byrnes
FOR VOTE: Cr Reece Byrnes, Cr Chris Cherry, Cr Meredith Dennis, Cr Nola Firth

The Returning Officer declared that Councillor Reece Byrnes is elected as Mayor until the next election to be held in September 2028.

The Returning Officer advised that one nomination has been received for Deputy Mayor:
  1. Cr Meredith Dennis was nominated by Cr Chris Cherry and Cr Nola Firth and has accepted the nomination.

The Returning Officer declared that, as there was only one nominee for the role of Deputy Mayor, Cr Meredith Dennis is elected as Deputy Mayor of Tweed Shire Council for a one-year term ending at the Ordinary Council meeting in September 2027.

The Returning Officer declared the following Councillors elected:

  1. Mayor for the period ending September 2028 - Cr Reece Byrnes.

  2. Deputy Mayor for the period ending September 2027 - Cr Meredith Dennis.

Cr Chris Cherry

RESOLVED that Standing Orders be resumed.

Cr Chris Cherry declared a Non-Pecuniary, Non-Significant, interest in this Item. The nature of the interest is that Cr Chris Cherry's family owns a Holiday park in the Tweed Shire that could be considered to be a direct competitor of this proposed business as it is dominated by short term sites rather than residential sites.  Cr Chris Cherry will manage the Interest by vacating the Chamber for discussion and not voting on the item.

Cr Chris Cherry temporarily left the meeting at 11:47am.

Cr Nola Firth
Cr Meredith Dennis (Deputy Mayor)

RESOLVED that:

  1. Council in relation to Development Application DA26/0311 for a caravan park with associated water reticulation system and road and demolition at Lot 7 DP 1072659 & Lot 8 DP 1072659 No. 1024 Cudgera Creek Road, Lot 250 DP 755701 No. 1183 Cudgera Creek Road, Cudgera Creek be refused for the following reasons:

  1. Pursuant to Section 1.7 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development does not satisfy Part 7 of Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016. 

  2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, insufficient information has been provided to be satisfied that the provisions of the State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021, Chapter 2, Section 2.10, have been met and that the development will not result in an adverse ecological impact.  

  3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, insufficient information has been provided to be satisfied that the provisions of the State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021, Chapter 4, Section 4.6, have been met in relation to potential land contamination and appropriate remediation. 

  4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development fails to satisfactorily address the provisions of Part 5 of the Tweed Coast Comprehensive Koala Plan of Management 2020, an approved koala plan of management under the State Environmental Planning Policy (Biodiversity and Conservation) 2021. 

  5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development is not consistent with the following Aims of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014: 

    1. to give effect to the desired outcomes, strategic principles, policies and actions contained in the Council’s adopted strategic planning documents;
    2. to promote the responsible sustainable management and conservation of Tweed’s natural and environmentally sensitive areas and waterways, visual amenity and scenic routes, built environment, and cultural heritage;
    3. to conserve or enhance the biological diversity, scenic quality and geological and ecological integrity of Tweed;
    4. to conserve or enhance areas of defined high ecological value; and
    5. to provide special protection and suitable habitat for the recovery of the Tweed coastal Koala.

  6. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development is inconsistent with the objectives of the RU1 Primary Production zone under the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014, as it would introduce a land use that is incompatible with the agricultural use and function of the land and may result in ongoing land use conflict.

  7. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development is inconsistent with the objectives of the RU2 Rural Landscape zone under the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014, as it would adversely impact the rural character, landscape values and environmental qualities of the site and surrounding locality.

  8. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, insufficient information has been provided to demonstrate that the proposal is compliant with the provisions of Local Government (Manufactured Home Estates, Caravan Parks, Camping Grounds and Moveable Dwellings) Regulation 2021, particularly regarding water supply and the disposal of sewage.

  9. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, insufficient information has been provided regarding the importation of fill as required under Clause 7.2 Earthworks of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014.

  10. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, insufficient information has been provided regarding the flood impacts of the development as required under Clause 5.21 of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014.

  11. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, insufficient information has been provided regarding the special flood considerations of the development as required under Clause 5.22 of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014.

  12. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, insufficient information has been provided regarding acid sulfate soils to demonstrate that the proposal is compliant with the provisions of under Clause 7.1 of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014.

  13. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, insufficient information has been provided to determine that the proposal incorporates adequate arrangements for the provision of essential services including suitable vehicular access, supply of water and the disposal and management of sewage as required under Clause 7.10 Essential Services of the Tweed Local Environmental Plan 2014.

  14. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development fails to satisfy the provisions of Section A19 Biodiversity and Habitat Management of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2008 in relation to the avoidance, protection and management of red flagged biodiversity values.  

  15. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development does not comply with Section B5 of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2025 due to unacceptable impacts on the scenic character and landscape values of the locality and is inconsistent with the Tweed Scenic Landscape Protection Policy. 

  16. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(iii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, insufficient information has been provided to demonstrate compliance with Section 2.3.12 of the Tweed Development Control Plan 2025, in relation to mosquito and biting midge impacts.

  17. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development will likely result in an unacceptable significant impact on the environmental attributes of the land in regard to flora and fauna.

  18. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the application does not include adequate information to demonstrate that the proposal will not significantly impact the locality by causing land use conflict, including but not limited to environmental impacts (natural and built) and social and economic impacts.

  19. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(d) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the assessment of the proposal has had regard to the 88 unique community submissions objecting to the proposal and the issues raised have not been adequately addressed or mitigated. 

  20. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, for the reasons particularised above, the proposed development is not in the public interest. 
      
  1. Council, in relation to the Class 1 Appeal against the refusal of Development Application DA26/0311, provides delegation under Section 377(1) of the Local Government Act to Council’s General Manager or delegate to conduct the Appeal proceedings on behalf of Council and to engage any necessary experts.

  2. ATTACHMENT 3 is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because it contains: 
          (e) information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks what interpretive signage currently exists across the Tweed Shire providing information about local wildlife, the natural environment, cultural heritage and local history, and whether there are opportunities and potential funding sources to expand this signage - for example, information about whales and other marine life at coastal headlands?

Acting Director Sustainable Communities and Environment replied:

Council currently has a range of interpretive signage installed across the Tweed Shire within parks, reserves, foreshore areas, walking trails and public open spaces. These signs provide information on local flora and fauna, environmental values, Aboriginal cultural heritage, European settlement history, coastal and estuarine processes, and other points of local interest. Examples include signage associated with coastal reserves, environmental restoration projects, cultural heritage sites and visitor destinations.
 
Specific to whales, an interpretive sign was recently renewed at the top of Norries Headland, Bogangar. There is also a covered information signboard at Hastings Point headland, near the seasonal camping / day use area. This signboard was developed in partnership with the Hastings Point Marine Centre and contains great information about the surrounding environment and includes information about marine mammals.
 
Interpretive signage is often identified and delivered through location-specific plans of management and master plans. For example, the Hastings Point Headland Management Plan identifies interpretive signage as a means of enhancing visitor understanding of the area's environmental, cultural and scenic values. Similar opportunities may also arise through future reviews of plans of management, reserve master plans and tourism initiatives.
 
Council recognises the value of interpretive signage in educating residents and visitors, strengthening connections to place and promoting environmental stewardship. There are opportunities to review and enhance interpretive signage across the Shire, including at coastal headlands and lookouts where information relating to whales, marine wildlife, coastal ecosystems and Aboriginal cultural heritage could enhance the visitor experience.
 
To support a more strategic and coordinated approach, Council will consider interpretive signage requirements as part of the development of the Open Space Asset Management Plan. This will assist in identifying existing assets, future priorities, maintenance requirements and opportunities for investment across the open space network.
 
Potential funding sources for new or expanded interpretive signage may include State and Federal tourism, environmental, cultural heritage and public open space grant programs, as well as developer contributions, partnerships with community organisations and sponsorship opportunities. Future projects would be subject to funding availability, Council priorities and ongoing asset management considerations.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Brinsmead asks could you please provide an update on the current status of DA22/0088 concerning the proposed telecommunications tower at Pottsville, including any anticipated timeframes?

Cr Kimberly Hone returned to the meeting at 1.54pm.

Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead returned to the meeting at 1.55pm.

Director Planning and Regulation replied:
﻿
I can advise that the development approval remains current and the applicant, Indara, has advised that all documentation required for the Construction Certificate has now been submitted to a private certifier. They are expecting the Construction Certificate to be issued by the end of this month.
 
While a firm construction commencement date has not yet been confirmed, the applicant anticipates construction will begin before Christmas. The overall construction program is expected to take approximately three to four months and includes construction of the tower compound, installation of Optus and Telstra equipment, and connection of power services.
 
Subject to those works proceeding as planned, Optus is currently targeting the facility being operational by the end of March next year, with Telstra expected to follow a similar timeframe. The applicant has advised that the two key risks to these timeframes are the availability of power connections, which are outside their direct control, and weather conditions during construction.
 
I have also been provided with a coverage map from Optus which indicates the tower is expected to significantly improve mobile coverage and in-building mobile service across Pottsville Beach and surrounding coastal areas, particularly in locations that currently experience weaker reception.
 
Given the map is quite detailed and technical in nature, I am happy to provide a copy to all Councillors following today's meeting for their information.
 
Importantly, the applicant has confirmed that Indara, Optus and Telstra all recognise the strong community interest in this project and remain committed to delivering the facility as soon as practicably possible.

The nature of the interest is that Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead's son is employed by Newton Denny Chapelle. Cr Rhiannon Brinsmead will manage the Interest by vacating the Chamber for discussion and not voting on the item.

Cr Chris Cherry

  4. Easement(s) be created over public authority reticulation services, if any. 

  5. All related documents will be executed under the Common Seal of Council.

  6. If reasonable objections are received, a report will be brought back for further Council consideration.

  7. ATTACHMENTS 5, 6 and 7 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:

    (e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

REASON FOR CONFIDENTIALITY

Local Government Act
This report is CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, which permits the meeting to be closed to the public for business relating to the following:

(d)     commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: 

 (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or 
 (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or 
 (iii) reveal a trade secret

(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law

(g)     advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege


Cr Chris Cherry
Cr Nola Firth

RECOMMENDED that:

  1. Council resolves to acquire a freehold and easement interest (Interests) in the land described as part Lot 21 in DP1082482, part Lot 1 in DP1075645, part Lot 4 in DP727425, part Lot 4 in DP1106447 and part Lot 2 in DP1107697 (Land) by agreement or compulsory process in accordance with Part 12, Division 1 of the Roads Act 1993 (Roads Act) and the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991 (Just Terms Act) for the purposes of a public road. 

  2. Council resolves to authorise the General Manager to negotiate with each person with an interest in the Land for the purpose of completing the acquisition by agreement and otherwise agreeing on any relevant matter in connection with the acquisition. 

  3. If agreement is reached, the Council acquires the Interests in the Land. 

  4. If in the opinion of the General Manager no such agreement has been reached following any required minimum period of negotiation, Council resolves that the Land be acquired by compulsory process in accordance with Part 12, Division 1 of the Roads Act and the Just Terms Act, and that Council:

    1. make application for approval from the Minister for Local Government in accordance with section 178 of the Roads Act to give all necessary Proposed Acquisition Notices (PAN) in accordance with the Just Terms Act;
    2. make an application to the Minister for Local Government and the Minister for Lands and Property in accordance with section 13(2)(b) of the Just Terms Act to approve a reduction in the PAN period (noting that the approval of a shorter period of notice under subsection 13(2)(b) requires the concurrence of the Minister for Land and Property under section 13(3) of the Just Terms Act);
    3. make each other application and/or take each further action as is necessary to obtain approval from the Minister, the Governor, the Office of Local Government or any other person or public authority as may be necessary;
    4. serve each PAN as may be required to be served; and
    5. take all actions as may be necessary, to carry out the acquisitions by compulsory process.    
  1. Council authorises the General Manager to complete and execute all documentation necessary to access the Land for the purposes of carrying out the road work and finalise and bring into force Council’s acquisition of the Interests in the Land.

  2. If the General Manager considers that an access agreement on reasonable terms with the owner of the Land cannot not be reached within a reasonable period of time, Council occupies the Land for the purposes of carrying out road works in accordance with section 175 of the Roads Act, and in doing so Council authorises the General Manager to issue notices to the Minister as may be necessary to enable Council to exercise those powers under section 175 of the Roads Act.

  3. Council’s seal be affixed to all documents necessary to complete this acquisition and registration of land and interests. 

  4. ATTACHMENTS 1-16 are CONFIDENTIAL in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, because they contain:
        (d) commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: 
             (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
             (ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or 
        (iii) reveal a trade secret
(e)     information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law
(g)    advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege.

 

The Motion was Carried
